tldr; why buy this when the original's now on Steam for much cheaper outside of steam sales

So RE3Make is a game that looked at the slight amount of cut content from the RE2Make and thought "Those are some ♥♥♥♥♥ numbers. Watch this" and proceeded to rip the still beating heart out of the original game like Kano in Mortal Kombat. Branching, live choices? Gone. Mine Thrower? Gone and replaced with a... mine grenade launcher type?  A more dynamic Nemesis that gave the illusion of actually following and adapting to you? Especially gone and turned into a set piece save for one single time at the beginning of the game. Dynamic and changing item placement each playthrough? Gone. Other boss fights outside of Nemesis? Gone and tossed to the wolves. How about areas like the Park, Dead Factory or the Clock Tower? 

Gone, gone and especially gone. The park is just gone, the Dead Factory got reworked into the NEST 2 (really creative there guys) and the Clock Tower is just faintly teased and then Jill just gets infected and passes out before she ever gets the chance to explore it. It's just another set piece for a Blood Starved Beast- excuse me, "Nemesis" boss fight."

The story itself entirely linear unlike the original game and feels less like RE3 and more like the SparkNotes version of RE3. Stuff like Jill's near escape in the helicopter before it gets shot down by Nemesis happens at the very *start* of the game, as opposed to later on in the Clock Tower. It's like the developers forgot why this scene stuck out and just kinda threw it in as RE3 iconography. Brad isn't stalked and killed by Nemesis at all, which absolutely takes away the impact of his shocking reveal and instead he just gets mauled by zombies. About the only thing I liked from the game was Carlos. I really liked him in the original and I really liked him here. It seems like it's really hard to mess up Carlos in general. 

Jill doesn't get off that easier. See, they nailed the "strong, competent ex SWAT" aspect of her character and her inability to back down, but they forgot or muted another aspect about Jill Valentine that I feel goes overlooked. Her compassion. In spite of everything she does and how many of her former fellow Raccoon City-ites she has to put down, Jill Valentine never lost her compassion for others. Despite how much she hated Umbrella for the Arklay Incident and her initial spat of hostility for Carlos, Jill couldn't bring herself to kick someone like Mikhail when he was down, bitten and clearly traumatized by the sheer loss of life around him. She was concerned, worried. In a weird way, Jill in the older games had the vibe of a concerned mother. 

Now Jill has that gentle compassion sanded off and it's been replaced by focusing more on the "action hero" aspect of her. More swearing, more screaming etc. They try to go for an angle of Jill having been severely traumatized by the events of RE1 and that could work, but the game spends so little time on her mental scars from the incident outside of one, maybe two nightmare sequences that it comes off as considerably more limp.

Which gets even weirder when you factor in Nikolai and the subtle changes to his character. In the original, Nikolai was there to collect data and wipe out evidence of Umbrella's wrong-doing, not especially complicated. He's mostly there to act not only as another hinderance to Jill but also kinda embody the traits of Umbrella as a whole. Uncaring, uncompromising and focused entirely on the bottom line; money. That's all Jill is in Nikolai's eyes, just another paycheck.

In the Remake, they try to make Nikolai this polar opposite to Jill, with how often he berates her for "hesitation" and her compassion when his first introduction is him just blasting one of the UBCS mercs in the face. On top of wanting to turn a profit, Nikolai doesn't even have loyalty to Umbrella as apparently a third-party hired him to further sabotage Umbrella and their efforts to bury the truth of Raccoon City. Nikolai has no loyalty, no love, no empathy for anyone around him. They even go to the effort of animating a bad ending of Nikolai quickly slashing Carlos' throat and knifing Jill in the face for Jill's hesitation and compassion for Carlos, her fear that she could kill him. 

It kinda feels like Classic Nikolai should be Remake Jill's antagonist and Remake Nikolai should be Classic Jill's antagonist in a weird way.

And what else can I say about Nemesis that hasn't been said million times over? The Tyrant in the RE2 Remake feels far more like Nemesis than the actual Nemesis we got in this Remake. In the original, while Nemesis showed up at specific times, the live choices of when to fight or what to do with him contributed to a feeling of organic and emergent gameplay. He was absolutely vicious, forcing you to either run or learn the dodge mechanic to stand your ground. Here, outside of the downtown section where he's allowed to kinda, sorta resemble classic Nemesis, he's a set piece just like nearly everything else in this game. It all feels just so hollow and fake, they don't even let Jill say her "You want STARS? I'll give you STARS!" line at the end of the final fight with Nemesis. And no disrespect to Nicole Tompkins, I'm sure she's a great person and heck, it's not like all of Jill's lines were the worst thing performed by humankind, but the way she said "You want STARS" feels like an extremely angry college student in theater trying to put on an "angry" voice. I dunno, maybe I'm just a bit too mean to her. 

It's weird, originally I played the RE2 Remake on PS4, having never played the OG beforehand and walked away feeling very happy. A revisit to the Steam version after playing the OG allowed me to better compare and contrast where the two versions' strengths and weaknesses lay. All in all, I still think OG 2 and RE2Make are both very fulfilling experiences that equally deserve to be looked at in their own right.

I played the original before RE3Make, and it just made RE3Make hurt all the more. It's all just so sad because I know there's absolutely a better game buried under here, it's not like there's nothing redeeming about the game. But as things stand, it's a glorified stand-alone expansion to RE2Make and I still wish I could get my money back.

I recently purchased the Raccoon City Edition, which includes Resident Evil 2 Remake and this game. After completing RE2, I moved on to this, and it’s inferior in nearly every way. Skip it you won’t miss anything..

Gameplay: This game is less of a survival horror game compared to RE2 because the guns are stronger, backtracking is minimal, enemies are less bullet spongey, and ammo drops are very generous, but that's the only praise this game can be given. 60% of the content that's present in the 1999 version isn't in this "remake" making the game very short, only taking four hours to complete on your first casual run. After that you'll be blitzing the game in less than two hours during achievement runs. There's no side content or gamemodes to experience after completing the main game. Nemesis is no longer a stalker compared to the original, all of his appearances are scripted and he's far less scary. He's simply more annoying on harder difficulties. Nightmare and Inferno mode is total bs the devs just increased enemy HP and spawned more zombies in tight spaces, contradicting the bullet spongey design they were originally going for.

Story: It's very short, the villains are lazily written and forgettable, and Nemesis was handled poorly they made him stupid for the sake of Jill's survival, even though he's the most intelligent tyrant in canon. The amount of plot armor Jill has is on par with the average shonen protagonist it really kills immersion. [spoiler] There are over SIX TIMES where Nemesis should of killed Jill, but two instances pissed me off the most: one where Jill survives a Rocket Blast point blank and recovers unscathed, another where Nemesis has her stunned after tossing her and DID NOT fire his flamethrower while looking directly at her.[/spoiler] Nemesis is meant to be an unstoppable force, but the cutscenes butcher his character just to keep Jill alive. 

TL;DR: Action focused gameplay, story is two hours long and the writing is terrible, too much cut content. 5/10 only pick it up while it's 90% off. The game is not worth half or full price.

A review for RE3R really deserves a 'mixed' option from Steam and here's why, if I reviewed RE3R as its own game it would easily be a very solid 7/10 rating.   If I reviewed it as a remake, however? 3/10, and that's being favourable.  

This game had a troubled development, as we know by now.  Developed in tandem with RE2R, RE3's team was the 'B-Team' with help from QLoc. As such, they had less of a budget to work with as CAPCOM was only just recovering from RE6 after 7's good reception.   Because of this, RE3R feels less like a full-fledged remake of a numbered entry and more like a DLC.

In a vacuum, this is an excellently-paced game. As my playtime shows, I got 100% within 5 hours (3 playthroughs) with knowledge of the game from previous platforms.  An entryman can easily beat this as their first RE in 5-6 hours and short games ARE good, nobody wants 300 hour open world slop. But, they didn't trim the fat to get to that short runtime, they removed iconic areas and features and replaced them with lazy, uninspired choices.  Let me break them down.

1: The intro sequence. In OG, Jill has been helping survivors for weeks in a raging summer. One night, her apartment explodes and zombies besiege her home (Farewell to my home...), she races to a nearby warehouse and meets the cowardly Dario, then fights her way through the streets and bumps into Brad who sets the tone perfectly by warning her something is hunting all of the STARS members, culminating in his brutal iconic death to Nemesis outside of RPD.  In the remake? Nemesis shows up after a weird forced first-person sequence at the beginning then leaves you alone for a while, Brad is killed by generic zombies instead which reduces Nemesis' terror-factor, and Jill runs Nemesis off a car park roof with a police car and Carlos saves her.   It's a needless change but it does so much to undermine the very monster featured on its box art.

2: The RPD. Jill cannot explore it at all. No melancholy revisiting the Office of her comrades, no anger as she reads over the files of the corrupt Chief Irons covering for Umbrella, no magnum in the STARS office and Jill thinking of Barry as she finds it, and no iconic Nemesis bursting through the west hall window.  Instead, Carlos goes there for ten minutes to recover some CCTV footage with Tyrell and then you're gone. 

3: The power station.  In the OG, they built tension with passing glimpses of something climbing the walls on your way there. In the remake? A weirdly fetishist cutscene where Jill is inseminated orally by one of the Deimos, who then just run at you next to convenient barrels and can just be shot through fences. The tension is removed just to have a shock cutscene. Why? 

4: Dead Factory and Clock Tower removed and trimmed down. Instead, we get NEST 2! It's NEST from RE2R but shinier, and with pale heads.  It's very obvious the B-team saw the RE2R team doing NEST and decided to do their own, but it didn't make the game better. You go through mostly empty labs save for paleheads and hunters, then you fight Nemesis with the railgun and escape.  In the OG, you go through Raccoon Park to the Dead Factory because it has a helipad to escape, and in the process you find the aftermath of a huge battle between the US Army and the deadly T-103 Tyrants.  It was peak, and the rail gun belonged to the US Army who deployed it to try to stop the Tyrants, subtly hinting that it can be used on Nemesis who is also a Tyrant variant. That was so much better and I don't know why it was replaced with a generic lab.  RE3R even blueballs you at one point: A Tyrant capsule appears, and Jill focuses on it, and you think "oh damn, they're gonna give us a Tyrant fight", but then you just get mobbed by more Hunters instead.

5: Nemesis. The dynamism is gone. He doesn't appear in set zones and no longer can ambush you at any time in them, there's no live-select choices to run or fight him. You can still get items from him if you down him which I do appreciate, but that's where the praise ends. He goes from scary, Terminator-like abomination to a pest at best and on replays you know he's only scripted to show up in 3 locations on the streets and all tension is removed.  Even his forms have been downgraded: in OG3, you damage him over the course of the campaign, breaking his limiter jacket, dousing him in acid, burning him, etc. and he visually changes to have tentacles, or leaking purple acid blood.  In 3R? He goes from humanoid to a dog then a bigger dog, and then a wall blob.  Not quite as threatening if he's that fragile.

6: No more ammo crafting with the reloading tool.  RE3 OG introduced crafting to the series, and weirdly in a post RE7 world, RE3R didn't include it.

7: Carlos' part of the game where he braves a hospital full of Hunters and zombies is still there, but they pad the runtime by giving you a wave defense part where you can see the game actively turn dead zombies to blobs of blood to save resources. This wasn't needed, at all. I would have much preferred if like in the OG, Carlos had to fight Nemesis to stop him breaching the door to get to Jill.

Now what does the remake do that I think is better than the OG? A few things.
Carlos' characterisation is MUCH better, Hell I would say most of the human cast is. Mikhail is more fleshed out, and even Tyrell who dies fairly unceremoniously in the OG has a subtle arc of being an Umbrella loyalist to believing in Jill's goal and helping her secure the vaccine, and Nicholai while still evil has a lot more gravitas.  Jill isn't as soft as she was in the OG, but her vocal performance is great and Nicole Tompkins really sold her trauma and aggravation with Umbrella. 

The Dodge mechanic is leagues better. In OG you just shoved enemies away, 3R turns it more into an offensive tool allowing you to score crits or roll past whole hordes of enemies, which really helps the pacing for a 'never stop running' type of story. If you did actually need to never stop running if the game was true to the OG, this mechanic would be regarded as a series best IMO.

Music is fantastic, when you can hear it.  The music for NEST 2 and the final battle are two particular favourites, and the Staff Credits theme has been touchingly redone. 

Movement and the overall feel of controls are among the series' best. Jill feels great in motion, and Carlos feels like Chris Redfield with more cardio. I wish the Dodge made a return in Requiem, but alas, here's hoping it does in REX.

Unlockable content is MASSIVE, putting even Requiem to shame.  Requiem has made me appreciate 3R's unlockable content a lot more: multiple costumes, dozens of weapons, Inferno Difficulty which outside of the final boss is not only superbly balanced but actually changes item locations, giving you Hip Pouches and the Magnum early, some key items are granted to you sooner, and Jill gets different rewards from the gemstone puzzle.  The SKELETON of this game is so damn good, it's the meat on the bone that's not prime. 

Closing out, the most important question likely to be asked is: is this game worth the £4.99 it's often on sale for. 
Yes, of course.  5 hour first playthrough as a newcomer minimum, dozens of unlocks and a really solid extra difficulty in Inferno will take you well over 10+ hours  for your first time.  £1 per hour of gameplay, this earns it and then some.

It was, and still is not worth the £34.99 it sits at without a sale, however.  There's a reason RE2R goes on sale for more than RE3R, the critical reception and the breadth of content in comparison.

Oh, I guess 3R has Resistance too which I had fun with on PS4, but it's dead now.

[h1]Going to say now while I recommend it, it's only if it's during a sale and if you're willing to overlook that it changes a drastic amount from what the original RE3 was.[/h1]

After a few weeks to sit on it, occasionally peek back to slowly chip at nightmare to start an inferno run, and play a bit more with what the game has to offer I came to the conclusion I was a little hard on this game with the negative review. Do I think it disrespects the source material? Kinda yeah. Do I think there's problems? Just like any game I've ever played, yes. Is Nemesis done dirty in this one? . . . Hold that thought because yesn't is the answer.


The story in this is RE3 reimagined to be more modernized and "Action Oriented" while still maintaining a bit of the survival horror the original had, there's entire sequences cut or changed due to what was originally slower paced and definitely more nuanced narrative. However, there are things that I think the remake does [i]better[/i] than the original that gets overlooked, namely the NEST 2 chapter/part/whatever you'd call it - in the original by this point [spoiler]it's an abandoned water treatment facility that umbrella used as a front for studying experiments done in the area[/spoiler], but that's the entire high and low of it there and in my opinion the last 30 minutes of the original fumble pretty badly where the remake does a much better job with certain characters and a more badass if linear ending.

The gameplay is what took a massive hit, and it's painfully different due to how many features were cut; No ammo press mechanic or tiered ammo powders, just the RE7/RE2make combine gunpowder + chem to make specific ammo (and no bonuses for making the same ammo multiple times either). No branch choices like either fighting the monster or fleeing into the police station, puzzles are made more linear so there's hardly any need to backtrack, [i]personally I kinda like the fact that backtracking is more optional than a required thing, I've never cared to backtrack through a resident evil out of the near entire franchise, and RE3 OG didn't change that either.[/i]
But despite what was removed, the dodge was improved to be far more consistent - especially if you're in some way disabled and need some forgiveness to the mechanic - while giving proper iframes to compensate for how wide grabs get, and the focused shot critical hits feel really good here just like in RE2make to boot. There are more positives unlisted but to keep it concise it's not [b]all[/b] bad here.

Characters' personalities, lines delivered, when they were delivered, and how they act between eachother also changed greatly, Jill is kind of an idiot and I strongly advise if you want context watch anybody play the first 15 minutes of the game and you'll understand, Carlos is much more respectable and just all around a normal human being with a want to save everyone he can, Nicholai is even more of a prick than in the OG and honestly that's one of the best improvements this game does head over shoulders to the original, and Nemesis.. well in my opinion he mostly [i]sounds[/i] the same if not better here, but he's not really fun as a "persistent threat" and he shines much better in his scripted fights which I know kills it a lot for many people - but as a cinematic experience it's still not terrible.

OST and Soundscape I think is genuinely the worst part of the remake, it breaks the bones of so many good things from the OG to try and put them back together in a "Familiar but reimagined" way that it either comes off as noise noise noise, or unmemorable on a good note. It's not bad when looking at it objectively and asking if they even tried to make it sound good, but it doesn't do good to do right by the OG which a remake needs to do.


[h2]And now for a TL;DR[/h2]
I'd say this game gets scathing criticism at times for what is honestly not a terrible game, I think it's overpriced and is only worth about $20 even with the updates it had gotten, but for the people either who never played/don't want to play the clunky fixed camera + tank control experience of a PS1 title this isn't half bad at all to retell the story coherently. For fans who did play the OG/saw the OG start to finish it's definitely much harder to recommend, maybe try the demo or watch the first episode of someone's playthrough to see if it's worth it despite how different it can be from the original, and of course still get it on a half off sale at minimum.

I didn't play much with the infinite ammo  rocket launcher but I'm sure it's as fun as it always was, I personally say this game is a must play if you like the series even if you don't like the series I think its a good gateway into the games. Resident Evil 3 being my second RE game played in the franchise is the weakest in my opinion. That's not saying its bad, it just didn't meet the expectations RE2 flawlessly executed. I never played the original RE3 but reading online i know a lot has been taken out from the original and not been put into the remake, so this is coming from someone who has only just played the remake.

I had a great time playing RE3, it felt like i left off where i finished in the RE2 remake, i loved how you revisit certain parts of the map from RE2, i loved how it gave you a different perspective of the police station and gave you answers to events in RE2 ( like how it became overrun in the first place) RE3 felt more like an action packed, cut scene type of game. The story was fine, the characters were likeable and also had some personality jill, carlos and Nicolai are solid aspects to the game and each one of them play their role perfectly. It did everything well just like RE2 but was just noticeably way shorter. 
Three things i did find disappointing was i found this game really easy on my first standard run. The game just throws so much ammunition, guns, and healing items your way you're basically unstoppable for a good first chunk of the game. I found that killed the immersion and pacing of the game because i found myself killing everything in my path because i had the ammunition to do so. If i got hit it was no big deal because id have 15 healing items so it didn't feel like i was being punished for my mistakes. 

I feel like RE3 was more straightforward like here's a gun and  healing items blast your way through, it didn't have that much progression of getting to and from places, like finding keys to unlock doors or finding important items to progress.RE2 just had a nice feeling of progression which RE3 really lacks on. I found myself more on autopilot in RE3 play through as it just felt like i was running and gunning and there isn't anything wrong with that. I just really enjoyed the progression and puzzles in RE2.

Another disappointment to me was Nemesis was nowhere near as a threat as Mr.X from RE2 was. Nemesis only showed up in scripted parts of the game unlike Mr.X stalking the corridors of the Racoon police station and showing up at random times. After the first few scripted Nemesis chase scenes, i got use to him not sticking around so i really had no feelings compared to what Mr.X had on me. It started to feel like oh yeah he's going to chase me for 5 minutes in a cinematic chase scene and after that i can go on to doing what i need to do without him being around. Apparently Mr.X was suppose to be a prototype of what nemesis should be. But honestly Mr.X was a lot more intimidating and unpredictable which added to the overall immersion of the second game.

That being said i still think its genuinely a fun polished game, the gameplay felt the same as RE2, it felt smooth and snappy, the inventory and UI felt and looked clean, and i like how they added you can dodge which RE2 didn't have.
Again RE2 being a flawless masterpiece, it set the bar real high, but this game just doesn't quite meet that bar. Its a great game bit short but it did exactly what it set out to do and i enjoyed the experience.

Even though i never played the original i personally enjoyed this game a lot and would play it again in the future but at a higher difficulty.

I still remember the first time I stepped into Raccoon City back in 1999. The static-filled streets, the oppressive silence, the distant groans of the undead—it felt like stepping into a nightmare that never quite let go. So when Resident Evil 3 Remake was announced, I wasn’t just excited—I was cautious. Nostalgia is a powerful thing, and tampering with it can either elevate a classic or hollow it out. Thankfully, what we got is something more complicated… but still undeniably special.

From the very first moments, the remake captures that same suffocating tension I fell in love with decades ago, but through a modern lens that feels immediate and visceral. Raccoon City is no longer just a backdrop—it’s alive, collapsing in real time. Fires rage, civilians scream, and the sense of urgency is constant. This isn’t just survival horror anymore; it’s survival in motion.

And then there’s Jill Valentine. This version of her is sharper, tougher, and more human than ever before. She’s not just escaping the city—she’s fighting through trauma, rage, and exhaustion. As a long-time fan, it’s honestly refreshing to see her given this much depth. Her interactions, especially with Carlos, feel grounded and natural in a way that older titles couldn’t quite achieve.

Of course, we have to talk about Nemesis. Back in the original, he was terrifying because he was unpredictable—a relentless force that could show up at any moment. In the remake, he’s more cinematic, more scripted… but no less intimidating. There’s a different kind of fear here. It’s less about when he’ll appear and more about how overwhelming he feels when he does. The sheer scale and aggression he brings to each encounter still made my heart race in ways few modern games manage.

Gameplay-wise, it builds beautifully on what Resident Evil 2 Remake established. Movement is smoother, gunplay is tighter, and the addition of the dodge mechanic adds a layer of skill that rewards timing and composure under pressure. It’s not just about conserving ammo anymore—it’s about mastering encounters.

That said… I’d be lying if I said everything sat perfectly with me. As someone who knows the original inside and out, I couldn’t help but feel the absence of certain locations and moments. Some of the slower, more exploratory sections that gave the original its pacing and identity are noticeably trimmed down. The game moves fast—sometimes too fast—and that sense of lingering dread occasionally gives way to a more action-driven rhythm.

But even with those omissions, there’s a clear passion behind this remake. It doesn’t replace the original—it reinterprets it. It’s like revisiting an old memory that’s been sharpened, rearranged, and retold with modern sensibilities.

In the end, Resident Evil 3 Remake feels like a love letter written in a different handwriting. It may not hit every nostalgic note long-time fans were hoping for, but it still captures the spirit of survival, fear, and resilience that defined the series in the first place.

And as someone who’s walked these streets before… I’m just glad Raccoon City still burns as brightly as ever.

When I played the older "Resident Evil" games on Playstation, it was a fresh idea on action games. Being able to play a horror style game and participate in killing zombies and it's creators. Finding a limited supply of weapons and learning how to manage limited resources, such as ammo, healing items, and learning to create new items out of other items. It was an early type of survival game. Plus, being limited to save your game, as you could only save if you had ribbons for the type writer.

And then, they added bonuses based on the difficulty as well as how fast you beat the game and how well you beat the game. Along with the action scenes, you also had to solve puzzles plus find keys for locked doors.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is, of course, the remake of the Playstation version, just with more and better 3D details. This is the continuation of the first 2 games and continues to tell the story of Raccoon City. You play as Jill Valentine, and at certain times, you play as Carlos. As you play s either character, you are trying to piece together the clues, as well as collect items, to help you solve the mystery of what happened to all the people, as well as learn about where the zombie infestation, comes from.

The game is played in a few genres. The main one being action, where you have your trusty weapons and you find ammo along the way. The only this is, you are going to have to be very limited in your use of ammo as there is not a lot of it. You will need to use your ammo sparingly as you play. You can also combine items to make more ammo as you progress in the game. Along the way, you will also find such things as keys to unlock doors, parts to unlock puzzles, codes to unlock safes, and other various items in order to progress in the game and story.

Of course, as part of the action, you will have to deal with many zombies. Learn how to take them out quickly so you can progress with little loss of ammo. Your main battles will be against boss battles and one scene where you battle several zombies at one time from multiple directions.

Overall, I had a lot of fun with this game and the graphic details were very good. However, I did have a few personal issues with the whole game. One of the main problems I had with this game was that, it was a lot easier to play this game than it's Playstation counterpart.  I would almost swear the Playstation version was a lot harder to play than this remake. ( Keep in mind, I am talking about the 1998 version of Resident Evil 3 was harder, not this version. ) My other personal gripes are as follows...

1.) The game was a lot shorter than the Playstation version, at least IMHO.

2.) There weren't as many zombies to battle versus the Playstation version that had a lot of zombies, at least IMHO

3.) Nemesis looked more like a cross between Aliens and human hybrid, in fact, the more I battled the bosses, the more it looked like it came from the Aliens lore than from it's Resident Evil counterpart. What was Capcom thinking when they made Nemesis look like he does?

4.) I will say I expected a lot more out of this game because of how much they put into the game itself as well as it's story line and the overall size of the game. I really expect a much longer gameplay and more places to go.

The only reason I gave it a thumbs up is because it is a fairly good game and it is fun to play, and a lot of stuff to unlock once it's beaten, just don't expect to have the game last long. I managed to beat this game, and unlock everything in 8 hours. ( Which is also the time of this review. ) Once you unlock everything, there's not really much else to do or any reason to replay the game. A bit disappointed in the whole game as it's very short, but it is fun to play, for the most part. ( I got this game on sale as a bundled deal. If you do decide to get this game, only get it because your a fan of the series and try to get this game on sale, and if possible, as a bundled deal. )

Ремейк Resident Evil 3: честный боевик, который не предаёт

С ремейками Resident Evil у меня отношения сложные. После того, что Capcom сделала с оригинальной четвёртой частью, я стал относиться к ним с огромным скепсисом. Но ремейк третьей части - это совсем другая история. Он не притворяется тем, чем не является. И за это ему можно простить многое.

Никакого когнитивного диссонанса

Resident Evil 3 (оригинал) никогда не был хоррором. Он был динамичным, почти аркадным боевиком с элементами преследования. Ремейк не пытается переписать этот жанровый диагноз. Он с первой минуты заявляет: я - экшен. Быстрый, жёсткий, ритмичный. В этом его главное достоинство. Он не заставляет вас пробираться по коридорам с фонариком, не навязывает ложное чувство беспомощности. Вместо этого - идеально отточенное уклонение (с замедлением времени), выстрелы, которые ощущаются весомо, и враги, которые не ждут вашего решения.

После той пафосной и выхолощенной «тактичности», которую натянули на ремейк четвёртой части, ремейк третьей ощущается как глоток ледяной «Колы». Он не затянут. Не перегружен QTE. Не пытается заставить вас плакать над судьбой второстепенного персонажа. Просто: вот Джилл, вот Раккун-Сити, вот Немезис, который иногда проламывает стену или падает сверху, чтобы дать вам пощёчину. Всё по делу.

Джилл и Карлос: живые люди, а не манекены

Вот где разработчики действительно преуспели - так это в характерах. Джилл Валентайн в ремейке - это не фарфоровая кукла в мини-юбке (как в оригинале) и не суперсолдат без эмоций. Она - злая, уставшая, но не сломленная. Её диалоги с Карлосом - лучшие сцены во всей игре. Они перебрасываются колкостями, спорят, подкалывают друг друга. Это напоминает ту самую химию между Леоном и Эдой в оригинальной RE4, которой так не хватает в ремейке. Карлос вообще получил отдельную благодарность: из латиноамериканского «мачо-пушечного мяса» он превратился в живого, самоироничного, надёжного напарника. Его сцена в больнице - возможно, единственный по-настоящему хоррор-момент во всей игре, и она работает именно потому, что нам не всё равно.

Никто не ломал героев под «современные стандарты». Они остались собой - просто получили больше глубины и нормальную мимику.

Реиграбельность: то, ради чего возвращаются

И главный козырь ремейка RE3 - это желание запустить игру снова. Здесь после финальных титров не остаётся пустоты. Открывается магазин бонусов. Хочешь ракетницу с бесконечными патронами? Пожалуйста, копи очки. Хочешь бесконечный пистолет или штурмовую винтовку с бесконечным боеприпасом? Легко. Или хочешь пройти игру в режиме «Кошмар» или «Ад», где враги расставлены совсем иначе, а Немезис в первой же схватке бегает быстрее, чем ты? Для этого тоже можно прикупить в магазине полезных монеток, повышающих защиту или атаку. Это не просто накрутка сложности - это переосмысление уровней, заставляющее выучить каждое уклонение.

Игра знает: ты придёшь не за сюжетом. Ты придёшь выбить S-ранк, открыть классический костюм Джилл и в сотый раз эффектно уйти от ракеты, выпущенной Немезисом. И она не стесняется этого. В отличие от некоторых других ремейков, которые пытаются быть «серьёзным произведением», но при этом дарят вам плюшевого волка за сбор всех сокровищ.

О недостатках: коротко и честно

Да, игра короткая. Да, это не оригинальный RE3 с выбором маршрута и живым Немезисом, который следует за вами через районы. Да, из неё вырезали часы с часовой башней и парк с червями. Я не буду спорить: это минус. Но я предпочту короткую, плотную, переигрываемую игру жалкой пародии на саму себя. Ремейк RE3 не врёт в системных требованиях и не врёт в обещаниях. Он говорит: «Я - боевик на вечер, перепроходи меня ещё пять раз(если захочешь)». И он это выполняет на 100%.

Сравнение с ремейком RE4: честность против пафоса

А теперь - буквально вскользь - о том, почему этот обзор вообще появился. Я избегал ремейка четвёртой части как огня. После выхода Resident Evil Requiem (девятой части, где Леон наконец-то снова стал собой) я всё же прикоснулся к RE4 Remake - но не к основной игре. Я знал, что меня вырвет от того, что Capcom сделала с ней. В основной сюжет ремейка я намеренно не играл, но видел достаточно: я смотрел обзоры так называемых «фанатов», которые сами не играли в оригинал 2005 года и не понимают, за что его любили. Они попросту не заметили отсутствия того самого густого тумана, создававшего атмосферу. Не заметили отсутствия стресса при стрельбе - того самого ощущения, которое в оригинале было чем-то средним между неуклюжестью первых частей и экшеном последующих. Не заметили отсутствия Леона Скотта Кеннеди - живого парня, который был не прочь пошутить, а внешне выглядел как латиноамериканец, коим он и является. В ремейке же он превратился в угрюмого типа с внешностью левого прохожего из подворотни. Этого хватило, чтобы убедиться: основная игра ремейка - катастрофа.

При этом я дважды перепрошёл оригинальную RE4 за Леона (для чистоты восприятия) и прошёл DLC Separate Ways и режим наёмников в ремейке. Проходить их пришлось скорее от скуки, но стоит признать: эти режимы получились качественными. А вот то, что они сделали с основным сюжетом ремейка - повторюсь, катастрофа.

И ладно бы это был просто неудачный ремейк. Но качество RE4 Remake намного спорнее других частей серии, и не просто так. Разработку перезапускали: по слухам, изначально проект вели на аутсорсе силами студии M-Two, а потом Capcom в попыхах передала его внутренней команде Division 1. Видимо, именно поэтому основная игра выглядит так, будто её склепали на коленке, в то время как DLC и наёмники (вдохновлённые режимом из Village) получились на удивление съедобными. Capcom выпотрошила душу оригинала. А те, кто называет это «шедевром», либо не играли в игру 2005 года, либо забыли, за что её любили.

Итог: 8/10 - лучше честный боевик, чем пафосная подделка

Если вы, как и я, устали от ремейков, которые ломают оригинал ради ложной «серьёзности», дайте шанс ремейку третьей части. Он не идеален. Но он честен. Он не ломает героев. Он не стыдится своей аркадной природы. И он дарит то самое чувство, которое в современных играх встречается всё реже: когда после финальной битвы тебе не хочется выключать консоль, а хочется сразу запустить новое прохождение - с уже купленным в магазине бесконечным оружием, под новую музыку, чтобы снова размазать Немезиса. Потому что, чёрт возьми, играть должно быть весело. А не «аутентично» и «киношно».

Ставлю 8 из 10. За реиграбельность, за живых персонажей и за то, что эта игра - не предательство.

RE3 remake is such a disappointment. So I've replayed this numerous times and decided to do so on PC after already playing this on PS4, and this was only because it was thrown into a bundle which made buying the remaining games and DLC I didn't have on PC cheaper. If this game was not included within that bundle, I would not have purchased it again unless it was on a very deep discount (that 90% off when it comes around? Best time to get this hollow reimagining). On its own, RE3 remake works well enough as a survival horror game and has fun gameplay mechanics like its predecessor, but RE3 remake fails to be a serviceable retelling of the original, iconic Jill Valentine story. 

The original game was already the weakest of the original trilogy in my opinion just because RE1 and RE2 were so good, and RE3 had a few downsides, such as reused assets/locations from RE2, a shorter campaign, the story, while it is still good, is a step back when compared to the previous installment's zapping feature and cross-campaign narratives to tell one overall story. A remake could've expanded on the story and the locations featured, adding more narrative depth and giving us a sprawling Raccoon City to explore without the limitations of PS1 hardware. 

If you've read any review of this game, you're probably aware that RE3 remake cuts a lot of content from the original or reduces it significantly. Raccoon City is condensed to a few streets and alleyways, the Clock Tower and Park are entirely skipped, including the Grave Digger boss, the factory is replaced with NEST 2, an area of reused assets from RE2 remake and its name appropriately communicates the lack of imagination they had with this remake. Some of the other unique gameplay elements, like the choice mechanics, Nemesis' ability to pursue the player in numerous locations during exploration, and randomization of items, enemies, etc. in each playthrough are gone as well. So much of the character and identity of the original Resident Evil 3 is stripped away and sacrificed to create a mediocre retelling of a classic RE story. What also hurts is that RE3 remake doesn't really add anything new or interesting to replace what it cut.

Now with the original trilogy on Steam, there is much less of a reason to play the RE3 remake other than to experience it for yourself and make up your own opinion; however, I find it to be a bland, mediocre remake that fails to recreate the same magic that its predecessor was able to.

I beat this game in half the time it took me to beat RE2. Is that a good thing? I'll let you decide.

So, I have very mixed feelings on this game, so I'll begin with the pros.
First, seeing Jill Valentine again was awesome, though it sucked that Julia Voth didn't return to model Jill, but the new model isn't bad. Also, she clearly has more character here than she did in RE1, making her far more interesting already. Carlos was a decent character, and seeing his development in this game was enjoyable. Second, the gameplay was...fine? I'll touch on what I dislike later. I enjoyed the new dodge mechanic introduced to the game, and the quality of life changes were very welcome. Lastly, I enjoyed the environments. Being in the streets of Raccoon City was awesome, and some of the set pieces were well done. And...that's all the nice things I have to say about this game. So...

The cons. First off, despite Jill and Carlos being interesting enough characters here, NO ONE else was. I genuinely did not care for any other character besides the two protagonists. This sucks because I enjoyed the NPC characters in RE2. Second, the story was soooo rushed! Like I mentioned previously, I beat RE3 in 7 hours, meanwhile it took me 14 to beat RE2, and 18 to beat RE1. No wonder I didn't care for any of the characters, the story moved on from everyone as soon as it could. There were really only two returning characters throughout the game, and neither of them were that interesting. Third, Nemesis was a letdown. He only seemed to have appeared during scripted segments, whereas the Tyrant (Mr. X) in RE2 had the entire second RPD segment to do his thing. Despite Nemesis serving as such a "big" character in the plot, he really did...nothing? He appeared a few times, slapped Jill around, and that's it. And for a game remaking a game called "Resident Evil 3: NEMESIS" it really felt like NEMESIS didn't do much at all. His boss fights were better than RE2's fights though (but that's not a high bar). Fourth, the lack of ink ribbons is disappointing. Such an iconic piece of Resident Evil ripped away because of what? Hardcore barely felt difficult because I could save whenever I wanted. They didn't even limit one save per typewriter or anything, just legit "save whenever you want" PLUS autosaves. And while we're on the topic of Resident Evil losing it's iconography, HOW did they mess up on the horror this bad. Nothing was scary in this game! Nemesis was at first, but he quickly got old (somehow). Nothing gave me that chilling vibe like the first two games gave me. And somehow there are little to no puzzles? Resident Evil, the series known for it's survival horror and puzzles, lost BOTH of those things in their third game, really? Lastly, the story is so lazy. Seriously. Three...THREE games in a row do you go from upper ground, to a basement, followed by sewers, and lastly, a lab. It's getting old. They somehow managed to do something so often that it got old, while also doing away with what they did best, making this game feel so out of place while also fitting in? This is why I'm mixed on the game. I like elements of it, like there is clearly some love for Resident Evil here, but it's also missing so much that I just can't recommend this game to anyone.

Also, sorry if this formatting is a bit messy. I accidently deleted my old review before posting it so I had to go over my (mental) notes and rewrite everything down.

So, overall, don't play this game unless you're a hardcore fan of the series, and even then, I can't promise any enjoyment.

The internet will try to convince you this game is bad, when in fact it is a pretty good entry (in isolation, at least). Sure, it is shorter compared to previous entries and feels like it rushes you to the ending and to some extent, that is a fair criticism. Another crucial mistake is not featuring the Clocktower segment from the original. Sure, the game manages to retell its story in a different way but you can't shake the feeling that the whole deal screams limited budget.

Gameplay-wise, it is similar to the Resident Evil 2 Remake with some improvements here and there. It is faster, more intense, and less puzzle-oriented, but it still maintains that sense of imminent danger if you are clunky or reckless, balancing survival and action aspects while leaning more toward the latter.

Story-wise, it retells the events of the original in a less campy, more grounded, and serious tone well. The characters are more well-developed compared to the original, and the game features my favorite version of Jill Valentine. Nemesis, on the other hand, has been dumbed down from being a looming menace in the original due to random appearances to all of its appearances being scripted and it basically failing its task in stupidly funny ways.

Overall, the remake is a fine addition to the series but I'd recommend getting it on sale. The pacing and missing segments are the game's biggest issues and the chances the developers will revisit the game anytime soon are pretty low. While the events of the Resident Evil 2 Remake take place over a single night, it still takes longer to beat than a game whose story spans multiple days. Again, it's a good game in isolation, very well-optimized and smooth, fun and engaging, but its very different compared to the original.

I should preface with the fact I got this game on sale for 4.99 and I have not played the OG. So I went into RE3R blind only knowing who Nemesis, Jill, and Carlos are. So while I cannot comment on the comparison to the original, I can on this as a standalone. Personally I'd say its a decent 7.5-8/10. The game is on the shorter side especially compared to 2R and 4R, but it still has the same fun gameplay as 2 which is a plus. The story is pretty good building on Racoon City and it connection with the outbreak. Jill and Carlos are great I have zero complaints both of them personality wise and gameplay wise are highlights of the game in my opinion. What holds this game back for me is Nemesis, despite being cool in design and boss fights, just is not near as good as Mr. X is in 2R. The game as mentioned is much shorter with the S rank times being 2 hours for everything but hardcore with is an 1 hour 45 min. And I'd be remiss if I did not mention the cut content others have mentioned from the original game. While I do not have experience with the OG, I can't in good faith not ding this game for cutting content fans of the original would want to see especially since that makes this game not as faithful a remake as it should be. Overall I do not recommend this as your first RE title if you are getting into the series, I'd reserve that for 2R or even 7 as that is how I started years ago. But if you are into the series and especially the story i'd say pick this up when it goes on a good sale.

RE3 Remake is underrated. It's a fantastic game and so far my favourite in the entire franchise. The gameplay is intense, dynamic and engaging. The amazing character design and interactions between characters make it impossible not to like them. While it's still a survival horror game with limited resources, you won't be hiding from monsters feeling helpless and weak. When playing as Jill and Carlos, the highly trained special operatives, you feel powerful as you fight evil to save Raccoon City. Another thing I really liked in RE3 is the linear story which actually makes sense, something that can't be said about RE2 where the scenarios overlap and don’t really work from a narrative perspective. 

As for the negatives, RE3 could definitely be longer, but despite that it’s still great entertainment. It’s worth playing RE3 and RE2 together because even though they are totally different they complete each other storywise.

Для начала хочу сказать, что я не обзорщик и не игрожур. Поэтому здесь я буду описывать свои чисто субъективные впечатления от игры, которая меня неожиданно удивила. И, к сожалению, не в лучшую сторону.

Начну с того, что на данный момент я закончил первое прохождение на сложности «Хардкор», и, к сожалению, сам геймплей и механики меня крайне сильно разочаровали. Причём разочарование настигло меня практически с самого начала игры, ибо моя первая встреча с зомби оказалась отличной от того, что я запомнил по второй части.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Во-первых.[/b] По моим субъективным ощущениям, у поражённых вирусом гражданских изменилось поведение в плане захватов главной героини. Если во второй части один-два выстрела в чувствительную точку зомби вводили его в стан и позволяли просто пробежать мимо него, то здесь количество выстрелов увеличилось до четырёх-пяти. Если во второй части те же самые два-три выстрела по коленям приводили зомби к потере конечности и заставляли его просто ползать за тобой, упрощая возможность носиться по локациям и изучать их, то здесь это ощущается иначе.

Дополнительно зомби практически во всей игре получили увеличение характеристик, которое позволяет им очень быстро передвигаться и при этом оставаться очень тихими. Если в ремейке второй части зомби, перед тем как провести атаку и схватить тебя, должен был перейти в некоторое состояние, которое подразумевало, что он готов к захвату и тебе не стоит попадать в зону, которая триггерит ненавистную мной grab-атаку, то в третьей части зомби находятся практически перманентно в состоянии готовности к захвату. Из-за этого наблюдаются куда более рваные анимации, возникает ощущение нечестности и злости, когда тебя хватают, хотя ты не слышал противника и в предыдущий раз, когда его видел, помнил, что он находится достаточно далеко. И всё это в совокупности изменяет ощущение от игры: стиль игры, которым ты пользовался во второй части, по большей части здесь вреден и обычно приводит к смерти в третьей.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Во-вторых.[/b] Б[i]о[/i]льшая аркадность приводит к тому, что на локациях везде раскиданы боеприпасы, и, как итог, я никогда в них не нуждаюсь. Я не беспокоюсь об их количестве и могу расстреливать всех зомби на локации, доводя её до состояния, когда никто мне не мешает её исследовать, что приводит к отсутствию ощущения незащищённости и создаёт дискомфорт. Если прибавить к этому изменившийся геймплей по взаимодействию с зомби, то в итоге я стреляю 25/8 просто потому, что могу.

[hr][/hr]

[b]В-третьих.[/b] Особенности механики персонажа. Теперь, играя за персонажа, я могу уворачиваться. И увороты поначалу ощущались как какой-то рак, ибо попасть в тайминг атаки моба требует от тебя выучить особенности их анимаций. Далее, приходится приучить себя не держать пустым магазин, который теперь может начать автоматически перезаряжаться, если ты выстрелил последний патрон. И самое ужасное — это невозможность увернуться, пока ты перезаряжаешься, что превращает игру в мини-стратегию, где тебе нужно думать перед каждой перезарядкой: а стоит ли мне это делать сейчас, или я могу потенциально получить по лицу и мне стоит сначала отбежать от в безопасное место.

[hr][/hr]

[b]В-четвёртых.[/b] Камера здесь — полноправный противник, которая во время захватов очень любит втыкаться в стены или в любые высокодетализированные камешки, бордюры, заграждения, ящики и всё, что ещё может лежать у вас под ногами. И в процессе игры, когда тебя окружает толпа или какой-нибудь особый противник хватает тебя при полном здоровье, подразумевается, что ты можешь отмахнуться и побеждать дальше. Однако камера втыкается в препятствие, и ты испытываешь боль от того, что не можешь прицелиться, не можешь сориентироваться, где находятся противники, не можешь в итоге выйти из сложной ситуации и отправляешься на последнее сохранение.

[hr][/hr]

[b]В-пятых.[/b] Босс. Схватки с Немезисом — это что-то, что ощущается либо как простая прогулка, когда ты просто бегаешь от него и стреляешь по нему, либо как минное поле, где каждое твоё движение должно быть абсолютно выверено и ты должен точно выучить все тайминги как своего персонажа, так и атак босса. А если прибавить к этому всё вышеперечисленное, то победа над второй стадией полностью заряженным персонажем превращается в испытание, где ты должен держать в уме, как перемещаются зомби, как прыгает Немезис по арене и как лучше всего сменеджерить всё оружие, что ты принёс с собой, чтобы удачно пережить этот бой.

Отдельно отмечу, что игра не особо понимает, в каком состоянии находится твой персонаж, поэтому ситуации, когда тебя по всей арене кидает Немезис, а потом так складывается, что ты лежишь под ногами зомби и у тебя запускается анимация захвата, в которой игра забирает управление, могут повторяться часто. Ну а если Немезис начинает раскручивать свой болт по арене, а ты не успел, не смог отойти или увернуться, то отправляйся на чекпоинт, потому что игра не отдаст тебе управление, пока персонаж не встанет, а косплеить Александра Пистолетова Немезис будет долго...

[hr][/hr]

I think *Resident Evil 3 Remake* is a good game overall, even though it has some clear flaws. One of its biggest strengths is how it plays. The short length actually works in its favor in some ways, especially when combined with the difficulty modes. On higher settings like Inferno, Jill’s dodge mechanics become extremely important, and mastering them feels both challenging and rewarding. Taking down Nemesis after countless retries is incredibly satisfying, and this aspect helps the game stand out as a very different kind of Resident Evil experience.

That said, as a fan of the original *Resident Evil 3*, I do have some issues. Jill’s character feels quite different here. In the original, she came across as more caring and protective, which made her stand out. In the remake, she feels more aggressive and constantly uses harsh language, which makes her blend in with more generic action-oriented characters. Because of that, she’s personally less likable to me.

The map design is another downside. The environments feel too closed and compact, with very limited exploration. This takes away from the sense of freedom and tension that the original game handled much better.

Nemesis is also a bit of a disappointment in terms of buildup. Unlike the original game, where his presence felt more gradual and threatening, here he appears in a more scripted way, which reduces his impact.

I also feel like Jill’s default character design is a bit off—this is more of a personal preference, but it didn’t fully match how I imagined her.

Overall, despite these issues, *Resident Evil 3 Remake* is still a solid game. It offers a fun, challenging experience, especially for players who enjoy mastering mechanics and pushing through higher difficulties.

There are a lot of negative reviews for this game, and I started playing it with those in mind. However, I didn’t want to just take people's word for it and decided to check it out myself. I should clarify right away that I bought the game at a 90% discount.
After finishing the second Resident Evil, I was really impressed; I loved it and decided to keep exploring the franchise. In the second part, I enjoyed the moderate difficulty, interesting puzzles, and the heavy atmosphere. All of that is completely missing in the third part, which really disappointed me. The survival elements are gone too: playing on the highest difficulty, I never once ran out of ammo, and fighting the boss in his different forms wasn't challenging at all. Speaking of the main villain — he’s not scary at all, he’s badly scripted, and just looks ridiculous.
For some reason, they turned the third part into an epic action movie with non-stop fighting. Out of the whole game, I liked the hospital location the most, and that’s only because it felt similar to what I saw in part two.
What I disliked the most was how much they simplified and "casualized" everything. I already mentioned that the puzzles were removed, but the game also leads you by the hand like a child. There are constant hints on where to go and what to do; you don't have to use your brain at all. Plus, halfway through the game, I found out there’s a parry mechanic, and that’s when it just turned into a circus. You can simply dodge a crowd of zombies and run past them, and when playing as Carlos, you can just punch monsters and they fly back. I also want to mention that the game is extremely linear and gives you no room for exploration.
On the bright side, I liked the visuals. The game looks great, and the graphics are nice. The story is just okay — it’s simple, but that doesn't make it bad.
In the end, I’m not saying the game is terrible. I’d rate it as just an average game that an inexperienced gamer would probably enjoy, but it’s definitely not worth the full price. This game feels more like a DLC compared to the second part.

My final score: 4.5/10

[h3] Resident Evil 3 [/h3]

This game is complicated for me. I personally had a great time replaying it. I replayed it in a single day, taking roughly 6-7 hours. Yes, it's short. Yes, they cut lots of content. And yet, I still had a great time. I had a lot of fun playing as my second favourite RE character Jill Valentine, whom is criminally underused by Capcom btw. I had fun with the instant action segments and setpieces, I had fun exploring the smaller open areas and moving on to the next. I enjoyed the contrast between this one and the immense Police Department we got to experience in RE2. 

I do have my problems with this one however. This game feels more like a 2.5- a DLC, even. It reuses textures from RE2 in the most blatant way and it's not even trying to hide it. I'm pretty sure I've seen the same zombie over a million times while replaying RE2/3. The 'main villain', if you can even call him that is super generic and boring. Yet another evil russian military guy, how interesting! To me, Nicholai is not even the main villain of the game. It's obviously Nemesis. That aside, I thought the Carlos segment was also a tiny bit too long and I missed playing Jill all the time.

If you can look past this games extremely short length, reuse of textures from RE2 you will have a great time. This game also pretty much introduced the gimmick mechanics for all the main characters, which I absolutely love and pray they keep for all future entires. Jill can dodge, which I know some people didn't like or thought was simply too broken to be in a game like this, but I LOVED it. Jill is a character with whom it makes sense to have her move like that... I hope when they finally use her again (REX, please...) they give us the dodging mechanic for her again. Seeing how they gave Leon his knife parry back for RE9, I am hopeful they give us something like that for Jill.


All in all, I had a great time even when it was really short. I will be playing RE3 OG for the first time soon, seeing how they shadowdropped these games a few days back. Capcom, bring back my wife Jill Valentine. PLEASE.

Gameplay wise it is classic RE survival horror with all that entails, and does its job well enough on all fronts.
Is it great? No. Is it as terrible as some people claim it to be? Maybe, but only in comparison to its original predecessor and remake siblings 2 and 4. There's still potential fun to be had with it, which is why I sway towards recommeding it rather than not. Play it, form your own opinion.

IT DESSERVES THE TIME

The remake of Resident Evil 3 is a visually stunning experience with smooth, responsive gameplay. Movement and combat feel fluid, and the controls are easy to pick up, making it very accessible even for newer players.

That said, if you grew up playing the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis, you will definitely notice some major differences. A number of iconic locations, segments, and mechanics from the classic version were either removed or significantly altered. Areas like the clock tower and certain branching paths are no longer present in the same way, which can make the remake feel more linear and, at times, shorter than expected.

One thing that personally stood out to me was the sprint system. It does not really feel like a true sprint, more like a slightly faster jog. I wish there was an option to actually run faster or at least toggle a more intense sprint, especially in high pressure moments. Compared to Resident Evil 6, where movement felt more dynamic and you had better control over running, the movement here feels a bit limited.

It would also have been really cool to have more camera options. An optional first person perspective could make the experience feel more immersive, similar to Resident Evil 7: Biohazard and Resident Evil Village, and even newer entries like Resident Evil Requiem are starting to include this feature. It would also be cool to have a fixed camera angle option similar to the classic Resident Evil games, which could add a nostalgic feel and a different kind of tension.

On the technical side, the game runs very well. I personally did not encounter many bugs, and the overall performance is smooth. Character models, lighting, and environmental details are top tier, especially thanks to the RE Engine. The game also has strong replay value if you are aiming for 100 percent completion, unlocking higher difficulties, infinite weapons, and bonus content.

However, one thing to note is the game’s length. On Assisted or Standard difficulty, experienced players can finish it in around 2 to 4 hours, which is noticeably shorter compared to other entries in the series. While this does not necessarily ruin the experience, it might leave some players wanting more, especially fans of the original.

Overall, I would give Resident Evil 3 Remake a solid 9 out of 10 Nemesis. It is a polished and fun remake with excellent visuals and gameplay, but the removed content and changes from the original make it feel like a different experience rather than a faithful recreation.

I know it’s generally seen as the weakest of the modern remakes, and even though I never played the original, it’s hard to ignore how often people say key parts of that experience were cut. From what I’ve seen and heard, it seems like something important got lost in translation, even if I can’t directly compare it myself.

That said, taken on its own, it’s still a fun ride! The residents are still evil, and Jill Valentine is a solid lead, even if she hasn’t quite hit the same level for me as Leon so far. For context, this is my third RE game, after RE4 and RE2 remakes, so I’m still relatively new to the series.

Gameplay-wise, there’s not a ton to break down since it closely follows that of RE2’s formula, just with a bit more speed and a few new additions. Gunplay still feels good, impactful without making you feel overpowered, and the added weapons are a nice touch. The boss encounters with Nemesis are a highlight. They can be a little frustrating at times, and I definitely had a few moments where things weren’t clicking, but it never felt overwhelming, just a matter of locking in and pushing through. Dodge, dodge, and dodge. 

Where the game stands out less is in its level design. Compared to RE2, the environments feel noticeably smaller and more linear, which seems intentional to keep things moving. It’s not a bad direction, but I did miss the layered, puzzle-box design of the R.P.D. and the satisfaction that came with exploring it.

Overall, it may not reach the same highs as the other remakes, but there’s still a lot to enjoy here!

Overall: 7.5 Residents / 10 Evils.

ABSTRACT:

Although extremely short, Resident Evil 3 Remake is a great video game, with satisfying gameplay and an entertaining story.

GAMEPLAY:

This third entry follows the same gameplay cycle as the previous remake, meaning you, the player, have to solve puzzles, get ammo and weapons, and need to fight your way through. 

There is little innovation between titles (RE2 & RE3), but there are improvements, as seen in players' defensive capabilities. As Jill, you are able to sidestep and perfect dodge, meaning you can evade damage, and as Carlos, you can also sidestep, but instead of dodging, you parry.

The gunplay feels as good as in the previous title, with both characters having distinct loadouts, and although the game is shorter, you will still need to manage ammo, so beware.

STORY:

In RE3 you play both as Jill Valentine, a badass super-cop, and as Carlos, a mercenary. 

Different from RE2, these stories generally take place in the same locations and at the same time for the two characters, as these develop a bond of trust and mutual respect throughout the experience.

Sadly, from what I understood, the story was heavily shrunk down, so maybe give the original a try if you are looking to immerse yourself more in the RE franchise. (GOG normally has good deals.)

CONCLUSION:

Being my second Resident Evil, I was extremely pleased; the story was short, but it was also very interesting. The game felt responsive, and it had some very tense moments that will not make me forget the experience. 

I recommend Resident Evil 3: Remake, but only if you get it on discount; otherwise it's overpriced for the amount of hours you get.

The game cuts most content from the original, such as most of downtown, the restaurant fight, and the story was changed. Most importantly, the Dead Factory section of the game has been completely removed.

One other complaint I have about the game is the fact that they made Nemesis, one of gaming’s most beloved and feared antagonists, a pushover. In this game, he is basically an afterthought who shows up at certain times while you are running or fighting a zombie and makes you go, “Oh great, him again…” While in the original, he would go out of his way to make sure your playthrough was unique just with his presence, because they gave you choices that led to different outcomes.

Don’t get me wrong, I love this game and how it continued the trend of Resident Evil 2 and modernized the franchise, but with it being 40 euros MSRP, I just cannot justify it compared to Resident Evil 2. I got it for 4 euros, a price I can actually justify.

As for my ranking, I will give this game a [b]6.5/10[/b]. I really thought hard about this, and I just can’t give this game a higher rank because it would be an insult to the other games that have a 6.5 and above. It is very clear this game was rushed, and it also appears to have been worked on alongside the Resident Evil 2 remake, meaning the team was short-staffed when working on this one.

The soul and the potential are there; they just were not given the time or resources to fully realize it.

In the end, the Resident Evil 3 Remake feels like a game that had all the right ingredients but didn’t quite come together the way it should have. You can clearly see the strong foundation built from the success of the Resident Evil 2 remake. The visuals are excellent, the controls are smooth, and the modernized gameplay works really well. But where RE2 felt complete and carefully crafted, this one feels trimmed down and, at times, almost rushed.

The scariest part about this game is how mediocre it is. So this was the last of the RE Engine, Resident Evil games for me to play as I have wanted to play it for a while, but was never going to buy it with how short it is and the fact that they cut out so much content from the original. I played it on gamepass a couple of years ago and since it was recently very cheap on the spring sale, I thought I'd get it for my RE Collection. So what did I think of it? 

As you can probably tell from the score and my first written line, I didn't enjoy this at all. I put off playing this game for so long, even playing the RE4 Remake before playing this because it just seemed like a glorified DLC or stand alone expansion being sold to us at full price which just put me off from playing it, and I was right! or at least imo. Now to clarify, I never personally played the original game but I did watch my parents play it as a kid and and while I don't remember much of it, I do remember Nemesis and how he was just this unstoppable force of nature, with his iconic "STARSSSSSSSSSS" line. It is on GOG though, so I do play on playing the original at some point. 

Graphically and gameplay wise, this looks and plays almost exactly like RE2 remake pretty much to a fault. The original game from what I have researched was designed to be a spin off from the original RE2 and they did that again here, even down to you revisiting some of the same locations from the RE2 remake. It makes sense from a story perspective as much of this game takes place before RE2, but from a level design perspective it's really damn lazy because they don’t do anything to change up the location to make exploring it feel new really. 

Gameplay wise, it's basically RE2's combat but with a dodge move (that is cool when you pull it off) and some more punchy weapons like an assault rifle. It plays fine for the most part but it just feels like this remake is borrowing too much from the other, better game. The combat has much more of an action focus and it's fine at doing that, but I feel like they needed to do more to make it feel good to play. RE2's combat was slower and more methodical because it was a more classic survival horror game, and not really meant for an action orientated title. If you think of something like the OG RE4 or Dead Space 2, those games do a good job of being action oriented and making the player feel powerful. Here it just feels clunky as all hell for that style of game. The enemy types are also just very limited (and recycled from RE2R) with their only being basic zombies, gammas, hunters and then Nemesis. Action games need more enemies than this. It just felt like I was going through the motions and focusing on taking out enemies quickly rather than using the full combat kit. 

The horror is basically non-existent with what little there is with Nemesis, but he lost his luster pretty much almost immediately. You know what would have been scary? If Nemesis was an actual stalker enemy like Mr. X in RE2R and not limited to just scripted events. Even going outside of the Resident Evil franchise, when I played a game like Alien Isolation, the tension that I felt whenever the xenomorph was nearby as I hid in lockers or under tables was iconic. That would have been great here since Nemesis is such an iconic horror game villain, but here he’s just an annoying monster who just never dies and keeps coming back constantly. 

The story was okay but I honestly stopped caring after a while. Jill Valentine is a cool and iconic video game protag, but the characters around her are just bland in this game and the story is just the usual Resident Evil story, without any real surprises or tension filled moments. I know the series often has cheesy, B-movie plots for their games, but here it just felt like the boring kind and not the it’s so bad, it's good kind. 

This is just the type of game that makes me cynical about the AAA game landscape, until I play a good one or a creative, passion project indie game that makes me feel better. RE3R is just a huge disappointment. But ya maybe when it's cheap it on sale but otherwise not worth it.

TL;DR
My review is negative if we consider the full price as the standard.
But if you can get it for around £3/€3, it’s worth it.

------------------------------------------------------

I’ll start by saying I paid £3 for this game, and honestly, that’s about what it’s worth. At full price, this would have been a hard sell.

This could have easily been a DLC for Resident Evil 2 rather than a standalone title. A huge portion of the original game has been stripped away — entire sections of the story are missing. The Clock Tower is gone, and overall the experience feels heavily trimmed down.

One of the biggest issues is Nemesis. His AI has been completely changed: instead of being a dynamic, unpredictable threat, he’s now heavily scripted. Half the time he attacks, it just triggers a cutscene, which kills the tension. He feels more like a recurring boss than an actual predator. Even when you lose him, the game practically tells you it’s safe — Jill literally sighs in relief, removing any sense of danger.

Ironically, the main source of tension comes from the lack of ammunition rather than the enemies themselves.

The level design also feels outdated in places. The hospital section is especially bad — corridors are blocked by things like wheeled carts and wheelchairs, yet the game treats them as solid, immovable barriers. It’s honestly ridiculous; replacing them with debris would have made much more sense.

Then there’s the length: around 4 hours is just too short, especially when parts of the game reuse locations from previous titles, like the police station. It feels padded and yet still incomplete.

The challenges don’t help replayability either. I got around 350 kills in a normal playthrough, clearing every enemy I encountered, but the game expects you to grind up to 2,000 kills and more with different weapons. That means multiple full replays with little real reward. I’ll probably play it once more on a higher difficulty, but that’s it — I have no motivation to go for 100%.

Resident Evil 3's remake is [i]not[/i] a bad game, but it feels more like a Resident Evil themed game than a Resident Evil game. Exploration is virtually non-existent in this highly linear title as you Dark Souls dodge roll or Shoulder Charge + Haymaker your way through the game. Every once in a while, a disfigured and highly aggressive delivery man pops up so you can hit him with a grenade and collect your UberEats weapon upgrade or ammunition. Said delivery man, Steve Nemesis, has no buildup or pacing to make him feel threatening, as all of Steve's encounters are scripted and tend to be back-to-back. There's no point in planning out your routes and killing enemies the majority of the time, as you'll often never return through a location, or the game will simply spawn in new enemies to replace the ones you killed.

Unlike Resident Evil 2, which comes with a variety of unlocks, challenges, and bonus game modes, Resident Evil 3 only has the Shop, which is designed to help facilitate an even more breakneck pace through an already short game. 

The game looks pretty good even at standard HD resolution, and runs well, which is great. I do think it's worth playing through at least once if you snag it on a sale, but you can't go into this hoping for more of what RE2 and REmake offered without facing some disappointment. But if you want to beat a Hunter half to death while shooting it full of bullets, it can be a fun ride. I just can't recommend it as a Resident Evil game specifically. BUT after a few playthroughs, I think it stands on its own merits, as long as you don't go expecting actual survival horror from it,

I think the saddest part about this game, is that the most likeable part of it is playing as Carlos and his character as a whole. And that really says something. All the other side characters are meaningless. They are all super flat and you do not get engaged to them at all as the player. And Jill has to be one of the worst main protagonists I've seen. Her "cheesy" one-liners don't work the same as Leon's and that is really apparent. She is such a shallow and poorly written character.
People call this game a bad remake and while I haven't played the original game, I would argue that this is just a bad game in general and not just a bad remake. And yeah I've heard the common issues: most of the content has been cut, Nemesis is completely different and so on..
Nemesis just doesn't work the way he is implemented here. I can barely recall him chasing me and he is supposed to be a "stalker" type enemy. All of his encounters are scripted and all of his fights are just glorified "shoot him till he's dead". Not really fun or engaging. The final encounter with him is poorly designed and on Inferno difficulty, it's just blatantly unfair. If you aren't great at the dodging or haven't practiced it, then all I can say is good luck. There is one attack that will stun-lock you, until you die with nothing you can do about it. Blatantly unfair and boring design choice.
The map design of this game is so horrible. Very small and limited map area. Especially the first area. Seemingly reused assets for the unnecessary 10 minutes in the sewers and the stroll through RPD as Carlos. Only decent areas were the hospital and lab, but they are both towards the end of the game. The lab is super linear as well.
One good thing is the small "backstory" element on how Marvin got infected in RE2. That's it really.
The zombies in this game also just feel more like a nuisance, than a genuine enemy. And they are not scary at all.

All in all, RE3 remake is a super disappointing remake of the original game and a subjectively bad action horror game. The horror is not there and the action is okay at best.

While I am particularly well-informed when it comes to how this fails at living up to the standard of the original iteration, I did have the advantage of experiencing this first hand without having properly played the classic. I only know a ton about Resident Evil 3's first outing due to my unhealthy obsession with watching video essays and reading articles and threads on games that I have yet to play. So, I can confidently state that this is still a solid game nonetheless, all things considered, so as long as you take it as it is, a flawed reimagining that lacks in a lot of the meat that was there in what came before.

And it does help that I am the type that enjoys the traditional third person perspective quite a lot, especially when it comes to action/survival horror games. The gameplay loop is satisfying, from the exploration, resource management, and up to the combat itself. I dig the dodge and perfect dodge system quite a lot, especially whenever my counter attack results in a critical head pop. I can easily recommend this just with the caveats I had already spoken of. Since it is a short game, it is also easier to replay. So, you can take that aspect as a positive if you're like me that appreciates brief experiences, mainly since a lot of these games don't have proper chapter/mission select options.
