Technically good, but it feels rushed in a way that RE2 never did. Keep in mind, I didn’t play the original RE3, so I don’t know what was and wasn’t cut from this game. However, it feels significant. 

The short runtime compared to RE2 creates a constant feeling of “sprinting to the end”, and that vibe is basically the whole problem. It never stops feeling like you’re aggressively being pushed forward. My issue with this is that Raccoon City is genuinely beautiful to look at, and I wanted more time there. Instead, you’re quickly hurried through it. It would’ve been a great chance to open the game in a way and naturally expand on RE2’s level design. Instead, a lot of the environments end up feeling inferior to almost anything in that game, with a couple areas that do come close.

Mechanically, the dodge system is the main win. Perfect dodges feel great. Outside of perfects it can feel, and look, clunky. The fact that your character will not shoot while manually running is another odd addition. Everything else is pretty well copied over from RE2 remake but with a lot more action involved. 
Story-wise, Jill and the remaining STARS members tied to the mansion incident are being targeted by NEMESIS, a tyrant with a G-embryo infused into his brain. The game’s focus is more on the T-Virus and continued research at an Umbrella facility — it explains how the outbreak spreads and the city falls — but it does surprisingly little with NEMESIS himself, even though he’s the point. The NEMESIS encounters are pretty goofy, and he has multiple clean attempts to kill Jill and just… doesn’t.

I’ve heard a lot of criticism about Jill being too aggressive and poorly written, but I think she feels down to earth and realistic while still developing off herself from the events of RE1. I think the short runtime hurts her the most. We rarely see her sit down and reflect, and the idea of survivor guilt gets introduced to her but it never really gets paid off.
Carlos is fun and doesn’t feel overshadowed by Jill. Caring, flirtatious, and good comic relief with dialogue that feels natural. I was worried he’d get corny, but I just ended up liking him more as the game went on. If he was this great in the original, I'm shocked he's never shown up in the series again. 

Bottom line: solid game that needed more development time. I don’t agree the developers of this should never do another RE remake. What they were able to create is well done, but they needed a more complete vision and way more time. Recommending this in 2026, as it’s usually super cheap. At standard price it feels incomplete.

Resident Evil 3 is a thrilling, fast-paced survival horror experience that delivers intense action while staying true to the spirit of the series. From the moment the game begins, it throws you right into the chaos of a collapsing Raccoon City, and it rarely lets up.

One of the biggest highlights is playing as Jill Valentine, who is portrayed as strong, resourceful, and determined throughout the story. Her interactions with Carlos Oliveira add a lot of personality to the narrative and help keep the pacing exciting as the outbreak spirals out of control.

The game’s presentation is excellent. The environments are incredibly detailed, the lighting and effects look fantastic, and the sound design really pulls you into the tension of surviving a city that’s completely falling apart. Combat feels smooth and responsive, and the dodge mechanic adds an extra layer of skill and excitement during intense encounters.

Of course, the real star of the game is Nemesis. His relentless pursuit creates constant pressure and some truly memorable moments. Every time he shows up, it instantly raises the stakes and keeps you on edge.

While the game is more action-focused than some other entries in the series, it still delivers plenty of suspense, great set pieces, and cinematic moments that make the experience feel like a blockbuster horror movie you get to play.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 is a highly polished and exciting addition to the series. It’s a fun ride from start to finish with memorable characters, intense encounters, and impressive visuals that make it well worth playing for any survival horror fan. 🧟‍♂️🎮

**Resident Evil 3**… a fast-paced survival horror experience filled with tension and constant danger. The story follows **Jill Valentine**, one of the last surviving members of S.T.A.R.S., as she tries to escape the collapsing **Raccoon City** during the outbreak.

From the beginning, the game throws you straight into chaos as Jill is relentlessly hunted by the terrifying **Nemesis**, a bio-weapon created by **Umbrella Corporation**. The detailed environments, modern visuals, and cinematic action sequences create an intense and thrilling experience as you fight to survive and uncover more about Umbrella’s experiments.

However, despite its strong presentation, the game does have some noticeable downsides. The overall length is quite short compared to other entries in the series, and several locations and moments from the original game were removed or simplified. Nemesis, while visually intimidating, is more scripted than many fans expected, which reduces the sense of unpredictability. Some players also felt that the focus on action slightly weakens the classic survival horror atmosphere.

Even with these flaws, the game still delivers a fun and intense ride with memorable moments and strong characters. A solid remake that shines in action and presentation, but feels a bit too short for its potential. **7.5–8/10** 🎮🧟‍♂️🔥

I went into Resident Evil 3 Remake with pretty high expectations after playing the other remakes, and I came away with pretty mixed feelings.

The biggest thing that stood out to me is how short it is. If you’re mainly focused on the main story, you can finish the whole game in around five hours. That by itself wouldn’t necessarily be a problem, but a lot of content from the original game feels watered down or removed, which makes the experience feel even shorter. Because of that, this ended up being my least favorite remake in the series.

That said, it’s not all bad.

Jill looks incredible in this remake. The character model and overall presentation are great, and the updated graphics definitely make the game feel modern. Some areas still look really good and the production quality is clearly there.

But there are a few things that really held it back for me. Nemesis, who should feel like a constant threat, ends up feeling very scripted compared to the original game. Most of his appearances are tied to specific moments rather than dynamically hunting you, which removes a lot of the tension. Enemy variety also feels reduced, so you end up fighting the same types of enemies more often.

Another thing that surprised me is that even though the graphics are newer, I still feel like Resident Evil 2 Remake and Resident Evil 4 Remake somehow looked better overall. Those games just had a stronger visual atmosphere and level design.

Mechanically, this one also feels like the weakest of the recent remakes. It’s still playable and fun in short bursts, but it doesn’t feel as polished or satisfying as the others.

Overall, I’d say it’s worth playing if you can grab it on a steep sale. If you’re a big Resident Evil fan, it’s still interesting to experience. But if you’re expecting something on the same level as RE2 or RE4 Remake, this one might end up feeling a bit disappointing

It took me only 7 hours to beat the story. It’s a good horror game, but honestly, it’s not as good as RE2 Remake or RE4. It feels more like a fast action movie than a scary survival game.

Gameplay: Fast and Straight to the Point

The biggest thing about this game is that it is straight to the point. There is no wasting time you just run, shoot, and survive.

The Good and The Bad: Being straight to the point is a double-edged sword. It’s great if you want a fast game, but it’s bad because we needed more details, more depth, and a longer story. Everything feels a bit too simple.

The Dodge: You can quickly move away from zombies. If you time it perfectly, you feel like a pro! It makes the combat feel fast and exciting.

Boss Fights: The fights against Nemesis are epic. He is a beast! These moments are the best part of the game.

No Puzzles: There are almost no puzzles. If you like using your brain, you will be disappointed. It’s mostly just run and gun.

Character and Weapons

You play as Jill Valentine, and sometimes you play as Carlos.

Carlos Segments: His parts are way too short! I wanted to play as him more, but the game finishes his story too fast.

No Upgrades: You can’t really customize your weapons like in other games. The weapon list is small, and there isn't much strategy.

Visuals and Performance (The Frustrating Part)

I’m a bit disappointed here. Even on high settings, the graphics look pixelated and blurry sometimes.

Graphics: The zombies far away look muddy. I spent an hour just trying to fix the settings to make it look okay. It’s not as polished as RE2 Remake.

Value for Money: Wait for a Sale!
Don't buy this game at full price. It’s way too short for $60.
Pro Tip: Wait until it’s on sale for around $10. For that price, it’s a great weekend experience!

Pros (The Good Stuff)
* The Dodge Mechanic: Moving and dodging zombies feels amazing.
* Epic Bosses: Fighting Nemesis is top tier action.
* No Wasting Time: The game is fast and straight to the point.
* Cheaper on Sale: It is a must-buy if the price is low.

Cons (The Not-So-Good Stuff)
* Too Short: 7 hours is not enough. We needed more depth and a longer campaign.
* No Puzzles: It feels too simple compared to other RE games.
* Graphics Issues: Some textures look bad and pixelated.
* No Weapon Customization: You can’t build your dream gun.

Final Rating: 7/10

Did you enjoy RE2? Did you revel at blowing away pesky zombies? Did Mr X gives you the creeps? Perhaps you enjoy the puzzles littered around the game, and how about that plot twist? If this strikes a chord then we're of the same mind...

Sadly, I'm afraid you shouldn't expect the same from RE3. Not only are Jill and Carlos mighty annoying (and seemingly less reactive than Leon in RE2), but the boss fights (be prepared for a LOT of them) make you wonder how on Earth you were ever meant to uncover the tactics required to clear them without jumping on Google. Admittedly I played the titles back to back, so I may have noticed the changes easier than someone who picked it RE3 up from scratch, but who doesn't play run throughs on a franchise like Resi. 

I'm not sure I've ever played a more frustrating game...note the key word, frustrating, not frightening. RE2 set a sinister and chilling environment, with a survivalist feel, dragging yourself from save room to save room, not knowing what's around the corner, add to that the odd pursuit from one of the series most eerie villains (Mr X). RE3 becomes more like a shoot 'em up, this time with perhaps the series most jaw-droppingly outrageous villains, now I'm not talking genetic make up, massive gnashers or weapon upgrades but more the constant battles from start to finish, it gets really dull, really fast. Don't get me wrong, it still has the RE feel to it, but there were WAY too many moments of unbalanced gameplay throughout, within the first 5-10 minutes of gameplay when ammo is low, I opt to plug 4-5 zombies near a fence to clear a path in advance, one minute later and a cut scene strikes in which they're all back in their original places...thanks for that. 

Jill's reactions can be very lax with large enemies too, meaning her stance sometimes prevents you from aiming and firing before you get struck by something, most annoying when you're required to run and gun in many boss fights. Fast forward mid-game and I found myself facing some speedy opponents that literally appeared mid room with no clear entrance, not to mention a late-game scenario with a secure glass cell containing a sole zombie which upon returning to it suddenly contains another 4 zombies, with no method of entry apparent. All in all, I'll give it a 4 out of 10, 3 of these points are for nostalgia-sake. 

Despite the fact it's a game that includes the undead, a sinister pharma group, special unit cops, freakish monsters, Russian villains that belong in a Rocky film and an ever changing boss that hangs around like a bad fart at a funeral...it's just plain silly.

RE3R on it's own is alright. It looks amazing and runs flawlessly even on highest settings, but it definitely has some pacing issues and some questionable moments and decisions. The actual story is pretty good, however I felt like it leans too much on the cinematics, as there is a cutscene every ten seconds. The problem I have with it is that it's apparently very unfaithful to the original. Which I've never played. This is the problem I have with Remakes in general. They tend to change / replace or straight up cut out a lot for no meaningful reason. As someone who never had the opportunity to play the original RE games, the Remakes are my only saving grace, and it just leaves a void feeling, knowing that the Remake you just played contains only about forty percent of the original game. I wouldn't have an issue with it at all, if the original games were on Steam and I could simply just play them. But they ain't. Still, I feel like RE3R on it's own is not a bad game, and it's worth playing if you've never played the original.

EDIT: Okay, so they released the original games (RE1, RE2, RE3) on Steam and I already played through the original RE3. There are a some things I have to mention. The Remake feels like a completely different game, that has some eastern eggs and references to the original RE3. The title is the same, the main plot is more or less the same, but overall, these are two completely different games. The characters have the same names, but completely different personalities. Sixty percent of the original game is nowhere to be seen in the Remake. Raccoon City is huge in the original, but in the Remake it's watered down to three streets. The Remake completely removes The Bar, The Restaurant, The News Building, The Clock Tower, The Gas Station, The Park, and two underground boss areas, along with the said bosses. Although the main story is more or less the same, there are a few changes and rearrangements, which seem completely unnecessary. All of that being said, I'm going to reduce my final score for the remake from a seven to a six. It's still a decent game, but apart from the graphics and the audio quality, the Remake is a massive downgrade in every regard. However, I would still recommend playing both versions, as they are fundamentally different games and offer very different experiences.

RE3 Remake fails at both being a remake of Resident Evil 3: Nemesis but also it fails at being a fun game in its own right. It takes the RE2 Remake engine and style but decides to go full action with its gameplay. Gone is the tense exploration of RE2 and it is replaced with scripted sequences of action as Jill goes full Ripley against the weirdly-no-longer-titular Nemesis. The action scenes are exciting, I'll give the game that. The problem is when you actually play the game. This is ultimately the same system as RE2 Remake. It's not fast. Enemies are easier to kill but still spongey, with even basic zombies taking 5 headshots to kill. An endless knife makes it easier to save ammo but also slows the game down dramatically since you have to take the time to stab every zombie on the ground to make sure it's actually dead and not just faking it. A new dodge mechanic makes bosses far more viable but zombies have also increased their reach drastically so it's never as effective as it feels like it should be. 

Basically, the exploration is almost entirely gone, replaced by action that never feels as good as the original RE4, let alone RE4 Remake. Bosses often require stupidly specific actions in order to win, puzzles are sometimes nonsensical and really only result in more ammo to keep up with the too-slow-to-be-fun shooting.

This is for folks who simply must play every Resident Evil game in the franchise. For everyone else, play literally any of the other entries instead. The story has no real bearing on any of the other games so it's easily skippable. RE2 Remake, RE4 Remake, RE7, RE8, RE9 are all fantastic games. You can even get the HD versions of RE1, RE0 or Revelations 1 and 2. And if you'd prefer a more action approach for some reason, RE5 and 6 are here too. I've had a better time with all of them (maybe not 6...) than I had with 3 Remake. This is a big no from me.

Also, Carlos sucks. Worst protagonist in all of Resident Evil. Of all the things to remain true to in this remake, why did it have to be his casual sexism? Was that supposed to be endearing? It wasn't in 1999 and it still isn't now.

As a bystander and a fan of more action-oriented Resident Evil games, I don’t really understand what all the fuss is about. It’s one thing to call out the game for it being made in a haste, resulting in a buggy, unplayable mess, and it’s another thing to call out a decent game for not answering one’s expectations.

I played this remake for the first time and… I enjoyed it.
I heard people saying that the game is way too short (something like “It lasts 3 hours and that’s it!”), that it was rushed, and so on.

Gameplay-wise, it feels like a great stepping stone between Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 4. We can’t quite mow down the zombies as we do in RE4, but it isn’t really all about running away as it was in Resident Evil 2. Especially the middle part of the story—it's basically a nose-peek in the Resident Evil 4 gameplay.
You can actually kill most of the enemies in the game, and you’ll end up having a lot of unused ammo in the end. Well, that’s how I personally played it: RE2 was way harder for me in that sense.

Story-wise, it’s also decent. It doesn’t convey the entirety of RE lore, sure, but it’s a good game in terms of story to entertain one for a couple of evenings. That is, if you play it carefully and if you are paying attention. If you rush the game, it’ll end up being finished in one sitting.
The characters, weirdly enough, felt more alive to me than they did in RE2. But that’s a whole different tale to tell.

The ending [spoiler] twist that the vaccine got destroyed just for the sake of upcoming established lore to happen is an underwhelming move, but what can you do about it, right? [/spoiler]

Overall, the game does indeed feel like a massive DLC to Resident Evil 2: the exact same game engine, the exact same graphics, sometimes even the exact same animations, but gameplay- and story-wise, it is still a very solid title. Compare this case to GTA 3 and GTA: Vice City, the latter being developed in 1 year in a very hasty manner, feeling unfinished and more as a DLC to the former, but it is still considered a timeless classic. The same applies here: it’s just an average game that was developed in under a year. It is not supposed to be something bigger than it should be, as I said before—this is merely a stepping stone.

Certainly, the original version of the game felt way more fleshed out; it had more lore and more cutscenes, the remake retconned some things here and there, but the final product really isn’t as bad as people discuss it to be. It is also worth remembering that developing games was a way easier task in some ways than it is nowadays, and the real question is why Capcom rushed RE3 Remake that much, when it could've gotten the attention it really deserved. In the end, though, I think there is only one completely unconditional reason to hate this game—and it is the price. $60 for such a game is WAY too much to pay on its release date. Also, no DLCs, and instead we have to pay for the content that should have been unlocked for us after completing the game.

But nowadays, considering all things? It's alright, nothing more, nothing less. Especially on sale.
It certainly lacks some other game modes as an example, but the game’s being this short was actually a good thing for me: growing tired of longer games that require you playing for more than 50 hours to 100% complete them—the more or less relaxing experience that RE3 has provided for me was a breath of fresh air, which motivated me to come back to gaming overall.

While I have yet to complete the game, I'm writing this review becasue I don't think I want to play any further. Allow me to explain.

I'll start off with the good: Seeing more of Racoon City is nice. The events of the game take place before, during, and after the events of RE2 so you will come across locations - and maybe a character or two - from the previous game as you traverse through the zombie infested streets.

Jill is still a top notch character. Battle hardened after the events of the mansion, REmake 3 gives a new breath of life into the character along with a nice redesign that feels different yet familiar.

The Nemesis is a mixed bag for the game. Unlike Mr. X - who is continuously on the hunt for Leon/Claire throughout the majority of REmake 2 - the Nemesis encounters are scripted chase scenes. And while they can be intense sequences, the downside is Nemesis doesn't have as big of a presence as MR. X did as a result.

His redesign is cool, though.

Now the bad:

The game is too linear. Unlike the previous game where the map was essentially a series of small mazes that gradually open up into one big maze as you progress, REmake 3's maps are very small. So much so that you can get through them in less than 15-20 minutes, and they're no longer connected to each other either.

There are also sudden, random, spikes in difficulty in certain sections.

In your first Nemesis encounter you will find yourself reloading saves so many times just to try and find your way around the flat faced ♥♥♥♥♥♥. And not in the fun "Ah it got me this time, but I'll get passed it in the next round!" type of thing. I'm talking "Oh, you are just piling on obstacle after obstacle in front of me while trying to have me evade your scripted monster that runs like Usain Bolt..." type of difficulty spike.

There is an evade system but good luck getting the timing right as, unless you're beyond an arms length away from the enemy, the window of success is about the size of a squirrel's scrotum. And if you do get cought by a zombie there is a very poorly implemented QTE that is supposed to let you shake off the zombies, but you STILL take damage if you succeed it's just less (and in a later stage of the game that little detail will bite you in the arse a lot).

They should've just kept the secondary weapon mechanic where you use whatever knife or explosive you have in your inventory at the time to shake them off, thereby avoiding damage while also damaging the enemy instead.

SPOILERS AHEAD

This brings me to the main reason why I'm most likely done with this game due to the difficulty spike. The random appearance of a Horde Mode in the final Carlos section of the game.

Everything I brought up about the random difficulty spike culminates in this section. You have to spend an indeterminant amount of time defending a barracaded door in the reception area of a hospital room from an endless horde of zombies, mutated zombies, and hunters (those big, fast, bullet spongey green things from RE 1). It is so out of place in an RE game and overstays its welcome after the first few minutes.

And your tools of defence are the handful of ammo and gear the devs decided to provide you for this section, a dodge mechanic that barely works, and a QTE that may as well not be in the game as it does bollock all.

It is clearly there to pad out the run-time of the game and adds nothing else beyond that. If there's a mod out there that cuts this section out entirely, install that before playing this and save yourself a headache.

It's a shame, too, because if it weren't for the random difficulty spikes and the poorly done dodge and QTEs, the game can have a lot of fun moments. The Nemesis boss fights are pretty fun and intense. The shooting mechanics feel way better in this than they do in REmake 2, the game LOOKS amazing graphically and the voice acting is solid all around.

If you still want to check it out despite the drawbacks I just mentioned, then wait for the game to be on sale like I did.

Who knows. Maybe I will come back to the game and beat it at some point - at which time I wil edit this review to reflect more complete thoughts - but until then I think I'm done with REmake 3.

Survival Through Chaos – Огляд Resident Evil 3

Загальна оцінка: 9/10

Resident Evil 3 — це стрімкий жах на виживання, який замінює певну методичну напругу серії на терміновість, видовищність і постійний тиск. Дія гри розгортається в останні години розпаду Раккун-Сіті. Гра ставить гравців у чоботи Джилл Валентайн, коли вона бореться з міста, захопленого нежиттю, за яким невпинно полює одна з найвідоміших загроз франшизи. Не дивлячись на те, що Resident Evil 3 більш спрямований на дії, ніж його попередники, він забезпечує цілеспрямований кінематографічний досвід, який підкреслює імпульс, інтенсивність і виживання під час переслідування.

Візуальний дизайн і атмосфера: 10/10

Раккун-Сіті зображено як місто у вільному падінні. Палаючі вулиці, будівлі, що руйнуються, і клаустрофобічні інтер’єри створюють відчуття хаосу, яке пронизує кожну територію. Неонові вогні мерехтять у заповнених димом алеях, а вузькі коридори та зруйновані вітрини підтримують напругу. Середовища можуть бути більш лінійними, ніж попередні записи, але вони багаті деталями та візуальною оповіддю, підсилюючи відчуття, що місто вмирає в реальному часі.

Історія та персонажі: 8,5/10

Resident Evil 3 робить сильний акцент на розповіді персонажів. Джилл Валентайн зображена стійкою, рішучою та емоційно обґрунтованою, а Карлос Олівейра привносить тепло та людяність у хаос. Розповідь рухається у швидкому темпі, штовхаючи гравців вперед швидше з нагальністю, ніж таємницею. Незважаючи на те, що ця історія менш зосереджена на повільних відкриттях, вона досягає успіху в забезпеченні високих ставок виживання та емоційної ваги, посилюючи відчай від втечі з приреченого міста.

Геймплей і механіка виживання: 10/10

Геймплей більше схиляється до екшену, ніж до традиційного survival horror, але основна механіка все ще наголошує на управлінні ресурсами та розумному прийнятті рішень. Боєприпаси залишаються обмеженими, цілющі предмети дорогоцінні, а зіткнення часто змушують гравців вибирати між боєм і втечею. Додана механіка ухилення надає бою більш динамічного відчуття, виграшного часу та усвідомлення ситуації. Хоча дослідження відходить на другий план, петля виживання залишається захоплюючою та напруженою.

Звуковий дизайн і музика: 9/10

Звуковий дизайн посилює відчуття терміновості гри. Вибухи відлунюють вулицями, віддалені крики сигналізують про небезпеку, а звукові сигнали ворога тримають гравців напоготові. Саундтрек врівноважує напружені екшн-теми з моментами жаху, а знайомі музичні мотиви створюють враження від серіалу. Аудіо працює разом із ритмом, гарантуючи, що напруга ніколи не спадає.

Відтворюваність і цінність: 9/10

Resident Evil 3 є більш компактним досвідом, але він заохочує повторне відтворення через режими складності, розблоковування та майстерність його механіки. Знання поведінки ворогів і розташування предметів підвищує впевненість, але невпинний темп гри гарантує, що повторні заїзди залишаються захоплюючими, а не рутинними. Його менша довжина компенсується його інтенсивністю та фокусом.

Висновок: 9/10

Resident Evil 3 — це захоплюючий жахливий досвід виживання під високим тиском, який акцентує увагу на втечі, переслідуванні та імпульсі. Хоча він жертвує деякими повільнішими, дослідницькими елементами попередніх записів, він компенсує це сильними персонажами, незабутнім дизайном ворогів і безперервною напругою.

Остаточний вердикт:
Resident Evil 3 — це скромний, агресивний розділ у серії, який перетворює жах виживання на відчайдушний спринт за свободу. З Джилл Валентайн у його основі та Немезидою, що насувається на кожному кроці, він фіксує паніку міста на межі та доводить, що іноді виживання полягає не в дослідженні, а в тому, щоб вижити з нього.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is, in my view, one of the weaker entries in the franchise — though still enjoyable overall.

I completed all difficulties and earned all achievements, so I experienced everything the game had to offer. While I had fun with it, it doesn’t quite reach the level of most other Resident Evil titles (excluding 5 and 6, which I feel went too far into action).

The opening section is strong. It’s intense and action-packed, and it immediately sets the tone. Jill’s portrayal is excellent — she feels capable, grounded and believable. I genuinely enjoyed her character in this remake.

Nemesis is the standout element. On a first playthrough especially, he is fast, aggressive and brutal. He adds urgency and real pressure. In some encounters, he feels even more threatening than Mr. X from RE2 due to how relentless he can be.

That said, there are moments that feel slightly odd. Nemesis is powerful enough to blast through walls and doors in certain scenes, yet in others he doesn’t — even when it would make sense. It’s not a major issue, but it does slightly break immersion.

The hospital section wasn’t my favourite area, though I did enjoy playing as Carlos. His segments added variety.

One thing that stands out compared to other entries is the lack of additional single-player content. Resident Evil 2 Remake had The Ghost Survivors. RE4 and RE8 have Mercenaries. RE7 had substantial DLC like Nightmare and Bedroom. Resident Evil 3, however, lacks a meaningful bonus mode to extend replay value. While it launched with Resident Evil Resistance, that online mode didn’t replace a proper single-player extra. That feels like a missed opportunity — especially considering the potential to expand on Jill and Carlos further.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 Remake is polished, fast-paced and enjoyable — but it feels condensed. It’s a good game, just not one of the strongest in the series.

Of all the mainline Resident Evil games to remake, RE3 was probably the one that had the most to gain from such an undertaking. 
The original is a great, if somewhat undercooked game - it featured branching story paths and some minor item randomization elements that gave it some great replayability and while it didn't add much to the formula established in RE1 and almost perfected in RE2, it had plenty of fun ideas to offer that really only needed some extra time and attention to really shine - which a remake would have been the ideal opportunity for!

But no. Instead of a modern day gem like RE2R and RE4R, we got this and the awful joke that was Resident Evil Resistance instead. 

No more branching paths or randomization at all and the majority of the original game's content has either been cut outright or reworked into small, linear "cinematic" setpieces (a blight upon gaming, far as I'm concerned) instead, resulting in a game that takes about 3-4 hours to beat on a blind playthrough. 
Also, since Capcom hadn't yet mastered the RE Engine, even the presentation suffered in that enemies can no longer be dismembered and freeze in place upon death now, damaging the already immensely toned down atmosphere even further - hell, during one segment enemy corpses even dissolve to improve performance.

As for replay value, pretty much the only thing they gave us is the legitimately untested disaster that is the unlockable Inferno difficulty - as anyone will tell you that actually managed to finish that nonsense: That difficulty mode is an absolute mess.

This game is a waste. And frankly, the fact that they tried to justify that waste by including an even more halfbaked multiplayer title that literally nobody asked for kind of makes it even worse in my mind. 
I hate it and I genuinely would recommend anyone curious about the game to just play the original PSX version instead and maybe watch a playthrough of this remake on Youtube instead - as is the case with most "cinematic" games, you won't miss anything of value.

The Resident Evil 3 Remake is a really bad adaptation and is really mid as a game as well. Everything about it is a major downgrade from the original except for Carlos, who is actually a character and not a white guy doing a bad hispanic accent. I really don't understand why they cut cool stuff like the clock tower and instead put an entire remake original section where Jill gets face ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by multiple bugs. I understand that they did not have much time to make this, and for the amount of time they had, it's definitely not [i]bad[/i], but it's also not very good. 

I was really hoping Jill and Nikolai would get some real characterization in this, but both of them barely have anything actually going on, especially Nikolai, who I think needed the most new character stuff cause he is really boring in the original. Unfortunately, he is also really boring here, which makes it worse because they tried to give him characterization but it just ended up being generic mercenary guy. I'm sad they didn't do anything with Jill's PTSD cause the intro made it seem like they would.

Nemesis really suffers in this remake because they clearly wanted to make him somewhat different from Mr. X, when what they should've done is lean more into that since Nemesis played like Mr. X in the original. Have him be a more aggressive version of that who's always around instead of just in scripted sequences. It adds so much more to his character without actually doing much. In general he feels like a way less nuanced version of the character, which for a character that doesn't have that much going on like Nemesis in the first place, is not great. He looks cool without a nose though, but the main game has a nose so that's not even good. 

Overall, while I've said a lot of negative stuff, the game is very much an extension of Resident Evil 2 Remake, giving it a pretty decent foundation for the gameplay. The game looks really good, it has some cool environments, albeit not nearly as cool as Resident Evil 2 Remake but still cool nonetheless. Once again, I really like Carlos here, he's the only character in this whole game who benefits from its existence. I still had fun in some segments and there were a lot of cool moments, but even the coolest moments in this game lack the impact because of how fast the game is moving. You don't get nearly enough time to get to know these characters and to get properly invested in their story.

Also, these characters swear way too much to the point where it takes away from the actual dialogue.

Overall, it's an okay game and a really bad adaptation that lacks so much of the nuance that its 90s counterpart had. The original isn't perfect, but it's much better than this.

Final Rating: 5/10

I recommend this game but I would be cautious and I would definitely wait for a sale. RE3R is definitely the worst out of the RE remakes. I would definitely tell you to pick 2 or 4 over 3. I never played the original so I don't hold the frustration of the people who played the original. I do know there is a lot of cut content and there seems to be a lot of recycled assets from RE2R. The game is incredibly short, definitely had more playtime in 2 and 4.

So far I have only sh** on the game so why do I recommend it? As someone who never played the original, the remake is still overall a positive experience at least to me. While a much more linear experience than 2, I still enjoyed seeing the story of Raccoon City from another perspective and while adding more depth to what happened to RC before [spoiler] the big ol nuclear warhead wiping everything out [/spoiler]. Having the game split between Jill and Carlos was an interesting choice, but with how short the game is combined with only two segments where you play as Carlos, it could have honestly been better spent on more locations to explore as Jill rather than play as Carlos.

Nemesis was a big let down compared to Mr X in RE2R. Nemesis was more of a plot device in this game than as a threat. Some segments you could down Nemesis for loot and others they make him invincible as a plot point to force you forward in the story. Mr X was by far scarier to come across in RE2R, showing up randomly when you're trying to do something and having to change your plans or waste precious resources to stun him for a bit. Nemesis showing up was always scripted, felt like just another mild threat to deal with.

Gameplay is very similar to RE2R but limb dismemberment is not present and there is a dodge ability. The dodge ability allows you to avoid attacks more easily and if you execute a perfect dodge, allows you to slow time to get critical hits easier on enemies. The lack of limb dismemberment is a step backwards forcing you to shoot at heads to do anything for normal zombie enemies. If you loved the puzzles in RE2R, prepare to be disappointed as you could hardly call these puzzles, more like fetch quests.

As of writing this, the price is on sale for $9.99 which I think is very reasonable. Do not get the game at the full price which at this moment is $39.99. With how short the game is, $40 is a rip off. Is this game great? No but I still think it's decent. Besides the spin-off games, this title is the worst RE to come out after RE7 but I do think it's still worth playing once at least.

RE 3 Remake has its ups and downs for sure, but I think it's quite the good game to help someone who is just starting to get into the resident evil franchise. Does it Cut a lot of what was in the original game? yes, yes it does. Large chunks where taken out either as a time constraint or whatever, and some parts like the hospital hold out section with Carlos feels rushed and a little lack luster, (Especially on repeated playthroughs) but overall I still think the games a great time for what it's worth and a fun REremake to boot. Does it win out in any competitions compared to the Re2 and 4 Remakes hell no. but its still a very fun time. Fun enough to warrent me going for all of the Achievements aswell.

GAMEPLAY:
Resident Evil 3 Remake plays pretty much identical to the Resident Evil 2 Remake, with the over the shoulder camera, fluid gunplay and pretty good enemy designs especially when it comes to nemesis. Granted Nemesis is only in scripted squences and only decides to chase you down when you get to those sequences before he gets to his second phase. But what is given to the player when it comes to him as an antagonist is fun, and hectic espeically if you havent cleared out every single zombie that was in the way before he decides to go after you. 

The sections that the game allows the player to run through, be it Racoon City, the sewers, The hospital or Nest 2 are fairly short but fun to run around in regardless. The little amount of puzzles that there are, are pretty good and did stump me atleast once or twice. But on repeated playthroughs especially when you know what youre doing and know where you're going, It's really easy to finish the game in Under 2 hours especially with the infinite Ammo weapons and especially with the rocket launcher.

Its same old same old RE3 it follows jill valentine and Carlos escaping Raccoon city and uncovering them making the T-virus before the City gets nuked. RU:
Если RE2 была про медленное выживание и экономию каждого патрона, то Resident Evil 3 — это чистый адреналин. И, честно говоря, мне такой подход понравился гораздо больше. Игра не дает тебе заскучать ни на минуту, постоянно подбрасывая новые эпичные ситуации.

Джилл Валентайн — настоящая икона: Забудьте про новичка Леона. Джилл — профессионал, и это чувствуется в управлении. Система идеального уклонения (Dodge) полностью меняет правила игры. Когда ты в последний момент уходишь от удара и замедляешь время для контратаки — это дает нереальный кайф.

Динамика и темп: В RE2 ты мог полчаса топтаться в одной комнате, решая загадку. В RE3 события сменяются со скоростью пули: побег от взрывов, перестрелки на улицах, битвы с боссами. Это концентрированное удовольствие без «воды».

Раккун-Сити во всей красе: Вместо пыльных коридоров участка нам наконец-то дали погулять по самому городу. Неоновые вывески, горящие переулки, атмосфера наступающего апокалипсиса — визуально это на голову выше замкнутых пространств второй части.

 Немезис — это не Тиран
Да, Немезис чаще появляется по сюжету, но зато КАЖДАЯ встреча с ним — это событие. Он быстрее, умнее (он использует щупальца и огнемет!), и битвы с ним поставлены как в лучших боевиках. Тиран в RE2 просто уныло ходил за тобой, а Немезис заставляет твою кровь закипать.

Графика и детализация
Движок выдает просто запредельную картинку. Лица персонажей, детализация оружия и то, как город медленно погружается в хаос — это эстетическое наслаждение. Игра ощущается более «дорогой» и современной.

ENG:
While RE2 was all about slow-burn survival and counting every single bullet, Resident Evil 3 is pure adrenaline. Honestly, I enjoyed this approach way more. The game never lets up, constantly throwing you into epic situations without any of the fluff.


Jill Valentine is a total icon: Forget Leon being a rookie. Jill is a seasoned pro, and you can feel it in the controls. The Perfect Dodge mechanic is a complete game-changer. Nailing that timing, dodging an attack, and slowing down time for a counter-shot is incredibly satisfying.

Dynamics and Pacing: In RE2, you could spend half an hour stuck in one room trying to solve a puzzle. In RE3, the events hit you like a freight train—explosive escapes, street-level shootouts, and massive boss fights. It is concentrated fun with zero filler.

Raccoon City in all its glory: Instead of just dusty police station hallways, we finally get to see the city itself. The neon signs, the burning alleys, and the vibe of an oncoming apocalypse—visually, this is a massive step up from the cramped spaces of the second game.

Nemesis vs. Mr. X
Sure, Nemesis shows up in more scripted moments, but every single encounter with him feels like a major event. He is faster, smarter (he literally uses tentacles and a flamethrower), and his boss fights are staged like a high-budget action movie. Mr. X in RE2 just kind of followed you around at a snail's pace, but Nemesis actually gets your blood pumping.

Graphics and Detail
The engine delivers top-tier visuals. The character models, the weapon details, and the way the city slowly descends into chaos are all a total blast to look at. The game feels more expensive and modern overall.

Resident Evil 3 is my favorite of the classic games, I love exploring Raccoon City, I loved the way the story altered slightly based on your choices, I loved the Nemesis being an ever present threat.

When REmake 3 first came out, I really, really needed it to be good. RE1 and RE2 fans got their perfect remake, now it was my turn.

So when the game first game out, I looked past a lot of it's flaws, and came away from it thinking "well, its not as good at REmake 2, but it's still pretty good!"

Fast forward 6 years, I no longer have that desperate need for the game to be good, and I replayed it as part of a "Raccoon City / Leon S Kennedy marathon" in preparation for Resident Evil: Requiem.  Boy oh boy, do I not enjoy this game now that I'm looking at it with unclouded eyes.

The game feels rushed, the amount of content cut from the original could be it's own game, there's so much. 

The pacing is ridiculous, you get one open area encounter with Nemesis, one boss fight with humanoid Nemesis, and everything else is a scripted event or is a fight with generic monster dog Nemesis. 

The gameplay in general is also just a general downgrade from REmake 2, with awful level design, frustrating new enemies, constant backtracking, and unsatisfying exploration. Also, every boss fight is poorly designed, either made way too easy by the dodge mechanic, or made frustratingly difficulty by how inconsistent the timing on the dodge mechanic is.

The dodge mechanic in general just isn't implemented well, the timing on when you're supposed to dodge vs when the enemy is winding up an attack is always different, even the same attack from the same enemy feels like it has different timings sometimes, most notably the tentacle attacks from the ne-alpha parasite zombies.

There's only good thing I can say about this game:

Raccoon City looks beautiful, and the character designs are all great, whoever was part of the visual side of the dev team did their job perfectly.

Otherwise, do not recommend at all.

A solid game, but lacking compared to its brothers. RE2R was a near perfect remake of the original RE2, a near perfect survival horror game, not removing much in terms of gameplay from the original, only removing a few character moments that ultimately didn't affect the game's story all too much. RE4R was even better, adding new mechanics to the game such as parrying, improving on the original game's pacing, basically just making the game better in every conceivable way. Honestly with how good the remake is, sometimes it's hard going back to that original. RE3R, however, cuts a significant amount of content from the game, with its replacements being... subpar, to say the least. The clock tower and park were both omitted, the new "Nightmare" and "Inferno" difficulties, primarily inferno, feel super unbalanced, and designed with the new shop items in mind. Oh yeah, the shop. RE2R was so much fun to replay because you didn't get extra advantages on a replay except your enhanced knowledge, except for the infinite weapons, which with the exception of the knife all penalise you, locking you out of the perfect S+ runs. RE3R does NOT penalise you, even giving you the bolt cutters and lockpick from the shop, and inferno difficulty seems balanced with the coins in mind. If I had to estimate, around 60% of the original's runtime is cut from the remake, making it pitifully short. My first playthrough of the game, for example, was 3 HOURS LONG, compared to RE2R's 10. My point with this whole thing is, while it's still at its core a great game, it's the only game of the remake trilogy so far that I couldn't consider a straight replacement of the original. There's just too much missing for me to say with full certainty that the original is rendered obsolete with this game now out. Also, asking the same price for this as RE2R is a disgrace, £20 is the lowest I could imagine buying this game for, or around 25$ for you Americans reading this.

Nemesis no longer sounds like a geezer who’s been smoking 5 packs a day for forty years. That’s the only improvement they’ve made to him in this remake. Everything else is a ruination of him, and that’s irredeemable because he’s the star of the show. The original game recognised that, referencing the eponymous antagonist in its title - Resident Evil 3: Nemesis.

Every encounter with Nemesis is scripted. There are no dynamic encounters. Those are entirely absent in the remake. Moreover, every encounter feels like a cutscene because there is usually only one way in which the player can respond to the threat of Nemesis. This severely hinders player agency and that is felt throughout the game. 

This remake is far too linear. Even if you haven’t played the original, and compared to RE 2 remake, you feel like you’re on a conveyor belt from start to finish. RE 4 can legitimately be described as very linear too, but the wide open spaces and multiple environments alongside many other positive features like enemy variety make it work in that game.

I’ll admit, putting comparisons aside, this game can be enjoyable to play at times but, ultimately, this is a remake and standards have been set with expectations to follow.

One of the major features not carried over from the original is branching decisions (made during quick time events), which contributes to the conveyor belt formula of the remake and feeling of loss of influence in shaping gameplay and narrative outcomes.

Rather than cutting major sections and mechanics from the original, CapCom could have considered making improvements across the board - just like they did with RE 2 Remake, which was very well received in that regard.

I recognise it’s tempting to play this remake due to its positive features like the obvious improved graphics, and the more intimate ‘over-the-shoulder’ perspective, but this should be recognised as an unsuccessful remake.

With that being said, CapCom is one of the most consistent games development companies in producing high quality AAA releases. Resident Evil 4 remake was excellent, and that was released a few years after this.

However, this game is a reminder that they are not perfect, and they should be called out on the mistakes they made.

I would recommend playing the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. Choosing not to buy this game will reduce the risk of repeated failures.

If you do end up buying this game, don’t expect to be impressed in the manner in which you would playing any other Resident Evil game (other than 6 perhaps).

This game was an absolute chore to get through. I only bought it as part of a remake trilogy Steam Sale, and seven years after release, at that. I knew how poorly fans of the franchise felt about it, but I still went in with an open mind. My enjoyment/irritation ratio was around 40/60.

This game is a zombie shooter whose mechanics lend themselves better to a survival horror (which RE2R was). This is why the fact that they rushed it out just over a year later docks even more points than usual. The game is trying to wear clothing that doesn't fit.

It's a good thing they give you tons of health recovery items, because wading through streets neck-deep in enemies is virtually impossible with how clunky the dodge mechanic, and overall movement is (again, clothing that doesn't fit). Being unable to move 10 feet without getting stopped by some excruciatingly long animation where a zombie bites you gets VERY OLD, VERY FAST. There's even an animation where a zombie ON ITS ABDOMEN, ON THE GROUND, will grab you and climb ALLLLLLL THE WAY UP YOUR ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BODY just to bite you in the neck, and somehow, Jill "Super Cop" Valentine just lets it happen and doesn't even attempt to move, dodge, push it away, or fight back AT ALL. Are you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kidding me? GFY. Maybe that would've flown in RE2R, which was more of a survival horror that not only didn't flood you with zombies in the first place, but also made it possible for you to actually escape zombies, as well as STAGGER THEM with gunshots to the head (which almost never happens in this one). As I said in the beginning though, it doesn't work in this game. The mechanics were very obviously imported from RE2R, and they just don't work because this is not the same type of game that RE2R was: a survival horror.

The Nemesis (main persistent boss) is one of the most infuriating enemies I've ever dealt with. Just chases you and chases you and chases you, blocks your path, knocks you down constantly, dodges don't work, and boom, dead again. The first time I actually managed to ACCIDENTALLY dodge one of his punches, I was genuinely shocked. I thought he was just meant to be annoying and impossible the whole game.

The hospital stretch of the story as Carlos slows the pacing down to an enjoyable level again, returning the game to that survival horror feel that works much better for its mechanics than the fast-paced, shoot-em-up vibe of earlier sections. Then when Jill makes it to the underground facility, another enclosed, labyrinthian space with tight corridors, it helps keep the game in that ideal survival horror zone, but it just can't shake its jittery mechanics.

This game was obviously made at the same time as the RE2 remake so they could milk as many sales as possible, which already deducts a substantial amount of points in my book. If they managed to pull off a good game despite that, more power to them, but they really didn't, and it shows.

Playing Resident Evil 3 Remake was like visiting an old friend that always reminds you of good times, but now they've grown to be a husk of what they once were.

The highlight for me here in this remake was Nemesis. The constant on-edge feeling given from his presence even after he had left the area is what really shines here in this game, I constantly made sure my guns were reloaded and health was at a high percentage just because of the chance he would burst through a wall Kool-Aid man style. Every time I heard his footsteps or saw an open environment from which he could of attacked at any angle , it created real panic, and those moments are the kind of fear I expect from a horror game.

The pacing of the remake often felt rushed in a lot of areas. The story moves a little too quickly from one set piece to the next, leaving little time for you to actually familiarize yourself with and fully explore areas without backtracking a ton. The scripted Nemesis areas also feel a little too noticeable after a bit and aren't really blended in well which disconnects the flow of the gameplay for me. Nemmy is what makes the remake fun for me, but he can almost be called a double-edge sword with the way he makes the game sometimes feels more like an on rails thrill ride than a well-paced RE experience.

My biggest disappointment for this game was unfortunately the lack of content compared to the original Resident Evil 3. Several memorable areas like the ENTIRE clocktower area and park were missing, as well as Nemmy attacking within RPD. Gravedigger also isn't present here as a boss. I can acknowledge from the development lifespan of this game that it was meant to just be RE2R DLC, but why even make this a standalone experience if you weren't gonna give RE3 the same treatment and care as the previous title?

Overall, I gotta pretty mixed feelings about this one man, I loved RE3 with all my heart as a younger gamer and it felt like they cheaped out on my favorite installment in the series and I'm definitely a little sore about it.

[h1]A great game but a bad remake?[/h1]
[hr][/hr]

This seems to be the general consensus about this game.
[b]However[/b]... I disagree.

[hr][/hr]

RE3R has some good things going for it. Namely solid visuals overall and improved dodge mechanic compared to the original game.

The story in the original game always has been minimalistic, being all about surviving and escaping Raccoon City.  
Now I feel the Remake made unnecessary changes in the second half of the game regarding the protagonists' goals which severely dampens what the actual story is all about: [b]Survival[/b].

The 1999 game made use of a show, don't tell narration style.  
The Remake manages to convey less with more.

[hr][/hr]

The original game had four main locations to explore as you progressed through the game.

[list]
[*]Raccoon City's streets (including the R.P.D)
[*]The Clocktower
[*]The Park
[*]The Factory
[/list]

Out of those four. Only [b]ONE[/b] has been preserved.  
You'd think at least it would have been expanded?

[b]Well you'd be wrong[/b] as the opposite happened.  
Raccoon City streets feel so much smaller now.

Oh? New locations you say?

[b]The sewers![/b]  
An 8-minute adventure in a place that only exists for the sake of cutting corners and reusing assets from Resident Evil 2 Remake.

Oh the generic looking lab that is replacing the Factory as the game's final area?  
It looks strangely close to the laboratory from RE2R...

The short hospital section of the original game has been expanded a bit.  
It is a welcome addition but simply doesn't compensate for the loss of Clocktower or Park sections.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Now Nemesis.[/b]

The short build-up leading to its encounter is absent from the Remake as you'll meet him in the literal first 2 minutes of gameplay.

The then semi-dynamic stalker antagonist that oppressed you for the majority of the game, chasing you across rooms and taking away any semblance of solace you thought you had...

Well, it's a complete shadow of its former self now.

A lot of its encounters are scripted set pieces and the few times he's actually roaming around, he's a minor inconvenience that can be taken down with extreme ease.

Which in turn really lessens the forced boss battles with it.  
To think they had a good blueprint for a stalker type threat in RE2R.

[hr][/hr]

RE3R gameplay feels identical to RE2R with the addition of dodges.

Although, shooting zombies feels way less satisfying due to the lack of dynamic limb dismembering that you could use at your advantage in RE2R.

The zombies here feel more rigid and don't react as much to the lead you shoot in their flesh, which is a major let-down for a game that is mostly about shooting zombies when it comes to its gameplay.

[hr][/hr]

A lot of people complain RE3R is short.  
That is true.  
It was also true about the original game.

[b]However[/b] the Live Selection feature from the original game has been completely scrapped.  
It added some decision making that would change how the events of the game unfold.

The 1999 RE3 was slightly less linear too, the Remake plays more like a traditional TPS game where you simply press forward towards your next objective.

The RNG aspect of the original also has been ditched, affecting the ammo placement and also enemies placement and spawns.  
Those things added variance across multiple playthroughs thus increasing the replay value tremendously.

The higher unlockable difficulty modes in the Remake change some enemy and resource placement but in a fixed way though.

[hr][/hr]

The whole Mercenaries game mode has been cut as well in favour of Resident Evil Resistance, a trash multiplayer game which is its own can of worms at this point.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Other things didn't make the cut in RE3R:[/b]

[list]
[*]Several weapons missing.
[*]A whole boss encounter.
[*]Some minor enemies.
[*]Unlockable costumes. (More than 5 depending on game versions. Remake has 1 unlockable costume and 1 DLC costume)
[*]Numerous puzzles. (The Remake has 2 and barely requires any thought)
[*]The respect for the original material.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

Even trying my best to not compare the Remake to the 1999 original.

Everything that's left is a mediocre action game that doesn't manage to live up to the standards set by RE2R.

It's lazy in many aspects and an opportunistic release to make profit off the hype RE2R created.

[hr][/hr]

It's the Hollywood recut of the original title. Filled with cutscenes, setpieces and a lumbering Nemesis revealed from the get go, with zero build-up to the character, much like how they've handled Birkin in the previous game. They just dump the big bad monster on our head removing all sense of dread from the encounter. Sadly, the setpiece laden action fest beginning sets the tone for most of the game.

The main issue here is the level design. After the initial (demo) portion of the map, the game becomes very linear. The core of classic RE is exploring maze like environments, juggling resources and having tense encounters. Effectively, one third of the formula isn't here. No more planning which order to visit areas, just move forward, shoot, and dodge, since levels are mostly divided into small, linear chunks.

The second misstep is Nemesis. The centerpiece of the original game is reduced to the usual boss monster found in any action game. You run around, wait for an opening, shoot the weak spot. This is not what Nemesis was supposed to be. People were expecting a souped-up version of Mr X, a monster who stalks the player throughout the game. This only happens in the demo portion, after that it is dropped for typical boss encounters.

In my eyes, this further suggests that the demo was intentionally crafted to sucker people, since it has one of the very few non linear levels and it is the only place where Nemesis pursues the player like he's supposed to. Maybe it's wrong to assign malice to it, but it feels like you've been tricked into buying a much smaller and simpler game than you were led to believe. Big disappointment.

Survival Through Chaos – A Review of Resident Evil 3

Overall Rating: 9/10

Resident Evil 3 is a fast-paced survival horror experience that trades some of the series’ methodical tension for urgency, spectacle, and constant pressure. Set during the final hours of Raccoon City’s collapse, the game puts players in the boots of Jill Valentine as she fights to escape a city overrun by the undead—and relentlessly hunted by one of the franchise’s most iconic threats. While more action-driven than its predecessors, Resident Evil 3 delivers a focused, cinematic experience that emphasizes momentum, intensity, and survival under pursuit.

Visual Design and Atmosphere: 10/10

Raccoon City is depicted as a city in freefall. Burning streets, collapsing buildings, and claustrophobic interiors create a sense of chaos that permeates every area. Neon lights flicker through smoke-filled alleys, while narrow corridors and ruined storefronts keep tension high. The environments may be more linear than earlier entries, but they are rich with detail and visual storytelling, reinforcing the feeling that the city is dying in real time.

Story and Characters: 8.5/10

Resident Evil 3 places a strong emphasis on character-driven storytelling. Jill Valentine is portrayed as resilient, determined, and emotionally grounded, while Carlos Oliveira brings warmth and humanity to the chaos. The narrative moves at a brisk pace, pushing players forward with urgency rather than mystery. While less focused on slow-burn discovery, the story succeeds in delivering high-stakes survival and emotional weight, reinforcing the desperation of escaping a doomed city.

Gameplay and Survival Mechanics: 10/10

Gameplay leans more toward action than traditional survival horror, but core mechanics still emphasize resource management and smart decision-making. Ammo remains limited, healing items are precious, and encounters often force players to choose between fighting and fleeing. The added dodge mechanic gives combat a more dynamic feel, rewarding timing and situational awareness. While exploration takes a back seat to momentum, the survival loop remains engaging and tense.

Sound Design and Music: 9/10

Sound design heightens the game’s sense of urgency. Explosions echo through streets, distant screams signal danger, and enemy audio cues keep players constantly alert. The soundtrack balances intense action themes with moments of dread, while familiar musical motifs ground the experience within the series’ legacy. Audio works in tandem with pacing, ensuring the tension never truly lets up.

Replayability and Value: 9/10

Resident Evil 3 is a more compact experience, but it encourages replay through difficulty modes, unlockables, and mastery of its mechanics. Knowledge of enemy behavior and item locations improves confidence, yet the game’s relentless pace ensures that repeat runs remain exciting rather than routine. Its shorter length is offset by its intensity and focus.

Conclusion: 9/10

Resident Evil 3 delivers a thrilling, high-pressure survival horror experience that emphasizes escape, pursuit, and momentum. While it sacrifices some of the slower, exploratory elements of earlier entries, it compensates with strong characters, unforgettable enemy design, and nonstop tension.

Final Verdict:
Resident Evil 3 is a lean, aggressive chapter in the series—one that transforms survival horror into a desperate sprint for freedom. With Jill Valentine at its core and Nemesis looming at every turn, it captures the panic of a city on the brink and proves that sometimes survival isn’t about exploration—it’s about making it out alive.

This was the first RE game that I played. I loved every second of it. A month ago I played the original 1999 RE3: Nemesis. Since then I view this as a completely different game.  I still love it, because as a game itself it's still good - just a bit short. It has stunning graphics, the story is good, the intro pulls the player in, and the characters are really well built up. I only didn't like that after the intro, the game doesn't really go deep into Jill's emotions and her trauma. 

And the atmosphere is top notch, the constant feeling of being chased is properly goes through the entire game. Of course, later you can learn that Nemesis is scripted, but the first time experience doesn't really suffer from this problem.

So overall, as a seperate game, pros:
[*] Story
[*] Graphics
[*] Characters
[*] Atmosphere
[*] Dodge mechanic
[*] Mimics
[*] Difficulty

Cons:
[*] Short
[*] The game doesn't dive deep into character's background
[*] A few bugs
[*] Inferno 3rd form Nemesis fight will test your nerves

If I view as a remake, these can be added to the cons:
[*] Many skipped parts and some bosses - including very iconic ones, like the Clock Tower or the Park
[*] Too many differences from the original
[*] Scripted Nemesis

Fortunately you can buy it with good discount price quite often. And I really recommend that everyone should play it as a standalone game, and not comparing it to the original.

PS: Capcom, would you please stop neglecting Jill? It would be much appreciated :)

Just finished the game and I must say: I really enjoyed Resident Evil 3 Remake! Much more than I initially expected. Since I never fully finished the original RE3 back in the day (I played until a bit after taking control of Carlos at the Clock Tower), I approached this remake without much nostalgia. After reading reviews from friends and other players, I honestly thought this would be a bad game — and that probably helped me appreciate it for what it is.

The game feels a bit rushed at the beginning, especially in the city streets. Some iconic locations like the RPD (with Jill) and the Clock Tower are missing, which makes parts of Raccoon City feel like they pass by too quickly. I also felt that the sense of urgency around the nuclear strike could have been better used to create more pressure throughout the story, like the original game did.

Nemesis, while visually impressive, was a bit disappointing as a threat. For such an advanced bioweapon, he rarely feels truly dangerous from a gameplay perspective, and many of his encounters rely more on cutscenes than on real player interaction. I missed the feeling of being constantly hunted in a more unpredictable way. But, I still enjoyed all of his battles.

That said, I loved almost everything else. Jill is one of the highlights: human, determined, not a cliche action hero. She takes damage, gets exhausted, but keeps pushing forward, trying desperately to save a city that is clearly doomed. Her movement, personality, and resilience made her feel very real.

The weapons and crafting system are excellent, staying true to classic Resident Evil mechanics. And the hospital section… absolutely fantastic. Dark, oppressive, full of enemies, and with the return of Hunters, it delivered some of the best survival horror moments in the game.

One detail I really appreciated was how RE3 Remake connects directly with RE2 Remake. Seeing Carlos blow open the wall in the RPD bathroom, and later passing through that same area with Leon and finding it already destroyed, is a small but brilliant touch.

In the end, RE3 Remake is, sadly, too short and imperfect, but very fun and atmospheric. It may not fully honor all aspects of the original, but as a standalone experience, it is intense, well-crafted, and definitely worth playing.

Recommended.

Resident Evil 3 Remake – Detailed Review

Resident Evil 3 Remake is a visually impressive, action-focused reimagining of the original classic. While it succeeds in delivering a cinematic and polished experience, it also makes several design choices that hold it back from reaching the same legendary status as Resident Evil 2 Remake. What’s here is good—sometimes very good—but it feels noticeably trimmed down.

Gameplay & Combat

The combat is one of the strongest parts of the game. Gunplay feels smooth, responsive, and impactful, especially with the added dodge mechanic that gives Jill more mobility and encourages aggressive play. Enemies are satisfying to fight, and higher difficulties demand smart positioning and resource management. Boss encounters are flashy and intense, though many rely heavily on scripted moments rather than emergent tension.

Atmosphere & Visuals

Graphically, the game looks fantastic. Raccoon City is brought to life with incredible detail, lighting, and environmental storytelling. The early city sections are easily the highlight, capturing a sense of chaos and collapse that fits the story perfectly. However, the game moves through these locations quickly, rarely allowing players to soak them in or revisit them meaningfully.

Story & Characters

Jill Valentine is excellent—confident, capable, and well-acted. Carlos is also a standout, adding personality and depth to the narrative. The story is engaging but feels rushed, with key moments happening back-to-back without much downtime. This pacing works for action but hurts suspense and emotional weight. Players familiar with the original will especially notice missing or shortened sections.

Nemesis

Nemesis is intimidating at first, with a strong introduction that sets high expectations. Unfortunately, he quickly becomes more of a scripted set-piece than a persistent threat. Unlike Mr. X in RE2 Remake, Nemesis rarely creates unpredictable pressure, which reduces his long-term impact as a horror icon.

Exploration & Puzzles

Exploration and puzzle-solving take a noticeable back seat. While there are some light puzzles and optional upgrades, the game rarely asks the player to slow down and think. This makes the experience more linear and less replayable from a strategic standpoint compared to other entries in the series.

Length & Replay Value

The biggest downside is the game’s length. A first playthrough can be completed in a single sitting, and even subsequent runs feel brief. While higher difficulties, challenges, and unlockables add some replay value, they don’t fully compensate for how short the main campaign is.

Pros:

Stunning visuals and strong atmosphere

Smooth, satisfying combat with dodge mechanics

Excellent character portrayal, especially Jill

High-quality sound design and voice acting

Fast-paced and polished experience

Cons:

Very short campaign

Significant cut content from the original

Overly linear level design

Nemesis is mostly scripted and underutilized

Limited puzzles and exploration

Final Verdict

Resident Evil 3 Remake is a solid action-horror game and an enjoyable ride, but it falls short as a remake. It feels more like a streamlined reimagining than a faithful adaptation. If you enjoy action-heavy Resident Evil games like RE4 Remake or RE5, you’ll likely have a great time. Just don’t expect the depth, tension, or longevity of Resident Evil 2 Remake.

As an OG fan since '96, and Nemesis being one of my favorites, you'd think I would complain like many others. However, I actually quite love this game, even with its flaws. The majority of complaints seemed based around three things: 1) Content per dollar (complaining it isn't enough for a full priced game), 2) Outdated expectations, 3) Comparing it to RE2R.

Me personally, I buy games on sale, so that isn't a factor for me. As for the cut content, I get it. The clock tower section, the worm boss (which honestly sucked anyway so who cares?), etc. Also, the quicktime Nemesis scenes could have been 10x better if they were live action. But the downtown Nemesis section is awesome, the Hospital section is true horror, and the graphics, game play, story, and the shop system are great. The shop added a ton of replay and I strongly prefer it to re2r. Its too bad there wasn't the infinite magnum, the gatling gun, or more included costumes.

As for RE2R, I do love that game and it has more overall content, but that was also the case with the originals. 2 was always a bit more true horror, and 3 a bit more chaotic action horror. 2 had 4 scenarios, 3 just 1. Also, people seem to act like re2r was a masterpiece and re3r a total mess, but I just don't see it. re2r totally screwed up the scenario system and rushed it at the last minute, it makes no sense in canon, there are overlapping boss fights rather than 100% unique to each scenario, there is no zapping system making for interesting decision making, etc. I'm not complaining, its a great game, but the reputation of re2r as a masterpiece and re3r a let down just makes no sense to me and seems a contradiction. They're much closer than that in my opinion, even if the edge goes to re2r. I sure wish re2r had the shop system, though. Way better way to unlock items and add replay incentive.

The length of the game is actually about the same as the original, so that claim is a misnomer. As for expectations, I no longer expect remakes to be super true to the original, but its neat when they are. I embrace a re-telling and reimagining of the games so long as it isn't butchered. In the end, this game left a lot to be desired, but on its own is a very fun game and the first I've 100% completed in quite a while due to replayability.
