[h1]The Nightmare Within[/h1]

When I rose from my desk, still shuddering from a nightmare in which I was slowly transforming, I went to the bathroom and gazed into my own face. The cold water from the tap ran over my hands, and I immersed my face in it, as though trying to wake myself more fully. It was a stark, biting chill, enough to clear my gaze, to remind me that I was still here—alive. I whispered to myself, I am not infected.

Perhaps it was an omen—the dream, the mirror. I stood before it, yet somehow, I was losing myself. That infection—that thing—on my face felt like the echo of something I’d witnessed in the Spencer Mansion. Something corrupted, something devouring me from the inside out.

The water had only startled me, but it also gave me a clarity I could not ignore. I had to leave the city. I had eaten, a small comfort—pepperoni pizza. Brad called with a tremor in his voice, and soon after, a figure in black, monstrous and towering, breached my apartment. He tore through the bedroom wall, and I, dazed but not yet defeated, sustained a blow. I fired, a direct shot to his head—vital, I thought—but it did nothing.

My ribs throbbed, and I fought not to limp. The pain in my side became a small echo against the terror that followed as I fled the building. In the street, I found Brad.

The city, now twisted, was overrun with these infected souls. The people—the people who once were—were transformed, unrecognisable, as though they too had fallen into the nightmare I had witnessed. The shot I fired felt like a shot at my own soul, haunted by the knowledge that I too could become one of them at any moment. Survival has come to mean something new in this world—a desperate scramble to understand what this infection truly is and what it can do.

While others cling to memories of lost loved ones, I move through these streets, amongst the transformed. I toil, I fight, my only goal to reach the train where the survivors and the Umbrella team await. The horror I carry is not just in what I’ve seen, but in the constant possibility of becoming it.

I caught myself, for a fleeting moment, feeling the weight of this city. I paused to observe its ruins—food still sitting uneaten, cutlery still in place, some items warm as though just abandoned. This city once had life, and now, it only has the remnants of it. The streets feel eerily deserted, and yet the nightmare lingers.

What is this nightmare I foresaw? Am I the host of my own nightmare?

When I saw Kendo, the grief in his eyes was enough to make the air feel heavier. He had lost everything—his daughter—and whispered her fate with the sadness of someone who had already died inside. But time was not on our side. I could not linger in reflection, for the Nemesis—the monster clad in black—was still pursuing me, relentless, as though his sole purpose was my annihilation.

The Umbrella soldiers named him Nemesis, but to me, he was a nightmare personified. He would stop at nothing to eradicate those he deemed a threat. I did not stay by Kendo's side, but now, Nemesis had me in his sights. How does one fight a nightmare? A thing that does not comprehend reason, nor pause to negotiate, nor even flinch at the sound of a scream? No weapon could still it.

This nightmare—this Mare of the night—came to life from the dreamscape and stood before me, incarnate. He wields a flamethrower. I feel the scorch of fire on my skin. I can smell the burning plastic and latex that shrouds his form. The wind stirs with each swing of his arm, but still, he does not falter.

In the dream, the world shatters—a stone thrown at a mirror, the glass breaking. Here, though, no matter how many times I splash water on my face, the nightmare remains. It is here. It is real.

And so, I flee. Like in a dream, I run, I hide. And yet, this is no mere dream. This is reality, and I must face it, even as it seeks to swallow me whole. The only choice left is to keep moving, to fight the nightmare with all I have.

I find a moment of respite in the underground, and for a brief breath, I think I am safe. But then the explosion comes. Mikhail sacrifices himself, Nicolai betrays us, and I am left to pick up the pieces.

A city can never be dreamed so intricately—its fall, its ruin, the loss of someone barely known, and yet now so real. At last, when Nemesis mutated, I knew my chance had come. I would end this, here and now.

The weight of it all sits heavily within me. My limbs are exhausted, my feet numb. I feel as though the nightmare has taken root in my very being. But when I stand over Nemesis’s mutated form, I know—this is not the end of the nightmare. No. This is merely a new chapter.

The nightmare has been here all along—the city, the transformation of its people, Nemesis. What was missing was only for the nightmare to turn its gaze upon me. And when it did—when Nemesis struck me with his dart—I knew nothing more.

What is this nightmare I now inhabit?

I had always feared the unknown, the transformation I might undergo. Yet, as I face the terror of reality, I see the nightmare in a new light. If the city has fallen, then have I too? Even if a cure exists, can it reverse the transformation? What of my mind, my soul—does that also belong to them now?

I thought back to my flat, where I first felt the dread. I thought I was transforming. But no—I was resisting, fighting. I was terrified, but I did not surrender. Not easily. Not yet.

And so, the dream that was once a vague vision on the wall becomes my purpose: to stop Umbrella, to halt their plans. The nightmare has become my relentless guide, pushing me forward, toward a goal I now see clearly.

The perseverance that Carlos saw in me, the “supercop” he called me, is not just survival. It is something far deeper. It is the strength that comes from refusing to become the nightmare, from refusing to let it consume me. It is a strength born from my integrity, from my bond with those like Carlos who fight beside me.

For him, for those I’ve come to know in this nightmare, I will not fail. I will not vanish. I will remain whole.

In the end, it is not just about surviving—it is about choosing to remain.

It plays exactly like this: go in one direction because its a new area and you need to reach your objective, never stop and think about what you should be doing because you havent reached an obstacle yet, great you found what you needed and you also found a shorter path to your objective so you dont even need to backtrack. All of this is actually just fineee like it didnt get tired bc its a short tight paced game with great sections and moments and you are always progressing. [h1] A Thrilling Return to Raccoon City! [/h1]
[h2] Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5) [/h2]



As a long-time fan of the Resident Evil series, I was thrilled to dive into the Resident Evil 3 remake, and it did not disappoint! From the moment I booted up the game, the stunning graphics and atmospheric sound design pulled me right back into the eerie streets of Raccoon City.

Visuals:
The graphics are simply breathtaking. The environments are beautifully crafted, and the character designs, especially for Jill and Nemesis, are top-notch. It's a feast for the eyes!

Gameplay:
The gameplay feels smooth and responsive. The controls are intuitive, allowing for a seamless experience as you navigate the tense encounters with both zombies and the relentless Nemesis. The dodge mechanic adds a fantastic layer of strategy to combat, making each encounter exhilarating.

Pacing:
The pacing is well-balanced, keeping you on the edge of your seat without feeling rushed. The game masterfully combines action and exploration, ensuring there's always something to keep you engaged.

Atmosphere:
The soundtrack and sound design elevate the tension throughout the game. I found myself jumping at every corner, which is a testament to how well the atmosphere was crafted.

Replayability:
With unlockable modes and challenges, there’s plenty of content to keep you coming back for more. I love trying different play styles and seeing how I can improve my runs!

Giving a negative recommendation as there is no in between Yes/No recommendation. It's not because it's a bad game just a missed opportunity for a RE3 remake. It was developed by Capcoms B team as the main team was developing RE8:VILLage and it definitely shows. The remake is missing quite a few scenes and features from the original with entire sections cut short or entirely removed from the original. In the original Nemesis acted more like MR X from the remake with nemesis stalking you throughout the whole game but in this REmake it's only within the first section of the game. It also gets rid of the QTE/Diverging pathways where you had to make a choice to either fight nemesis or run away during certain parts of the original which affected outcomes during certain story beats in the original.

But the primary downside of this REmake is just how short and the amount of content that was cut out. The original RE3 felt more like an expanded RE2 with a bit of back tracking between certain sections of the game but it's entirely non existent in this version. Once you finish the first open section of the game in REmake it pretty much becomes a linear corridor game. They also removed the entire clocktower section which included puzzles and encounters with Nemeis which has been removed nearly entirely and only used as a 10 minute boss fight.

It's honestly just quite disappointing, the original RE3 was shorter than RE2 but not by much but still took 5-6hrs to complete if you didn't die on a first play-through and wanted to rush to finish but with this REmake i was able to finish it in 1 sitting in just under 3hrs without rushing and trying to explore as much as i can but the game doesn't give you time to explore as entire sections of the game are cut off as you progress without you even trying. 

There's also no extra content (Not including the Multiplayer which no one plays anymore in OCE). Once you finish the game that's pretty much it. REmake 2 had 4 Scenarios, Whether you played as Leon or claire 1st/2nd affected the story (Known as Leon/Claire A/B), 4 extra "What If" type scenarios about a few of the characters in the game including Kendo, The mayors daughter Katherine and a Surviving soldier during Operation Nestwrecker. A plethora of hidden modes including HUNK's 4th Survivor mode and multiple versions of Tofu survivor  plus a hidden wave based mode based on the sheriff from the start of the game during the gas station scene which added hours of extra content trying to perfect each run of those modes in as little time as possible but nothing like that in REmake 3. There are a hand full of challenges to do during REmake 3's story (Complete without saving, heal once etc) but its not much compared to the amount of extra content in REmake 2.

I also don't know how to explain it but it also feels weird to play, like it feels like a cheaper version of REmake 2. There's strange mouse acceleration which is noticeable when trying to line up on zombies heads and the menu navigation behaves weird with a mouse, as if it was designed to be done with a controller. Also some button prompts don't show up, for a lot of the interactions it shows Mouse 1 to be used to open doors, crates etc but you can also use the F key which feels more natural and more responsive, a lot of the time using mouse 1 to open doors and crates doesn't work well. There's also the interaction with the knife, in REmake 2 if you hold space you can pull out the knife but in REmake 3 you have to actually equip it. The controls also feel more jerky and idk how to explain it, it just feels like a cheaper experience than REmake 2, it's especially obvious during the hospital standoff scene where waves of zombies are pilling through the windows but as you kill the zombies they just explode into a mist of red blood as the game cant handle having that many bodies loaded in and it just looks like a cheap effect compared to how it was done in RE 4/REmake 4 where the Ganados melt into a brown goo which fit in with that games story.

All in all i do, but don't recommend this game. It's graphics are amazing which is to be expected from REngine at this point being one of the best looking engines out nowadays and the story and acting is a massive step up from the original but with the amount of content cut/shortened i wouldn't pay full price, considering how REmake 2 is 10$ cheaper with hours more content in just the main story alone, and that's without including the hours of extra content in the "what if" type modes. 

Also Nemesis's redesign sucks, i miss my leather daddy Nemesis which has been replaced with a drug addict covered in a trash bag.

I Definitely wouldn't pay more than 20$ for this game but REmake 2 is definitely worth the full price

Resident Evil 3 (2020) disappointed fans of the series. The campaign is extremely short (it takes 4-5 hours to complete), and the truncated plot and the absence of key moments from the original (for example, Live Selection-style choices) deprive the game of depth. Nemesis, the main element of the horror, has turned into a predictable "stalker" with scripted appearances, and not a chaotic threat, as in the original. 
Locations fly by too quickly, and the combat mechanics, although polished, do not save from the feeling of incompleteness. The multiplayer Resistance mode seems like an imposed addition, and not a full-fledged part. For the full price, the game seems overpriced, especially after the benchmark remake of Resident Evil 2. For fans - a fatal lack of replayability, for beginners - too superficial horror. It's a pity that the potential is used by a third.

If you aren't interested in reading a massive review, the long story short- This game is as short as this summary, nearly cutting over half of the original games content, and while it's not inherently a bad game, it's an awful remake. 

Before people complain and whine about my negative review, I am a huge RE fan, and I will nitpick this game like no tomorrow. I've been playing RE for nearly my whole life and I have played every single mainline RE title, including all of the remakes and some other titles such as OP: Raccoon City, both RE Outbreaks on the PS2, Revelations, The Mercenaries 3D, and Code Veronica- with that said, this is genuinely a massive disappointment. The original game, while obviously dated to modern standards, has SO much more in comparison. Many of the iconic locations and experiences like the Clock tower fight, the split path decisions, enhanced ammo, ACTUAL puzzle solving, a non-linear design, and costumes that aren't unlocked by pre-ordering (excluding the ONE costume you can purchase in game with points after beating it) are ALL missing. Not only that, but how do you manage to ruin Nemesis?? In the original game he was a genuine threat that needed to be avoided at all costs, and in this one he's been ruined by not only doing such a little amount of damage, but by scripted events and cutscenes. It no joke takes ONE grenade, even on Hardcore, to knock him to the ground. How do you ruin the one thing that made this game at least unique to 2??

Not to mention Jill. I don't usually pick at characters, and I think in each remake so far (1,2, and 4) each character has been remade very well, their personalities matched very well to their dialogue, and Jill has always been my personal favorite character throughout the series because she's nothing short of a badass, and not because of her awesome one liners and overly exaggerated fight scenes, but because of her ability to get ♥♥♥♥ done. I wish this game was like that, but in this game she is unbearable. Nothing but snarky and rude comments, sh*tty quips and "I'm the strong female lead, watch this badass move." I think everything she is in this game is stupid and not a legit reflection of her character as a whole, and I actively discard this Jill as the actual Jill Valentine. I feel like I sound like a sexist redditor when I say all of this, but they've turned Jill from a badass, kind of quiet, and very resourceful character to the stereotypical feminist wet dream. I'm fine with female leads, but I find this rework of her character very dumb and out of touch from who she actually is. 

On a good note, the RE Engine is an absolutely beautiful work of art, and this game is absolutely stunning. The optimizations alone are insanely impressive, running at 180 FPS consistently with maxed out settings with ray tracing enabled. The combat is also good, as it's nearly identical to RE2 remakes. Good graphics however don't take away from the not-so-good story. A turd wrapped in gold if you will.

This game in my opinion is nothing short of a cashgrab, only existing to profit from nostalgia while pissing on the people who have supported you. Charging 60 dollars at release for a game I was able to beat in under 2 hours on HARDCORE is nothing short of embarrassing. I understand that this game was in development during Covid, which obviously complicated things, but this is just inexcusable. You shouldn't have released this game. I'm hopeful that one day, they'll actually remake 3 properly, but until then, we have this absolute smear of feces on the steam store. I played this game so I wouldn't get bored during a week without internet, and it was honestly a very good call.

As a big fan of the OG RE3 of course I have many complaints, yes, but in general I had a good time playing the remake.

(POSITIVE STUFF)
- I love how everything was re-interpreted to make it more unique and fitting with the universe and set of RE2 Remake. It made sense, it was really nice to see that connection being (imo) more vivid than the og games.

- Giving Carlos another section was a big plus for me. At first I thought the whole section of RPD would be gone, but having not only a new set of missions there, but also playing as Carlos was a pretty big thing for me, probably one of the main missions I enjoyed the most.

- Side characters are cool. I definitely felt closer to Tyrell, in contrast to the og re3 where honestly i didn't care about him. It happened the other way around with Mikhail, it was one of my faves in the og, but this time around he was just there.

- The visuals, the voice acting, the essence of the characters was amazing 

- The dodge mechanic is actually really good, it feels so satisfying overall.

- Collectibles are fun. It usually gets tedious for me after a while, but given the fact that it's a pretty short game (4:30 hours on my first playthrough, being an anxious person that literally checks every corner just to see if I didn't miss anything), but I found most of the collectibles during my first run, and getting the rest of them wasn't boring or anything.

- The challenges were actually pretty fun, I had a good time farming kills with certain weapons, having a run without opening a box, etc. It was very enjoyable overall to get those objectives and honestly that's the only reason I didn't uninstall as soon as I finished my first playthrough. 

(NEGATIVE STUFF)
- The stuff they cut out served no purpose other than to make the game shorter. In the OG there was this feature where, depending on the ranking you'd get after finishing the game, it would reward you with different skins. I'm assuming they tried to implement some alternative version of it here by trying to make the game as replayable as possible, too, but that wasn't my cup of tea since there were a lot of elements that could have been re-imagined for this game, such as the clock tower or the park. My quickest run was 1 hour and 7 minutes, I replayed it around 8 times to get all the achievements. Getting a good 15 minutes more of puzzles would have been cool.

- Nemesis didn't feel as terrifying as it should have been. RE2 remake had a big thumbs up in making mr. x be such a pain in the ass and something to panic about at the same time, but this time it didn't hit the mark. There is stalking here and there, but I didn't find it menacing. Even on the higher difficulties it didn't make me feel the emotional intensity that the previous game did.

- The difficulty didn't feel... difficult. I would have expected to have more of a challenge during inferno mode, but I think the only section where I actually struggled with was the final boss (but that was on me, I wasn't dodging on time). Of course, you can make your own personal challenges (i.e. inferno with no boxes and no healing) to make it more difficult by yourself, but it isn't as rewarding.

- Puzzles weren't really difficult and barely a thing. Actually, I would have enjoyed a lot if puzzles changed between difficulties.

- "you saved my ass first". this is a literal line of dialogue by Carlos. Why is this a bad thing, you might ask. Because Jill didn't save his life to begin with lmao. The writing, to be really honest, wasn't the best.

- Taking ~20 hours to finish it 100% is still too short tbh.

“Resident Evil 3 Remake: A Zombie Tango in HD”

Introduction: Alright, fellow survivors, let’s crank up the nostalgia dial and step into Raccoon City circa 2020. “Resident Evil 3 Remake” is like that vintage vinyl you found in your uncle’s basement—scratched, a bit dusty, but oh-so-iconic. So, grab your ink ribbons and let’s chat about this undead jam.

Visual Overhaul: Remember those pixelated zombies? The ones that moved like they were doing the robot dance? Well, say hello to their HD cousins. These undead pals are juicier than a ripe watermelon at a summer picnic. Their heads explode like confetti cannons at a New Year’s Eve bash, and their hands? Let’s just say they’re not winning any hand modeling contests. Capcom went all out with atmospheric lighting, facial animations, and gore. It’s like they whispered to the zombies, “Hey, could you be more terrifying? Thanks.”

Classic Survival Horror, Modern Swagger: “Resident Evil 3” struts its stuff like a zombie catwalk. It’s almost as good as last year’s “Resident Evil 2 Remake.” The tension? Thicker than grandma’s gravy. The undead crowd control? More intricate than a Rubik’s Cube. And those criss-crossing hub areas? Like navigating a maze of zombie-infested IKEA furniture. Stick to the template, and you’ll be dodging Nemesis like a pro.

Short and Sweet (Maybe Too Short?): Now, here’s the catch: The game’s shorter than a TikTok video. Blink, and you’ll miss it. But hey, quality over quantity, right? It’s like a rollercoaster ride—you scream, you laugh, and suddenly it’s over. Just don’t expect a three-course meal; this is more like a zombie tapas bar.

Final Verdict: “Resident Evil 3 Remake” isn’t just a game; it’s a zombie tango in HD. Sure, the multiplayer mode stumbles like a tipsy survivor, but the single-player campaign? Magnificent. So, grab your shotgun, channel your inner Jill Valentine, and dance through the apocalypse. 🧟‍♂️🎶

As a connoisseur of fine digital entertainment, I have taken it upon myself to delve into the latest iteration of the Resident Evil franchise, Resident Evil 3. In my esteemed opinion, this game boasts several strengths, punctuated by innovative features that breathe new life into the series. Admittedly, it is somewhat disheartening to observe that certain content from the original has been excised. However, this does not detract from the overall quality or enjoyment of the game.

Resident Evil 3 leans more heavily towards action, yet it masterfully retains the tension that is the hallmark of the series. Some may argue that the game is lamentably brief, possibly the shortest among the modern Resident Evil titles. Nonetheless, I find that this brevity can be viewed as a strength. The adage "short and sweet" aptly applies here. In a landscape where many games are lengthy and exhausting, it is refreshing to encounter a title that can be completed in a single, exhilarating session.

Given its relatively concise duration, it might be prudent to acquire this game during a discount period. This way, one can fully appreciate its merits without reservations. Ultimately, Resident Evil 3 is a worthy addition to the franchise, offering a compact yet thrilling experience that is both invigorating and satisfying.

Growing up with Nintendo consoles I never got to play the original Resident Evil 3 as it was the only main sequence title that never got a re-release. For that reason I was pretty excited about the RE3 remake, especially after playing through the rather excellent RE2 remake. 

Having now finished RE3 I'm underwhelmed to say the least. RE2 was everything you'd want from a remake; it greatly improved the visuals and updated the gameplay in line with other contemporary 3rd person horror games. The fixed camera angles were gone in favour of RE4's over the shoulder style gunplay*, as were the tank controls and those loading screen doors. With more dynamic gameplay it almost felt like a new title*. Meanwhile RE3's big addition to the series is a finicky dodge button. So, yeah....

The thing is, I'd have been quite happy with another dose of RE2's gameplay in a new location, with new story and characters. Unfortunately RE3 takes a step backwards in a couple of areas, and I think it's best to start with the game's primary setting. 

So RE3 begins with Jill Valentine in her apartment in racoon city, a few days before she's set to leave*. Before she can do that, or wake up to the fact that the city outside her window is becoming a zombie infested nightmare, a giant melted action man wearing a bin bag crashes through her wall and proceeds to chuck her about. This is the game's primary antagonist, nemesis, and he hounds you at various points throughout the game. He's basically a more scripted version of Mr X from RE2. So Jill's objective is to escape the city before it's destroyed, whilst avoiding being tongued to death by Nemesis. Early on she runs into Carlos, a man having a really bad hair day and the game's other playable character. 

Now as far as settings go this doesn't sound too bad. A tense cat and mouse escape through a rapidly collapsing city full of zombies and other umbrella monstrosities sounds pretty exciting, but you've got to remember this is a remake of RE3 and the technology in those days couldn't handle expansive locations with multiple routes and large scale scenarios. So instead the RE3make is largely set in a collection of linear streets, alleyways and enclosed roads, as well as a few buildings. There's very little freedom and exploration is limited, even in the larger buildings, one of which is the racoon city police department. Now you only get to explore a little bit of the police station as those doors need to remain locked for Leon and Claire from RE2, who will be arriving in a few hours having never apparently watched a news programme, but being there highlights how much better the level design is. RE2's station is much more enjoyable to explore and poke around in, and it's far less linear. You also feel like you're uncovering the story of not only the police station, but of wider events. It is, dare I say it, a rather iconic location, and one RE3 doesn't come close to replicating. Even the part in the hospital still feels railroaded and the area you can explore isn't all that big.

Length is also an issue. I finished RE3 in around six and a half hours, and that was with my rather sedate gameplay style. Unlike RE2 there's only the one campaign, you just swap over to Carlos at various points, but I don't think I'd have wanted to play through the entire campaign again (albeit with slightly different events) with Carlos anyway. It just didn't grab me like RE2's campaign did. There's also no additional mini campaigns or trials like in RE2, it's barebones and I had very little desire to replay the story like I did when RE2.

It's also less of a horror game than RE2, possibly due to the open seeming environments, but there's very little in the way of building tension and it lacks RE2's atmosphere. A relentless killer chasing you down could have been tense, but all of nemesis's appearances are scripted to some degree, he's not free roaming like Mr X is. Due to the more cramped environments, nemesis encounters can actually be quite frustrating, especially outside his boss specific fights. This is probably why they added a dodge button, but as I've already mentioned it doesn't always work, sometimes throwing you right at the enemies you're trying to avoid. Other enemies in the game also have these annoying one hit kill attacks that can be tricky to avoid in such cramped environments, especially the fast moving hunters.

Overall I'm rather reluctant to recommend RE3, especially at full price, because what we have here seems more like DLC than a full game. It's short, linear and lacks replayability, and the story isn't anything to write home about. The gameplay, whilst more frustrating than RE2's is still pretty good however, so if you can pick it up cheaply in a sale and you're a fan of the series, I'd just about recommend it.

*It has its problems to be sure. The story is still naff as are the boss battles, which feel like they're missing (ironically) a dodge button, or the option to strafe. The arenas for the bosses are also too cramped making them frustrating. I'd also have liked more cross over between Leon and Claire's campaigns, as they appear to exist in different dimensions.

As a fan of the Resident Evil series, I will start this review by saying I have never played the original Resident Evil 3. This already puts me at a bias because I know a large amount of negative reviews are garnered towards the fact that Capcom changed and/or cut out a majority of the story/gameplay. This aside, I will give an honest review of the game from my POV. If your issues with the game lie with what I just described, this review will be pretty irrelevant to you.

First thing is first, the storyline is considered 'short' by many critics. For myself, the game took about 7 hours with standard difficulty and pretty normal pacing. Personally, 7 hours is a reasonable playtime for a video game. I can only think that the reason behind so many players disdain comes from the fact that almost all games released now have considerably long playtimes. However, I will agree that a $40 price tag for a 7 hour campaign is pretty unreasonable. If you can pick this game up on sale, it is 100% justified.
 
Secondly, the gameplay. It seems that a lot of critics have issues with the fact that the Nemesis encounters are scripted. Again, never played the original, so I don't know how the remake differs, but this is not an issue for me. When encountering Nemesis, I can certainly say that it got my heart racing and had me sweating a little bit. The encounters are pretty enjoyable, even if predictable. Other than this, the gameplay doesn't really differ from its RE2R counterpart, a majority of the same assets are shared. The only noticeable difference is that the enemy encounters are slightly more fast-paced with more action.

To wrap this up, I will be honest and say that the Resident Evil 3 Remake was slightly underwhelming. I was expecting something in the same caliber of RE2R, but what we get is a relatively linear experience which strays far from the typical RE experience (Centered around one major location, unlocking smaller areas and completing puzzles.) This doesn't make RE3 a BAD game, it just takes some time to get used to, as you get thrust into Raccoon City running from a giant with tentacles. What I did enjoy was getting to see different parts of Raccoon City, as we don't get to really experience this in RE2R. You get to see the T-Virus in all its glory on the first days of the infection, encountering many different iconic areas like the RCPD or the city hospital. The gameplay switch from Jill to Carlos is refreshing, and I really enjoy what they did with Carlos in the remake. 

This certainly is not my least favorite Resident Evil title, but I can say with confidence (so far) that it is my least favorite remake. That said, it is still a really fun game and certainly provides a memorable experience. My only suggestion is that you pick this game up on sale, and look at it in a different light when playing. Keep in mind, when the OG RE3 released back in the 90s, Capcom purposely took a different approach to try and separate it from RE2. This is unchanged at its core in the remake, which I can respect. A lot of players have issues with this, but I personally think it separates RE3 from the rest of the series and set the tone for more action-paced RE titles like we have today (RE4, RE5 and Village) -- they just did it better.

As someone who thoroughly enjoyed the RE2 Remake but missed out on the original RE3, I approached Resident Evil 3 Remake with high hopes. Unfortunately, my experience fell short of expectations.

Let's address the elephant in the room: [u]this game is short.[/u]

Unfortunately, my first review I tried to write was simply too long for steam as was this second attempt. I didn't want to be shallow in my analysis. I will find a way to safely post my full thoughts to read. I digress.

I like this game. Is it the Resident Evil 2 Remake? No. I may have a couple of comparisons here and there but I want to talk about this game in and of itself as much as I can. Ultimately, after completing all the achievements and even all the additional in game challenges, I am sad that it's over because at the end of the day I did really enjoy this game and I hope others can too. However, after watching an excellent video essay from a YouTuber named Pastra, it helped me understand where some older fans of the franchise take issue with certain aspects of this game and I certainly have my own gripes. However, as someone who knew virtually nothing before going in, never having played the original, and was experiencing the story, characters, and everything else RE3 (and frankly RE in general) for the first time. I enjoyed this game. I think it's one I can come back and visit again one day with some fondness.

[b]What I liked:[/b]

1. THE MENU MUSIC! A truly haunting track that sets the right tone for a game that could be. It gave me goosebumps the first time I heard it and when all was said and done after I completed the game for a final time I just sat and listened. There is beauty in its simplicity. The music was fantastic in other places as well.

2. The characters. I unfortunately cannot touch on every character as I did originally, so I will summarize. As a whole and in general I thought all voice acting performances were truly fantastic. You could tell the VA's put a lot of care and passion into their roles and it shined through in creating distinct and unique characters. I enjoyed experiencing the main casts arcs. [spoiler]Also ♥♥♥♥ Nicholai the evil, greedy bastard. Love to hate this man.[/spoiler]

3. The expansion of lore and of Raccoon City. In case some of you were unaware [spoiler]Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 3 take place at nearly the same time with overlaps in certain places with some events taking place before or after one another but not so in that any characters from either games paths cross. [spoiler]This overlap was super fun to experience for the first time, utilized well, and the charm never really left on subsequent playthroughs either. [/spoiler] Getting to see more of Raccoon city was a treat as well as lent itself to the world building that had begun to be established in RE2.[/spoiler]

4. The first time Nemesis pursues you around the city. He is faster, can dodge attacks, and has different tricks than Mr. X from Resi 2 and it re-ignited that fear all over again. It makes trying to navigate the rest of the tasks you have left to do in [spoiler]Downtown RC[/spoiler] incredibly stressful in the fun horror game kind of way.

5. The weapons. To be (unfortunately) brief. There is a fun variety of weapons between Jill and Carlos and the item shop weapons make a nice touch and can change up the dynamics of a run through.

6. The hospital section. [spoiler]To clarify I do [b]NOT[/b] mean the hold out section at the end after you've given Jill the vaccine. I very much do not enjoy that section and still don't.[/spoiler] This entire section induced me with so much dread at points that despite the fact I was playing badass Carlos I did not feel safe or confident. The atmosphere is set so right for this section of the game. The hospital is almost completely dark throughout and deathly quiet. The notes that are left to discover tell a tragic and chilling tale of the staff who tried to do the right thing but perished in spite of it to be left for you, the player, to fight off.

7. Nightmare and Inferno mode. I did enjoy the additional difficulty. Changing up enemy and item locations and it brings a fresh challenge and perspective to a game that can sometimes be challenging to grind through multiple times.

8. The look of Nemesis. Strictly speaking to cosmetics. I liked the look of this Nemesis particularly form 1 and his final form. Him busting through walls and the first time he gets fully revealed he is very intimidating. His look and pose on the menu screen is striking and hearing him mumble "STARS" as he pursues you is frightening. 

9. The first Nemesis boss fight. Short and sweet. I liked this one. Feels like how it should be and perhaps how more of them should have been.

10. New enemies. Once again to keep it brief. There are several new badies and varieties of enemies introduced into this game that add a fun new dynamic to navigating combat.

[b]Things I did not like so much:[/b]
Note this section will likely be much more spoiler heavy.

1. The utilization of Nemesis. As I mentioned, I liked the first time you are chased by Nemesis  [spoiler]throughout Downtown RC, however after that besides when he comes at you with the rocket launcher that's pretty much it. The game never has him chase you in the same way and that's frankly really a shame. To draw from RE2 Remake a bit, one of the key points of terror for myself was the point in which Mr. X begins pursuing and looking for you around the police station. His presence alone and the simple [i]possibility[/i] of him finding you while you are desperately trying to finish all tasks necessary adds an element to RE2 that is hard to match. Not to mention that Mr. X (particularly in Leon's campaign) comes for you multiple times and in multiple places. Making his threat a near ever present one and even when he's not around you're afraid that at any point he might be. This is where Nemesis falls short. He is meant to be the ultimate pursuer but it just doesn't feel like he does enough pursuing when it's all said an done. Furthermore, him dying to [b]ONE GRENADE[/b] is just sad, even if it is an easier difficulty come on. Once I learned this fact it made avoiding him trivial which is just not how it should be. The whole idea around the original Nemesis was risk versus reward. You could either run from him (you should) or stand and fight. If you decided to stand and fight and manged to temporarily knock Nemesis down you would be rewarded with rare weapon parts to build a powerful gun. But to get those rewards required a lot of ammo and resources and could perhaps be a detriment to you later down the line in your playthrough. In short, that's not the case here. Even if you're not comparing it to the original and you lack context, he's simply too easy and makes what should be an incredibly threatening and powerful enemy seem trivial.[/spoiler]

2. The lack of things to do post-game. Yes, you have Nightmare and Inferno mode and encouraged to play through the game multiple times. I am not a game developer so I cannot speak on the difficulty of making these things happen. But the precedent was set high by RE2 and one would hope they would be able to follow it a little more.

3. Aspects of boss fights. I originally had a lot to say here, however, since Steam is limiting me. Play the game and see for yourself how you feel.

4. [spoiler]The holdout section in the hospital. That is all.[/spoiler]

Overall, there are aspects of it I am at times 50/50 on but I ultimately have more likes than dislikes for this experience. The game looks gorgeous and I, personally think, passes the test for still being fun despite its flaws. As someone who is still fresh and new to the Resident Evil it feels the Resident Evil world is being rewritten and remade for a new generation of fans to enjoy and I am here for it. I truly appreciate you taking the time to read this review. I hope you find as much enjoyment out of this game as I did and hopefully in the Resident Evil franchise.

It's a tremendous step backwards coming from RE7 and RE2R though. I had such high hopes for this game being a massive fan of the original ever since playing it 24 or so years ago, but they cut so many corners with this remake that it would almost be funny if it wasn't so depressing.

The zombies are just copy pasted from RE2R, but like... from an earlier beta build seemingly? They still animate at like 10 fps once you move a certain distance away from them, like in RE2R. I could forgive that fact, but in RE3R limbs disappear into thin air when they're destroyed, and the physics are just absent once a zombie dies. I can't imagine any reason for them to have downgraded such a great feature after how well it was received in RE2R. Parity for the sake of the pathetic and underpowered console hardware maybe? It's a shame there isn't a setting on pc to fix this or the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 10 fps zombie lods.

The Live Selection system from the original has been removed. A lot of people were hoping that it would make the cut because it added some flavor and incentive to replay the game, but it's gone unfortunately. This game is 5 to 6 hours long on a first playthrough if you are being extremely thorough. The incredibly short length stands out even more without live selection to spice up subsequent playthroughs.

Numerous iconic areas and bosses from the original re3 are entirely absent, and the areas that are in the game have been trimmed severely. You wont spend nearly as much time exploring raccoon city as you'd like to unfortunately.

And the most egregious failure in RE3R in my opinion is Nemesis. On the positive side, he looks and sounds great. Neil Newbon does a lovely job making him look imposing with the motion capture he did for him. But unfortunately, basically every encounter with him is a fixed set piece. It no longer feels like he's stalking you throughout the city and that he could show up at any moment like in the original. 

Not everything is bad news in RE3R though. This game is absolutely gorgeous visually. Characters look even more godly here than they did in RE2R. Bless capcom for creating their RE Engine. And all the voice actors give seriously impressive and believable performances, helping to draw you into the experience. Jill and Carlos are particular highlights. I hope they keep bringing back Nicole Tompkins for any future RE projects involving Jill. She's awesome!

Do I recommend this game? Sure. Just don't go into it expecting an experience on par with the recent remakes or the original RE3. I thought for sure this game would be a 10/10 after experiencing the glory that was RE2R. But clearly things can go very wrong when capcom passes their projects off to a B team and outsources too much.

Steam Deck performance review of Resident Evil 3:
This game is listed as 'playable' but it's not that simple. Here is my steam deck review after spending +30 hours with the game and keeping all the graphical setting at its default. If you want a full review of the game itself, there are plenty of reviews online.

Long story short: It runs but I encountered several issues.

4. Severe and random audio glitches. Sometimes the audio will get out of sync with the cut-scenes and gameplay. Sometimes there will be no audio whatsoever. Sometimes (and most often audio glitch) there will be random loud 'static' noises while playing that could last a few minutes unless you restart the game and hope nothing worse happens.

As someone who never got into classic survival horror games, I do not know the differences between Resident Evil 3 Remake and the original. Even then, RE3R clearly comes off as a time-crunched remake of a more complete game. The moment-to-moment gameplay is satisfying, but that is mostly because of the mechanical polish that is borrowed from RE2R. The other aspects that made the previous remake incredible (the intricate level design, the replayability, and the omnipresent AI-powered threats) are all halfheartedly emulated. The focus this time around is on stretching the base mechanics of Resident Evil to encompass pure action and strict resource management. Admittedly the game achieves that goal, but that goal only highlights the missing ingredients. None of the content that is in the game is bad per se, but it does make the experience of playing RE3R come off as incredibly modern and supplementary. Did you like RE2R? Cool, here's another experience made with the same structure and components.

Technically the game runs well just like the RE2make. But unlike that, I have harsh words.

No Factory, no Park, Clock Tower reduced to a set piece fight. No lab in the centre of town. No getting the FEAR of having to run for your life from the Police Station because Nemesis is chasing you with a rocket launcher.

The first ten minutes of the game set it up decently that you were going to have this s**tehawk on you more relentlessly than the original game. Unfortunately it's now apart from a few areas just reduced to set pieces and that's pretty sad.

And then there's the whole case of them deciding to flesh out dubious bad guy to make him obviously bad bad guy from the start. You're left wondering why with the narrative way your character didn't just slot them early. There's even a 360/PS3 era style of horde survival at the hospital now they've cut that sequence out.

There's a QTE I failed that was drawn out for over a minute because I couldn't believe all you had to do was hold down ONE BUTTON for pretty much a minute. I just stopped to see what happened.

It's just a perfect summary for this game being such a great idea at the time that had so much promise but just felt rushed and lacklustre. [h2]Resident Evil 3 Remake plunges players into the chaotic streets of Raccoon City once again, offering a mix of intense action and survival horror.[/h2]

While it brings some improvements over the original, it falls short in certain aspects, leaving it a somewhat mixed experience.

Visually, the game impresses with its detailed environments and character models, bringing the nightmarish world of Raccoon City to life in stunning detail. However, the game's length feels disappointingly short, leaving players craving more content to sink their teeth into.

Gameplay-wise, Resident Evil 3 Remake offers a more streamlined experience compared to its predecessor. The controls are responsive, and the combat is fast-paced, with a variety of weapons and tools to dispatch the undead. However, the removal of certain sections from the original game, such as the clock tower and gravedigger boss fight, feels like a missed opportunity and leaves the overall experience feeling somewhat lacking.

Nemesis, the iconic antagonist of the game, is a terrifying presence that stalks players throughout their journey. His appearances are intense and nerve-wracking, but they can also feel somewhat scripted and predictable, lacking the same sense of unpredictability that made Mr. X in Resident Evil 2 Remake so terrifying.

In terms of story, Resident Evil 3 Remake offers a faithful retelling of the original game's narrative, with some additional scenes and character development added for good measure. However, the pacing feels rushed at times, and certain plot points are glossed over or left unresolved, leaving the story feeling somewhat disjointed.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 Remake is a solid entry in the series that offers plenty of thrills and scares for fans of survival horror. While it may not reach the same heights as its predecessor, it still manages to deliver an entertaining experience that will keep players on the edge of their seats, even if it leaves them wanting more.

"Resident Evil 3" oferă o experiență de joc explozivă și plină de adrenalină, în care jucătorii se luptă pentru supraviețuire într-un oraș devastat de un virus mortal.

Un aspect notabil al jocului este gameplay-ul său captivant și ritmul său alert. Jucătorii preiau controlul asupra lui Jill Valentine, o membră a echipei S.T.A.R.S., și trebuie să scape din Raccoon City, care este cuprins de haos și infectat de creaturi îngrozitoare. Combinația de puzzle-uri tensionate, explorare intensă și confruntări cu inamicii creează o experiență de joc echilibrată și provocatoare.

Grafica jocului este impresionantă, cu medii detaliate și modele realiste de personaje și monștri. Atmosfera sumbră și înfricoșătoare a Raccoon City este redată într-un mod autentic, contribuind la imersiunea jucătorului în lumea terifiantă a jocului.

Un avantaj semnificativ este inclusiv modul multiplayer asimetric "Resident Evil Resistance", care oferă o experiență de joc complet diferită și adaugă o varietate suplimentară la pachetul general al jocului.

Un dezavantaj potențial poate fi durata relativ scurtă a campaniei pentru unii jucători, în comparație cu alte titluri din serie.

În concluzie, "Resident Evil 3" oferă o experiență de supraviețuire explozivă și plină de adrenalină, care îți va ține inima la limită și te va face să te întorci pentru mai mult. Indiferent dacă ești un fan al seriei sau un jucător nou în căutarea unei aventuri înspăimântătoare, "Resident Evil 3" nu va dezamăgi.

Rating: 8.5/10

Resident Evil 3 Remake is a fantastic entry point for newcomers to the Resident Evil series. It delivers an exciting story, intense atmosphere, and beautiful visuals. While some might find the Nemesis less terrifying than the original or the story shorter compared to RE2 Remake, this remake offers a thrilling experience, especially for those who appreciate a tighter narrative and don't want a massive time commitment.

Pros (+):

+ Action-packed & Engaging Story: The game throws you right into the thrilling escape from Raccoon City, with Jill Valentine a former S.T.A.R.S. member fighting for survival amidst a zombie apocalypse. You'll encounter iconic moments from the franchise while experiencing the desperation and chaos of a city overrun by the undead.
+Stunning Visuals: The character models and environments are a step up from the previous remake. Raccoon City feels like a real, decaying city, and the character designs are incredibly detailed - you'll find yourself admiring Carlos' hair (among other things) in the midst of the chaos.
+Intense Experience: The game excels at building tension. Nemesis, a relentless pursuer, adds another layer of fear as you never know when he might appear. The sound design is superb, creating a truly unsettling atmosphere that will keep you on the edge of your seat (in a good way!).
+Great Voice Acting: The voice acting delivers the story like a high-quality mini-series, bringing the characters of Jill Valentine and Carlos Oliveira to life. You'll feel invested in their struggles and triumphs as they fight their way through Raccoon City.
+Perfect Length for New Players: The campaign is shorter than the RE2 remake, but feels perfectly paced and avoids dragging on. This is a great starting point for newcomers who might be intimidated by longer games, but still offers a complete and satisfying story.

Cons (-):

-Less Character Development: Jill and Carlos don't receive as much development as characters in the RE2 remake. While their personalities come through in their dialogue and actions, you won't get the same depth of backstory compared to RE2's characters.
-Nemesis Not as Haunting: The Nemesis enemy is intimidating, especially with his imposing size and mutated features. However, he doesn't stalk you persistently throughout the game like Mr. X from RE2 Remake. His appearances are more scripted events, making him less unpredictable and scary.
-Linear Story: The game lacks the branching choices from the original RE3, making for a more linear experience. There's a clear path forward, and you won't have the same level of replayability offered by the option to make choices that affect the story.

Neutral (+/-):

+/- Map Design: The map is well-designed and offers a variety of environments to explore, from the claustrophobic alleys to the burning streets. However, it doesn't quite capture the same open-world feel of the Raccoon City Police Department in RE2 Remake.
+/- Nemesis Difficulty: The dodge mechanic, a new addition to the remake, makes Nemesis slightly less challenging to avoid. While he can still be a formidable opponent, the ability to dodge adds another layer of defense that wasn't present in the original.
+/- Compared to RE2 Remake and Original: While a solid/good game on its own, RE3 suffers a bit following the phenomenal RE2 remake. Some content was cut from the original RE3, and the campaign is shorter. This might be a downside for players who expect the same amount of content as RE2 Remake.

Instead of typing up a very large, detailed series of complaints I will instead summarize it into a sentence:

RE3 REmake is an even more condensed and cut-content experience than the original was. If you were looking forward to the Cowboy Shotgun then you'll have to go play RE4 REmake.

Buy only if deeply discounted or through 3rd Party.

[h1]More than just an RE2 add-on.[/h1]

I can see why this isn't as highly revered as the RE2 Remake. It's shorter, it has only one campaign rather than two, Nemesis isn't as fun to deal with as Mr. X was, and the game straddles the fence between survival horror and action, and doesn't always know what it wants to be.

The interactive cutscenes feel jarring and out of place. Also, the game appears like RE2 with the same look and feel and the same gameplay mechanics (ie. typewriters, items boxes, inventory management, weapons crafting etc...), and yet it plays very differently because you're almost always moving forward to the next area, with not a whole lot of backtracking. Because of that, your surroundings never quite become a 'character' in the game in the way the RCPD did in RE2 or the Spencer Mansion did in RE1. RE3 feels more like a series of set pieces, akin to RE4 and RE5, rather than RE1 and RE2.

And yet despite those criticisms, I enjoyed this game a lot.

The visuals and sound are fantastic, there's some great enemy variety here (better than RE2), the boss fights were more fun than in RE2, and everything just felt bigger and more epic. Even though RE3 is sometimes thought of as an add-on to RE2, this is actually a bigger game in terms of scope and game assets. I wouldn't be surprised if it had a higher budget, as well. It just feels far more grandiose, in both gameplay and cutscenes.

But what RE3 lacks from RE2 is the pacing, the subtlety and nuance, and it has very few puzzles of any kind.
On the other hand, Carlos and Jill are both fantastically acted, the story here is better than it was in RE2, and the guns and weapons play are all great.

Perhaps the game deserved its criticism at launch because paying $60 for an 8 hour game isn't a great value. But now that you can find it for much cheaper (especially during Steam sales), I can unequivocally recommend RE3 Remake to just about anyone. It's a short campaign that only took me about 8 hours and I'm sure it could be done a fair bit faster, and yet I enjoyed this campaign immensely and would absolutely recommend it.

This game gets a bad reputation from RE fans in comparison to the original, but I think this is unfounded. I have played both, and I enjoyed the remake far more. I'm writing this review specifically to address the negative criticism as compared to the original.

One criticism I hear of the game cuts content. This is not untrue, but its very deceptive - it cuts and it adds. Its a full remake - the levels and stories are similar but changed. Some area have been cut completely, but they've been replaced with new areas that, in my opinion, make more sense for the game's narrative. As for the game's length - the game plays as long as the original. It might be a short game for today's standard's, but I would take a short experience full of love and care over an 100 hour content farm any day.

Another criticism I hear is that the game is too linear. It is more linear than RE2's massive puzzle box levels, but the levels still offer lots of variety and exploring and environment mastery you'd expect from an RE game. It is worth noting the original was more linear than its predecessors too. Both RE3 versions are not about mastering a single intricate space like RE1 and RE2, they are more about moving towards your goal. And that shows in both with smaller levels and more directed action.

In terms of level design, I might prefer the original by a slight margin. But the gameplay and narrative improvements in the remake are immense. The remake is more fun to play moment to moment, the narrative better conceived and paced, the character's more realized. A big criticism I had of the original was that it provided little narrative context to your gameplay goals - especially in the very beginning before you meet Carlos. You just went to the next room because it was the next room. I never felt that way in the remake.

Overall, I would give this game a 4/5 and I believe it improves on the original. However, while this game is very good, RE2 remake is still better imo. If you haven't played RE2 remake yet, pick that one up first.

Zombies have always been a staple in the entertainment industry, whether you’re talking about the Night of the Living Dead, (the grandfather of the slow-moving zombie genre) The walking dead, or the fast-moving intense action of 28 days later.  Whether it’s movies, television or the reason we’re all here video games, zombies have enthralled us for years.  The best-known zombie game is probably Resident Evil, while other games have existed, Resident Evil achieved a notoriety that no other game can manage to grab 
 
Whether your introduction to Resident Evil was back in the early days of the PlayStation 1, or you got hooked playing Resident Evil 4, one thing is certain if you play games you’ve played Resident Evil at some point in time.  This game in particular is Resident Evil 3, not to be confused with the 1999 release, this resident evil 3 was remade to better reflect modern technology and gamer habits. 
 
Story Line – Resident Evil, unlike the previous two games, has you playing a single linear storyline, while you get multiple protagonist Jill Valentine and Carlos Oliveira.  This game is set after the events of the first game and is set slightly before the events of the second game.  Jill is in her apartment waiting to leave Racoon city when all heck breaks loose.  With in a matter of minutes she’s being chased by an indestructible being known as the Nemesis.  This game was originally called Nemesis, but should have instead been called Jill Abuse Simulator, since the developers seemed to have a sick obsession with punching, kicking, throwing and slamming Jill into any and everything possible. 
 
The game features Jill and Carlos trying to escape Racoon city, traveling through multiple parts of the zombie infested city.  Will they survive?  Will Jill eventually stop being thrown into random objects?  Will Carlos ever tell Jill how he really feels? 

Gameplay – If you know you know, the game plays very close to Resident Evil 2 remake, and has fluid combat, the Nemesis chasing you during numerous parts makes the game feel more like run and gun.  Most of the core mechanics remain the same and if you enjoyed the previous remakes, you’ll enjoy this one as well.

Were it not for Code Veronica, Resident Evil 3: Nemesis would be the RE game that needed a remake the most. While it was a fun, hectic survival horror experience, it also suffered from a couple of downright unfair boss fights and puzzles (I have never managed to beat Nemesis at the clock tower without breaking his AI). It also doesn't feel as replayable as the first two entries. Hot off the heels of a smash hit in the Resident Evil 2 remake, Capcom had the opportunity to 'fix' RE3 and ensure it would be as beloved and alive in the public consciousness as the games on either side of it.

Well, now we know why Capcom calls them 'reimaginings' instead of 'remakes.'

R3make is not a bad game. It's a thrill ride with a breakneck pace and gorgeous visuals to boot. Raccoon City feels more real than ever as it burns down, and there are plenty of tense escapes to be had from the iconic Nemesis. During my first sitting, I played the game until my wrists hurt, and for a while I was convinced that the game was even better than RE2make.

Which is why I recommend finishing the game in a single session if you can; even at a relaxed pace, it should take five hours at most. If you don't, the flaws will start to show. You'll notice how much of the game revolves around wresting control from the player to deliver scripted setpieces, which while gorgeous do often veer into the routine of 'cutscene -> walk a few steps -> cutscene.' You'll notice that for some odd reason, the danger of RE2make has been cut out - it's extremely easy to tell when a zombie is truly dead here, because they stop ragdolling; Nemesis is easy to escape and only shows up when he's meant to. You'll notice the lack of open-ended exploration; organic discovery has been eschewed for tightly controlled 'moments.' And perhaps you'll get over how beautiful Jill looks in this game to realize what a cranky ♥♥♥♥♥ Capcom turned her into.

The designers giveth, and the writers taketh away. While Carlos has been granted a much-needed glow-up that transforms him from a bland stereotype into a likable co-protagonist, Jill's characterization has been butchered. Not only did she go to the Tomb Raider Reboot school of 'falling from heights the entire game,' but she's distinctly more generic and 'stock' than her previous incarnations. Her attitude during her first encounter with the Umbrella security team may be justified; the rest of the game, less so. Some of the writing, especially at the conclusion the game rushes into to keep from unravelling completely, is enough to make one wince - not charming enough to be campy, and not mature enough to be realistic.

R3make also precipitated an outcry over its omission of certain sections of the original game. I have mixed feelings about that. On one hand, it keeps the game moving along at a frenetic clip that's ideal for playing through in a single sitting. On the other, some of the cooler portions of the original RE3 have been lost. The lack of any gameplay modes besides the campaign is also a disappointment; I'm aware RE: Resistance came bundled, but I'll be reviewing that as a separate game. What I'm really asking is: where the hell is Mercenaries?

This is a fun game that controls well and looks gorgeous, but it doesn't live up to its potential. Somewhere in development, it was rushed. Unlike the first RE game's remake, which for casual players rendered the PS1 iteration obsolete, R3make feels neither definitive nor essential. I recommend buying this only at a hefty discount.

[h1]Nowhere to Run: A Heart-Pounding Escape from Raccoon City in Resident Evil 3 Remake[/h1]

Resident Evil 3 (remake) throws you headfirst into the nightmarish outbreak of Raccoon City. Reprising her role from the 1999 classic, Jill Valentine, a former S.T.A.R.S. member, fights for survival amidst the chaos. Unlike the more methodical exploration of the Spencer Mansion in the first remake, RE3 is a frantic race against time.

[h2]Story: A Desperate Escape with Unforgettable Characters[/h2]
The narrative retains the core beats of the original while injecting fresh scares and emotional depth. Jill is a fantastic protagonist – resourceful, determined, and voiced with impressive conviction by Nicole Tompkins. We see her vulnerability alongside her strength, making her a character you truly root for.

Carlos Oliveira, a U.B.C.S. mercenary Jill encounters, is another highlight. Their contrasting personalities create a dynamic duo, with Carlos offering both humor and a foil to Jill's seriousness. The remake wisely expands on Carlos's role, fleshing out his motivations and making him a more compelling character.

The story throws some curveballs at veterans of the original, keeping you on your toes. It doesn't shy away from the series' trademark horror, with grotesque enemies and unsettling environments. There's a genuine sense of desperation as Jill navigates a decaying city crawling with the undead, stalked by the relentless Nemesis.

[h2]Gameplay: A Thrilling Dance with Danger[/h2]
RE3 embraces action-oriented survival horror. Dodging and maneuvering become crucial as you face hordes of the infected. Ammo scarcity adds tension, forcing you to prioritize targets and make every bullet count. The remake streamlines some puzzles compared to the original, but they remain well-designed and integrated with the environment.

The constant threat of Nemesis elevates the gameplay. This hulking bioweapon is relentless, forcing you to adapt your strategies on the fly.  Whether it's bursting through walls or unleashing devastating tentacles, Nemesis injects a constant dose of adrenaline into the experience.

[h2]A Feast for the Eyes and Ears[/h2]
The RE Engine continues to impress. Raccoon City is a decaying metropolis brought to life in horrifying detail. The lighting effects are particularly impressive, creating a grimy, oppressive atmosphere that perfectly complements the game's horror elements. The sound design is equally top-notch, with the moans of the infected and the pounding soundtrack amplifying the tension.

[h2]Overall: A Must-Play for Horror Fans and RE Veterans[/h2]
Resident Evil 3 is a fantastic reimagining of a classic. It delivers an intense, action-packed experience with a compelling narrative and unforgettable characters. The visuals and sound design are top-notch, creating a truly immersive atmosphere. 

[b]Recommendation:  If you're looking for a thrilling escape from Raccoon City, filled with heart-pounding action and genuine scares, then grab your Jill Valentine cosplay and dive into Resident Evil 3. You won't regret it (unless, of course, you encounter Nemesis).[/b]

[h1] What does the RE3 remake offer you, and what can you offer the game? [/h1]

[h2] Meet Jill and Carlos [/h2]
Jill and Carlos are two playable characters; you play as one of them in a particular part of the story. Their mission is to escape Raccoon City before the missile strikes the city and its citizens, who have turned into zombies. They need to work together and survive all the obstacles on the way.
[h2] Meet Nemesis and company [/h2]
Nemesis will ensure you experience a nightmare. There will be times when the only thing you can do is run and try not to come into contact with him. Not to mention, you have company—zombies (different types that require different levels of damage to overcome). Sometimes they will act like abnormal titans, but they have a foot fetish and jump up when you least expect it.
[h2] Dodge master [/h2]
When an enemy is about to attack, pressing "space" (or whatever your shortcut for dodge will be) allows you to perform a dodge. This game doesn't test your shooting skills, but your instincts and demands quick responses from you.
[h2] Weapons [/h2]
Your best friends which make you feel less stressed. RE3 offers really good weapons—they sound good, they shoot well. A handgun is granted at the beginning of the game (an extra assault rifle is only available on Assisted mode), and later you can unlock a shotgun, magnum, and grenade launcher. The game is also friendly. If you miss the shotgun or grenade launcher in a certain location, it awaits you in a different location in the game.
[h2] Bonus shop [/h2]
By earning points from challenges, you can unlock useful in-game items. Infinite weapons are especially recommended in higher difficulty modes when the game is less generous with ammo and enemies are stronger.
[h2] Puzzles [/h2]
The game is not too demanding in terms of puzzles. Mostly you will have to look for technical parts. Locks and safe codes are for extra weapon upgrades or extra space, not necessary for finishing the game.

[h2] Pros and cons [/h2]

(+) Assault rifle on assisted mode makes the world more accessible and less traumatic.
(+) Various high-quality weapons.

Its a very linear than open world game funnelling the player into a specific path and whilst there is a small part where you can openly explore, there's very little to explore compared to 2, 4, 7 and Village. 

I would recommend the game if you're in the market for a small well built linear title with amazing graphics and sound built within the resident evil universe, this title will more than suit those needs.

"Resident Evil 3" holds a special place in my heart for several reasons. Firstly, its gripping storyline filled with suspense, mystery, and survival elements kept me on the edge of my seat throughout the entire gameplay. From the dilapidated streets to the eerie interiors of abandoned buildings, every environment is meticulously crafted to evoke a sense of dread and isolation. The attention to detail in bringing Raccoon City to life truly immerses players in its nightmarish world.

Furthermore, "Resident Evil 3" offers a perfect balance of action and survival horror gameplay. The strategic decision-making, resource management, and intense combat sequences kept me thoroughly engaged from start to finish. Whether I was carefully conserving ammunition or facing off against hordes of grotesque creatures, every moment felt exhilarating and rewarding.

Beyond its gameplay mechanics, "Resident Evil 3" also boasts memorable characters and a compelling narrative that kept me invested in the fate of Jill and her companions. The evolution of Jill's character as she confronts her fears and fights for survival resonated with me on a deeply emotional level.

In conclusion, my love for "Resident Evil 3" knows no bounds. It is a game that has left an indelible mark on me, not only as a fan of the survival horror genre but also as a gamer who appreciates rich storytelling and immersive gameplay experiences. I cannot recommend it highly enough to anyone seeking an adrenaline-fueled adventure into the heart of darkness.

As a remake, it fails in almost every single conceivable way that is possible. The main character has barely any personality, the supporting characters are forgettable, the villain feels slapped on at the last minute, the atmosphere is non-existent, and by far the worst part, the original namesake of the game is a complete joke. 
All of these aspects are so much better and more fleshed out in the original. Jill was an empathetic voice of reason who tried to keep everyone around her calm while still being realistic. Carlos was a charming if not dorky side character who was fun to be around. The atmosphere was dark, the city forboding. 
Out of Raccoon City, the RPD, the Clock Tower, the Park, and the Lab, 2 of them were cut, and 1 was shortened to a tiny Carlos section. Meaning this remake only contains about 22% of the original game's content. 
And that's not to mention that they completely removed the game's choice system, which they implemented to make up for the lack of multiple campaigns, further hurting the replay value.
Nemesis is an absolute joke. Honestly, it doesn't surprise me that this is the Nemesis we got in Dead by Daylight, since if they added the OG Nemesis, all of the matches would be over in 30 seconds. 
Nemesis has multiple opportunities to kill Jill, and just chooses not to. He gets stopped by a bookshelf in a cutscene, points a flamethrower directly in Jill's face and does nothing, walks super slowly, and is fully scripted with next to no RNG elements that made the original Nemesis so terrifying. 
He also transforms into a dog then into a wall. That is not what happens in the original. In the original, he mutates, yes, but those mutations make him stronger, but also more vulnerable. His original final mutation made him feel more like a dying animal desperately clinging to life. You deliberately saw the damage you were doing to Nemesis over the course of the game. In this remake, they throw all of that out the window and say "here's a sci-fi action movie set-piece, blow up the fleshy wall," BUT THEY HAD ALREADY HAD US BLOW UP A FLESHY WALL IN THE RE2 REMAKE.

The game feels too scripted. Zombies are placed along linear pathways, often surprise attacking with little chance for evasion. It really feels like there's little room for choice during gameplay. On repeat playthroughs, this linearity becomes very apparent, with many sequence feeling like a repetitive cycle of holding the W key, skipping cutscenes, and repeating this process.

The dodge mechanic feels underwhelming and almost useless outside of perfect dodges. It's often tough to time dodges for certain attacks, leading to unnecessary frustration and damage. Additionally, QTEs triggered when grabbed by zombies feel pointless, as you still take damage regardless of success, a clear step down from RE2's defensive items.

The treatment of Nemesis is disappointing. Compared to the presence of Mr. X in Resident Evil 2 Remake, Nemesis feels lackluster and scripted. The chase sequences, intended to instill fear and tension, fall flat as Nemesis's movements are hard to predict and lack the eerie audio cues that made Mr. X encounters so memorable. Instead of feeling like a relentless pursuer, Nemesis often comes across as a teleporting enemy that tentacle whips you.

[h1][b]Resident Evil 3 – Short, slick, and over before you are ready[/b][/h1]

[b]Verdict:[/b] Recommended on sale

[b]Context:[/b]
I am a survival horror fan who values pacing, replayability, and a campaign that feels complete, not rushed. I like tight encounters and memorable set pieces, but I also want enough meat on the bones to justify the time and price. I went into Resident Evil 3 Remake wanting that Raccoon City tension with Jill and Nemesis, and I got it, just in a smaller package than I would have liked.

[b]The good:[/b]
[list]
[*]Jill is a strong lead, and the game keeps her momentum moving forward.
[*]Raccoon City has great atmosphere, with that classic outbreak panic baked into the streets.
[*]Nemesis adds pressure and spectacle that keeps encounters feeling urgent.
[*]The whole campaign is brisk and easy to replay if you enjoy speedier runs.
[/list]

[b]The not so good:[/b]
[list]
[*]The biggest drawback is length, it can feel [b]too[/b] short for a full priced release.
[*]The pacing is so fast that some moments do not have time to breathe.
[*]If you want a longer survival horror journey, this may feel like it ends just as it gets going.
[/list]

[b]Who should play this:[/b]
[list]
[*]Players who want a lean, action forward survival horror campaign.
[*]Fans of Jill and the Raccoon City setting who are fine with a shorter ride.
[*]People who like replaying games for cleaner runs and faster clears.
[/list]

[b]Who should skip or wait:[/b]
[list]
[*]Players who want a long campaign with lots of exploration and downtime.
[*]Anyone sensitive to value for money, this is best when discounted.
[*]People expecting a slower, more methodical survival horror pace.
[/list]

[b]Final thoughts:[/b]
Resident Evil 3 Remake nails the vibe of a city in collapse and gives Jill a sharp, fun sprint through it. Nemesis brings the menace, the set pieces land, and the game rarely drags. The problem is it ends quickly, which makes it hard to recommend at full price. Catch it on sale and it is an easy weekend win.

Title: "Resident Evil 3 Remake: Dodging Zombies and Dodging My Own Screams"

Review:
If you've ever wanted to know what it's like to simultaneously sprint through a city overrun by zombies while also trying not to spill your coffee, Resident Evil 3 Remake has got you covered. Capcom's latest undead adventure is like a rollercoaster ride through Raccoon City, where the only thing scarier than the monsters lurking around every corner is the realization that you forgot to stock up on ammo.

Let's start with the protagonist, Jill Valentine. She's like the MacGyver of survival horror, turning every found item into a makeshift weapon with the finesse of a seasoned ninja. Seriously, forget about stocking up on rocket launchers – all you need is a trusty knife and a can-do attitude to take down those brain-hungry baddies.

And speaking of baddies, Nemesis deserves a special shoutout. This guy is like the Terminator on steroids, relentlessly pursuing you with all the determination of someone who just really wants a hug... or to rip your face off. Either way, it's hard not to admire his dedication to the art of zombie hunting.

But let's not forget about the real star of the show: Raccoon City itself. From the eerily quiet streets to the dimly lit alleyways, every corner of this urban nightmare is dripping with atmosphere. It's like a postcard from hell – if hell had a serious rat problem and a penchant for jump scares.

Of course, no Resident Evil game would be complete without its fair share of puzzles, and RE3 Remake doesn't disappoint. Whether you're deciphering cryptic codes or hunting down elusive keys, there's always something to keep your brain scratching while your trigger finger gets a workout.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 Remake is a pulse-pounding thrill ride from start to finish. With its heart-stopping action, spine-tingling scares, and enough zombie guts to fill a swimming pool, it's a must-play for any survival horror fan. Just don't forget to pack your nerves of steel – you're gonna need 'em.
