RE3 Remake:
Plus Points:
1. There are many new locations outside the RPD building in Uptown and Downtown that can be explored. The city feels vast and realistic, with the addition of shops like donut shops and drugstore that were not present in the PSX version.
2. The action and duels with Nemesis are plentiful and more challenging.
3. The antagonist character, Nicholai Ginovaef, is highlighted more in this remake, and the storyline is clearer compared to the PSX version.

Minus:
1. Many main story settings from the PSX version are eliminated in the Remake. Even if they are included, they are passed by quickly. For example, in the PSX version, there are stories in the Clock Tower and Raccoon City Park.
The sequence in PSX is : Uptown - RPD - Downtown - Clock Tower - Raccoon City Park - Hospital - Lab. 
But in the remake, it is : Uptown - RPD - Downtown - Hospital - Lab. 
The stories in the Clock Tower and Raccoon City Park are skipped and lost. The player only briefly passes in front of the Clock Tower and immediately fights Nemesis there without even entering Clock Tower at all. And there is no Racoon City Park at all like in PSX version.
2. The Live Selection feature (when encountering Nemesis and being able to choose the storyline path) is removed in this version. This feature was what made RE3 on PSX exciting, as the choices made determined different storylines.
3. Many exciting and difficult puzzles (such as the Base Vaccine puzzle in the PSX version's laboratory) are removed. The puzzles in the remake are not as challenging as in the PSX version.
4. Because Racoon City Park is not exist in this remake version, so you can't meet and fight with monster Grave Digger.

Overall 7/10

when the remake came out, I had not yet played the original. I religiously speed-ran this game as well as 100% within just days of release. I loved it. and yes, the game is fun and it is satisfying and it has at least SOME replayability (I think so anyway) but since playing the original, I despise this game so much as it genuinely could have been one of the best games of all time. This game had NEMESIS, probably one of, if not, THE most iconic RE enemy - and they removed his most iconic scene (brad death). This game could've literally done infinitely much more and I'm so disappointed. I mean the fact you see the clocktower in the distance, just to be forced to fight nemesis outside it but NEVER go in is so humiliating and I can only imagine how those who had played the original felt at that time.

My least favourite section like many others is the Carlos hospital section. This exists in the original but its not even CLOSE to as bad as this and in the original it literally lasts like 2 minutes. I feel like half of RE3 remake is just Carlos sections. I also wish Jill went into the RPD instead. I shat myself in the original when Nemesis smashed through the window of the RPD and that alone had me way more freaked out than any section of this game (and the original is/was over 2 decades old!!). I remember in RE2 remake people were theorising the hole in the shower room was Nemesis. And I was excited and hopeful for this too. But nope. Carlos just blew it up like in any old school RE puzzle fashion. Seriously? I was also hopeful for the brad death scene as that was EVERYWHERE as its such an iconic intro, but instead Brad just gets bit, dies off screen and Nemesis is revealed from the VERY beginning, before ANY zombie. The original had some sort of mystery and build up of there being something "dangerous" out there with everyone warning you before that iconic "STARS" as you see Brad, your STARS team member who was there in the first game (briefly anyways lmfao) get impaled. 

Now I like the new Carlos look and voice acting. His voice reminds me of Javier from TWD every time though (not a complaint!). AND ALSO Chris ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Redfield from Village. Why did they use the same VA?? Whenever I hear Chris in village I think of Carlos. I'm not a big fan of reusing VAs like that and not changing the voice much. Love the voice, just not on 2 big characters in the same franchise on 2 games released a year apart. 

I hate how the city section is just 2 freaking streets. Like what?? in the original you had all these allyways, streets, roads, with LOADS of buildings to go into like diners, apartments, the RPD, a press room, a bar, a gas station (which is just exploded in a cutscene in the remake), a power station, a few shops, a courtyard and probably even more that I missed. The remake was 2 streets separated by a donut shop. Come on man. And to top it all off, it was short as hell. You just needed to get power and route the train. In the original you needed to do that on top of fix the train, with fuel (not just any fuel, you needed to combine it with engine oil or something), I believe you also needed a wire and a battery. 

The failure of this remake is something I can speak to passionately about, and that's why I'm editing this today, as I did not flesh this out over 3 years ago when I wrote about it. 

All in all, this game is fairly good. But as a remake, it's horrible and overall could've been THE best RE game in the entire series. But it falls flat to mediocre. It is very very clear this game was rushed.

It's also absurdly short, linear in the bad way (complete with unskippable "walking" sections, playable cutscenes, essentially) and has absolutely no extra modes, not even the Mercenaries mode which the original game introduced to the series. A massive shame since RE3 Mercs is unlike every iteration after it, and I'm sure I'm not the only person who was sorta hoping to see if they would do a modern iteration of it. The game was notoriously rushed, like that shouldn't even be debatable anymore. It came out barely a year after RE2R, and consists of 80% assets recycled from that game. It's also like 3 hours long. So sadly, this is about as close to a cash grab as the series has come since it's renaissance with RE7. When people criticize this game, they do so because they wanted, and deserved, better. Capcom is capable of better, the 2 RE games released following this one are proof of that.

This review contains mild spoilers, beware.
I know this game has been very controversial due to the remake being worse than the original game and how lazily done it is. However, I don't think it's right to call it bad. Sure, there were a lot of missed opportunities and disappointments. But you can't deny that it also had so much improvement. The graphics and music were really good, it was thrilling and just makes you feel like you are actually in that apocalypse. The story was quite well written. The map was well designed, especially the downtown and shops. The characters are definitely something that made the game more appealing. I mean, just look at Carlos.

Now onto the things that really disappoint me: Nemesis. I have played the RE2 remake just before this and I was absolutely terrified of Mr X. The way you heard his footsteps all over the map and didn't know where he was until he suddenly found you was terrifying. According to the lore, him and Nemesis are both tyrants and Nemesis is one of the strongest tyrians ever created. This character was supposed to be a creepy stalker that didn't leave you alone through out the game. However, he was so bad that even the zombies were scarier. The first and second encounter we had was pretty good, especially the way he can enter one of the safe rooms was so unexpected and scared me to death. But the other encounters were terrible. In his first and second boss fight, he just ran around like a monkey and you had to wait until he stopped so you can shoot him and get him down. Hell, Carlos was even there to tell you which barrel he was standing behind so you can aim there. And his last boss fight was even worse. That was a huge monstrous creature but he fainted like a pillow princess just by getting shot in those orange pops. In conclusion, Nemesis was such a joke.

Onto the second thing I really didn't like about the game is how easy it is. This game is a survival horror game and the player is supposed to survive with low resource. As an example, RE2 remake Leon was a rookie cop who had his first day at his job. He had low resourse and wasn't that good at defending himself. Jill and Carlos however, they are completely over the top agents and you barely needed any resource. You could just press space and dodge attacks. The resource was also given a lot and they were so easy to find. It felt like a combat game than a survival horror game.

And the last thing I didn't like about the game was its play time. I play games very slowly, taking my time looking at every single detail, and my first playthrough took around 6 hours. I really wish it was longer.

To sum it up, this game has its ups and downs but I still recommend playing it. I bought it when it had a discount and I think it's worth its price.

"Resident Evil 3" brings the chaos of Raccoon City to life in a modern and action-packed remake. As a fan of the original and the RE series, I eagerly dove into this reimagining by Capcom, and while it delivers on many fronts, a few aspects left me with mixed feelings. PLEASE BRING RE1 and RE CV REMAKE. I WANT TO BE PART OF RE FRANCHISE.

Pros:

Stunning Visuals and Atmosphere: The RE Engine once again shines, delivering a visually impressive rendition of Raccoon City. The environments are detailed, and the ominous atmosphere is palpable, enhancing the survival horror experience.

Intense Action and Nemesis: The relentless pursuit by Nemesis adds a level of tension that keeps you on your toes. The encounters with this bioengineered monstrosity are thrilling and nerve-wracking, contributing to the overall sense of urgency. Little to Dodge is smart move.

Streamlined Controls and Gameplay: The modernized controls and gameplay mechanics make the experience accessible to both veterans and newcomers. The responsive controls add to the fluidity of combat and exploration.

Engaging Set Pieces: The set pieces and scripted events are well-executed, adding cinematic flair to the game. Moments like the escape from the city are adrenaline-pumping and showcase the game's action-oriented focus.

Cons:

Shorter Campaign: The main campaign feels noticeably shorter compared to other entries in the series. While the intense pacing contributes to the urgency, it may leave some players wanting a more extended experience. But I like it tho. expensive but shorter isnt good. Added DLC would be smart move.

Limited Exploration: The game's focus on action sometimes limits exploration. Certain areas feel more confined, and the sense of openness found in the original RE3 is somewhat diminished.

Conclusion:

"Resident Evil 3" is a visually striking and action-packed remake that successfully captures the essence of the original. While the shorter campaign and limited exploration may disappoint some fans, the intense encounters with Nemesis and the overall modernization of the classic make it a worthwhile experience.

This game tries to add some quality of life improvements over RE2, but in turn, the mechanics in question feel unnecessary, finicky, or just choppy.

This is a MUST own for any lover of survival horror.

Resident Evil 3, successfully reimagines the classic 1999 title, delivering a gripping experience that captivates players from start to finish. With 23 hours invested in this survival horror masterpiece, I can confidently say that Resident Evil 3 offers an adrenaline-pumping journey filled with intense action, clever puzzles, and a compelling storyline.

The gameplay mechanics shine, with tight controls and responsive movements that enhance the overall immersive experience. As Jill, I found the ability to dodge incoming attacks at close range to be a game-changer, adding a layer of strategy to the combat. The inclusion of Carlos Oliveira as a playable character in certain sections brought diversity to the gameplay, keeping the overall experience dynamic and engaging.

The visuals are stunning, showcasing the capabilities of the RE Engine. Raccoon City is brought to life with meticulous detail, and the character models, especially that of Nemesis, are both terrifying and impressive. The atmospheric sound design contributes significantly to the game's suspense, making every step through the desolate streets and eerie environments a nerve-wracking experience.

The primary antagonist, Nemesis, is a formidable foe that evolves throughout the game, creating a sense of constant dread and tension. The encounters with Nemesis are adrenaline-fueled, requiring quick thinking and precise shooting to survive. The variety of weapons, including customizable firearms and combat knives, adds depth to the combat system, making each encounter a strategic challenge.

The inclusion of additional difficulty modes and an item shop upon completion provides excellent replay value. Unlocking new weapons and items through completing challenges adds an extra layer of satisfaction to the overall gaming experience. The decision to tie the narratives of Resident Evil 2 and 3 more closely together enhances the sense of continuity within the Resident Evil universe.

While some locations from the original game were omitted, the rearranged storytelling and expanded dialogue contribute to a more cohesive narrative. The removal of multiple endings in favor of a focused story streamlines the experience, ensuring a more consistent and impactful narrative.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 is a stellar remake that successfully captures the essence of the original while delivering a fresh and thrilling experience for both long-time fans and newcomers to the series. With its intense action, atmospheric setting, and well-executed gameplay mechanics, Resident Evil 3 is a must-play for survival horror enthusiasts. I wholeheartedly recommend this game to fellow players, as it offers a memorable journey through the nightmare-infested streets of Raccoon City.

There are two aspects to consider when reviewing this game, through the lens of how it compares to the other resident evil remakes and how it stands as a game in general. That's where this game rightfully deserves a "Mixed" rating if it were possible so while I will ultimately recommend it, I think how you rate it should be through those lens.

Compared to the other remakes, this game is absolutely atrocious. It cuts a large amount of content and expects you to just forgive and it disrupts the pace of the story as well. It fumbles its depiction of Nemesis which really sucks when the previous game had the terrifying Mr. X. It recycles a decent handful of assets from RE2R and while on it's own seems fine, it's much more obvious when you've played the other game. Gunplay and Physics are incredibly downgraded compared to the previous title, dismemberment being removed entirely and all zombies having no collision and a fixed death animation. The story length is even outdone by the recently released RE4R Separate Ways DLC. There's zero replayability unlike the other remakes which had separate game modes and reasons to replay the story, RE3R possessing nothing of that sort. Why RE3R got shafted in it's overall development will forever remain a mystery to me.

Now as a standalone title, RE3R is a very serviceable title. For starters, the game looks REALLY good, there's absolutely no debate about that. The combat is okay, in relation to my earlier statement, it's not quite the same level of greatness of the other two but it's okay enough to have fun with. The dodge mechanic may suck compared to Leon's parry of RE4 but I mean I guess it's there if you want it. Overall, this whole game operates more like a DLC for the 2nd Remake and if you take that into consideration, you'll enjoy this very short experience. 

Just mind this, buy this on a VERY deep sale. I paid about $9 for it in the most recent Winter Sale and that's about the most fitting price for this game as a package.

RE3 is a lot of the same of RE2- good survival horror. There's only one campaign this time, but after you beat the game you unlock special features that allow you to buy exclusive weapons and other such toys to make the game spicy again. I didn't really play with any of those things since it's still playing the same map over again at the end of the day, but i'm sure others will appreciate the option.

I have a few nitpicks with some of the enemy designs having instant kill moves in confined spaces / spaces with multiple enemies, as the resulting deaths felt cheap rather than fair and my mistake, but it only happens in about three areas so it's not super prevalent or anything. 

Another slight issue is that perfect dodges / perfect punches weren't referenced anywhere where I could see them and I had to look up how they worked online rather than ingame, which is a little annoyingly obtuse for a feature that provided the dopamine peaks for my experience.

Really would've liked a Carlos mode since decking lickers out of the air was awesome and Jill's a lot more boring in comparison when you have to play as her again, but apparently RE4 remake has more of that perfect-counter goodness so i'm looking forward to that.

Here’s a tale from the real world about Resident Evil 3.

I played the original Resident Evil 3 when I was  a kid,  it was the absolute fear that made me put the game away and never thought of going through with it again. It was too much for a 10 year old child who wasn’t ready for the journey at that time.

Then time flied to my high school days. One day, I carried the old RE 3 secretly in my handbag to an IT class in school, planned to continuously accomplish my classified mission that I dropped off a long time ago. Unfortunately the most naughty classmate in my class found what I was doing and decided to stick his nose to my top-secret operation which no one else supposed to involve. So we made a deal. I let him play a little in exchange for not reporting me breaking discipline back to the class tutor. Sounds like Jill works with Carols in real world, huh? Not exactly like you'd imagined. 

Just like most of the innocents who never in contact with a RE game in their lives, he was soon overwhelmed and terrified by Nemesis and its lethal fellows who were lurking in Raccoon city and chasing him like witch hunters. He almost shxt his pants while trying to survive.

The story didn't end here. Later on, I was surprised this didn’t make him give up the game. On quite the opposite, he was stealthy taking Nemesis head on in front of the police station ever since, using the computer in class when day classes were over and no one was around(*we were in a boarding school, students had plenty of time after school when classes were over).

I shock my head every time I saw it. I thought the boy was a lost cause. It was my fault not over preparing myself and took him to the dangerous Raccoon City where he wasn’t ready for and obviously, it was too much for him. I didn’t know what the evil Nemesis had done to him, but he was obsessed about chasing Nemesis down ever since his first contact with it and the game probably didn’t expect this to happen either.

Back to the present day, I won’t say RE 3 Remake is a bad game, it’s quite good by the modern gaming standards in fact, a little short of course.
The problem is: it’s quite different from the old RE 3. They're like twins. Despite it’s hard to tell the difference by the looks of them, the personalities are not the same, you recognised it immediately by talking to them a little. If this makes sense?

To me, the old RE 3 is terrifying and challenging while RE 3R in the other hand, is a date sim with Nem Nem while he refused giving up the idea of bringing his grenade launcher to my party. Both games had done something brilliant which the other is lack of at some point. 

The old RE 3 produces the stress and terror of holding scarce resources while fighting off life or death situations, meanwhile, seeking a way to progress the story with super model figured Miss V, is real and an unique experience none like any other. The game is lack of considerations of a modern game and serious at it's best. The extreme tension it created is also something you wouldn’t experience in another game besides itself. Of course, if you don’t mind funny square heads and arms which work more like a cure in game nowadays to ease your strain a little.

The new RE 3 however, is a more balanced game which Capcom lowed down some difficulties here and there to suit more new comers while delivering the ultimate cinematic visuals that only a well made modern game is capable of achieving nowadays.

Despite it’s still a pity that Capcom never officially releases a digital copy of the original RE 3 anywhere in the world which the new RE 3 can’t replace. It is one kind of gems that you don’t want to miss as a gamer.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
An okay remake of the original PS1 Resident Evil 3, with similar story and gameplay, but with updated graphics. The game retains the "arcadey" feel of the original which is something to look forward to. However, a lot of content were removed and changed till you can barely compare to the original game. The game itself is exceptionally short and has way too many scripted events, feeling as if you're playing a visual novel game, rather than an action oriented game.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
It is a remake of the classic arcade game and generally a survival horror third-person shooter game where you play as Jill Valentine and Carlos Oliveira. Players must explore the environment to open doors and locks in order to proceed and/or upgrade equipment. Puzzles are required to be solved to gain access to areas and unlock equipment, since equipment and storage is scarce, players need to constantly manage their inventories.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
The graphics is extremely good and light, an obvious upgrade from the original PS1 game.

[h1]Audio[/h1]
Music and audio is relatively good, especially when using THX Surround.

[h1]Controls[/h1]
Controls are realatively easy and fine tuned both for Controller and on Keyboard+Mouse

[h1]Bugs & Issues[/h1]
1. Animation and movement is very janky as it will make you wonder, why would any character move like that?
2. Your "Sprinting" feels extremely slow, more like a slow jog, killing the mood of the entire game due to no sense of urgency
3. No bugs for the game found so far

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Overall an okay game, the only reason to get this game is nostalgia, as even re-playing the game feels more of a chore as it is too short with limited rewards. Players can actually finish the game less than 2 hours which is saying something (even some Demo games are longer, that is saying something), get this game only when on sale.

The Remake of 'Resident Evil 3' is still controversial. After playing the remake of the fourth instalment, I want to state that the negative bias seems hardly justified.
I recommend this game to virtually everyone who likes Survival Horror and Action Adventures - if you don't mind the horror aspect. There are some nasty and gruesome scenes in this game. The presentation is virtually flawless. And I think that is what matters here: The developers had a clear vision of how to modernize this game that has become absolutely unplayable on modern platforms. They cut some content, and they changed the atmosphere a bit to bring RE3 in line with RE0-RE6 which you can play now in a single uninterrupted line of game experiences.
What has been lost in terms of old charm and appeal is compensated by throwing out the cheesiness and silliness of the original dialogue, cutscenes and plot elements as well. Nothing shows this better than a comparison to the remake of 'Resident Evil 4' which definitely suffers from tacked-on action-sequences (the cave-segment is the worst offender) and the pirate-themed playground areas. [h3] I paid £5 for this and you should not spend more than £10 on Resident Evil 3 Remake.[/h3]

Resident Evil 3 for the PlayStation is my favorite out of the series. I remember going through the city, businesses, alleyways, parks, etc. It's truly in my personal opinion one of the best experiences on the PlayStation 1. When the announcement was made for RE3R, It was only a couple of months AFTER the release of Resident Evil 2 Remake. Immediately I knew this game would be rushed and have little development time. Only 1 year after the RE2 Remake release, we got RE3 Remake. 

Is this remake good? Well, It's not worth £40+ and it's not better than RE2R...but it's a fun okay game.  

It's very hard to NOT make a comparison to the PS1 version. The remake is missing around 2/3 of the content from the PS1. In the Remake, We're missing the crows, graver digger boss, spiders, and the brain suckers. Instead, they've given us more scripted nemesis encounters, head-parasite zombies, pale-head zombies, lickers from RE2, and an upgraded hunter that will insta-kill you even if you had full health. This isn't bad but it isn't good either. It's more like the bare minimum compared to the last games. 

They did expand on the sewer and gave an upgrade to one very intimidating hunter version. I can tell that the devs have tried to give an updated/modern version to some elements in this game and try to offer a different spin. There is JUST enough for this Resident Evil 3 to be its own thing. 

The Remake City is too linear. I don't feel like I am in a giant city compared to the PS1 version with multiple alleyways, bars, stores, etc. I would've liked for the remake to take advantage of a city that is full of zombies. Like maybe one street is too dangerous, but there are alleyways or maybe cutting through different buildings to get past would've been great. Maybe If I've cleared one street of zombies. In 5 minutes, a new horde will arrive. 

The game looks amazing and I have no serious problems with the characters. I guess my only nitpick would be the antagonist. Without too many spoilers, he is not great or memorable compared to a lot of villains in the RE universe. He's not intelligent or smartly written out. He has the typical motive that you've seen in other media. 

Nemesis is a MASSIVE let-down compared to the previous version and with MR X in RE2R. In the PS1, Nemesis is stalking you and can appear anywhere. He was a boss that would ruin your day. You had to run away from him because he was a tough SOAB. In the Remake, [spoiler] just chuck a grenade at him and he's down. [/spoiler].  

It's missing a lot of features from the PS1 and RE2 Remake. This should've been DLC rather than a standalone release. This game is still a fun and okay experience. There are plenty of unlockables and replay value. There are speed run challenges and ranks that I will jump back in to retry. I completed it in 4 hours in-game on my first attempt. This is why you should NOT pay full price.  

Despite my criticism. This game is good enough for one weekend. I'm a fan of Resident Evil and had an okay time playing this. I will jump back into it in the future. But If I know if I bought this on release. I would not have been happy. It's JUST good enough that I believe anyone can play this and have a good time.

Couple of reasons why this got so much hate was because of all the cut content from the original game, the campaign here was also incredibly short in comparison to RE:2 and the multiplayer included I think as a consolation was pretty much DOA, very bare bones, abandoned and plagued with cheaters.
This absolutely sucks balls, because the gameplay here is pretty much just RE:2 all over again, which isn't a bad thing because that game played very, very well - hell, this comes with a few new mechanics, like actual dodging, with a risk-reward system for you to also time your doges perfectly which takes a little to get used to and learn the timing of. That, plus your knife becomes more of a tool here than a last resort line of defence.
There's a lot of cool weapons here, crafting and looting is pretty much all the same here, and the map is a little more spaced despite being (obviously) linear, which works great for the gameplay and the new dodging mechanic, however it doesn't have the same horror charm to it as the cramped spaces and corridors of the RPD, not a massive problem for me, but definitely a notable change.
Did I mention how fu****g short the campaign here is? I have played the previous remake a good few times for leisure and I acquired a little over 40h just replaying that game like maybe 3.5 times, with some additional "fu****g around time" yet here in RE:3 I played that game through I think twice, and boom - a little over 7h xD 
Again, why play this extremely inferior version of RE:2 when you can just play RE:2 instead? Probably for the same or less money too. 
The most heartbreaking thing for me was the Nemesis, which on paper sounds so much scarier and overpowered than Mr. X could ever dream to be, buuut... He only really appears in some scripted events, to otherwise just hang around the same areas. He technically has a lot of tools in his arsenal, like the tentacle which he can use to not only slow you down but also travel extremely fast himself, in addition to being able to run and use some crazy weapons like a fricking bazooka or a flamethrower, like DAMN! In conclusion, it's RE:2 with a few new additions, mostly unchanged core, uninteresting campaign and for the same amount of money. Don't Play Resident Evil: 3 just stick to the 2

[h2] GOOD [/h2]  
[list]  
[*][b] Jill’s Apartment [/b]

[h2] BAD [/h2]  
[list]  
[*][b] Baffling Changes and Cuts [/b]  
Crucial locations and items from the original are pointlessly reworked or omitted—the police station sequence, watch tower, and more. The iconic “You want S.T.A.R.S.? I’ll give you S.T.A.R.S.!” line gets tossed out with barely any weight.

Without stopping to explore, the game is painfully short—there’s little substance to offset the quick runtime.

Too much was left on the cutting room floor. The remake feels stripped, with entire sections, puzzles, and encounters missing compared to the original.  
[/list]  

[h2] Final Thought [/h2]  
Resident Evil 3 Remake is a letdown for dedicated fans. It comes off as a rushed attempt to quiet the community—offering less content and a faster, shallower story. Having not played the original Resident Evil 3, I can say this game is definitely a fun game but is it better than RE2R? That's still up for debate. Most of the complaints for this game were the contents which are cut from the original, I can't have a say on that as I never played the original before so this review will be solely based on my experience in on the Resident Evil 3 Remake.

Starting off, the graphic is absolutely stunning and easily able to hold in own even in today's standard. The best part is it's well optimized and throughout my entire gameplay, I did not once encountered any stutters. The RE Engine is a work of wonder for sure. Similar to it's predecessor RE2R, the gameplay is linear and overall gameplay doesn't change must from previous game with the exclusion of few new in-game weapons and mechanics remains largely the same. There's few new types of enemies for sure but the concept are roughly the same. I'm not sure if it's just me but I felt that the gameplay for RE3R is much more refine and even the combat and dodges are more fluid than the previous game. The game's action sequences and boss fights are also more engaging than previous one and Nemesis is definitely a heck lot stronger than Mr. Stalker. Everything about this game for me as a whole is really fun but the story however could've been expanded more as it felt quite short and some plot points could've been utilized better. The game focuses more on action and less on horror elements. This isn't the case for RE2R as you might get chased around by Mr. X. In this game however, if you are to get chase. Usually it'll end up with a boss fight.

Another Improvement over the initial remake is that it's soundtrack and music are much better tailor for it's environment now. I really like the safe room music and when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan, the music changes too. This gives a much more tense feeling compare to previous game. Some other minor changes include how knife works. Now you don't need to collect them anymore as it'll be included in your inventory and won't be broken like previous game. This works well especially if you're on harder difficulty where bullets are really limited. However, the knife does deal less damage when compared to previous game. The graphics of the surrounding environment is also one of the highlights of the game. The entire hospital gameplay is really enjoyable.

Overall I definitely enjoyed this game despite it's minor flaws. However I do believe you can get this game when it's on discount because it'll be more worth that way as the gameplay hours and replayability doesn't really justify it's pricing. There's however the optional multiplayer game mode but let's be honest, ain't no way anyone is buying this game for that. I would give this game a solid [b]7.5/10[/b]. The puzzles and action element of the game is definitely the highlight and overall a good remake from Capcom.

The other fatal flaw is Capcom halting any further production on would-be DLC or even a Director's Cut with more content added after listening to fan feedback.

Long story short, pretty good game, very bad remake. Buy it if you love Resident Evil and don't mind a rather short action romp with Resident Evil's resident queen, Jill Valentine. Even if you're not the biggest fan, the game is still worth the price when it's on sale.

Every minute spent playing this remastered version feels like a thrilling trip down memory lane, but with the polish and sophistication of contemporary gaming standards.

Capcom's attention to detail in the remaster is commendable. The reimagined Raccoon City is more vibrant and terrifying than ever, filled with meticulously rendered environments that enhance the game's tense and eerie atmosphere. The updated character models, particularly of the protagonist Jill Valentine, are impressively realistic, adding depth to the narrative and engagement in the gameplay.

Moreover, the game's pacing and action have been expertly tweaked to suit modern gaming sensibilities. The balance between horror, action, and puzzle-solving remains as compelling as ever, ensuring that both longtime fans and newcomers to the series find the experience exhilarating. Resident Evil 3 Remastered is not just a remake; it's a masterful reimagining that pays homage to its roots while standing tall as a modern-day classic in its own right.

- - - Annoying Tid Bits - - -

* Priced at £32.99 full price (At Reviewers Date), and a playtime of 4 hours, that's £8.20 per hour of "fun". Think about that.

* I haven't played RE2 Remake in some time, but I am 99% sure that a great deal of assets used in RE3 have been taken from RE2. From a AAA game company, I would expect better than some cookie cutter nonsense.
* Chucking in another team deathmatch game to add as filler is just about all the proof you need in this company's confidence in this product. There is none!

- - - How To Fix This (Hindsight) - - -

* Scrap the team deathmatch game, and instead add a Mercenaries mode in the base game. +Adds replayability, possible multiplayer interaction, and a chance to introduce a faster paced gamemode for those particular players into that kind of thing.
* Adding new content on top of the original remake. A few more levels, including the original game's missing levels. +Adds surprise to those diehard original fans that know every inch of the original game with these new levels. It also fills up the game's runtime, and fixes the atrocious pacing between the final boss battles.
* Adding more puzzles. I thought RE was a mix of action and puzzle solving, but I didn't find it here. +Adds runtime and engaging player experience.
* New assets. Simple as that. I expect a few assets from previous games of course, but not this many.

Capcom's Resident Evil 3 Remake, released in 2020, brings the harrowing events of Raccoon City to life with a modern twist. While not without its differences from the original, the game successfully revitalizes the classic survival horror experience, offering a relentless and action-packed journey through chaos and terror.

One of the immediate strengths of Resident Evil 3 Remake is its visual prowess. The detailed environments, character models, and atmospheric lighting contribute to a stunningly realistic portrayal of Raccoon City in the throes of a zombie apocalypse. The transition to the over-the-shoulder perspective, introduced in Resident Evil 2 Remake, continues to enhance the immersive and dynamic nature of the gameplay.

The narrative centers around Jill Valentine's desperate attempts to survive the viral outbreak and escape the clutches of the relentless bioweapon, Nemesis. While the narrative adheres to the core of the original game, some fans may find the streamlined storyline and certain omissions to be a departure from the more intricate plot of the original Resident Evil 3. However, the character development, voice acting, and pacing maintain a high standard, providing an engaging experience for both newcomers and longtime fans.

Gameplay mechanics retain the strategic resource management and tension-inducing combat found in the series. The addition of more dynamic encounters with Nemesis introduces an element of unpredictability, keeping players on edge as they navigate the perilous streets of Raccoon City. The inclusion of dodge mechanics adds a layer of skill-based evasion to the gameplay, offering players more agency in avoiding danger.

The cityscape of Raccoon City is impressively realized, with detailed locations and interconnected pathways offering a sense of exploration. The integration of puzzles and environmental challenges complements the survival horror atmosphere, though some players may feel that the game leans slightly more toward action than horror compared to its predecessor.

Resident Evil 3 Remake boasts the same high-quality audio design found in its predecessor, with haunting musical scores and chilling sound effects enhancing the overall atmosphere. The attention to detail in environmental storytelling and creature design contributes to the game's immersive horror experience.

While the game received praise for its intense action sequences, some fans may express disappointment in the relatively shorter duration of the main campaign compared to Resident Evil 2 Remake. Additionally, the absence of certain iconic locations and scenarios found in the original may leave purists longing for more faithful recreations.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 Remake is a thrilling and visually stunning addition to the Resident Evil franchise. While it may deviate in some respects from the original, it successfully captures the essence of survival horror while introducing modern gameplay elements. The relentless pursuit of Nemesis, combined with the chaotic backdrop of Raccoon City's downfall, makes for an intense and gripping experience that should satisfy fans of the series and newcomers alike.

This game stands as a thrilling and intense installment in the iconic series. The game's storyline is gripping, weaving a narrative that keeps you on the edge of your seat without spoiling any surprises. It's a solid 8 out of 10 for its plot – there's a perfect blend of horror, suspense, and action, ensuring that the story remains engaging throughout.

When it comes to gameplay, Resident Evil 3 offers a balanced and challenging experience. It scores a 7 out of 10 in this department. The controls are responsive and intuitive, making navigation and combat feel smooth. Although there's room for improvement in some areas, the overall gameplay mechanics are solid and contribute to an immersive gaming experience.

The graphics in Resident Evil 3 are nothing short of impressive. With a 9 out of 10 rating, the game shines in its visual presentation. The attention to detail in the environments, character models, and lighting effects creates a hauntingly realistic world that enhances the overall horror atmosphere. The graphic fidelity is top-notch, contributing significantly to the immersive and eerie feel of the game.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 is a commendable remake that lives up to the legacy of the series. It blends a compelling story, engaging gameplay, and stunning graphics to deliver an experience that both fans and newcomers to the series will appreciate.

I'll keep it short about the things I, as well as I imagine thousands of other players, don't like. Or hate, whatever.

1. Cut out content. Well, imagine waiting for your favorite moments to be presented in a glorious remake, only to find that they have been cut out. I wouldn't mind them being reimagined, but there's a lot of stuff missing. I would love to get that extra stuff as DLC, let it be my loss, but Capcom, just get to work and do it right.

2. The most iconic boss, Nemesis. I was scared of the original Nemesis as a kid, and I still am. The new Nemesis? He is not scary, he is not dangerous, he feels like just another boss you see in every video game. Every encounter with him in the original game was stressful, but in remake, even while playing for the first time, it was "meh". To the point that I feel like Mr. X is more scary in RE2 Remake. Such a shame.

3. The Raccoon City. In the OG there were a lot of places to explore. The remake feels like they have shrunk the map and it feels really small.

4. Replayability. Even if you go for all the challenges, achievements, and earning "S" on all the difficulties, it won't take you much time. I won't get into RE Resistance, that's another story.

5. The original costume as paid DLC? That's just pathetic. It should be unlockable for beating the game on hardest difficulty, not behind a paywall. Also, the costume looks worse it was in OG RE3.

Even though it's the worst Resident Evil remake Capcom has released so far, it's still a solid game and I like playing it. It just won't be at the top of my personal ranking of RE games. That's about it.

Resident Evil 3, the latest installment in Capcom's iconic survival horror series, is a relentless rollercoaster of terror that will have your heart pounding from start to finish. As a longtime fan of the franchise, I couldn't wait to dive into Raccoon City once again, and Resident Evil 3 did not disappoint. 

First and foremost, the visuals are nothing short of breathtaking. Raccoon City has never looked so hauntingly beautiful, and the attention to detail in every decaying building and blood-splattered alley is a testament to the developers' dedication. The atmosphere is thick with tension, and the lighting effects add an extra layer of realism that immerses you in the apocalyptic nightmare.

Resident Evil 3 maintains the series' signature survival horror gameplay while introducing some exhilarating new elements. The over-the-shoulder perspective feels intuitive, and the controls are responsive, allowing for precise aiming when confronted by grotesque monstrosities. The addition of the dodge mechanic adds a layer of strategy to encounters, but timing is crucial, making every escape a heart-stopping experience.

"Resident Evil 3 Remake" is a comprehensive reimagining of the 1999 survival horror classic, "Resident Evil 3: Nemesis." This modernized version maintains the core essence of the original while delivering a fresh and thrilling experience. Here's an extensive review of why gamers should consider adding this title to their must-play list.

Visual and Audio Presentation:
The game inherits the impressive graphical prowess of the RE Engine used in the "Resident Evil 2 Remake," bringing Raccoon City to life with stunningly realistic visuals. The attention to detail in the environment, the character models, and the gruesome design of the creatures make for an immersive horror spectacle. The atmospheric sound design, from the groans of distant zombies to the explosive ordinance of the titular Nemesis, further pulls players into the game's terrifying world.

Story and Characters:
"Resident Evil 3 Remake" follows Jill Valentine, a former S.T.A.R.S. officer, as she navigates the zombie-infested ruins of Raccoon City. The narrative expands on the original plot, giving more context to Jill's character and fleshing out the story with cinematic cutscenes and interactions. The game also intersperses moments featuring Carlos Oliveira, providing an alternate perspective and gameplay experience.

Gameplay and Mechanics:
Capcom evolved the gameplay from the "Resident Evil 2 Remake," offering a faster-paced experience that aligns with Jill's character as a seasoned combatant. The addition of a dodge mechanic allows for more dynamic encounters with enemies and gives players a fighting chance against the relentless Nemesis. The game is more action-oriented, with plentiful resources and more opportunities for combat compared to its predecessor.

The Nemesis System:
The Nemesis, an unstoppable bio-weapon pursuing Jill throughout the game, is a highlight. This towering adversary has been reworked to be more terrifying than ever, with improved AI and unpredictable appearances that keep the tension high. His presence is a constant reminder of the stakes and adds urgency to the gameplay.

Exploration and Puzzles:
While "Resident Evil 3 Remake" streamlines some aspects of exploration compared to the original, it still offers a satisfying balance of combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving. The puzzles are intuitive and engaging, providing a respite from the action and rewarding logical thinking and observation.

Replayability:
The game encourages replayability through unlockables, difficulty settings, and challenges that offer rewards. Completing the game unlocks the shop where players can purchase powerful weapons and helpful items, incentivizing multiple playthroughs to acquire everything.

Production Value:
"Resident Evil 3 Remake" boasts high production values, from the quality of the voice acting to the fluidity of the animations. This polish extends to the user interface and overall design, creating a cohesive and user-friendly experience.

Tightened Experience:
The game streamlines the experience of the original, resulting in a more focused narrative and pacing. This approach may divide some fans of the original's more expansive exploration, but it also makes for a game that respects the player's time and keeps the adrenaline pumping from start to finish.

In conclusion, "Resident Evil 3 Remake" delivers a high-octane horror experience that successfully modernizes a classic. With its exceptional presentation, updated gameplay mechanics, and the ever-present threat of Nemesis, it offers both fans and newcomers a compelling adventure through the zombie apocalypse. While some may miss the depth of exploration from the original, the remake's cinematic flair and relentless pace make it a thrilling and worthy entry into the Resident Evil series.

So having JUST finished playing the game for the first time (haven't done any replays yet as of this writing), I must say... Resident Evil 3 Remake ended up being a big letdown for me in the end. I still had enough fun playing the game to finish it without it feeling like a chore to do so, and to be fair the game definitely HAS a few good things going for it (good soundtrack, immersive-looking world, a couple tweaks to some of RE2R's gameplay mechanics such as removing knife durability and adding a dodge mechanic that feels better than the original RE3's, and a couple good tension-inducing set-pieces such as the substation and several of the early in-game Nemesis chases, to name a couple examples), but sitting here reviewing the entire package now that I'm done playing it, my first impressions of the entire thing are mixed to negative, especially when viewing it as a remake of Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. 

In a nutshell, as a game that serves as a follow-up to Resident Evil 2 Remake I feel it's a letdown that doesn't measure up to it's overall more-polished predecessor, even if I admit the game is arguably fun enough on it's own depending on your mindset when playing the game... as a GAME. It's not a bad game to PLAY by any stretch, but it's a definite downgrade to everything the developers of RE2R had going for THEIR game, which still managed to keep most of the soul of the original RE2 as a survival horror game where you explore several complex, isolated locations with limited resources intact... which is more than I can say for RE3R, which on the whole feels closer to being a toned-down version of RE6 with an altered, compressed version of RE3's story than it does the original RE3, a game which cranked up the action from the original RE2 but was still at it's core a classic survival horror game similar to it's predecessor back in the day, albeit in a more open world (for the first half of that game, at least). 

Now, as a REMAKE of Resident Evil 3: Nemesis for the PlayStation 1... RE3R was simply awful. There's so much wrong with it in this respect that I feel that I could easily make my own dedicated video on the subject comparing this remake to the original on just this aspect alone, if I really wanted to. A short summary of things that come to the top of my mind, as of me having just finished the game, are as follows: Half the original game's content is missing (no clock tower, park, Dead Factory, most of Raccoon City's streets and buildings you get to explore are gone, no construction zone, the Gravedigger boss is completely gone, etc., etc..), a good bit of what DOES remain story/content-wise has been changed up in ways that feels inferior to the original more often than not, the changes in characterization feels like a mixed bag across the board (I do NOT like the changes to Jill and Nikolai's characters in this game, while everyone else I'm either neutral on or have no particular preference when compared to their original counterparts. Brad is the only character whose changed characterization I actually feel is an overall improvement from his original portrayal), the choice mechanic from the original game that influences how the story/game progressed is entirely absent (which was the source of most of the original RE3's replayability, but not here - apparently you play through RE3R once and you've already experienced everything the game's story has to offer), and they reduce the titular monster of the original game into a joke compared to his original incarnation -- one that the other characters treat more as an annoyance than a serious deadly threat to be feared (he isn't reduced to a joke in just story, either -- for most part he's been made into a joke during gameplay, too -- he's far less difficult than he was in the original game overall.). I'm just sitting here amazed at how much this game utterly failed to not only live up to my expectations as a follow-up to RE2R, but especially as a remake to one of my favorite games in the series. 

The game was arguably at it's best during the first 1/4, maybe a bit beyond that -- but once I defeated the Nemesis in his first actual boss battle, it seems like the overall quality of the game started to take a nosedive and kept going down all the way until the credits started to roll... which makes it quite frustrating for me because for that first quarter of the game I felt that I could see little hints of what this game COULD have been like if it had been given some more polish, but unfortunately a world where we got a remake of RE3 with a similar level of polish to the RE2 Remake is NOT the world we're living in right now.

So in conclusion, I'd recommend anyone who's looking into getting into the Resident Evil series to stick to the original game and avoid this remake -- the original is a far better game overall than this remake is, IMO. But if you absolutely MUST try this game for yourself, then get it on sale because I don't think RE3R has enough going for it to justify paying for it full-price... and even then I would STILL avoid playing it until AFTER you've played through the original Resident Evil 3 shortly beforehand, so that way you can experience all the differences from the original game for yourselves. But if you choose to think of and play RE3R as just a follow-up to RE2R instead of comparing it to the original game, then while it certainly could be a lot better... you could also do a lot worse than RE3R.

TL;DR Do not buy this game for any reason for any price. I’m not even joking - it’s that bad, mostly due to being 4 hours long at most, which is neither worth the full price nor the price it goes for on sale (10 bucks). Play the original. 

Earlier this year, I was greatly sick for a week. After recovering, I decided as a bit of a personal joke to myself to purchase this game while it was on sale for $10. I'd heard what people had said about it - It sucks as a remake, it's way too short, all that. But I did it anyway because I wanted more REmake gameplay and I saw no more fitting time to get some. 

Yeah, that was a mistake. 

Despite only being 10 bucks, this is one of the dumbest purchases of my life, and I am a clown for willingly, knowingly walking into this trap. I underestimated just how bad this game was and in how many ways it fails as a remake. 

I'll start with saying: I did get my wish - I got more REmake gameplay. Cool, nothing wrong there. Everything else though? Well, I'll summarize the main points: A hilariously inept and nonthreatening Nemesis, cut *important* content, references to the original being halfhearted at best, and overall a game so short that it isn't even worth buying on sale. I'll elaborate on each.

Nemesis: This guy is supposed to be a better, more threatening version of Mr. X from RE2 (a role he fulfills reasonably well in the original). Yeah no, he isn't - he only appears in scripted events, chases you for like maybe 5 seconds in gameplay, and the game gives you grenades to throw at him which will down him instantly if you really want him to stop his lackadaisical pursuit of you. In fact, that purpose is the sole reason why those grenades exist. In cutscenes, he also has Jill dead to rights multiple times, but manages to somehow ♥♥♥♥ it up despite being what is supposed to be an unstoppable, ruthless killing machine, and additionally gets stopped by the most basic of means. At the very start of the game, he breaks through a wall like the kool-aid man, but no more than 20 seconds later, he can’t break through a locked door with one punch. Oh, and to quote Jill herself in this game: [spoiler]"♥♥♥♥♥ can't even swim."[/spoiler] This Nemesis sucks and is not a threat whatsoever. If anything, you'll laugh at how bad he is at his job. 3make Nemesis dreams of being a tenth of the threat that 2make Mr. X is.

Cut content: Honestly, some content being cut from the original is fine, because not *everything* was important. For example, I don't care about the gravedigger being cut (he was a dumb boss anyway), but cutting the clock tower and Jill going to the police station? That's two vital moments of the game cut for...What reason exactly? Worse yet on both points (spoilers if you care): [spoiler] Carlos is the one who goes to the police station on a sidequest, but Jill, the STARS member, doesn't. As for the clock tower, you actually see it in the distance and you read a little informative pamphlet about it, but do you actually go there? LOL no. [/spoiler]

References to the original: Aside from the above, this game is desperate to prove that it knows it knows its original counterpart. There's a number of things from the original that are just kinda...there...and serve no real purpose other than to exist and delude the player into thinking they’re playing a real remake. "Haha, I promise we played the original RE3 guys, see? Look at my neat references!" Aside from the things mentioned already, one of the more glaring of these halfhearted references is Jill's "You want stars!?" line in this game, which is delivered at a really bad time instead of at the end of the game when Nemesis dies for good. You can tell the line was inserted randomly out of obligation because they knew people would notice and complain about its absence, but if it was going to be used at an improper moment, then it would have been preferable to have it absent. Come to think of it, "made out of obligation" actually describes this entire game's existence well.

As if the game didn't have enough problems, it is *short*, with very little if any replayability (I wonder why). I bought it on sale for 10 bucks and still felt robbed, and it is insulting that they tried to sell this garbage for full price. Obviously, they didn't try to hide the fact that this game was a cash grab in the wake of RE2make's success. 

In case it isn’t obvious, no, you shouldn’t buy this game. Being generous, it's worth 1 dollar per amount of play time, which comes out to 4 dollars at most, but aside from the fact that it will never be that cheap, to be blunt, I'd say it's barely worth a penny. I'd say this is the worst RE title by far...Or at least I would were it not for the fact that I'm going to pretend this game just doesn't exist. 

I have so many more problems with this game that it's difficult to list and expand on all of them, but I've tackled the key points, so I think you get the gist. The game sucks as a remake, is mediocre as a game, and too short to be sold as a full fledged game. 

Play the original. This game isn't worth buying even on sale.

[h1] The Good [/h1]

I played the The original RE3 on PS1, so this review is a combination of both comparison, and a fresh take. Resident Evil 3 remake immediately captivates with explosive intensity and some of the best action in the series, drawing players in from the start.The game successfully modernizes the experience of the original Resident Evil 3, creating an even more intense and exhausting gameplay. The graphical realism achieved through Capcom's RE Engine adds a remarkable level of detail to each character's performance, enhancing the overall immersion.



[hr][/hr]

[h1] The Bad [/h1]

• The focus on action and danger, while fitting for Resident Evil 3, may disappoint fans who prefer the anxiety and dark exploration elements present in other titles of the series.
• The remake's deviation from the original plot structure, omitting key decision points and multiple paths, makes it a slightly more limited experience and reduces replayability.
• Some enemies in the game can kill in a single strike, and certain encounters feel punishing, potentially frustrating players who prefer a more balanced challenge.
• The overall game duration, especially on an initial playthrough, is relatively short, ranging from 4-6 hours, which might be considered brief for some players.



[hr][/hr]

[h1] The Ugly [/h1]

• The change in the plot structure distances the remake from the original, impacting the potential for a more expansive and satisfying narrative experience.
• The lack of branching paths and decisions reduces the opportunity for players to shape the story through their choices, limiting the overall impact of player agency.
• The absence of unique endings based on player decisions, a departure from the original, diminishes the sense of consequence and variety in the narrative.
• The game's action-focused approach may alienate fans who were drawn to the series for its survival horror elements, potentially leading to a divided audience.

People love to hate this game. It's not perfect for sure, there's definitely room for improvement. But it's nowhere near as bad as people make it out to be. Not at all denying there are reasons to dislike it, but that depends on where your focus is. If those people would (pardon my french) get their heads out of their asses, they'll see there are more reasons to love this game than to hate it.

First of all, the game is NOT short. Look at speedrunner times, and you'll see even if by mere minutes, remake IS longer. The reason it feels short is because it is too linear. There is very little backtracking, and not a whole lot of challenging puzzles. That is pretty much all that this game is lacking.

In the original game, you would reach the cable car after clearing the Uptown and Downtown maps. Then you would need to get the car running. Remake starts at this exact point, so we can safely say we have those 2 maps removed. I'm not defending that they were probably forced to do this in order to meet deadlines. I (and pretty much everyone else too I reckon) would have gladly waited for another year, or 2, even 3, to get the absolute best game that we could have gotten. There's too much wasted potential here. You can see this in the game. There were clearly great ideas on the table. And some made it through, but unfortunately, the rest didn't.

But I still love this game. There may be heavy bias on my part because Jill is my absolute favorite character in the series, and my childhood hero. I've recently passed 400 hours in the game, and I enjoyed every minute of it. Sure Inferno Nemesis keeps pissing me off royally. But I like the challenge. There's nothing my Jill can't accomplish.

The game is not a frame by frame reworking of the original, unlike 1 and 2. There are a lot of changes and creative differences. Clock Tower is gone, but now you have the Sewers. Dead Factory is gone, but now you have Nest 2. Park is gone, but now you have an underground section of the Hospital - Hospital, which now you can explore with Jill. Unfortunately she doesn't go into RPD, as per the removal of Downtown map as I said earlier. It is what it is.

In the end the graphics are beautiful, Jill is gorgeous, fierce, brave and sassy, the storyline is improved, dodging mechanic is better, locations and the flow is more fluid, files are more part of the overall story and helps fill in many blanks, voice acting is top notch.

If a game has you wanting the work day to be over so you can come home and play it, it's a good game in my book.

[h1] Resident Evil 3: A Relentlessly Thrilling Rollercoaster [/h1]

Honestly, I’m glad Resident Evil 3 is a short game because it was really, really stressful to play. After six hours of it, I was thoroughly jangled, and just wanted a break from things trying to messily dismantle me. Before my nerves tattered and I evolved into a Strategy Dad, you see, I used to love a bit of survival horror. So I knew what boxes RE3 needed to tick - and it left great bloody claw marks through all of them.

Let's start with something seemingly dull but crucial: the inventory system. It’s simple, easy to manage, and extremely satisfying in its limitations. Crafting items isn’t just busywork here; it's vital for freeing up limited item slots by combining things. You're constantly thinking about what to stash where to maximize space. The scarcity of items and ammunition keeps you counting bullets most of the game, making looting both rewarding and necessary.

Shooting feels fantastic. Zombies' heads burst in a satisfying way, and each weapon feels suitably hefty. I played with aim assist on because I'm no sharpshooter, and it still posed a challenge. You might fare better, but I bet you won't find it a cakewalk.

The level design is top-notch. Play areas are modestly open, enough for exploration and backtracking, and every corner serves a purpose. It's navigable, thanks to the handy map feature that marks uncollected loot locations.

And I can't emphasize enough how great everything looks. The game is masterfully lit, with incredibly detailed textures. Even protagonist Jill Valentine looks almost real at times. But it's the details that truly shine, like weird in-universe film posters and adverts that make exploring a joy.

Fearwise, RE3 is spot on. The horror comes not just from jump scares but from a sense of constant dread. The environmental sound and lighting are masterfully used, making you feel perpetually unsafe. The game establishes this right from the start, leaving you on edge even during routine moments.

This is an action-heavy game with less skulking than traditional survival horror, but the dread carries through to the combat sections. The camera and controls are solid, but there's always a sense of unease. Even basic zombies are a constant threat, thanks to their erratic movements. Jill's running isn't a brisk sprint but the effort of a real human trying to escape, and it's refreshing.

The true star is Nemesis, a bioweapon with an obsession for Jill. His constant pursuit is genuinely oppressive, and it took me a while to realize I could fight back. As he transforms into more grotesque forms, the game maintains its horror, though his basic, imposing presence is often scarier.

Now, about the elephant in the room - the game's portrayal of violence against women. It's a theme, and it's presented with a hint of relish that might make some players uncomfortable. Jill's character design leans into sexiness, and she endures a lot of physical punishment. This aspect doesn't sit well in the current gaming climate.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 is a relentless rollercoaster of a game. It's an intense experience, visually stunning, with thrilling gameplay. However, its portrayal of violence may not sit right with everyone. If you're in the mood for a linear, day-long series of setpieces, this is it. But whether it's worth the price depends on your appetite for action-packed horror.

The story is a bit more action heavy than RE2, just like the original - so if you're switching to this after the RE2 remake, expect much more action-packed, linear gameplay. You don't get to explore as much as you do in RE2's police station.

Moving on, the game does look beautiful and mechanically plays very well, with the addition of a dodging system that honestly makes it steer away from survival horror and makes the boss fights a little bit too easy - encouraging you to try harder difficulties.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3046856216

Now, Nemesis was not very well received by fans, mostly because RE2's Mr. X takes up most of Nemesis' part from the original series (Nemesis used to be the "stalker enemy", much more unpredictable and terrifying), but I still think they did him fair and I've loved every single stage of the boss fights - I did find them a bit too easy, though, but they've been very entertaining.

What a disappointing game to play after the phenomenal Resident Evil 2 Remake....

Sure. the core gameplay of the 2nd game i still intact and amped up, just like the RE2 -> RE3 dynamic when these games came out back then, RE3 is more bombasting and action-packed than its more slower-paced predecessor. However while the original RE3 did enough to distinguish itself as its own game, RE3make fails to do so. Infact, in several ways it is actually worse than RE2make.

So let me tell you why:

- The grotesque gore simulation when shooting zombies in RE2make is gone in RE3make, you won't see the zombies' body disintegrate infront of your own eyes anymore and the visceral amount of damage a shotgun blast can do is only really shown on a headshot now.
- Nemesis isn't such a Nemesis anymore. Sure, he still shows up in the game, but all of his encounters are scripted, everything he does is pre-determined and there is only 1 section of the game where it does feel like he is actually hunting you, however that section takes up maybe 1/6th of the game, once you get past that point every encounter with him is scripted and always announced with a cutscene, and then half of those encounters are literally just "Press W to run away" What a step down from not just the original Nemesis, but even Mr. X who managed to be a formidable threat in RE2make.
- The Clock Tower section from the original Resident Evil 3 is completely gone, replaced with...nothing. This wouldn't even be so disappointing if you didn't even get to like, see the Clock Tower and read a pamphlet describing how it looks on the inside, only for there to just be a boss fight IN FRONT of it.
-The game is SHORT. like, REAL SHORT. It took me just about 5.5 Hours to finish the game from start to end on Hardcore difficulty, going into it mostly blind.
-Hardcore also isn't really a challenge I've never once struggled with ammo throughout my entire playthrough and actually had enough to clear every single room in the game of all enemies. Which I never had in RE2make. The only real difficulty on Hardcore comes from actually making sure you time your heals correctly and only use them when you hit Danger.

Is the game still worth buying though? Sure. Just not at full price. The Separate Ways DLC for Resident Evil 4 is just 10€ and about as long as this one and offers you more bang for your buck. However during a sale? when it costs around 10-15€? Sure.

You mainly play through this as Jill Valentine but switch over to Carlos (an Umbrella combat specialist) several times as well. Seeing things from both perspectives at different times in the story was pretty nice, and added to the overall experience in my opinion.

I played entirely on Steam Deck and it played flawlessly. I had it set to high/medium mix graphics, and locked it to 40fps and 40hz refresh rate. It took me a little under 8.5 hours to complete.

Overall, a solid entry in the franchise and definitely one I enjoyed. Highly recommend if you haven't played, just know it is more action focused.

That this still has the same price tag as the Resident Evil 2 Remake is appaling. This is basically DLC for RE2R. So much content from the original RE3 was cut that calling it a remake is honestly a disgrace. Imagine charging 60 bucks (originally) for basically a stand-alone DLC.

TL;DR This is a good game in a vacuum. Mechanically it's pretty good. The music is good, the atmosphere is good, the monsters are memorable. But as a *remake*, and a sequel to the RE2 Remake, it is very, very disappointing. But only in that respect. So if you want a remake of an original, this performs poorly. If you just want an isolated sequel to RE2R, then it's pretty good. What follows will go in depth about this opinion.

This game is conflicted in what it wants to be. It felt like it was being designed by two different teams at the same time; one that was committed to being a loving tribute to the original RE3, and one that didn't care.
On the one hand, you have the music; modern, atmospheric, bringing back the original RE3 score and perfecting it in one of the most lovingly nostalgic tributes to an OST I can remember hearing in a game. You have the atmosphere; dark, oppressive, bleak. The city is dying, death and despair are consuming it, and it FEELS like it. The environments are grimy, bloody, smashed, burning and crumbling. It sells the setting perfectly. It feels like a wonderful modernisation of the sights of RE3. It absorbs you into it. It looks convincing.

On the other hand, you have the plotline. It seems to rush through the story without letting any particular segment of it *breathe*. Like a tour guide leading you through a museum at a jog rather than walking through slowly, teling you the history and answering your questions.
You have the removal of whole segments from the original. The Police Station which should have been Jill's first stop, is never visited by her, and instead is a short detour for Carlos. The park is completely missing. The Clock Tower has been turned into a distant background landmark you may miss entirely if you're focused on your immediate surroundings and the boss fight that takes up most of the time it's visible. In the original it was an entirely separate location you had to explore. There were plot points tied to it; an escape route. It was a refuge, and a character-switch point.
Then you have the main antagonist, Nemesis. Arguably one of the most powerful and dangerous of Umbrella's various Tyrants. The original Pursuer of the franchise. He's been downgraded from a semi-persistent threat that pursues you from location to location to 3 brief encounters in the first 25% of the game and 3 setpiece boss fights for the rest of it. This is especially noticeable after RE2R's Mr. X and his stellar reimagining as a persistent pursuer; the role that should have been Nemesis's hallmark.
There's also the removal of the branching decision and diverging plotline system; a feature that introduced a lot of replayability in the original. As a result the game can be experienced in its entirety in one playthrough. The lazy difficulty system offers none of that replayability, as it can basically be summarised as "everything is faster and hits harder".

And then there's RE: Resistance, which is an online multiplayer subgame that was packaged alongside it, and which inherently has a low and dwindling playerbase which will eventually render it worthless. The development time for this would have been much better spent focusing on the main game itself and making sure it was as expansive and well polished as it really should have been.

It all just feels discordant. Like Capcom considered this game an afterthought while they worked on RE8. And it's a shame. Because the RE-Engine and the formula they achieved with the RE2 Remake could have made this game timeless.

I am giving this game a thumbs down because I imagine a lot of people coming to this game will be fans of the franchise itself, as opposed to new players coming to experience Resident Evil with no prior experience. On that basis, this game doesn't live up to its predecessors, neither RE2R, nor the original RE3. But if you just want to experience an RE game in the vein of RE2R and have no knowledge of the original, then this is a good game to play.

This game is a mixed bag, it's fundamentally very different from the original RE3, the focus on action is visible from the get go, the game is completely linear (with the exception of the initial run through downtown) and there are almost no puzzles on it. The combat for the most part is very good, the dodge mechanic is a welcome addition to the game, it was something that everyone who did runs for RE2R would have liked, the weapons in the game are a lot more useful than before, unlike RE2R now the shotgun isn't practically useless for everything other than zombies, and the harder difficulties don't put you in a situation where certain enemies become mandatory skips due to low damage (Lickers), the only real problem in the games combat being the stunlocks in the final Nemesis fight on Inferno. With combat out of the way, RE3 loses a lot of the charm from the original! Jill's personality has a series of changes which may or may not put people off (mainly she seems a bit arrogant at points) and the treatment of Nemesis is very lackluster (unlike what we got with Mr X, NEMESIS is completely scripted, outside of boss battles, he'll show up during 4 moments while free roaming downtown, other than that he's absent from the rest of the game), entire sections of the game where completely removed and the 3rd Nemesis fight is just a repeat of the second one but this time with Zombies added into the mix. The game also has a few problems including a problem with HDR that messes up your colors and a glitch that can cause your game to crash while entering the STARS Office with Carlos (if you are doing a non competitive speedrun save at the beginning of the RPD) and in true REngine fashion the game has very lackluster RT implementation and due to the forced TAA it's not a good idea to use FSR (or even DLSS if you do happen to install the DLSS mod). I'm having a blast with this game because I've been an RE fan since I was a kid, with that being said, if you are adamant that you want a full on perfect reenactment of the original game, I'm sorry but this game isn't for you, furthermore, if you want to get a good value out of this game, wait for a sale to buy it, because it's very short, even if you do want to replay it. I did my first run in 3h40 mins, the rest of my playtime has either been farming kills for records, or replaying the game on different difficulties. Notes: The Final Nemesis fight on Nightmare/Hardcore is BS! It's not difficult to dodge, but it's absurd!
