This is a controversial one. I think the largest complaint among fans are the differences between the original RE3: Nemesis and Remake. It's pointless listing all of them, but one of the posters on the Steam forums summarized it perfectly:

"Because it's basically a completely new game. It's vastly different than the original in almost every way.
People expect a remake to have more familiar locations and story of the original. Both RE2 remake and RE4 remake are a lot closer to the source material. In RE3 remake they took a ton of liberty and redesigned the entire thing completely for better or for worse."

The changes that I did like:[list]
[*]Chaos of the city being destroyed by the zombies is great, especially in the beginning.
[*]Storywise it's more focused, especially character development.
[*][spoiler]Brad dying a heroic death, instead of being killed by Nemesis, as if to make up for leaving Alpha Team to fend for themselves at the Spencer Mansion.[/spoiler]
[*]Jill is a bit too potty mouthed for my taste. She’s rude and snarky, but on the other hand, she every right to be, considering she mostly interacts with UBCS. At first I thought they ruined her character, but then I remembered that in the original she did slap Carlos at one point and was pretty hostile, though had a lot less dialogue to work with and didn’t swear. She does eventually warm up to Carlos, stops being snarky/sassy towards him, and seems to start liking him as a person. There is actual chemistry there, unlike in RE3: Nemesis. She’s also nice towards Brad and Kendo, people she knows and trusts.
[*]Some people complain about RE3R being more action oriented. The original was already very action oriented, especially for a fixed camera game. It had exploding barrels to kill groups of zombies for crying out loud.
[*]I’m actually shocked that people are defending RE3: Nemesis so much. I was always lukewarm towards it, being so action focused and padding out the run time by forcing you to backtrack through multiple long alleys in the first half of the game, and then the out of place Clock Tower section (which took 20-30 minutes to finish tops), pointless park, and awful Grave Digger fight. NEST 2 replaces the Dead Factory, which was essentially a lab anyway. It also reused assets like RPD. Nemesis was scripted as well, though admittedly he did appear more often. Live selection added minimum variety (it allowed you to discover an additional corridor with some items and that’s it), as did the random spawns each playthrough, increasing the replayability only a bit. For me it was entirely skippable, despite good ideas, Nemesis, and Jill.[/list]

My greatest disappointment with RE3R is that they failed to take a mediocre game with a good concept and elevate it into something truly great. They did redesign the entire thing, yet somehow were still too conservative, as if they were afraid that if they go too far, people will riot. Instead, they created a game that's only a bit less mediocre, and people hate it. For me it’s a tad better, more focused, and fun to play, but mostly forgettable. Buy it at a sale.

Resident Evil 3: Nemesis is a survival horror game developed by Capcom and originally released in 1999 for the PlayStation. The game received a remake in 2020, which I will be reviewing below.

The game follows Jill Valentine, a member of the Raccoon City police department, as she tries to escape the city during a zombie outbreak. She is pursued by a powerful bioweapon called Nemesis, who is sent to eliminate all S.T.A.R.S. members.

The 2020 remake of Resident Evil 3 features updated graphics and gameplay mechanics, but it also makes some changes to the original game. The biggest change is the removal of certain areas and events, which makes the game shorter than its predecessor.

In terms of gameplay, Resident Evil 3 is a mix of action and survival horror. The game features a dodge mechanic that allows players to avoid enemy attacks and counterattack. 

Compared to other games in the series, Resident Evil 3 is generally considered to be less successful than its predecessor, Resident Evil 2. The game received criticism for its shorter length and the removal of certain areas and events from the original game. However, the updated graphics and gameplay mechanics received praise from critics and fans.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 is a solid survival horror game that is worth playing for fans of the genre. However, those who are looking for a longer and more complex game may prefer some of the other games in the series.

Hot off the heels of RE2R comes RE3R, following a similar design philosophy, translation of Resident Evil 3: Nemesis to a new generation, and interesting story-telling aspects to boot! Sadly, it fails to live up to the expectations of RE2R.

PROS
+Yet again, the graphics are phenomenal, bordering on photorealistic.
+The character redesigns are all 10/10, hands down. Jill isn't fighting in a tube top, Carlos' new hair works pretty good, and Nemesis... well I'll get to him.
+Jill's undergone some changes that work well taken alone, though they are kind of awkward taken together. She's one part PTSD-stricken survivor (which makes sense from RE1), one part Sarah Conner-level badass (which makes sense considering she was in Delta Force before STARS), and one part genuinely-caring person (which makes sense considering she was one of the gentler members of STARS). Separately, in individual scenes, they work. Taken as a whole, it's a little wonky. Still a W in my book, though.
+Honestly, I now get why people like Carlos. Dude's the definition of a good guy working for the bad guys, but he still tries to do what's right. He's distinctive from other "soldier-type" characters, and I could totally see Jilos as a ship now. Don't know if I support it, but I see it.
+Mikhail is such a bro! Man's the definition of a proper Russian who's got your back!
+Nikolai is such a scumbag! Man's the definition of a crappy Russian who's only got his own interests in mind!
+Brad has a much better send-off than he did in RE2 or RE3. Man makes up for his actions in RE1 and proves why he's STARS material (most of the time).
+The title character from the original, Nemesis has been reimagined to be less of a super-Tyrant and more of a horrific abomination, becoming more animalistic every time he takes too much damage. Many disapprove of the new "trashbag" outfit, but I genuinely prefer it. It's like the bags keep him in the shape of something human(ish), and he reveals his true form as he sheds it.
+In a similar manner, each scripted encounter with Nemesis feels like a desperate run for safety, only becoming a fight when there's no choice. There are exceptions to this, which I'll cover under Cons, but there's no "oh ♥♥♥♥" feeling quite like watching him grab a rocket launcher and target you.
+Also, DAMN that introduction sequence was terrifying.
+Return of numerous elements from RE3. The one which stands out most to me is the dodge mechanic. While sort of unnecessary, it pairs well as similar, but different from Leon's parrying in RE4R.
+kid named FINGeR makes his Resident Evil debut! Jokes aside, the sequence is unpopular with many fans, but I love it sheerly for its massive BDE.
+That hospital holdout felt like some good, high-stakes, high-tension stuff! Loved it!
+Hunters are a pain in the ass.
+Solid replayability, and good post-game unlocks like alternate costumes, infinite ammo, and special gear.
+Oh yeah, btw the sound design is fantastic.

CONS
-To start with the elephant in the room: this game ships with Resident Evil: Resistance. It's the only way to get that game, which is an asymmetrical Dead by Daylight-style game. Honestly, it's pretty decent, and plays alright if you have multiple buddies to join up with. Unfortunately, the game is dead, so the only matches you'll (maybe) find will be solidly 300+ ping. In other words, we missed on a lot of stuff for an experiment that (to date) has crashed and burned. This only adds to the impression that RE3R is just a cheap cash-grab after RE2R's success. Maybe it is. I still liked it, but it's definitely not at the same level of excellence.
-It's a good thing this game has lots of post-release content, cuz dang is it short. Getting an S+ ranking in one playthrough of RE2R at highest difficulty must be done in under 5 hours (including both parts). In RE4R, that number is 5:30. In this, that number is 2 hours. This isn't a complaint on having less time, it's a complaint on there being less to do.
-Multiple missing elements from RE3 which arguably make that game better. Live Selection is the biggest one which bugs me, but others also cite the lack of multiple endings and the missing Clock Tower sequence as shortcomings (accurate, but they don't bug me as much, I guess).
-Remember how I said Nemesis was terrifying in scripted events? He's absolutely not outside of them. I was expecting something along the lines of Mr. X from RE2R: a constant presence keeping you pressured to be stealthy, careful, and constantly on the tip of your toes. Instead, he falls from the heavens and chases you while having access to a whip. Pretty unimpressive, to be honest.
-Worse, the thing goes down with ONE frag grenade on Hardcore! Not "stunned so you can get distance" like Mr. X, outright defeated with a loot drop! Disappointment doesn't begin to describe my feelings towards this.
-There's some hinting at what's going on behind the scenes with Nikolai, especially considering scenes from RE4R, but overall I felt more confused than anything in any scene where he was being evil.
-I know they only included one poisonous creature in the Remake, but I really wish there were multiple. I can't express how wrong it feels to cure poison with a green herb instead of a blue herb.
-Look, I love the FINGeR, and it's cool, but I gotta admit, it looks a little big to be man-portable.

Is it as good as RE2R or RE4R? No. Is it worth the full price? No. Is it worth playing on sale? Abso-freaking-lutely.

Of all the remakes when it comes to RE1, RE2, RE3, and RE4, this game would by far be my favorite in the series.... had it been a bit longer, and been more true to the original. :/

The original RE3 for the PS1 is a long and exciting ride, through MANY various locations in Racoon City. Where as this "remake" is a MUCH shorter version with MUCh... and I do mean MUCH fewer locations included.

So yeah...

As someone who got to know Resident Evil through the remake of RE2, I found the remake of RE3 an equally excellent game! 

The game is played from the role of Jill Valentine, the STARS officer who was already the protagonist of the first Resident Evil (AFAIK; never played it). The story begins during the outbreak of the T-virus in Raccoon City, following Jill's attempts to get out of the city alive.

Much like RE2, RE3 combines action-rich exploration with survival horror, though RE3 feels much more linear compared to its predecessor. A single playthrough took me seven hours, but according to an achievement it can be done in less than two hours. There is no incentive for a second playthrough (unlike in RE2, where you could choose between two protagonists and follow different stories). This makes the game somewhat short for its price, even on sale.

The game is played in the third person, featuring Jill as the primary protagonist, and Carlos in two shorter sequences. Both characters are likeable if somewhat bland; Jill certainly doesn't have as much personality as, say, Lara Craft from the Tomb Raider reboot, or Aloy from the Horizon franchise, or Elizabeth from BioShock Infinite, or many other characters from story-focused games. The plot likewise won't win any literature prize, but it works well enough to get things going.

From a technical standpoint, the game is fantastic. The graphics are gorgeous, sounds are great, gameplay is fun and engaging. I prefer this kind of action-rich horror quite a lot over the subpar jumpscare kind that has become popular in recent years. The gunplay is pretty fun, the exploration part is very much reduced to RE2, and Nemesis as a boss enemy is kind of bleh. 

Resident Evil 3 is a fun and interesting game to play through over a weekend, even if you aren't a particular friend of horror games (like me). I'm not sure if I'll ever play through the game a second time -- there are better games if you want a good story, and better games if you want cool gameplay -- but I'd still call this an easy recommendation, and I'm certainly looking forward to playing RE4 once the price drops in sales. 

I'd recommend buying the game on sale, when it's typically 75% off (10€ / 10$ / comparable prices).

Edit: Note that there are lots of mods out there that typically change only Jill's appearance. I used one that prevented Nemesis from chasing me around (because that got kind of tedious). Most mods are made for the non-raytracing version of the game, which can still be accessed through the beta versions of the game properties.

Note further that this game comes with some free multiplayer game thingy, which I'm told is not that great (due to cheating players, not because the game itself is terrible). I haven't checked that out, and don't plan to.

Resident Evil 3 remake is underrated. Its starts a bit on the rails but quickly gets into the open city. The controls are fluid and refined—some of the best controls in an RE game or otherwise. One of the best added features is the dodge mechanic. It's similar to the dodge in the the RE Revelations series but it actually works. It's more intuitive than the way they did it in RE2R where you couldn't dodge but had to carry a knife or grenade and use that to avoid grabs instead.

Another great addition are the "coin" boosts. You can really customize your play style if you are willing to sacrifice a storage spot. So, even beyond normal, hard, and even harder modes, you can tweak the difficulty from within there with the coins.

Jill and Carlos' characters are generally well done, neither too invincible, too weak, too arrogant, nor too obnoxious as are characters in many modern games. The Mikhail villain is a bit overly one-dimensional, though.

The upgrades and rewards systems are likewise actually attainable without being ultra-expert level player (like RE2R required) nor playing for a million hours. With moderate to generous repeated gameplay, you can achieve enough weapon kills and other reward points to unlock funner stuff — including the RE trademark infinite weapons which always make for a fun playthrough. There's also a very fun fire knife called Hot Dogger that won't ever break and will set enemies ablaze briefly with every strike.

The game was criticized for being too short or excluding some stuff from original, but what is actually there is polished and I don't recall a single glitch. You don't see much criticism of what is actually there - if this had been a DLC for RE2R, more people would rave about it. It's also a great game for single evening speedrun. The nightmare and inferno modes also mix up the enemy and item locations which makes for a very different experience.

[h1] Introduction [/h1]

Resident Evil 3 is one of those chapters which were in my backlogs for a while. I’ve heard earlier that game is too short, as well that it’s not such horror. As well metacritic score shows, that game didn’t match users so much. After I finished the game may tell that this game is well done.

[h1] Main plot [/h1]

The story is interesting enough. We see a story of stars officer - Jill Valentine, who has been in Raccoon city, when started an epidemic. During all game we see one story from two characters - Jill and Carlos. While to see the hole story for both characters in RE 2 we used to play a new game from another characters view, here we have answers immediately. But I still have a question to one episode - [spoiler] in last part of the game Carlos went in underground to find a vaccine, and missed for almost a day. When Jill woke up she decided to find Carlos. So Jill made a vaccine, and then found Carlos. What Carlos has been doing all this time in underground? [/spoiler] If game shows us all story from both sides it would be correct to make at least 15 min episode where shows ‘Carlos was walking and then felled down’ for example.

Although the story is interesting - it’s very fast paced. The whole game I had no time to stop and get a rest, at this time I had a new cutscene, or a fight. So while previous part was more about puzzles and searching for keys, this part is more about action.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

Technically main mechanics were taken from RE 2 remake. Almost all mechanics are the same, but we now have an option to parry. It makes game much easier, because after each well done parry the scope automatically rises on opponents head.

The game more looks as a shooter then horror, what is true. Before each big fight game gives us enough bullets, and during all game I had no filling of weapon deficit (have played on normal level).

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

During the whole game I had only one crash, but otherwise game is done perfectly. Despite the fact that the game is very quickly passed on the plot, there are no complaints. Yes, the game is not long, if you know what is happening, you can really go through it in 3-4 hours without difficulty. It took me 7 hours, despite the fact that I went through it without straining and died a lot of times.
But in general I had enough fun, and enjoyed the game.

So when people say, "I can't believe they cut out the clock tower in the remake!", I'm thinking "I don't even remember the clock tower."

Judged on its own merits, RE3make is a fun romp. I enjoyed it way more than the original, for sure. But it's just not the masterpiece that RE2make was. It lacks the depth and replayability of that game. I think that comes down to the linear nature of RE3; With 1 & 2, you finish your first playthrough thinking, "Oh yeah, I could have done this first and saved myself so much running around." Here, every playthrough is more or less the same. And yes, the "Nemesis Choices" of the original would have helped a bit in that department. 

After a while, RE3make feels like you're just running from one boss encounter to the next. And then it's over in ~6 hours. Is it worth $60? Nah. But catch it on sale and it's worth experiencing. But just like with the original, I know that I'll be returning to RE2 when I want to get my zombie killing fix.

It was short, and I feel like it doesn't have too much replayability, but I very much enjoyed my time with this game. I do wish it was longer though.

### Visuals 9/10 ###
- Awesome graphic
- Very detailed faces and character expressions in cut-scenes
- Very atmospheric light/shadow ambiente
- Various zombie designs
- Played on 3070 with all settings to max and no dlss: Constant fps above 100

- The characters all stay very flat, but at least you play Jill most of the time
- Carlos is likable, but there is zero backround story
- All characters act absolutely cliché

- Very very generic
- No surprises
- If you want a good story, play RE 7 + 8 :)

### Gameplay 9/10 ###
- Port to pc is very well executed
- Fast and easy to learn key layout
- Aiming goes really well with mouse
- Still quite difficult in differenct situations (played on hardcore)

RE3 Remake has been maligned as the weakest of the remade entries. And, to some extent, I see why. It lacks the looping level design of RE2 Remake's excellent RPD puzzle box and the systemic flexibility of RE4 Remake's combat sandbox. 

Still, this is a handsomely mounted production, with gorgeous animation and effects. It takes the increasingly grotesque imagery of RE2 Remake's morphing monstrosities and amps it up to 11 from essentially minute one. Nemesis is intimidating in his first, Terminator-esque form and only becomes more and more fantastical and grotty as the game progresses. If the goal of RE2 Remake was to make Mr. X's footsteps trigger a Pavlovian terror, the goal of RE3 Remake is to have you hooting and hollering with every sick evolution of Nemesis's form. 

Just like every RE since the dawn of time, replays are a pleasure. If the first playthrough can be seen as Act 1, with you fumbling through the game, scraping by with just enough ammo and cautiously checking corners, round 2 is Act 2, where your mastery of the systems and extra items awarded for round 1 let you blast away with relative abandon. It's always a cathartic release. 

I'd say that this is worth it at any price, up to $60 USD, but this is regularly on sale for significantly less. Don't let the bad mark this game has keep you away from a good time.

When you blast open a zombie's head with the Lightning Hawk, nothing is more satisfying. Variety of guns allows for different approaches to the game. There's only one boss in the game and that's Nemesis - I personally loved every single fight I had against him.
The game is optimized well, just like RE2 Remake, probably because they're both using the same RE Engine. Like with RE2 Remake, in RE3 Remake, I managed to maximize the graphics and still play the game smoothly at 144 FPS, which is my monitor's refresh rate.

From the moment I loaded the game, I was immediately struck by the stunning graphics and attention to detail. The environments are richly rendered, with crumbling buildings, eerie alleyways, and blood-stained streets that create a truly immersive and harrowing atmosphere. The character models are incredibly lifelike, and the facial animations are top-notch, conveying the fear and desperation of the protagonists as they navigate the apocalyptic city.

One of the standout features of Resident Evil 3 is the gameplay. The controls are tight and responsive, making movement and combat feel smooth and natural. The addition of the dodge mechanic adds an extra layer of strategy, allowing players to evade attacks and counter with well-timed shots. The inventory management system, a staple of the series, adds to the tension as players must carefully manage their resources, balancing ammunition, healing items, and other supplies to survive the relentless onslaught of enemies.

Speaking of enemies, the creatures in Resident Evil 3 are some of the most terrifying and challenging foes in the series. The iconic Nemesis, a relentless and powerful bioweapon, stalks players throughout the game, providing constant tension and making every encounter a heart-pounding battle for survival. The other mutated creatures that populate Raccoon City are equally grotesque and formidable, forcing players to strategize and adapt to their unique abilities.

The story in Resident Evil 3 is engaging and well-paced, providing a thrilling and intense narrative that keeps players on the edge of their seats. Playing as Jill Valentine, a member of the elite S.T.A.R.S. team, players must navigate the city, uncover the truth behind the outbreak, and find a way to escape before it's too late. The story is complemented by well-written dialogue, memorable characters, and a sense of urgency that drives the action forward.

In addition to the main story, Resident Evil 3 also includes a multiplayer mode called Resident Evil Resistance. This mode allows players to team up with others online and play as survivors trying to escape from the clutches of a player-controlled Mastermind who sets traps and controls the undead. While it's a fun addition, it doesn't quite match the intensity and thrill of the main campaign.

One area where Resident Evil 3 falls slightly short is its length. Compared to previous entries in the series, the main campaign feels relatively short, clocking in at around 6-8 hours of gameplay. While the game makes up for it with replayability through multiple difficulty levels, unlockable content, and new game plus modes, some players may find themselves craving more content after completing the main story.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 is a worthy addition to the iconic franchise, delivering heart-pounding survival horror gameplay, stunning visuals, and a gripping story. The intense combat, terrifying enemies, and immersive atmosphere create a truly memorable experience that will keep players on their toes from start to finish. While the main campaign may be relatively short, the overall package is a must-play for fans of the series and anyone who loves a good horror game. Get ready to face your fears and survive the nightmare of Raccoon City in Resident Evil 3!

A very good game with a well staged and exciting but short campaign in what is perhaps the most iconic horror setting in the video game landscape.  But sadly not a very good remake because instead of adding more content to the original source, the developers dropped a lot of it due to budget constraints. So much that for many fans it was no longer justifiable with the modernized gameplay and new look and mood alone, as with the RE2R.

Most of my review and comparisons are between this and RE2 Remake.
- I would highly recommend this. Even at $40 I would feel this would be worth it.
- RE Boomer fans are impossible to please because they don't know what they want and they all want different things.
- I enjoyed this far more than RE2 Remake. This felt more like RE4's playstyle. Fairly linear, little backtracking, more story, less puzzles, more action.
- I never played the OG on PSX. This game standing on it's own is fantastic. I would honestly replay this over RE2 Remake.
- My playtime casually was 11 hours. The playtime on howlongtobeat between this remake and the RE3 OG on the PSX, is about the same. 6+ hours. But a 6 hour playthrough is not possible imo if you play casually. Unless you're rushing and skipping stuff 4 hours seems not possible at all on a first playthough. Yes, RE2 Remake is a longer game if you do leon + claire 2nd scenario. But RE3R's story is more interesting.

Pros
- Jill. She's is now my favorite RE character.
- There wasn't constant pressure like RE2 Remake with Mr. X where you would run to the other side of the police station, only to have Mr. X appear right in front of you. In RE3R, if there is pressure, it is temporary and not constant.
- Wielding the knife in RE3 remake made more sense than how RE2 remake did it.
- There's no durability to the knife in RE3 remake, which i would prefer but you also can't use it deter a bite either.
- Scripted animation sequences were well done, the graphics overall were also very good.
- Characters were very high quality, and so were the animations. Mocap I'm guessing was used.
- I saw very little reused assets from RE2 remake, other than the police headquarters which was less than 1/8th of the game, and even that wasn't exactly identical.
- The story was far more interesting and action packed than RE2 Remake. But less horror survival.
- The music was absolutely significantly better than RE2 Remake in every way. RE2 Remake music was either weak or non-existent/silent in areas it shouldn't have been.
- I really enjoyed the boss battles. I died a few times, so they felt challenging, but not impossible and they weren't easy I felt.
- I didn't feel the game was a walk through the park or overly difficult.
- The dodge mechanic is handy.

Cons
- The laser sight could have been graphically improved other than just a red dot on the HUD...
- There are a few bugs, but nothing I felt was a deal breaker, such as collision areas blocking my shots when they should have hit the zambies. Sometimes dialog only occurred if I died first and replayed the scene.
- I still don't know what pressing A repeatedly during a zombie bite does... I always get bit and take damage.
- There were a few textures (very few) that could have had an increase in res. Fire maybe, nade explosion particles, and a few environment textures I saw, but that's all.
- The fire in some places looks somewhat poor and planar, and the animation rate for it felt a little too low to me.
- The animation LOD budgeter kicks in at a distance that's a bit too close. This also occurs in RE2, but since you're always inside and you don't seem zambies at a distance usually, you don't notice it as much. So it looks like it's an RE3 only thing but it's not. Basically, when you view zambies from a distance, they animate at a low sampling rate so they look choppy, but I only noticed this in RE3R about 3 times total.
- The fire hose sequence with the water spraying at the beginning of the game was quite poor imo, but it's a minor forgettable thing.
- The biggest thing I felt could have been better in RE3R were the 1 shot kills/insta deaths. Several times there was nothing I could do to avoid it or I would get stun locked and get his 3 times in a row resulting in death. Mainly with nemesis a couple times, and definitely with the dudes in the 2nd half of the game. So I saved often. I died about 30 times for my first run though this game. Fortunately, there is usually a save point before the 1 shot kills seem to occur, so not much time was lost and it wasn't as annoying as it could have been.

Note: Some of these things there are mods for to correct, so that might be something you could look at.

Overall the things I noticed that are negative are also minor. The biggest thing being the 1 shot kills. But, despite this, I would definitely suggest playing it anyways, but just make sure you save liberally to avoid some frustration.

It's short. Like very much so. As someone who replayed Resident Evil 2 (remake) just before going through this, I spent about 6 hours on an A scenario of RE2, and it took me about 4 to finish the game here. And it's counted 3 hours and a bit in-game time. Based on that alone, I can't really recommend it, unless you're really into replaying the game over and over again to unlock everything in.

I'm going to compare it mostly to RE2. They removed the mechanic of countering a zombie attack with a consumable (knife or grenade), to instead have a dodge move, which consistency is kinda dubious. It's not a bad idea in itself. The only slight issue I have on that matter is that it usually feels like you dodge an attack more out of luck than out of correctly timing the damn attack. They also streamlined the game systems a bit, there are now only 2 plants, blue disappeared, not surprising since the poison mechanic is barely in the game. The details point to it, and I'll say it: the game is definitely more "actioney" than RE2 Remake. There are heaps of munitions in the game, and even more heaps of zombies. That's not in itself a bad thing, just something to know.

The way in which I consider it worse though, is the level design. At the start, after a very scripted and linear action sequence, you're allowed into an open-ish network of closed down streets and houses to go through, working as a place to go back and forth to unlock every closed door or safe. But the actual mandatory stuff is very linear, with very little back and forth involved. And it only gets worse the further the game goes. There's a guest appearance from the RE2 police station, but cut down to a small section. The later part of the game don't improve much, with very little back and forth to be done, except for completionism sake.

Overall, as a casual RE enjoyer, I didn't enjoy RE3 remake much. And that's mostly due to 2 factors, the shortness, and the linearity. It's an absolute killer, especially since the lack of variations (like a different scenario or B scenarios) hinder the replay value a lot.

I feel like I need to write a positive review to offset some of the negative ones. This game is great. I played the original years ago when it came out and was always luke warm to it, Code Veronica was a far better sequel to RE2 in my opinion. So I was less excited about trying this remake than I was for RE2. However, I was pleasantly surprised, this game was really fun! It had a nice mix of action and traditional RE elements, and I feel like the new additions and design choices only improved the game. 

The nemesis can still be a pain, but I feel like the pacing and overall story structure of this version makes far more sense. Both to modernise and just generally improve the original game. 

One of the complaints I've seen a lot is length and value. While I agree this is not a $60-70 game, it definitely fits in that $30 range quite nicely. I feel like people who complain about this game's length are the same people who keep buying and praising the 100+ hour bloated collect-a-thons that Ubisoft churns out every year. Quantity does not equal quality and a game like this proves that in spades. About an 8-10 hour campaign for a first play through is perfectly reasonable and enjoyable. All these people who say they are "thorough" and "collect everything" in a first playthrough, and yet, also claim it took them 3 hours are simply full of $hit. I like to play lots of games and I enjoy a mix of short and long campaigns to mix it up; it's about quality. if a game is tight, cohesive, and enjoyable at 10-15 hours that's great. 100 hour games can be enjoyable, but are also exhausting! Especially when bloated with needless things included just to pad the run time. 

This game, while linear, has an enjoyable enough gameplay loop that subsequent playthroughs can still be rewarding, but they're totally optional as well. 

Basically, if you like RE and want to play a solid game, you can't go wrong here.

RE3 is a short and sweet romp through a by-the-numbers 90’s zombie film, and if that alone should convince you to give it a red hot go, don’t let me dissuade you. RE Engine is optimised, efficient and beautiful. The first playthrough is the best. 

However, the gameplay does not cultivate the same level of game mastery of RE2, where strict boundaries in a variety of circumstances forces creative inventory management, or death. 3’s challenge came from figuring out the best spot to grind grenade launcher kills (demolition site) and listening to the line [i]“Carlos, maybe you can knock that pillar down with that explosive!”[/i] several dozen times. To those out of the loop, the point shop items(including more inventory space, permanent health regeneration and the infinite rocket launcher) [b]DO NOT[/b] impact scoring across playthroughs, and cumulatively generate the point currency progress game wide, even if you load a save. The infinite rocket launcher trivialises the game, turning every encounter into a pre-firing slaughter, further lowering the difficulty of an already non-threatening game. As evidence, I beat Inferno with an S rank without healing items, and with the only deaths in the final boss fight, with the rocket launcher as a crutch. 

RE2Remake has spoilt me on the series. The risk, challenge and the feeling of championing it makes the experience something I’ll need to compare other games too, and unfortunately, RE3 has fallen victim to a biased gamer. All this has done is make me envious of RE4.

I haven't completed the main campaign yet but I just wanted to put it out there that this game doesn't feel "short." I read and heard so much criticism about this game and was put off from buying it until now when it was on sale. I will say that this would have been amazing DLC for Resident Evil 2 remake as it's set at pretty much the same time...it would've been one hell of a package to have both games together as one with maybe some added magic to bring both games together!!

I didn't play the OG Resident Evil 3 so, for me, this feels like another great Resi game.

One thing I'm finding consistently annoying with the remakes is the dynamic/RnG health that enemies appear to have. I really do miss the old days of knowing that a head shot meant something OR explosives were really powerful. Pumping in 6-10 headshots and half a dozen knife slashes to a single zombie who still decides to stand up again just crazes me sometimes (as well as the fact that animations make placing your shots near impossible!) I hate that blowing off the head is a rare, crit move that only happens a few times per playthrough. I understand this has made combat more scary and relevant for the modern day but I still feel that knowing where you stand with damage output lead to a lot more enjoyment. 

The new "feel" works well and feels progressive for the times but they do not in anyway replace the original games. Resident Evil 2 OG had better scenarios and story telling and, apparently, Resident Evil 3 OG had a lot more content that was cut from this remake!! Capcom could have really changed the times and made these remakes something special...instead they've done an OK job which still stands up as decent gaming.

Definitely worth picking up in a sale if you're a fan of the franchise. I'm consistently buying Resident Evil games at sale as I feel they're approach to DLC is just money grabbing at it's worst. Can't wait to play Resident Evil 4 remake but that won't be until at least Christmas 2023 as I won't be buying it at full price...

NOTE: I'm around 9 hours in on my first playthrough....probably got another hour or two remaining..?!?!?

This is basically an additional short campaign for the RE2 remake and I don't think I'm being hyperbolic when I say that it is worse in every single way.

I think calling it an expansion pack is giving it too much credit. It's a hollow, short and unsatisfying experience.You're railroaded from start to end, the game has an unending hard-on for bland boss fights.

It overall feels like watching a B-tier movie, but with all the campiness and charm sucked out of it.

At its core, it is a competent shooter engine coupled with some of the most uninspired level design I've seen.You would think that after laying the groundwork with RE2 (RE3 uses exactly the same engine and reuses a lot of assets), the developers would have been able to deliver a premium experience with RE3, since all the work except level development, voice acting and a few assets is already done.

What was actually delivered was in line with my lowest expectations for the game.
- The levels are short and require almost no effort from the player to traverse. There is little creativity or exploration required. Just go down the corridor. It makes Half Life 1 feel open ended.
- There isn't a single level in the whole game I could describe as interesting or well done.
- You are forced into mindless chase cinematics frequently.
- None of the dialogue or story is good or advances the series in any way.
- The inventory management and available items are bland.
- The enemy types pose no real problem and very limited interactivity with the player. You just get the right ammo type and down them instantly. This also means that none of the enemy variety actually works in practice, and the game has every low enemy variety to begin with.
- Gunplay is unsatisfying. As per RE2 formula, normal zombies are bullet sponges. For special zombies you have so plentiful and effective ammunition it doesn't matter. And if you didn't have plentiful ammunition, there wouldn't be much you can do, as the environment is so linear and lacking, that there's nothing else the player can really do if they don't possess the tools to quickly dispatch an enemy.
- I hope you like fighting Nemesis in five different boss fights, most of which are contrived and specific about how you're supposed to deal with your enemy.

RE3 amplifies all of RE2's flaws and throws all of its strong points right out the window. I can't think of a single reason you would want to play this game except out of some grim completionism for the series. Even if you have the game already bought I would encourage you to exhaust other options first.

Review:

As someone who played and finished the original game, I can say that the remake is a game where too much was cut out and it was rushed. Jill's dialogue is a bit soulless, and some of her facial animations are robotic. There seems to be a problem with the motion capture, but who knows?

There are unnecessary puzzles added to extend the game, and there are some unnecessary enemy additions to add challenge to the game. At the same time, since the game lacks horror elements other than atmospheric horror and the tension given by the nemesis, they used a few cheap jump scare tricks. 

The city modeling is well done, and it reflects the zombie apocalypse atmosphere really well. It's fun to feel that atmosphere while walking through the alleys. As in the original game, resource management is one of the things that makes this game good, and I think exploring and looting is a pleasure in this game.

I can say that the cutscenes are generally well done, and the action sequences are great. Especially the fight animation on the roof in the last scene was really good. Compared to the 2nd game, the particle effect and zombie deform physics are far behind. There may be many reasons for this, except that it was a rushed job.

The feeling of hitting is behind compared to the 2nd game, except for the modified version of Jill's basic weapon and the Desert Eagle-style weapon. I couldn't get the same feeling I got in the 2nd game with other weapons. Also, the M4 gun is extremely underpowered compared to the real thing. It's funny that you can take down a zombie with the M4 in 15 rounds, even if you shoot it in the head... (Note: I finished the game on Hardcore and Standard difficulty, so I don't know how it is on Easy).

If you are not loaded enough in the boss fight before the last boss fight of the game, you may have trouble. Usually, in Resident Evil level designs, boss areas have bullets and supplies, but there are not enough of them in this episode. If you don't play smart, you can die due to a lack of resources. You need to loot the environment well before entering this fight, and spending extra time for this is a bit annoying in the last stage of the game...

Overall, I liked the remake of Re3, an old cult game, even if it's not worth buying at full price the moment it comes out. It is a game that you can buy on sale and enjoy.

[h1] RESIDENT EVIL [/h1]

The Resident Evil franchise, a household name these days, set the gold standard for survival horror back in the day alongside its main competitor, Silent Hill. As a result, with such a legacy come great expectations and with the franchise finally back on the right path, post-RE6, what better way to excite and wow fans than by remaking one of the most iconic entries in the series.

[h2] REMAKING NEMESIS [/h2]

Following in the footsteps of the fantastic Resident Evil 2 remake, RE3 does away with the top-down perspective for a much more comfortable and atmospheric over the shoulder view. 
It still utilizes the RE Engine that was originally shipped with RE7 so in the visual department it's an absolute feast, especially here where the environment feels much more varied than the last remake. 
Gunplay is still extremely solid, although some weapons are somewhat underpowered despite their appearance, and great care has been given to the sound once again with meaty sound effects and catchy tunes. 
Exploration is a big aspect of the game ,as is a tradition in the series, meaning you will often run out of supplies, forcing you to scavenge around the levels which are quite well designed although admittedly not as impressive as RE2's in terms of ambition and scope. Also big props for the quality-of-life improvements ported here from RE2, like the game showing when it's safe to discard a key item or when you are done exploring an area. 
That's a comment that comes up quite frequently in fact when discussing this remake; it does a lot of things well just not as well as the last one, the tyrant stalking you being one of the many examples to be brought up as this time around the titular Nemesis is reserved mostly for cutscenes and scripted sequences, but it's still a great spook when the lad shows up. There's much more banter and dialogue between the characters with more screentime given to the sidecast in this one, compared to RE2's mostly cheesy back-and-forths between Leon and Claire which led to nowhere. Overall, there was clearly a bigger focus on story and characters, a lovely change from the drab storytelling we saw previously.

[h3] CONCLUSION [/h3]

Now, while i personally never got the chance to enjoy the original, it has to be mentioned that many sequences from the classic game were completely cut and certain mechanics were also axed from the gameplay department. For first time players like myself ,however, it isn't that noticeable as the whole experience feels very well interconnected with a clear beginning, middle and satisfying conclusion to a truly fun remake of a survival horror masterpiece.

Another great remaster for the series, I didn't have too many of the issues with the game like some of the die hard fans of the IP seemed to experience.

I thought it was pretty much an extension of the previous remake with a couple of nice little quality of life changes that made the game-play a little more seamless. The most notable two (at least for me) being the addition of a dodge function which I was dying (sometimes literally) for to be included in RE2R, and another smaller change being certain inventory management aspects such as not having to go into the inventory EVERY time you pick up an item. Small things, but frequent things.

Other aspects of the game however seem to have regressed, for some reason you can no longer break out of an attack with your knife or any grenades you might have laying around in your inventory.

A lot of the criticism seems to be directed at the length of the game. Whilst I largely agree, I think I have an unpopular opinion by saying that there isn't that much less content, maybe a few hours, than the previous game. I think RE2R does a better job of making you think there's more content than there actually is by splitting it up into 4 "individual" playthroughs which in reality differ by about 10% each between them. 

Resident Evil 3 is a singular story which only changes in difficulty. Despite this, although I enjoyed my first playthrough of 2 more so than 3, subsequent playthroughs of 3 are much more enjoyable as they're packed with more action and combat rather than puzzles which are something that aren't as fun to replay! I think this installation drags on a lot less and acknowledges its length correctly and I found that I had finished it with all the achievements just before it got stale rather than after, like it was beginning to after 30 hours of RE2.

I'd say if you liked RE2, or even if you're completely new to the Resident Evil universe pick it up! It's a fun little adventure and plays quite smoothly. But get it on sale! I wouldn't pay more than the £8 it costs on sale. Though it is a great game, it's a short one and therefore doesn't justify its £35 base price.

Half-decent game, terrible Resident Evil game. Lemme preface this by saying I absolutely love Resident Evil 3: Nemesis and have probably put more time into it than any reasonably sane person should, and after running through this...this just ain't it, chief.

RE3: Nemesis had some fantastic elements to it. It was the first game in the franchise to utilize a dodge and counter mechanic, which was fantastic! Granted, it didn't work very well and was difficult to get the hang of, but once you'd get the hang of it fighting Nemesis got really fun, really fast. Being able to explore Raccoon City at your own pace was fantastic, and sure, some of the backtracking could get tedious, but it was among the best horror games in its day. This is like a really low effort reboot. Most of the iconic locations don't even appear, the sequence of events is all mixed up, Jill doesn't even really act like Jill, and what were they even thinking with that Nemesis redesign?! They went from a genuinely intimidating boss to Crooked Nose McGee over here. Bad decisions all around. It was also disappointingly short, and the only really good elements to this remake were the Hunter Alpha redesigns and the pale heads. I don't even want to talk about the Hunter Gammas, that was too strange.

After they did such an amazing job with RE2's remake, I'm still bewildered as to how they went so far wrong with this one. There are next to no puzzles. The Clock Tower was cut completely, along with 50% of the total game if not more. Brad's death in the original had a purpose, here it's just lazy writing. The entire game can be summed up as lazy writing. Take notes, this is NOT how you design a good remake. As a Resident Evil fan, I'm disappointed beyond measure. Really the only thing they DID get right was fixing the dodge mechanic, but Resident Evil 3 should not be a game you can easily run start to finish in under an hour.

Thanks to stunning visuals brought to life using Reach for the Moon Engine, Capcom successfully reintroduces its classics to both newcomers and long-standing fans of the series. Veterans can revisit the past with an updated looks and modern spin on the gameplay, while rookies get to comfortably check out what the fuss is about – without the hassle of getting an over 20 years old game to run on modern hardware. If I was to boil down the RE 2 remake to a single contribution they made to wider audiences – it would definitely be the unrelenting presence of Mr. X chasing the player around Racoon City’s police department and the memes that came along with it. Imagine if you will, an entire game based around this concept. You now have a decent idea what Resident Evil 3 is about. 

Admittedly, this may sound like a recipe for the ultimate thrill – don’t get too excited though, as RE 3 remake does come with its fair share of caveats. Some of them dutifully carried over from the original RE 3: Nemesis. In short, it is a fun title; although not quite as good as RE 2 remake was. Answering why exactly that is will require exploring the game in greater detail.
[url]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2947731092[/url]
[b]Came in like a wrecking ball[/b]
After a certain dream sequence, reminding the player that despite its shenanigans RE 3 remains a survival [i]horror[/i], the player is introduced to Jill Valentine. One of the few survivors of the Arklay incident from the first game, Jill is about to end her investigation regarding Umbrella Corporation’s involvement in the Racoon City. At least she intended to, until a 2,5 meter tall worth of evidence bursts through her apartment’s wall within first 5 minutes of the game – starting what can only be described as a frantic escape sequence... that never truly ends. This title’s opening does a stellar job at introducing a stark departure from Resident’s usual slow-burn initial act. For better or worse, RE 3 puts a much heavier emphasis on action elements, favouring combat and chase scenes in place of wacky puzzles and convoluted machinery.

Contrary to many entries in the series, rather than spend substantial amount of time in a single location, Jill’s struggles take her to multiple places throughout the ruined city. Some very familiar to all who played RE 2 remake first. Story of RE 3 takes place at the same time its predecessor’s and it provides some further context for the events of Racoon City outbreak. On that note, lore elements are rather downplayed too, as Jill has precious little time for exploration with Nemesis constantly breathing down her neck.

[b]Nemesis-T Type[/b]
Speaking of the devil, the towering monument of mutated flesh that is Nemesis, not Jill, is the true star of this title. Starring in movies and having a guest appearances in other games (looking at you Dead by Daylight), it may be the best known Resident Evil character. Nemesis also is the first enemy introduced into the game, it is immediately showcased as an unstoppable force – it walks through walls like they were paper, being set on fire accomplished mostly a reveal of its toothy visage and RE 3 straight up tells the player that shooting it is a waste of bullets. Judging by positively stellar first act of the game, Capcom was seemingly trying to make a game after a Alfred Hitchock’s quote “A good film should start with an earthquake and be followed by rising tension”. To the developer’s credit, they did nail the earthquake part.
[url]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2947731124[/url]
It’s high time to address how Resident Evil 3 remake actually plays. While all of the series’ building blocks are still in place, this title has a much more streamlined and simplified map design. Circling around areas as key items open up previously unavailable sections is not entirely gone. However, it’s on a visibly lesser scale as instead of relying on items and puzzles for pacing, RE 3 prefers to drop Nemesis on top of the player’s head. Such means of reinforcing the sense of urgency makes sense from a design standpoint. On the other hand, it is a double-edged sword as it makes the player hurry their way through the shortest game of the series, taking under 6 hours to complete.

Likewise, the combat needs to be taken with a grain of salt. While Nemesis encounters are reasonably paced, RE 3 leans towards shooting your way through narrow areas even in sections without the big bad. Perhaps not a flaw in itself, coupled with the fact that remakes sport the lowest enemy variety in the series, doesn’t make it a virtue either. On that note, the franchise at large seems to withdraw from giant animals as enemies, which were fairly prevalent in the original three games. Would a giant burrowing worm make RE 3 a better game? We will never know; but the original had a secondary boss, while the remake doesn’t.

[b]An overly cinematic experience[/b]
Probably my biggest critique of this title revolves around the Nemesis itself. Bluntly put, the brute makes too good of an entrance for RE 3 to stand a chance at maintaining the tension throughout the entire game. Two kinds of issues stem from this root. Firstly, while the sensation of fear is uniquely subjective and the franchise at large has a reputation for being more survival than horror, the notion is upped to eleven in this game. In terms of tone, RE 3 is like Michael Bay had a go at making RE 2 better in his explosive image. Secondly, the first half of the game is significantly more impactful because the player needs to complete objectives, despite Nemesis' presence on the map. However, during the later stages of the game, the big bad becomes a reoccurring bossfight instead and the chase sequences take place within cutscenes rather than actual gameplay.
[url]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2947731512[/url]
Speaking of cinematics, there is a lot of scripted events and cutscenes throughout RE 3 remake. I am tempted to say they take up as much as a third of the overall playtime. Truth be told, they are worked into the flow of the game so well, that only during the second playthrough did I fully realise their scope. Nonetheless, while skipping cinematics, some sections during which I could swear I was the one making Jill run, didn’t require my involvement at all. It made me wonder if the weird single-key QTE were there to prevent the screen saver from popping up while watching.

[b]Gone with a blastwave[/b]
Writing from a perspective of someone who have played nearly every Resident Evil game released on PC, I think the series is at its best when it takes place primarily at a single vast location. While RE 3 is hardly the only action-oriented entry (take RE 5 and RE 6), they consistently seem to remain a step behind the games in which puzzle elements are more pronounced. Wacky as they may be, the ludicrous mechanisms and secret passages they tend to operate are integral part of Resident Evil’s identity to me.

Ultimately, Resident Evil 3 remake is a fun ride despite the game’s flaws. I would be surprised if this title was anyone’s first voyage into the franchise. If you somehow did end up picking this one for the big bad – Nemesis makes all the impression you could wish for. Should you happen to have played RE 2 remake previously and would like to see more, this game is a fairly safe bet – as long as you bear in mind RE 3 action-packed antics and shorter runtime. Inferior to its predecessor as it may be, falling short of greatness still leaves plenty of room for decency – something this game squarely accomplishes.

I think this game is inferior to RE:2 in nearly every way, except for having marginally more enemy variety and marginally more interesting boss fights. Specifically:
* RE2 had more intricate levels and gradually acquiring key items made backtracking meaningful. RE3 has much simpler levels and thus fewer incentives for being thorough. You have to backtrack for puzzles, but because there's less detail in every level, there's little to do but run straight to your destination
* RE2 had Mr. X which added a lot of tension to the first half of the first playthrough, and disappeared before he got old. Capcom could have at least matched this with Nemesis. Instead he appears in cutscenes for brief setpieces only. 
* RE2 was consistently good from start to finish. RE3's best level is its opening act, which, while not as good as the police station from RE2, had similar pacing where you gradually unlocked a large open level through key items and mission objectives. This set decent expectations for the rest of the game, but those expectations were immediately betrayed by having smaller and less detailed levels for the remainder of the game
* RE2s big antagonist was the situation that Leon and Claire found themselves in + 2 extremely powerful monsters. RE3's antagonist is an extremely powerful monster and an irredeemable human who predictably puts the protagonists in a bind through the entire game and could have and should have been shot by Jill after just one or two interactions.

When it was announced that Resident Evil 3 was getting a remake, I was under the impression that Nemesis would be Mr. X 2.0. That's on me, and I think that expectation set me up for disappointment. Still, I feel like the cutscenes and the opening act showed a lot of promise, and that the remainder of the game failed to deliver. I don't think this game is particularly good, and wouldn't consider this game to be worth the time.

When it was released in 2020, I heard that some people don't like this remake because of it high priced and  they're also cut quite a lot of content from the original one. Almost 3 years after it released, I decided to play it and this is my review.  [u]// click for the full review[/u]

[b]Story[/b]
You will play as "Jill Valentine" attempting to escape from Raccoon City after the whole city was infected by mysterious virus that turn everyone to zombies. But then Nemesis show up, a biological weapon with the determination to hunt down all S.T.A.R.S. members including Jill. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2944327600
It's quite short (around 4-5 hours in the first playthrough) in my opinion but it's also contain a very good and intense story. So, with the price on sale and the quality of it, I really glad I played this game and you should try it out as well as I do.

[b]Graphics[/b]
I'm never disappointed in RE-Engine. It can provide insane lightning and textures with a really good optimization for desktop. Atmosphere around Raccoon City and other places in game give us creepy feeling but also gorgeous in itself. Even though, ray tracing seems not to be as good as I expected. Of course lightning and reflection is better but keep it in mind that it will cost half of your frames.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2944326142
[b]Gameplay[/b]
Survival horror genre games should make player always feeling under pressure and think about every step they're going to make because ammo and healing are limited, fight or run based on resources they have at the moment. But with some explorations, it turns out that you can just killing every thing and still have almost 150 handgun ammo left at the end in standard difficulty also a tons of healing too. Even Nemesis is super weak that can be down with a single hand grenade. This make me questioning myself is this suppose to be in a survival horror genre or should it be in actual a action horror genre instead. Puzzles also not challenging and require a brain to beat. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2944326273
However, it was really fun to play :)

[b]Conclusion[/b]
For me who never play the original version before, this is may not be a good remake but it's definitely a good game. Also recommended to pick it on sale around 80-85%, not worth a full price.

A solid remake with some issues here and there.
The Story is pretty average but it at least gives a decent enough job as to progress the game forward in the way that it does. The characters are also just fine. Jill is decent enough to play as with Carlos being a bit more enjoyable due to his personality being both serious while able to throw a joke here and there. The villain of this game kinda feels like "generic evil Russian" with their goal being about money, but still does an alright job. The coolest character in the game is of course Nemesis which it being this unstoppable force that will do anything to get the job done and feels like an actual threat to Jill. 
The Setting of Raccoon City is really enjoyable to play through with every environment feeling like it has gone through hell and is infested with the undead. From the streets to the underground lab, every location you venture through does a great job at creating a perfect environment. 
Visually, its impressive. Performance was solid throughout my playtime and i had not encountered any bugs or glitches. Art Direction is also on point with it following in the same footsteps that RE2 remake went with. 
Sound and Audio are pretty good with it again following the same queues that the previous remake went with. 
In terms of gameplay, it's more of the same with some little things added on. If you have played the RE2 remake, you'll feel right at home with it being exactly the same when it comes to movement, gun play and inventory. One of the new things that have been added was the dodge/parry ability you can perform that can really help you out in a tough situation. The enemies are also pretty similar with the zombies well.. being the same since the last game, however there are new additions that do switch things up with the way players will approach the game. Nemesis itself is also a really nice challenge for the player with it acting like the Tyrant did in RE2 whereas he cannot be killed, but his abilities differ from Mr X as Nemesis with run at you and even grab you from long distances which can put you in a tough situation. The boss fights are really well done with each fight you have against Nemesis being different and tougher than the last one due to them evolving and becoming more powerful.  
Finally, there are some things that i feel that hold the game back from being as great as the previous remake. First of all, this isn't the full RE3. Instead (for some reason) this game is only a portion of what the original RE3 had to offer which i find confusing as to why they wouldn't go all the way out to give fans a full game and charging a £33 price tag on it. It may not be a full price, but this is still way too much for a 5 hour game (if even). One nit pick i had with the game was the way it overloads you with ammo to the point where it doesn't become an issue whereas RE2 made ammo sparse and forced the player to think carefully with how they would use that resource which was a really fun and challenging way to engage the player. The last nit pick i think i have with the game is the fact that it can be annoying when trying to dodge/parry enemies as sometimes it could be an insta death if done in a certain direction. 
Overall, Resident Evil 3 follows the remake trail quite nicely even with an alright story, but i would recommend getting this game on a discount as i don't agree that a 5 hour experience is worth that much money and the fact that it isn't the full story of the original.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is a solid game that offers an updated take on the classic survival-horror title. While the game introduces some new gameplay mechanics and impressive graphics, it's not quite as strong as its predecessor, Resident Evil 2 Remake.

One of the main criticisms of the game is its length. The campaign can be completed in just a few hours, making it significantly shorter than Resident Evil 2 Remake. This short length can leave players feeling unsatisfied and wanting more. Additionally, the game's pacing can feel rushed, with certain areas and plot points feeling underdeveloped. Another issue with the game is Nemesis, the relentless enemy who pursues the protagonist, Jill Valentine, throughout the game. While he's certainly an imposing threat, his constant appearances can become tiresome and annoying. It feels like the game is trying too hard to make Nemesis a memorable enemy, and as a result, his character design and behavior can come across as contrived.

Overall, while Resident Evil 3 Remake is not as strong as Resident Evil 2 Remake, it's still a solid game that's worth playing for fans of the series. Its short length and contrived enemy may be drawbacks, but the game's updated visuals and gameplay mechanics make it an enjoyable experience.

[h1] As a gamer I recommend it, as a resident evil fan I only feel disappointment :/  [/h1]

This game objectively is good/ ok-ish, but as a remake is really barebones and it lacks in so many ways in comparison with the original and with the remake of resident evil 2. I recommend people to buy it at a heavy discount but this is in no way a complete game, they decided to cut half of the game just to put a multiplayer mode call "RESISTANCE" that was already dead a month after release, Capcom keeps trying to make RE multiplayer games  with no idea of what people want, we want coop game, no call of duty or Dying light clones. Please stop, they ended up hurting the campaign just for the sake of it...

[u]  [b] The good stuff [/b] [/u] 

This game has good qualities to it, this is by no means a bad game (although it was a rip off at 60 dollars at launch so I didn't buy it at that price) so let's start. 

The voice acting is superb, specially Jill, I love seeing a "new game" with her as a protagonist again, I like her new design but I still like her old one a bit more but it's still great, although is sad to see is such a short game :/. Nemesis design is great too, and how racoon city looks is just breathtaking, gameplay is very similar to RE2 but is a bit faster thanks to Jill's new dodge technique. The game is overall fun and I liked it, there are certain story moments that are great but the more I look at it the cons start to pop up more than the pros sadly.

[u]  [b] The bad stuff: The game that it will never be [/b] [/u] 

The remake of this game cuts so many stuff from the original, no clocktower, no park, no exploration, no anticipation, almost no puzzles, no dismemberment system as RE2, and the list can go all day. RE3 remake is extremely linear, the game is filled with scripted moments that makes nemesis to not be a menace at all, in RE2 remake MR.X was a chasing menace made to kill every witness of the racoon city incident, chasing you across the RPD in such unexpected ways and it was terrifying. But in RE3 Nemesis only has 1 real persecutor segment and is stunned with a battery in the most lame way possible, the beast that is meant to kill all the STARS members to avoid spreading the information of the mansion incident, is now just a predictable enemy that doesn't chase you after the first 20 min  of the game.... this is not how is supposed to work and now makes sense why Nemesis is no longer on the title of the game.

The overall map of raccoon city is now limited to just 2 streets and like 3 hallways, this is supposed to be the Racoon city game, but the city segment is so short that is really sad, all the locations are there but they are just cameos  and references, so they are closed in one way or another as if it was a fan game instead of a AAA remake like RE2 was, and after this section nemesis won't chase you anymore because they rushed their "animal" form so quickly for the sake of action set pieces that is no longer menacing, he just becomes a boss everytime you see him :/. So the rocket launcher nemesis is basically limited to a 2 minute sequence... like why??? that is his signature  weapon and is now just a cameo for 5 seconds because is just a run segment so you don't even see him using it. So, going back to the map, now is just City => Sewers => Hospital => Lab and yeah RE2 only had 3.5 locations but all of them were connected via puzzles but in this one they are shorter, they are not connected, you just see them once.

They also completely eliminated the decision making of the original, making this 100% linear in level design and 100% linear in story too. Now you can't choose if you want to explore the city but you can't choose story elements either, so the replayability of this game is non existent. And it sucks because they touched the PTSD of Jill on the beginning of this game but just a little bit, and is such a miss opportunity because if they had included more nightmares and more story choices they could've made a really good exploration of her character, but after the intro she just becomes a bad ass character with no build up :(.

[u] [b] Conclusion [/b] [/u] 

I am negative overall but I actually enjoyed the game, but this game could've been such a masterpiece just as RE2 was, imagining a complete racoon city with interconnected puzzles with nemesis chasing you across all the city as MR.X did , making decisions in the game with multiple endings, giving STARS members more screen time and exploring how umbrella is chasing Jill and how she deals with it thanks to her PTSD and her lack of trust in others.  that is a game I imagined after finishing RE2 remake, and is obvious this game was not made by the same team. This was made by a different team at capcom and it really shows. The RE2 team is working on the RE4 remake so I am excited for that one. That's why I can't recommend it as an RE fan, Capcom gave this game, THE NEMESIS GAME, to a secondary group and took half of their resources to make a trash multiplayer game that was dead a week after release, the lack of time and love put in this proyect is shown if you compare it with RE2 or the original RE3. As a separate thing , yeah is good, is decent. But capcom just chased the easiest and laziest  way to make money, and it sucks this game will always be remembered as the game it will never be :'(.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is an undeniably good-looking game that falls short in a few categories but excels in some others. I haven't played the original title so I won't be making criticisms on certain aspects that have either been removed or expanded upon as I'm yet to experience the 1999 game for myself.

I wrapped up my first playthrough of the story in just under 5 hours, and I've played through it a few more times since, in order to obtain as many achievements and collectables as possible, totalling to 21 hours of playtime. 

Although the story is on the shorter side, I think the shop system that can be found in-game following your first completion of the story adds a level of replay ability that increases the value of the title and makes it easier if you are aiming for 100% as it lets you cut certain corners that would typically make the experience feel drawn out and just not as enjoyable upon a second playthrough.

Another thing I really enjoyed about this game is the amount of colour that can be found throughout raccoon city and how Capcom was able to make it feel as though the city was once a living, breathing entity where thousands of people once went about there everyday lives until all hell broke loose.

My main criticism with the game is the lack of bosses that you go up against throughout its duration. Unlike the resident evil 2 remake where you explore a plethora of different environments and have a boss fight that matches up with the zones theme. The only boss you face in this game is a variation of nemesis that is often reused at least once more. For instance, the clock tower fight where nemesis seems to be in an animal-like state is almost the exact same as the nemesis you face for the first time in the underground facility. 

Overall, I think that the resident evil 3 remake is a game that excels in several categories but also falls short in others. Long?
The Gameplay:
It's a pretty standard, over-the-shoulder shooter. The gameplay is nearly identical to that of the RE2 Remake with some differences. These differences (like the knife taking up a weapon slot in your wheel) are pretty annoying coming right off RE2R, but it's still feels nice enough to play. The puzzles aren't too difficult, and it's fairly puzzle-lite considering it's a Resident Evil game. It's pretty much memory puzzles and mazes.
The good thing too is that (1) you can turn ray-tracing off and rest assured that the game is still going to look awesome and (2) it's flawless from a mechanical standpoint. As-in: no bugs. Ever. It's got that final polish and then some extra shine on top.
The Story:
Now, I won't talk about content cut from the original. I didn't play it. As far as I can tell, this trimmed all the fat without realizing that the fat gave it flavor. All the story content is there, but there's less impact, and the story is more linear overall.
That being said, the story is solid, but it's also a hard one to get wrong. Jill's primary goals are to escape RC and save as many innocents while she does it. Carlos isn't really given much of a story in this at all which is sad since it's his only appearance in the franchise and odd because he's the secondary protagonist. He's effectively a supportive himbo that pops up to remind you how awesome you are.
The ending is tragic with Raccoon City being destroyed (presumably with some people not evacuated yet) but lacks the impact due solely to how linear and resistant to deviation the storyline is. I mean, we're told people are still alive in RC, but we, the player, never see them. These citizens have no material presence to the player, and I like linear stories. It's saying a lot that I think that how linear and rigid it is is a flaw. Even if it was just a few encounters with people other than UBCS, it would have helped in the emotional impact.
Despite this, I like it so, so much. Jill is wonderful, Nemesis is my personal nemesis, and the fall of Raccoon City is horrifyingly sad particularly if you have the repertoire of the first, second, and prequel game under your belt. It's an intrinsic part of the original RE story.
The Problem:
It is very easy to complete this game in an hour and a half. I have, and I don't speedrun. Ever. My first playthough took just over three solely because I took my time and got super turned around. That means that I would literally bleeding minimum wage if I bought it at the 2022 full price. Luckily, I bought it on sale, and I still kind of feel like the playtime hasn't warranted the price. If you aren't 100% into the game and know you'll replay it, this might not be the best game to buy. Luckily, I do really like the game and replay it a lot. It's a nice game night. Something simple that you can play in one sitting.
And Resistance just seems like an attempt to pad out the price. Particularly with the new RE:Verse on the field.
So if you nab it on a wicked sale? It's a good choice. Otherwise, you'll get more playtime-to-price out of RE2R and the (at the time) upcoming RE4R.
And gosh, I hate to leave it like this. It feels like I'm saying don't buy it, but it's so very good, and I love it very much. This just shouldn't be a priority buy, and it's still cheaper than most copies of the original game I was able to track down. Just be in it for the story instead of expecting hours of gameplay to go back to.
