Dear Resident Evil 3, you get a blue thumb because I love your universe, I like the atmosphere in these early episodes of the franchise... But frankly you were that close to getting a red thumb.

Let's get things straight: although you'll most certainly have a good time with this remake, Resident Evil 3 is quite similar to Resident Evil 2, but worse in every possible aspect. Players can clearly feel that this game was rushed to benefit quickly from the success that Resident Evil 2 had: reuse of countless assets, scenes from the original game removed, very short campaign and no mercenaries mode... damn, what a waste. I can't really forgive Capcom for doing this, they could have taken their time to develop a complete game that would have been a real tribute to the original. Instead, the only feeling I had when I finished the game was that I was missing something, that my experience is not complete until I play the original game.

Concretely, the first big problem with Resident Evil 3 Remake is the level design. RE games are known to have a brilliant design in their early stages (mansion, RPD, train, Baker's house...) and get annoyingly more and more linear until the end. With this RE3R, you can skip altogether the first part: after a first hour (at most) where you can still have the illusion of an interesting layout of keys and locked areas, you'll realise that even Raccoon City is not very difficult to figure out and to navigate in a linear fashion. Beyond this point and unlike in RE2R for example where 2/3 of the game are just one, huge map with excellent design, RE3R is split into several segments of a few minutes to one hour each. This effectively linearises the game even more, on top of preventing the player from trying to reach areas/items they couldn't reach immediately.
The gameplay is exactly the same as in RE2R, except for a few downgrades: no blue herb anymore, no possibility of countering zombie attacks with knives or grenades, and fewer (and much more basic !) puzzles... This is in my opinion one big failure here, there is not a single puzzle worth mentioning in this game, and even less so a challenging one. Puzzles are a trademark of the Resident Evil series so I don't really understand what happened there. Finally, if you've already played RE2R, you won't feel much of this tension when playing RE3R. Seeing the layout of the different maps, you can almost predict when a jumpscare is gonna happen and, well, that obviously defeats the purpose of the jumpscares. The staging reuses everything that RE2R had, except that this time, there is no surprise anymore.

But hey, Nemesis saves the party, right ? I am sure that, just like me, many of you dreamt of this RE3R with great cat-and-mouse sequences with the horrific Nemesis, using the same AI (or better) than that of Mr. X in RE2R, in a great level design that makes the hunt even more thrilling, like the RPD did. Well, forget about all of this ! Capcom apparently didn't have enough money to hire Nemesis for the job, so they hired NemeScript, his twin brother suffering a very rare disease that prevents him from moving until he hears the typical sound of a clapperboard. Seriously though, the first 20 minutes of the game are gimmicky cutscenes mixed with QTE where you'll see Nemesis from every possible angle, but for which no AI programming was necessary. Beyond this point, even in the Hardcore mode (the hardest mode available for the first playthrough), you have to really screw up to give Nemesis time to actually chase you down in more than just the main street of Raccoon City. If you play even just a bit cleverly, you'll notice Capcom always leaves a grenade at the right spot so that you can just throw it at him and leave him call for his mama for one minute, time during which you will continue shopping around without caring about his poor soul. And once you're done with this map, Nemesis will never be anything else but a protagonist of other cutscenes, other QTE and some boss fights. This is a huge letdown for all of those like me who were looking forward to epic Mr.X-like moments with Nemesis. If you are looking for this, RE3R is definitely NOT the game for you.

RE3R is still blue-thumb worthy in my opinion because I love this franchise, and probably if RE2R hadn't existed, my view on this game would be a bit different. I still loved the atmosphere of this game, the graphics and especially some very well-made facial animations. But for all the reasons above, I'll have a hard time forgiving Capcom for rushing the development so much, considering that the original game and some of the RE2R elements were great material to do so much better.

Before I go into my review, I really need to make this clear. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE. MAKE SURE IT'S AT LEAST 50% OFF IF YOU'RE INTERESTED IN BUYING THIS GAME.

RE3 Remake is a good game. Unfortunately, it's VERY lackluster compared to it's older sibling (RE2 Remake). The game is shorter than RE2, it lacks puzzles, and to top it all off, Nemesis was wasted potential.

If you've played the RE3 demo that came out a while before the full game, you may remember Nemesis behaving like Mr. X, which was really cool. Only difference was that he was even more relentless and he could even RUN. That sold me back when I played it. However, upon playing the full game, imagine my disappointment when I learned that these instances of Nemesis chasing you like that only covered A FIFTH of the game. A short game, even. After that part, every Nemesis encounter ends up just being a fight around an arena. As he NEVER chases you like Mr. X did in 2, which really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks.

RE2 had plenty of post-game content you could play like "4th Survivor" and "Ghost Survivors". And even then, you could always play the main game again because it has so much replayability. This game however, has ZERO post-game content outside of it's main game and unlockable difficulties. And even so, the replayability of RE3 is significantly weaker than RE2. Granted, this game does have a shop menu where you can get secret weapons, stat coins, infinite weapons and so on, but honestly, that's about it.

Despite all of this, why did I still enjoy this game? Because the gameplay was fun! Having access to an evasive roll for Jill and a counter for Carlos was sick, which also made sense since those two are VERY experienced in combat compared to Leon and Claire in 2, who are just rookies. The story wasn't bad, which doesn't really say much since the story in RE games are not so consistently good (Except RE8 which is the best RE game story wise). And despite me criticizing the replayability of this game, it was still there. But what was most important for me was the atmosphere. The design of Racoon City being thrown amidst chaos was a sight to behold, since in RE2 you were mostly in RPD and at the NEST. There certainly were moments where I enjoyed the view whenever the opportunity was there.

This game had a lot of swings which hit and missed. Fortunately for Capcom, there were enough hits for me to enjoy the game despite its many flaws. But again, I can't in good conscience recommend anyone to buy this game at 60 bucks. It's just not worth it. If this game had post-game content like "Mercenaries" mode, then MAYBE I'd recommend it at full price.

Verdict: Good game, but buy it when it's on sale.

On September 28, 1998, 24 hours prior to the events of Resident Evil 2, former Special Tactics And Rescue Service (S.T.A.R.S.) member Jill Valentine attempts to escape from Raccoon City. Most of the population has been transformed into zombies by an outbreak of the T-virus, a new type of biological weapon secretly developed by the pharmaceutical company Umbrella. On her way to the Raccoon City Police Department, Jill runs into fellow team member Brad Vickers, who is killed by a new enemy. This creature, Nemesis-T Type, is a bio-organic weapon programmed to target surviving S.T.A.R.S. members, witnesses of Umbrella's experiments. As she evades Nemesis, Jill encounters three surviving members of the Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service (U.B.C.S.): Carlos Oliveira, Mikhail Victor, and Nikolai Zinoviev. Nikolai explains to Jill and Carlos that a rescue helicopter can be contacted if they manage to reach the city's Clock Tower and ring the bell.

As they make their way to the tower, Nikolai is presumed dead, while Nemesis corners the remaining members of the group on the cable car headed to the tower. Mikhail sacrifices himself with a grenade, causing the car to crash into the tower's main courtyard and separating Jill and Carlos briefly. At the Clock Tower, Jill summons the helicopter by ringing the Clock Tower's bell before being confronted by Nemesis, which destroys the helicopter and infects Jill with the T-virus. Jill manages to temporarily defeat Nemesis but falls unconscious due to the T-virus. Carlos finds Jill and takes her to safety within the Clock Tower. Three days later, he finds a vaccine for Jill's T-virus infection in a nearby hospital. He then returns and administers it to Jill, saving her.

After she regains consciousness, Jill proceeds towards the Raccoon Park and enters the park caretaker's cabin. There, she runs into Nikolai, who reveals that he is a "supervisor" sent into Raccoon City to gather combat data of Umbrella's bioweapons. Nikolai retreats, and Jill is confronted by a massive worm-like creature. Jill defeats the creature and escapes to an abandoned factory at the rear of the park. Inside the factory, Jill meets up with Carlos, who tells her that the U.S. government is planning to launch a nuclear missile into Raccoon City to eradicate the T-virus infestation. After confronting Nemesis and grabbing a keycard needed to escape, Jill learns from the factory's control tower that the missile attack on Raccoon City has begun, with only a short time left before the city is destroyed.

Depending on the path taken by the player, Jill's final encounter with Nikolai will differ. In one version of the events, Nikolai will attempt to start a gunfight with Jill, only to be taken by surprise by Nemesis and killed. In another event, Nikolai will hijack Jill's intended escape chopper, and the player must choose to either reason with Nikolai or destroy the helicopter. If Jill negotiates with Nikolai, he reveals that he has killed the other supervisors and boasts about collecting the bounty placed on Jill by Umbrella before escaping. Regardless of Nikolai's fate, Jill makes her way to the rear yard and confronts Nemesis one last time. After an intense battle, Jill defeats Nemesis with the help of a prototype railgun before meeting up with Carlos and escaping the city via a helicopter. If the previous escape chopper was stolen by Nikolai, Jill and Carlos will instead meet up with S.T.A.R.S. Alpha Team's weapons specialist Barry Burton, who helps them escape in his helicopter. The nuclear missile vaporizes Raccoon City, and Jill swears revenge on Umbrella. A newscast then briefly details the destruction, and offers condolences for the lost lives.

Talk about mixed feelings for a game...
On the one hand, it looks fantastic, the guns feel pretty good, zombies are legit threatening and sound design and voice acting is great. 
On the other hand, most of the boss fights are just not fun and sometimes downright annoying, sometimes the controls just seem to wig out (why am I sometimes just not aiming, even though I'm clearly holding the trigger?) and the main enemy of the game, Nemesis, is not nearly as interesting or threatening as he should be (Mister X in the RE2 remake felt much more dangerous, at least on first playthrough).
Also some design decision are truly baffling. While moving certain parts around (such as the police station being later in the game) was actually a great decision in my opinion, some of the coolest and most interesting parts of the original RE3 were straight up removed, such as the clock tower (my favourite part of the original) and most of the first city part. Instead we get a slightly longer lab section, that just feels way less interesting and out of place. And [spoiler]fricking Barry was removed from the end (wth Capcom?)[/spoiler]. Also certain parts of the game were handled in cutscenes, and could have easily been short playable sections or mini-boss fights. And finally, the last part [spoiler]of Carlos gameplay in the hosptial[/spoiler] seems like another attempt to recreate the tension of the famous "house defense" from RE4. But it falls utterly short, it was annoying, unfun and my least favourite sequence of the entire game. Really bad implementation.

So it's not a bad game overall and it looks great. But compared to the RE2 Remake, it falls short of completely capturing and improving on the original and also is shorter, as replayability is much lower without a "B Campaign" with a second character. I do recommend it. but before you play this, check and play the RE2 remake. If you really like it, get this game (on sale) to get a game that plays very similar, with a slightly different setting, feel and of course story. If you didn't really feel the RE2 Remake, you should probably give it pass, as it does nothing better, just different (and sadly some things worse)...

I love Resident Evil. I've played the originals and remakes to death, getting the highest rankings in all of them (including CV). Of the OG RE games, RE3 is my favorite, so I was both excited and wary about playing this game, especially with everyone complaining about its length.

Honestly, its length is not the issue. The requirements for getting the S ranking for most of the difficulties is 2 hours, which is about the same as the other Resident Evil games. The issue is its linearity - this is what makes the game feel short, especially in your first playthrough. Additionally, some of the content from the original is removed or remixed (the Clock Tower segment is cut completely; Carlos goes to RPD instead of Jill). So I understand when some people feel like it doesn't live up to the original.

What's more confusing to me are the negative comparisons with RE2 remake. I love RE2 remake, but I don't feel this game falls short against it in any way. There is more variety when it comes to enemies and environments, the game looks better, Jill is hotter than Claire, and Carlos is cooler than Leon (especially once you equip him with his original costume). It's not shorter than RE2. If people's criticisms about 3 compared to 2 is what's keeping you from getting this, don't let them stop you - it's just as good.

Resident Evil 3's long-awaited reimagining, and the direct follow-up to the absolutely incredible Resident Evil 2 reimagining, ended up being a tad bit disappointing in my honest opinion. I didn't think it was bad in any aspect, but it didn't really go above and beyond at any point either. Because of the varying degrees of success each aspect of this game had, and because I'm particularly passionate about this title playing it a ton on console, I want to talk about every aspect of it. For the sake of simplicity, this review will be divided into 5 categories: Graphics, Audio, Gameplay, Story, and Conclusion/Final thoughts. Without further ado, let's talk about this controversial title.

[b]WARNING: This review will contain some spoilers on late-game enemies, bosses, and story events. For convenience and hopefully not worsening someone's first playthrough with spoilers, I'll censor any mid to late-game information (I consider mid-game to be after escaping the city streets as Jill and playing as Carlos for the first time).[/b]

[h1]Graphics[/h1]

Oh boy, do I have a lot to say about the graphics. As expected, this game looks excellent. The assets and characters look great and realistic, the lighting perfectly compliments the mood the game wants to portray, and the enemies are just as unique and well-designed as the ones present in both RE2 and the original RE3. The human characters were mo-capped and modeled on real people's faces, which make them look incredibly realistic and seem like people that'd actually exist. The new monsters, namely the Ne-Alpha Zombies and [spoiler]the Paleheads[/spoiler] are interesting new additions that spice up the gameplay. The modern designs for the original monsters, especially Nemesis, Gamma Hunters, and [spoiler]Beta Hunters[/spoiler] are phenomenal. Gamma Hunters in particular immediately became my favorite enemy from this game, simply because of how much cooler and scarier they look in the remake, as opposed to the silly frog-looking things from the original. I think [spoiler]Nemesis Stage 3 was a wildly improved final boss, both in behavior and design, as opposed to the kinda plain blob from the original.[/spoiler] I did have an issue with [spoiler]Nemesis Stage 2, though. It turning into a big quadrupedal dog creature was a bit of a step down from the bipedal Nemesis with tentacles in place of one arm we saw in the classic. If he had just stayed bipedal until the final boss battle, I'd have liked him a lot more.[/spoiler]

[h1]Audio[/h1]

Great as always. Sounds had very similar attention to detail present in the RE2 remake. Gunshots and monster noises are more echoed in larger areas, and tighter in smaller rooms. Jill and Carlos, as well as the many side characters, had talented and believable voice actors that clearly had a good deal of passion when voice acting for the game. Nemesis' new voice is more appropriately deep and grainy, and adds to the immersion. Every sound fits well, and nothing seemed out of place.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

RE3's gameplay is pretty similar to RE2, being the direct sequel. Same over-the-shoulder camera angle, same enemy weakness system, and same exploration and item collection systems. However, this game is WAY more action-oriented than the original. This isn't necessarily bad, and there are still some good horror moments scattered around, [spoiler]mostly being the RPD and Hospital sections as Carlos,[/spoiler] but I would have still liked a little more horror and a little less ridiculous satirized action. As little as 30 seconds into the game, you encounter Nemesis, who immediately tries to kill you. Many more enemies, much more ammo, and new strong weapons are available. The initial character selection and 4 separate playthroughs are no longer available, only occasionally swapping between the two main characters in one run, which I didn't really like. I loved the branching paths Leon and Claire had in their playthroughs, and the swapping between Jill and Carlos just seemed a little too much like an easy way out. Speaking of easy ways out, why is so much content cut from the original. In particular, the entire clock tower exploration segment of the original was cut, with the Nemesis Stage 2 fight being the only remaining portion, and the Grave Digger boss was left out completely. I understand the newer RE games are made very short intentionally, to increase replayability, but is one additional boss enemy THAT much more to ask for? One thing I absolutely loved about the game, and by far my favorite aspect to this day, is [spoiler]the unlockable new difficulties, Nightmare and Inferno. Nightmare and Inferno are pretty much identical, minus the tougher enemies and less save opportunities in Inferno, so I'll group them together. The sheer amount of unique new enemy and item placements in this mode is so awesome, and a huge improvement to the "2nd run" from RE2. Nemesis Stage 3 becomes a ridiculously aggressive and difficult final boss, even with the infinite rocket launcher, and actually fun to fight compared to the sad pushover we fought in the previous 3 difficulties.[/spoiler] Overall, I think the gameplay is just more of what RE2 did, which was a smart choice from the developers.

[h1]Story[/h1]

This story ties itself into RE2's story much more clearly than the classics. I liked seeing [spoiler]the fate of Marvin and the reasoning for a few of the things that happened in the RPD,[/spoiler] and I liked that RE3 took place before, during, and after the events of RE2. As for the not tied-in things, Jill is a police officer with some PTSD from the events of RE1 (though I wish they didn't sexualize her as much as they did, adding breast physics and zooming in on her ass while she army crawled through small spaces were absolutely unnecessary), and Carlos is a forgettable wacky guy that can shoot a gun, and is literally never ever mentioned in future RE games. Nemesis isn't given any further character development, which was a huge missed opportunity considering he's quite literally the only boss throughout the whole game and by a colossal margin the most popular and memorable character in Resident Evil history. Files are an intriguing bit of world-building and lore to keep you invested in the RE franchise, but aren't really necessary to understanding the RE canon.

[h1]Conclusion/Final Thoughts[/h1]

Looking back at the game 2 years after, I thought it was kind of good. It doesn't hold a candle to almost any other mainline RE titles, obviously, but it's a pretty good time and something you wouldn't really get bored of, being a lot shorter than other mainline Resident Evils. The graphics are just as stunning as the game's predecessor, and the story isn't atrocious considering Resident Evil has never been strong in the story department. This game is NOT like Resident Evil 2 Remake. It is much faster and more action-based. If you are looking for an investigative adventure horror like Resident Evil 2 Remake, do not get this game.

You can’t shake off enemies if you are grabbed. There are multiple more aggressive enemies and they are faster than you can run, or they can attack you from a distance. It is a different pace of gameplay than Resident Evil 2 Remake. There are still areas you can explore and collect keys, but be sure to backtrack early and pick up things you are interested in as soon as you find them. Because if you progress too far in an area and trigger the stalker enemy, you can forget any ideas of exploration or item collecting, the game is on rails now and whatever you missed you probably won’t be able to get it.

The stalker enemy, Nemesis, is not like Mr. X. He is horrible. He is faster than Jill can run so you are forced to deal with him every time he shows up. You cannot kite him around like Mr. X because he will just jump over the geometry and be right in front of you. If you do manage to out-do his pathing in a small area, he will just instantly grab you with a tentacle and drag you to him. Sometimes Nemesis will do a shout that stuns Jill, and will then do combos on her, which is death if you are not at full health. Jill also gets stunned between the hits, so if you are caught by one you will lose a ton of health. Also, common zombies can grab Jill and kill her while this is happening. Lastly, the only way to deal with Nemesis, and most enemies in this game, is to use the dodge button in a very small frame window. It’s not like other Resident Evil games. It’s a mechanic that belongs in a fighting game or other hyper-twitchy reaction-based game. It is terrible.

Do not get this game if you want more of Resident Evil 2 Remake. Do get this game if you liked the action of Resident Evil 6 but wanted it in the Resident Evil 2 setting.

I should stress before hand that while I am recommending this title, this could've really gone either way, and the only reason I'm not giving it a thumbs down is because the game does just enough right, even if it does so much wrong.

As it was developed alongside RE2 Remake (mainly towards the end of 2make's development/release cycle) it shouldn't be a surprise that this plays very similar to that. It does have some slight changes to make it more action oriented in comparison, mainly with the removal of the Self-Defense items and replacing it with the dodge system, which credit where credit is due definitely feels more functional compared to the original RE3's dodge system.

However, the game suffers from two massive problems; incredibly linear, and surprisingly short run-time. While 2make was missing some stuff compared to the original RE2, that remake at least still felt like a complete experience. With 3make on the other hand though you can feel the missing gaps in terms of content. Sure, the hospital section is definitely improved (minus the horde battle at the end) but otherwise the game feels very bereft of content. What's even stranger though is that the developers went out of their way to design and program things in here that are then barely used. The dodge/punch system in itself is a n example especially in comparison to 2make, but even newly designed and programmed enemies that function very differently are used for an area or two at most before being ignored for the rest of the game, which begs the question why go to all that effort. The same also applies to many of the weapons, especially with some of the new ammo mixing mechanics and with some weapons immediately getting their weapon upgrade parts one room immediately after getting the weapon, which again begs several questions of "why bother." It also doesn't help that Nemesis, the namesake for the game, feels very underutilised and ultimately forgettable as an antagonistic force.

The game's point system makes it seem like the main appeal for this game is to try and beat it over and over to keep collecting points to unlock more options, which in itself is not necessarily a bad idea, it would just need more actual options to make that seem worthwhile (ie other weapon types, costume varieties, extra modes, etc.) So while this game is definitely lacking and hard to recommend, I can't exactly hate it either because for all its faults when it works it works, and fundamentally it's not a bad game. RE engine is still fighting the good fight, it's nice to see more of Racoon in this engine (even if there realistically should've been more of it though) and character design feels overall better/more consistent compared to 2, especially with the faces. More than the rest, this is definitely something you would wait to get on sale, as it's original price point is frankly way too high relative to the amount of content you're getting with this one

After playing this game pretty much back to back with the Resident Evil 2 remake, I can definitely give the Resident Evil 3 remake a strong recommendation! I loved it, and if you liked RE2make, I think there's a very good chance you'll like this too. 

While it's the same engine with fundamentally the same gameplay, RE3 does lean a little bit more into the action side of things, with some more linear scripted sequences, and fewer puzzles. Combat is also tweaked. Sub-weapons work a bit differently, and there's a new dodging and counter system that's very risk vs. reward, and satisfying when used well.  Compared to RE2, I didn't feel quite as vulnerable while playing as Jill in RE3. While that vulnerability was part of the appeal of RE2 for me, I don't see it as a detractor for RE3. In my opinion, it's interesting to see the same system being used in a slightly different way, giving the game its own identity. I liked both styles equally, and they compliment each other well.

The high praise for the visual presentation and overall atmosphere from RE2 again applies here. Everything is extremely well-staged. The Nemesis sequences are relentlessly intense, and Raccoon City is superb, both aesthetically and as an example of great level design. I found the way that RE3 takes place at more-or-less the same time as RE2 very cool, especially when playing them one after the other. Again, both of these remakes compliment each other well, and I know that alternative perspectives on the same event is a key part of this series' history and appeal. In terms of story and character, I liked Jill's run more than Leon's from RE2, but liked it slightly less than Claire's.

There are some minor caveats to this review. Firstly, I am a newcomer to the franchise, and have not played any of the games released prior to these most recent remakes. From what I understand, RE3make is less faithful to the original than RE2make is, but that's not something I can really comment on in detail, neither pro nor con. Secondly, I know that this game's length has been an issue for some. Depending on your playstyle, It's about as long or slightly shorter than a single RE2 run (i.e. just Leon or Claire, not both). The length doesn't personally bother me, as I've recently been craving short but detailed gaming experiences, but the shortness should be brought up regardless. Unless you're the type of player who wants to engage in multiple replays (to be fair, the game is very replayable), then the value of this game at full retail price might be a point of contention. Personally I think it's worth it just for how well-made it is, but full disclosure, I did buy both RE2make and RE3make in a sale bundle, so that might influence my thoughts here.

These caveats aside though, I really liked this game, and can't wait to see what comes next.

[h1]PROs:[/h1]
✅ A fun, polished, and straightforward action-oriented experience.
✅ The persistent Nemesis boya is fun
✅ Several welcome quality-of-life improvements (quick looting, better item management).
✅ A new dodge mechanic that adds to the fast-paced action.
✅ A great unlockable system that encourages a few playthroughs.
✅Kinky parasite

[h1]CONs:[/h1]
❌ A significant step down in atmospheric horror compared to RE2 Remake.
❌ Feels like a downgrade in several areas (gore, physics, immersive sound).
❌ Counter mechanic gone (nade/knife)
❌ I personally found this version of Jill to be annoying.
❌ Feels too short and content-light for its full price.

[h1]Comments:[/h1]
It's impossible to talk about this game without comparing it to the masterpiece that was RE2 Remake. While RE3 is a fun and polished action game in its own right, it feels like a step back in almost every area that made RE2:RE so special.

RE3 trades the slow-burn survival horror of RE2 for action. This isn't itself bad, just a matter of preference, but I personally missed the tense atmosphere. The difference is perfectly captured by the main antagonists: while Mr. X was a terrifying, unpredictable stalker, Nemesis feels more like a scripted, pestering dog you take for a walk. He's fun, but not scary.

The gameplay has some welcome quality-of-life improvements, like quicker looting and a new dodge mechanic. However, the trade-off is the removal of the excellent defensive counter-system from RE2, which I felt wasn't worth the trade-off. The game also feels like a visual and technical downgrade in some surprising ways. The gore and physics are toned down, corpses despawn, and the sound design is far less immersive.

Ultimately, while the story is straightforward fun, the game is incredibly short and feels more like a full-priced DLC for RE2 than a complete, standalone title. It was enjoyable for a few runs to unlock everything, but it's definitely not worth the initial price tag and is best picked up on a sale.

[h2]Non-Nostalgia Review. It’s Not As Bad As People Say It is. Recommended On Sale: 8/10[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[i][b]For Linux and Steam Deck:[/b]Gold Experience. Requires Glorious Eggroll’s custom Proton-6.18-GE-2 or newer.[/i]
[hr][/hr]
Hot take, I prefer this to RE7 or RE8. Not having played the 1999 Resident Evil 3, I don’t have any of the hang-ups that many of the veteran RE3 players have with the game and just play the game as is. That’s not to say that the complaints from veteran players are illegitimate – they certainly are valid. 

However, reviewing the game without any baggage I can say that the game in of itself, isn’t bad, in fact, it’s rather good. Is it better than Resident Evil 2 Remake? No, but it’s still a fun game, a story that continues directly from RE2R and has a good cast characters. 

Is it perfect? No. The controls don’t really lend too well for the sort of action RE3R is gunning for but it works well enough. The puzzles are nowhere as interesting as it should be and the map is much too linear but the curated linear levels are done well enough to at least give you 8 hours or good fun. 

And yes, just like RE7, the game is kind of short. You can complete the game in 8 hours, so if you’re the value-conscious type, it is far better to get this during a sale rather than buying it full price. But all in all, I’d recommend this game no problems. 
[hr][/hr]
[h3]What’s Great[/h3]

[table]
[tr]
[td]1. Graphics is excellent. [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]2. Voice-acting is great. [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]3. Paced really good for an action-game.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]4. Still retains the Resident Evil atmosphere and feel despite the heavy action.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

If it’s one thing you can depend on Capcom, is making really good looking characters. Jill has never looked more stunning, even the side-characters like Carlos and Nikolai looks good. What’s even better is that the voice-acting really sells the performance. Nicole Tompkins really sells it as a veteran cop caught in a conspiracy. Jeff Schine makes a great debut as Carlos Oliviera before returning as Chris Redfield in RE Village, and Nell Newbon makes a convincing mercenary as Nikolai Ginovaef. 

Make no mistake, RE3R is an action heavy game. There are a lot of set pieces and gunplay and while the controls, movement and enemies don’t exactly lend well for an action in 2021, how the game is paced is really good. The action is interspersed with moments of puzzle-solving and none overstay their welcome, in fact some of them feels too short. Amazingly though, Capcom manages to do all this while still retaining the familiar Resident Evil creepy atmosphere and feel. 
[hr][/hr]
[h3]What Could’ve Been[/h3]

[table]
[tr]
[td]1. Nemesis could’ve been more threatening and his fights could’ve been better. [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]2. Controls and movement are sluggish for an action game. [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]3. Levels are too short. [/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

A valid complaint here is Nemesis being disappointing. For such an imposing figure that appears frequently during gameplay, he doesn’t really evoke a sense of dangerous predation that Mr X did in RE2R. The set pieces that involve escaping from him are just uninteresting quick time events. 

Secondly, for such a heavy action game, the controls and movement feels sluggish. Enemies including zombies, hunters, face-huggers, pale-faces and especially Nemesis move and attack fast with wide and long reach. In contrast, Jill and Carlos is slow and maybe I’m wrong, but their dodge skill doesn’t even have i-frames and technically isn’t a dodge, rather they’re just sped up movements. 

Why couldn’t they just give us faster walking and running speed, replace the dodge with an actual roll as well as include a dedicated melee attack like a round-house kick from RE4. That would’ve made a great action game. 

Lastly, the levels in RE3R is just too short. No, I don’t mean the moment to moment gameplay, I mean the level itself feels small. I realize that the original RE3 had the clock tower section that has been cut in RE3R and even never having played the original RE3 I can feel that there is something missing, and it gives validity to a lot of veteran players complaints. 
[hr][/hr]
[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
Is it that bad? No, it’s not. On the contrary, it’s good but it’s not as good as it could be. I wouldn’t necessarily recommend this game at full price, but I definitely would recommend this game on sale because on the whole, RE3R does a lot of things well.

My original review of this game was negative and I had given it a thumbs down and didn't recommend it. However, I recently started playing this game again and have put a lot of hours into it and so I felt like I should update my review to reflect my most recent thoughts and feelings about this game.

If you would like to read my original review you can do so, I left it below the dashed line. I do think that what I originally wrote was valid and should be taken into consideration, however I think this game is ultimately a good/great game after all and I wanted to elaborate on that.

First off, something I didn't mention in my original review is that this game has great graphics and presentation. I think the new RE engine is great and I find myself constantly impressed with the quality and results.

Another thing I would like to address is this game has great replay value. I know some reviewers have complained about the length of the game being too short but it's got some fun unlockables and achievements as is typical for the Resident Evil franchise. I've always wondered why more games don't take the approach the RE franchise has had for replay-ability as I think it's the optimal way to go. Also, regarding the length of the game, it's actually setup well for doing speed runs, which can be a fun way to squeeze more value out of a game after all the achievements and unlockables are completed. 

This game also has a cool feature that is actually fundamentally important in some of the higher difficulties. This is the dodge mechanism that previous RE's don't have. At first I thought it was a gimmick but it's something that is very useful and I highly recommend mastering it. There is an item that you can unlock after beating the game that will make your dodge even better and I recommend carrying that around with you so you can maximize your dodge-ability. I recently did a speed run where I beat the game with only the knife and I was able to dodge through the entire first section without needing to use any weaponry. However once you get to the sewers you can't just simply dodge past the Gammas or they will literally swallow you whole.

And finally, I had some massive complaints about Nemesis in my original review, however with some experience he becomes easier to deal with. I will say that on the two hardest difficulties (both are unlockables and are not available in the beginning) Nemesis's final form is brutal and cheap. You will have to completely master the dodge to have any chance against him at these difficulties. 

All in all, this is actually one of my favorite Resident Evil's now and I do highly recommend it. For me it's a top 3 Resident Evil, along with the REmake and REmake 2. I really take my time with games, but this one was done in a few evenings. I never played the original so I can't compare it to that, but it is a downgrade from RE2 Remake in every possible way to me. 

It looks gorgeous and Jill is just wow! Loved Carlos and his fluffy hair too. The environments are also very well done. It ran very well on my PC. But it isn't scary. It isn't satisfying at all. The dodge mechanic is neat until you realise it trivializes most of the zombie encounters. The boss is boring. Some of the boss fights are of the run around in a circle variety which is lame. I don't know how it went in the original, but after a while seeing Jill getting bounced around from cutscene to cutscene just got dull. The Nemmy does look great though. My main complaint is the short length and the lack of puzzles and exploration.

The amount of hate and criticism this game has gotten is pretty amusing to be honest, and a lot of it is blown way out of proportion. But that's just the age we live in currently, people form their opinions quickly based on very little information and either ride that hype or hate train until it derails, and nothing can convince them otherwise. 

That being said, some of the criticism is justified: 

- The game is less good than its predecessor, RE2 remake. 
- Nemesis is a bit underwhelming.
- There is some cut content from the original, most notably the Clock Tower and the Park areas. 
- A bit too many quick time events. 
- The game is probably too short to justify a full price $60 price tag. 

But, here are some strong points about the game: 

- The graphics are incredible, especially the lighting effects. 
- The ambiance of the game at the start is well done, you really like feel like you are experiencing a city falling apart. 
- The soundtrack is excellent. 
- The voice acting is great and the characters feel alive, especially when compared to the how corny the original was. 

Mostly importantly though, the game is a blast to play. Whereas RE2 was more about conserving ammo, RE3 allows you to blast the hell out of everything you see. The weapons are fun to use and combat is satisfying.

The last thing I will say is that there is way too much rose-tinted nostalgia about the original RE3. I played the original when it came out and I love it, but it had its weaknesses. The choice system that was in the game was pretty pointless,  encounters with nemesis were a huge chore as the dodge system was broken and you would end up spending most of the fight shooting him off screen, and the dialogue was laughably bad. 3make is the most barren interpretation of a Resident Evil experience maybe ever. A surface level attempt at recreating the successes of RE2make with none of the same reverence for the source material. Many people have already talked about how it cuts content from the original and how it ruins Nemesis by restricting his appearance to scripted encounters, and all of that is true, but what's even more frustrating imo is the complete amnesia Capcom seems to have towards the original game's atmosphere and pacing. OG RE3 seems to have been retroactively pinned by many as "the moment Resident Evil started becoming action games" because of its increased emphasis on combat and more challenging encounters, but this ignores the fact that it also has some the scariest sequences in the franchise, tight inventory management mechanics, and a memorably tense atmosphere. It is a horror-thriller experience through and through.

3make ignores all of this creates a linear action game with horror window dressing. It's beautiful and uses the same general gameplay template of 2make, but feels so lazy and hollow in comparison. Locations lack character and believability, and combat scenarios are so by-the-books it often feels more like a playable version of a Resident Evil-themed haunted house ride. It's also dumb easy except for occasional cheap difficulty spikes, like bosses that require you to manipulate the game's camera in unnatural ways in order to dodge its attacks with the required hyper-precision (a problem that would appear again in RE Village). 

I can't say it's horrible, but considering it's only about 4 hours and feels mostly meaningless, I absolutely can't recommend it above the original RE3. This may honestly be my least favorite RE game, even more than RE6. At least 6 felt like it had character and intent.

Having played through RE 0, RE 1 & 2 remakes, I can say without a doubt this is the most fun I've had so far playing this series. Is it the best? No. Is it a fine time that offers high replayability with very fun and sometimes scary gameplay? Absolutely.

To quickly get the negatives out of the way, the zombie graphical details have definitely been downgraded from RE 2 Remake, which is a shame, as that game's dismemberment system and remaining bodies was very satisfying, This was probably done to save on memory resources, as there are more enemies onscreen at a time, and the areas are larger. However, that results in it's own problems, as the RE engine has trouble rendering far objects at full framerate. This was in RE 2, but was far less noticeable due to the map layout. Yet another issue I have with this game is that it is definitely less scary than the previous two, and while I know that it is an intentional design choice in keeping with the original, it is beginning the trend of more action oriented gameplay that I know the series became known for for a while. Also, a small but annoying feature is the ability for the hunter enemies to one-hit kill you, which isn't a problem with the Gammas, but for the Hunter β's, they are fast, can stun you, and have a very deadly one hit kill animation. Lastly, the cut content and reduced Nemesis encounters do hurt this game's replaybility, and I absolutely wish they were included, as they would have made an already great game even better.

But regardless of those issues, I still think this is a great game. The gameplay is even smoother this time around, with an additional dodge mechanic that adds a whole other level of strategy to the game. Nemesis, when he is his first form, is incredibly terrifying and knuckle-whitening. He plays great, has a very well made moveset, and is unrelenting. Even when he simply becomes a series of bossfights, they are well designed, and make you feel like a badass. The fact that you can unlock a series of extras to have in the game on repeat playthroughs provides it with a lot of replay value, giving you that cathartic release when you drop Inferno zombies in 1 clip instead of all your ammo. Despite my saying that this game isn't as scary as RE 2, there are 3 areas within the game that are as if not more scary than RE 2, and those areas are the power plant, the RPD, and the hospital. These areas capture that isolated and spine-chilling feeling from the previous game. However, much of that tension can be found in the music, which brings me to my next point: the music is amazing! Unlike RE 2, where the only memorable music is the boss music, this whole game features absolutely incredible tracks, some pulled straight from the original. Lastly, the graphics are great. Besides from those few issues mentioned above, this is one of the best looking games out there right now. All I can say is that this is a great game, and if you were a fan of RE 2 Remake, or the original RE 3, I'd say give this a go. Just know some content is missing, it's not as scary as it's forefathers, and Nemesis isn't as quite ever-present as Mr. X might make you think.

Plays more like a junky side campaign for Resident Evil Two than an actual game of its own. Boring story, clumsy combat and repetitive environments.


As the game opens it establishes a fairly interesting backstory for the protagonist, however that backstory becomes largely irrelevant as the plot just becomes: there's zombies, don't die. That's basically the story of this game. There are zombies. Do not die. In five hours the game fails to construct any kind of more interesting overarching narrative than that nor does it really fill the survival struggle with any kind of engaging character interactions; besides Carlos aggressively flirting with Jill right to start. Which is just creepy and off-putting.

The combat is similar to that of the previous game to an extent, fairly rudimentary shooting with little gameplay variety. In an attempt to make the combat more interesting since it's being recycled into another game; the developers added a dodge feature. Except it's not really a dodge feature it's more of a quick-time-event disguised as a reactive dodge. While playing as Jill players can press the dodge button to stumble rapidly in a direction to avoid attacks. However this dodge has no invulnerability frames and thus often fails to actually protect players from harm. To trigger the real dodge, which has invulnerability frames, players need to press the dodge button right before an attack reaches them. Except this mechanic isn't explained to the player at all; which makes the game a frustrating mess until it is learned.

Many enemies in the game will ram themselves into the player's face then trigger an attack, forcing the player to perform their quick-time-event dodge just to avoid it. Until the player realizes how this works they are potentially doomed to take damage over and over because they don't understand their primary method of avoiding harm. Even when learning how the mechanic works, players must still learn the timing on each individual enemy attack to be able to utilize the dodge fully. This perpetual system of trial and error creates a spectrum of extremes where the player either cannot dodge attacks at all because they do not know the timing, or cannot get hit at all because they now know the timing and thus can consistently dodge.

There's also no stun-lock protection in this game, so players can straight up just get stun-locked into a game over by certain enemies or groups of enemies. Enemies may randomly attack twice in a row when a dozen other times they only attacked once, or have artificially accurate tracking on their attacks, or have attacks with basically no telegraph that are consequently impossible to dodge at close range in a game that is constantly about fighting in close quarters. The game hides enemies around corners, or has them approach from out of sight on multiple occasions to ambush the player and lock them into an unfair grapple. Unlike the previous game there's no way to counter grapples, players just have to mash a button to force the enemy off them. Except even if players press the button extremely fast they still take damage anyways, which makes the whole mechanic of being forced to mash the button at all feel pointless. 

Players are also constantly forced to stop and repeatedly stab every zombie they knock down, to check if the zombie is actually dead or not while also conserving ammunition. Resulting in a decent chunk of the gameplay becoming consumed by the player rapidly spamming their knife attack on most enemies at least once or twice to avoid future danger.

In general the combat in this game is very punishing yet so clumsy, cramped and cluttered that the game mostly ends up punishing players for its own mechanical shortcomings. Playing on the easier difficulties may reduce the impact of these unfortunate moments but they still occur all the same, and playing on the harder difficulty actively makes these situations a defining aspect of the gameplay experience.

Another baffling design choice was adding a weapon into the game that is borderline necessary for at least one boss fight, but carrying that weapon is completely optional and thus the player may end up in that boss fight without it. Yet if players do bring this weapon they can amass enough ammunition to basically stun-lock certain bosses and trivialize the fight. The also game has multiple moments where it transitions from cutscene to gameplay abruptly with no warning at all yet punishes players with an immediate game over if they don't react instantly. Multiple achievements in the game even spoil upcoming plot elements.

Not only does this game include multiple maps that are reminiscent of those from the previous game, which makes the atmosphere feel stale, but it also has players outright return to one that was in the previous game.


Repetitive and terribly balanced combat with an emphasis on meaningless quick-time-events that overshadow the already skimpy shooter combat system. Strung together by a monotonous, empty story with little to no intrigue or depth. All of which takes place in very same looking generic environments, at least one of which is directly ripped from the previous game under the guise of this story taking place at approximately the same time. Which doesn't even make sense as the environments are slightly changed from the previous game in ways that canonically do not coincide with the fact that this is supposedly happening at around the same time.

This game doesn't even manage to just be a bland repetition of the previous game, as the combat system has now been skewed around jumping through quick-time-event hoops yet this core mechanic is not explained to the player nor does it properly work some of the time. And even when it does work; it's just boring. Now the sensation of blandness has transformed into the feeling that this is just a really overpriced and badly balanced DLC campaign for the previous game.

First, a little about me. I have loved Resident Evil since 1998. To me, all of 13 of the mainline/"numbered" games (Code Veronica included, since it is basically 2.5) are at least decent (RE6, RE0), while others are amazing game changers (RE2, RE4). RE3 Remake is easily in dead last at #13, beating out the very contentious RE6 and the less contentious RE5. There are a number of reasons why.

1. The two highest difficulties aren't unlocked by default. This isn't a grave sin by itself, but it amplifies the pain of the next reason.

2. The game is far too linear. Even with Nightmare and Inferno attempting to shuffle things up, all of the key items tied to progression are in the same spots. To put it in perspective, I beat the game 4 times, once on Assisted, then Hardcore, Nightmare, and Inferno, all S rank without guides. My slowest time was 1:42:20. That is still 3 minutes faster than the shortest par time for S rank which is 1:45:00 on Hardcore. The par time for Nightmare and Inferno goes up to 2:00:00, but I did both of those in around half the time. The 28 hours I have played is artificially inflated due to AFKing with the game running. I'd put my actual time around the 12 hour mark.

3. [Spoilers ahead] Nemesis is pretty limp compared to Mr. X from RE2 Remake or Alcina from Village... hell, even Mr. X in RE2 or Nemesis in original RE3 do a better job of being intimidating and/or difficult. This is made worse by the fact that Nemesis is the only boss in the game. Sure, the fights are different-ish and other RE games have recurring bosses, but this is the only RE that has a single boss. On top of that, all of the fights are rather simple... except...

4. [Spoilers continue] Stage 3 Nemesis, the final boss. Someone at Capcom played Dark Souls, took one look at Bed of Chaos, then thought "You know what RE3 needs? This piece of garbage! Everyone adored this fight, right?" There isn't an encounter before this one that requires you to use the perfect dodge mechanic. You can get by without it on Nightmare or lower, you might need healing items though. As for me, I did every run without healing, save for the one time you are forced to. Inferno Stage 3 Nemesis was one of the most tedious boss fights I have ever experienced. If you are trying for S rank (5 saves or less, in time), it is almost mandatory that you take a save before that encounter. Leave the no save runs for after you have practiced Inferno Stage 3 Nemesis a ton. That is, if you even want to play the game again after mopping up S rank Inferno. Which leads us to...

4. No drive towards replayability. The only reason I slogged through 4 times was to complete all of the Records and I want to 100% every RE game on Steam. There were a couple Records that required me loading a save and downing enough zombies with a particular weapon, but the amount of grind required for that was minimal. Completing all Records gives you the exact amount of points needed for all the Shop unlockables. Another segue!

5. Where you at, unlockables? A whopping ONE costume for Jill and none for Carlos, unless you pay real money. A few underwhelming, non-infinite weapons. Some passive-granting inventory items that are alright I guess, but don't switch up the gameplay in any significant way.

6. The cardinal sin of RE3 Remake: No Mercenaries or alternate modes of any kind. This falls under replayability and unlockables as well, but the lack of modes is exactly why this game should have been $30 at launch. It feels like a RE2 Remake DLC rather than a full-sized game. Some of you may be saying "Hey, RE3 comes with Resident Evil Resistance!" To that, I say that it may as well come with a giant box sent to your house. A box that contains a spring-loaded boxing glove with spikes attached to it. A glove that targets nothing but the crotch. I'd talk about RER, but this review is long enough as it is.

4/10, better than a nonstop beating to the groin. Glad I waited for a sale.

Good game, meh value for money (which I think has been overly criticised). Yes, this is a short game and they removed the clocktower and a couple of side bosses, but actual player data shows that the overall game is roughly the same length as the original (6.5-8 hrs for the original, 6-7.5hrs for the remake). The real issue is the lack of extra game modes (2nd run, What If? scenarios, Mercenaries/Raid mode, etc.). The Resistance multiplayer was supposed to fill that void but it’s not very popular.

Still, I think the VASTLY improved achievements and bonus shop do a lot to encourage replays. There’s a huge range of achievements, some of which are easy to get casually, and some big ones which substantially change the way you play (speedrun, no healing, no item box, Nightmare & Inferno). Each achievement gives you points which you can spend on anything you want in the bonus shop.

Unlocking a few bonus items on your 1st playthrough, then using them for a challenge run to unlock even more is really satisfying. You get the satisfaction of blitzing all the enemies while still being challenged in a different way (like time efficiency or inventory management). Also, Nightmare+ difficulty reshuffles item and enemy placements. It’s NOT a whole new game but there are enough surprises to liven up a replay. Bearing in mind that RE2make’s Leon A, Leon B, Claire A & Claire B were all 90% identical, that’s not so bad.

Overall, I finished RE3make 4 times (Standard, Hardcore speedrun + no healing, Assisted no item box, Nightmare) and felt my time was well spent. By contrast, in RE2make I finished Leon A, started Claire B and got bored, started Claire A and got bored, then put down the game.

I recommend this game with a heavy heart. R3make is a seriously fun game that could’ve been so much more. The remake inspired me to play the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis, but in turn made me realize how uninspired the R3make is. In terms of character control, graphical fidelity, and the writing/character development in cut scenes, the R3make makes obvious upgrades over the original. Jill controls wonderfully making combat fluid and dynamic. In cut scenes, Jill and the rest of the cast feel well written and fully realized with some of the most human-like facial animation I have seen. The RE engine renders Racoon City in gorgeous detail but this ties into where the game faulters. Where RE2R went all in on the Racoon City Police Department, sewers, and labs, R3make level design and scope pales in comparison to the original. Racoon City streets are significantly underdeveloped, the sewers and labs feel copy pasted from RE2R, and the infamous clock tower is somehow absent. The hospital level in R3make is the only noticeable improvement, but even that is hampered by a wave defense segment that feels out of touch with the rest of the game. Taking R3make on its own for what it is, the game delivers a very fun and action heavy Resident Evil experience. However, it fundamentally fails as a remake and makes one wish what could have been.

[b]TL;DR[/b] Didn't play the original so I can't compare it to that but I hear there is a lot of cut content. Falls short of Resident Evil 2's masterpiece of a remake. However, worth playing if you can get it for more than 50% off the asking price.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Another great showing from the RE Engine. Disappointingly reuses many assets and locations from REmake2. Almost forgivable because they are obviously set in the same location, but there is just not enough new stuff to be okay with that.

I do think there is an improvement over REmake2 (and RE7) with the facial animations and modelling. Claire looked a little unusual in REmake2 but Jill looks incredible. Carlos is also very handsome and cool and I would like to see him return Capcom pls.

[h1]Sound[/h1]
Less atmospheric than REmake2 since we don't have the great location of the police department to spend most of our time is, other than that it is still great.

I do need to complain about the voice lines in this one though. In REmake2 there was swearing and corny dialogue but it feels like they turned up the expletives to 11 in this one. Jill has such a potty mouth and no it does not make her sound badass, it makes her sound childish. Jill [i]is[/i] a badass, of course, but her dialogue hurts her more than it helps her.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Trades REmake2's intricate interconnected level design of the police station for more linear streets. Ammo is abundant so you can just shoot every enemy now as well, but the enemies are not as challenging as they are in other games like RE6 or Village. The dodge move breaks any remaining ounce of tension that enemies would provide, including Nemesis who is just a total non-threat.

Carlos's section did feel like more of a fun shooting challenge but even that along with Jill's sections are stuck between survival horror and action - and never quite succeed at either. Definitely falls a bit short of almost every other RE game I've played in how enjoyable I found it.

Also, 5-6 hours at most of the story for a full priced game is no good. Probably so short cause of cut content of which I am told there is a lot of. Very disappointing.

Resident Evil Resistance was fun for a bit but it kinda sucks unfortunately. Also it's probably dead - I dunno I didn't check.

[h1]Story[/h1]
Survivor in a zombie apocalypse who is currently being hunted by a bio-organic weapon. It's a mix of Jill trying to survive, hesitantly cooperating with Umbrella agents (Carlos and friends) and trying to put a stop to whatever is going down. [spoiler]Of course, you know how that ends if you played REmake2.[/spoiler] It didn't really stick with me, but I wouldn't call the story the strong point of many Resident Evil games.

I do still love all of the characters though.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Unfortunately, this feels like a rush-job pushed out the door as quickly as possible to ride off the success of the wildly successful REmake2. I feel bad for fans of the original who did not get the remake that these classic games deserve.

Ok so i had this on release day in 2020 and completed it a day or so later. Total standard diff time was 4hrs. I enjoyed it back then but something felt off after the credits rolled.......it felt incomplete. I wanted to come back to the game later to complete and then speedrun it to leave an honest review. Here it is...

For those of us that remember (or were alive) when RE3 OG was out in '99, that game was FULL of terror. The tank controls, the slow walking, discovering that Nemesis can open a door and follow you through to any room INCLUDING a safe room! Yea that was real terror in the 32-64bit era. 

This on the other hand is more like a super polished, high performing, Bugatti level masterpiece of visual definition....minus all the terror. Its not that i do not like the game, its just the way it is presented. More effort has gone into showcasing the defining achievements of what made the REengine so good in RE7/RE2, whilst forgetting that RE3 was about telling the Raccoon City story from a different perspective. So much content was left out from the OG game, which made this shorter, less difficult, less anxiety inducing. Correct me if i am wrong, but is that not what RE is all about....Fear?

I fully appreciate that gone are the days of story-rich games that are under 1megabyte in size😂, i mean visuals cost right....but if i could speedrun this remake in 50mins and yet spend 7+hours in the OG RE3 from '99, what does that say. You honestly don't need to think much in this, it is basically run-and-gun. The Inferno mode you unlock adds a few surprises to the already learned PT's that you did to unlock said mode, but that is it. Credits roll for the 5th time and you are left like me.....wanting more.

Over-hated and overpriced. This game may not be for everyone, but it's certainly a LOT better than haters want you to believe. There's a persistent group of toxic naysayers that'll insult anyone's intelligence for liking this game, but keep in mind these are the same people who bought it at full price at launch without doing their research. Guess they aren't as smart as they claim to be...

I definitely agree $60 is kind of an excessive asking price, but if you can get it for less than $20 on sale then it's a deal. Taking a deeper look it's important to start with why you might not want to play RE3:R.

Cons:
-Cut content. This is a fair criticism as some cool locations were cut from the original game that are definitely missed. Puzzles are also far more rare, which is kind of a fun staple of the series. One thing to consider though is that even though content was cut, stuff was added as well. Both this AND the original clock in at around 6 hours to beat for a casual player and I don't think enough people bring that up. 
-Gameplay is more linear than RE2:R. I don't mind being on rails a bit, but this game felt a little too straight forward at times for a RE game.  
-Nemesis pathing is weird. He's not like Mr. X in RE2 who actively stalks you for a portion of the game (TBH, I don't mind this because I hate that mechanic) BUT Nemesis just kind of warps in front of you and at times randomly pins you into a corner. Feels awkward/forced.
-Replay value is a little weak. They do have a cool upgrade shop, but the incentive isn't as high as the multiple routes found in RE2.  
-The story is lackluster overall and feels like a tacked-on side story. To be fair, I thought original was like this too. What really saves the story is...

Pros:
-Characters: JILL. Oh god, I love Jill. She has the PERFECT level of Resident Evil cheesy dialogue--"♥♥♥♥♥ can't even swim"--and badassery without going too overboard with either. I know some people prefer the edgier/grittier characters, but I can't say no to characters like RE 3 Jill and RE4 Leon--"Where's everyone going? Bingo?" Carlos is also far more likable in this version in my opinion. He just seemed so bland in the original. Now he's like Keanu Reeves with fluffy hair. Does that seem bland to you? Well, ♥♥♥♥ you. Side characters aren't much to write about, but Jill and Carlos end up carrying all the weight.
-Fun gameplay. If you liked the gunplay in RE2 then there is more of that here along with more action and even some better mechanics. I much preferred RE3's dodge to RE2's defense items. Granted, I like a little more survival-horror in my RE, but the action take is pretty fun too. 
-Graphics are excellent with a good enough rig.
-Music (both new and returning) are solid. 
-Good keyboard and mouse support.
-Strong mod scene. You've probably seen the screenshots and reviews highlighting the sexualized mods, so those are there for you if that's your thing, but there are also really awesome mods that aren't oversexualized as well. I spent a portion of the game with Jill wearing things like her BSAA outfit from RE5 and Doomslayer-style armor. NEAT! 

So my stance is to not let the negative part of the fanbase get to you and to make the choice for yourself. Sure, the game has its flaws, but if those aren't enough to deter you then there is a pretty fun game waiting for you. Just make sure to get it on sale.

I honestly don't know what people's beef with this game is. I get that it's missing a lot from the original PS1 title, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. I was never a fan of the puzzles in the original anyway so the missing puzzles didn't bother me at all. Some folks complain about the length of the game but I can't think of a single RE game that wasn't designed to be beat in less than 3 hours soooooo.... Overall I like the changes made to the game. Nemesis constantly stalking you in a game like this would have been a little too much to handle in my opinion and just wouldn't work for newer RE games. It worked with Mr. X because he was slower and a little easier to avoid, but with how fast Nemesis can move in the original and the fact that he can carry weapons would have made this game a massive test of patience. So I get why they did what they did with it. 

Same goes for several game sections that were removed or toned down. Pacing-wise it just made sense to take it out or "trim the fat". I always felt like the original game was a little sluggish anyway so the fast pace feels right at home.

[h1]A disappointing follow-up[/h1]
This has a lot in common with the original RE3: made using assets and locations from RE2 (remake, in this case), adds a few new enemies, adds a new dodge mechanic, and has a shorter story than the original in lieu of not having to play the game twice with a different character.

Graphics-wise, it's just as good as RE2make without turning your GPU into a jet engine (Nvidia 3060, as of this review). The way the Hunter variants were implemented were a lot better than the palette swaps in the original RE3. No Brain Lickers, but that's okay since they were nothing but poison-inducing Drain Deimos palette swaps. It also has condensed exploration mechanics to match with the areas that get permanently closed off at certain points of the story like the original. And the final boss battle is AMAZING; the music is phenomenal and Capcom retooled it wonderfully for a modern adaptation.

Where it goes wrong, on the other hand, lies with the titular Nemesis. He's what you expected from a souped-up Mr. X. But unlike the original which features a second humanoid form with tentacles, we get a giant dog-like mutation. I would've been okay with that form solely as a Dead Factory boss fight, but they introduced him at what should've been the Clock Tower level in place of Tentacle Nemesis. We don't get the terror of having to evade a weaponless, yet still dangerous humanoid monstrosity through the tight corridors of the Hospital, but we get the same boss battle lazily repeated with one added tentacle's difference. And sure, the Tyrant's smart, but how do you expect us to believe that a monstrosity bigger than a Hummer could stealthily infiltrate a facility that has human-sized doors and passageways? At least show him eating a Cerberus corpse inside the waste disposal pit to repair damage from the previous battles.

And, as expected from the previous remake, the story has changed in this adaptation. And the vast majority of these changes are [i]not[/i] good.

Brad isn't as important as he was in the previous story. Instead of dying to Nemesis to show how the big guy was specifically targeting STARS members, he gets offed by a zombie horde like an idiot five seconds after you meet him. Jill never goes to the police station unlike the original, as she would logically do for help in a T-virus outbreak. Which means Nemesis doesn't smash up the walls you expected him to plough through when you played RE2make. Instead, Carlos and Tyrell (who's been remade into a friendly teammate instead of a one-off guy who dies, which I'll admit is a vast improvement from the original) go there for a new plotline reason.

It would've made more sense if the RPD Station was the place where Jill met up with the UBCS. The Clock Tower level was completely cut out in favour of expanding the Hospital; which I wouldn’t complain as much about if it were still an evacuation point like the original game, but it’s nothing more than a Dog Nemesis boss arena. There’s no Gravedigger, either. He wasn’t that good of a boss in the original, but we needed something like him to remind you that Nemesis isn’t the only major threat.

And as for the Dead Factory, there’s no explanation as to [i]why[/i] the place is dead in the first place. They could’ve explained it away with the Delta Force raid that was shown in one room in the original, which would’ve given them an excuse to reintroduce the armoured zombies from RE2make’s DLC. But no, the place just inexplicably fell to the virus.

Then there's the canon clash with RE2make. There seemed to be no way that Leon and Claire wouldn't have bumped into one-another more than once while running through the RPD Station, but since that was also a problem in the original, I was willing to overlook it. In RE3make, a building right next to the RPD gets torched, which logically would've lead to the entire block burning down. And how could Tyrell get to the STARS office when the only way not blocked by a locked door is blocked by a skin-searing steam vent courtesy of Carlos and some C4?

There's no bonus minigames like Operation Mad Jackal in the original, which takes away from the replayability.

Also, Carlos doesn't look like he'd be accepted in [i]any[/i] military unit with that haircut, let alone a disposable mercenary company. 

Instead of being a nice expansion to RE2make like the original RE3 was to the original RE2, this just seems like a half-hearted attempt at churning something out to ride the previous remake’s hype. Don’t buy it unless it’s heavily discounted and you’re curious.

WARNING: You cannot turn easy mode off once you turn it on. If you're not doing well in a particular segment, the game will ask you if you want to turn on "assisted" mode. Save 2 different save files constantly or risk accidentally hitting assisted mode and being forced to restart from the beginning.

As for the game itself, the gameplay is not as tight as the Resident Evil 2 remake. In RE2 the environments are much tighter and you have to plan your route accordingly to conserve ammo and also not to take hits from zombies. In RE3 they enabled this annoying dodge mechanic which acts as a supplement for good game design. You can pretty much dodge through any attack as long as you get the timing right which should in theory make the game easier, but in reality it makes the game incredibly inconsistent as what the game considers a "dodge" vs a "hit" is very unclear. The gameplay is fun, entertaining and fast most importantly. It’s the “end of the world” and it shows, everything must be done now, you can dally, but there aren’t many reasons (in game) to do so. You go from Point A to Point B moving the story along and I really enjoyed that. While puzzles (as in previous games) can be fun, it did reach a ridiculous level where every building in the city, town, map had several puzzles for even mundane things. The change to mostly scripted events against Nemesis are a welcome addition. While in RE2, Mr. X was an unstoppable force of whom you had to escape and would take several minutes or more away from you when you were trying to move forward, here, Nemesis is an unstoppable force of whom you have to escape but only when it is required.

Having Jill and Carlos be more seasoned, with more effectiveness in combat also didn’t detract from the experience, after all, both are veterans and it shows in the game and the enemies the encounter. 

The visuals and the environment look just as great, if not better than the previous remake. More so, the contrast between the different levels and sections. A destroyed Raccoon City, the sewers, the hospital, even NEST. Each one had its own charm and even when going from one place to another, you could really admire the details. With that, the music and soundtrack were always on point. Helping the tense moments feel even more tense.

VA and characterization, I really enjoyed the changes they did to all the characters. Especially to Brad, and making him actually act like a S.T.A.R.S. member. The changes to Jill and Carlos (especially the appearance) are really awesome and make perfect use of the engine and the games future. I know that, canonically, Carlos Oliveira doesn’t appear again, but with the remake and potential remake and more games in the future, I hope he does since he had great chemistry with Jill and was a fantastic partner overall.

I do hope that they end up doing a remake of RE1 and RE: Outbreak which was an interesting game, at least spiritually, and regarding the option of having several protagonist and even downer endings.

I'm not sure if I enjoy this or RE2 remake more, but it's hard to compare since they are relatively different games. This game leans more into the action which means that you both get more ammo and more enemies at the expense of horror. It is still an action horror game, but it isn't scary in the way that RE2 or RE7 are.

The main antagonist in this game is more memorable due to how over the top he is and he also looks way cooler. He feels like less of an obstacle and there's an actual point in fighting him outside of the boss arena since he drops weapon attachments and other loot. I recommend fighting him with grenades as to not waste ammo.

I prefer handling unlockables the way that they do in this game where every record (in-game achievement) gives points instead of unlocks so that the player can decide for themselves what they want to unlock. This means that the cool, strong weapons aren't gatekept behind higher difficulties so that everyone who's willing to put in the effort has a chance to use them. There's also no S+ grade so you actually get to enjoy the unlocks while also being a completionist. I'd argue that inferno is more difficult than hardcore in RE2 which makes this a welcome change.

I prefer Jill and Carlos over Claire and Leon. Claire is cool, but Leon just feels so bland and he's only redeemed by being the pretty boy poster child of the franchise. I'd prefer to have Chris, but that wouldn't really make any sense. To be honest, most main characters in this franchise are pretty bland. Anyway, I really like Jill and Carlos in this game because their dynamic is just so fun and they feel more realistic in the way that they act, at least within the confines of the RE universe. They aren't completely calm and collected all the time and they have feelings across the entire spectrum. Carlos is also really hot.

It feels like someone with a leading role had too much say in the design decisions due to how horny and fetishistic parts of the game feel. Whenever you're crawling they really seem to focus on Jill's ass and you can even angle the camera to make it focus on it even more. Tentacles are also pretty common. The worst offender however is related to a spider. I really don't want to elaborate further.

Overall a pretty enjoyable experience. I have some nitpicks like how the dodging mechanic feels inconsistent and that the aiming can feel a bit sluggish, but they aren't enough to make it feel like a bad experience. I wish that it was slightly longer however and that there were some bonus modes, even if it would just be another instance of mercenaries. I'm a newgen RE fan (RE7 and forward) so I don't have the originals to compare to, but apparently the original had more content in the campaign.

In conclusion, this is the worst from the best RE games for five last years. If you played all except RE3, you probably should give it a chance. But if you're not... So, you'd better play RE2 remake, Re VII or VIII (even Revelations in my opinion more interesting).
