[h1]Introduction[/h1]
[b]Resident Evil 3[/b] is third-person survival horror and yet another remake of the cult classic.  It features a story mode and a brand new multiplayer.

[h1]Pros & Cons[/h1]
[b]Pros:[/b]
+ Great pacing, keeps you engaged from start to finish
+ Interesting story with a lot of memorable moments
+ Solid gameplay 
+ Fun multiplayer mode with a fresh idea

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Shorter than previous game (around 6 hours)
- Replaying the game doesn’t give any new content
- Multiplayer is ruined by pay/grind2win progression system

[h1]Story[/h1]
Contrary to its’ title the game is a direct sequel to the first game of the series. You play as Jill Valentine, a police officer from special unit S.T.A.R.S, who had her run in with the zombies, and now searches for a way to bring the company behind those experiments to justice. While she’s rummaging through the paperwork, zombies overrun the city and her home is invaded by a big zombie-looking bloke dubbed Nemesis. Thus begins her adrenaline chase around the city. 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The remake ditches some of the levels from the original in order to preserve the pacing of the events. Some fans might not like this change, but I think it’s justified. Though there’s one aspect I’m missing from the original is the decisions, that influence how you get to certain locations or take you to different locations entirely. While you miss out on some content on the initial playthrough, it adds to the replay ability, that the series usually cultivate. 

In other aspects this game is similar to the previous Remake, but focuses on action rather than exploration. For that it also introduces a new mechanic – dodging, it makes evading enemies a bit easier and is invaluable when fighting with the Nemesis. 

[h1]Multiplayer[/h1]
Additionally, the remake introduces a brand-new asymmetric 4v1 multiplayer mode. In which four players playing as survivors must complete 3 levels by collecting keys or destroying certain objects. Pitted against them is the mastermind, a player, who can spawn zombies and traps in order to stop them. It’s a fun concept, hampered by the progression system. 

The problem is, the game is balanced towards player’s equipment not skill. As you progress you unlock cards that enhance your abilities as survivor or allow spawning more powerful zombies as Mastermind. This makes it near impossible to win, when you have worse equipment than your enemy.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Even with such a short campaign this game deserves a recommendation. It keeps you entertained the whole time without wasting a second. If you're looking for a fun multiplayer mode, you will probably be disappointed, unless you have 4 friends to play with.

Plays well and runs well like any other resident evil game, but there unfortunately are some glaring concerns.

PROS:
-Smooth controls
-Gorgeous graphics and environment just like resident evil 2 remake
-Controls well, but the dodging system feels very wonky and you either get hit or grabbed most of the time
-Decent story, but it is quite different.
-Has moments ingame where you go to the police department like in resident evil 2.
-Takes place slightly before resident evil 2 and if you played that first this game is a slight prequel.

CONS:
-Nemesis is sadly a joke, sure he looks good, but he doesnt appear threatening or intimidating in comparison to his older self in the original resident evil 3. Even Mr X was more fearful since the monster actually does what nemesis was supposed to do, he sadly is also predictable and doesnt appear as often as you may think, I would estimate that he shows up about 3-4 times in free roam chasing, other parts he is either a cutscene, a scripted run through obstacles, or a boss battle. Oh, and he is also the ONLY boss that you fight in this entire game as well.
This is coming from someone that adores nemesis and is even one of my favorite B.O.W's, but sadly, he does not do it justice in this game, his final boss battle is also stupidly easy, Even on hard mode you just had to play patient, otherwise all the previous boss fights are actually somewhat challenging. But just cause a boss is difficult doesnt mean its good. Sorry capcom, you weakened my boy in terms of what made him originally great.

-Low variety of weaponry, and mostly leads to you finding upgrades for your same 5 weapons you carry the rest of the game.

-The dodge mechanic is very buggy, and like I stated up above, it doesnt work very good. You are better off just keeping your distance and running away like in the RE 2 Remake.

-The story is different then the original game, and it sadly is boring in comparison, but I can appreciate Carlos.

-Characters weren't exactly terrible, Jill's role was decent and played well, if anything Carlos was the spotlight in terms of good character, you even get the opportunity to play him in certain portions of the game and hes pretty fun. He also punches zombies. However, I put this as a con because you dont really get the choice to play both characters like you could in RE2 Remake.

-This game, is RIDICULOUSLY short. Thats not even an exaggeration, I was fooling around, getting lost, finding items, died multiple times not knowing where to go, and yet I still managed to beat the game in 6 hours. I bet if I knew exactly what I was doing I could probably beat it in 3-4. Hell even speedrunners are capable of beating it in under an hour. There is no excuse or reason to release such a short game at full price if you are not going to offer enough content to satisfy your customers, and nobody cares about the lame RE Resistance game either.
Make this game longer, add more cut content and make this game more worthwhile to enjoy then half assing it.

In conclusion, this game was sadly a disappointing short title, however its not a horrible game, its actually decent and plays as good as resident evil 2, its just lacking so much. Resident evil 2 did everything correct in terms of what it strived for, horror, great controls, awesome reinventions of the older characters Leon and Claire, lots of replayability, and overall had a climatic and powerful survival horror experience. Even the final bosses were good and quite the challenge at higher difficulties. But Resident evil 3 remake just sadly didnt do it for me, at least not the way I feel it should be. 
My verdict for this game is a 5.5 or 6/10. It lacks so much of what made the original game great, and instead was a quick cash grab project with a mediocre story that can be beaten within 4-6 hours, and thats including you screwing around for a long time like I did. To quote another reviewer "Resident evil 2 Remake is a perfect example on how to reboot your franchise, but Resident Evil 3 Remake is a perfect example on how NOT to reboot your franchise.''

With that being said, dont buy this game at full price, you WILL be ripped tf off. I say this game should have been a DLC for Resident evil 2 instead of it being its own game. This is worth 10$ at best, buy at your own risk, or if you really love Resident Evil like I do.
I will give it a thumbs up because I love Resident Evil, but for gods sake Capcom, make this game more worthwhile for others to enjoy, it severely needs the attention.

[h1] Gameplay / Story [/h1]

Resident Evil 3 takes place a few hours before and after the events of the second part. The playable character this time is Jill Valentine, who is already known from the first part. It was made by S.T.A.R.S. suspended and about to leave town when the disaster in Raccoon City takes its course. The city is overrun by zombies and there are hardly any survivors. However, through her work in the manor, Jill is already well prepared for the horror that awaits her. Umbrella France (the company's European headquarters) sends its new Nemesis project to Raccoon City. Its mission is to kill all S.T.A.R.S. members as they know about Umbrella's illegal bioweapons research. The player therefore meets Nemesis several times in the game without being able to finally defeat him before the final. During the escape from the city one meets some of Umbrella's soldiers, they have the task of evacuating civilians and high-ranking Umbrella shareholders, but without their knowledge they are also used as "guinea pigs" to test the effectiveness of the latest virus generation. For a short section of the game you slip into the role of the U.B.C.S. soldier (Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service) Carlos Oliveira, who has to find an antidote for Jill, who is now infected with the T or G virus. The plot ends with the destruction of Raccoon City by a nuclear weapon and the successful escape of the two playable characters.

Resident Evil 3 is the only part so far in which the so-called live selection concept is used. The player is faced with an unexpected situation in which he has to choose between two possible solutions. An example of this is a brief earthquake in which the ground behind the player collapses and a heavy object rolls towards the player at the same time. The decision is to either dodge the object or jump into the previously created pit. Another new concept is the manufacture of ammunition. While this could only be found like other items in the previous parts, in Nemesis it can now also be made from three types of gunpowder in different combinations. Depending on how often you make ammunition with it, you can also make better ammunition with it over time.

[h1] Combat system [/h1]

There are different types of weapons such as knives, pistols, rifles, shotguns, grenade launchers and flamethrowers. Some can be found in the course of the game and for others you need keys or have to solve puzzles. There is the right weapon for every type of enemy. Ammunition is rather in short supply, but it all depends on the level of difficulty, as this varies. Later you will be happy about every available shot in your pocket.

[h1] Information / Review Deutsch [/h1]

Resident Evil 3 ist ein First-Person Horror Spiel, welcher von CAPCOM Co., Ltd. entwickelt wurde. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2555741974

[h1] Gameplay / Geschichte [/h1]

Resident Evil 3 spielt zeitlich wenige Stunden vor und nach den Ereignissen des zweiten Teils. Spielbarer Charakter ist diesmal Jill Valentine, die bereits aus dem ersten Teil bekannt ist. Sie wurde von S.T.A.R.S. suspendiert und ist gerade dabei, die Stadt zu verlassen, als das Unglück in Raccoon City seinen Lauf nimmt. Die Stadt wird von Zombies überrannt und es gibt kaum noch Überlebende. Jill ist jedoch durch ihren Einsatz im Herrenhaus bereits bestens auf das Grauen, das sie erwartet, vorbereitet. Umbrella Frankreich (Europas Hauptsitz der Firma) schickt sein neues Projekt Nemesis nach Raccoon City. Es hat den Auftrag, alle S.T.A.R.S.-Mitglieder zu töten, da diese von Umbrellas illegalen Biowaffenforschungen wissen. Der Spieler trifft deshalb mehrfach im Spiel auf Nemesis, ohne ihn vor dem Finale endgültig besiegen zu können. Während der Flucht aus der Stadt trifft man auf einige von Umbrellas Soldaten, sie haben die Aufgabe Zivilisten und hochrangige Umbrella-Aktionäre zu evakuieren, werden aber, ohne ihr Wissen, gleichzeitig als „Versuchskaninchen“ verwendet, um die Effektivität der neuesten Virengeneration zu testen. Für einen kurzen Abschnitt des Spiels schlüpft man so in die Rolle des U.B.C.S.-Soldaten (Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service) Carlos Oliveira, der für die mittlerweile mit dem T- bzw. G-Virus infizierte Jill ein Gegenmittel finden muss. Die Handlung endet mit der Zerstörung Raccoon Citys durch eine Kernwaffe und der erfolgreichen Flucht der beiden spielbaren Charaktere. 

Resident Evil 3 ist der bisher einzige Teil, in dem das sogenannte Live-Selection-Konzept verwendet wird. Dem Spieler tut sich hierbei eine unerwartete Situation auf, in der er sich zwischen zwei Lösungsmöglichkeiten entscheiden muss. Ein Beispiel hierfür ist ein kurzes Erdbeben, bei dem der Boden hinter dem Spieler einstürzt und gleichzeitig ein schwerer Gegenstand auf den Spieler zurollt. Die Entscheidung besteht darin, entweder dem Gegenstand auszuweichen oder in die zuvor entstandene Grube zu springen. Ein weiteres neues Konzept ist das Herstellen von Munition. Während diese in den bisherigen Teilen nur wie andere Gegenstände gefunden werden konnte, kann sie in Nemesis nun auch aus drei Arten von Schießpulver in unterschiedlichen Kombinationen hergestellt werden. Je nachdem wie oft man Munition damit herstellt kann man mit der Zeit auch bessere Munition damit herstellen. 

[h1] Kampfsystem [/h1]

Es gibt verschiedene Waffenarten wie z.B. Messer,  Pistolen, Gewehre, Flinten, Granatwerfer und Flammenwerfer. Manche findet man so im Spielverlauf und für andere benötigt man Schlüssel oder muss Rätsel lösen. Es gibt für jeden Gegnertyp die richtige Waffe. Munition ist eher Mangelware, allerdings kommt es ganz auf den Schwierigkeitsgrad an, da dies variiert. Man wird später über jeden zur Verfügung stehenden Schuss in der Tasche froh sein.

You know how a lot of great games will feature a slogfest DLC that you feel compelled to beat, since you enjoyed the base game, even though the DLC isn't as well developed and doesn't feature as fun of gameplay as the original game? Yeah that's basically RE3 (2020) compared to its predecessor RE2 (2019). Hell, you would probably be better off just playing the original RE3 Nemesis from 20 years ago, because this game isn't even a complete remake of that entire game. One frustration I have with this game is there are like 1,000 mini-cut scene interruptions, and the sequencing is so jagged that you take 4 steps forward, cut scene, you take another 3 steps, cut scene. And most of the cut scenes involve Nemesis or zombies popping up right in your character's face, so you basically have to Quick Time Dodge within a couple frames of regaining control of your character, or you're resetting to checkpoint. Then, the sheer amount of content cut from RE3 is the biggest shame... It's particularly baffling since the clock tower sequence/location was like the centerpiece of the original game... but then they also went and completely re-designed this game's ending so that it now feels like a lame rehash of RE2's final act (in the labs). As a fan of the series, it's difficult to understand. It's like the devs had one shot to get the remake right, but I think they were more concerned about the multiplayer Resistance feature or meeting a deadline or something, and now we're left with this half-baked campaign which they are STILL charging full-price $60 for... laughable. To me, REmake 3 is a proper transition between the old-school Resident Evil's and RE4 in terms of gameplay and horror. This game features the combat system from REmake 2 but it also includes a dodge button in place of the sub-item menu. There are generally more enemies around and they are arguably some of the toughest in the series, but you also get good weaponry and a lot of ammo to account for that. Overall, I'd say this game is much more combat focused than its predecessor, but there is a decent amount of survival horror aesthetic such as the inventory system and choosing when to shoot and when to run.

My biggest gripe with this game was the lack of exploration compared to the prequel. REmake 3 is set within multiple different settings, much of which are smaller than the RPD or equivalent Resident Evil setting. As a result, there are a limited amount of places you can explore. Additionally, the game after the first section is linear with most of the puzzles just having you find a key or equivalent item to get past a locked door or blocked area. The puzzles were butchered as well with only a few being within the game. 

I know other people complain about the short length of the game, but I didn't really care much about that. I only wish they had included more areas to explore and such. Although I never played the original, I know there was a fair chunk of RE3 that was not remade so I would warn those expecting a full recreation of the 1999 game.

Overall, this is a pretty good game. I still liked the pacing and gameplay of REmake 2 better, but this style was certainly refreshing, although it could have been executed more thoroughly.

Oh boy, where do I begin?

I guess with some positives.

-Good Graphics as is standard with the RE Engine.

-Fun Gameplay despite a couple of really odd design choices and a few segments that were just awful. (Brainsucker Hallway)

-I like the new Carlos, Mikhail and Nikolai, Jill is alright, I don't hate her, but she has some lines that just felt... Meh.

-Plenty of replayability.

-Good mod support with an active community.

-Hospital section with Carlos was genuinely fun and the first time the game actually feels like Resident Evil.

Now on to the things I just could not excuse, starting with one of two massive elephants in the room.

 -The first problem is that the game is really just a glorified DLC for RE2 rather than a proper remake like we've seen with RE1, RE2 and recently RE4. A LARGE chunk of the game is missing, like over 50% of the original was just cut and remains absent. No Zoo, No real pharmacy level, NO CLOCKTOWER, no Grave Digger. It really is just a small portion of what the original offered back in 1999... As such the game really suffers from it. You can beat the game in 4 to 6 hours on a blind playthrough.

-The second and most glaring for me is the Nemesis. He is soooo incompetent and weak in the remake that is feels like a slap in the face to fans of the Iconic Tyrant. So many times he will grab Jill and have her dead to rights, only to outright let her go so she can run away and he can pretend to chase her. Like he's been replaced with an amusement park animatronic... 

In the original, when he has Jill or ANYONE in his hands, they're dead. That's it. He did NOT mess around. Now he's been reduced to just aura farming for the sake of some dumb scripted "HECKING EPIC!!!" set piece where you either walk forward to completely avoid him, or be led into a cutscene where Jill just kinda casually nopes out and she's safe. 

The segments where you are forced to actually fight him really aren't better either. On any of the first 3 difficulties, Nemy can be easily defeated with a single grenade, or cheesed outright just by walking into a near by building he isn't programmed to enter. 

It really is the biggest disappointment I've seen in the entire franchise. He simply isn't a threat. Instead he's a punching bag for Jill and Carlos and that persists through the entirety of the game. With Jill and Carlos constantly taunting him, calling him degrading names and just not being all that bothered by what is supposed to be an imposing presence.

-Some of the enemy redesigns feel like a downgrade, with the most notable examples being the Brainsuckers. Once terrifying creatures that took a lot of effort and ammo to actually dispatch, now replaced with an annoying and tedious form that infinitely respawn, taking maybe 2 or 3 bullets to kill while they relentlessly dog you and all placed in what is easily one of the laziest and tedious environments in the entire game. Thankfully they only appear once.

-I also wasn't a fan of the new enemy type, the Nemesis Parasites. These guys are waaaay overused and dodging their absurdly long "tail?" swipe felt more frustrating than rewarding.

To sum it all up, the game feels like a massive downgrade from the original but it's still not a bad game per say, just not a very good remake that feels like it fundamentally misses what made the original so beloved. For that reason I'm giving it a Thumbs Down, but if you don't care about the original or never played it and like the combat of RE2R, you might enjoy this one.

Otherwise just stick to the original.

The original PS1 RE3 is one of my favorite games of all time. I played the hell out of the first three PS1 RE games, but I played this one the most by far. I really loved playing through the remake. It's a pretty different game, but not in a bad way. At least not in my eyes. 

The game play in this one is a lot like the RE2 remake. The biggest change is that you can dodge in this one. I wish they would patch it into the RE2 remake as well. Dodging just fits these games so well and it allows you to play much more aggressively than you would have otherwise. It's also probably why Nemesis is SO aggressive in this. The last boss fight is completely bonkers and almost felt impossible. It wasn't, but there were times where I thought I was done for.

Some of the changes from the original are a bit of a bummer. There's no life choices in this one. So you don't get the little moments that can change your routing or skip a boss fight or two. I kind of get why that isn't in here. It would be much more difficult and expensive to code the extra animations and stuff at this fidelity. Maybe some day it gets patched in or something. I'm less concerned about that removal. The bigger thing is that there are entire areas missing. You don't go into the clock tower and you don't go into the grave yard. That's a little bit more difficult to forgive. Seeing a high resolution clock tower would have been awesome. It isn't a long portion of the original version, so plot wise we aren't missing much of anything without it. It's just such a cool place to run through that I wish I could see it. The grave yard is meh. Don't miss that or the graveyard boss much. And to make up for it the hospital section is much larger and so is the lab. So it's a bit of a trade off.

I bought the DLC that unlocks everything. I did that for a few reasons. One is that I played the original so much I didn't feel like unlocking everything again. The bigger reason was to get access to Inferno difficulty. I heard it was stupid hard and it is. I was running around with boosted defense, regenerating health and infinite ammo and I still died 16 times. About 8 of those were just on the last boss. I'm pretty sure most of those deaths were just me being unfamiliar with the remake. Some of it is that the enemies are dialed so high in that difficulty that if you aren't paying attention for a second it's just game over. When I finally beat the last boss my hands were shaking. It's been awhile since that has happened. I like that there's a difficulty that seems specifically designed with the infinite weapons in mind. I know you can beat Inferno mode without them, and I salute anyone that good, but personally I don't see how I could have possibly done it without them. It was difficult, but really fun.

I'm not sure why there's no Mercenary mode in this. In RE2 they brought back Hunk and Tofu, so why not Mercenary mode? I would say it's probably an upcoming DLC, but this game has been out for a year now. Hopefully they give us that. I always liked playing as Nicolai and making him die to the first zombie. 

I completely recommend this game. Especially if you liked the original version or the RE2 remake. It's pretty impressive Capcom managed to make solid remake versions of the first three games.

While not as good as number 2 and definitely not as long, Resident Evil 3 still manages to be a fun game that is (at least during the first half) an unrelenting, intense and as atmosphere rich like its predecessor. 

Set during the same time period of Resident Evil 2, RE3 depicts the first moments of the downfall of Raccoon City and the immediate threat of the T-virus amongst its population. While RE2 is a slow burn thriller which slowly ramps up its pace as the game progresses, RE3 is set on creating a cinematic action packed game with big bombastic set pieces and rarely lets the characters have a quiet moment before the next big event, this is most notable in the opening 20 minutes which is a full throttle, action packed, tense sequence of Jill navigating her way through the city as the outbreak and chaos is unraveling. 

The first half of this game is probably the best half as it is Jill exploring the streets trying to get power to a train, once you play as Carlos for the first time thats when the game loses its footing and the cracks begin to show; unlike RE2 where Mr. X would just show up to ruin your day, Nemesis has heavily scripted moments and you can go large portions of the game without having to worry about him showing up, I personally like and dislike this change as it does add some great action moments and every Nemesis encounter becomes more stressful as he adapts from his previous encounter, but on the other hand it removes the unpredictability of Mr. X and the fear his footsteps create.

Over all RE3 isn't a bad game its just a completely different style to RE2 and comparing RE3 to RE2 isn't fair on RE3 as this game is trying to create a new and noticeably different experience, it ends up depending on your preference of style and genre. 

However one thing that can't be excused is the price tag for how short this game is.

Assuming you are here because you loved Resident Evil 2 Remaster, and you want more: can confirm, more is what you'll get. However not necessarily every part of RE2 you'd expect.

What are the main criticized points of RE3 Remaster?
1. Cut short compared to RE3 original, in favor of a multiplayer mode nobody asked for.
2. No replay value
3. Not that horror-focused anymore.

All that is true. Regardless it is a bloody fantastic prequel / sequel to RE2. The gameplay system you liked in RE2, inventory management, zombies and the way they die or don't die, camera handling, key finding and backtracking, it's all there. The gameplay is the EXACT same as RE2, the engine is the same as RE2, and all this is the best I could wish for. However there are some design differences you should be aware.

1. There is no pursuer like the Tyrant of RE2. The Nemesis is far more deadly, however only appears at scripted parts of the game. For some, this is a negative as it removes horror, fear from the gameplay. Look, RE2 had the Tyrant pursue you in the latter half of the police station, at most 30% of the game, so it's not that big deal if you ask me to reduce that to 10% (certain sandbox locations will have the Nemesis follow you around at specific parts of the game, i.e. you explored it already, got a key, got to go back to start, but it hunts you now). In exchange, you get more boss fights and better ones at that, more adrenaline filled and better designed bossfights, and some of the horror elements are definitely there if even for short periods of time (hello city power station!).

2. Sadly, the time:money value ratio is much lower than RE2. Once you complete the campaign, there is no extra second campaign to play to fill out blanks in the story (RE3 is a prequel to RE2, but ends sometime after RE2, and as you revisit some old locations from RE2, you'll do things that'll leave it in a state that you found the place in, back in RE2, however the story progresses beyond the ending of RE2). What you get instead is an ingame shop where you can purchase various powerups or key items that will appear in your inventory / stash so when you replay the game, you can unlock lockers, chests, doors etc. way sooner, enliminating much of the backtracking or allowing you speedruns. The more achievements you do, the more points you get to spend on various items, including some badass weapons, and a character skin. Shame on CAPCOM for making an even nicer skin a paid DLC. 

3. I did not play the original RE3 so I cannot say what was cut, but as far as I know there are some points in the game where you can take route A or route B, to end up at the same goal anyway, which could've indeed increase replay value. There is no such thing, the game is completely linear. Do with this information as you will, I just want to add that I did not mind it being linear in a way RE2 also was linear in it's second half: there is exploration, there is finding extra equipment, hidden keys and lock combinations, all of that is there, only you move from small sandbox to small sandbox way faster than  between RE2 sandbox locations.

I would advise you to get this game if you liked RE2 and want more of it. I'd go as far as to say, as both a negative and a positive that this is a giant standalone expansion pack for RE2 that you must get if you want to have a much richer, fuller RE2 experience, because it's great for that, but this includes that RE3 feels like a standalone expansion pack, an extra campaign like NieR Automata's "playthrough C" , and less so as a game that can stand on it's own. It's a great deal at 9,99-14,99 at most.

Forewarning, I haven't played the original so my opinion is based solely on my experience with the remake and I have only played RE2R and R7 before this.

Everything happen during the events of Resident Evil 2 but with different characters and some new locations so while it's not as long because the story switches between the 2 characters at certain points it can last for a good 7 hours when played reasonably normal pace if you're the type to look at every nook and cranny looting whatever you can. However, It's more focused on action and less on exploration meaning that resource management takes a bit of a backseat and puzzles are a bit nonexistent. The gameplay is very much the same only exception is the addition of a dodge roll with Jill and a bash stun with Carlos which are both helpful in their own respective situations but honestly the dodge is amazing to get past enemies, it takes a bit of getting used to with the timing however but when it clicks you'll want to use it a lot more. Story was good, characters were well-written and the voice acting impeccable; it feels a bit more on rail because exploration felt more streamlined but I wouldn't say it's a bad thing personally I don't mind a more story-focused approach. Enemies are a bit more distinct than 2 but it's nothing exceptional and bosses were good maybe except the last boss which is a bit generic in its design .Replayability-wise it's rather limited to increasing the difficulty unlike playing a different character and there's an item shop  that let you buy weapons and items to make runs faster, not a big fan of the implementation but it's decent enough. Fun facts before I conclude, both remakes were developed relatively at the same time by 2 different development teams that were barely communicating with each others outside of technical stuff since they were both using the same engine so that explains why they are this different and also that it isn't rushed contrary to what some might be tempted to believe. Anyways I think it's a fun game it's just important to know what you're getting into however I wouldn't recommend at full price unless you intend to replay it a lot and even then it's a bit short of that front and if you're counting on the multiplayer that comes with it, don't it's not worth it and very much dead population-wise. 7/10

I recommend this game...if its on sale. 

That's how I bought (for $15) it and I am happy with that choice, even if it meant waiting months to see the price I was okay with spending which I recommend to everyone else interested. 

Fun Value: 6/10
The game itself is fun, it has enjoyable aspects: some limited but cool exploring, discovering guns, blowing up zombie heads, and I found replaying the game overall fun. I have beaten it FOUR times up to this point to fully ascertain the story. Combat is decent, shooting zombies can get old. Dying and being grappled by zombies especially gets old, and Nemesis will spam attacks. You'll be happy autosave is a feature otherwise certain moments would make the game very frustrating. 

Gunplay: 5/10 
I unfortunately found the most important mechanic in the game one of the most disappointing. I like shooting zombies, but not so many times it becomes a tedious task. Shooting zombies can feel like shooting a sponge (depending on difficulty). I played Assisted-Hardcore and zombies just become increasingly more annoying than something difficult. Difficult does NOT mean giving an enemy a bigger health bar. Sure they are zombies, but five head shots with a pistol of any kind should dismantle anything. In addition, aiming feels kind of slow and wonky, waiting for the reticle to come together is lazy and make the game irritating as its easy to waste ammo at a zombie point blank. No matter what "excuse" people would justify that with, I DGAF. Other games do it better, RE2 did it better. The 3rd person perspective is also all sorts of f*cked up. You can be in a very close vicinity and the camera will be way too close up. I noticed in encounters/fights with Nemesis it was especially worse. 

Story: 4/10
It kind of sucks, and the characters and their acting does not help. Even with the lack of content removed from the original story of RE3: nemesis, this rendition does to do anything fun or better. There is just a lack of sustenance, having Jill battle Nemesis four times is too repetitive. Big evolving bosses do not make games better FYI. There are no meaningful relationships between characters, even the main antagonist is quite boring. I felt a lack of motivation going through the game, as in "why are we doing this?" Just because the game placed us here? The game's storytelling does not set the stakes high enough to justify the characters motives, its underwhelming. Jill is not a fun character, she has cheesey dialogue, and says very cliche one liners. They could have tried a little harder. I suppose it stays within the originals because they were not all that clever either, but honestly I think its worse than it ever was; RE6 level of dialogue cheese for example. Carlos is my one exception for characters in the game, he's not perfect with his dialogue, but out of all the characters he has the most meaningful and convincing persona. Other characters are there literally just to take you from point A to B, and then die in very ridiculous ways.

Graphics and Sound: 9/10 
Easily one of the best aspects of the game, however that is with most games these days. That said, Capcom did a good job on the sections that ARE in the game. Lighting is pleasant, nothing stood out as ugly or odd. Character models look good, some zombie models are re-used which is kind of lazy. Guns sound pretty good, can be a little quiet. Other effects like : zombies moans, destruction, ambient noise, and environmental noise are good. No major complaints. 

Biggest Gripes: 

The story is short, the content removed from the original makes this rendition beatable in under 4 hours (if you take your time). Imagine trying to race through it? You can beat the game in ONE hour and THIRTY minutes. Its very easy, maybe they intended that because speed running? Well, I would rather have a longer game that is: lengthy, meaningful,  and challenging rather than a DLC length half ass story. This "game" could have easily been a DLC for RE2. Its kind of sad to say. The pacing, in this game  there are odd transitions when you are fighting and then forced into dialogue with another character either: radio or in person. Thankfully the radio dialogue is skipable. The part that frustrates me the most, is the walking dialogue, why make this something people have to do forcefully instead of a cutscene? Ohhhhh, the game would be shorter! Right, so that's the only reason really, if you could skip random dialogue and walk sections, this game might actually take 1 hours to beat. Its a part of the many artificial game lengthen-ers. Cutscene can also feel so meaningless because they lack any meaningful content. Lastly, Raccoon City feels so small, it almost seems like its not even important with the how little we can see.

Best Part: 
The hospital, its easily the most immersive and "scary" part of the game. I found this to be the most atmospheric, despite being small and limited.

TL;DR: A solid game that misses the mark by comparison.

[h1][b]Context[/b][/h1]

This is a remake of the classic PSX title Resident Evil 3: Nemesis (1999). It uses the same RE Engine as Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil 2 Remake. I have done 2 full playthroughs of this game, once on stream. My latest run took 4 hours and 44 minutes across two streams, and I only got a C-rank. I did not use any enhanced/"cheat" items during either playthrough. Because this game was built on the foundations of Resident Evil 2 Remake (RE2R), Resident Evil 3 Remake (RE3R) has a lot of the same mechanics and gameplay imp lementations. For a more detailed rundown of these, please see my RE2R review [1]. This was because of its much shorter development cycle, which is evidenced by the fact it comes only a year after RE2R's initial release, whereas Resident Evil 2 Remake (2019) had 2+ years to follow-up on Resident Evil 7 (2017). Overall, the game has been tweaked to fit a more action-oriented gameplay loop and tone.

[h2][b]Narrative[/b][/h2]

This game follows up on Jill Valentine, the heroine of the original Resident Evil 1, who is now suffering from PTSD after the events in the Spencer Estate. She has audio-visual hallucinations of the event, and nightmares about being turned into a zombie. The events of RE3R take place before, during, and after the events of RE2R. We see the initial spread of the pandemic through her eyes, her attempts to help civilians, as well as her initial encounter with Nemesis, a "perfected" version of the Tyrants we saw in the last two Resident Evil games. Nemesis, unlike Mr. X, can use a variety of weapons and serves as the main opposing force of the game. There is also Nikolai, a shady member of the Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service - a paramilitary group. Nikolai is only interested in acquiring the cure for the T-virus, much like Ada Wong from RE2R, in order to help further the goals of his mysterious handlers. Another member of the U.B.C.S., Carlos Oliviera, serves as both a foil and ally to Jill in the same vain as Chris Redfield. Like Ada Wong in the previous game, he also has an extended portion of the game dedicated to controlling him. Together, the two of them try to locate Umbrella's lab, manufacture a cure for the virus, and escape Raccoon City before it is destroyed by the U.S. government.

[h3][b]Gameplay[/b][/h3]

Unlike RE2R, you spend a lot more time exploring the streets of the city, rather than inside a manor environment. You do get to revisit the police station, even seeing Lieutenant Branagh, but this section of the game is  much more linear in nature. The following underground portion is much the same, and leads into one of the many chase sequences against the aforementioned Nemesis monster . The game does not spend much time in any singular location, and uses these encounters as a means of transitioning between them. In some respects, this makes Nemesis feel like an unstoppable force of nature, but it also feels very tired by the end. One could argue that this helps the player relate to Jill, who is equally fatigued by the finale, but that may be up to individual taste. Personally, I wish I had more time to explore Raccoon City. This game's combat is more arcade-y in comparison to RE2R, in that individual shots have less weight and damage to them, but you are given significantly more ammunition overall. Also, unfortunately, the developers chose to force dead enemies to dissolve into goop rather than allow their corpses to remain in the environment. So, unlike the previous game, you'll always know when you're done shooting. The defensive knife item has also been made unbreakable and given a broader moveset. This has allowed more skilled players to do knife-only runs. Jill and Carlos, unlike Leon and Claire, are highly-trained survivors. As such, they've been given additional movement and defensive options such as dodging and countering enemy attacks. All of these add up to a much more streamlined, and therefore action-focused, scenario. There is only a single campaign, but Carlos does have two portions of the game dedicated to following him.

[h1][b] Bugs [/b][/h1]

A common bug in this game at the time of playing was the field of vision becoming horribly narrow after doing a perfect dodge. This could not be manually fixed without reloading the game, and made several boss fights much more difficult.

[h2][b] Overall [/b][/h2]

As a modern remake of a classic Resident Evil game, RE3 Remake is serviceable but not perfect. It's shortened development time hampers its ability to improve on the designs of RE2 Remake, and provided many people with doubts about the series of remakes going forward. This is especially heightened after the release of sensitive business documents suggesting that we will be receiving a Resident Evil 4 Remake in the coming years (potentially 2022). As a next step in Jill's story, it was great to see her back in action after a brief respite. It's unfortunate that her following appearances in Resident Evil 5 and Revelations 1 are lacking. In this game, she's a strong female character with agency, whereas sequel entries make her much more of a damsel. I would recommend this game only after playing RE2 Remake, so that you can appreciate the small callbacks and additions to that game's systems.

Taking place during Resident Evil 2's events, Resident Evil 3 sees series heroine Jill Valentine attempting to escape the zombie-infested Raccoon City, while a hulking monster—Nemesis—hunts her at every step. In addition to staying alive, Jill must prevent the United States government from obliterating Raccoon City with a nuclear weapon. The former S.T.A.R.S. special forces operative must use all of her training to overcome the insurmountable odds.

True to the franchise, Resident Evil 3 focuses on item management. Though you obtain numerous weapons throughout the adventure, you must make every bullet count as ammo is in rare supply. There are many instances where it is best to avoid zombies and conserve the little ammunition you possess. Although it’s tempting to carry all the ammo and weapons you find, limited inventory space forces you to consider what to tote into combat. Even when you find hip pouches that expand the available inventory space, you must always be mindful of your stocks. In a way, item management becomes its own game within a game.

Because of item scarcity, it pays to scour every inch of the expertly designed levels. Not only will you find ammo, healing items, and weapons, but you’ll often end up connecting different stage sections by unlocking doors or lowering ladders. Doing so gives you easier access to previously visited locations, faster travel to any nearby save rooms, and an effective means of avoiding unnecessary or unwanted encounters. Careful exploration also yields safe combinations or access codes for locked doors. It is immensely satisfying entering once inaccessible rooms and finding them loaded with the aforementioned items.

Resident Evil 3 doesn’t have as many complex puzzles as Resident Evil 2. Outside of the rare puzzle where you're tasked with aligning railroad tracks or mixing chemical agents, most puzzles simply require you to pull levers or flip switches to open doors or raise elevators. The challenge comes from finding a way to reach said levers and switches. While some players may find the lack of puzzles disappointing, it helps the game maintain a fast pace. Considering how much time you spend running away from Nemesis, it makes sense to cut back on puzzles and focus more on the action.

You’ll find Resident Evil 3's gunplay sluggish if you’re used to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare or Doom Eternal's lightning-quick shooting mechanics. However, the shooting speed is perfect for this slower, more methodical experience. Handguns, shotguns, grenade launchers, and other weapons deliver a satisfying, crunchy impact whether you’re playing with a controller or mouse and keyboard. You can enhance the weapons by finding attachments that are scattered throughout the levels. This includes a dot-sight scope for the handgun, a larger barrel for the magnum, and a grip for the shotgun. There aren’t many mods available, but the ones you find make you a more effective zombie slayer.

Dodging is an extremely useful new mechanic. Performing a Perfect Dodge just as an enemy attacks not only prevents you from sustaining an injury, it also slows time. This gives you a small window to either attack or flee. Each enemy’s attack speed differs, so you must alter your Perfect Dodge timing to match a monster's offense. This gives you the incentive to learn attack patterns, which in turn will help you survive encounters.

Jill isn't the only controllable character. During certain parts of the narrative, you'll play as Carlos Oliveira, a soldier trying to fix the mess his company, Umbrella, made of Raccoon City. Aside from carrying an assault rifle, the main difference between the characters is their respective dodges. Where Jill performs a true evasion move, Carlos punches forward, knocking zombies back with his fists. You only briefly control Carlos, but his segments add a small and welcome dose of variety.(sometimes like call of duty zombies LMAO just kidding)
Where Resident Evil 2 featured two distinct campaigns, Resident Evil 3 only has one. That said, if you take your time and search every stage area, you’ll get around 10 hours’ worth of gameplay. You can extend your playtime by completing in-game challenges, which include killing enemies with specific weapons, completing the game on higher difficulties, and upgrading weapons.

Completing these challenges rewards you with points you can use in the shop (found in the Bonuses section of the main menu). You’ll also unlock concept art and 3D character models. Despite the (relative) brevity of the campaign, unlocking bonuses amplifies one’s overall playtime.

I play and beat the original 1999 Resi 3 every year before Halloween. Sometimes I just start a run of it for no reason whatsoever, other than the joy it brings to my life. I have probs played through the OG of this game like 40+ times and I love that game (and all the old fixed camera ones) so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much. We could talk about any of the old school games and the convo will never end. I am a bit of a resident evil nerd. I own all the games, and the remakes, yes all of them, even the hand held titles. I own the physical copies of all the games, collectors and directors cuts of the OG games, I have the board games (resi 2 tabletop is awesome game!). This game franchise is what started my love of zombies horror and monsters. And yes I am very aware of the missteps the franchise has had over the years as well, im a fan but not a blind one. 

Here is my thoughts on the originals.

The original resident evil 2 was an increase in action, bullet count, scope, even the fear factor was increased! its a masterpiece (play n64 version or play hd texture pc version there a load of fun!)

When Resi 3 nemesis came out back in 99, it def did not have the same level of ambition as the OG 2, however it was a super solid title (my number one when playing the old games). Why is that? because it has item and enemy randomize, quick fun action, a perfect game length, Some choices through out the way to change up the playthrough (which made up for only having one character to play this time around), Nemesis could follow you between zones and almost seems like this threat that can come out of nowhere to ruin your day, and its a bit more of a straight forward experience than the second game in terms of back tracking and puzzles (in my opinion atleast).  All of these factors led to the game being kick ass and for me a timeless gem.

So how about the new one?

Well history repeats itself in many ways. The resident evil 2 remake was very ambitious in terms of sound design, graphics, mood, horror, and much more. Most importantly it felt like the Resi 2 remake added a lot to the overall experience. This Resi 3 remake does not live up to that level of ambition, however it does offer an increase to action, fluid combat (just like the original when they gave jill her dodge mechanic), better cut scenes/character animations, higher enemy counts, but oddly some toned down physics and graphics. Notice however I didn't say this one added to the experience the prior started building up!

This is were I come to the cons of the game.
Its much shorter than the original with many sections cut out, cut down, and boss fights being missing.

Nemesis is a joke in this game, design n whatnot is fine but the fights are to easy, aside from the final encounter which i just call the wall of death which is one of the most cheesy dark souls like boss fights ive ever seen and it has no reason to be in the game.

Its to easy, especially with the books and shop system it actively encourages you to use, and if you dont you have 1 hit enemies and zombies that would take 20+ rounds to kill (on the inferno difficulty) so you need the items to balance everything and get a good experience, which is fine, but this how the game encourages it replay-ability, at least at first. 

Some of the guns need a little more umph on the impact, idk they felt better in the prior title, might be because of enemy physics/the reaction of the blast. You can def tell there is a lot less gun play when you blast a zombie apart in resi 3 remake versus resi 2 remake.

No story choices in gameplay, the path you take, or how you deal with nemesis. Was a thing in the old game, why isn't it here? Would have really added to replay value..... 

Then you start downloading mods and speed running the game and this is were i get into the pros of the game.....

Ease of play
Its much easier (for me atleast) to just pick this one up and play through it all than it is the resident evil 2 remake. I think this is a combination of the increased action, linear nature, smoother combat, and straight forward puzzles. Some of that might not be a pro for all Resi players, which it very well shouldnt be, but my point is it all contributes towards a game thats easy to sit down and play through start to end so take that how you want. 
Like ive only beaten resi 2 remake maybe 4-6 times, and Resi 3 remake i've probs beat 12-14 times. 

More Fluid Combat
(does make the game to easy once you master it)

Higher Enemy Count
(always a good thing, except when it results in weaker model physics and AI.... which I think happened here)

Jill
(Jill is the first character i ever played back on the PS1 Resident evil 1 when i was like 4 or 5 years old, this isn't my fav version but still cool to see her again)

Overall its really fun, worth the buy for a big resident evil nerd, and def worth the buy on a sale if you like zombie action shooter games or the franchise even a little. But my main issue is this. I said i like the original because it added to what the prior title brought to the table. This remake takes away from the original, and the remake, in terms of progress. While having a few steps forward it has some real noticeable steps back, which is ultimately the reason i give it a 7/10 for a hardcore resident evil fan, and a 5-6 out of 10 for anyone else.

After waiting like a good boy for the reviews on this game to drop before I just mindlessly threw my money into Capcom's pocket, I decided to let this one sit for a while before picking it up. A little research convinced me that the initial hype wouldn't last long, given the reviews, and that I could probably get it nice and cheap (actually, at 1/3 the price) if I just waited a few months. Having looked into the game, I knew what I was getting into, that the remake paled in comparison to the original, but I completely underestimated just how true this was going to prove.

First of all, I just want to say that I am a Resident Evil fan. Not a fanatic of the series, but a fan. I've been playing these games since the first one dropped on ps1, not to date myself.

Second of all, I would be wary of any game that literally has an achievement that's awarded by completing it in under 2 hours. Sure, it'll probably take you a bit longer than that, but such an achievement does speak to the overall length of the game. Other than achievement hunting, this game offers dismal replayability value and I feel like I was able to see everything worth seeing and get everything worth getting (save one pistol attachment) in my very first run. I can find no good reason, nor have I the slightest urge, to replay this game again, meaning its probably doomed to rot in my Steam library for all time.

Honestly, it feels like gimmick, nothing but an interlude into whatever fresh heck multiplayer nonsense it came with.

All characters, including Jill, are pretty bland and generic, and the plot is in such a rush to move you to the next action scene that you don't really get to know or care about any of them. The whole experience left me with one question in mind: When did Resident Evil games stop trying to be scary?

Resident Evil 3 relives the old past like the virus brings the dead back to life. 

And even if the remake is one of the most controversial games from Capcom, I think that the positive features outweigh the missing features and this game is relatively good. The game offers impressive scenes and action which were implemented impressively. The game is more focused on a lot of action, gunfire, explosions  compared to Resident Evil 2 Remake and a quiet look around a neglected and destroyed city was rather in the background. Well, this point is also due to the fact that you are being chased by a mutated monster called Nemesis from the umbrella organization that has the task of killing all S.T.A.R.S members.  Therefore, I will explain the main factors in the game 

- (Level design)

Anyone who has played the original title will notice that a lot has changed and for everyone else, however, this point is initially irrelevant. The game itself gives a good overview of the raccoon city and also the city is impressively adorned with many details, especially easter eggs and other references to resident evil 2. The impression of a crumbling city that is overrun by zombies has not missed its impression. The locations are varied and exciting and you never got bored so which is a good plus for the game. Some scenes from the original are missing, but many essential points have been taken into account and incorporated. The design of the levels is really detailed and doesn't feel empty or boring and also leaves creepy feelings in certain places like in the hospital mission. I am of the opinion that the only controversial part of the game in the form of the game design is that it differs from the original but also it has brought to light better in some parts of the game. The level design is therefore also one of the strongest pros in the game.

- (Playstyle and movement)

The game itself feels very fluent and the movement system seems to be even better than in the 2 remake. 
Moving, dodging and shooting are very pleasant in the game and also fun. There is no way to complain about the controls - everything is simple and well designed. 

- Story (without Spoilers)

The story of the game is of course based on the original of the game, but there are still big differences. 
Rather, the original seems to serve as a kind of template and a game has been created which is similar in many ways or even stayed the same but also looks way different. The story itself is very well done and starts out great and you are thrown directly into the fire which I like to greet very much. As already mentioned, the level design is very varied and the same applies to the story where the whole story is very enjoyable entertained. The stories of the protagonists come out very good and build up very nice over the time. The story itself is very exciting throughout and comes across as impressive.  I don't find it so attractive to walk through empty corridors all the time or to play casual puzzle games as in the old original. Here in the remake, they always ensured action. But it is a matter of taste what you find better. Even if more potential would have been possible like more playtime or original parts, the story of resident evil 3 remake has been done very well and some kind of points better than the original in my opinion. 

- Protagonists (Jill, Carlos, Nemesis)

- Jill Valentine

Jill is one of the main character in the game and one of the best characters in the entire franchise. 
First of all, I really want to inform everyone who dont know the background of her story is that she had an eventful history before the events of raccoon city and was a member of the US Delta Force where she was a highly decorated part of the demolition squad. After that she worked on a task force called S.T.A.R.S that poses a threat to the umbrella company and therefore they tries to kill its members. Compared to Claire, we are playing here with an experienced soldier who is well versed in dangerous situations. She has got a new look which shows up nicely ( Sasha Zotova). Finally a female character who looks really natural and not like a western character in a Japanese art style like Claire. Many female characters in video games are mostly based on their looks and have a lot of naked skin, but their characters are mostly terribly annoying or don't match to the story after all. This new Jill valentine offers a lot more and is superbly designed and is also one of the most likable characters in the entire franchise. She looks a lot cooler, harder and her character fits much more to her background story and they did a really good job so far on her. Jill's character is very similar to a talented and comradely person who is passionate about others and she seems very emotionally and interested in the fate of their fellow attendants. So she's a strong personality and completely unafraid of unknown threats and has a casual cool manner and a nice sense of humor. She is definitely one of the best female protagonists ever created and has grown even further after that fine-tuning.

- Carlos Oliveira or John Rambo ?!

At first I thought s.... this is John Rambo but where really impressed with the look he got. 
He appears a little bit later in the game that has been said but without to spoiler very much but the impression he gives is very cool. Like Jill, he himself is a very empathetic person who is also interested in saving the city and has no problem endangering his own life in order to protect the others. He is also characterized by a strong personality and also has a funny sense of humor and he always seems to have an overview when it comes to the needs of others. He also works much better than in the original and his character finally comes into its own, which is really well done. Carlos also gets along very well on his own in many situations and supports the others as well as he can. He is not a lonely wolf, but one who can also push trough as a one man army. In my opinion he is an underrated protagonist in the entire resident evil franchise and it wouldn't hurt to bring more of him in the future. 

- Nemesis

It is incredibly weird to take apart a personality that is neither human nor really talking except saying STAAAARS... in a deep monster voice. Nonetheless, I also wanted to take a closer look at this Nemesis. Nemesis is not just a merciless killer and pursuer who mindlessly pursues his targets. He seems self-confident and also sadistically brutal that does not immediately kill its victims but still plays around with its prey like a cat to a mouse. Even if he has no convictions or personal goals of his own, he pursues his goals mercilessly until the end regardless of what may happen. The way he cheekily throws a flamethrower in front of our noses and then unpacks his new toy makes him kind of entertaining. Nemesis seems to have two sides to attitudes. Once the cold, merciless pursuer with cunning tactics and also there is an uncontrolled, crazy manner when he dont get what he wants. I wouldn't say it is better than the original, but also not worse and also well presented in the game. 

- (Game conclusion)

In the end it is a good game that was implemented even if there was a lot of potential upwards. It is up to you which type of Resident Evil you prefer, be it creepy or pure action. I think that both remake parts 2 and 3 were implemented very well and I find both very good and also recommend part 3 of the game. It's also an excellent game for newbies to get started and get a taste for Resident Evil.

The rating system in Steam is too primitive compared to the actual rating systems needed for games; you either thumbs up, or thumbs down -- you either loves the game, or hate the game; black or white, no fifty shades of grey in between. That is not the case for Resident Evil 3 Remake. It is a game with greatness and failures. It did well with mature graphics engine and fluent optimizations, but also comes with a "meh" level character build, unrealistic combat system and over-simplified story. As a game built in 2020s, it enjoys fantastic graphics and motion capture; but the naivety of story line and hollow character conversation are too much for me. I don't even have to spill out how much did the current design deviated from original Biohazard 3; Jill now has a new face and new set of clothes, Carlos shows up right in the beginning with a cute fluffy hair style, and Nemesis can break through walls to grab Jill in the throat/leg 3 times in a row without killing her immediately, a S.T.A.R.S member are dumb enough to be bitten in the arm by zombies while his only job is to hold the door, and our evil Nikolai is evil because the drama needs an evil antagonist, without a reason. All the story telling and character building were crafted for pupils in elementary kids, not serious adult players -- Heck it won't even convince a teenager! It is so hard to indulge myself in the atmosphere of this survival game while the story is such a cutie. It is a horror game, please behave like one! 
Also, I bought this game primarily because I was an avid fan of the original game -- I still remember the mysterious & enchanting music when I solved the music puzzle in the clock tower; I still remember the shivers it gave me when the colossal worm dragged Jill underground; I still remember the heat of emotion when Carlos found unconscious Jill on the ground, wounded and infected, and headed alone to find her a cure in the dark hospital complex...All of this, either completely removed, or changed into a childish drama with no visible real human emotions, and the whole game ended in just 3-5 hours, a half-ass game compared to original. Why develop such a Resident Evil 3 Remake in the first place if you decided to change so much? Why not develop another story at all? I am not convinced by many of the developer team's decision, but I cannot change what is done/It is what it is. I need to play The Last of Us series again to feel some real human dialogues and real world reactions again, instead of some drama show dolls.

To follow up after those bad jokes, I have not played the original Resident Evil 3 Nemesis, but I have seen a few playthroughs of it and I've watched various videos talking about it's story/enemies/choices/weapons/characters/etc, giving me what I think is a decent look into a bit of what has changed from then to now with the remake. I do believe this is still an alright game for most of today's audience, although it is very upsetting and frustrating that they cut out/changed important plot points, areas, enemies and mechanics out of this compared to the original. The clock tower scene? Gone. The park and Gravedigger fight? Not here (I THINK they removed Gravedigger and the original hunter gamma and mixed them into one, creating the new hunter gamma we have in this remake?). The water treatment plant? gonzo. Dead factory? Nope. 

Giant spiders, giant crows, original hunter gammas, and other enemy types are missing from here too, and the brain suckers/drain deimos don't wander the streets anymore since now they're stuck specifically to the electrical substation. A few enemies being mixed with others or removed doesn't sound like a hugeee deal, but it makes this game's already low enemy variety even lower I would say. Adding to the TLDR recap of stuff they've removed from the original in this: they eliminated roughly six guns, freeze rounds, ink ribbons, the choice system that changes the story and ending, enhanced ammo, Nemesis forms, several different types of enemies, whole areas, the puzzles, roughly six costumes, the mercenaries, the original creepy ambiance, etc.

 Even though I've talked a lot of bad about it so far, there are parts of this game that have improved upon. First off, we do have larger extended sequences in this compared to the original. We have a large sewer network, a much more expansive hospital, and a new massive underground Umbrella lab to go through. Next, the graphics are definitely pretty, and help improve on both the visuals of the environments and characters/enemies. Nemesis looks much more imposing and Jill and Carlos look a lot prettier than their original 1999 models. Finally, the controls and camera angle definitely help transition this title smoothly into the much more faster paced action focused design that Resident Evil 4 brought to the series, although that doesn't necessarily make it better than the original fixed camera angles to many people. Side note, inventory control is easier with the increased inventory space you get from pouches co,pared to the original, and to some, they may prefer the newer crafting style in this game since you don't need to carry a reloading tool to create ammunition (although you can get one in game to increase how much ammo you gain).

Again, although I haven't personally played the original, and there's A LOT I would have liked to see from the original game make it into this game, I still enjoyed this title. I would say this is not as good as the remake of 2, since it is much shorter, a lot more linear, and not as faithful to the original as 2's remake was. I still think I would really like to see just remasters of the original 2 and 3 games, but I don't know if or when they would happen. If you're able to look past this not being an EXACT remake as the original, I think you may be able to enjoy it. 

Whether you're new to 3 or not, I hope you can enjoy this experience and make the most out of your purchase if you do decide to get it. I recommend grabbing this on sale, it's not worth more than $20-30 in my opinion, and that's with the fact that you get Resident Evil Resistance alongside this purchase.

Don't get me wrong, while I'm not the biggest fan of the RE 2 Remake I think they did a solid job with it overall. But with this one... Not so much I would say. Since it is mostly a direct continuation of the RE 2 Remake, -well it mostly takes place during the previous title actualy- I have no other way than comparing this one to it and in comparisant at almost all aspects, this game is a stepback unfortunately. 

It lacks great level design, uses the same locations a lot of times and since if you want to stack up on valuable items you have to walk through each level a couple of times and it gets very tedious, most of the "improvements" -or changes I would say- from the previous remake are minimal and other than some slight graphical improvements -if you count lense flare as one for example- are also mostly UI related -and not welcomed in my point of view- then on top of all of these, characters other than Jill herself are paper thin and underdeveloped/used and the same can be said about the story too, enemy variety is insufficient and their designs feels rather lazy -especially compared to the enemies from the latter half of the Resi 2 Remake- there are almost no puzzles present in the game which is a really lackluster thing especially when you think this is a mainline Resident Evil title and finally the game has a few bugs and overall feels unpolished and is shockingly short. There. Almost all my discontent about the game without going into the details and spoilers.

HOWEVER, if I should go into the details and [u][b]spoilers[/b][/u], why would they change how items look in the map anyways for example? Those little literal jpegs of the items were easily recognizable and neat in the Resi 2 Remake, why make them minimalist signs and group them under certain categories? I would really like to see what an item exactly is without going through the hassle of dragging the cursor on it -no matter how minimal this might seem it really is annoying especially in a game where your main goal is to stack up on vital items- and to be honest the inventory screen considering the minimal changes done to it from the previous game make it feel kind of "weightless" and cheap if you get what I mean. Other than these I didn't really like how Hunter... Umm..."Beta"s I guess play out, They just feel unfair to fight against and why introduce them while I'm playing with a side character instead of Jill, you know the character that I feel the most comfortable with, in the context of comfortably dodging that is? Seemed like a weird choice to me. Oh and I don't know if is it only me but dismembering enemies seemed less detailed in this one compared to Resi 2 Remake. I remember being able to see zombies' goddang tendons and such after shooting them enough times in that one but in this game their limbs just almost "pop" off from their bodies. Another annoying thing was the part where we defended the room Jill was in, it was just uninspiring level design funneling enemies constantly and such. And lastly the penultimate fight with Nemesis felt a bit annoying and unfair than challenging. Just a little bit though.

Overall I can't really recommend this one because the only reason I've played this was because I love the series and the genre, so much so that even if it is a mediocre game I mostly end up satisfied with it, if not completely. I had a blast with Resident Evil 3. Although it did not live up to Resident Evil 2 Remake and cut a lot of content from the original material, I still enjoy it mostly. Note that I did not play the original game, but I have watched gameplay videos of it.

[b][u]Things that Resident Evil 3 did well[/u][/b]

• [b]The introduction.[/b] I personally prefer the remake's introduction to the original one. Also love them FMV moments.
• [b]All of the characters' personality shined really bright in the remake.[/b] (Jill being a total badass, Carlos being extremely likable and charming (I have the hots for him), Nikolai's antagonistic side)
• [b]The face models are just so beautiful and scream their respective characters.[/b] New Jill is dead gorgeous and Carlos sent me to Cloud 9 multiple times with his cutscenes.
• [b]Controversial take, but I LOVE the Nemesis redesign.[/b] It's just so well done and creepy, especially when he's charging at you with that freaking big frame of his.
• [b]The story (on its own) is pretty cohesive.[/b] I actually love how it connected back to Resident Evil 2 in some way and gave it an ending.
• [b]Inventory management is awesome as usual,[/b] one to be expected from Resident Evil. (I'm gonna ignore the 5th and 6th game here)
• [b]Some enemies (apart from Nemesis) really keep you on your toes and make you really anxious.[/b] (F*ck you Hunter Gamma)
• [b]The boss fights are pretty epic and satisfying.[/b]
• [b]The atmosphere of Raccoon City streets and the hospital.[/b] I forever love how Raccoon City looks and feels.
• [b]The soundtrack of Resident Evil 3 is simply amazing.[/b] The save room music is soothing but still reminds you of the danger ahead. The Nemesis chase music and hospital ambience had my hair stand on end. I also stayed through the credits just to hear that Staffs & Credit song. (The best piece of music from Resident Evil)

[b][u]Things that Resident Evil 3 did not so well[/u][/b]

• [b]The length.[/b] With double the price tag of Resident Evil 2, I expected Resident Evil 3 to be packed with content as well. The average play time of a playthrough is 4-5 hours which is disappointing. (I spent like 8-9 hours for my first playthrough because I backtracked and tried to 100% map exploration). I wish they didn't cut that much content from the original.
• [b]Level design is way too linear.[/b] Compared to Resident Evil 2 where you are encouraged to backtrack, Resident Evil 3 only features a few backtracking before it forces you to a new level.
• [b]Lack of puzzles.[/b] There are only 2 puzzles in this whole game! What the hell!
• [b]Nemesis is far less threatening than Mr. X,[/b] despite being the poster tyrant of Resident Evil. I was disappointed that Nemesis only chases you through scripted events and he can't even enter buildings! Mr. X definitely did a better job at being a stalker.
• [b]Lack of bonus content.[/b] They just encourage you to replay the games in multiple difficulties instead of offering us extra modes like Resident Evil 2 did.
• [b]One dialogue from the original game that got placed in such a terrible way in the remake:[/b] "You want S.T.A.R.S? I'll give you S.T.A.R.S!" They put that line where Jill gets cut off like 80% of the time and players would miss it! Horrible treatment to an iconic quote.

[b]All in all, I would pretty much recommend Resident Evil 3 when it's on sale.[/b] It's a short blast, but still a blast at the end of the day. Thankfully Capcom has acknowledged the criticism towards the game being unfaithful to the original material, and here's hoping that Resident Evil 4 Remake wouldn't have the same treatment that this game got.

An excellent and well-paced follow-up to the RE 2 remake that, much like the original, offers a different gameplay experience without sacrificing the vision of the original, or the tangible fear the Resident Evil brand is so well-known for.

It's important to remember that RE 4's genre-defining action-oriented changes didn't come from nowhere - the streamlining of the punishingly difficult and often tedious gameplay of the 1st and 2nd games in the series began with RE 3: Nemesis, and this remake captures this change in style. This is Resident Evil without the faff - without tedious backtracking, wandering around trying to figure out where the hell you're supposed to be going, or sections where your goal is to perform a time-consuming task while some unstoppable a**hole follows you round the room trying to force you to restart from a save 5 minutes earlier. Resident Evil 3 was and is Resident Evil for people who value their own time; for people who like a game that wants to tell a story, impart an experience, and let players overcome its obstacles in a manner other than losing hours of their life to obtuse trial-and-error. 

That's not to say that it hinders your ability to explore or make choices - the opening area in particular is a gorgeous mess of explorable obliterated city streets, back alleys, and neon-fronted shops littered with zombies - it's just that the way it is designed doesn't make you drop the controls at any point and go 'I can't do this anymore'. It cuts the fat from RE's sometimes bloated formula without losing the tension. Jill's increased mobility and a slightly more abundant amount of ammunition allows the story to drive forwards at a reasonable pace. If you're swayed, as I was for a time, by the 'the game's not long enough' crowd, then there are a tonne of games that are as 7-8 hours in essence but double that time with untelegraphed insta-kill sequences that'll force you back to a save point 5 mins prior through no fault of your own, or make you sneak everywhere on pain of restart. If your idea of value revolves around slogging through the same excruciating section again and again and vowing never to return when you're finished then I'm sure The Evil Within is cheap to buy right now. But I've got a life to live, man, and this might be the only survival horror game that hasn't felt like it was intent on wringing the longest hours of my life out of me. 

At no point was I bored or pushing through my own absolute tolerance for frustration to progress. At no point did I hit the 'god, is this thing nearly over' point and realise that I was only half-way there. Its challenges are well-designed and never so opaque that they require constant, pointless do-overs to understand, and it balances punishing sections with segments of catharsis. Often, it's simply Jill's palpable, well-acted personal drive that was motivation enough to spur me ever-forwards. RE 3 had a vision, told its story well, spooked me hard, and my first thought when I was done was 'I want to give that another go'. Even the fantastic RE 2 Remake had me finished after 1 play-through - I felt no compulsion to play what is basically the same campaign again and take a slightly different route through the same locations, because the route I had to take the first time was often meandering and time-wasting. And that game withheld some of its narrative from me as punishment. RE 3 doesn't f*ck you like that. 
 
There's a tonne of replayability here for anyone who wants it as well, and the reward for doing so is unlocking special weapons or key items from the get got that both reduce the amount of time-wasting on the next run and fundamentally change certain elements of the game's challenge. In short, the game rewards you for completing it. Makes sense, doesn't it? If you're looking for the horror equivalent of a 47-hour long Lord of the Rings Directors Cut, then this will never be the game for you. But if you're looking for a really enjoyable survival horror game with a tonne of actual, genuinely motivated replayability, an awesome protagonist, some really memorable moments, and one of the best-paced Resident Evil narratives released, then this is it. It's a different beast to RE 1 and 2, but then it always has been.
