[h1]KitKat Reviews #8[/h1] 
[h1]Resident Evil 3 (2020)[/h1] 

[h1]Game Plot:[/h1] 
This game takes us to Racoon City in 1998, the same time as Resident Evil 2 (2019), where we follow a former Special Tactics and Rescue Service (S.T.A.R.S.) member Jill Valentine. We first appear in her apartment moments before we find out what is happening in Raccoon City. Immediately after getting a phone call about Raccoon City's news, she is attacked by a Biochemical Organic Weapon called Nemesis developed by Umbrella. She is chased out of her apartment and heads to a rooftop to get picked up and removed from the chaos. The helicopter was attacked, and Jill was found by Carlos, who took her to an Underground operation. They needed her help to bring people to safety, and so began her night of terror, fighting the night to help others Survive.

[h1]Personal Opinion About Plot:[/h1] 
To be honest, this is a continuation of the last game in the Resident Evil Series. This game seems to be like another story they could have added into Resident Evil 2. I can tell they just wanted to add this game onto their production line just to show off or get money, either way. But I understand they need to produce what the public wants.

[h1]Game Gameplay:[/h1]
Like my Resident Evil 2 (2019) review, the original Resident Evil 3 game uses tank controls and fixed camera angles. The remake features "over-the-shoulder" third-person shooter gameplay like Resident Evil 4 and more recent games in the series that allows players the option to move while using their weapons, similar to Resident Evil 6. The assisted and standard difficulties mode deviates from the original by featuring autosaves and allowing players to save as often as they would like inside safe rooms. If the player chooses to play on "Hardcore" difficulty, players will be required to collect and use a finite number of ink ribbons to save the game's progress, much like in the original game.
While exploring different areas, players can find and pick up items that can help them survive and escape. Certain items, such as herbs and gun powder, can be combined to make healing items and ammunition. Items can also be inspected for clues gaining access to certain areas or items hidden throughout the game and can be discarded after use.
Overall combat varies depending on difficultly. Assisted difficulty allows aim assist and health recovery along with weaker enemies while hardcore difficulty has stronger enemies and has scarce ammo for players to find. Combat will also vary depending on who players are fighting. Enemies will generally come after players after they are spotted and can be killed or crippled to slow the down. Zombies will attempt to break into the station through windows but can be stopped if the windows are boarded up beforehand. Certain enemies must be fought in order to progress through the game and cannot be avoided.

[h1]Personal Opinion About Gameplay:[/h1]
Overall, the features that went in the game were much like any other Resident Evil game. Of course, shooting and puzzle-solving have returned with a vengeance from Resident Evil 7. The style of gameplay with the environment, music, etc. l, turns this game into an excellent immersive experience, but for my parents, it was more like a movie because they weren't playing, of course.

[h1]Personal Opinion on Graphics:[/h1] 
Much like Resident Evil 2, the graphics are top-notch, and their work in the games has stacked each other. Having teams design 3D models that are only seen once is impressive. This is what makes a game pop but it lacks in Storyline. 

[h1]Personal Opinion on Sound Design:[/h1]  
Compared to Resident Evil 7, I'm sad that the music score has a few nice soundtracks, but the music is appropriate to the producers' environment. They made music for background environment properties. Resident Evil 7 tells stories about what type of a situation you're in and when to panic, and when to run. Each environment that its theme, and each boss had their soundtrack that was up-close and in person. Here we have Resident Evil 3, which changes from the first person to the third person. This brings too many environmental soundtracks." Other than that, AMAZING ON 7.1 SURROUND.

[h1]Things needed to be Fixed like Bugs:[/h1]
Nah, no bugs! Only a few things you can do with enemy's that suspicious but, all's well!

[h1]Final Thoughts:[/h1] 
This a great test on their RE Engine and adds a step forward in their games. I'm looking forward to the series they are making and the new game they are releasing soon!

Is this a fun game? Short answer: yes. Is this a good Resident Evil 3 remake? Debatable. I have never played the original game, however, from what I have been told, much of that game did not make it into this game. In fact, from what I have been told, this is less a remake and more a re-imagining of RE3. So with that in mind, if you want to play this game to recapture the experience of the original on modern engines, you might be a bit disappointed.

From here on, spoilers do be here. Warned, you have been. Care, you should take.

So I will list the cons first:

This game is short:
My first play through, getting about 80% of the collectibles and taking my time exploring and figuring out what I need to do, took me a scant 8 hours of game time. This was on the standard difficulty. By the time I got the infinite ammo weapons, I was able to clear the hardest difficulty in just over an hour. You are not going to get your moneys worth if all you do is play the campaign once and then shelve it. 

The final boss can be cheap:
Stage 3 Nemesis can one shot you if you get hit by his combo. It will not matter if you have the defense buffing coins and are in full health. If you get caught by the combo, you will die. To be fair, this is the hardest difficulty and one should "be guud" but there is a difference in getting killed by a hard hitting boss and being stun locked into death.

The damn Charlie head:
This sequence is by far the cheapest, most annoying thing in this game. Bar none. Full stop. On the lower difficulties, the head rolls as normal and you are not likely to die unless  you get hung up on a corner or stand still. On the higher difficulties, the devs made the choice to speed the head up to an insane speed. You have to be nearly PERFECT with your movements or you will be crushed. Repeatedly. Nothing ruins an inferno speedrun like getting caught at the charlie head for an hour.

The collectables:
*lights cigar, takes drag, drinks adult beverage* So the collectables. 56 Files, 20 Charlie statues and about 10 or so weapon upgrades. Not too bad but the files in particular can be frustrating, not only do you have to have the file, but you have to open it and look at it till the end. Still, these arent too bad, I just wish they had a better way to track which of the files/dolls you have and dont have so you dont have to track them down one by one if you miss one.

The sound effects *caveat*:
I only have one issue with the sound effects with this game. What the hell is up with the sound level of the firearms. They all sound like airguns and not actual firearms. 

The Pros:

The Map: 
This thing is nice. It clearly marks any object you have seen in game. Not only that, but the map will tell you if you have missed an item in an area by staying red. Once the red color leaves an area of the map, you know you have gotten everything in that spot. 

The Dodge:
Get good with the dodge mechanic. This is amazing for weaving between enemies, especially during speedruns where you dont want to take the time to kill a foe. Dodge is your friend.

Choose your reward:
So this game does away with the achievement specific rewards and has a shop that you use points earned by completing records during gameplay. This is a godsend, you can get the infinite launcher after just a run or two assuming you know which records are the big point records and know how to get them quick.

Overall:

This game IN AND OF ITSELF is very fun. The combat feels nice and the mechanics are fun to toy with. However, being a RE3 remake, you inevitably have to compare. 

The game progression is so linear that anyone with any form of experience with shooters will finish the first run no later than 7 hours. This is due to lack of puzzles as well. Puzzles in RE games are the reason why playtime goes up the charts. But this one just foregoes it and thus not keeping faithful to the RE franchise. 

As a stand alone game it is fun. As a remake it fails. Too many key locations cut, and a HUGE missed oppertunity to make a open sandbox for exploration that is not plot essential. You're out in the damn streets of Racoon City but you are confined in a small area bounded by various debris which ultimately leaves you feeling trapped. Which is hilarious considering Jill is OUT IN THE STREETS! Huge missed oppertunity. 

I recommend this game to people who are not hardcore RE fans because they will feel lacking and their inner fan boy will rage at the cuts this game has made. I also recommend this game as long as its below $40.00 due to very limited replay value and the game experience is short due to linear gameplay and lack of puzzles. 

The long part:

List of pros: 
> Bad box art blue boy cameo had me laughing for a good 5 minutes.

> Visuals: All models looks polished. Jill is hot. Nemesis looks bad ass. Carlos is the beef cake eye candy for the ladies. 

> Combat system feels nice despite it being a little strange with its cancel animation frames in between knifing.

> Just dodge/counter mechanic is fun to play with.

The Cons:
> As a RES3 remake, it fails because it cuts out the feel of open streets with lots of twist and turns. This remake is VERY linear. It missed a great oppertunity to have a larger sandbox for extra exploration (easy to add because you don't need to script important plot or cut-scenes). 

> Core locations are cut from the original.

> Jill's supercop banter would have been fine but she comes off as kinda of a B***h. Too over the top.

> Somethings that don't make much sense even in the realms of the RE universe. Like the very first chase. Nemesis' choices are VERY Questionable. Take a huge guess who is gonna be a spy? I WONDER WHO IT COULD BE!?!?! DERRRRRR. Seriously, hes so obvious hes basically a Saturday cartoon villain in the RE universe.

> Replay value is cheapened as everything is scripted with no variation (with exception of ammo synthesis having a RNG). The only real replay value is the game shop.

> Too many rehashes of the recently remade RE2. Part of it is because despite being in the streets, the sandbox is simply too limited. Never do you feel like you are in a open ended street where you could go different places. This problem could have been solved by adding a plot-free map extension for casual exploration. BIG missed oppertunity (I know I said that already but this was a huge miss!).

> Lack of puzzles to stomp new comers. The map size is fine. The exploration size is lacking. Thus the game feels short for first comers. I finished this thing in 5 hours first run. All thanks to linear paths, and little to no puzzles to stomp me. Puzzles are a staple to RE games. Thus not very faithful to the RE spirit.

However, I didn't realize how much was cut from RE3 Remake until I played the original. Entire locations, branching choices and storylines, and more were cut. RE3 Remake feels like an entirely different game that shares only a few pieces of DNA and references with the original.

RE2 ('19) being praised so highly despite the missing content from the '98 original, doing the same boss fights in the same rooms at the same times no matter the scenario, and not fixing continuity issues within it's own version (boss fights not included in this example), let Capcom think it was okay to cut stuff out, but they were more careful this time.

After an invigorating Resident Evil 7 which toned down the action and upped the horror, Capcom gave us a fantastic remake of RE2. While it wasn't perfect, it was the closest Capcom ever got to the classic Resident Evil formula since Resident Evil 4 ruined it. Unfortunately It didn't take long for Capcom to drop the ball and end their winning streak. This remake of Resident Evil 3 which came out less than a year after Resident Evil 2 is a disappointment. It was obviously rushed to be bundled with a terrible Resident Evil multiplayer game nobody asked for and it shows. This is not a triple A title. It's a budget game at best, or an add-on to RE2.

A lot of assets are recycled from the RE2 remake. The gore and zombie damage have been toned down. Nemesis is completely scripted and nothing close to Mr. X which freely patrolled the RPD precinct. What a wasted opportunity! They could have expanded that concept and have Nemesis patrolling Raccoon City looking for you. Instead we get one area early in the game where you can run away from Nemesis in any direction, but all the other chases are scripted, linear and mostly cutscenes. One chase has Nemesis following you around with a flamethrower while you go up staircases and ladders. There's only one obvious path and nothing else to do. This isn't fun. 

There is a total of 2 puzzles in the game and they are incredibly easy. The only open area of the game is at the beginning and was already seen in the demo. After that, the games is linear and there isn't any exploration. The original game featured a lot more of Raccoon City streets and locations.

This time around, there are no randomized items, enemies or branching paths. The very things that made RE3 stand out from RE1 & RE2 and extremely replayable.

Bloodsuckers have been reduced to spiders spawning in a single portion of the game where you have to run around a maze to reset breakers. I'm pretty sure I played the exact same segment in one of the Metro games. So tired and unoriginal.

Sound is a mixed bag. Like for the RE2 remake, the music is toned down when it's not completely missing. The guns sound very weak. The voice acting is great, especially Carlos and Jill. For some strange reason, Nikolai's voice is lower than everybody else. How nobody noticed that before the game was completed is beyond me.

The graphics are fine, but like the other RE engine games, you need to waste a lot of time tweaking the many settings until you get something that looks good and runs smooth. The character models and monsters look great. The environments vary from great to terrible. A lot of 3D assets such as the cars look awful. They lack details and are often out of proportions. One of the delivery truck in the game appears as wide as a mini when Jill stands in front of it which is ridiculous.

I experienced a very annoying issue with the controls. Sometimes my character would stop aiming and turn around while backpedaling even though I was still holding the aim button. This resulted in the character presenting its backside to an enemy and taking loads of damage.

Finally the game is short...very short. Even with obvious padding such as clearing the hospital twice as both characters or that pointless room full of industrial lifts and elevators. Yes, the original RE games lasted just 3 hours IF you knew  exactly what to do, but the exploration, puzzles and unforgiving difficulty easily made the first attempt last 8 to 10 hours. That is, if you could finish at all. I remember restarting the original Resident Evil many times because I ran out of ammunition or healing before finally making it to the end.

I wish Capcom had spent a couple of years to make an even better RE3 remake than RE2 instead of this disposable action game with no heart or passion.

Yes, it's true that this is more of a spiritual remake than the Resident Evil 2 remake: RE2 REmake was 60-75% locations from the original (drastically improved graphically, of course) and 25-40% entirely new locations. The RE3 REmake is about 5-10% locations from the original RE3 and 90-95% entirely new. While the basic layout and progression of the game is the same as the original RE3 (City Streets > Police Station > Hospital > Lab) these locations themselves have an entirely new layout and design, as opposed to the RE2 REmake which largely stayed faithful to the original.

However, being an actual fan of the original RE3 - and one without a romanticised memory of that game - I'm able to remember that the locations in RE3 were never really that memorable to begin with. I'd be hard pressed to say the locations in the original RE3 were as iconic as the Mansion in RE1 or the Police Station in RE2. As such, I really don't care that they chose to recreate and redesign these areas from the ground up in this REmake, and I can't help but feel that the people crying about these changes are just looking for something to complain about.

The only locations from the original RE3 that are faithfully recreated here are the Police Station areas - which are basically just reused maps and assets from the RE2 REmake. This also seems to be a big bone of contention from some reviewers - "Why am I paying for a game that's 50% content from a game I already paid for???!!!" First of all, it's not 50%, it's more like 10%. Secondly, the ORIGINAL Resident Evil 3 revisited the Police Station from Resident Evil 2. If they'd chosen not to do that this time these same people would be complaining about it not being faithful enough to the original RE3. Again, looking for something to complain about.

The next common (and tired) complaint about this game is that it's both too short and too easy. Well, its length is actually startlingly close to the length of the original RE3. Yes, you could complete the original RE3 in less than an hour if you knew what you were doing. Of course, both the original and this REmake were not MEANT to be played just once. There are various rewards for beating the game several times under various conditions. As for being too easy, there is literally a setting called "Difficulty" in the options that sorts all that out for you. It's amazing to me how few people seem aware that most games have something like this. 

The other complaint I hear is that this game is too action oriented instead of horror. While it's true that this game has more of an action vibe than the RE2 REmake, it's still nowhere near the level of Resident Evil 4, 5 & 6 - this game is still firmly grounded in the Horror genre. And, again, I'm old enough to remember the original Resident Evil 3 which was, itself, more action oriented than its predecessors, and this was a complaint heard about that game at the time.

Now, personally, I actually liked a lot of the breaks from the original RE3 - kept it from feeling predictable. The story is exactly the same (with actually some improvements), the progression of the environments is basically the same, it's just the specifics that got altered but, in my opinion, most of these changes are welcome.


The Resident Evil 2 REmake was so phenomenally good it's hard to find many scathing reviews of it. But people like to be contrarian, like to give the impression that they're more discerning than the average, and slamming the Resident Evil 3 REmake is an easy way to give that impression. The fact is, most of the people who negatively reviewed this game decided they were going to do so before they even played it. It wasn't about the game, it was about their own egos. They're the same people who automatically dislike the sequel to a movie, or the second season of a TV series, because they think that's the "correct" view to hold that makes them sound smarter.

If you were a fan of the original RE3 but aren't so deluded as to think it "untouchable" then you will enjoy this REmake. I will say I think it's a little overpriced, but if you pick this up in a sale for £20 or less you shan't be disappointed.

It's hard to rate this game for me because the original Resident Evil 3 Nemesis was my favorite of the first old 3, with that said the game is good although it lacks content to justify it's release price tag.

Now with the review in dept...
Great Acting and characters, this is by far the best RE in terms of character development to me, I love this new Jill and even more the new Carlos, the rest of the cast even with it's short screentime is very good thanks to great acting.
Graphics, it's RE Engine, so you know, total eye candy and very well optimized, the delimb and gore is downgraded on the negative side, on the plus side there is better shading, I think (personally) RE2R had some issues balacing shading, strong lighting and screen space reflections, on RE3R they improved on this, the areas are also more open and detailed for the most part, no more cars with low poligons and textures on the street like in RE2R.
Now my biggest beef with this remake, the pacing, I have no issues with removing the clock tower or the park, I do have issues that they didn't add much to replace it, there's a part of the game after you switch from Carlos to Jill that feels very VERY rushed, you get back to Jill for some small walk and boss fight then going back to Carlos again, this very part seems rushed, short and WAY too linear, after that you go to the hospital as Carlos, this part in the remake was greatly expanded upon in contrast to the original and I have to say it's the best part of any RE I ever played aside from the zombie endurance at the end, I actually never felt this afraid to move on thanks to the setting, sound and also the amazing redesign for the Hunters, boy do they make me uneasy...
Also a very negative point, no Mercenaries, something I love on this RE is gameplay, the perfect dodge mechanic, it's so rewarding to pull off and it's a wasted oportunity to not create a mercenaries mode with great replay value just like on RE5/6. And no, Resistance did not click with me at ALL, if anything they could probably not add it and charge the same and my opinion would remain the same, hardly feelt like  it´s part of the same product package or makes up for it's release price tag.

And that is it, it's a mixed bag with Very Highs and Very Lows but still a great modernized take on the old one for our current times. Now if it had a good Mercenaries mode, a couple of nice open areas to explore that isn't underground wastes, that would make this my wet dream of a game. Sadly although good and sweet feels like a wasted oportunity and a dream of what more it could be.
If you can get it on the cheap then go for it, otherwise very disappointing.

Overall a fun experience, if a bit on the easy side (I played on normal). Some of the issues might be better on harder settings, but this was the base level so that's what I picked. Also has some tedious parts to it that happen too often.

For weapons:
I was drowning in gunpowder, way too much and I never really needed to use it. The starting pistol was kinda eh, didn't really care much for it, felt too weak and didn't sound all that great. Shotgun is amazing, and ammo was plentiful enough I got use it throughout no issue. Grenade launcher was pretty cool, though I think having 4 types of ammo for it was maybe a bit much. Outside of a boss encounter, I never used the mine type, and the acid type I tried, but it didn't do anything explosive didn't already do, so not sure why I'd use it.
Assault rifle was basically the pistol but full auto. It felt weak, I hated it but was forced to use it. In controlled bursts it was tolerable, but still lackluster. Frag grenades were powerful, but their sound effect didn't match that unfortunately, so they weren't super fun to use.

For the gameplay:
Overall pretty solid. I like the inventory management and picking and choosing what to bring, deciding how much healing/ammo/weapons to bring vs having space to pick up things as you go. There was a lot to pick up, so it never really felt like I was struggling with supplies.

My biggest gripe was the Nemesis boss that kept appearing constantly. From the very first encounter with him, where you can do nothing but just walk basically, I was already getting disappointed with him. He's showing breaking through a solid wall with absolutely no issue, yet several times we shut a door in his face, and whoops guess that'll keep him at bay. Like, what ? Why is that even working, it kills all the tension instantly.
Then there's the matter of him just straight up teleporting ahead of you in chase sequences. One notable example, I was coming out from a building, he jumps down and pretends to be scary, I ignore him and go up a ladder, he doesn't give chase, for some reason, then as I go down the path, guess who comes walking around the corner. He does, with no real way of having gotten there. This happens several times, and it's just annoying.

He never felt threatening or dangerous or scary. Just incredibly annoying. And he appeared waaay to frequently, it felt like he showed up every 30-45 minutes, sometimes several times in a row. That combined with the fact that things that shouldn't keep him at bay, somehow does repeatedly, and it's just a massive bother, more so than a "oh snap" moment when he pops out of nowhere like a jack-in-the-box for the tenth time.

You also fight him as a boss like 4-5 times ? Maybe more, hard to say because it all just starting blending together and was really the worst parts of the game imo. That's not even mentioning how you could easily get stunlocked and wombo combo'd to death while in recovery animation still, that's always fun.

If you can look past that though, I still enjoyed the game for what it was, even if it was a rather short experience. It was fun. Would I replay it ? Probably not, because there was a lot of scripted encounters, so it would all feel very samey to do again. But it was fun enough I can still recommend it, even if this review might seem negative.

RE3Make is a fine game, but it feels like it was rushed in more ways than one. Let's get all the negatives out of the way. 

Jill already feels like she's a complete character and that's honestly a big downfall for people who never played OG 3 or know Jill as a whole. While I like the fact she's suffering from PTSD, the fact she stays like she's some bad-ass woman from the beginning to the end of the game just feels... off-putting. Honestly, she should've been more portrayed as from going from her original growth (just wanting to live to being confident in herself, yet still showing restraint) to becoming the bad-ass women we know from RE Revelations & RE5. 

Secondly, the story length & exploration. It is pretty short, clocking in at 5 1/2 hours on a blind playthrough with no guides or anything external helping out. What OG 3 excelled in was making sure you could actually explore the entirety of Raccoon City's downtown area and giving you a good variety of options. The downfall of OG 3 was mainly being too explorative, sometimes feeling open worldy. In RE3Make, it feels the opposite. It feels too cramped and like there's not enough wiggle-room at times. While I get that's how RE2Make was and it did well as that's how OG 2 was as well, the whole spectrum with the 3rd game was vastly different despite being in the same city.

Not really any negatives aside from those however.

Voice Acting & Sound Design felt real nice, the new dodge & counter mechanic flows *really* well and it feels so satisfying to correctly pull it off. Carlos feels more like a character than from his original counterpart and Nemesis actually felt threatening when he appeared rather than just, "Oh no he's got a Rocket Launcher.. whoo..." And story isn't bad at all, feels improved. It's just too short to enjoy to the full extent. Plus Shop system makes replayability available alongside inner speedrunning.

[i]Rather than reviewing the game on its own, I'll instead compare keypoints to Resident Evil 2 while rating them from 1 to 5.[/i]
[b]
[h1]Gameplay (5/5):[/h1]This is classic Resident Evil gameplay, no doubt about that. However, when compared to Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 3 is a lot more action oriented rather than survival horror. You get a lot more ammo and more variety on firearms available for you to shoot, burn or explode zombies. There is even a dodge mechanic which was not present in Resident Evil 2 which at times is severely overpowered if used right. Oh right, we finally get actual explosive ammo for the grenade launcher here too which is always welcomed in my book.

[h1]Story (2/5):[/h1]Older Resident Evil titles were never praised for anything groundbreaking regarding story. The remake also suffers from the same flaws. Its got a couple of interesting characters but thats about it. The game is also humorously filled to the BRIM with scripted near-death / near-miss moments which make Call of Duty look like a masterpiece. These sequences will not really make you feel in danger due to the nature of it being scripted, you'll instead laugh at how dumb these scenes look.

[h1]Length (1/5):[/h1]There ain't no sugarcoating this one: The game is SHORT! I managed to beat my first playthrough in just under 4 hours without skipping cutscenes or rushing my playthrough. Compared to Resident Evil 2, there is a huge difference. Yeah, Resident Evil 2's 4 scenarios were essentially replaying the entire game again and again but every scenario had different enemy or item placement and even slightly different progression routes which made it feel fresh and increase the playtime immensely. Resident Evil 3 has only 1 scenario which is even shorter than 1 Resident Evil 2 scenario. The Mercenaries has been cut for something else which is...

[h1]Resident Evil Resistance (What the hell is this crap/5):[/h1]I can only comment for myself but I don't like Resistance. I was never a fan of DnD gameplay or any Multiplayer Resident Evil game which pretty much renders Resistance obsolete for me. Capcom should've instead created additional Single Player gamemodes such as bringing back Mercenaries or even something similar to Ghost Survivors from Resident Evil 2 which would work perfectly in Resident Evil 3 due to the more action oriented gameplay! Hell, we could've had another scenario where we play more as Carlos, the possibilities are very varied.

[h1]Soundtrack (4/5):[/h1]Resident Evil 2 soundtrack was a major letdown which forced me to use the original soundtrack from the PS1 version. Resident Evil 3 however improves on this subject a lot. Various tracks are remixes of the original PS1 version which is what Resident Evil 2's soundtrack should've been in the first place! However, unlike Resident Evil 2, you can't use the original PS1 soundtrack on this one unfortunately.

[h1]Nemesis (2/5):[/h1]Nemesis on its own is an alright enemy. However, compare him to Mr. X and he's pretty much rendered obsolete. Whereas Mr. X was found both in boss fights and during exploration of the RPD roaming around, Nemesis is pretty much reserved only for boss fights which is a major step down. He's not even that threatening during boss fights due to the dodge feature. Mr. X was a constant threat which heightened the tension immensely where Nemesis won't really come after you unless the game makes it painfully obvious that you'll get into a bossfight.

[h1]Bossfights (3/5):[/h1] Resident Evil 2 failed to deliver good bossfights. Most were average and one was downright stupid and not fun to play at all. (you'll know what I mean as soon as I mention "large containers").
While not really a big step up, Resident Evil 3 improves on this issue by making boss fights much more faster paced and generally more fun to play due to this nature.

[h1]Gore (1/5):[/h1]I gotta discuss this separately because Capcom really screwed up on this aspect. Zombies can no longer be gibbed on their legs and ragdoll physics have been completely removed. Something cool about zombies in Resident Evil 2 were these 2 key points. Gibbing legs meant that they were much less mobile and ragdoll physics made it really hard to tell if the zombie was really dead or not. Resident Evil 3 instead goes full 180 degrees and falls on its neck regarding this aspect. [/b]


[i]In conclusion, this game is NOT worth it at full price. For me it wasn't even worth it at the 20 euros discounted price that I got it. Its definitely a good game, its got great gameplay but it suffers from the exact big issue that Metal Gear Solid: Ground Zeroes suffered from: The length of the game is too damn short. If you can find a deal for maybe 15 or 10 euros, then I'd say grab it and play it, otherwise don't bother.[/i]

I finally got around to RE 3 Nemesis Remake. In the afterglow of completing this game I have unexpected confession. I just might have enjoyed it a tad more than RE 2 remake but that doesn't mean you should accept my personal nostalgic bias as irrefutable fact! You see RE3 remake didn't run as smoothly as its' predecessor. I experienced lag and minor errors in certain places. Fortunately for me nothing was game breaking. Likewise RE 3 remake is much shorter than RE2 remake but to its' credit I found its' straight forward fast paced antics refreshing. Aka, I'm not the biggest fan of convoluted puzzles,fetch quests,and back-tracking unless they are done "just right". I felt RE 1 Remake and even RE: 0 handled that particular game mechanic trinity perfectly but by contrast RE 2 remake came off as much more tedious. Your opinion of course may vary depending on the type of person you are and that is fine. Regardless to me it was nice RE 3 remake's solutions were much simpler and required far less "pieces".

The first aspect critics seemed to get in a tissy about (Myself included) beyond cut content was Nemesis when compared to Mr. X. To get to the heart of the issue, Mr. X would follow you into more areas at randomized intervals whereas Nemesis's chase sequences are  scripted and on rails whilst pertaining to specific triggered events. However in the big guy's defense let me just say those meticulously crafted "face offs" between him and Jill Valentine are terrifying. In one instance I was ascending a building under construction as the flames from Nemesis's flame thrower kept rising. In another tactical moment Nemesis untethers a "big bobble head" from a toy store rooftop only for it to go rolling after Miss Valentine like a boulder from an Indiana Jones movie. Nemesis even has his own special kind of infected he takes control of to further stalk Jill which is a new ability added to his beefy arsenal. Also unlike Mr. X, Nemesis often drops down from higher vantage points to surprise you and his super speed even allows him to quickly sidestep bullets or rockets from a rocket launcher with greater ease. While Nemesis may not be as "persistent" or unpredictable as Mr. X depending on where you are in the game he is still a menacing presence. Combine all this with his last wild card that allows him to mutate into different variations and at least to me personally he was a scarier foe than Mr. X by far. (I felt the exact same way many years ago when I played thru the original RE 2 and original RE3)

While I'm not always fond of celebrity simping I will admit begrudgingly the voice actors and voice actresses in this game did a great job to the point I even cared about the side characters like Tyrell, Kendo, and Brad. Of course the performers behind Jill,Nikolai, and Carlos gave a stellar performance. Everyone this time around feels that much more like a real breathing human being!

Beyond all this you should know what you are getting. Mainly you are in a city during a zombie pandemic and are trying to survive long enough for help to arrive. If you played the other RE games you know the lore behind Umbrella and the T-Virus. You know Jill in particular was one of the main protagonists from the first game. (As well as RE Revelations 1 and she has a more mysterious role to play in RE5) They do a good job delivering the plot details to you in a way that feels natural. (News reports,advisories,newspaper clippings,secret files,etc.) If anything it reminded me too much of the dire straits we are in right now but I digress. I know if I give my opinions on those "sensitive topics" this review is more likely to be nuked from orbit!

The game looks great for the most part beyond some of the effects looking blurry as if there's an unseen coat of vaseline on certain reflective surfaces. (Though admittedly when Jill looks at herself in the mirror at the beginning of the game that particular section is crystal clear with none of the  graphical jank you will uncover later on.)

All the musical scores made me feel anxiety,suspense,or outright fear so the audio deserves a positive mention as well. (I "love" the sounds of "splatters" and weapons firing to boot!)

At the end I'm surprised I like RE 3 Remake as much as I do. It doesn't innovate the genre or give us a huge open world with 1,001 hidden secrets but it is a semi-good 80's zombie movie in gaming form. RE3 remake might be just what the doctor ordered depending on the type of person you are. (But please fam,get it on sale as I do not think its' short length warrants the full 59.99 price tag. Maybe after RE Resistance is fleshed out more as an additional mode whilst including single player campaigns I'll change my mind!)

Welp! Finally sat down and finished RE3make. I'm sorta mixed on the game. The story, setting, atmosphere, and especially the score (like holy hell, that revised save room theme is beautiful, just makes me wish this remake did the same thing Spyro Reignited did and include both the original and revised OSTs to choose from), all excellent and gameplay mostly carries over pretty faithfully from the groundwork laid out in RE2make but it feels ever so slightly less refined (and I find it hard to describe). 

I think my main issue really is that a lot of the design philosophy that made the OG game so unique in the series is missing. Nemesis (despite his incredible redesign) has been very under utilized here. He used to stalk you if you didn't fight him one on one and that's a missing feature here, which is a pretty big let down. I was also reeeeally hoping to hear Nemesis' main encounter theme redone, as it was downright terrifying back in the day (hell, it still gives me chills x.x).

As for the characters and how Capcom told their story this time around, it's such a saving grace here, such faithful recreations of their designs, attitude, line delivery, just 👌👌👌 so good!

Idk, I just feel as though the player freedom I felt in RE2make (and the series legacy for that matter) was sorta lacking in this remake, it felt a helluva lot more linear. Once you make it passed the initial ouside city portion, it's like a glorified corridor... sorta lame. Also! The whole clock tower portion was cut from the remake... just... 😖😓 that was aesthetically my fave section, it had soooo much to appreciate! I was really looking forward to seeing that building brought to life in the RE Engine and it's a crying shame it was omitted.

I'm definitely glad this was made though and I certainly am grateful to have had a chance to experience one of my all time fave games from my wee bab days done up in such a pretty package but... my expectations were higher and given how good RE2make ended up being, it's hard to blame me 😋

Still though, no matter what I've said above, I still very much recommend you play this remake, especially if you're as big of a fan of 3 as I am.

Its clear this game was rushed out the door due to the success of RE2 Remake, because you can see it at every step you take.

Whole sections from the original have been cut out. Where's the  factory? Gone. What about the park? Gone. The gas station? You only get a 2 seconds glimpse of it, from a cutscene. The Clock Tower, the City Hall, all of that is gone.

Some other locations have also been changed or mixed with some new areas of the city. There's places where you spent a lot of time in the original going back and forth that now you simply can rush through in seconds and never go back.

Its a shame because the city is so well done. The whole atmosphere is great, and places like where you find Dario are crafted with so much attention to detail that you can't help but think IF ONLY they hadn't cut so much from the game...

But the cut content doesn't end with just some locations, enemies like crows or the Grave Digger are also nowhere to be found. 

The puzzles? There's not even a single one, unless you count the diamonds from the monument or the railway control as puzzles, which would be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ laughable.

Even such an iconic moment from the original game if not THE MOMENT, which is when you first encounter Nemesis at the RPD, has been cut out too...
[spoiler]Now you don't even know what happens to Brad. Did he died right there where you left him? Did he escaped and died later? How did he managed to get from that bar to the police station? We'll never know.	[/spoiler]

The story has been changed a lot too. 

Some of these changes I can live with, but some others follow the same pattern as the rest, as if they were more concerned about putting all thought and effort into reaching the launch deadline rather than trying to make the remake as good as possible...

The beginning was changed for one I particularly didn't like much. The ending has changed too. Like mentioned earlier, whole areas are missing, and some fights were also moved/changed. It's not good.

I understand this was a remake and its supposed to be different and that would've been a welcome change if only they had shown some more respect for the original material, just like they did with previous remakes of the franchise.

Nemesis is more annoying and stupid than challenging or terrifying like in the original. They somehow thought it was a good idea to introduce him within five minutes from the very start of the game... 

THUS COMPLETELY REMOVING ANY SENSE OF SURPRISE OR DANGER TO THE FOLLOWING ENCOUNTERS THROUGHOUT THE REST OF THE GAME. 

What the ♥♥♥♥? When one of the best things about Nemesis in the original game, was how he introduced himself to the player...

And the sections where you encounter him through the city, pfft, you can see then coming a mile away. 
[spoiler]There's one part after you restore power to the tracks where all the zombies vanish and you can easily predict that he's going to appear, which he does... And to be fair its not scary, or surprising, its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid.	[/spoiler] While in the original, you never expected him to come out of that tiny window, it was probably the most 'OH ♥♥♥♥' moment in the game, which this one is lacking. Instead of 'oh ♥♥♥♥' moments, there's plenty of 'ha, I knew it' moments. Lame.

I could keep going on, since there's so much stuff that feels wrong... 

Why remove the ink ribbons? It completely defeats the survival horror aspect if you'll be stumbling upon saving machines every 5 minutes and you don't have to think or managed how you save, just save scum till the end...

There's even one ridiculous segment when Nemesis is chasing you with the flamethrower where you get 2 saving machines and 2 vaults in the span of 2 minutes. Literally, 2 minutes, while he is chasing you and you're supposed to be desperately running for your life, you get to sit down, relax, save, manage your items... Ah, whatever...

But because of that, and the fact that you practically never run out of ammo and healing items, makes the game not feel challenging at all. Hardcore mode is a joke, Nightmare is what Hardcore mode should've been, and Inferno what should be unlocked after beating the game on Hardcore (Nightmare).

Very disappointing, and what's worse, is that we'll never get a proper Resident Evil 3 remake anymore, this was it, and such a wasted opportunity...

Shortly before this came out I remember hearing the devs say it would be faster paced and geared more towards action and shooting. This held true. It feels very much like being inside a movie. The voice acting is pretty good and the animations are top of the line. The seamless transition between cinematic and gameplay is well done. This engine was amazing in the RE2 remake and this has stayed true as well, with the lighting/shadowing/reflections being key to such a realistic atmosphere.
There is constant intensity and the music fits it well.
They added a little dodge mechanic which works well when timed just right and I seriously wish they would retroactively add that into the RE2 remake.

There are a few cons though. For fans of the original, this one feels rushed. I don't mean the development, I mean the game itself feels like it might be shorter. [spoiler] I've only played something like 3 hours now and I have already gotten to the part where you administer Jill with the antivirus  in the hospital as Carlos. I remember in the original it was quite some time before I even met Carlos and quite a long time before I took over as Carlos and that when I DID take over as Carlos it wasn't for too long of a time. In this one, you meet Carlos pretty much right away, take over as Carlos not too long after and you play as him multiple times. While this isn't meant to be a step by step remake of the original, it might throw some people off a bit. Just keep an open mind because playing as him isn't all that bad...it is just annoying since he can't access Jill's items and he has a punch/shove instead of a dodge. Also, you will return to the police station but as Carlos instead of Jill and it will feel a bit annoying clearing the same halls you may have already cleared in the previous title. I feel that as fast as the game seems to be going, they shouldn't have reused as much stuff from the last game...makes it feel more like a detailed expansion than a standalone title. While the original did this too, it still felt like a proper long game. [/spoiler]

The only other con I can think of off hand is despite how amazing the game LOOKS, the sound effects are far more important to me when it comes to building an immersive environment and they aren't that great. The guns sound especially weak and there is nothing else really that stands out as terrific.

All in all, worth it but not even close to as good as the RE2 remake.

EDIT: Wow, shocked at how short the game is. Blew through it in 6 hours. [spoiler] no tunnels filled with giant spiders, no graveyard with underground worm creature, shocked at how much was cut. Still not a bad experience, just do NOT buy full price. [/spoiler]

When Capcom announced they'd be remaking Resident Evil 2, I was apprehensive. I doubted they'd be able to do the game justice. News of the radical departures Capcom was taking from the original just added fuel to my concerns. Yet, my concerns proved unfounded. Capcom produced an excellent Remake. Could they repeat that feat? I wondered when I heard about this remake. I'm afraid this time around, with the Resident Evil 3 remake, the answer is a bit more complex.

Resident Evil 3 takes place before and after Resident Evil 2's story, during the T-virus outbreak that turned Raccoon City into Zombie Central. The original was the most actionized game in the classic trilogy, giving the signal for the direction the series would subsequently take. Still it was very much a classic Resident Evil game. The remake takes all that action up to eleven. It's not even trying to be a survival-horror game. The already rudimentary puzzles have been effectively taken out. Options and branching paths have also gone the way of the dodo. Nowhere throughout the game is there any real pressure or fear. Instead you get a completely linear and (relatively) bombastic action-shooter. Entertaining? Yes. Faithful to the vision of the original? Hardly. Good? Hm...

The action focus permeates the game. Positively and negatively. The attitude of the protagonist is a good example of the tone of the game. Jill is for the most part confident, at times even assertive. She knows what she wants and won't be deterred. Narratively, this is justified. Jill isn't some greener than broccoli rook like Leon, or a rank-amateur like Claire. She is a battle-hardened veteran, a member of an elite police unit. Plus, she has earned her zombie apocalypse stripes during the Arklay mansion incident in the first game. Jill is overall a great character. Even so, the game does take it too far at times. The things Jill survives, during cutscenes, are simply impossible for a normal human. Cars crashing down several stories, rockets exploding right next to her. It's too much. Makes me wonder why Umbrella bothers with bioweapons when they could just clone Jill.

Visually the game is a treat. Yes, it plays more like Resi5 rather than the game its based on, but it's still wearing the right clothes. Action-focused or not, this is still good ol'Raccoon city. With its RPD, slow lumbering zombies, enormous sewers and secret high-tech underground labs. Not some jungle filled with Rambo zombies wielding assault rifles that leads towards a rock punching duel inside a volcano. This is still the real original setting and style. Only prettier than ever. Jill and the other characters look and feel right. With the exception of a few strange facial animations here and there, I have no real complaints on the aesthetics front. In fact, some of the deviations from the original here were good. I enjoyed the new more distrusting dynamic between Jill and Mikhail for instance.

On the other hand, the action focus hurts the titular Nemesis, making him one of the game's greater disappointments. When compared to Mr.X from the previous game, that much more so. Nemesis is the bioweapon that pursues Jill throughout the game. At least narratively. But gameplay-wise you don't see much of that. All encounters are scripted and much of Jill's interactions with her pursuer happens via cut-scenes. Frequently over-the-top and heavy on action ones, with explosions that would make Michael Bay turn green with envy. As a result the whole pursuer gimmick falls flat on its face. It doesn't really feel like an unpredictable danger, a looming threat, just another typical obstacle to overcome. In the previous game you had to constantly listen for Mr. X's loud, ominous footsteps, dreading the next time he catches up with you. Now [i]that[/i] was a pursuer.

The other great disappointment is length. The game simply doesn't have all that much content. The original Resident Evil 3 was also the shortest to that point, this is even shorter. Some areas have been left out and as mentioned above the story branches have been nipped, making the game completely linear. It also lacks any extra modes, like Mercenaries. When contrasted with the previous Remake this feels even more strange. That one had extras, along with the two scenarios of course. But no, this game is 6-7 hours to finish and that's it. The end. No more. Well except Resistance. I suppose realizing this shortage of content Capcom bundled a completely separate asymmetric online game called Resistance to the package. Does anyone care? Seriously who asked for this? People want to play Resident Evil 3, not another half-assed online façade for a casino.

So, is it good? I had fun with this game while it lasted. Yes, it is primarily an action game, but despite some excesses, a mostly enjoyable one. It also takes place in a great, classic setting. But it's not really a classic Resident Evil experience nor does it last that long. For a €60 game, the amount of content is decisively lackluster. I am glad I didn't pay full price for this. I believe the game is worth a shot. But only on a good sale.

It's difficult to review this game without mentioning the RE2 remake, so I won't fight it. Compared to RE2, this game is very disappointing. RE2 started with the original game, built on it, modernized it, and made a definitive version that fits very well with what gamers expect nowadays, whilst still maintaining the spirit of the original.

RE3 did the opposite. It wasn't very close to the original at all except for the basic premise. The story was different, the game route was different, MANY areas and bosses were cut (at least a third to half of the original game), and ALL puzzles were cut. The only puzzles present could be solved by a child and they basically give you the solutions anyways. There isn't any survival horror left, it's just a third-person shooter. You get more than enough ammo on Standard difficulty to kill everything in your way.

I beat the game in 5 hours - and I was stopping to smell the roses. On top of being extremely short, there is basically no replayability either. Unlike RE2's Tyrant, this game's Nemesis is not dynamic. He shows up at the exact same places every time. In fact, the whole game is completely linear, with everything being the same every time. You can't even play as a different character or do a different route like in RE2. Once you've played it once, all there is to do is use points to buy helpful "boosts" in the in-game store, and play the same campaign over again.

The visuals, music, sound effects, and characters were all good. Gunplay still feels tight like in RE2, and you will be doing a lot more shooting in this game, so it's good that it holds up. The Hunter Beta is a good reimagining of a classic enemy. The Hunter Gamma is pretty terrible, and defeating it is more a measure of how well you can shoot a flame grenade into its mouth before getting insta-killed than anything else. The Drain Deimos is not at all threatening, except in the VERY distasteful and unnecessary scene where it throat-****s Jill.

All in all, the game is mediocre if you get it for $20 CDN / $15 USD. Do not buy it at full price. I have no doubt that the cutting of content and dumbing-down of gameplay was for the sake of finishing the multiplayer component. Nobody asked for that, and RE3 was - and still is - some RE fans' favourite in the whole series. I am very disappointed to see them treat the game this carelessly. They totally wasted the opportunity to remake a great game, most likely so they could push the microtransaction-riddled disaster that is RE: Resistance and make more money. Now there is no way RE3 fans will ever get to play a good remake.

RE2 shows how to remake a classic game the right way. RE3 shows how to do it the wrong way.

There's a lot of hate for this remake, most of which seems related to expectations for the remaster vs. reality. As newcomer to the series, I can only judge this game as a standalone item.

I played the RE1 and RE2 remasters just before this. I loved that those games centered around a primary location. It felt like it created an icon of those places, opposed to the usual "on rails" feeling in many story driven titles. In other games, you often find yourself rushing from one bit of scenery to the next so quickly that there's little to retain or worth remembering. That was one of the only pieces that felt "missing" to me from the Resident Evil recipe I was getting used to.

The graphics are stunning, although oddly demanding on the highest settings. Am RTX 2070 super really struggled to kick out 4k resolutions at decent settings, so I had to settle for 1080p. Not heartbreaking though.

The story itself is a bit shallow, only providing you pieces of the puzzle. However, I think that actually gives the Resident Evil titles a reasonable cohesive feeling. Tiny bits of plot add up over the entire series, opposed to other games which build something new with common threads. This definitely works for me!

In the end, I consider RE1 and RE2 better games overall but this was still money well spent at just about $1 per hour. There's plenty of replayability if you are into that kind of thing, with some cool features you unlock after your first playthrough. But there's too many games out there now to just grind one over and over in my opinion!

Let us get the obvious out of the way. This game is short. Especially compared to the RE:2 remake that came before it. That game was at least twice as long as this one and it had a campaign that could be played through from the perspective of 2 characters which added extra replay value since. But unfortunately length isn't the only flaw this game has. 

It feels a lot more streamlined than the previous remake. The levels are a lot more linear, supplies are more abundant and save places are everywhere. The places you go through don't feel as mazelike and grounded as they did in the previous remake. You don't get the sense that you are in the place you are in. You just run through the level, get the item you need and then move on to the other area. Another problem is also that the levels feel really familiar since the game basically takes place in the same place as the previous remake. So you are going through smaller versions af levels that were a lot more fleshed out the last time you went through them. There is no longer any puzzles, there is no longer a mazelike map where you need to find multiple items to progress. You only need 1 item which usually is at the end of the level. 

The Nemesis is very weak in comparison to mr. X in the previous game. Whereas that foe felt like he could jump at you at every moment this one feels very scripted only appearing in specific places in the game and for a game centered around him he really doesn't appear much. 

The story is paper thin and the characters are walking clichés which is not unexpected but it feels especially so in this game due to how short it is. The story just move too quickly for you to be invested in what little is going on, the characters and their relationships. All it is there for is to give context to shooting and as far as that purpose is concerned it does an alright albeit very rushed job at that.

The game looks amazing (the only issue being the lip synching sometimes) just like the previous game, it plays amazing too just like the previous game and the music is amazing just like the previous game. That is what saves it for me. The game has a strong foundation and as much as I dislike the length being short and it being a lot more streamlined, I still enjoyed my time with it and I think you would enjoy it as well if you liked what was offered the last time.

Wait for a sale and get it. It is worth a playthrough despite the flaws it has. Oh, and getting grapped by a zombie which triggers a short animation is still annoying as frick.

Unlike the success of RE2R, this game is a blueprint for how NOT to make a remake. This was a major letdown. But there are a few stellar things I'd still like to praise, which I'll get to shortly. Now, as for why I'd "recommend" this with the many issues it has, is simply because of my undying RE bias. Let the dissension commence.

Pros: 
- Gameplay is fun. It's smooth and easy to get used to.
- Visually stunning. Loved getting to see downtown Raccoon City in the RE Engine.
- Despite his disappointing appearance, Nemesis' functionality is fairly solid. A lot of scripted chases, but the terror he provides is still what I was wanting. He's a menace to get by and creates tension and fear around every corner.
- Character designs were great. Carlos benefited the most in terms of his character redesign.
- Opening escape sequence was great.

Cons:
- Let's get the worst offender out of the way: CUT CONTENT. Removing the sequence at the clock tower, the park area, the power plant, etc. But that's just the areas. Getting rid of the multiple endings from the og, someone deciding it was good idea to not include Barry in the end scene and many more frustrating story elements they decided to remove. I digress.
- Nemesis' appearance. God awful. Plain and simple.
- The bad hospital defense sequence. Hoards of enemies that come in easy-to-manage waves. Not challenging at all. Feels lazy and carries on for far too long.
- Two Nemesis boss battles having pretty much the exact same patterns of attack. And aside from a subtle change in the second fight, its really easy to figure out. More laziness.
- NOT ENOUGH NEMESIS. For a game literally based around this hulking monstrosity, they failed to give him enough of a spotlight.
- And lastly, this game felt extremely rushed. So much more time and care needed to be applied here.

Overall, if you're looking for a good remake, turn away. This game isn't for you. But if you're looking for great gameplay with amazing visuals, go right ahead. So if you do decide to embark, I hope you're able to enjoy. --- [b][i]7.7/10[/i][/b]

Meanwile, same old clown show in the reviews from "true" OG fans, crying that Capcom "stole" their precious original by cutting content. Just play the untouched classic if that's your jam. RE3R's job is plot glue between old RE and the sequels.

City's burning, every second counts - no room for clock tower riddles or slow-burn horror. Devs repeatedly stressed the characters' experience: Jill's a battle-hardened cop who survived Spencer Mansion - what's she got to fear, why should surviving this mess be a real struggle? Rhetorical as hell.

Shoehorning RE2R-style puzzles would've dragged the pacing to a crawl, bloating runtime artificially. Doesn't make sense narratively or production-wise - can't just sell the same game twice. That's why RE2R and RE3R feel similar yet worlds apart in gameplay: they're different games.

Gameplay post-100%: Combat mirrors RE2R - aim sway and weak enemy feedback hold it back from top-tier action, but mods for guns (grabbed via full exploration) fix it fast. Pace ramps up huge. Unlike the first half of RE2R here they're generous with ammo, so you can comfortably mow down zombies and use the environment to your advantage.

Overall, I think Capcom squeezed out the maximum here and delivered a solid entry in the classic series - a great game you can beat in a couple of evenings.

An engaging, although immensely flawed "remake" of the PS1 classic. 

How does RE3R compare to its original counterpart?
-No more choices/diverging paths/only one ending.
-Less Nemesis encounters/he's easier to take down/has disappointing drop supplies.
-Less weapons, costumes and overall unlockables.
-Mercenaries mode replaced by an inferior Dead by Daylight-esque "Resistance" multiplayer.

Despite all its faults, RE3R is one of my favorite modern entries in the series. The dodge mechanic is smoother and more rewarding than it felt in the original. Knife-only runs are a blast, especially after unlocking the Hot Dogger. The visuals are outstanding and everything plays out like a movie. While physically different from their classic counterparts, Jill and Carlos are still charming and likable protagonists. The story more or less follows the original's structure, with some changes here and there (ex. Tyrell has more screen time and Brad has a different fate). The writing is nothing special, but it's concise and to the point. There are plenty of interesting files to read; anyone into the series' lore won't be let down. RE3R also has an active modding community, thereby any issues (regarding the characters' looks and so forth) have plenty of fixes.

Been a huge RE fan since 1998, and will always defend the classic fixed camera games. I sympathize with anyone who may be disappointed with RE3R, being a fan of the original myself. But I've considered the production issues which played a role in RE3R's faults. For one thing, Capcom wasted resources focusing on its accompanying multiplayer, when they could have spent more time expanding the campaign itself. RE3R was also developed between RE2R and RE8, the latter which promises to have more replayability, as RE2R did. With these thoughts in mind, I must give credit where credit is due. Even with its short length and missing content,  RE3R is still fun with what the development team were able to achieve.     

Again, the problem with RE3R isn't so much what's in the game, but what's missing. Just as the game reaches its peak it ends. It's unfortunate, although I still recommend RE3R (especially on discount) to anyone who enjoys zombie media and modern RE.

What a letdown. Resident Evil 3 (first played on the Dreamcast in the days of my youth) was my favorite of the Resident Evil series. After the monumental success of the Resident Evil 2 remake, I could not have been more excited to see what Capcom had in store for its titular fan favorite villain, Nemesis. With the popularity of open world games becoming more the norm, and an enormous pantheon of game history to bring the horror filled streets of Raccoon City in a full scale livable nightmare was an enticing second Christmas. However what we instead got was a lackluster spit in the face to Resident Evil fans, with its stripped down map, removal of puzzles and weapons and benign and unintimidating Nemesis that becomes less and less interesting as the game slowly dies by every hour of play. Resident Evil 3 confuses difficulty and challenge by throwing in late game bullet sponge monsters to consume the resources you so carefully conserved in an attempt to trick you into thinking this game is in anyway a frightening or provocative experience. In a game that is set in a sprawling metropolitan city, Resident Evil 3 remake is a linear A to B to C adventure that guides you to the same predictable ludicrous uninspired endgame as every other Resident Evil game before this. With very little new to see or experience, and even less to see or collect than the original, this game is like trying to finish a movie you have already seen after taking a Benadryl; you want to see it through to the end for nostalgia's sake, but you are just so damn tired and bored, its hard to care.  

        Resident Evil Resistance was what Capcom instead exchanged finishing Resident Evil 3 hoping it would be such a success it would eclipse the otherwise above stated issues of the core game. RE: Resistance is a sad and poorly executed many vs 1 game that has never been all too successful to begin with. Games like Evolve and especially Dead by Daylight, already have proven themselves fun games with a strong replay-ability that continues to generate intrigue and interest and stays on top by its fan base alone. RE Resistance on the other hand, was a dead on arrival copy and paste venture that served only as a limp reminder that two unfinished and mediocre bundled games will never be as good as one superbly made game as they did with Resident Evil 2. 

        Make no mistake about it, while the graphics and sound design of Resident Evil 3 are truly top notch, the high note of the games first hour is unsustainable as the game jumps to a paint by numbers formula of familiar Resident Evil tropes with uninspired and boring set piece mechanics. By the second hour of play, you really feel when the game designers decided to rush the game to the finish line and bail on fully fleshing out Resident Evil 3, in favor of including a second rate mercenaries replacement no one asked for and even less enjoyed. Resident Evil 3: Nemesis remake is a six hour campaign game with zero replay-ability with a shocking $60 price tag. For these and so many more reasons, it brings me true sorrow to have to say, that Resident Evil 3: Nemesis remake is best forgotten in the guile's of video game failures with Aliens: Colonial Marines, No Mans Sky and Marvels: Avengers.

It has a lot of quality, the RE engine is incredible and tons of work was put into making this, it definitely shows. However, the fun is very limited.

 It is short, which is how it was for RE2 remake. You would then expect something similar to what RE2 remake does, and have a ton of replay value. Unfortunately this does not. There is 1 route, unlike the 4 remixed ones from before. Puzzles are nearly non existent as opposed to the tons of memorable, quality ones from before. Even after playing through twice on standard, I can only remember the subway station and vaccine mixing puzzles. The focus is clearly placed on the combat in this entry. 

The combat is fun I guess? The dodge/counter mechanic is cool and so the encounters are made more challenging from a shooter perspective, designed for the player to take them head on as opposed to thinking how to approach it. The tactical options you had before are less rewarding, The knife does less, and is a tool you can safely forgo starting once you leave the first section of the game due to the sheer amount of gunpowder and ammo given, and how gimped it has become.

 By reinforcing zombie limbs health and making it nearly impossible to kill a zombie on the floor with a knife, and having VERY few areas that are backtracked to constantly, on top of extra mobility options in the dodge, there is less incentive to clearing a room out and spending ammo. It is almost never truly necessary to confirm a zombie is fully dead, besides in small rooms. 

Overall less thinking goes into how you play which is something I truly admired about RE2 remake. It is one of the only games to make me come back to and try it again after so many hours. I used to never do challenge runs, but RE2 got me started. It did everything so right, and I still feel like I have so much more left to do in it after more than 80 hours. This can not be said about RE3 remake. After only around 10 hours I feel like I did everything I wanted. There feels like there is no incentive to go back and try again, there is nothing left missing because there is no alternate route or interesting mix to the gameplay that is worth the time. The shop is an interesting idea, but the rewards are hard to care about personally, because they are not unlocked by completing a specific objective. Do a couple misc. challenges in records, get currency, and you'll have a ton of extras to save time in the next playthrough. 

I like difficult games, and turning up the difficulty in games that do them well, but the difficulty modes added here I don't care about at all because the base game is just so mediocre. 

Lastly, multiplayer. I don't care about any of the RE games multiplayer besides 5's because that was coop and it was cool playing through an RE game with a friend. It feels like Capcom knew this game was short, so they threw it in to get more people playing and to make the initial $60 sting less. This did not work for me.

In conclusion, there is not a lot here. I am very glad I picked this up on sale, because I would genuinely be mad otherwise. A multiplayer I don't care about, a campaign that is okay and doesn't do a lot of what I admired from RE2 remake as well, and extra difficulties I also don't care about makes for a game I cannot recommend to people who liked RE2 remake, maybe to people who only play through a game once for the spectacle of it, and even then ONLY on a really good sale for how short it is. It is just really hard to care about this game. Maybe my tune would change if I had never played RE2 remake before?

I believe that the length of RE 3 together with the many cutscenes (I'll explain this later) made the game much less scary (because of the reasons explained below). For example, in the aforementioned RE games, there was more time for me to enjoy the atmosphre and build the tension. Progression was slow and I felt really uneasy. Each section of these previous games had me immersed in them, and of course, scared as hell. In RE 3, the sections were really short and didn't give me enough time to really experience them. Now I have to come back to the cutscenes problem. I don't think the cutscenes were bad, but the way they were used was odd. For example, at some parts, it was like the cutscenes were being used instead of letting me play the game. At other parts, they would take place before I felt I was really done exploring or going through a section. In addition, I had the impression there were too many cutscenes in a short period of time. When I was about to start getting imersed in the game, there was a cutscene and the section was over. It felt like having to leave a party during the fun part. It's disapointing, frustrating. I played the original and remember savoring each section of the  game. I was always on my toes. I spent a long time running around the streets of Racoon City, the Clocktower, the park, to mention a few. I don't mind the changes, I just think the game had so much potential and at the end of the day, you beat it and it doesn't feel like it should. With all that said, I still recommend RE3, but not for its full price. I bought it during the autumn sales for a very good price and don't regret it at all. I guess that if you are a fan of the franchise like me, it's still worth it.

[h1] Content [/h1]
To start off, I want to say I absolutely love this franchise. After this one, I can say that I've played all Resident Evils from 1 to 6, even the mess that was Operation Racoon City, so I am indeed a fan.

If you want to buy this because you liked RE2 Remake, I'm here to tell you that this game is not like it, in any way. I have almost 60 hours of RE2 playtime and unlocked every achievement, even going as far as beating the game without using recovery items and the inventory box, so yeah, you could say I like RE2 a lot. And that's why I bought this game, because I thought it would at least be just as good, but it was NOT.

It seems like they took literally every good thing that RE2 has and toned it down. This includes even playtime. I beat this game on hardcore in just a little over 7 hours, and this game doesn't feature a challenge mode like RE2 and doesn't have a second campaign. It does have unlockables and challenges, but nothing else. All you get is Jill's original campaign to play, so at least it must be deserving of an Oscar, right? No!

[h1] Story [/h1]

There's nothing special about it, it's the regular Resident Evil story. It's not the best, but it's still way better than RE5 and RE6, though. 

Jill and Carlos are well developed, and so is the villain. I never felt like the characters were shallow, and they actually have believable reasons to do what they're doing. It's not a The Last of Us by any means, but it's still very enjoyable.

[h1] Music [/h1]

Audiowork in a game is important, and unfortunately this game missed it by a long shot, because all(and I mean ALL) high points of the game had a very weak music choice, and this spoiled the best fights. When you're fighting Nemesis, the game decides to play a soft, calming song for some reason (???), and it absolutely takes away the epicness that was supposed to come with the fight. What's more fascinating is that they went the complete opposite direction with RE2, where the songs were absolute bangers and gave you a rush during every boss fight, which is the right choice. When you're exploring a dark place and are expecting zombies, the game plays a very unsettling music that fits the moment very well, but it drops the ball HARD during the boss fights. It's a shame, because the boss fights were very good in my opinion, and the music spoiled all of them.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

The gameplay is the same as RE2's with some minor tweaks. Now you have an unlimited knife and you can't use it to cancel zombie grabs, but you do have a dodge button. if you time it right before a zombie grabs you, Jill rolls to the side and the games goes on slow motion, allowing you to hit him with a critical shot if you choose to do so. I didn't dislike it, I feel like it's good to have some change to the gameplay, but I'm not exactly crazy about it. It's ok.

The zombies are also more well-balanced. They're not the bullet sponges anymore like in RE2, and it actually feels like you are doing damage to them when you shoot. Enemy variety didn't improve a lot, tho. You still only have regular zombie, stronger zombie and weird-big-zombie-thing 

[h1] Problems [/h1]

There was only one problem I encountered, and it's beyond me to know why the hell CAPCOM released the game without fixing this. During one of your fights with Nemesis, he has one specific attack that he transforms his arm into a whip and starts swinging it around. If you fail to get enough distance and dodge, he will hit you and get you stuck in a stun-lock until you die. Jill takes YEARS to get up after being hit, and it's more than enough time for Nemesis to combo you to oblivion before you can even heal. I died in this fight with Nemesis more than the entirety of the rest of the game, only because of this move. By the time I managed to finally beat Nemesis, I had died TWENTY FIVE times, and I was almost losing my mind. I don't have a clue how CAPCOM left this go unnoticed, because it's game breaking.

I also have a small nitpick. I know RE is not supposed to be realistic and everything, but the direction they took with RE2 gave me the idea that they were going to show at least some realism. For example: in RE2, Tyrant has a move where he impales Leon with his arm, and this is an insta-kill, and you can understand how that would kill Leon. In this game, Jill can get a meteor to her face and she would just get up normally like nothing happened. Nemesis here has a move where he just chews Jill's intestines for a solid 3 seconds and launches her at MACH 5 to the side, and you'd think that it's an insta-kill, but it's not. Look, I know it's a game and all, but when you're hit with such a move and don't die, this breaks the immersion completely.

[h1] Is it worth it? [/h1]

This is one of the games that deserve a "maybe", but unfortunately Steam doesn't have these.

You should buy it, but not for the current price. If you can get it for 60% off or more on a sale, go for it! Don't get me wrong, the game is not bad. Far from it. I had a blast for the most of my 7 hours, but the disappointment was huge, especially after I liked RE2 so much.

I'm not recommending it simply because the biggest reason that makes it worth buying is when it's on a sale. I hope CAPCOM doesn't do the same to the inevitable RE4 Remake they're making.

Edit: After playing RE 3 Classic on an emulator, I can confidently say that this game is whole light-years below the original. Go download a PS1 emulator and play RE3 Classic that you'll have way more fun with it than with this game
