After finishing the remake of Resident Evil 2 - which I consider as one of the best survival horror games ever made - I said to myself, that if Capcom will keep up the pace and won't change too much during production of Resident Evil 3, it will be almost as good as RE2. The problem is that not only they did changed some things for the worse, they also removed a lot of locations known from the original Resident Evil 3 from 1999.

The difference between remakes of Resident Evil 2 (2019) and Resident Evil 3 (2020) is pretty much the same as the difference between originals from 20 years ago. Today, just as back in the old days, RE3 lacks the explorational aspect of the game (such as searching for clues, combining items, solving puzzles) but it speeds up the pace of overall gameplay (Nemesis is not Mr. X) and it upgrades our moving abilities (dodging, counter attacks with melee and guns). There is a little bit of nostalgia when it comes to visiting areas known from RE2, but it is not taking too much of our time. Visually it stays the same as RE2, since it runs on RE Engine, and it looks beautiful. My biggest problems with this game concerns five things: Nemesis, disengaging idea of game saving with ribbon ink, lack of Live Selections, removing important locations from the original 1999 RE3 and short durability of the game.

1st flaw: Nemesis. One of the most iconic figures in the history of video games - who haunts Jill Valentine throughout all the game - is nothing like Mr. X from Resident Evil 2. While the script of Mr. X was made to search random areas and he could be always after us, Nemesis is scripted to show himself only in specific locations of the game. It makes him predictable, it kills element of surprise and it destroyes replayability of the game, which was an important part of RE2. In 1999, on hard mode, every time when player managed to put Nemesis down, he was dropping elements of a STI Eagle (a powerful pistol), which was a reward for us for fighting with him. If you're expecting something special for defeating Nemesis in RE3 Remake - don't hold your breath, man. Though I don't like his design so much comparing to his original version, he still looks pretty impressive in action, especially when he is rushing on us. This guy is a beast, but he has nothing on Mr. X in my opinion. See for yourself.

2nd flaw: lack of ink ribbon. This classic solution known from original Resident Evils does not exist anymore in RE3. Now you can save your game every time when you find a typewriter. I had no idea how important it was in this serie until they took it away from us. Removing this idea inflicts tremendously the tension of the gameplay. Knowing that you can save your game at any moment without consequences makes this game too simple in my opinion, and we have to remember that Jill Valentine can dodge and counter-attack enemy attempts to bite us. For 2019 RE2 vets this game will be too easy. Though after finishing the game we can change a difficulty for even harder ones (like Nightmare or Inferno) until we will play the last one, most of the players will probably lose their curiosity to finish it.

3rd flaw: no Live Selection. It was a feature from 1999 Resident Evil 3 which was giving a chance to the player of choosing a path during important moments of the game. For example, during our first encounter with Nemesis, Jill had a chance of fighting him or run away to the RPD station. During another encounter we could run away through the basement or hide in the kitchen. In original RE3 we had 10 Live Selections. It was one of the most long awaited aspects of the game that I wanted to see in the remake, but unfortunately Capcom decided not to implement this feature in the remake. Such a waste!

4th flaw: Removing of important locations from original. I will keep it simple: no clock tower, no factory, no park.

5th flaw: short duration of the game. During my first playthrough I finished the remake in 6 hours.

So what? Is it worth our time or not, you might ask? Honestly: despite all the flaws I have pointed out it's still a game worth playing. It has great pace, Nemesis is pretty intimidating at the start, RE Engine delivers great visuals, heavy weapons are satysfying to use against zombies, Jill Valentine herself is much more interesting than in the original and even if RE3 wasn't remade as well as RE2, I would still recommend this game. It's one of the most interesting AAA games of 2020, and even if hardcore players can be a little bit dissapointed, it still delivers a pretty intensive gameplay. 7/10.

[h1]▶️Introduction[/h1]
Resident Evil 3 2020 is basically the next remake in Capcom’s lineup. The game offers current-gen visuals, new voice acting and modernized yet classic gameplay that made Resident Evil a household name. The game was developed and published by [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/capcom]Capcom.[/url]

Release Date: 3rd April 2020

Last known update: 3rd September 2020

[h1]🎩Small-talk:[/h1]
[i]Let’s hope Capcom Remakes more games![/i]

[b]Smalltalk[/b]
It was only a matter of time until Capcom would release another Remake after the huge Resident Evil 2 remake success. Resident Evil 3 Remake is, in my opinion, a very good game, people do criticize the length of the story but in all honesty Resident Evil 2 had a similar 7-hour story, the only difference is that you basically replay it with some changes.
The Remake stays true to its identity and that’s something I cannot critique personally.


[h1]🎮Gameplay:[/h1]

[b]Basic Resident Evil mechanics:[/b]
Resident Evil 3 Remake is a 3rd Person Horror / Adventure Game where you can use guns and other things to protect yourself, keep in mind that by wasting bullets you're not going to go much further that why this game is simply not considered a shooter. Within the game, you walk around the map trying to solve various puzzles in order to unlock a door, sadly the puzzles are pretty uncommon compared to the previous remake. Roaming around feels pretty normal and you can find items and put them in your inventory, keep in mind that you have limited slots available and you have to be pretty efficient with the item’s use or simply try to obtain more Inventory slots by finding small backpacks. Solving puzzles is quite simple, there are most of the time useful clues within the Map, sometimes there are pieces of information in some Documents that you found, or it’s already within an item which means that you have to inspect/ examine in order to find something useful. Overall there is a lot of backtracking but the Map is built like that in order to make it a little less annoying.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2106951415

[b]Combat:[/b]
Once again, nothing much changes between the two remakes. Usually, you will find yourself fighting against normal infected people that require 3-4 headshots or even more. Wasting bullets will not help you either as you will have to melee your way through them. Granted your Knife doesn’t have limited uses anymore but it is a lot less useful now compared to Resident Evil 2. The melee mechanics in this game are truly and utterly inconsistent, you will almost always get beaten by a zombie once or twice in the melee fight. The shooting mechanics, on the other hand, became a little more consistent, I can remember that the previous shooting and damage model in RE2 was a little inconsistent but in this game things actually improved a little. Lastly, the last major difference is the fact that you actually spend most of the time in different locations fighting zombies which is a slight improvement because of the change of scenery, on the other hand, due to that puzzles are a rarity and most of them are actually boring.

[b]Other aspects:[/b]
[*]Boss fights with the Nemesis are truly fantastic, each time you beat him he comes back stronger and cooler, I personally liked Mister X a little more but Nemesis sure as hell fulfills his role. 

[*]Jill is a weird character, Resident Evil is basically all about Horror and the unknown, Jill, on the contrary, is a Veteran and you can tell because she almost always is unfazed and basically feels like Shadow of the Tomb Raider where you play as a killing machine. 

[*]The dodge mechanic is pretty cool but it is just another inconsistent mechanic at the end of the day.

[h1]🎭Story:[/h1]
Be aware, spoilers ahead!
 
You play as Jill Valentine who was the character you were playing with in the first Resident Evil game. After having some pretty bad dreams about becoming an infected you wake up and get a call by one of your colleagues. While talking everything turns upside down as Nemesis breaks through walls in order to eliminate you. You may ask, who or what is the [b]Nemesis[/b]? The Nemesis is basically the main antagonist and he is a literal bio-weapon with the main goal/purpose of eliminating all of the surviving Special Tactics and Rescue Service (S.T.A.R.S.) officers, including yourself. The main difference between him and Mister X is the fact that the Nemesis is a lot more agile, quicker, and can use modern weapons. After reaching the train in the Racoon City subway you meet Carlos and Viktor. After understanding your mission you will fight the Nemesis multiple times with him having multiple forms, but right after defeating the Nemesis Nikolai who’s the second antagonist shows up and at that moment the “dying” Nemesis succeeds in infecting Jill. Later on, Carlos finds Jill and brings her to the hospital that actually has the cure for the infections. After encounters with infected and mutated ones Carlos gets the cure and runs to Jill in order to save her. Keep in mind that Carlos’s friend and partner Tyrell is looking after Jill. Lastly, Jill reaches the facility that actually can produce the cure. In that facility, she will have to totally defeat the Nemesis using the Rail Gun. After finally killing the Nemesis she will have to leave both the facility and the CIty as the people above the system decided to nuke the city in order to stop the infected from spreading. As you reach the Helicopter Nikolai stops both of you and explains his plan and that money was the reason for everything, luckily you succeed in injuring Nikolai and you decide to not kill him and leave him alone on the rooftop. Truly a nice Action / Horror story. Still has a lot of plot-holes.

Resident Evil 3 Remake had a high bar to surpass as follow up to the arguably one of the best remake from Capcom. While I found this fun to play and I can spend hours in it, sadly Resident Evil 3 Remake fell way too far. 

My major issue probably how it feel really short (albeit around the same length as per scenario of Leon or Claire) and some area from original got removed or just glazed over quickly. With how Resident Evil 2 Remake focused more on RPD Station, I expected this game to cover Raccoon City. It did, but only like 1 hour (maybe 2-3 hours for first timer). Nemesis were not the overwhelming force like he was, even pale compared to the anxiety inducing Mr. X from the previous one. The mechanic somewhat changed too, I don't mind it, but I still prefer Resident Evil 2 Remake mechanic where zombies limbs can be destroyed and you never sure  if they truly dead first time around. This game more like the usual zombie, shoot till it dead. Another issue I have was the difficulty spike, Inferno was fun up until you get to boss part where you literally get one hit killed by most, and the last boss in Inferno was probably the hardest on any Resident Evil series I ever did.

Now the good stuff. The visual, vibe, and atmosphere are great, can feel the dread when outbreak Raccoon City happened (again shame it was too short). Jill was quite different than the original, I would say more realistic human. I still prefer the original, but came to like Jill newest depiction after a while (same as Claire). Can be quite challenging while still feel fair. The game have pretty good replayable value, stuff to unlock. It have some great moment and I explore side character more compared to original, so I will say good job on that.

This game have potential to be more, but sadly Capcom did not give it enough time in the oven. I feel quite mixed feeling about it. While I did not fully satisfied from the high expectation, but I really enjoy the game. Something that I feel definitely easy to pick up and play anytime. So with that I give this recommendation, but buy it on sale for better value, unless you already know you will really like this one.

You've heard everything that's wrong with the game, so I'm going to skim over those things to focus on what's right. The new character models look great, though Capcom's own offerings in terms of costumes are lacking compared to RE 2. There's also a multiplayer component that was poorly maintained after launch--but its still engaging and fun, just hampered by the lack of obvious functions that should be present in a persistent online multiplayer experience. Some iconic moments from RE3 classic has been cut from the game completely, and compared to RE2 REmake, its much shorter and much more action fueled. That was the case with the original trilogies but the caveat always was that Jill just needed an escape story and so that's why RE3 was created. After roughly 22 years the popularity of the franchise, following the success of RE2 REmake should've caused Capcom to handle the game with a little more care. The main story, like Resistance had the potential to be memorable in its own way but that wasn't the case. Considering how over 95% of the assets from RE2 was carried over, this game should've been a DLC but I digress. So on to the good parts. Jill feels faster and more athletic with her dodge mechanic, and you get a nice slowmo effect when you execute a perfect dodge. The controls are tight, and the game maintains a constant sense of surprise of and tension at all times--never knowing what is around the next corner, or when the Nemesis will just burst out and try to take your head off with a savage punch. My first playthrough took 6 hours, now I can complete the game in two and a half hours and the best speedrunners can do it sub 50 minutes. But I've put 52 hours into the game. How?

While I would have liked to see more of Nemesis and have a more fleshed out city section in the start with cool encounters with the games antagonist, I enjoyed the story we got. The the challenges system and opportunities to get special items from the item shop were also a great addition to this remake.

Gun play and weapons feel satisfying especially when you pop heads and the addition of a counter/dodge system was much needed in this instalment of the series.

I personally feel nemesis was a little too present in the start, it was evident the developers tried to cram him into the short city arc in the start as much as they possibly could. This made him more annoying and less menacing than he could have been with more time to flesh this story arc out.

The visuals are amazing, one of the reasons I love the newer residents evil titles is their attention to detail and sprawling environments and this game has that.

Overall, I enjoyed the game and have replayed it a number of times, that's what I like about the games duration, it doesn't ask too much of you... unless you play on the nightmare and inferno difficulties without any shop items. The game is plagued with cutscenes that end up doing way more harm than good - the few times that the game is allowed to be a game, it's actually quite fun.  The problem is that the game tries to do way too much to highlight the intensity of almost every action sequence rather than just letting the characters do their thing and letting the situation grab you.  It's like it's trying to pull you out of the driver's seat every 10 seconds to show you how intimidating Nemesis is rather than letting you encounter it for yourself.

The game is also way too short, though that may be a mercy considering how much fun the designers were keen on letting you have.

The soundtrack is nice though, easily one of the better ones this year.

All in all, the best parts of RE2 were stripped out in favor of taking control away from the player as much as possible.  When the game is allowed to be a game, it's fun, though those sequences are too few and far between to warrant a high price tag.  The game is okay if purchased for [i]maybe[/i] $10-20 or so.

[b]Resident Evil 3[/b], while has great intentions, lacks many notable attributes compared to its original counterpart in scope, storytelling, and overall length. As the original, initially released in 1999, it follows Jill Valentine, one of the last surviving members of her police squad, uncovering the ongoing story of Raccoon City being infested by an unexplained viral outbreak. During Jill's journey she's followed by sidekicks, foes, and constant endangerment while attempting to fulfill her impending "last escape" before the city is completely destroyed.

What Resident Evil 3 does right primarily involves creatively designing and expanding Raccoon City. Areas are filled with endless signs of chaos that ultimately overshadowed better times for former residents now turned infected or dead. It expands deserted and trashy streets, buildings, and many more with colorful decorations when they aren't totally vile and brooding. Other noticeable alterations involves its characters similarly to Resident Evil 2's modern rendition by giving their personalities more layers.

But those aren't enough to detract from the game's lack of content since there's truly missing and rushed elements. Not to say there's nothing there to surprise newcomers, and perhaps hardcore fans, but what's left for them are beyond from what would've improved the experience. Throughout the story fans of the franchise would notice extensive changes that are either immediately different or never given enough time. To some audiences theses alterations wouldn't entirely prevent enjoyment but there's enough oddly produced ideas that would've required further questioning and adjustments during development.

Aside feeling totally rushed, another of its biggest mistakes that cannot be ignored are its downgraded mechanics. Compared to the first sequel its portrayal of violence and collision detection have somehow been ruined by awkward precision and overpowered AI. Capcom having enemies programmed to tolerate pain isn't new but has proven here to be a terrible concept as it greatly reduces the assurance they're permanently dead. Now, instead of literally cutting and shooting through their seemingly fragile bodies, players are forced to frequently gamble with their time, patience, and items especially upon encountering hordes.

Once again, as the original, Resident Evil 3 unfortunately feels like an expansion pack to its predecessor rather than an entirely new story that offers anything groundbreaking. It introduces ideas that feel less of an improvement but certainly cutting corners to fulfill the game's frenetic length. It's a shame because even with its main antagonist heavily advertised as its selling point Nemesis feels conveniently attached, while predictably terrorizing anybody, than surpassing expectations. So much could've been done but alas was clearly made with the intent to be more direct than fully explored.

It was supposed to be Jill's last escape but couldn't run far enough to achieve the greatness as its predecessors.

[h1]Resident Evil 3 Review[/h1]

[hr]
[h1]Overview[/h1]
Resident Evil 3 is a fun game, but it is also one of the less memorable entries in the series for me. I played through it multiple times while going for all the achievements, and while I did enjoy my time with it, the experience feels much smaller compared to other Resident Evil games.

The game looks great and plays well, but it is extremely short and very linear. It often feels more like a smaller follow up to Resident Evil 2 rather than a full standalone experience. Still, despite its issues, it is an enjoyable game if you know what to expect.

[hr]
[h1]What It Is[/h1]
Resident Evil 3 follows Jill Valentine as she attempts to escape Raccoon City during the outbreak while being hunted by a powerful bioweapon known as Nemesis.

The game mixes survival horror with a stronger focus on action. You move through a series of scripted locations while fighting enemies, solving a few puzzles, and progressing through the story as the situation in the city continues to spiral out of control.

Compared to other Resident Evil titles, the campaign is much more linear and straightforward.

[hr]
[h1]Graphics and Presentation[/h1]
One thing the game does very well is its presentation. The graphics look excellent and feel like an evolution of the Resident Evil 2 remake engine.

Character models, lighting, and environments all look great. The opening sections in the streets of Raccoon City are particularly impressive and create a strong first impression.

Overall the game looks fantastic and runs smoothly, which helps carry the experience even when other parts feel lacking.

[hr]
[h1]Gameplay and Combat[/h1]
Gameplay leans more toward action compared to other entries. You spend a lot more time shooting enemies rather than carefully avoiding them.

Jill Valentine feels great to control and comes with a dodge mechanic that allows her to evade attacks. When it works, the dodge feels very satisfying and can help you escape dangerous situations. However, the timing can feel very strict and it never fully clicked for me even after multiple playthroughs.

The mechanic seems especially designed for encounters with Nemesis, where quick reactions are much more important.

[hr]
[h1]Level Design and Exploration[/h1]
The biggest weakness of the game is how linear it is. Exploration is very limited and there is very little backtracking compared to Resident Evil 2.

Many sections feel heavily scripted, and once you finish an area you usually do not return to it. This makes the game feel much smaller than other entries in the series.

The opening section in Raccoon City is probably the most interesting part of the game. Unfortunately the later areas do not offer the same sense of exploration.

[hr]
[h1]Story and Length[/h1]
The story itself is solid and the characters are enjoyable. Jill Valentine is a great protagonist and the overall narrative works well.

However, the campaign is extremely short. A normal playthrough usually lasts around five to six hours. If you know where to go and what to do, the game can be completed even faster.

There is even an achievement for finishing the game in under two hours, which shows just how short the campaign really is.

Another disappointment is that several locations and features from the original Resident Evil 3 were removed in the remake. Areas like the clock tower and other locations from the original game did not make it into this version, which makes the remake feel smaller than it could have been.

[hr]
[h1]Achievements and Replayability[/h1]
Going for 100 percent completion is fairly straightforward. Because the game is short and very linear, it becomes easy to memorize routes and objectives.

Multiple playthroughs are expected if you want to unlock everything, but since the game is so short it never becomes too overwhelming.

Still, the lack of variety means that replaying the game can start to feel predictable.

[hr]
[h1]What Works[/h1]
[list]
[*]Excellent graphics and presentation
[*]Jill Valentine is a strong and fun protagonist
[*]Fast paced action focused gameplay
[*]Nemesis creates some intense encounters
[*]Short playthroughs make achievement hunting manageable
[/list]

[hr]
[h1]What Falls Short[/h1]
[list]
[*]Campaign is extremely short for a full price game
[*]Very linear level design with little exploration
[*]Several locations and features from the original were removed
[*]Dodge mechanic timing can feel inconsistent
[*]Replayability feels limited compared to other Resident Evil games
[/list]

[hr]
[h1]Verdict[/h1]
Thumbs up. Resident Evil 3 is a fun but very short experience. The graphics, characters, and action are all enjoyable, but the game feels smaller and more linear than many other entries in the series. It is definitely worth playing, but it is best picked up on sale rather than at full price.

I absolutely love this game! I am a huge fan of the original and even though there are certain aspects I wish they kept, Capcom did an amazing job with creating a modern interpretation of this classic. The pacing, THE PACING, is phenomenal. The plot of the game is about Jill trying to escape the city before time runs out and it really did feel like your life was on the line in every moment as you were being rushed through the remains of an overnight viral outbreak. The game was longer than the original, which was to be expected, so I'm glad I got to play as my second favorite heroine (Ada will always be #1) for a longer period of time. Unlike most fans, I'm happy that Nemesis didn't operate like Mr. X. We don't need a stalker for every game and it was honestly one of my least favorite things about the original RE3. The additional plot points that weren't in the original (Bard and his team creating the vaccine, Tyrell and Carlos patrolling the RPD, and an underground Umbrella facility beneath Spencer Memorial) really tied things together beautifully. I highly recommend this game, especially if you were obsessed with the original like I was in my childhood. 

Side note: I was hoping that Capcom would release more bonus content such as costumes and a side mission involving Tyrell and/or Nicholai but it seems they have finished production completely on this title. That's fine since I can always mod and there's also RE:Resistance, which btw is a gigantic addition and really makes the purchase price worth it. Resistance reminds me a lot of RE:Outbreak which is my absolute favorite RE title.

I purchased and completed Resident Evil 3 on PS4 -- going so far as to earn the Platinum Trophy -- and I've just finished collecting all of the achievements on the Steam version too. So obviously, I really enjoy the game. 

That's not to say it doesn't have issues. It does, particularly if you're a fan of the original and you aren't happy with the content that was cut from the remake. I know a lot of people are upset over the removal of the Clock Tower, but I was more upset by the loss of the Grave Digger fight. It was my favorite encounter in the original version of Resident Evil 3.

Still, the remake is pretty strong in its own right. The short campaign makes for a decent speed run game, the scripted encounters with Nemesis are pretty good, and it has good set pieces. The redesigned RPD and Hospital segments are good, and it's rewarding unlocking all of the special weapons and items.

If you're really put off by the missing content from the OG version of RE3, then by all means wait for a sale to pick it up. Either way, I think it's worth your time to play.

To preface, a friend purchased this game for me solely in an effort to piss me off, knowing that I already had a poor opinion of this remake of one of my favorites. It isn't the worst game I've ever played, but it is easily the worst Resident Evil I've played. As a big fan of the series, I was horribly disappointed with this game.

PROS:
+Jill and Carlos are genuinely enjoyable and I do like their presentation in the remake. 

+Nemesis (in his original and second forms) looks much better than the original and feels like the prototype monstrosity he's meant to be.

+the gunplay is passable and the combat roll is an interesting feature that creates a higher skill ceiling in its own way.

CONS:
-this game is wildly short; I played RE3 on-and-off while streaming for friends, and finished my first, blind playthrough in about 5.5 hours. Entire sections of the original were cut out and/or crammed together for the worse.

-there is pretty much no replayability to RE3 Remake, you've seen everything it has to offer in a single playthrough. The unlock shop is the only incentive for playing the game over and over, and all it offers are various things to buff up the player.

-the story is dumbed down and stunted compared to the original (a feat, to be sure), with things like the Live Selection sequences and alternate pathways to your objectives being completely cut. No alt endings, either. It's like a "Greatest Hits" album of RE3 without any of the greatest hits.

-there is no real tension or horror in this game at all, and the only pressure it ever created was through horribly unfun segments like the Hospital defense.

-gameplay-wise, the titular Nemesis is an absolute joke of an enemy and takes little effort at all to beat down. On top of this, his final form looks and feels like a bland rip of Evelyn from RE7, and he presents no difficulty at all.

-the only real difficulty to be found in this game is via its top two difficulties, the highest of which is called Inferno. If you have not more or less mastered your jukes and the dodge roll (alongside purchasing various unlocks), this difficulty is near impossible. The final boss becomes a test of how many perfectly-timed rolls you can do in order to avoid guaranteed death. 

-the gunplay is passable and decent, but the overall gameplay here is not good enough to carry this game if you're not already a fan of RE. This is a poor RE game and a poor action game to boot.

-the Hunter Gammas are a lame gimmick and look stupid as ♥♥♥♥ lmao

Oh boy I've been eager to finish this game to finally post a review, (slight spoilers ahead) because DAMN I have quite a bunch of things to say. 
Overall I do give a "thumbs up" if that means anything, but I am quite unhappy about a lot of things, so here we go.

First off, as you might've already heard, this game is RUSHED, and it's not just the length either, which is the sad part. The game is about 3-4 hours long, with full exploration I might stretch it to a generous 5, but it's not just that, even the content that IS in the game just isn't entirely great. There are recycled assets, recycled LEVELS, bad sound mixing and overall some strange or straight up bad design choices.

Apart from the first level, which is AMAZING, it's just a huge downfall from there, because apart from the first level, the only original levels are the hospital and the underground lab, from which neither is particularly interesting. The first level is pretty much roaming and exploring the Raccoon City streets while solving some obstacles, and that's great, it's exactly what you'd want in an RE game, but even this level has one huge problem: once Nemesis starts chasing you towards the end, Jill crouches behind a garage door and then closes it, effectively cutting the level suddenly right there and then while you might've still had some items you left to collect later. As the inventory in the early game is very limited, I used to juggle items around the safe area and the streets so I can get most, if not all of it, but then without any warning I was pushed by Nemesis to escape the streets and Jill closed off the entire area before I could've even finished the gems treasure box, which was irritating.

But well, once you get past that, it doesn't get any better, there's a sewer level again, which we've all seen before and nobody likes, another visit to the police station which we've already seen in RE2, then finally a new area, the hospital, but that one isn't particularly interesting in anything, and then apart from some subway/small street sections or annoying generator repairs, you just get to the underground lab, which is fine for the most part but it's pretty much just an ending boss-rush of Nemesis forms.

Audio mixing is a bit strange aswell, the overall game is kinda quiet, Carlos' and Jill's voice actors are fine while Nicholai for example is super super quiet? Music is kinda quiet aswell, I thought it would pump some adrenaline a bit more, the soundtrack isn't even quite remarkable aswell, just some classic action movie stuff, it doesn't anchor the experience, but it's nothing crazy.  So don't know what they screwed up there with the audio.

And apart from the crazy sudden entire first level area lockoff, there's just overall some weird or bad design decisions. Nemesis is mostly scripted, it doesn't really chase you, it's mostly just a few scripted scenes where you hold or click a button for "interactivity". His dog-form transformation also isn't particularly unique or interesting and just makes him less badass really. Jill's new design is actually quite amazing in my opinion, I think she's super hot, and together with Carlos they are my favorite characters in this game. Carlos did a great job, his voice and character is great and fun. Even the character switching decision would've been fine if the game was longer, but with this kind of length, Carlos' campaign is pretty much half of the game and that's not good, we want Jill, not Carlos. If the game was longer then the Carlos sections would have been a nice and interesting break, but it isn't sadly. The "zombie defense" part would've also been ok if it didn't suffer from the same issue.

Also no idea why "Hunt for the fuses (0/3)" ever sounded like a great objective to anyone. The game is already mostly just item hunting, there's only a really few real "puzzles", and even those aren't too difficult (but that's fine by me as I hate puzzles, just pointing it out). 

The graphics are a huge plus, as those are super clean and polished. Character models look great, animations super fluid and believable. Facial animations also stunning. Controls are good and menus quick, easy to navigate and responsive.

The new "dodge" is super overpowered, it should have some more of a cooldown. Once you learn the timing, nothing can hurt you really if you're smart with your movement and timings. It's a fine addition as Jill should be rather agile, but it should have been toned down a little bit.

n the original, it added gravitas to nemesis' intro by having it kill the other STARS member. it also kind of was brad's way of making up for abandoning jill, chris, and wester at the start of RE1.

having brad be the one to, for all general purposes, kill marvin removes all of marven's heroics in outbreak. if anyone was not aware, marvin got his injuries in the line of making sure a goup of cops and survivors were able to escape, staying behind as he already took a bite. it was an awesome moment of self-sacrificing heroics, and one of the reasons marvin has been one of my favorite RE side characters for decades.

as for the big licker nemesis: V-ACTS isnt supposed to work on tyrants, they use a different strain of the T-virus. you'll note that while tyrants do mutate without such lings as limiter coats, they dont mutate like the rank and file zombies do. example, in lore, the RE1 outbreak was caused by airborne dispersal of the T-virus by T-001, and that strain used V-ACTS to mutate zombies into crimson heads. the RE2-3 outbreak has a mutant strain in which V-ACTS transforms zombies into lickers. in RE6, the C virus (being partially derived from T-veronica) uses V-ACTS to turn zombies into bloodshots.

nemesis' weapons. instead of his gatling, he has a flamethrower. many BOWs have a weakness to fire, and it does not make sense to equip nemesis with a flamer. nemesis is indeed singleminded in his pursual of his targets, but he does not care about collateral damage at all. this means nemesis could potentially do more damage to his controllers' operations than his target.

and the rocket launcher. i dont even know why they bothered including it. in the original, the rocket launcher served the plot purpose of shooting down the rescue helecopter, which then destroys the clock tower. the only thing it accomplishes here in R3make is launching jill over a barricade. he doesent even follow, even though he's been jumping much higher things the entire time previous to this. the entire section where you're dodging rockets really makes the rocket launcher look extremely worthless, as nemesis was much harder to deal with when he was unarmed.

quasi-QTEs: there are many situations in the game that handle like "playable cutscenes," but are not true QTEs (thankfully, there is a bare minimum of those.) in these "quasi-QTEs" you're basically stuck in a cinematic, and the only input accepted is the input that progresses you. the action basically stops until you do what the game wants you to do.
the most egregious offender is the "hostage situation" scene. this brings me to my next point.

there are also numerous times in the game where your controls are randomly disabled. for example, the entire starting sequince does not let you run until the game gives you the prompt. many other times running is disabled. i lost count of the times jill would take some tumble in a cutscene, and after, she's in her low-health idle animations regardless of your actual life value. running is then disabled until she "catches her breath." or all of the times you're on the radio, but you cannot open a door or pick something up. you cannot even open your inventory or aim after you've taken a hit until the recovery animation completes.

mechanics are janky as all get out, especially dodging. after unlocking the shop, i now see why. in order to reduce dodge jank, you must first beat the game. then you have to spend some of the points you earned (and inventory space i'm assuming) to hold an item which reduces the jank. it seems like a REALLY bad developer idea to "increase replayability."

overall, i feel RE2make was the better game. mr x feels more like nemesis than this nemesis does. RE2make did not outright remove the most memorable setpieces of the original game. it just feels like R3make is a step backwards.

First, I'd like to say, that this game, should have been released as a 20-30$ costing expansion to RE2 remake.
And, instead of a traditional review, here's a FAQ:

[b]Q: Why an expansion, and not a stand alone game?[/b]
A: because, while there is some replayability, once you finish it, you are done. Best example
is RE2 remake: it has 4 scenarios, so that's 4, different enough, playthroughs. Plus all the extra content.
There isn't much extra in RE3 remake (I don't count that bundled online game as an extra).

[b]Q: So it's not worth the full asking price?[/b]
A: I got it at 60% off, I recommend you to get it for that price, or lower, too.

[b]Q: How is it different from the original RE3?[/b]
A: There are quite a few areas and enemies missing from the original. And mercenaries mode is missing too. The only thing that is there, is the unlockables.

[b]Q: If I want only 1 game, should I get this or RE2 remake?[/b]
A: RE2 remake, it's better in nearly every way.

[b]Q: So is RE3 remake a bad game?[/b]
A: no, not really. It was simply handled badly, and it should've had most of the missing areas/etc
(or new ones) from the original. That online game should have been [i]it's own thing[/i].
This probably would have delayed the release of the game, but for the better, I'm sure.

[b]Q: If I liked RE2 remake, will I like this game?[/b]
A: yes. Just make sure you buy this one, at a discount.

[b]Q: How's [spoiler]Nemesis[/spoiler]?[/b]
A: personally, I liked his redesign. The transformations, though they make sense, could have had a bit more bizzare look. When I played RE2 remake, with each new [spoiler]Birkin[/spoiler] transformation, I always thought "what the hell is that thing?". I never thought that, when fighting [spoiler]Nemesis[/spoiler]. It's not as short as some people are making it out to be.  A full playthrough on hardcore difficulty took me a little over ten hours.  Granted, I like to take my time and fully explore most of the games I play, so your mileage may vary, however I suspect that the folks who clocked in a four or five hour playthough were probably playing on easy or normal.  On those difficulties, exploring everything and stocking up on items probably wouldn't be as necessary.  No shame, but I do wish reviewers would be more transparent about stuff like that.  Anyways, there are a couple of things I want to address about Resident Evil 3.  First off, regardless of the difficulty you play on, this one is more difficult than previous games in the series, for a variety of reasons.  Fortunately, this is balanced out by the addition of a dodge roll, which when timed well slows down time.  If you aim your weapon immediately after a perfect dodge roll, it will auto lock to the weak point on the enemy you just dodged giving you free headshots.  This is extremely powerful and effective against all enemies, but it won't always save you.  There will be times when you get overwhelmed or backed into a corner, but dying is rarely frustrating due to the generous number of save points and checkpoints throughout the game.  Not only are save points numerous, but you no longer need ink ribbons to save, even on hardcore difficulty.  Finally, the level design is such that it gives you the options and tools you need to deal with most situations.  If you are observant and quick on your feet, you will be able to use the environment to your advantage in a number of different ways.  I never played the original RE3, so I can't really compare it to that, but judging it as a sequel to RE2 Remake, I'm hard pressed to find anything negative to say about it.  The bottom line is this: If you loved RE2 Remake, but thought that maybe it could be a little more difficult and frantic, then I think you will love RE3.

I have never played the original RE3 so there is no question of petty nostalgia getting in the way of my playthrough but boy after the pleasant surprise that was RE2 I was expecting so much more from this one.

Simply put:

Story
the story is serviceable if not a bit generic but I never play an RE game for the story (except 7). The characters though are a bunch of hollow husks with very little personality or anything to get me invested in them. Kendo (the gun shop owner) has more character in the 1-minute cut-scene he appears than any of the other characters.

Gameplay
The controls are tight and responsive, and the moment to moment gameplay feels good. The zombies are amazingly well rendered and killing them is a blast.

Graphics
The graphics are great, each monster feels appropriately juicy when you shoot into them and the general appearance is quite stellar with plenty of environmental details

Sound
The sound is good, special mention to the ambiance in the hospital that kept me on edge throughout.

Game Design
Here is where it all comes tumbling down, the game design is horrendous. Here is a list of my largest gripes:
I regularly found myself just missing important items and notes throughout the game.
Regularly, new enemies would show up, with no clear explanation or introduction, creating a lack of tension and build-up, and no clear path to defending myself (after wasting nearly all my pistol ammo on those white zombies I had to shelve my pistol for the rest of the game due to lack of ammo, right after getting an upgrade)
Some monsters would do a special cut scene move and one-shot me even if I was at full health, and with no clear windup animation
Nemesis is a joke, gone is the tension of hearing the enemy coming or making tough decisions to keep from attracting their attention, this guy runs after you for 5 minutes and then you fight him during set-piece arena battles.....awesome...
Exploration becomes redundant (and useless) because Capcom reimplemented the cleared room color system they introduced in the RE2 remake - which tells the player if they have cleared the room of items directly in the map menu. 
Usually, in RE games, the environment loops on itself and grows as the player unlocks doors and explores the area. New enemies spawn in places you have visited previously to keep you on the edge of your seat. Instead, here you have 2 very small areas that can be explored and the most interesting one was in the free demo, everything else is a linear playthrough.

I am a veteran of the classic RE games, RE3 being my favorite one of the first three. When Capcom said they were remaking RE3, I wasn't sure what to expect. After all, RE3 is either loved or hated by the fans. As someone who loves it, I couldn't really think about how they were going to pull it off. Having beat R3Make multiple times on all difficulties, I can say that it's a good game, but it is also very different.

First off, I, like most of the fans, was disappointed to see some areas cut out of the game. The clock tower was my absolute favorite segment of classic RE3 and it's disappointing to see it not present here along with the park as well. The city segments feel pretty lackluster as well. It seems like mostly back alleys and less like in the big city. Other locales are pretty short lived, except for the hospital which I think was great and retained the survival horror aspect in a game that is mostly action.

Second, Nemesis is cool but he is not nearly as cool as his original appearance. I will say that the combat is light years better of course, and actually suits the play style of running/fighting with Nemesis more than the original. In the original, I often cheese Nemesis in Hard Mode to get all his drops. Fighting him head on is an exercise in frustration. In the remake, he is obviously still challenging but the mechanics work so much better that the fights are enjoyable. The dodge is pretty easy to master but it works great. The dodge in the original was so bad and often got you into MORE trouble, that is if you could time it perfectly in the first place. The Nemesis fights are the best part of the game, and radically improved over the original game.

However, gone are the randomized items and live events that I enjoyed as well and added much to the game's replay value, especially with speed running. This also kind of hurts the design a bit, because in the original you did backtrack a bit, but you were otherwise free to tackle getting the items to start the trolley anyway you wanted. In this game, it's a mostly linear progression the entire way. I feel like some of the things that happen in this game during cutscenes could have been turned into live events, which would have been much more entertaining and added tremendously to the replay value. The set pieces during these segments are pretty fun to watch though.

I was really disappointed in the puzzles in this game. In classic RE3, there are puzzles that require some trial and error or thought (the water puzzle comes to mind) while most of the progression is done with fetching items. The majority of "puzzles" in this game are finding item to use on another thing that half the time is in the next couple of rooms anyway. The railway puzzle seems like it will be complicated at first, but its easily defeated. The puzzles in the original were really interesting due to the randomization aspect where each puzzle could have different solutions, but that is not the case here. At its best, you're dodging drain deimos to trigger 4 switches to restore power and nuke a drain deimos hive. Otherwise, it's just find item, use it really soon.

Difficulty-wise, this game is much too easy. On Normal, I had a ton of healing items and ammo. I only died once. Nightmare however, the game gets a tremendous difficulty spike. Inferno is another league altogether. One hit deaths are common place, but ammo is still pretty much hand over fist. Speaking of ammo, the crafting system of the original game is essentially gone. I don't know what the point of acid rounds are, as I only found 2 Explosive B items in my first run, which didn't seem to do anything to Nemesis. Hunters are pretty easily ignored, otherwise they work wonders on them. 

In fact, flame rounds seem nearly useless too. I don't see a use of these rounds on any of the other enemy types besides Hunter Gammas or regular Hunters, and there are so few of these enemy types. Mine rounds are exceptional and perhaps too powerful on lower difficulties and damn near useless in Inferno. I would have preferred freeze rounds like the original. Explosive rounds seemed to be the most effective in that they actually stunned Nemesis and seemed to deal a good amount of damage, and were good at clearing mobs and destroying Hunters and just giving the overall needed breathing room that you'll be desperate for in Nightmare and Inferno. Magnum rounds are actually useful now and easily made, and of course makes for the best weapon, one shotting Hunters on lower difficulties and being the only weapon I think to bring down palehead zombies. You are thrown a lot of gunpowder As too. I did not run out of handgun ammo the entire game which was great, and shotgun ammo was found in droves, barring the harder difficulties of course. I basically had enough shotty ammo to last through the sewers with extras, and then I got even more after that.

The re-imagined characters are awesome! Jill is still a badass. As much as I enjoy the cheesy dialog in the original, the actual acting talent here is welcomed heavily. Carlos is still comedic but in his serious tones he is well delivered and much more likable. Tyrell is a new character and he also is very likable. Nikolai and Mikhail are well acted for the most part.

I haven't had the chance to play Resistance yet. I mainly focused on the single player experience as I enjoy it more. R3make is pretty damn good, but the lack of randomization, omission of live events and iconic areas, and worthwhile puzzles especially really hurt the replay value for me. Still, I had a lot of fun playing and would still recommend this to another RE fan, whether they like the original or not. Hell, going through Inferno is a testament in itself (Final Nemesis is just ridiculous!)

Get it in sale and I promise you'll not regret it

I never played any of the original Resident Evil games, and have only played the remakes, so I have no idea how this game compares to the original. All I can do is judge this game on its merits, and on that, it falls far flat. 

The game is just as fun as Resident Evil 2, except a bit more focused on action and less on puzzles and survival. Instead of the large sprawling areas like in Resident Evil 2 (Police Station, Sewers, NEST), the game is much more linear - you explore much smaller areas, and pass from one area to the next with no way to return to the previous area. Resident Evil 2 was a survival horror puzzle game, with some bits of action sprinkled throughout. This game is the opposite, it is more of an action game, with a bits of exploration and survival sprinkled throughout. There are very few puzzles in this game - I *just* finished the game as I'm writing this, and I can only remember one puzzle, although I'm sure there are more. That's not to say it's not fun, as the action segments and boss fights were really well done. It's definitely a fun game, and worth your *time* (but not your money).

The problem is, that I paid $60, and did not get $60 worth of enjoyment out of the game. I don't see how Capcom can justify charging $60 for this title.  Having played Resident Evil 2, this game pales massively in comparison in terms of content. It took me only 5 hours in-game time (7 hours real time, considering deaths and restarts etc) to beat the game. By comparison, Resident Evil 2 took me about 8 hours just to finish one of the 2 campaigns, and then the second campaign took me another 6 hours or so (playing on Hardcore). Then, in addition to the 2 campaigns, Resident Evil 2 had bonus modes where you could play as new characters in challenge scenarios. Resident Evil 3 has none of this.  Instead, they package some multiplayer mode called Resident Evil Resistance. This multiplayer mode might be fun, for all I know. Maybe it's a blast! But I just don't care, I'm not interested in multiplayer, I don't come to Resident Evil for multiplayer. I come to Resident Evil for survival horror, low on ammo, struggling to survive action games. Not for multiplayer games. 

The game is essentially a DLC Third Campaign for Resident Evil 2. There is nothing about this game that makes it a "sequel" to Resident Evil 2 - aside from the level design differences, it is exactly the same game.  A lot of the textures and enemies look exactly the same, and even some of the same characters are re-used. Even some of the same areas from Resident Evil 2 are re-visited. It should have been sold as a $30 add-on for Resident Evil 2. I imagine that if this game weren't a remake of an older game, and this amount of content was sold for $60 today, it would be getting absolutely shredded by reviewers.

For the record, I originally beat this game on the Xbox One X and it took me roughly three hours. I picked this up on a Steam sale to complete my Resident Evil collection. With that out of the way, the linearity of this game is honestly insulting to the player after completing RE2. The game itself isn't horrible by any means, but certainly not worthy of holding the same moniker as the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. 

Nemesis being scripted isn't my biggest gripe with the game, and this is because the original Nemesis was also a scripted monster. However, where this does become an issue is knowing this game is following in the heels of the Resident Evil 2 remake, and that game managed to make a scripted enemy far less noticeable. Nemesis, in comparison, the seams of his AI are showing, and it ain't pretty.

Honestly, this game is a step in the wrong direction after both titles released before this, and this is partly due to the length of this game. Listen, Resident Evil games are not long games, they're simply a giant puzzle that slowly unravels itself and you get more efficient with every playthrough. I'm not saying Resident Evil 2 remake is a long game as those four campaigns are essentially identical to one another, but this game doesn't even try to make light of its breezy pace. 

For those who are interested in one playthrough, which many gamers who aren't hardcore Resident Evil fans are likely to do, then the value will diminish quickly. This is because those who don't want to try the harder difficulties will be treated to an end-game experience of either nothing or the highly-ridiculed Resident Evil Resistance multiplayer mode after finishing the game. This is a massive step back from the original Mercenaries mode that complemented the end-game experience in the original before transforming it into what we know it as today. Resistance, on the other hand, was nearly dead-on-arrival, and is now best left untouched.

However, this story was not only short enough to beat in one decent sitting, but also lacks the innovative qualities that other Resident Evil games portray through their puzzles with what I can only describe as a lazy effort. Also, from the perspective from somebody who enjoys replaying through Resident Evil games on a consistent basis, this game holds little to no replay value to me. In fact, each subsequent playthrough seems to result in my interest being deteriorated further.  This doesn't seem to be an uncommon thought shared among various Resident Evil fans. 

 It's worth noting that this game is surely to sit well with a select group of Resident Evil fans, namely due to its emphasis on action. Although the original RE3 was considered action-packed when compared to its predecessors, this one is just ridiculous as they even have you fend off hordes for an extended period of time. This Mercenaries style mini-game has no place in the main story, but alas, it's here and it's silly. I really want to like this game, I tried very hard to enjoy it, but ultimately, Capcom had dollar signs in its sights with this release. I have high hopes for Resident Evil Village so at this rate, maybe just wait for that game?

Heck, if you want to play this game, I say you should. I don't think mine or any Steam review should really stop you from enjoying something that you're interested in, the only exception is that I recommend you get it on sale and not buy it at its original asking price of $60.

Spoiler-Free Opinions;

I would like to start by pointing out these are only one persons opinions, nothing more. I am not a longtime player of Resident Evil, I am not a reference in the genre. I did not grow up playing much console games. Thus, was never really introduced to the Resident Evil franchise. My first experience was pretty much the first movie with Mila Jovovich in theaters.. no wait! not WITH Mila in the theaters... (not that that would have bothered me at all... you know what I mean! ). So, I had never played a Resident Evil game before the Resident Evil 2 remake/re-imagining, that I really loved. This has led me down this rabbit hole of simply being curious about the story, lore and playing every game in the series.

After finishing RE2 Remake, I decided to postpone RE3 Remake to go play the RE1 HD Remaster, which I seriously enjoyed. I am now looking into getting the Original RE1/2/3 for Playstation as I also recently decided to get a PSOne and CRT TV for the full experience. Waiting to find the Original 1-3 games for PS1 at a decent price, I decided I'd go ahead and continue the series on PC.

While I have not yet completed my first run in this RE3, I decided I'd share my opinions with you, maybe a potential buyer/player; I've seen enough of it that I feel pretty confident with my opinions. So here goes... enjoy!

To start, I would just like to say, this is in no way a comparison. Whether the original is better or not is not the point here. I'm taking this game, for what this game is, simple as that... and I seriously wish more games would have the level of detail, polish and organic feel this game has. From the slow pace, eerie lighting and sound design, this is really among the best I've ever seen.

A game can easily be dissected into different scores and then given a total impression... but, for myself this always means nothing. I like to spend time with it and see how it feels, how it relates or what I get from it. With RE3 Remake (I'll call it RE3 from now on) I get the suspense from the dramatic contrast in lighting, the incredible play with shadows and the very subtle play with sounds. The graphics are also great, but I feel graphics just compliment everything else and help create such an immersive environment.

I feel like I am halfway between a video game and a next gen animation movie, I feel completely immersed and totally absorbed into it. The way the characters speak and comment on small details here and there, their movement -during play and cutscenes- is absolutely top of the line.

I did have some adaptation time to adjust to the fact enemies are often bullet-sponges, something I generally stay away from. In my mind, I favor realism over fiction (a bullet to the head should drop anything/anyone).. but I appreciate WHY it is the way it is. If they reduced the amount of bullets to kill, they would have to ramp up the zombie count to compensate... effectively changing the atmosphere and slower pace drama Resident Evil is known for. With this fact in mind, I've come to appreciate why things are the way they are.

One minor detail I truly appreciate is how well kitted out the characters actually are. I love seeing all the pouches and detailed clothing gear everyone has. It's a detail that proves to me the devs we're really perfectionists and cared about what they were doing. Something that I really appreciate, especially with the amount of games that come out botched, rushed and broken with so much skimped on or later added as "dlc". Here, you pay for a full package, and you get a full package.

I've noticed a few comments here and there about the music and sound not being as strong as in the original; I can't comment on the original, as I am still in the process of acquiring it. As for this version of RE3, I find the sound design subtle. It's there when it matters and it doesn't distract when it shouldn't. There was an incredible balance that was put in to avoid cheap scares or to avoid being overwhelmed with sounds and to keep the atmosphere visually suspensful. It works perfectly for my taste.

The movement aspect and the way the bodies animate (walking, turning, strafing, running, pain, etc..) is really top notch. I haven't noticed any area where there is any glitching, or sudden moves that appear unnatural. This all just helps every aspect of this game blend in and create what I feel is an extremely organic feel. It feels like it should feel. That being said, a few Nemesis moments are slightly over-the-top... but can you really complain about "over-the-top" while playing "Resident Evil"? 

All in all, when you take every aspect of the game and how well they blend together, this feels like a work of passion from the devs. Their care and attention really shows and I honestly wish so many more games could come with the same level of care and passion. This game, along RE2 remake are seriously some of my favorite games to have come out in recent times and in my entire time of gaming for that matter. 

This makes me incredibly anxious for the next Resident Evil 8 game.... until then, I have all the others to play. I haven't been excited about a game or series of games in a very long time. Actually, since Mass Effect 1 to 3. 

My only regret is having put these games off for such a long time!

Happy gaming everyone.

Resident Evil 3 is a remake of the game that was originally released in 1999, where the tank controls and fixed camera angles have been replaced with a modern control scheme and a third person camera perspective. 

I never played the original version, so my review will judge this like a new game, rather than comparing it to the old one. I’ve played most of the other Resident Evil games though (this is my 10th RE game) and speaking as a fan of the franchise, I mostly enjoyed RE3.

[h1]The Good[/h1]

•	The main playable character is Jill Valentine, but you’ll also control Carlos Oliveira during a couple of missions.

•	Weapons include knife, pistol, shotgun, grenade launcher (which has four different types of ammo), assault rifle and magnum, as well as throwable grenades and flashbangs.

•	There are a few different enemies including zombies, dogs, hunters, a strange lizard monster, and then there’s the Nemesis who shows up at various times for some tough boss fights.

•	Ammo and healing supplies are limited, so you need to manage your resources carefully. The level design is quite linear with not much opportunity to just run past enemies, so its important to have good aim to not waste bullets. There was one boss fight near the end of the game that I won with my last shotgun shell.

•	There are a couple of basic puzzles to solve to find extra items or weapon upgrades. You can use gunpowder and explosives to craft different ammo types, which was especially useful for me because I didn’t actually find the magnum during my playthrough, so instead of giving me ammo that I couldn’t use, I was able to craft ammo for the guns I did have.

•	Story is on the same quality level as most RE games (in other words, “fine”), but the cutscenes are exciting and voice acting for Jill and Carlos is great.

•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.

•	Graphics look fantastic. I didn’t encounter any bugs or crashes and I had a perfectly smooth framerate throughout.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]

•	It took me just over 7 hours to complete, which isn’t good value for the £50 price. Lots of other reviews have mentioned that some content from the original version has been cut out of this remake, which is a shame because if they’d included everything I think it could have solved the biggest complaint.

•	Okay, the £50 also includes the Resistance multiplayer mode, but I’ve watched gameplay footage on youtube and it looks really bad. There’s no way I’d consider playing it instead of my preferred multiplayer games, so that doesn’t add any value for me.

[h1]The Recommendation[/h1]

This is not a direct remake of RE3, there are several story beats and missing characters/enemies that were present in the original and I'm cool with that. RE3 for PSX was the first survival horror game that I forced myself to complete. 

I was a young teen and followed a GameFAQs guide all the way through because things like health item conservation, inventory management, and the dreaded ribbon based limited save system terrified me almost more than the zombies and random jump scares. I'm glad I did make my way through that game because survival horror soon became one of my favorite genres and the original RE3 will always hold a special place in my heart as a result.

That being said, I really don't understand all the hate people have been giving this game. RE2 Remake was a masterpiece, but it also changed several characters and story beats, some of which I disagreed with far more than what we saw in this game, yet it was pretty much universally praised.  RE3 Remake follows suit and cut out a lot of content present in the original, but at the same time, to me it had the same overall feel and all of the important story points were hit. I didn't really need a big fight with the graveyard worm or all of the back and forthing through a tiny alley picking up the battery, oil, cable, etc for the train car, those were just fluff to begin with. I did however like the homage to the jewel puzzle at the top of the subway area.

Also, to everyone complaining about reused assets from RE2, did you hit your head or something? RE3 did the same thing because they're supposed to be happening at about the same time canonically and both groups went to the RPD for STARS related business.

I do think a few mechanics fell flat. 

For one, they took away the actual usable knife from RE2 Remake and left us with the usual infinite durability pointy metal stick of uselessness in it's place, which was rather disappointing. 

They turned the grenade launcher into a joke for boss fights. It was basically knockdown tool that is useless for actually damaging Nemesis. Seriously I tested it out using an infinite ammo trainer and it took almost 70 explosive shells to take down clock tower Neme because you could only get in one shot when he fell to the ground because it would knock him back on his feet and I suspect he had a lot of iframes that contributed to wasted ammo. By contrast I could usually two or three cycle him with sufficient shotgun shells. 

Coins and infinite weapons not affecting rankings breaks the game. The original game had the infinite weapons unlocks, but would affect your ranking if you actually used them. So you could have some fun with them, but you wouldn't get a top ranking which actually meant something at the time. Now you can just cheese your way to full S ranks without breaking a sweat even on Inferno. And seriously, automatic health regen in a RES-E game? I could understand maybe MAYBE taking you out of Danger into caution, but full heal? Might as well say you've got a zombie proof vest on if you have both defense and health regen coins in your inventory. Still, they're "optional" unlocks so you don't have to use them, but then I also don't have to use any of the guns to beat the game either...so are they "optional" as well? but I digress.

Overall I think this is a great game and remake done right. They cut out a lot of the story/puzzle/backtracking bits to focus more on action and a better sense of momentum moving forward which I think works if you can separate your nostalgia for the original from this new experience. Also, the final battle against transformed slug Nemesis was probably the most epic I've had in a long time. Sure it's still just pushing in a bunch of batteries, but the scale and the overall look and just all it's parts moving in concert was quite amazing. Though the over emphasis on dodging, especially at higher difficulties was a bit much considering how long her could chain attacks and how quickly he could move to a new pattern making rather frustrating to get a couple shots off, even when using bullet time if you're not using the coins to help survive being wombo'd.

Highly recommend if you're a fan of the series or looking for a good action survival horror game.

Some people complain about the length of the campaign. I finished it in around 8 hours - playing RE:3 sign-unseen, but speedrunners can do it under 2 hours apparently, so your mileage may vary.

My only complaints in this game stem from the level design. Resident Evil games generally lends itself to puzzle solving and key-opens-door "mansion adventure" puzzles in a tightly designed map where everything is connected. RE:3 breaks from this mould and uses RE engine to provide a more disjointed, run-and-gun kind of game - resulting in the possibility of missing items along the way and giving you no chance to go back to find them. The puzzles are not particularly strong either, leading me to think that they've dumbed the game down a bit further to appease casual players.
Nemesis doesn't have the same dread that the Tyrant from RE:2 had either. I enjoyed the fact that Tyrant roamed the map in RE:2 - providing that horror element. I know some players complained about that part of the game, but personally I liked it. Nemesis by comparison is just grotesque and seems to show up unannounced - requiring newly introduced quickmoves to dodge, and I don't think it really worked as well in this game. 

In any case, high difficulty levels are still there and repeated play and planning will unlock more achievements for the hardcore players, looking to get the most out of the game.

What RE:3 lacks in bonus material (the different character playthroughs for one, and the speedrun bonus levels another), it includes a strange "Resistance" mode which you can install separately. This contains a random map, online game where the core gameplay elements of Resident Evil 3 are on display for endless replayability.

Still a great package though, and a bit of a mix-up from RE:2 to keep it from being stale. 
Still I prefer RE:2 to this entry though, and I know the campaign length is going to bother many Resident Evil players who have become used to 20+ hour campaigns in the other instalments of the franchise.

[h1]Better than the original[/h1]
I've played pretty much every RE game except the Outbreak games extensively, and I played the original RE3 a week before the remake came out. For me, the remake [i]replaces[/i] the original, which isn't how I felt about the fantastic RE2 remake, but people who really love the original won't like the remake.

Instead of being a 1 to 1 remake of RE3, they changed things to make the story and flow of the game a lot better than the original. This upsets a lot of people who wanted a more faithful remake, but I've always felt the original RE3 is significantly worse than RE1, RE2, or Code Veronica.
[b]What's Changed? (Story Spoilers)[/b]
Some areas are cut from the latter 1/3 of the original. The clock tower and the park sections are gone. The original's final area, the lab/water treatment plant, is also different.
In their place, the remake expands on the hospital vs the original, and changes the final lab section to make it more believable within the rest of the game's story. Some story elements are also changed, but they're minor and IMO vastly improve the story and give it a more serious tone.
Jill gets more time to know who the mercenaries are, instead of only getting to know Carlos. Nemesis shows up much earlier, and doesn't kill/infect Brad. Jill never goes to the RPD, but Carlos does. The final lab area is underground and connected to the hospital. Everyone knows about the impending nuke headed for Raccoon City much earlier than in the original, and it's changed to a public emergency broadcast on TV and radio. In the original, you only hear about the nuke headed for Raccoon City because the lab/water treatment plant apparently has an alert system set up to warn about incoming nukes. I mean, that's hilarious, but the original RE3 in particular gets so silly it's more unintentional comedy than most of the other classic RE games.

[b]What's Changed? (Gameplay spoilers)[/b]
OK, here's where I do think the remake has a few flaws, but overall I'd still rather play this than the original any day. Overall changes:
There are less puzzles in the remake. This is mostly because the cut places from the original had most of the puzzles, but they also had the worst puzzles. It kinda sucks because I do like puzzles in my RE games, but the original's clock tower, park, hospital, and water treatment/lab puzzles are almost all bad compared to the other classic RE games. That said, they kept a lot of the cool natural-ish puzzles from the city section in the remake, and those were the best ones.
There are no "Live Scenario" choices like in the original. In the original, I'd say they get an A for effort and a D for execution, because most of the choices have a good or bad outcome for you, and it's really not clear which one is gonna be which. It would have been cool if we had some choices in the remake, but I'm satisfied with the removal of something poorly implemented.
A lot of the minor randomization in the city segments is gone. I don't think this is a big deal, but it is to some. I mainly mention this because the random elements in the original really just amount to what kind of enemies and how many enemies show up in a few areas. I don't view this as a big problem, because it's way too easy to savescum until you get no enemies in an area in the original.
You play as Carlos more. He gets 2 segments where you control him, and they're both a lot longer than his section with the hospital/clinic in the original. I think these segments also give him a much better story/character arc than in the original.
Nemesis doesn't randomly show up and chase you through some areas anymore, and he doesn't drop as much cool stuff. I think this is a letdown, but he still chases you for almost all of the downtown/city segments of the game, and in those parts, you can down him and collect some loot. Instead of dropping parts for new guns, he drops 2 parts for the starting handgun, and 2 boxes with ammo inside. That's obviously way down from all the stuff you can get by beating him every single time in the original, and definitely disappointing.
The biggest letdown for me is no Mercenaries game mode. I always felt that was a great addition to the original, and I wish they'd included it in the remake.
There are tons of unlockables once you finish the game. I think this is great and it's why I've spent the time I have on this game. Unlockables range from RE7 style passive bonus items that take up inventory slots, weapons (some with infinite ammo), and some other upgrades like extra inventory or early access to a couple key items that open some locked areas. You get these unlocks by completing challenges in the game, and most of these challenges are tied to achievements. I liked this. That said, it looks like Capcom's now selling DLC to unlock everything if you really want to skip playing it or just feel like you're struggling to beat Nightmare or Inferno difficulties. And that reminds me.
The game has more difficulties than RE2 remake's Assisted, Standard, and Hardcore. Beating Hardcore unlocks Nightmare, and beating Nightmare unlocks Inferno. What I really like about this is Nightmare and Inferno have item locations shuffled like Madhouse difficulty in RE7. It won't really change the overall flow of the game, but you get some weapons earlier in some difficulties, and some key items are hidden in new locations, etc. so it's not just Hardcore but the enemies do more damage and have more health.
Jill's action dodging is a lot easier to learn than it is in the original RE3, I'd say. I feel like the original's attempts to add more action to classic RE kinda flopped because they aren't really well explained, but I know if you can master them, it feels great to dodge your way through zombie hordes or prevent Nemesis from ever hitting you. Remake is as satisfying, but I think it's easier to learn. I'll explain, because it's not like this review isn't way too long already!
Dodging in original RE3: You need to be aiming and press a button and a direction at the right time. I honest to god can't remember what button it is, mostly because the original RE3's in-game explanation says "you can dodge by pressing buttons."
Dodging in RE3 remake: You need to press the dodge button plus a direction. If you hit the aim button right after a perfect dodge, Jill auto-aims at the enemy's weak spot and you get a little bit of bullet time to hit them, or she does a high damage slash with her knife if you have that equipped.
Basically, they took out the "you need to be aiming" part in the remake, and it makes dodging feel more intuitive. You can still totally screw up dodging if you pick a bad direction, but that's just needing to be aware of the environment (don't dodge in the direction of something in the way).

After Resident Evil 2's remake, I'd say most of us were pretty excited to see Resident Evil 3 get the same treatment. If you've researched this games development at all, you'd know it was worked on by a dev-team much lower on the Capcom totem pole and they had only a fraction of the time the Resident Evil 2 developers got. Thus we have a remake that really isn't even a remake at all. It cuts a ton of the original game out unceremoniously and it feels more like a dlc for the last remake than a new game on its own.

And of course, they charged full price for this, when they knew it wasn't worth the same as the previous game.

To start off with the big issue, the length. My first ever play-through of this game on launch completely blind, took me less than four hours. The previous game was twice that length, not to mention the two characters/A&B paths which added tons of extra hours to the game. Instead, there's no different character play-through's and the game expects you to play through the one campaign on repeat to earn credits for the in-game shop. I mean, this is fine? But its nowhere near as satisfying or varied as before.

Just to give you an idea of how shallow the game actually is now, I'll tell you this. I'm not a speed-runner at all, but by rushing the game I'm consistently able to beat the game in about an hour on standard difficulty, with no glitches. That's actually embarrassing.

Now granted, on a technical level, the game is still really impressive. The RE engine is a knockout. The new character models and environments look amazing, but what's the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ point if the game itself lacks all heart and soul. The clock tower segment, probably the most iconic part of the original game is gone, only being cheekily hinted at instead.

The nemesis himself is also completely messed up in this game. He is only in his prime form, I.E his original iconic look for the first third of the game, after that he just looks like any other bio-weapon.

There's plenty more to say, but in the end if you've played it at all you'd already know, its incredibly disappointing. The fact that Capcom charged full price for this, is honestly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disgusting, because the total content on offer here is piss poor, and its a disrespect to the original title by sharing its name.

Although it's my favorite series, i waited for a good sale before getting REmake 3. Why? Because obviously its a short game and i wasnt gonna pay that amount of money for a 5-6 hours game even if its an RE entry. And let's be real, its the same game made with the new RE Engine.
