After a quality remake of Resident Evil 2, Capcom brought us a re-imagining of the Last Escape so I pre-ordered it, expecting the same quality. However, where RE2re shined with heightened horror and dark corridors, RE3re falls flat and without any tension. What happened?

Where RE2re was great at, was the atmosphere and tension building. While RE3 was more action oriented, there were many factors which made it different and still build the tension - random items, random encounters with Nemesis, different dialogue depending on where you went next and choices which made progress slightly different. All of this has been cut from the remake. Instead, we begin in Jill´s apartment in 1st person which I thought was a cool aspect but this gets ruined by Nemesis literally stomping in within 5 minutes. You get no time or chance to do much before you are forced into a scripted sequence of running away from him. In the original, Nemesis appeared first time at the station about 30mins in.

I´ve thought this might improve, but unfortunately, it just didn´t. The pacing of the game is way off and I had trouble playing through first two hours and feel interested. It felt forced and the fact that Nemesis appears in set points now, the element of surprise is completely gone and he becomes a nuisance instead. While you could always outrun the original Nemesis, the fact you had no idea if he will be there once you enter an area added a lot of pressure to your exploration. In remake, you can slowly walk through a burning building and not be afraid he will jump you.

Another problem is the absence of almost all the puzzles except making the tram, I mean, metro, operational. Other than that, the gem puzzle now only yields extra items which are not necessary to collect. Also, the horror elements are greatly diminished and Carlos gets the best parts, essentially. This brings us to another problem - length, or lack of it, and cut areas. It is a shame that the Clock Tower is now only a back drop for a boss fight and city is smaller. The original music makes a return, however, I found it didn´t play enough throughout the game. The Nemesis boss fights are all scripted and boringly predictable. The last two are basically mere copies of each other with only minor differences.

Overall, while the graphics are great and I liked the new Jill, Carlos and the rest of the characters, the whole experience felt like a let down, in comparison to the almost perfect rendition of RE2re (except the B scenarios). First part of the game feels way too rushed and when things slow down with Carlos, it´s getting back on track. However, Jill gets the short end of the stick even in the second half and I did not find her parts as enjoyable. I can only hope that RE8 and RE4 remake will not suffer the same as this remake. It gets 6/10 due to the high price and the play time is really low, so get this on a sale if you are a Resi fan.

I went into this game expecting an experience similar to RE2 but much more expanded and polished in the rough areas of its predecessor. The problems came with the game's pacing. The campaign is overall satisfying but lacks variety (even with the swaps with Carlos).
Besides the cut content arguments, which are absolutely valid when you factor in how long the original was and, for example, how long RE4 was. Capcom had the huge opportunity to forgo areas of the original for larger and more consistent additions. Level design could've also been improved a lot and we see a bit of it in the initial area where you can drop down a ladder to make backtracking much faster and safer but such opportunities are simply not present anywhere else in the game.
The new enemies are cool looking and it's nice to see some returning ones like the Pale Heads from RE2R but others don't make much sense or are simply frustrating, especially on higher difficulties, like the Tentacle Headed Zombies which have the absolute hugest range I've ever seen, are impossible to dodge without landing a perfect dodge and can hit you even while being knocked on the ground in a stun state since the tentacle head and the zombie body are handled as two separate entities.
There have been some areas expanded as the Umbrella Labs and Hospital but overall they add next to nothing in terms of story-telling and don't justify sacrificing having Jill at least visit the police station or playing as Carlos and Tyrell handling their Umbrella tasks on the side while Jill could've been exploring other parts of the city.

Next is Nemesis which was conveniently removed from the title.
Makes sense since he's absolutely underwhelming, especially after he changes from his 1st form. People who played the original felt a sense of dread while exploring since they didn't know that Nemesis's appearances were scripted but here, because he appears in so few set pieces, it's just so disgustingly noticeable.
Basically, Nemesis is a threat and chases you only for a very minor part of the game: in the starting area after restarting the generators in the power plant. That's about it. He doesn't chase you in the sewers, in the Hospital or in the Umbrella Labs. Just the starting area in the short while you are forced to go back to the Railway Company to fix the tracks to the station for the train (which is also one of the very few puzzles in the game), back while you run to the station and right after you're done with the Kendo set piece (which is indeed pretty good, given how his character had already been expanded in RE2R).
That's it. After that you'll barely see him again, until he triggers two gimmicky boss fights with doggie Nemesis and the final fight against corroded Nemesis.

Gameplay-wise the game is pretty good. The combat system is the solid one we've already seen in RE2R with the addition for a dodge roll for Jill and a stun punch for Carlos that if done with the correct timing will give players bullet time and auto aim them on the weak spots of the enemy they dodged\stunned.
Again, if you're good this system completely trivializes fights since you'll be able to dodge through everything and to balance it out the Inferno difficulty (unlockable after beating the game on Nightmare) has zombies doing Triple lounges at you from 5m away, completely fills entire areas to the point that they're barely navigable without spamming perfect dodges and in certain setpieces has literally zombies falling out of the sky for no coherent reason other than providing more obstacles for the player in an attempt to surprise\ambush them.
Also, I have my personal gripes with how the critical shots are handled being so disgustingly rare even with a fully upgraded handgun and how inconsistent sometimes handguns feel with zombies usually dropping down in 4-5 bullets to the head but sometimes soaking 7-9 bullets to the head for no apparent reason.
Also, it's absolutely insane that you can get S Ranks in all the difficulties while using Item Shop items which range from a buff to the dodge\stun that makes it easier to land perfect ones all the way to passive auto-healing items and the infinite rocket launcher who utterly trivializes basically the entire game. It doesn't matter if ammo is reduced and zombies are increased in the higher difficulties if I can infinitely nuke them and 2-3 shot regular Nemesis while he tries to chase after me the few times he actually can.

Factor in that there's been also a decrease in the content in the game itself. At launch the game has no other mode besides repeating the same main campaign over and over at higher difficulties and some of the unlockables have gotten severe downgrades. A notable one are the 3d models you unlock by getting achievements: in RE2R the models are all animated showing different kinds of walking cycles or attacks of the characters\monsters and even the weapons; in R3R all the unlocked models are static, completely lacking animation with the exception of the parts influenced by the game physics engine (ie: dangling clothes, garments, and the likes) and there are no 3d models of the weapons either.

The music is overall better than RE2R and nothing can be said about it.

Last but not least, the cherry on top: the price.

This game isn't worth 60$, period! At best it's worth 25$-30$ for what it offers...so, why aren't the people outraged? Simply, they bundled with a poor man's version of Dead by Daylight in Capcom's latest attempt to produce a game that could be one of those "games as service" you see around a lot.

So, BONUS! ! ! I'm gonna talk also about Project Resistance!

The game came out with a bunch of anonymous characters nobody really cares about. Their description in-game are atrocious like "edgy girl who somehow while looking so young is like a super journalist who can find any information for the right price but also somehow got abducted by Umbrella", they're also very stereotypical but cartoonishly stereotypical unlike the characters from the Outbreak games who felt much more interesting and grounded: they were bartenders, policemen, journalists and mechanics that simply got caught in the Raccoon City incident and fought to find a way out.

Here the situation is similar but also far less interesting, the characters (Cowgirl, Big Man Tyrone, Nerd kid, etc.) are all abducted by Umbrella and involved in some experiments...that's it. They can't really escape or rather they have no storyline or endings like the Outbreak characters, they aren't involved in the RC incident at all but are instead involved in these experiments in these sterile looking and cramped environments where the Mastermind plays their deck of cards spawning zombies and traps left and right and occasionally the big boss they can temporarily use (though the controls of zombies and bosses are absolutely clunky to an outrageous degree). Also, the players will always perform the same 3 tasks with no variation whatsoever.

Again, in Outbreak you could all independently explore maps rich of lore information, setpieces, iconic monsters and boss fights all leading to different endings for each character and couple of specific characters depending on the actions during the last level.

Also, in Resistance the low number of characters, given how the gameplay pans out, forces players into using certain ones. For example, the girl with medical skills is always absolutely necessary while other characters are completely forgotten most of the time simply and rightfully because their skills are too weak or too situational.

Finally: the game came out with lootboxes. After each match you get a small amount of RP based on your performance and with those you can unlock, you guessed it: cosmetics for the survivors and skill upgrades for the Masterminds which come out of a randomized lootbox. 

But, hey! You can shorten the grind by buying boosters. Imagine my shock!

I think that the difficulties do actually make replaying the game super fun for different reasons than speedrunning Resident Evil 2 Remake (I do it very casually compared to the pros, but my Leon A time was around 1 hour 7 minutes so I'm no slouch). I don't even think I can go back to playing RE2make without the dodge mechanic, and I loved that game dearly before RE3make came out.

There is one big stinker in all of this though. There are no stipulations for achieving S rank (S rank is now the highest achievable rank in all difficulties) on inferno mode. In RE2make you weren't allowed to use the infinite ammo weapons to achieve S+ mode. Now in RE3make you can use the infinite ammo weapons along with any of the other 'shop' items, that can quickly turn the difficulty of your campaign down several notches, to achieve S rank. This really hurts because you could do a 'no shop item' run, which is super impressive, and if it's slower than your meme-y rocket launcher run it won't find a spot on your results screen. There's no reward for that level of challenging yourself either. This is a very disappointing change in my opinion. 

They streamlined puzzles too. The RPD section with Carlos has the west office safe and the 2 lockers on the second and third floors respectively. These have the exact same codes as they did in RE2make so I clearly have some bias here as I knew the codes without ever having to try and figure them out organically although from what I can tell it might be even more simple than it was in RE2make. Other than the RPD section there are 2 safes in the game. 1 with Jill and 1 with Carlos. Jill's is '9 3 7' and Carlos's is '9 3'. I'm terrible at remembering codes so when I used to speedrun RE2make I would always have a cheat sheet pulled up on my separate monitor. I would never have to do something like that for RE3make because the codes are the same minus 1 number. Also, the RPD west office safe code is '9 15 7'. Jill's safe and the west office safe being so similar really rubs me the wrong way. I don't even know if I really consider the lab puzzle 'm h l' to even be a puzzle either.

Those were the things I thought the game did poorly, but this doesn't reflect my opinion of the game as a whole. Overall, I still think the game is worth playing despite the change to the ranking and puzzle systems from RE2make. The core gameplay is much more fun due to the heavy action theme they took. Pros.
Story is pretty similar to the original. There are noticeable differences, but overall, it's the same story I remember from the one I played as a kid. Graphics are nice without being a huge burden on the computer. Game play was ok. Not great, not terrible, just ok. Well made characters with facial expressions that fit the mood of the story. Not just the usual blinking eyes but full on facial expressions that look pretty realistic. You can see surprise, anger, relief, humor. Really nicely done. 

Cons.
Even though the story is similar, you can see A LOT of places where they cut things out. Not sure if it was to slim up the size of the game, or just to hurry it out the door and make money, but everything about it feels smaller and less engaging than the original. A lot of puzzles were cut out or reduced to go find this key which is pretty much in the room next door and come back and unlock this door. Early game seems to have a lot of back and forth and then nothing but a straight line. I miss the choices you could make when you encounter Nemesis. Depending on how you chose, you could drop him with background traps instead of having to face him every time. Which brings me to the next con. In the original, you only faced Nemesis a few times, and each time you would be given a choice in how to handle the encounter which could result in Nemesis being defeated for the time being and it was practically a guarantee that it would be a long while before you saw him again. This game cut content, cut out weapons, cut puzzles, only to push Nemesis on you every freaking step of the back and forth journey through this game. Add onto that the drastically reduced amount of ammo and gun powder you find, and it gets annoying really quickly. It just seems like it was a lazy attempt at a cash grab. If you are getting multiple achievements for completing the game in under 2 hours, and with the  slash to the types of weapons, gun powder, and puzzles that they cut out, it just seems to me like they just wanted to get this out the door as quickly and cheaply as possible, which is a shame, because the original was one of my all time favorite games. If you play this remake, and also play the RE2 remake, you can see a huge difference in the amount of effort that went into RE3. Where RE2 is recognizably a remake of the original with pretty much the same puzzles and the same layout as the original, and then you look at this game and understand how much was cut out, you can understand why I had trouble giving this a thumbs up. Yes it was fun. Was it as fun as it could have been if they had kept the same effort as the second remake? I don't think so. Yes, it had the same characters, and some of the story was recognizably RE3. Was the story as good with some of this missing stuff gone? I don't think so. Still, if you just treat it as its own game, and not think of it as a remake, then yeah it was ok. If you ask me if it's worth $60? No way. If you think about it, for the 2 hours of content you get, it should only be worth $20.

So after doing nearly everything possible in the game, at 56.3 hrs on record as of today, here's my take on it:

Overall, this is a great game with fun mechanics, decent enough story, and naturally great graphics as well. That being said, if you are like me and coming from the high that was Resident Evil 2 Remake, this IS inferior to that remake. There aren't any branching pathways or different routes available to play, similar to Leon A/B and Claire A/B. It is a single route centered around Jill. The campaign itself is also fairly short in comparison to a single playthrough from Re2R. I explored and took my time taking in the environment and was able to squeeze out five hours. In Re2R, my first playthrough was 12 hours long. My biggest gripe with this remake is that Nemesis is restricted to scripted encounters which does dull down the pacing compared to Mr. X who was a constant threat. 

Keep in mind that this also takes a more action approach compared to the more methodical survival horror that was Re2R. There is plenty of ammunition and supplies given to you and considerably more enemies to plow through. A particular fun mechanic but again also contributes to this being more action-driven is a "perfect dodge". When done right, Jill can completely bypass an enemy's attack as well as locking onto a weak point in slow-mo.

As much as I want to say Capcom nailed it again, that would be doing their previous work, Re2R a disservice. This game IS fun but you definitely get the vibe that they cut out a lot in an effort to rush this out after their success with Re2R. Rather than $60, this would be more fairly priced at say $30-$40 price range. Hopefully they will take the community's feedback to heart and make up for it with their eventual Resident Evil 4 Remake.

Let me start by saying Resident Evil 3 is an awesome game. As someone who has never played the original, this was a blast from start to finish.
[h1]Story[/h1]
As I said, I'm new to the series, having only played Resident Evil 2 Remake and Resident Evil 5, the story is well... confusing. Don't get me wrong, it's interesting, just not very newcomer friendly. There are a couple of times where a character shows up and he's like "Hey, Jill! It's been a while, how are you?" and I'm just sitting there thinking "Who are you and why should I care about you...?"
However, there are tons of pickups like letters and newspapers to tell you more about the events that happened days prior, if reading is your cup of tea.
[h1]Graphics & Performance[/h1]
The game is beautiful and runs butter smooth. I especially love the lighting effect and all the reflections. The zombies look very scary with all their grotesque features. Jill herself looks awesome as well, you'll be able to see the blood, sweat and dirt on her body, as you take damage and progress through the story. You're in for a treat!
I did encounter some sort of weird flickering bug on some cars, it was like being at a rave party and it was very annoying, but nothing a simple restart couldn't fix.
The load times are very fast, especially if you're using a SDD, no problems there.
I also encountered one random hard crash out of no where, I have no idea what I did. Fortunately it never happened again.
[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
I played on hardcore difficulty, and let me tell it's no joke. The zombies are no pushovers, they'll take like 6 bullets to the head before they go down and even then, they'll sometimes come back up to bite you, so make sure they're really dead, dead. Ammo is scarce so don't go around wasting bullets! When playing as Jill that is. Carlos has an M4 with 300 bullets and plenty of ammo scattered around for his rifle, he might as well have unlimited ammo.
I had no issues with the controls or the camera at any point in the game.
I enjoyed everything the game had to offer, the survival horror is really on point here! except for that one part: ([spoiler]Where you play as Carlos and have to defend a door from incoming zombies, like literally 30-40 zombies. Horde mode style, it felt really out of place compared to the rest of the game.[/spoiler])
The boss fights were awesome! They're intense and will test your skills, some bosses have obvious weakpoints while others don't, or perhaps I'm just dumb. At one point, I was doing so badly, Jill had to break the fourth wall and be like: "Maybe if I use this one specific gun and fire ahead of him, it'll knock him off."
My biggest gripe with this game is it's length, I have 6.3 hours on record and I've already completed the game. I took my time looking for loot, checking out the scenery and everything else. For 60 euros, I expected more.
[h1]Overall[/h1]
A solid [b][i] 7/10 [/i][/b] from me! The game is great, very short, but great. If you're looking for a new zombie game or a survival horror game with fantastic graphics, this game is for you. Just don't expect a very long experience.

This game is not true to the original and it's very short. It has a lot of cut content.
We don't have the Restaurant, Press Office, City Hall, and especially Clock Tower or Raccoon City Park.

There are some major changes to the story, like RPD segment given to Carlos and Brad's death being reimagined (for worse imo). Jill witnessing his death by Nemesis was an iconic moment in the original and it's not present anymore.
Other minor changes that I dislike are: they changed the first encounter between Jill and Carlos, the subway section is at the beginning now, and they removed Barry from the game (he is the one who rescues Jill with the helicopter at the end of the original).

But the main problem with this game is that it doesn't feel like a classic RE game and more like RE6 most of the time, particularly in the second half. And it's actually pretty simple to understand why.

[u]LACK OF PUZZLES AND BACKTRACKING + SCRIPTED NEMESIS[/u]

The reason why the original was so great was because it had (like every classic RE) a crazy amounf of puzzles - in fact the best puzzle in the original for me was the music box puzzle in the Clock Tower, which is no longer present. And it also had many key items that you needed to get in order to unlock previous areas that were blocked when you first passed them. This was also true for RE1 and RE2, which essence were perfectly captured by their remakes.

The amount of puzzles and key items in the original meant a lot of backtracking and having to pass narrow alleys multiple times, facing zombies each time. Simple things like going back to Dario's warehouse later on to use the crank and get precious ammo or realizing that Dario actually left his shelter, leaving behind free gunpowder for you.

And the fact that you had to backtrack and at the same time run from a crazy stalker Nemesis made that game an amazing and satisfying adrenaline rush.
There is NO adrenaline and desperation element with this Nemesis, because you don't have to backtrack nearly as much (or at all), so you encounter him very few times. And I'm only talking about the first half of the game obviously. Because in the second half Nemesis just becomes a dog-looking scripted mess, similar to the Ustanak in Resident Evil 6.
This makes me almost shed a tear. Realizing that they butchered the VERY essence of the original game. In most sequences, you can close a door on Nemesis and if you immediately open it again, he is no longer there. It's downright disheartening to realize how scripted he becomes.
In the original, he could even appear in the restaurant OR the press office, depending on which location you visited first. Changing not only the fight completely, but also changing how you encountered Carlos for the first time (and if i remember correctly, even changing his dialogue with Jill).

[u]LINEAR PROGGRESSION[/u]

This critique has been given a million times, but I'd like to reinforce it.
Not only the game lacks backtracking and puzzles (in fact it has only ONE real puzzle: the vaccine puzzle in the last segment), it takes even a step further and completely blocks certain areas from being revisited via scripted events.

For example: once you enter the subway station after reactivating the subway system, JIll will roll down the metal shutter, making the city completely inaccessible and FORCING you to move to the subway, even if you forgot some items behind.
Not that it makes any difference in this game anyway, since there are no key items that you absolutely need to get to solve puzzles or unlock areas. But nonetheless it's a very clear way to force a linear path for the player, which goes ABSOLUTELY against the essence of the original (or any classic RE for that matter).

The area that feels most like Resident Evil is the hospital. Especially in the Intense or Nightmare difficulties. Tight corridors teeming with all sorts of real threats, TONS of backtracking and key items that need to be obtained in order to unlock rooms.
Funnily enough though, the worst part of the game is actually at the end of this hospital act, when there's (no joke) a HORDE gameplay where you need to hold your ground during a timer, spamming ammo and throwing grenades. This is SO Resident Evil 6 that I really question myself if Capcom actually learned their lesson.

[u]MAJOR LOST POTENTIAL[/u]

I also want to express my frustration about how this game feels like an insane wasted opportunity.
Let's take a moment here and realize that the 3rd game is the final act for the iconic Raccoon City trilogy and could be so much bigger and groundbreaking.
Granted, the original RE3 was designed at first to be a spin-off and had a very smaller team plus lower budget, thus resulting in a product that had a slightly smaller scope than the previous title (although, looking back, not as much as people usually say).
But this is precisely what gave Capcom the opportunity to surpass everyone's expectations for this game, making an epic final act for the trilogy. Like, cmon, this is THE game that takes place in the streets of Raccoon City. They could have made the city so big and scary to explore.
Rather, Capcom not only didn't expand Raccoon City, they made it linear and therefore it feels significantly smaller than the older version.

So, to sum it up:
The reason why this game fails as a remake is not only the cut content, but also (and mainly) the fact that its essence was lost.
IMO if Capcom wanted to have all this creative freedom, then they could just apply it to RE8 (RE7 was a great game btw) instead of butchering a classic one.

And, of course, let me not finish this review without mentioning:
- No Mercenaries mode. RE3 was single-handedly the game that made this type of minigame a staple in the series.
- No live action choices . Massively decreasing replayability.
- No Ink Ribbon. There are typewritters and chests EVERYWHERE (this is not an exaggeration).
- No Blue Herbs. Why blue herbs if they removed the spiders, right? They also removed crows. You can hear crow sounds in the game and they are even present in the concept arts, but removed from the game. Go figure.

You can also clearly see this game was rushed when you realize the zombies are basically the same as the previous game (same models) and a ton (A TON) of assets were reused from RE2R, and yet the game is much smaller and less ambitions. Shame.
This is not the first time Capcom puts a AAA price tag in a half-baked product. Cough Street Fighter 5 cough.

An absolutely amazing follow up to last year's RE2 remake.  The visuals and audio design are just as good, and the fleshing out of many characters from the 1999 original make this game feel like it has a lot more depth in it's narrative.  While some areas are missing from the original game, this game's pacing makes you forget about what is missing and focus on what is right in front of you. Having played the 1999 original and this version, I need to address the main complaint I've heard with this game.  The game is "short".  However, upon completing my first run, I noticed that my play time clocked in at just over 5 hours (the game doesn't count cutscenes in this). I find that people complaining about this is a bit odd, considering that my first playthrough of the 1999 release clocked in at just about the same time, and that was also without any guide and a good amount of exploration. Both games offer a similar run time, so I'm a little confused where the complaint that the remake is too short is grounded. Yes, the Mercenaries mode was removed, but Capcom seemingly replaced that with RE: Resistance. Buying custom weapons with infinite ammo after completing the game is still an option for those who want another playthrough too, and Capcom expanded on this with more items you can buy to aid in the number of increased difficulties you can play on. Where the original does take some time to slow things down for more classic RE exploration, the remake makes sure you constantly feel the stress of trying to run from everybody's favorite monster. Nemesis' return is fantastic.  He feels huge and even more intimidating than before.  He is the driving force behind the game's blistering pacing, and truly makes this game feel like Jill's last escape.  Both games offer an excellent story to cap off the Raccoon Trilogy and both deserve a playthrough today.

This is a great game. A beautiful remake. It has it's flaws, but Resident Evil 3 was intended to be more of a deeper look into one of the protagonists of the original game.  We catch up to Chris and Claire in Code: Veronica X.  We see a more fleshed out Leon in Resident Evil 4.

THIS IS JILL'S GAME.

As combat veteran myself, I could clearly see all the hallmarks of PTSD.  Recurring nightmares. Disassociation. Drug Abuse. Mood swings. Survivors guilt. Reckless behavior. Deeply suspicious of others intentions towards you...

Now for me, Jill is no longer just eye candy.  Most people won't like the changes made, but I loved them. Was never a fan of puzzles. Glad they cut most of those out. I loved them when I was nineteen and playing Nemesis for the first time on PS1... Now I see they cut away from the sense of urgency for Jill and Carlos to get the hell out of Raccoon City.  And speaking of Carlos, this guy is cool, confident and just reckless enough to earn Jill's respect. I love how they make going to the police station more than just fan service to Resident Evil 2. It makes sense that Carlos and Tyrell are given orders to find a scientist that may be holed up in the RCPD. I think their mission gives more credibility to the U.B.C.S., not just an excuse to shoehorn another character into the game.
I have to say I loved the emotion of this game.  The doomed city is tragic in every sense of the word and the incredible Resident Evil engine's ability to create emotion on the character's faces makes this game far more than the sum of it's parts. Little emotional outbursts that grab you like a fine piece of music... Jill's tear falling from her face just before she pulls the trigger in her nightmare at the beginning... the remorse on Marvin's face before Brad bites him... the awesome Sam Jackson moment from Tyrell... Ballsy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. lol the resolve in Jill's face when she tells Tyrell that Carlos isn't the only professional. Hell, even in Resident Evil 2's remake, Sherry kissing her mother on the cheek after she dies... that ♥♥♥♥ tugs at my heart every time I see it.

First and foremost, this isn't a remake.  It's a REIMAGINING.  After having played and beat this game many many times, there is nothing here that remotely resembles a 'remake' so much as it does a 're-telling' of the events of RE3.

That said, as an long time, OG Resident Evil fan since my childhood, I gotta say I'm disappointed with the amount of cut content and massively missed potential with the final game we got as opposed to the original game it was "remaking."  They cut entire levels, like chunks of the city, the clock tower, the park, the cemetary and the treatment facility in favor of expanding some levels like the hospital and, of course, the scripted Nemesis chase sequences.  Speaking of, the air of dread and tension are gone now considering that Nemesis no longer sporadic with his appearances and chases.  Now most of his sequences are heavily scripted and his boss fights are laughably easy compared to the original.  And lastly, the split second choices you could make in the original game during "dangerous" moments that could decide both your game route and ending are now GONE as well, leaving the game feeling hollow and routine with just ONE ending (sans the obvious bad ending, which is the only point in the game your given ANY choice at all).

It's so sad because as a 'reimagining' they could have went all in on telling a fresh new story with new and exciting in-game events and locations that could've fleshed out Raccoon City and the characters more than the original did.  Instead, Capcom took the easy way out AGAIN and opted to cut content to meet deadlines while cashing in on the success of the RE2 Remake (which was also inferior to its original counterpart).  Shame, too, because the gameplay itself is GREAT and is fun to play while harkening back to what made the originals great (aside from the lack of puzzles, but those aren't as dearly missed as much as the levels that were cut).

Tl;dr:  I still recommend this game, but probably when there's a sale because it IS rather short and sweet.  For anyone aside from longtime RE fans, I'd play the RE1 and RE2 Remakes before deciding if this game is worth your time.  7.5/10*

After being completely blown away by Resident Evil 2 Remake, I had super high expectations for this one when it was first announced. Unfortunately, the experience falls short. Quite short, in fact. It seems like the bigwigs at Capcom saw how wildly successful that Remake 2 became and wanted to push out a third entry as fast as possible to capitalize on that success…

You start out as Jill Valentine; a member of RPD’s Special Tactics and Rescue Service or S.T.A.R.S and a survivor of the Spencer Mansion incident of the first game. You are now desperately trying to escape Raccoon City which is infested by zombies after the Umbrella Corporation had unleashed the T-Virus upon the entire city. After a phone call from an old colleague, all hell breaks loose again…

I will say that the games presentation is very well done. The characters, visual and audio effects are top notch but not quite enough to carry the rest of the game. Those of you expecting to take a full-on trip down memory lane hoping to see various aspects of the original game remade will be disappointed as some areas such as the clock tower and park have been removed as well as appearances of a few enemies. It’s more of a re-imagining of RE3 than a true remake.

Gameplay wise, it leans towards more action and less horror and tension. Gunplay remains largely unchanged from Remake 2 and the new gameplay mechanic which is a dodge roll and when timed correctly, lets you avoid an enemy’s attacks without taking damage and gives you a follow up attack afterwards. Again, very action-y gameplay.
 
Puzzles and back tracking are absent as well as alternate pathways and alternate endings makes it very linear in its progression and while it makes a great game for speed running, it makes for a poor Resident Evil game overall. This game feels like it should have been a DLC for Remake 2 instead of a fully-fledged standalone entry.

I cannot really recommend this one if you are a RE fan. IF you feel the need to play it, get it on sale for a deep discount as it is not worth it at full asking price.

Contrary to all of the reviews, which are mostly positive, the game has a lot to offer. It it highly dependent on how you play, and I've spent quite a number of hours in this game since its release than Resident Evil REMAKE 2. Just like its original counterpart, Resident Evil 3 REMAKE is more action-oriented than its predecessor.

Jill is a remarkably beautiful character. Her attire is realistic, and attractive, she has an attitude to match. Carlos' redesign is spectacular, and his personality is very likable. The dialogues shared between Carlos and Jill are quality content, with depth to each of their characters.

The new Raccoon City is marvelous; stunning posters with subtle hints of the still extant life is remarkable, all while offering a sense of dread which makes for a truly enjoyable experience. The world is more enriched when compared to the previous REMAKE, with more areas to explore in the mess that is Raccoon City; the various sights of Easter Eggs and homages to Capcom's previous titles can be found if you look closely, and the sounds of agony, cries for help, and the numerous people scattering about the city really bring it all to life.

The dodge mechanic provides a much-needed gameplay addition to the intense situations the REMAKE throws at you. Time your dodge just right, and you're rewarded with a "bullet time" counter-attack able to dish out the damage, or buy yourself an escape.

The jump scares and the photo-realistic undead are underwhelming this time around, but that was to be expected with a more action-oriented focus. The story is underwhelming this time around with a majority of locations cut out from the original, and the real time selection options trimmed from the mechanics as well. For veterans like myself, this is a disappointment, especially since when compared with the Resident Evil 2 REMAKE whose campaign was more fleshed out. Those are, in my opinion the only setbacks to an already well done title!

I encourage you to play this game, newcomers or veterans! Personally, I opted to play in Hardcore difficulty, as ink ribbons are no longer an issue, and you can familiarize yourself with the locations rather quickly. If you're a fan of survival horror, check this out, and enjoy it!

Love-hate relationship with this game. It's outright impressive. I'm enjoying it, but I feel it's lacking and I'm neither a pro nor purist of anything gaming or otherwise. I'll keep it short and helpful here, but I want to ramble some about the cons, but the cons in this game are very scant, but also very specific. 

Please keep in mind, this is just a game review by some rando Steam kid. It's not written by a professional in a professional way and doesn't claim or intend to be.

PROS:

STORY: Rock solid retelling of the RE3 story, now through an up-close and terrifying over the shoulder perspective. The pacing of the story suits the urgency of escape. There's really never a dull moment or any point where it seems as if the story is dragging. At times, there's hardly a moment to breathe before being launched into the next boss battle or staggering into a new and dangerous enemy. Each segment seems carefully designed to flow from one point of interest to the next. The POV switch segments allow players to see both sides of the story with retold narrative clarity.

GAMEPLAY:
Newfound depth in character control and combat tactics. A step up from even RE6, which revamped the controls for combat to suit the games challenges very well. Here, we have the "Perfect Dodge" mechanic, born from the original RE3 dodge mechanic and put through a 20 year refining process that gives RE players an unseen level of mobility that can make Jill like greased lightning. At 20 hours in, I can at least use it well enough. It seems quite overwhelming for zombies and perhaps even the Nemesis. However, not as reliable against BOW hit boxes and recovery speed. It's less effective when you're hurting, mind that.

The gun play is more centered around a stationary firing mechanic, where standing still for a second lets players get a bead on a target, and moving will bloom the crosshair and sacrifice substantial accuracy. The over the shoulder camera can be controlled freely so there's rarely an issue of not being able to see what's going on. 

SIGHTS AND SOUNDS:
(Specs: CPU:i3-8100 3.6ghz RAM:32gb GPU: Zotac gaming RTX 2060)
It's a good looking game. Beautiful even, if grotesque monstrosities and a certain infuriating, treacherous Russian cockroach doesn't sway the bias on beauty. Voice overs and voice quality has been completely revamped to AAA quality from the PS1 original voices, of course. Zombie moans and creature groans raised the hairs on my neck and kept my camera vigilant. Bite marks appear on Jill's neck for a little while after taking damage. She can spatter herself in zombie viscera if a head shot makes a full statement as it lunges for her, she might even find herself having to catch the corpse and shrug it off. 

Bullet and knife wounds persist temporarily on zombies, and when head shots make a full statement, they do not provide a guiltless sense of satisfaction, even in all their ultra-violent spectacle. Not only do zombo heads bust open in a red splash of semi-solid confetti giblets, but there's this signifying white FLASH that accompanies the gun shot along with the splurting and sploshing of prize fluids. Rockin' zombie heads feels a little like shooting scary water balloons. BOW's are another story. So far, it seems the only recourse to dealing with BOW's "efficiently" is attention to detail and extreme prejudice.  

CONS:

STORY: 
Seems short. I know, I'm a general fan. Every Resident Evil is short and always has been short. They're all made to be able to speed run in just a few hours. 

Let me be less obtuse. 

I didn't think the demo was literally the beginning of the game. Feels like the "game" doesn't start until after we meet Carlos. Then, its like a "survival horror sprint." I was hoping there would be more sections of the city. Town Hall. The Clock Tower. The Park... I thought there might be optional fights like the giant worm in the park. I thought there might be a couple more paths like in the original RE3 that would change certain encounter points. The encounter with Nicholai in the cabin. Or the option to fight Nemesis, hide from him, or use the environment to quickly deal with him. The story doesn't take me in a direction where I feel like I'm trying to escape from a whole city block with a few ways around it. A lot less is involved with accomplishing tasks and old style RE puzzle solving sections are truncated if not riding in the back seat entirely. This pacing worked for RE:4, but that game was fundamentally different. It works for this one because of the redesign, but there are still a few missed opportunities depending upon how things are approached.  

GAMEPLAY:
Very minor nitpick...NEMESIS has too much screen time. I almost feel like all his screen time is why the game feels like a sprint even now that I've beaten it several times. And when he shows up, Jill doesn't pee her panties anymore. No black and white slo-mo screen with the heartbeat count down giving you several seconds to decide what to do before the monster is upon you and you don't have any choice but to fight it out, sacrificing your ammo and health for a worthwhile reward, should you survive. Nemesis is persistent, as he should be, but it feels like he's literally around every corner. There's hardly a solid 10 mins of puzzle solving or exploration before Nemesis is back on the scene. And not only back on the scene, but progressing the game forward in scripted boss fights that flow into cut scenes. 

For me, the intense and quiet moments in RE are just as important as the butt clench moments. There's a balance between quiet exploration and apprehensiveness and raw butt clench time that is best kept. There's very little buildup in RE3 Remake. It's just much much ballsier Jill's balls to the wall from the beginning to the end. This isn't all that scary. It's more of a mutant-zombie romp like Left 4 Dead, but that's not a bad thing. 
There's nothing wrong with mutant-zombie romps. 
I generally like them and I generally like this one.

NEMESIS: 
Easy to deal with. Kind of. I think his forms are overdone. I don't think he needed the Sahagin fishman form. His shirtless, battle worn form with the tentacle whips would have been much more dangerous. He's faster and it would be at least necessary to attempt to perfect dodge him.

JILL: 
Talks too much. But I guess I would be spicy and intolerant too if I were dealing with as much trauma with as many pills as she is. Her nightmares must have been filled with zombies, so its not like she hasn't seen BOW's and other such horrors every night since the Mansion incident. I can see why she doesn't fear or respect the Nemesis at all in the slightest, thought it does nothing to help immerse me as a player in any sense of fear or dread either.

It's really ok, but noticed. I'll call it character development. 

BONUS CONTENT: 
There is nothing of value here aside from the item shop. Nothing here will bring you back to the game aside from the item shop. All you get is a harder difficulty with random enemy spawn locations...If that's your idea of a reward, have at it. A difficulty mode is just a setting. There isn't a mercenaries mode like I had hoped for. You just get shop points for beating the game and doing certain things. Then you get items. If you want more to play, you can try Resident Evil RESISTANCE which I highly...Advise everyone to avoid. Forget that it came with your game. 
I've run the tutorials and that's as far as I'm willing to go. 
I'm not waiting for reviews. 
I think I saw a lootbox.

I guess that's it. 
Final verdict is a solid hell yeah. 
I recommend the game but... It still feels like there isn't enough here and I don't feel like I'm being too greedy in saying that.

The game is short and sweet, but do not let that deter you. That's part of what makes it sweet. Capcom masterfully makes you want to play this game over and over again, seeking to maximize different play styles on each go round. 

This game is certainly not without its flaws, but its more action oriented pace (in comparison to Resident Evil 2 Remake) is equal parts refreshing and addicting. While its action elements offer different and faster combat options, the game retains the same flavor the Resident Evil franchise is known for, that being maximizing your routes and efficiency. 

Circling back to the flaws, three things stick out. First being the boss battles with Nemesis. These are reminiscent of Zelda boss battles in the sense that the game has a rather clear and obvious way for you to proceed. Should you choose not to, you will waste endless amounts of ammunition. 

The second flaw of this game centers around the inconsistency of the CTEs and the overall lackluster implementation of them. In one sequence you may have to press a button to trigger an event, while in another it happens automatically. Some of the CTEs make sense, while others take away from the gravitas of the situation at hand. 

The third and final flaw, and its a small gripe when considering the overall experience, is the lack of paths for the player to chose. I only bring this up because it existed in the original and it would have been interesting to see this implemented to have an option of differing story elements or weapon acquisition based on player choice. 

RE3 is a flawed experience, but not one you should miss out on if you enjoy the series. Its refinement of pathing and min/maxing your runs is the true hook and its not one that should be missed. Oh and one last thing..... STARRRRRRSSSS

This game put me in an awkward situation, like it is a decent game, but also very, very disappointing, I want to trash it completely but I can't as it is still a decent game. 

Other than the obvious lack of content that everyone is complaining about, the most disappointing part is how wasted Nemesis was in the game, when the game was announced, I was very excited as I thought, so as everyone else, would think Nemesis will be a upgraded Mr.X, and personally, I also intrigued with the first person trailer and thought it would be cool to play the game in first person, it will be quite a unique touch to do that in RE2-like environment. Imagine playing as first person while Nemesis can pop out anytime and ♥♥♥♥♥ slap you with his bazooka. But of course we got none of it.

Based on the low effort and badly written event and scenario, dull character development, linear game experience, glitches, out of place texture, and the time gap between RE2 and RE3 release, it is not hard to see this disappointment is caused by rushing, not sure why they do that tho, as I am sure most fans are willing to wait for 1 or 2 more years for a better product, which will almost guarantee to get them better sales number. At the same time, you can see there are still some nice details put in the game, it almost feels to me like the dev team are trying their best to make RE3 as good as they envisioned, but the higher up just going for the opposite direction.

If you're willing to overlook the parts from original Resident Evil 3 that they did not include in this remake you will find RE3R to be a very enjoyable experience, especially if you go for the harder difficulty clears. I will say that while I do miss the parts they didn't include I can overlook my nostalgia and accept the game for what it is: A brief but enjoyable experience. Linear? Yes. More action oriented? Definitely. However I don't feel that these are bad things, in fact I think they lend themselves nicely to the replay factor of RE3R. These two things allow for multiple clears without investing hours upon hours of gameplay. Original RE3 was not a massively long game either, especially not if you knew where to go and what to do.

As for Nemesis himself while I do agree he mutates from form to form way too quickly he was never really that much of an issue in original RE3 either. Once you figured out how he worked it was very easy to dictate when you were and were not safe. I think the issue that people are running into is that early on you are 100% safe from Nemesis as long as you don't turn power on to the station. Before that you are free to roam Raccoon City without fear of him popping up somewhere. 

The fun and difficulty of the game can be found in anything Hardcore and above, with and without the shop items. I enjoyed unlocking the bonus items by going through the game multiple times. Loved that it was more action oriented and shooting zombies actually felt like they would die versus being complete bullet sponges. The story was also ironed out better in some places, characters expanded, etc. my favorite thing in this game is the chemistry Jill and Carlos share as you go through the game. Only complaint you'll really hear from me is the Perfect Dodge mechanic. Yes you get better at it as you play more but sometimes it can feel a bit wonky, which can allow for things like Nemesis to wombo combo you on higher difficulty.

Anywho, while I enjoy the game immensely I would recommend purchasing it when it is on sale for a bit cheaper. If you are trying to decide between picking this or RE2R up first, go with RE2R. As far as atmosphere goes, I prefer the tone and atmosphere of the original, particularly of downtown RC. The original felt more quiet and lonely, which heightened the eeriness of the occasional moaning zombie. The sky wasn't dark, but rather brown and hopeless looking, showing for the first time that you don't necessarily need darkness for horror in RE. The city felt abandoned and we got to witness what a ghost town RC would have been like. The color palette felt metallic and industrial. The Remake RC was more chaotic and apocalyptic. The city felt like it kept living while the residents had gone. You hear announcements, advertisements, and radios. That, as well as the beautiful clock tower set-piece and NEST2, made the game feel shiny. The atmosphere was just as potent - just different. In short, Remake3 felt apocalyptic while OG RE3 felt post-apocalyptic.

The game's length, to me, is perfect - just about the same length as the original RE3 was meant to be: Jill's urgent "last escape" from RC. Now, is it too short for it's MSRP? For most people, perhaps. Some will play through it once and never pick it up again. Some will play it again and again over the course of many years. It depends on the time you choose to give it. The price, people will forget about. The game, however, is a welcome entry into the new RE canon that will be solidified and remembered forever.

The game does have its negatives (that have been discussed extensively) but there are not, per se, any bad parts of the game. There just could have been even more of the good, and seeing that potential can be frustrating.

A fun re-imagining of an amazing classic game. RE3R is a an experience that keeps you captivated throughout. its breakneck pace combined with fantastic survival horror mechanics create a fantastic action romp without losing the identity of the series. 

Jill Valentine, a much loved character returns and is at her very best as the protagonist of this story. Nemesis remains the imposing threat he always was, making Mr. X from the previous instalment pale in comparison. The sheer terror that this evolving, persistent monster invokes as it pursues you through the game is truly brilliant; unfortunately the presence of Nemesis is not quite the same as it was in the original, being a part of certain action set pieces and short chases rather than being a seemingly constant threat like he was in the original game. Nevertheless, his role in the game is still effective.

Where Resident Evil 3 falls a little short is.... well the fact that it is short. Unless you're an avid completionist, you're only looking at 4-5 hours of gameplay as you escape Raccoon City which does allow for the experience to be mostly devoid of filler content (although there is a little of that). That said, I would have preferred to have seen more of Raccoon City and been allowed to explore the environment more freely, similarly to what we saw in Resident Evil 2 (2019) - the variety of environments is still excellent but having them be so disconnected from one another seems like a poor choice especially when considering the structure of the original RE3.
However; the game offers a large amount of replayability with numerous challenges to complete, unlockable difficulties, shop items that affect gameplay and a large amount of unlockables. The inclusion of the Resistance multiplayer game also serves to justify the seemingly high price point of this game. 

My final criticism is more of a personal preference issue. Where the original RE3 had some branching paths depending on player choices (though these had little impact on the story) this remake is devoid of those options. Gone are the options to evade or fight Nemesis at certain points as well as other small options. This game instead follows a linear structure which is by no means a large negative, more a missed opportunity.

Overall; Capcom continue their streak of releasing top quality titles, both from a gameplay and technological standpoint. RE3 further demonstrates the capabilites of the RE Engine with this ambitious entry. Graphically this game looks astounding and it is clear that everyone involved in its creation were passionate and talented. A truly fantastic experience - but wait for a sale I'd say.

TLDR: If you have no nostalgic connection do not buy.
I grew up playing the original Resident Evil games, spending countless hours in Raccoon City. Resident Evil 2 is still to the day one of my favorite games and the remake does a fantastic job of bringing the game to current gen. Although, it is not without its issues. These issues carry over to the remake of the third game, that was already a weaker game, in my opinion.
As it is a remake of an older game, I feel there is a need to compare the two, as this game is not meant to be played in a vacuum. However, if you would like a quick opinion: Would I recommend this game to someone that has no nostalgic connection? No, no I would not. There are far better games there, that will give a lot more content for this price. 

The problems that the original Resident Evil 3 suffered from are present here and Capcom have also stripped a lot of the aspects that gave Resident Evil 3 its own identity. The original had ‘quick time events’ where you were given two option and the story would -slightly- branch depending on your choice. This gameplay element has been completely removed from the remake and there are no different story paths to follow, apart from an extended death scene if you mess up at the end. 
The Nemesis is what gave the original game its most uniquely identifiable characteristic and, in the remake he feels watered-down. There is a lot of misinformation stating that the Nemesis is now fully scripted and that this was not the case in the original, however, he was heavily scripted in the original, it was done better, and he did feel ever present. I played the game expecting to be on the edge of my seat, waiting for the Nemesis to jump through a window or burst through a wall. This happens once in the game. The Nemesis’s music score and the creepy way he called out “Stars” is also missing. This combined with the fact that he mutates out of his most recognisable ‘human’ appearance very early on, just makes this version of Nemesis inferior. 

The main issue I have with the second games mechanics is also present in this game. The inconsistent damage to zombies, makes them more infuriating to engage than difficult. Unlike every other enemy in the game, there is no consistent way to predict how many bullets a zombie will sponge up. Meaning that the best way to deal with them is wait for the critical and run past them. I do not find this cheap trick a fun way to play the game and in higher difficulties it is pretty much required. 
One of the best, if not the best aspects of this version is Carlos. I genuinely think he had the better playable sections this time around. He is also very likable and well written. The more action focused gameplay also suites the heavily armed ‘soldier’ nicely. The game also runs very well on PC and looks absolutely stunning. The way in which knives and defence items are used has changed in this game. The knife is fairly useless and will not be used to avoid bites if equipped, however, a dodge mechanic has been implemented and I have to say I prefer it. It is also infinitely better than the one in the original! 
Visually the game is stunning and a far improvement over the original game, but this time around the game has lost a lot of its identity and it is much harder to tell the difference between the two remake games. There is also less nostalgic driven exploration here, there is nothing that comes close to exploring a realistic rendering of the R.P.D. There was so much that came together to make the second remake feel special and enjoyable and there is a lot missing here. From what I have written you may think I do not like the game, but I do I really did enjoy it. I just realize it is an objectively worse game than the second remake. Which given this is similar to the original version, it was kind of inevitable.

Les choses sont simples : le jeu n'est pas à la hauteur du remake de RE2.
Au-delà des considérations nostalgiques qui font regretter l'absence de pans entier de scénario que l'on avait pour la plupart hâte et envie de retrouver, le problème du jeu est ailleurs.

La paresse tout d'abord. 5h17 pour finir le jeu une 1ere fois en prenant le temps d'explorer un minimum...c'est bien trop peu. Paradoxalement, une fois terminé, je n'ai pas eu un sentiment de trop court, mais plutôt de "enfin" (j'y reviendrais). Les nouvelles zones sont courtes (la station électrique...inutile et inintéressante) et, pour certaines, clichées (un labo, des égouts, ou relève du recyclage honteux. Certes le commissariat est présent dans le RE3 original mais il avait le mérite d'être différent, ici ce n'est pas le cas. Rien de nouveau, on peut même ouvrir des coffres et casiers de RE2...avec les mêmes codes. Limite si on veut être casse pied, RE3 se passant avant, il devrait être ouvert dans RE2, ou notre route aurait dû être différente... Bref. Et je ne parle même pas de l'absence complète d'énigme pourtant emblématiques de la série.

Le gameplay n'est pas mauvais. C'est le même que RE2. Il ne devrait donc pas y avoir de soucis...sauf que ce n'est pas si simple. Le rythme étant plus rapide, et le jeu clairement plus porté sur l'action que son prédécesseur, des ajustements sur la vitesse de déplacement et la flexibilité de notre personnage aurait dû être faits. Résultat, j'ai l'impression en dirigeant Jill, de conduire un poids lourd. Sa vitesse de course est trop lente et ne cadre pas avec son animation accentuant l'effet de lenteur, et la caméra se replace régulièrement dans des directions étranges rendant son esquive (seul nouveauté de gameplay) hasardeuse. Même chose avec Carlos, même lenteur, mais pas d'esquive (?), seulement un coup d'épaule qui vous laisse immobile pendant quelques secondes qui paraissent interminables et vous laisse trop souvent vulnérable.

Le Game design enfin, n'est pas à la hauteur non plus. Il brise même ses propres règles. Un cadavre au sol ? Le joueur prudent aura tôt fait de mettre un coup de couteau (ou une balle pour les fainéants) pour s'assurer que les morts le soient bel et bien. Ça marche...parfois. Sauf si un script décide de ramener ses zombies à la vie par les besoin d'un piège grossier qui procure plus un sentiment de dégout et d'injustice que de peur. 
En parlant de pièges, je ne compte plus les fois où je suis mort (oui je dois être mauvais, pensez ce que vous voulez) juste parce que l'on se retrouve face à un monstre qui vous oneshot (je déteste cette mécanique, surtout quand le risque n'est pas clair) et qui plus est, est trop gros pour la zone (les "grenouilles" et les égouts en autres). Même chose lorsque l'on doit faire sauter un mur et que une fois la détonation passée, 12 zombies et un licker vous tombent dessus et vous ne pouvez pas reculer parce que votre chemin précédemment ouvert, ne l'est soudainement plus. C'est cet aspect qui transforme la plutôt satisfaisante 1ere moitié de jeu (2h environ) en un supplice qui m'a perso fait me dire une fois le jeu terminé "et ben c'est pas dommage".

Je vais faire l'impasse sur la bêtise du traitement du Némésis (après un mister X impeccable c'est incompréhensible), l'absence de nombreux personnages, le scénario simpliste et expéditif, et une surenchère de mauvais gout, pour conclure en disant que RE3R est un jeu fainéant, maladroit, très joli et bien, réalisé (c'est ce qui le sauve) mais frustrant et décevant, surtout après un RE2R quasi parfait.

A more action based and fast paced sequel to RE2, similar to their original PS1 forms. New features: Dodge mechanic allows for more aggressive AI especially on higher difficulties to compensate for your added mobility, making the game more action and skill based. As for difficulty beating Hardcore unlocks Nightmare which is an "Arrange mode" of the game, changing enemy and item placements as well as making enemies especially Nemesis more aggressive. There is also an in-game store which is funded purely by in-game rewards to unlock permanent optional bonuses to help beat the game if you are struggling.

Resistance: This multiplayer game is attached to RE3 and seems to be the main focus of the post-launch development. As a result this could be a negative point to you if you don't care for multiplayer games and only want to play RE3.

That said, the game is a blast; much more action packed than RE2R, and using a dodge mechanic in place of subweapons makes things a little more skill based. Landing a few perfect dodges in a row feels really ♥♥♥♥♥♥' good. The chase scenes are really fun, and Nemesis bursting through a wall, or landing in front of you when you don't expect it are great for keeping you on your toes. Seeing Raccoon City from another perspective is pretty great as well, and finding the little details or references to other Capcom games is nice, as a treat. The boss fights are pretty good, although I couldn't stop laughing during the last scene when Jill picks up a huge ♥♥♥♥♥♥' railgun. Nightmare and Inferno difficulty are cool additions, but they just kinda remix where a few items are, or give you less supplies. If you want an additional challenge, I'd recommend for sure. Would have been cooler if Capcom put in an actual randomizer mode, but it's really not that big of a deal, I guess. 

Now, for the stuff that wasn't too great. 
- Only one campaign, and no word on any DLC coming.
- No bonus costumes, besides one for completing the game the first time, and two pre-order ones.
- Nemesis only chases you through the streets briefly; everything after that is a scripted encounter.
- No real reason to replay the game, besides grinding out shop items.
- No S+ ranks, and using shop items such as unlimited ammo weapons and the stat-boosting coins, won't restrict your ability to get an S rank, which is the highest in the game.
- YOU CAN USE SHOP ITEMS FOR S RANKS. COME ON.
- In the unlockable concept art, it sucks to see drawings of other areas from the game that got cut. Not really that big of a deal, but still.
All in all, I got this as a gift, but the $60 price tag still seems a bit steep. I'm sitting at like 29 hours, and I've finished all but 3 of the achievements, with a couple records left to finish. Definitely feels a bit rushed, with Resistance tacked on to fill out the $60 price tag.

Overall RE3 was a good game, near great even. The controls and quality of life improvements over RE2 REmake were simple but effective, such as not having to examine every item like the 10th time you picked up handgun ammo--it just drops it right in the inventory. Graphics are about the same in LOD and immersive effect as RE2, which is still saying a lot, because my God that game was pretty. Over the course of a 3-4 hour playthrough, there were rarely parts that seemed filler or dragged for no reason. Enemies were generally solid and fun to fight. And then there is the level design and environments--which leaned on the great side . . . for as long as you could SPEND in any particular place.

Now, time to break this up into a pro and con list. Cliche, but effective. Here we go.

!!!PROS!!!

--Okay, look, lots of people like to comment things like 'graphics don't make a good game.' Perhaps not on their own, but for a person like me who really enjoys and appreciates good art and the immersive quality it brings, that is an absolutely integral part of any game . . . Especially, something horror focused. This game receives an A+ in that department. That's something I have also found Capcom does well (particularly character models and costumes (the availability of which will be listed in the 'con' category). Lighting is sensational and heck it might be a mess, but they did such a good job on Carlos' hair, I wish 'I' had that hair, lol. Meshes were built well and detail on most assets is astonishing. Zombies look like zombies, but the kind that I'd be scared of.
--Combat is simple but so good! It just feels good. I for one have been glad that they switched over to the RE4 over the shoulder design for this and RE2. It almost made RE2 feel like a Resident Evil 4 '2.' Lol. Which lots of us would love. Here it very similar with the obvious addition of the dodge feature. While I do like the dodge feature, it can be a bit tough to execute properly which we will get into in the con section. And damn, where Hunters were sorta a pushover in RE1 and others (I mean you quickly found out shotgun/grenade launcher beats the hell out of them), they are scary again in this game because their programming has been updated.
--Environments. Exploring (walking 20-30 minutes through) Racoon City was an utter joy while it lasted. Come on, it was the reason most of us were here. And the parts I got to experience were superb. The hospital part was good, well detailed and creepy . . . and Hunters, ugh. The lab (the part I dislike most in RE games, wasn't bad at all. Just like 2's wasn't IMO). I didn't mind at all returning to RPD either. Familiar but challenging. And ambiance. Oh, ambiance . . . Don't yall just love how they also add in the random creaking and clanking? **unfortunately, this part is also continued in the con section**
--Dialogue: Generally, the voice acting was fantastic. And we all know what sort of voice acting we got to bear goofy witness of in all the originals. It was just really well done. **Also continued as con**
--Finding those bobbleheads is fun to me personally so that's a pro.
--There is quite a lot of replayability because of the shop system. I mean I have 40 hours on record currently, and will play again.
--There were very few instances where you were forced to do some very mundane task (like sitting on a turret on the back of a Humvee and feeding an el gigante cousin a machine gun sandwhich). I abhor that kind of thing in games, especially horror games. Remember that part in Dead Space 1 where you had to shoot the asteroids? I just . . . really don't like that kind of crap. Mercifully, this game skipped all that BS.
--Carlos was cooler than I thought he'd be.

XXXConsXXX

--Too SHORT!!! Period! This game can be completed in an hour and 30 mins on Nightmare. And I am nowhere close to a speedrunner. And the worst part? They ENCOURAGE this by giving you achievements for completing in under 2 hours. Or for S rank, at least. On your first playthrough expect it to take 3 and a half to 4 hours. I walked most of the way through this game on first playthrough to be thorough and because I feel like it enhances the first experience. It still took me less than 5 hours. Honestly, I hate to say it, but this would've been an appropriate $30 DLC for RE2. Which leads us to . . .
--Environments: We should be spending 3-4 hours in just the CITY part of RC. If not more. The part we did get to experience was so good. WTH? I was expecting far, far more. I would've expanded on the hospital part too; it should've taken like 1-2 hours. No dice. And then there was no Clock Tower, which I understand was in the original. I never played the original for this game, but the Clock Tower and Park sound very interesting. To me the lab part was about the right amount of time, because it isn't what I played the game for (although it was good). I played for the city streets, man!
--Dialogue: Okay, I can't be alone on this, even though I know some will disagree with me. But I HATE how they rebranded Jill as some sailor-mouthed teen. I mean, F this . . . M F er, that. F ing take the hint, this. Are you F ing kidding me, that. F you. What the F . . .  I feel like I'm playing Ellie from TLOU . . . you know, if she swore (lol). WTH, is Jill fresh out of Middle School? DON'T GET ME WRONG! It's not that I have a problem with swearing in games. It's that SHE was not THAT character in any other game I've played. Then they completely rebrand her this way. For what, because it's the flavor of the game generation? Jill was timeless. Next, we're going to have Samus Aran advising Ridley to 'go f yourself, you f ing prehistoric, armor-stacking, stalking F.  I thought Clair was bad in RE2. In a shorter game, Jill managed to swear more than twice as often. As a person who likes Jill for the strong female protagonist sweetheart she was, this is honestly a disgrace to her. It's literally every other line with her. And not even when she's stressed, which I would have been on board with. Horrible branding decision IMO.
--The last form of Nemesis where you send him to whatever Hell can accommodate a 13 foot bioengineered mutant--and by 13 foot I mean 113 foot, and by bioengineered mutant I mean infuriating piece of ****--by way of the admittedly awesome railgun, was the most enamel-grinding moment (or 30) of my gaming career. Don't agree, try it on Inferno. And to anyone who wants to comment wiseguy stuff like 'oh, you just need to get gud, bro,' let it be know I'm partial to challenging games. I mean 100% completion in DS 1-3 and Bloodborne partial. Oh, and 100% completion of RE3 Remake. It was literally the worst boss experience of my RE life and I never want to do it again. It was NOT fun, whether you mastered the dumb dodging sequences or not. Yes, I know it's trivial on anything less than Nightmare--pretty much 'cause he doesn't attack you and just has a little toddler tantrum with the floor while you charge the him-killing railgun. That's even more in support of my point. He was a terrible last boss. First fight. Not bad. Nothing really new, but not awful. Second and third fights, even more fun. Last fight, God-awful. At least the game wasn't named after him this time . . .
--Oh, and it was REALLY too short.

All in all, I did enjoy it, though. Capcom has some really good stuff on their hands. It was just rushed. Could've definitely used another year of development or something. Oh, well. Hopefully the Code Veronica REmake and RE4 REmake will be 10+ hours on a normal playthrough like they should. PLEASE, PLEASE, PLEASE, Capcom, do not disappoint me with RE4--Best game EVER!
