TLDR; If you're a long time fan of the Resident Evil Series and you enjoyed last years RE2 remake, you will most likely enjoy this title, The Story mode is about 6-7 hours long overall, so if you think that's a little on the short side, I'd wait for a sale, but it is worth playing, and what content you do get is done very well in my opinion. 

FULL REVIEW:(SPOILER FREE) 
So here's the deal, games like this put me into a difficult spot. I really, love that Capcom has finally decided to stop chasing this whole "action adventure with zero horror" tail. (Im looking at you RE6) So last year when we got RE2 remake, I was ecstatic. Bought it day one and dove in head 1st, and it was very well done overall. It received critical acclaim and rightfully so. Finally a game dev listened to us, finally our cries were answered. 
When something like this happens, you need to back up their decision to give us what we wanted with our wallets. The community did just that and the game did very well in sales. Not long after that, RE3 remake was announced, and after what we got at the start of 2019, how could any of us NOT be excited all over again? Were we dreaming?
 I, like many other longtime fans of the series had all but given up hope a few years ago, Capcom had run the series into the ground and it was over. Or so we thought. Now we could relive the past and enjoy a lot of the roots of the series that made everything so awesome and fun, with the addition of newer, polished game mechanics, story telling and visuals. WAY TO GO CAPCOM! TAKE OUR MONEY!
It's funny, cause more often than not, companies are a lot like people, they mess up, eventually see the error in their ways, then begin to shape up, and they begin to get comfortable again after getting praise. Its time to come out and say it, overall this game, while very good, is a step back from RE2 Remake. I'd say its a mixed bag, RE2 does some things better than RE3, and RE3 does some things better than RE2. At the same time, RE3 has some missed opportunity, which I will get into after a comparison table between the two games.

Lets break it down like this:
[GRAPHICS]: TIE
While RE3 has slightly better lighting than 2, things like hair effects are slightly worse, though side by side, they are very close, and both look great. 
[GAMEPLAY]: TIE
This might surprise some, but I say this is a toss up purely because they are just a bit different. RE3 boasts a dodge/counter attack move that is absent in RE2, and while awesome, they removed RE2's defensive weapon counter attack when grabbed, so RE3 helps to keep you from getting bitten, but RE2 can save your a$$ after the fact. In RE3, once you're grabbed, that's that, you're gonna take damage. RE3 also stops the character for a split second before opening a door, where RE2 does not, I see that as neither a positive or a negative really, it could keep you from accidentally opening a door too fast, or slow down an escape.  
[SOUND DESIGN]: RE2 
Overall, the sound in both games is fairly top notch, but I'm giving the nod to RE2 because it has a sound feature that is surprisingly lacking in RE3. RE2 has better Headphone support. It supports Binaural sound natively, which makes playing it very immerse, especially later on in the game when you get chased by Mr.X. Why was this absent in RE3? Its small things like this that make RE2 feel like a more fleshed out release. There is also a character in RE3 (Nikolai) that has very low dialog volume compared to everyone else. Aside from that, both games have great audio.
[PHYSICS]: RE2 
Remember when I said that while good, RE3 is a step back from RE2? This is a big reason why. Ragdoll physics were completely removed from RE3, and limb dismemberment was severely altered, and that effects more than just aesthetics here, this can and does directly effect gameplay. In RE2 Zombies can actually trip over other zombies that are downed or dead on the floor, it looks awesomely hilarious and it can buy you some time to reload, heal or escape. In RE3, zombies just clip right through anything on the ground as if it wasn't even there. 
As far as the limb dismemberment goes, along with gore in general, it has been toned way down. The amount of gushing blood is reduced to almost nothing, and severed limbs just vanish upon destruction. I also found it a bit harder to actually take limbs like legs and arms off, and I don't recall a single time I was able to saw a zombie in half with a shotgun. I don't see a single reason for this design choice, none at all. Was it cause of the kids? Its an M RATED GAME, they aren't supposed to be playing it anyways! 
[CHARACTERS/DIALOG]: TIE
Both games have great character interaction and dialog, I personally think that Jill and Carlos had somewhat better chemistry than Leon and Claire, but RE2 has other character interactions later on that even out the playing field. Neither title misses a mark here. 
[PACING]: RE3
Here's one spot where I kinda preferred RE3 in some ways. Even though RE3 has a shorter campaign, it actually covers more area. There is a lot less backtracking through the same areas than there was in RE2. In RE2's defense, its following the original RE2 from 1998, a lot of which takes place in the same areas for longer, but RE3 still manages to keep mixing things up, just when an area starts to feel a bit old, the game moves you away from there. Maybe this attributed to its shorter length, but all in all, the timing of events feels really good. 
[REPLAY VALUE]: RE2 
RE2 hands down has more replay value, two separate character campaigns with different weapon loadouts and scenarios, PLUS B side scenarios AND Ghost Survivor runs. There's just more content to be had in general. 
[OVERALL]: RE2
Which brings me back to: RE3 is a step back from RE2 and has some missed opportunity. 

First lets tackle is everybody's favorite, p*ssed off, hellbent on ripping your spine out of your a$$ tyrant, NEMESIS. 
When RE2 hit shelves last year, everyone was saying how Mr.X was gonna be made to look like a b*tch by Nemesis. He was basically, in the minds of gamers, gonna be Mr.X; A relentless force to be reckoned with, that you can't stop, only slow down, but could sprint and pummel you to mush and wield weapons. Basically your worst nightmare on steroids. In reality what we got was a bunch of scripted events. Don't get me wrong, they are still intense as hell, but I don't think that's how fans were thinking he was going to be implemented. 
The idea of Mr.X was really interesting and stressful, even annoying at times, but man, talk about feeling someone on your a$$! He mimicked the pursuing nature of the Original Nemesis from 1999 a lot, while mixing things up to make the tension even higher at times. It just seems odd that they would lay out the building blocks to make something so well, and then just totally go the other way. 
Maybe they had their reasons, but a lot of us were left scratching our heads nonetheless. 
Another missed opportunity in my opinion was the chance to make Jill and Carlos have separate Campaigns like Leon and Claire did in RE2. I feel like this could have opened up a lot of neat possibilities and lengthened the game a considerable amount. 
I bring these up for one reason; People are slightly disappointed in Capcom.
RE2 was made well and sold well, RE3 is made well, but commits a cardinal sin, it downgrades elements of design, thats a pet peeve for a lot of gamers. RE3 is worth a play and yes, it could have been better, but here's the real worrisome part to me; We want more of these remakes. We want Capcom to look at RE3 as a lesson, give these remakes your all, they are worth it, to us, and to your profits, its a win-win, just please don't go soft, remake Code Veronica, give it the same if not better treatment as RE2, you wont regret it. Build it and they will come. 
Having said all of this, RE3 is still worth a buy, I did enjoy what was there and you should too. 

Thanks for reading everyone, 
-Taco

There are higher unlocked difficulties that scramble zombie locations. This would be fun! However, the only "difficulty" comes from everything getting boosted to a one-hit kill. It gets boring quickly.

There is a lot of asset reuse. It does reuse the RE 2 police station, but that was part of the original RE 3 so it gets a pass. However, the first hub area is used twice (three if you backtrack for items), and the hospital is used twice. There are really only three other areas, which are linear corridors used to connect the hub areas. This results in a lot of padding used to stretch out what little game there is.

To give it credit, the first playthrough is fun. But between the location reuse and the lack of major change between difficulties reduces the replay value to near 0.

Wait for it to go on sale. It is worth around the $30 to $40 range imo.

A great game, though also definitely a step back from the RE2 remake.

RE3, like RE2 before, is a very enjoyable game with some great moments. It works almost exactly the same as RE2 did - same shooting mechanics, inventory management, weapon parts for upgrades, etc, with the main difference that now there's a dodge move to avoid enemy attacks and performing a dodge with perfect timing (just as the enemy is about to hit) activates a slow motion effect and allows an instant counter at the enemy's weak spot.

The game's drawbacks start with the story - the pacing is awful and there are portions of the original game that were removed but should not have been. Without those portions, the game feels needlessly short and a bit lackluster. In terms of pacing, there's just no build-up - the game starts right off the bat with a chase sequence and introduces new characters way too soon into the game.

The dodge move, while useful, is too hard to pull off properly, often requiring pixel-perfect timing in order to actually work and sometimes not even then. There is an unlockable item that makes it easier for dodges to be made, but you shouldn't need an unlockable item just to be able to properly use the dodge move.

Nemesis in this game feels more annoying than creepy. While Mr. X in RE2 felt menacing without feeling overwhelming, Nemesis in this game just feels annoying, as his attacks are incredibly hard to dodge. The saving grace is that at the very least you can instantly down him with a grenade (except on Nightmare and Inferno), but it'd be much more interesting to make him actually interesting to fight outside of the scripted boss fights.

Because the game relies so much on the dodge move, boss fights in this game are a lot less interesting - basically just wait for the boss to attack and hope you dodged in the right direction and then counterattack, or get hit and feel annoyed that your dodge didn't work because you didn't dodge in the right direction.

The one thing I really liked about this game is the unlockable system, which allows you to collect points to buy different items including inventory upgrades, stat boosters, special weapons, etc, instead of relying on the player getting specific ranks at specific difficulties. The unlockable items also make the highest difficulties a lot more doable.

Another thing I liked about the game is how the story matches the story from RE2 and explains some of the events from that game.

No opinion on the multiplayer - I haven't tried it.

Overall, it feels like they should have remade RE1 before they did RE3.

Still recommended, though I hope they pick the quality back up for the RE4 remake.

I finished Resident Evil on the Gamecube, Resident Evil 2 from 2019 and Resident Evil: Revelations on the 3DS. I hold both remakes to high regards when it comes to concepts, level design, mechanics, storytelling, bosses and enemy variety. Those games also made me tense with dread and disgust at times and even empathy for some of the characters. The Crimson Heads in REGC are still enemies that give me the creeps for how cleverly created they were because they affected both the overall mechanics and level design. One of the other creatures in REGC still holds up as the scariest thing I have ever seen in a video game so far and if you played it and you understand what I mean by empathy, you know that creature I'm referring to.

The game, a supposedly exploration-based third-person action survival-horror game, screams identity crisis even though the product itself is definitely more action than horror as in the original title from 1999. Resident Evil 3: Nemesis has always been one of the more controversial titles and, rightfully so, it was the first step towards the development of Resident Evil 4. The game's original design couldn't really seem to work with the action-driven style yet felt the need to include puzzles and non-linear level design. This title is more of a reinterpretation, not a remake or reimagination.

The first sign of warning for me happened when the lack of ink ribbon was spotted as I chose the Hardcore difficulty. Now, one could say that I expected the same quality experience of Resident Evil 2 which isn't wrong because the game gained attention and acclaim from the back of an impressive video game. Resident Evil 3 is nothing more than an highlight reel, but it doesn't even include all of the highlights. It even is afraid to expand its story, enhance its formula or even keep the nuances in design.

One of the one thing that really ran this game into the ground was a massive clash with the narrative and its difficulty setting. Yes, I can understand the notion that the game has different spots for enemy placement including items. However, you are all aware that the Nemesis-T Type can create a different kind of a zombie with a parasite. That NE-Alpha enemy type shouldn't appear before you see that non-interactive sequence of Jill witnessing the creation of the NE-Alpha. Yet it does on Nightmare because the game simply clashes with its stoy. Now one could say that the difficulty is unlockable... but you can be awfully unprepared and have your run being destroyed because the game pulls a 180.

Oh and can we be honest about the fact that the dodge system is unresponsive, breaks its rule and doesn't give you enough invincibility frames to get out of bad positioning? You shouldn't be punished for doing something that the game recommends you to do... especially when you have tutorials and button prompts in your face during the first minutes! And the most insulting part? You can buy a token within the game after finishing the title as you collect points. This token enhances your dodging. That is absolutely insane and a straight-up admission that the mechanic is defective! I could understand in a FromSoftware game where dodging can be a direct consequence to the failure state but we are discussing apple versus orange. What's the point of integrating a mechanic where, after a perfect dodge, you can aim and shoot yet put yourself in the worse situation when it's completely out of your control?

I could have accepted some of its faults and its linearity but I knew when there was a nightmare so I couldn't get into the narrative. I ended up knowing when the game took the controls away from me. That escaping sequence? Jill is holding the Shift button for me! Sure you eventually get the gun but the game fails to teach how to use it because the entire scripted sequence requires no shooting, dodging or even thinking.

However, here is one of the most insulting part of the entire product. The Nemesis-T Type is the cover boy! He has been heavily marketed but you only see the creature for maybe 10-15 minutes excluding boss battles. All of the sequences involving the Nemesis-T Type are heavily scripted, there's no threat or sense of dread when the creature is on the screen. And you know what it also does? It lessens the impact of the Tyrant Mr. X from Resident Evil 2. Nobody should expect the next Alien: Isolation Xenomorph but the Tyrant wasn't shown that much in the trailers or pictures which made it such a formidable foe...

If you find some key items and you go back to some other rooms before you progress with the actual key item within the story, you may observe that, if you have dodged enemies (not spending ammo or grenade or even taken a bite), you can realise that some room layouts completely change when its comes to enemy positioning. This is a direct contradiction to the philosophy of Resident Evil since its inception! Enemies must be part of the level design! Once you get out of this philosophy, you fail to create a Resident Evil game.

Resident Evil 3 is a great game but it's not without it's drawbacks and to some it can be pretty divisive on whether it's worth buying or even playing it.

PRO
- RE Engine is great so it plays really well, no crashes, glitches or bugs
- The environment of Raccoon City and it's other areas all look really nice
- The characters and enemy models again all look great
- The gun play is as fun as always with lots of weapons to get
- The "shop" is available to buy different items/weapons that can help after completing the game by completing different challenges
- Various difficulty modes and achievements that keep the replay value up
- Interesting moments that contain crossovers with Resident Evil 2

NEUTRAL
- It comes with Resistance, a 4V1 online mode. It's hit or miss with people and kinda D.O.A.
- The levels can be pretty short if you know what you're doing
- Nemesis doesn't chase you and only appears in scripted moments. Can be hit or miss depending.
- Less focus on puzzles and more on action. Was explained before release but again, hit or miss with fans
- Once you have the infinite rocket launcher, which is pretty easy to get, the game is too easy even on nightmare and inferno (Nemesis goes down in one hit when chasing for example)
- Nemesis fights are a little weird and underwhelming, they're not scary just strange
- The new dodge mechanic is a nice addition but it feels like it hardly works that well. Sometimes I can get the timing just right but others I'll get grabbed even though I rolled before the zombie attacked me.

CON
- Lots of content has been cut such as areas to go and interactions with certain characters
- As such the story feels awkwardly pieced together and a lot shorter
- It can be completed in around 6 hours and that's with exploring and getting all optional items
- Zombies seem to stay alive even after putting them down twice
- The button mash to escape a zombies grasp is useless because you WILL get damaged every time
- You cannot use the ESC button to get out of animations, such as a zombie grab, that you know will kill you so you have to sit there for ten seconds watching your character struggle knowing it will end in game over
- Some enemies have a one hit kill which feels unfair at times
- Some zombies will play dead until you get close enough where they are GUARANTEED to damage you even though you have put bullets into them to make sure they're not playing dead
- Higher difficulties say items and enemies are moved around, didn't really notice much different
- Jill's new persona doesn't come off as cool or badass, she's actually kinda annoying her constant use of the F word and her constant cold and sarcastic attitude towards people trying to help her.
- Gore has been severely toned down. Even though heads still explode from critical shots, limbs don't come apart from the body even if shot directly with a shotgun or rocket launcher like they would in Resident Evil 2.

Even though this game isn't what we all expected or even hoped it would be it's still a decent one and it's nice to see it all remade in a new engine with new game play mechanics. I would however definately wait for a sale because it will be over quick and it can't justify the price tag unless you know you're gonna be playing it a lot. Also don't expect any addition onto this, as far as I know the only updates are going to be the for online game mode.

A brilliant follow-up to the RE2 Remake, and a gorgeous reimagining of the original RE3. Gameplay is as polished as RE2 Remake, but with some quality-of-life tweaks. For instance, your knife does not break! You also get a dodge and a lot more ammo. All of these things make the game feel a lot more action-oriented, which honestly made it a less stressful experience than RE2. 

Other than gameplay and the obvious visual improvements, there are also drastic changes to the characterization and narrative. Diehard fans of the original may feel it deviates too much, but I love how the story plays out. Jill and the side characters have actual personalities and realistic dialogue. They've ditched the goofiness and meandering, tightened the plot, and created a balanced flow of rising and falling tension. The way the story progresses and finishes is much more satisfying than the original. Not to mention the banter of the characters in this one is highly enjoyable. 

I also loved seeing the numerous little tie-ins to RE2. You can see that some of the actions of the characters in 3 affected things in 2, and if you remember the safe and locker codes from 2, they're all the same in this one!

There was, for instance, no good reason to cut Jill's trip to the RPD and have you explore it with Carlos. Getting to play with Carlos more than once is nice but there was so much room to expand his role without removing even more from Jill's. Could've had him rescuing survivors for the train, adding to the tension when Nemesis invades it. Could've made his trek to the Clock Tower playable. But mostly, could've just let us explore RPD with a STARS member, for once. Such a wasted opportunity.

Story beats were just lacking overall. Brad's demise was uneventful at best. We barely have a brush with Kendo. About 2 seconds of Marvin. No interactions with survivors. Not even a whisper of Leon or Claire or any RE2 cameo. The one lucky character to have his screen time drastically improved is Tyrell, so if you're a fan of that guy, hooray.

Removing story choices AND not expanding on the storyline AND not even including something to the likes of a scenario B (even though that was pretty lazily implemented on RE2R) coupled with the removed content just makes for such a hollow campaign. 

Adding 500 difficulty tiers does not make up for lack of actual gameplay. That's, 1. a mostly technical challenge that doesn't even appeal to a significant portion of players and 2. something hardcore players already figure out for themselves (that's what knife-only, no damage and such and such challenges are for).
"Make monster die harder and player weaker" is a poor, artificial stratagem to sell as replay value.

Puzzles are pretty much extinct and replaced almost entirely by fast paced fetch quests which, without a slower more intricate puzzle in between to buffer, get a little grinding towards the end.

The Nemesis, aka the thing the game's supposed to revolve around, is probably the biggest letdown. Even though I found the later-game fights entertaining, his redesign is quite off-putting in all but his final form. His iconic growling of STAAARS is so subdued he seems to be coming off a cold. I don't mind the encounters being scripted as they were in the original as well and that didn't detract from the threat one bit (also I found Mister X's incessant presence annoying rather than tense), but his silly Wesker powers and how you're set up to fight him is very anticlimatic.

The only time it was really a pain to fight him was right before the sewers, 'cause the small corridors gave him a good advantage but also cut off a lot of his nonsense superpowers. It felt more like fighting Nemesis should.

Not all's lost as the script is actually pretty great and the reimagined characters are excellent, well acted and voiced, and well animated (given a sturdy enough rig, well rendered too). Lots of enemies were recreated in a fun, menacing new light (the Hunters specifically, loved fighting them) and some areas are a definite upgrade, like the hospital which was pretty boring in the original but turned out to be a remake highlight with its tight spaces, creepy lighting and constant tension.

The dodge mechanic and controls are tight and if you don't mind a short romp you'll probably be well entertained for a couple playthroughs. 

But all in all I can't recommend paying full price for what honestly feels like a cash grab DLC rather than a standalone game. It feels rushed, unfinished and uninspired. Veered too much into RE5 territory for my taste and didn't do the original any justice. Fair at a half off sale.

Okay, I'll be honest, I am a new fan to the Resident Evil franchise. My very first game I played was Resident Evil 7 since that was the "talk" about during the time I purchased it. I loved Resident Evil 7 despite being first person for a survival horror game! In fact, I think it made some instances a lot more scarier in my opinion. I wasn't a big fan of the action approach on the DLCs. When I was doing a Let's play on it in my YouTube Channel, I personally had a blast on it.

I then went and purchased the Resident 2 Remake because of being remastered and I was told that Resident Evil 2 and 4 were one of the best survival horror games in the franchise, Once again, I've recorded and uploaded videos of my playthrough on this game. I really enjoyed the Remake and I felt there was a good comparison to the original RE 2 based on gameplay videos and lore behind it. 

So once again, I was having high hopes for this remake, Resident Evil 3. I did my playthrough of the game and well... here are my thoughts.

First off, I loved some of the scenes in the game such as Nemesis's different mutations and the railgun scene. I felt that the game mixed well with a combination of both survival horror and action to the game. I also loved the great connections to Resident Evil 2 as the game progressed.  Graphically, the game look beautiful. A huge upgrade compared to the original! 

Now let's get on the negatives. Right off the bat, gameplay wise, it was just reused mechanics in the Resident 2 Remake.  Nothing much was changed besides the addition of quicktime events. I HATED how the event don't really give out a vivid explanation if you need to "hold" or "tap" a certain key. They are almost the same on how they were displayed. I dislike how they removed the feature of using a knife, grenade, or flash grenade to stop zombies from biting you. They wanted you to use the new dodge mechanic that was barely explained or not mentioned at all in the game. If you get too close to a zombie, you were forced to get bitten. The playtime for the game was really short then expected. I managed to play the game in 5 hours and I felt that a lot of lore and background from the original was left behind. I like how in Resident Evil 2, you have the choice for the A or B routes but instead of that, both Carlos and Jill were combined in one story. If Carlos had an entire route instead of mixed in with Jill's Story, then I bet the playtime would have been significantly larger.

It was good to see Nemesis in the RE Engine, but i felt like Nemesis was like another William Burkin boss as Nemesis  had mutations similar to Burkins. Like each boss had a Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, and Stage 4 (Blob Form).  Don't get me wrong, some of these mutations of Nemesis were cool, but all I saw was William Burkin sometimes.

Now what do I think of the game overall? This game is alright overall.  Well I don't think its worth the $60 asking price if you are just looking into the singleplayer content. I only RECOMMEND to get this game when it's on SALE. I haven't played the RESISTANCE co-op yet but if you just want this game just for the main singleplayer game, then wait for a sale. 

To sum it all up, I don't HATE this game, but it doesn't mean I LOVED this game. It's a great game but not worth its asking price. Capcom has greenlit a Resident Evil 4 Remake so I am really hoping they don't wash it out like they did here. Personally, I think there is other games that need a Remake more than RE 4 such as Resident Evil: Code Veronica.

I want to start off by saying I did have some enjoyment playing RE3, but compared to RE2 it was really disappointing. While RE2 had 4-5 years of development RE3 only got 1. While playing RE2 it was tense and immersive the entire time. Everything was scary, everything was a threat. This time around, It got very "action gamy" very quickly. 

While playing I wrote some things down that I wasn't a fan of but first let me say the entire first act was FUN. I enjoyed running around a Jill in the city, having to dodge the Nemesis and zombies because I wasn't sure when would be the next time I got a few more rounds for my hand gun. Unfortunately  that changed way too quickly.

CONS-

Not a Puzzle: While Re2 had me running around back and forth trying to figure out what was going on, RE3 didn't have any of that after the first act. It becomes very liner and one dimensional. It feels very much like RE5 where your goal it to get from Point A to Point B with some zombies in the middle. There's an Object that needs a Item that you find at the end of Point B then head back to Point A.

Bad AI: In RE2 the AI was smart, the AI was terrifying . A licker would chase you from room to room until you A) Killed it B) reached a safe place. The Zombies would bang down a door and attack you. MR.X was searching and hunting. In this game. I door cheesed so many of the zombies from basic to the variants. They just go back to their original point and reset. 

Lame Nemisis: The scary thing about Mr.X is he was CONSTANTLY EXISTING! You couldn't fight him, you didn't see him until he wanted to PUT YOU THROW A WALL. There was no fighting Mr.X there was only running. With the nemisis that was only for the first Act, and dear god let me tell you I LOVED IT, but the good times cant last forever. They make the nemisis a constant script battle. He's never hunting you or chasing you. You never run into him, crap your pants, and run in the other direction hoping he will go away. He's a constant boss fight and an annoying one. The boss fight goes as this 

NEMISIS IS MAD, hit him with explosives. NEMISIS RUNS IN A CIRCLE hit him with explosives so he falls. NEMISIS FELL shoot his heart. Rinse and repeat 5-6 times before he "dies" They do the same fight TWICE. 

SHOOTING GALLERY: The scary thing about RE2 is the ammo conservation. You weren't guarantied to kill a zombie with your ammo. You might have knocked the same zombie down 6 times in the same run only to have it come up a 7th and fight you like you had 60 rolls of toilet paper. In this game you have SO MUCH AMMUNITION and they die some much more often. Most I've had a zombie come up is twice. The section you play as Carlos there is no fear. You have an ASSAULT RIFLE. I am not afraid of zombies if i have an ASSAULT RIFLE. Also his final fight is a pseudo Nazi zombies wave shooter. It was boring. 

ACTION GAME NOT HORROR: So what took me out of the "horror" were the enemy placements. They used the same formula of "suspense". There's a big space, you havent fought in a little bit. Then BAM ENEMIES. Or the thing that gets me is the clumping of zombies. When done right and I'm suppose to be like "Nope not doing this: that keeps me in the game. When i'am suppose to go through them because of the linear path it becomes a chore. I'm not afraid of them anymore. They are just annoying.

ONE TIME APPEARANCE: So the thing that gets me is when they introduce a zombie type (Spider/Dog/Tentacle monster) They have very little screen time. Yeah they used more of the tentacles but the dogs only had 4 in the game... the licker, once. The spiders were so PARANOIA inducing but they only had one part, with a meaningless mechanic. They really could of used them more. All the archetypes had strong things about them but we barely see them. 

DODGE: Adding the dodge was a good and bad thing. I love that they allow me to avoid fighting a singular zombie in a small area to conserve ammo but the downside is IT ISN'T USED THAT WAY. It's a combat roll, it's so much action that if i have to dodge I ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up somewhere to end up having to use it, and it seems to work out 50/50. I'd find myself doing my best impersonation of Ultra Instinct Goku, dodging all boss and zombie attacks, but then 20 seconds later it just doesn't work anymore. It turns a tense situation into A) Welp, just going to become Danny Phantom and dodge everything. B) ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ JILL! 

Yellow Tape: So one thing I loved about RE2 is it wasn't hand holding. You have to figure out puzzles, it was open. You had to explore. In this game any "hidden" path is marked with yellow tape. Rather then having me investigate the area to figure out the next thing I have to do, the game just air traffic controls me down the lit up run way. 

Normal = Easy?: So while playing through normal I refused to craft any ammo, and I still had MORE THAN ENOUGH to get through the story. I had to make myself feel stress of ammo conservation by not crafting anything. 

No Poison?: So I remember in RE2 they had a blue herb for dealing with poison. With the spiders it would have made sense. Give me another danger to worry about. Give me another resource I have to manage thanks to the fear of death. There's only Red and Green, and there is SO MUCH. 

Autosave: Quick way for me to know a fight was coming up was autosave. It wasn't just after an objective, but when they expected me to die. You know what does that? ACTION GAMES. You get rid of the  if I know the guy hiding behind the door in a spooky clown outfit says "hehehe, you're goinna get SPOOKED"

Forced Characterization: Jill goes from ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to Chummy with Carlos in such a cannon valley way. Carlos seems like a white knight the entire time, not a real person. He takes Jill's ♥♥♥♥ and never response in any sort of genuine manner. He reminds me of a middle schooler who has a crush, and lets their crush bully them in hopes that their crush will reciprocate feelings.

TLDR: Did I enjoy the game? Parts. Did it feel like Resident Evil? No Should you buy it? Not at the moment.

First of all let's point out that resident evil 3 remake is in a tough spot, when reading reviews remember that remake will be compared not only to Resident evil 3 original but also to Resident evil 2 remake, Those are two titan size shoes to fill, so don't be so hard on it.

In short;
Is it a good game? Yes
Is it a good remake? No

If you want to know specifically what's wrong with this game, keep reading.

I will not complain about action since we have to remember the original RE3 nemesis began with Jill jumping out of an explosion with an M16 and the dodge mechanic was also in the original. So yeah action has always been a part of RE3. 

Here is a list of everything wrong with this game.

1) Cut content: There are lots of removed locations and nearly ALL puzzles from the original that were replaced by nothing, just removed and added nothing in their place. Removing content has a bigger consequence then just enraging the fans. Everything was put there for a reason in the first place, for example, the lockpick in this remake makes absolutely no sense. In the original the lockpick had a function other than it's utility to open doors, it was there to take away one slot from your inventory so most of us would simply leave it in the item box which would be a problem when we ran into a locked door forcing us to keep going back to safe rooms hence doing backtracking. In this remake this doesn't work because when you have all pouches you have twice the amount of slots than the original so you'll never need space. Also since there are so many removed puzzles and key items, your inventory is never full so you never have the need to go looking for an item box....Hell there is even an achievement that consist in finishing the game without opening the item box...why do this? 

2) So you loved the return of the ink ribbon in RE2 hardcore difficulty?...Yeah RE3 was like "lol no" and they removed it.

3) They removed the Grenade/knife button. If the game is more action focused, why remove a button that makes combat faster? to me it is a contradiction, instead of having a grenade button you have to open inventory to equip every time you want to use one(same with knife). Of course this can be fixed by assigning it to a shortcut but you only get 4 so you'll be wasting one on your knife and another on a throwable.

4) Pacing is really fast. Don't get me wrong, the original also had a very fast pace, you would get shotgun in the first 10 minutes and magnum or G launcher very soon after that, in this game too. You get guns really fast which is not that bad because strong enemies start appearing really early in the game. My problem is, I'm not even 10 minutes in the game and I already have upgrade attachments for my guns, geez let me at least play around with them a bit before upgrading them.
Same can be said about the story you meet your companion very early unlike the original which had you explore the city before meeting the fist survivor, this gave the feeling that the city was destroyed and empty, you never get this feeling of loneliness in this game, you see some NPC citizens running in panic but they are not enough to make it look like a chaotic city and at the same time they are too many to make you feel alone and abandoned, so it ends up somewhere in the middle which is not good.

5) The city is too small.
This is a big deal, somehow they managed to make raccoon city streets smaller than the original, the first part of the game before clock tower is honestly only like 4 streets and each street has 2 or 3 locations to explore. That's it...which is bad and in my next point I explain why.

6) They dropped the ball on NEMESIS!!!!:
Such a waste of potential. In the original RE3 nemesis was this harassing presence that appeared whenever you least expected it, kept you always worried about when it was going to show up. Sadly back then they had hardware limits so all the nemesis encounters were scripted. Twenty years later RE2 releases and gives us Mr. X, the character that made everyone's experience different stalking you non stop regardless the difficulty you played, he was a true harasser it seems like it was what they always wanted nemesis to be. So you would assume the NEW NEMESIS will have this chasing  mechanics implemented in RE3  remake right???? WROOOOOOOOOOONG!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! All of Nemesis encounters are scripted. Why? I don't know. 
It's not only that, in the original RE3 Nemesis was way more imposing, by the time you got to clock tower you've had fought him 5 or 6 times, you knew how strong he was and why you should fear him by then, but in the remake you've seen him only 3 times of which one is a mandatory fight and the other two are scenes where you don't even have to fight him but run away, which I must add running away from him is a thrill but in my previous point like I mentioned city is too small for him, you'll run away from him a block or two and chase is over... This is the part of the game that really hurts to see how poorly it was handled, you had the potential , you had open streets and the Mr X mechanics, could have been the perfect playground for Nemesis... and you blew it Capcom...

It's still a great game though. I would recommend it, just remember you are comparing it to some of the best titles in the franchise, it doesn't live up to expectations like RE2 did but that doesn't mean it's bad, not being better than the best doesn't make you the worst you know.

So yeah definitely recommended when the price drops around 30$.

For what this game was, I enjoyed it. It was however too rushed and had too many issues that outweighed the good. 

                                                                                       -Pros-
       1.    The combat was satisfying with the dodge mechanic, and the rest was pretty much Resi 2 remake so its hard to mess that up. 

       2.    The zombies are more challenging, since this time around they are not confirmed dead when you hear an audio q. They play dead *sometimes* and get up later to surprise you. For rest of the enemies it seems as if they were designed around the dodge mechanic. You will get hit a lot without using it. 

       3.     The voice acting is fantastic and the characters are interesting. Carlos especially is an improvement from his annoying character in classic Resi 3. 
       
       4.     The models and graphics are fantastic as well. Not a single character looks strange or out of place. This is the Jill I now prefer they go with in the future. 
       
       5.     The guns are satisfying and the gunplay is fun and challenging. Enemies can be quick or sway alot, so its tough to hit your mark, but that's not a complaint. 

       6.     Nemesis looks and sounds great. His boss battles are some of the best ive seen in Resi, visually. 

                                                                                        -Cons- 

       1.     They removed lots of content from the original. Enemies such as giant spiders (again), crows, and Grave Digger are nowhere to be seen. Locations such as the park, the clocktower, and the factory are cut. The RPD section is shortened enough for you to question whether it would have mattered if they removed it as well. It felt like a cheap way to pass campaign time by reusing Resi 2. Barry Burton is also cut from the story. 
     
       2.     Capcom once again decided to unnecessarily tamper with OG character concept for no reason. This opinion may differ to people, but to me Capcom changed Hunter Gamma so much, it isn't even the same monster. It looks as if the lead designer took heavy inspiration from Resi 5's Uroboros enemies instead of just making the og concept look better. Hunter Gamma is a different type of the hunter series. A cross between Human and Amphibian, but in this it looks like a dinosaur with small chicken's wings.. Brad's death is also changed from being killed by Nemesis, to giving a prequel backstory to a character. The scene in question was 10 seconds, it was lame and really wasn't necessary at all. It took away from Nemesis and Brad.
      
       3.      The game is really short and unsatisfying for a $60 game. My first play through was 5 hours on standard and 7 hours on hardcore thanks to many deaths. I get that the og game was short, but that game was made in 1999.. A remake should not repeat that problem.
       
       4.       The game is $60 but reused soo many assets. Resi 2 remake reused the graphics and little assets but the majority was made from scratch.  You will find many reused zombies models, and if you played resi 2 remake over and over, the zombie sounds and their behavior will be less effective this time around. The RPD is the same and lickers are used again with the same tricks to startle you. The dogs have no real point in this compared to the last game as they are thrown at you in much smaller numbers for no reason as they are so frail and easy to deal with coming down a long corridor.
      
       5.       The puzzles are lame. The 1999 version had them and its part of every classic Resi game. I understand puzzles aren't everyone's forte, and it may not be streamer friendly, but they could have included a few difficult optional puzzles for the classic Resi fans.   
       6.       Nemesis has significantly less scenes. In the classic game, Nemesis would show up more than 10 times. It gave Nemesis his notoriety in Resident evil as the one boss who stalks. Now he only freely chases the player in one section of the game for a couple minutes and the rest are scripted scenes and or boss fights. You run into him 5 times here. 

       7.       The camera is dreadful. In boss fights, the cam will be up in your face. It makes dodging bosses so much more difficult, and the distance between you and the enemy will feel far even though they are much closer than they appear. Dodging enemies is also inconsistent and will make you want to rip your hair out after getting grabbed when you shouldn't have.    

All in all the game seems rushed, and was compensated with a game mode that nobody asked for to reach a $60 price tag. I hope Capcom does not continue this trend of making half baked remake games. I would like to see Outbreak or Code V done right. Hopefully they take their time.

If the Resident Evil 2 Remake was a 9/10, Resident Evil 3 Remake is an 8/10. It's a great game still, but it's not quite on the level of awesome Resident Evil 2 was. Having never played the original RE3, I can't compare it to the original in any way, so instead this review will be looking on it on it's own terms.

So, what does RE3 do right?
[list]
[*] Graphically, the game is still downright gorgeous. All the character models are wonderfully designed, and the maps themselves are beautifully made and have a huge impact on the game's atmosphere.
[*] The overall gamplay loop is still satisfying, the guns feel satisfying as hell use, the new additions since RE2 like the dodging are a ton of fun once you get the hang of them. Inventory management is still super important and part of what makes the game so fun.
[*] Voice acting is top notch. RE2R had a number of lines that came off as kinda awkward or poorly delivered, but everything about RE3R felt a lot more believable in terms of delivery.
[*] The characters themselves are way better presented than in RE2R. Jill and Carlos have actual chemistry which was missing between Leon and Claire, which helps make them more engaging as characters. The story in general is way better than the one in RE2R.
[*] Tons of replayability with the additional difficulties from RE2R and the Shop system that's unlocked in NG+.
[*] The campaign itself is fun and engaging, even if it is on the shorter side. It's important to keep in that mind that both RE2R and RE3R actually are really close in length, both games needing 2 hours for S rank, RE2R just felt longer because it had more puzzles than RE3R. Once you knew what the puzzles were you could finish RE2 super fast. Though that does lead into the first big complaint with the game as well...
[/list]
As for negatives with the game:
[list]
[*]For people only interested in 1 playthrough, this game will likely be underwhelming. There's more action set pieces and significantly less puzzles than in 2, so you'll get through it faster than RE2R. For comparison, my first playthrough in RE2R took me 8 hours, whereas my first in RE3R took me 5 hours, with my S rank times for both games being very similar in length.
[*] There's no minigames at all after you beat the story. If you're someone like me and enjoyed modes like Fourth Survivor, the Mercenaries, and modes like that, there's none of that at all in this game. Instead, RE3R gets 2 additional, harder difficulties called "Nightmare" and "Inferno", and while they are a ton of fun as they mess with enemy and item spawns to make it more fresh, the lack of fun minigames like the aforementioned Fourth Survivor does hurt the game.
[*] Nightmare and Inferno, for as fun as I had with them, do have some serious issues with some things being cheap. Nemesis-infected zombies and the final boss in particular being the worst offenders. They both have combos that can take you from full health to dead without you being able to do anything and your window for dodging those attacks is so small even with the dodge book it can feel cheap and unfair when they kill you. 
[*] Nemesis feels way more underwhelming than Mr. X did, at least on Hardcore. He's not really that much of a threat most of the time he's around as he's relegated to set pieces, so you usually aren't gonna be trying to loot stuff while dealing with him. On Nightmare and Inferno he's legitimately terrifying as he's a lot faster and can kill you extremely fast, but before then he feels underwhelming as hell.
[*] This is more of a nitpick than anything, but the gore has been turned down from RE2R. While crit headshots still cause their head to explode, dismembering zombies feels super toned down, as I can count on my hand the number of times I've seen an arm/leg pop off, let alone cutting them in 2 with a shotgun. I understand it's likely due to how many more zombies are on screen at once, but it is kind of disappointing regardless.
[/list]

Overall, I'd say the game is really really good, but I'd probably recommend waiting for a sale, especially if you're only looking to doing one playthrough. The lack of post game minigames like the series is known for is a huge downer, and in term of overall time to complete, I managed to 100% the game in about 40 hours, so even for people who intend on doing most if not everything in the game will probably knock it out really fast. Still a ton of fun, but there is a serious lack of content with the game. Hopefully we'll get a minigame or two similar to Ghost Survivors sooner rather than later.

Some voices were quieter than others, the music is great but it is quiet and doesn't have many hard hitting moments. I wish they would've done a better job with the mixing.

What I loved: Graphics. If you played the RE2 Remake from last year, it's very similar here. Looks great. Storyline wise it works well and fits into the greater RE narrative. Some environments and events are pretty cool. Nemesis looks awesome.

What was okay: Nemesis had a certain growl in the original, and when he said "S.T.A.R.S." it was super creepy. They changed his voice to be less intimidating and less pronounced, which is a bummer. This game is more of a bunch of little maps that don't connect, so if you were hoping for another RE2 situation where you constantly run around the same locale, you won't get that here. Additionally, I feel like they toned down the zombie damage/limb removal aspect from RE2 Remake, and they got rid of ink ribbons and knife degradation. Not entirely bad, but I enjoyed the mechanics from the older games so it's a bummer it's not here, not even on Hardcore difficulty.

Lastly, I beat the game on Hardcore the first time through, took me about 6-7 hours and that's collecting almost everything (I missed a few things but I looked hard). That's the in-game time, but it doesn't count map/inventory time and cutscenes so in all the game took me closer to 10 hours to finish. I don't mind that, it was a tight 10 hours that I enjoyed but if that's a concern for you then be warned.

Overall: Loved it, it was perfect and I'd say RE2 Remake is the better game, but I still highly recommend it for RE fans new and old.

[h1] Capcom even remade the controversy of the original RE3 ... in a way. [/h1]

The game lost a lot of its strength of its predecessor without backing it up with many strengths of its own and a lot of reused content..yep, sounds similiar to the situation when the original game came out. Anyway...

[h3] The Good Stuff [/h3]

The gameplay system is probably the only thing with no big problems. The same system as RE2 Remake but with the Dodge function like the original (and minus the self defense feature, but I guess dodging AND saving yourself with the knife  would make things too easy).
Dodging works well and getting a perfect dodge roll even gives you a window to retaliate, which you are going to need when Nemesis is after you.

Nemesis is truly a threat to you, jumping in front of you to cut you off or pulling you closer to him with this tentacles. Unlike Mister X, Nemesis is more pro-active in the attempt to kill you and unlike Birkin, Nemesis has more variation in his boss fights (which is only possible thanks to the dodge mechanic).

But not everything is well with Nemesis...

[h3] The Bad Stuff [/h3]

He is way too underutilized, the only time he can show his true potential is in the first area of the game and even then its over in a matter of minutes. The rest of his encounters are mostly scripted chase sequences and his boss fights. The other areas are too small for him to work anyway, which surprises me as the biggest flaw of the Remake is this: Cut content.

The cut content and areas are hurting the game in so many ways: The main story is, even for a classic RE-title, quite short (first run took me about 6 hours including cutscenes and my fastest time being a little bit over an hour) and the missing puzzles and "Live Selection" feature and makes subsequent playthroughs dull.
Of course the unlockable difficulties, which changes some enemy and item placements (but not key items and only minor changes) helps a bit, but it could have been a lot more engaging with the "Live Selection" and different routes in place.
The only thing that saves the replayability is the Item Shop, where you can exchange points from completing records for new weapons (mainly infinite ammo guns) or other trinkets, which help you to tackle the harder difficulties.

The missing Mercenaries Mode is also something I don't understand, it would've worked so well with the gameplay system of RE3. Coupled with it's own Item Shop for unlocking new characters, costumes and loadouts it would've been a blast to play.
Well, we can only hope that it finds its way back into the game as DLC (like Ghost Survivors for RE2Remake)...but according to insiders, Capcom has no plans for DLC's...shame if it's true.

The bundled multiplayer game RE:Resistance is a topic I can't say much about as I only played it for a couple of hours and lost my interest pretty fast and I don't seem to be the only one. The multiplayer is dying quickly and I'm not surprised, nobody asked for this and I don't have to feeling that this multiplayer experience is well polished or thought out.
People would've shown a lot more enthusiasm if it was more of a co-op experience like Resident Evil: Outbreak or even better, just remade that game and bundled it with RE3. THAT would've been a lot more interesting.

[h3] Verdict [/h3]

With all that said, I don't think it's a bad game, just a mediocre remake with a lot of wasted potential. You can still have fun with it, but I would recommend that you should wait for a good sale before buying it.

In the remake of RE2, the devs tried very hard to create a 1:1 copy of the police station, and imo they did a very good job of it. It was not 100% perfect, but it was very well done. The layout of the police station was more or less the same, but filled with new puzzles, monster placement, etc. The RE3 equivalent of the police station is the streets of Raccoon City, which the devs made no effort to create a 1:1 copy of in the remake. It's difficult to draw a line and say when the city streets officially end, but I would maybe say at the very end of the game when you enter the Dead Factory (conveniently cut and replaced with NEST2). The "mean streets" of Raccoon City have always been my favorite part of RE3. I recall being fascinated by the idea of exploring a zombie-infested city when reading old gaming magazines back in 99/00 and looking at screenshots of RE3. The fact that the city street sections were completely gutted and replaced with new content which has no relation to the original is probably my biggest complaint about the game. Remaking RE3 and making no effort to preserve the original city streets sections from the beginning, all the way to the cable car, through the clock tower, through the hospital, and lastly through the park and into the Dead Factory is like remaking RE2 and making a brand new police station with no resemblance whatsoever to the original, or remaking RE1 and making a brand new mansion. It's absurd, but for some reason it happened in RE3, and it really made me mad. 

Another thing that really bothered me was that the most iconic weapons in RE3, the STI Eagle and freeze rounds were not in the game. The STI Eagle is a handgun that you craft after defeating Nemesis on hard twice. He drops the parts and you combine them and then you have a handgun with a much higher crit rate and firing speed. The STI Eagle is essential to speedrunning RE3, and it was probably my favorite weapon in the series, but of course, the devs didnt think it was important enough to include. 

Anyone who has played RE before knows the grenade launcher has explosive rounds, flame rounds, and acid rounds. They're cool, but not as cool as freeze rounds. RE3 is the only game in the series (that I can recall) that has freeze rounds. I don't know why they were removed, but they were iconic to the game and should have been included in the "remake". 

Nemesis himself really pissed me off. I'll admit the remake of 3 made me so mad that I only finished it three times, but I never felt that there was any incentive to fight Nemesis at all for bonus drops, and there are times in the game where he legitimately felt invincible and you had no choice but to run (the chase outside the bug nest and the chase in the burning building come to mind), whereas in the original you can fight him every time if you want and he will drop loot. When Nemesis appears it felt like a completely linear scripted event where you run from A to B and that's it. In the original Nemesis would disappear if you run to certain spots, but he was free to chase you great distances and you had the freedom to kite him around and fight him where you felt comfortable (no more getting him stuck on corners and defeating him with pistols in the remake...). I know Nemesis drops a silencer which is cool, but beyond that I don't know and hated the game too much to look much further than that. 

It also really pissed me off how they completely cut the clock tower (that goes back to first paragraph), but related to that, the fight with Nemesis outside the clock tower was ridiculous and now Nemesis is a dog which runs on walls??? In the original, Nemesis maintains his humanoid form until the very last encounter where you kite him around and line up the railgun shots. Fighting dog-nemesis was really stupid. 

So they cut all the city content and replaced it with random garbage, but they also removed any sense of exploration and backtracking. You no longer have to gather items to turn on the cable car because now the cable car is actually a subway car. The game had no puzzles whatsoever outside of that subway power puzzle, which really sucked because the gas station puzzle, the clock tower puzzle and the water sample puzzle were some of the best in the series (the latter is notorious for being confusing and frustrating the first time you do it). All RE games feel linear to some extent, but this game was a straight line from start to finish, I couldn't believe it. 

I consider Gravedigger to be an essential part of RE3, but they cut him too. Hanging out in the comfy graveyard shed before the final Gravedigger fight is essential to the RE3 experience, but of course that had to be cut. 

NEST2 was the dumbest thing I have ever seen. I can't fathom how that was given the go-ahead by someone at Capcom. "Yeah guys we're going to remake RE3. We will cut everything from the game, including the final area and just make up something and call it NEST2 and link it to the hospital for convenience because we're lazy and want money for nothing." Unreal in my eyes.

Also no branching paths/choice system.

I don't review games often, but seeing this one get more hate than it deserves made me want to post something. I can understand why it's difficult for people to be more objective with a game like this, as it is part of a long-running series and is a remake of a beloved game. But we really should try to do just that.

Judging it by only what it is, I would say it's fantastic. The graphics are astoundingly good (I had the pleasure of playing at 4K60 in HDR, with nearly maxed-out graphics settings). This game is really one of the best-looking games I've ever played. The detail and atmosphere is incredible. The game mechanics are extremely polished: shooting feels good, running feels good, and the design of the game is obviously well-planned and executed.

Is it worse than the original? I can't say because I never played it. Is RE2 remake better? Probably, but if so, not by much. I think of it kind of as an Alien/Aliens situation. The first movie was more straight horror, and the second one was kind of action-horror. But both are terrific at what they do.  RE3 remake is a well-oiled action horror machine.

Is it short? It depends on your perspective. RE games don't tend to be that long overall. The game clocked my first playthrough at about 7 hours. And for those who haven't played it yet, the game doesn't seem to count the cutscenes nor your game pauses in that time. My total playtime (time I was actually playing the campaign) after my first completion was 11.5 hours. I don't consider that short, especially for this type of game. In addition, the design of this game indicates that it was meant to be replayed over and over, and mastered and manipulated with in-game unlocks. There's plenty of fun to be had beyond your first playthrough.

Is it worth full price? That is totally subjective. As far as I'm concerned, it is as much as any other game can be. It has a sky-high production value, great gameplay, and is the type of game I will likely go back and play again and again over the coming years. I've had an absolute blast with it in a way that few games can deliver.

I definitely recommend Resident Evil 3 Remake.  As with nearly any game, there are some caveats.  These caveats may lower a score, but certainly not lower it to the point of not recommending it.  RE3 is a fantastic game, and if you are into Resident Evil, survival horror, action horror, or even just action itself, you should buy this.

I own both RE2 Remake and RE3 Remake, and both are cinematic and gameplay masterpieces, as far as I'm concerned.  However, while RE2 tracks the original closely, so that you basically get an "upgraded original", RE3 takes (too) many departures from the original, and it certainly feels like they are cutting content that should be there.  If you don't know about the original, you may not miss anything, but if you know about the original, you can't help but feel disappointed at the lack of inclusion of certain entire areas, like the interior of the City Hall / Clock Tower area or the park.  On the other hand, some additions are made.  Basically, this is a new game, and unlike with RE2, you can't really say, "Oh, hey!  I know this room!"  Pretty much everything is different.

Many say that this game is short, and that's true, but it is extremely cinematic.  If you have played RE2 Remake, this game is basically one scenario of one character, like "Leon A / First Run".  However, I would say that this single short campaign has more replay value than any of the individual RE2 campaigns.  I am not into 60+ hour open-world games, myself, as I feel that they tend to drag.  RPGs often have you grinding to level up, and throw story elements very sparsely through the game.  Basically, if you take a 60-hour game and compress it so that only the exciting and story-moving elements remain, you get this.  You will likely not be bored at any point, and while there is some backtracking (especially to optionally unlock previously-unreachable items), you will feel like you are always moving forward.  That is good in my opinion.

The difficulty of the game is pretty much for everyone (particularly after beating it).  At the start are 3 difficulty settings.  "Assisted" gives you an assault rifle, extra storage space, healing when on "danger", you take less damage, and you deal a bit more damage.  There is also a "Standard" mode, and a "Hardcore" mode.  After "Hardcore", there are two higher difficulties that change around the game and give you as much of a challenge as you could possibly handle.  On the other end, after beating any mode, you can "buy" (with in-game credits earned) items that can significantly increase your power, defense, and healing, so much so that on "Assisted" with both power increases added, you can take down most zombies with just one headshot from a handgun.  On top of this, in the "store" (again, just using in-game credits), you can buy various weapons, including some with infinite ammo.  This really rewards replays of the game, and makes it so that you can replay the game in a vast number of ways and tweak things, including power, costume, and weapons to your liking.

The story of RE3 runs like a movie.  In fact, on YouTube and such, there are compilations of cutscenes which, when put together, make a movie that is more enjoyable to watch than the vast majority of Hollywood blockbusters today.  The graphics, voice acting, and choreography are top-notch, and the story is pretty good as well.

Before I end this review, I have to mention two MAJOR problems.  A lack of Nemesis and a lack of Raccoon City.  I was actually not a fan of RE3 and didn't like a fast pursuer in an RE game.  But even I was disappointed by the severe lack of Nemesis.  If you only want to fight against his base humanoid form and check out Raccoon City, then just download the demo and be done with it.  That's basically it.  While Nemesis comes back and you go through more of Raccoon City, the downtown area in the demo is the best it is done.  While I won't spoil too much, after chasing you a bit, Nemesis then becomes a prop during scripted events.  Then, he transforms into a totally different creature WAY too soon in the game and you're left scratching your head and thinking, "Was that it?"  Also, the methods by which Nemesis transforms (both times) is laughable, and easily the worst part of the story.  Raccoon City, for its part, has its outdoor areas soon turn into indoor areas similar to those that we've already seen a lot of in the series.

Those hoping for a 1-to-1 remake of 1999's RE3: Nemesis will be disappointed.  And I truly wish that Capcom would add these missing places to the game, because this has the potential to blow away the original if those extra parts are added.  Even so, if you think of RE3 Remake as a new Resident Evil game that stands on its own and has no shoes to fill and nothing to prove besides (still) being one of the best games of 2020, then you will like this A LOT.  In fact, just as a RE game to play for fun, this is my favorite.  The story in RE2 is more impactful, but playing through RE3 is just more "fun".  Compared to 1999's RE3, this one does some things worse than the original, but it also does some things better.  In the end, this is so divergent that it must be classified as a totally new game, but as far as my opinion on it goes, it is still a great game.

Ok so after Resident Evil 2 was released Resident Evil 3 was released just over a year later introducing us to the relentless nemesis creature. With the recent remake of Resident Evil 2 it was pretty much a dead cert we would get the Resident Evil 3 remake shortly after.

So this is my Pros and Cons from my 11 hours spent on the game and my overall thoughts-

Pros

GREAT GAME, BAD REMAKE

In it's own rights, RE3 Remake is a fun game worth playing. However there are some things that must be noted. Like the original, there is only one campaign, however the live select feature has been completely removed, also removing any possibility of alternative events from happening. This is significant because a single thorough playthrough of this game's campaign only takes around 6-7 hours to complete. Upon completion a shop opens up where you can spend points earned by completing various challenges. This shop allows you to by items such as special weapons, and gear that you can use on further playthroughs. While this features is nice if you are interested in obtaining any of these weapons or gear, not everyone will care enough to have this greatly lengthen their playtime. The only other thing to help freshen up further playthroughs is nightmare mode. In this mode, item and enemy placements have been rearranged, and enemies deal more damage and receive less damage. While this is nice for a challenge and will slightly tweak the experience of your playthrough, it will not change any story moments or set piece encounters. Something to keep in mind when weighing a $60 purchase. Especially if the included multiplayer mode RE Resistance does not interest you.  

Game length aside, lets talk about the game itself. When it comes to gameplay RE3 Remake obviously shares a lot in common with RE2 Remake. For the most part the controls and gameplay are the same, with some tweaks giving RE3 Remake a more action oriented focus, just like the original RE3 had. These gameplay features include exploding barrels scattered throughout the city and a dodge mechanic that has replaced the defensive knife mechanic from RE2 Remake. The knife in this game no longer has a durability meter, however it can only be used as a normal weapon, and will not defend you from a zombie bite, as it did in RE2 Remake. While RE3 Remake has you out in Raccoon City, I was surprised by just how closed in and small the environments felt in this game. You begin in downtown, but only remain there for about an hour or two at most. It is here that you will interact with Nemesis in a way that best emulates encounters with him in the original RE3, but more on that later. For the most part RE3 Remake, keeps the environments smaller and more streamlined when compared to the more Metroidvania approach that RE2 Remake had. You will not remain in most areas for very long. The game is always pushing you forward to new areas, often with set piece moments similar to the alligator sequence in RE2 Remake, but longer. While you visit more locations in RE3 Remake then you did in RE2 Remake, many of these areas are more linear, with not a lot to exploration to be had.  

Nemesis is something that needs to be discussed as well. Unlike Mr. X in RE2 Remake, who would dynamically chase you throughout the RCPD Building, Nemesis will only show up at specific moments. Even in downtown where it is made to feel like he is dynamically pursuing you, he will only show up at set moments in the story. Not long into the game Nemesis takes a bit of a backseat and will only appear for boss battles for the remainder of the game. While Nemesis' implementation is not bad, it has been more streamlined and reduced in comparison to his role in the original RE3.

As a remake, RE3 Remake completely fails in my opinion. As a longtime fan of the original RE3, like many others I was disappointed to see the campaign take so many liberties with altering game events, settings, and encounters. Much of the content of the original has been cut or altered. A few of the locations that have been cut from the original are the park, graveyard, and clock tower interior. With the cuts of these locations, also comes cuts of whatever monsters you would've encountered in said locations. RE2 Remake reimagined much of the original's content, however it was done so in a way that still evoked the sensibilities of it's source material, and still hit most of the same story beats, and moments that made the original a classic. RE 3 Remake is barely recognizable to it's source material.

Much of this review has been spent comparing RE3 Remake to the original RE3, as well as the RE2 Remake, but how does RE3 Remake fare in it's own rights? When you view Resident Evil 3 Remake as it's own game, it holds up much better. The gameplay is tight, there's a lot of tense, creepy, atmospheric environments and moments to experience, and overall this is a well made Resident Evil game. Regardless of it's short length RE3 Remake is definitely worth playing for anyone who has enjoyed the recent Resident Evil games. Although you may want to wait for a sale.

If you're buying this game expecting the same respect to the original that the RE 2 remake had, buckle up for a bit of disappointment.  The gameplay is on par, the controls pretty smooth, but the content has been gutted.  Bad.  Huge swaths of the originals content, specifically the clock-tower and the park, are just gone.  Mercenaries mode?  Gone.  Maybe they'll add a version of it as DLC, but as of right now nope.  At least in the RE2 remake, while alot of the content was tweaked a little bit to fit the new way the game was played, you still experienced almost all of what the original had to offer.

Also, the unlocks are no longer tied to what you do, but how much you do based on an in-game point system for doing certain actions.  No more infinite weapons unlocked for clearing that hard earned S+ run (S+ isnt a thing in this remake).  The nemesis encounters, while the first is entertaining and has a bit of intensity, the rest are literally on rails.  There is no choice on how you encounter him like in the original, which made a huge impact on the replayablilty based on your choice to fight or run.  There is no surprise to his appearances, the game pretty much announces to you when the next fight is based on the placement of safe rooms and supplies.  In the original the threat of Nemesis appearing felt almost constant.  

But the real cause of why I'm making this review, and will change it if Capcom fixes it, is the after-clear content, specifically the Nightmare (and by extension Inferno) mode.  The game changes slightly in ways I won't spoil here, but the most unforgivable thing is how phoned in the last boss fight is.  The final boss is essentially unchanged mechanically, but as he does more damage and Jill flinches on any hit (you can't access your inventory as you recover from a stagger), any hit you take is almost always chained until you die.  My Nightmare run was going smoothly, and I was enjoying experiencing the little changes here and there, but this fight is a brick wall compared with the content leading up to it.

A few other nit-picky misgivings:
-Reused zombie skins (who you'll recognize from the RE2 remake), almost to an embarrassing degree.  At one point I was fighting a band of 4-5 twin zombies.  I get this is a more action oriented game, but nothing takes me out of immersion like this kind of laziness.
-Next to no puzzles.  
-At a certain point in the game, you essentially play a zone protection mini-game.  It goes on for way too long, and it feels almost like you've been ripped from a resident evil game and stuck in some call of duty zombies shtick.  ♥♥♥♥ like this doesn't belong in a resident evil game (hopefully not anymore).

All in all, Capcom is showing a bit of relapse into what made Resident Evil 6 a roaring dumpster fire.  If you aren't aware of the original, this game can be a good bit of fun.  If you have, this game deceptively allures you with assuming the same care and respect to the original the last remake had, but betrays that trust in a great many ways.  I would wait until it's on sale before purchasing it however for the amount of content it contains.  You're better than this Capcom.  I'll be looking at your next couple releases with a good bit of caution after this.

This is a hard one. I don't normally give negative reviews to what are essentially good games, but sometimes a game just fails to hit the mark. As a veteran of the original series (I love my tank controls), I feel that this entry could've really used some more time in the oven. It's not bad, it's just really short.

The original RE2 was short, but had multiple layers of replay value through its different characters, separate campaigns, and the zapping system. The cuts made to that game's remake were pretty small and easily overlooked due to most of that replayability remaining intact. The original RE3 was also fairly short, yet a single run would still take you longer than a play through of RE2 by about an hour at least. Had the game areas been more faithfully recreated the way they were in RE2 Remake, then this game would stand next to it as a worthy sibling. However, the cut areas really degrade this entry from what it could've been. 

Uptown - Practically removed from the game (it's there, but it's a one-and-done), as is the connection that the uptown/downtown areas had to the front gate of the R.P.D.. This alone destroys what was perhaps the best designed area of the game, leaving only a shadow of the former horror of wandering Raccoon's infested streets.
The Clocktower - Removed entirely, used only as a backdrop for a boss fight. What was probably the most iconic area of the game is now gone completely. I sure do miss shoving Nemesis off that ledge...
The Graveyard - If you were waiting for that HD Gravedigger boss fight, it isn't here.
The Industrial Park & Waste Management Plant - Honestly these areas of the original sucked and playing fast and loose with this part of the title was really what it needed. I have nothing bad to say about the last half-hour of this game.
Mercenaries Mode - The fan-favorite originally debuted here, but did not return for the remake.

But the most glaring strike against this title was that they removed the greatest strength of the original version; the Enhanced Ammunition vs. Enhanced Weapons mechanic. In the original, you had to decide between either mixing lots of ammo to take on Nemesis whenever he appeared in order to drop him for an enhanced weapon part, OR mix ammo often in order to get enhanced ammunition, which deals more damage but is not compatible with the enhanced weapons. So you chose between Normal Weapons + Upgraded Ammo, or Upgraded Weapons + Normal Ammo. The removal of this feature is akin to the blow RE2 Remake suffered with the removal of the Zapping System. Difference is, RE2 Remake still has multiple ways to play through the campaign, while RE3 Remake has only one.

All said, it's not a bad experience by its own merits, it just isn't what it really should have been, or needed to be. Especially for your $60. This really should have just been 'The Nemesis Campaign' $30 DLC for RE2. Then they would've gotten stellar reviews and could've re-branded Code: Veronica as the official RE3 like it always deserved.
