TL;DR, it's fun game, but if you came in expecting to play it more than once or expecting anything like the original RE3, you're going to be heavily disappointed.  

    I'm a long time Resident Evil, but have always been a bigger fan of the original trilogy.  When REmake 2 released, I was not only shocked at how much I thoroughly enjoyed the update, but preferred it in some aspects.  There was a lot to love; the visuals were amazing, the vast amount of replayable content was staggering, the dialogue was pretty sound, and the rework parts for both Sherry and Ada are very welcome.  The gameplay was great, but there in lies my issue with what I imagined what was to come.  The gameplay felt action-oriented which they made work given, but I asked myself if this could work for the eventual REmake 3.  So on to the actual review of the game...

    REmake 3 does some things extremely well when it does excel.  The game looks phenomenal sans a few really low textures for pictures which are a bit jarring.  The controls are pretty tight, but the dodging mechanic is almost too generous this time around.  It's not its inclusion that makes it easy; it's the fact you can dodge 3 times before stumbling to avoid any strike.  Capcom did make the mechanic way more user friendly, but reigning it in a bit would have done more for the difficulty which brings us to a first gripe. 

    It bothered me in REmake 2 as well, but the zombies in these games soak so many bullets that it takes away from that headshot experience that's so satisfying in the series.  It felt so rewarding to score headshots and know you could save that extra ammo for an enemy in a location you'd pass through often.  REmake 3 tries to rectify this by giving you so much ammo that you never really have to worry about running out which is traditional for the action game approach they wanted to have.  This ultimately makes the enemies feel less threatening no matter their sheer number.  

    The story arcs and story choices they left out of REmake 3 is just a baffling design choice in general.  It could be argued that the choices in RE3 weren't significant, but they had story paths unique them with their own dialogue and consequences.  It made you want to play the game again to see how things could have gone with the path not taken.  Even the Nemesis encounters were choices the player made, but we'll get to Nemesis in a bit.   One of the most iconic scenes in the Clock Tower is just gone because they didn't include it in this update.  The park is just gone.  Several bosses are just gone even without reference.  This contributes the already short game being updated into an even shorter, less dynamic experience.

    Nemesis in this game is just a pale comparison to his former self.  He's just not scary.  He doesn't surprise you the way he used to mostly in part to this game wanting to turn him into an even bigger plot device than he was while also scripting his encounters with you.  (To play devil's advocate for a moment, I will say that because the game doesn't load between rooms like the original games that the game had to take a different approach to being chased down by Nemesis.  I just don't find it be a good solution.)  I can't say too much without spoilers, but as it's been said over and over by others, he's just really annoying at worst.

    I can't really recommend this game full price to any former fan or even newcomer.  There's not enough content to justify a 60 dollar price point, and there's not enough of soul of the old game to justify even an nostalgia buy.  I'm not even going to bother with that abomination that is the multiplayer, but hey, you might enjoy it if you want a discount Dead by Deadlight that's somehow even less functional.

This is one of those times where I wish I could have "Mixed" as an option. [b]As a game, Resident Evil 3 is enjoyable at best.[/b] I decided to wait about a week before writing a review so that I was able to collect my thoughts. 

I must preface this review by stating [i]I have not played the original Resident Evil 2 or 3 games, so I cannot judge its accuracy as a remake;[/i] but I adored the Resident Evil 2 remake and it sits comfortably as one of my favourite games of the last decade. As a result, I will be drawing comparisons to RE2. Releasing only a year after Resident Evil 2, I had high hopes for Resident Evil 3 but worried that it not enough time may have been devoted to it as a result. Resident Evil 3 was exceptionally short. [b]For your money's worth, I would recommend waiting until this title is at least 50% off.[/b]

Overall, I only thoroughly enjoyed one segment of the game, and that was the hospital segment, besides that, the game felt heavily condensed. If you enjoyed Resident Evil 2 like I did, this will not be in the same vein as that. It's still a good game, it's just short and not worth its price tag in my own personal and subjective opinion. The character models are gorgeous, the graphics are stunning and the performance is superbly optimised, much like it was in the Resident Evil 2 remake. The RE Engine shines through this remake.

I played through Resident Evil 2 six or seven times, but after my second playthrough of Resident Evil 3, I feel absolutely no impulse to go back to it.

I've never written a negative review before, but I felt this was made quickly as an attempt to cash-in on Resident Evil 2's success without replicating or improving upon the formula successfully. Should they do any more remakes in the future, I hope they give it the same love they did Resident Evil 2's remake and not what appears to be a hasty effort in this one. This is not to discredit the wonderfully hard work the developers put into this game, they all did a tremendous job, but a decision was made somewhere to dedicate less time to this game and it shows. It's with sadness that I leave a negative review. This is RE3-lite, with elements from other REs, and the recent Tomb Raider/Uncharted games. There's still some fun to be had here, if you can ignore the numerous issues/upsets. Wait for a sale, or go play the definitive version that is the original RE3. (Seamless HD version is neat!)

[h3]Positives[/h3]
+ Fantastic visuals. Impressive character animations, as well as facial animations.
+ Good voice acting, and improved character development on most characters.
+ Quality soundtrack. Many are enhancements of, or remixes from RE3 original.
+ However little they may be, there are still ties to the RE2 Remake. (RE2R).
+ The hardest difficulty modes remix a few things. Makes repeat playthroughs slightly palatable, since the live-selection/branching paths system is now gone.

[h3]Negatives[/h3]
[b]#1: Rushed to market with largely recycled content[/b]
This truly took Capcom and partners 3+ years to make?
- Every normal zombie is recycled from RE2R. You can see recycled assets everywhere. Just play RE2R before this, and have fun spotting them all.
- For all the areas removed from the Original, a new section was added. [spoiler] Of course, it's NEST 2, so they can reuse assets from RE2R's NEST. Ever wondered why the pale heads are in RE3 now? You got 'em on RE2R's Ghost survivors mode. If the graveyard was in RE2R, we may have gotten it here, simple.[/spoiler]
- Did you know these, about the new underwhelming Nemesis?
[spoiler] 
- His 1st form animations, are all from RE2R's Tyrant/Mr. X - just sped up, along with a "get-over-here" move, and a jump.
- Many of his animations from the flaming rooftop battle are exactly from RE2R's Super Tyrant fight vs. Leon. This includes the scream.
- You know why his second form is a beast now? So they can recycle the animations from RE2R's licker, and Berkin stage 4 vs. Claire.
- Don't get me started on the battle with his second form towards the end. It's a shameless rehash of the one above, with zombies thrown in, along with a lame gimmick. Can cause cheap player deaths, due to wacky stun locks and camera issues.
[/spoiler]

[b]#2: Inconsistencies, and immersion breakers[/b]
- On max settings, while the game ran at a smooth 60 FPS, the zombies that were afar, moved at 30. This happened with the flame/fire effects at times also.
- Noticeable clipping through objects. More from zombies in Carlos' segments than Jill's.
- With the grenade launcher, why does Jill load 6 rounds all the time? Even when she is supposed to load just one, or switch grenade types? FFS, it's a 3-second animation that matters during tense encounters.
[spoiler]
- During the RE4 inspired Hospital sequence, the zombies inexplicably explode, and disappear on death. Even their bloody puddles vanish, leaving a spotless floor! They're no special zombies either, just the ones you've seen since the beginning of the game. (That were from RE2R anyway.) Furthermore, in the first floor of the Substation office, zombies just vanish post death after a while. Not as immersion breaking, but the Drain Deimos (spider-like creatures) spawn infinitely, and go poof on death.
[/spoiler]

[b]#3: Can't help, but compare[/b]
[u]vs. RE3 original: [/u]
- Over an hour worth of content, including some fan-favorite puzzles, areas, enemies, and costumes are cut out. (The new city is good, but way too small for exploration.) The Mercenaries mode, and live-selection are nuked as well. Sans live-selection/branching paths systems, the campaign replayability is a tad too monotonous.
- Nemesis is not as scary, nor threatening. They're trying to make each of his encounter unique, but there's not much to be excited about, when they're so short and easy.
- Laughable how the freeze grenades are out, yet the mines are in.
- For people saying, "Hey, RE3 original was derivative, building off of RE2 back in the day!" Certainly, it was 1999, yet RE3 had enough quality content to be different from RE2. It never felt like a cash grab, and it took less development time than this remake claims to have taken.

[u]vs. RE2 Remake: [/u]
- Downgrades galore. Lack of zombie ragdoll physics, limb dismemberment, extra game modes, and most importantly, overall polish. Puzzles are fewer, and watered down too.
- Mr. X is a way better Nemesis, than the Nemesis here. X is slower, yeah, but he is a walking tank that causes anxiety and paranoia with his near constant, plus random presence.
- Intense action/horror moments happen more on gameplay, and less on cutscenes.
[spoiler] - While the callbacks to Kendo and Marvin are nice, they only last for a few seconds. Carlos using the C4 near S.T.A.R.S office explains the damaged walls there, but what about the third floor? Where you get the spade key in RE2R? Would've been cool if Nemesis caused this destruction though. Who am I kidding? Nemesis is reduced to a dumb jobber that goes down to a single frag grenade on Hardcore difficulty.[/spoiler]

[u]As a $60 package:[/u]
Project Resistance never looked appealing to me. I was then ticked off when I heard the presence of a lootbox system. While they are not paid lootboxes, you can pay real money for booster packs, to get loot drops faster. Hats off, Capcom! I'll stay far away, thank you very much.

I know I might catch some flack for saying this, but I like the Original RE3 just a little more than the original RE2. With that said, I feel that the RE2 remake is better than RE3 remake but not by much. I'll deliver my spoiler free review and include spoilers at the end for people to read.

Resident Evil 3 is a third-person over the shoulder shooter survival horror. You play as RE1's returning character Jill Valentine, the game starts and you are immediately  attacked by a hulking super zombie-mutant named Nemesis, however this attack is very scripted and acts simply as a rough introduction to the game. The opening of the game right after meeting some soldiers you get access to a somewhat open (and small) area of Raccoon City (a fictional mid-western town).

The game-play is almost similar to RE2 remake except for the knife/grenade defense weapons just becoming regular weapons and the introduction of a dodge system that when executed perfectly gives you a pseudo bullet time auto lock on the attacking zombie/monster. Puzzles are completely absent from the game (except for maybe one near the end but it was pretty simple to solve, at least for me). Nemesis behaves somewhat like Mr. X for the first section of the game, after his first actual encounter he will stalk you from area to area and unlike Mr. X, he does not follow sound clues and moves much faster being able to jump from behind you to in front of you at a moments notice. Nemesis only stalks you for a little bit though so it is not too overbearing or overwhelming.  The game does have 3 levels of difficulty at the start and two locked difficulties that I ended up really enjoying more than I thought.

The story is alright, most of the story is found through all the files you find scattered throughout the game with some exposition given from dialogue exchanges between characters in and out of cut-scenes, almost all of which can be skipped.  The original RE3 I do not recall having a really deep story but I do remember a somewhat forced romance at one point (from one the play-throughs) between the two main character which is almost completely absent from the remake, I feel this was for the best as now instead of being lovers they feel more like people working together to survive. Very earlier on and at the halfway point it does become apparent that Jill does seem to suffer from PTSD from the events of RE1 which i do feel adds a sprinkle depth to her character.

To sum it up, its a good game. I really liked it and if you are reading this and still on the fence about getting it, then just wait for a sale.

***SPOILERS***
[spoiler]
If you are reading this because you were one of those that played the original and were hoping that RE3 remake would get the same treatment as RE2. I can say it did, sorta, and at the same time it didn't. Nikolai got his evil turned up to eleven. Instead of being a prick of a supervisor that just team-kills because he thinks it will give him some kind of leverage against his company he becomes insanely evil with no point to his actions. The choices get removed but the way the game played I feel that they would have ruined the immersion a little. While the actual opening of the game (where you get to the subway) feels open you are only there for a little bit, once you know where to go to get everything to progress this part will feel terribly short and linear. The rest of the game is more linear. I personally feel that Hardcore mode and Nightmare mode are how the game was suppose to be played.

Nemesis I feel had an excellent mechanic to him that you don't get to truly enjoy. You only get to experience him in the downtown area and he acts like Mr. X on steroids; he jumps, he screams, he upgrades zombies (not really, you only see him do it once and they just appear here and there after that). Once you figure out his weakness (the weird metal heart on his chest) and get a decent handling on the dodge mechanic he does become a little easy. After the Subway we goes to stage 2 Nemesis, the original this was when he gained extra tentacles and loses his jacket, in this one he gets big and is more like a licker and a dog had a baby the baby grew to the size of a van. When he goes to stage 2 all encounters are scripted and you only fight him twice and you get a quick-time event with him. I feel the stage 2 nemesis is incredibly underutilized. Stage 3 nemesis, in the original when it became a giant amorphous blob that just spews acid and you have to hit it enough so it gets in front of a stationary rail cannon, this time he becomes a giant amorphous blob with teeth and limbs. I do feel that RE3 remake stage 3 nemesis was actually pretty good, i liked how it ended and i liked how you end up killing it. 

The last thing i want to talk about is the cut content from the original, The grave digger along with the graveyard and park are gone, the clock-tower is gone, smaller areas like the water fountain and bar are gone (the bar is there, but only in a cut-scene) the mini-gun as an unlockable as well as the mine-thrower are gone.  I know gravedigger was there as padding in the original but it was replaced by the hunter gammas which only linger around the sewers and lab area and will instakill you. I don't understand why they cut the clock-tower, i mean its still there but you just run by it. the hospital area is greatly expanded upon as well as the lab which is no longer disguised as a water treatment facility. The mini-gun being removed as a unlockable was kinda a bummer, the mine-thrower is replaced with mine rounds for the grenade launcher.[</spoiler]

I like this game, but it's simply not worth the asking price, and is nowhere near as good, significant, or relevant as RE2's remake.

The game is short and very linear with little meaningful exploration.  Much of it is a rehash of RE2's remake. There's 0 replay value (unlike in the original or in RE2's remake).

As an example, there are a total of 8 "puzzles" in the game, and that's using the term as loosely as possible.

- Safe (new)
- Subway (flip some dials to match the answer given in the same room, on a giant screen)
- Safe (copied from RE2, same location and combo)
- Locker (copied from RE2, same location and combo)
- Locker (copied from RE2, same location and combo)
- Safety deposit room (copied from RE2, no need to find keys, just type in the code you see in the same room)
- Safe (new)
- Mixing puzzle to produce an end-game item

The majority of the above are optional and pointless.

Additionally, there are a few key items you need, but they're placed directly in your path and you never really have to go looking for them. The fire hose from the demo is the most difficult to find.  There are also 3 gems you collect in the beginning area of the game to insert into an object, but there's no puzzle.  You just slot them in and get handed an item.  You'll likely find all 3 gems without even looking for them or thinking about them.

There are a few other crates with weapons or attachments, but the only things you have to work for are the weapon crates you get from stunning Nemesis.  Everything else is just handed to you on a silver platter.  Nemsis is a lame excuse of a Tyrant.  Mr. X is by far a more dangerous, engaging, and fun threat.  Nemesis is completely scripted, and the majority of the encounters are nothing more than cinematics and guided set pieces with quick time events.  The dodge ability makes him pretty useless, tool.

That's not to say it's perfect, as I'll stand by last year's RE:2 being better, hands down. However, it's still a good game, though needing a little more polish to live up to it's predecessor. 

It lacks a few of the mechanics from RE:2, like using the knife or grenades to escape being bitten. While being able to dodge is supposed to replace it, it doesn't quite make the cut and leaves you being bitten more often than not. Now, it's not difficult to pull off, but taking out the ability to defend yourself in a grapple with an enemy makes the quick time event completely pointless. You get bit, regardless of how quickly you smash the button and fill the meter. If I'm missing something, please let me know, but I played through the whole game and not once saw any indication of escaping a grapple like in RE:2. 

The second major point here is the change of pace from RE:2. If you're going in expecting the same environment as RE:2, you'll be disappointed. The developers gave RE:3 a more action-oriented feel. This isn't terrible, but it isn't what I was looking for in a RE game. Especially not from a RE:make of one of the PS1 trilogy. I'd prefer they'd stuck with the slower pace and the scarcity of resources of the previous game. This is what adds to the horror. The fleeing from an unstoppable monster. The feeling of hopelessness in the character's struggles. Look, I love gun-slinging and battling epic monsters as much of the next guy, and I know those elements existed to some degree in the originals. That's not the issue here. The issue is that they are now front and center, rather than just small piece of the game. The focus here felt like how RE5/6 went off the rails of the original games and focused on the fighting, rather than the surviving. 

Overall, this is an awesome game and I definitely recommend picking it up, but I wanted to share my thoughts on it. If it helps others potential players make a better decision in buying or scrolling past, then all the better. I sincerely hope Capcom, in the event of another remake, can do a better job and focus on what made Resident Evil/Biohazard great, and not follow the path they did to RE6.

The acting was varied from 7, RE2 and RE3. 7 was okay, RE2 was good, RE3 was somewhere between 7 and 2.

Gameplay? I personally think it is great that they used the game and gunplay from RE2. I thought that was the best part. Carlos's rifle loses a lot of accuracy after firing short bursts. One would think that he would have had some training in firing short bursts or something. Nemesis? Oh boy. Let me put it this way, Mr. X was scary and remained scary after I played RE2 for the seventh time. I feel as if the people who greenlit the idea to make Nemesis a demon dog thing after the first boss fight was focusing on what is "cool" rather than what is scary. I'm fine with the hermetically sealed trash bag look and the elongated teeth, but it's a bad sign when there is a mod of the original Nemesis model for download (last time I checked).

After all that, the biggest cherry on top for me is the lack of real thought provoking puzzles. The need of more action over puzzles has been a real drag when there's no fun for people who love puzzles like me. So I'll preface this review by saying: Unless you're a massive fan of Resident Evil and/or have a lot of money that you're willing to spend on a game, you should probably hold off on this one until a sale or they add more content, or both.

With that out of the way, I do genuinely like the game, the RE Engine is still really nice and the gameplay, while similar to RE2 Remake is still very good. I know that Capcom cut out a lot of story content such as the park and the clock tower, but if my memory serves me right they weren't necessarily major sections of the game, and Capcom did expand on certain sections of the game, primarily the Sewers and the Hospital. Capcom also added two new difficulties, Nightmare and Inferno, that provide a pretty significant challenge (unless you use the shop items, then it's really only the final boss).

That being said, the game just doesn't have 60 dollars worth of value in it. By this, I mean there are no specific rewards for beating the game on the highest difficulties with an S rank, and speaking of rank, Capcom removed the S+ rank that was in RE2 Remake, and I honestly don't know why. So there's no S+ rank, no specific rewards for completing the game on the highest difficulties, only ONE costume for Jill if you didn't preorder, and frankly Carlos' "costume" just changes his hair.

Overall, the game's story mode is enjoyable, though I find that Nemesis is sorely underutilized in this game, which is sad because the short amount of time that Nemesis actually chases you is really a strong point for the game. The lack of other content outside of the story is what really hurts it in my opinion. Hopefully, much like they did with RE2 Remake and it's Ghost Survivors mode, Capcom adds more free content in the future to add some more replayability, as after only 20 or so hours I've perfected the game in terms of achievements and in-game challenges.

I'm recommending this game because I thoroughly enjoyed it. BUT for anyone on the fence, I do not recommend it like it is and for its current price. I recommend this game on sale. Get this game on sale. DO NOT pay 60 bucks for it. They slap that price on there because it's a AAA title with amazing graphics. It's not a bad game, but not enough content to justify $60. Yes, it comes with a mulitplayer game, but the single player experience should be just as worth it.

The bonus unlockables like infinite ammo guns has a much better system than RE2, which was absurdly hard and annoying. RE3 actually made me want to go back and play to get them.

The gameplay is improved with a dodge mechanic. It's a little clunky, but better than RE2, and I know it's a remake so it should be like the original, but I feel like some things could be changed if they make it better. The characters in the RE2 and RE3 control like garbage, and for no reason at all.

Visually stunning, I would say better than RE2. The characters look amazing and Nemesis is incredibly cool, not just with his design but his mechanics. Mr. X fast walking to you is terrifying enough, but this tyrant runs, leaps ahead of you, trips you with a whip, and uses weapons.

That being said, Mr. X is scarier. Why? Nemesis is not an ever-present threat as he is made out to be, not "relentlessly pursuing" the player. You can't hear his loud footsteps like Mr. X or anything, he's not always in the area. In fact, if you go far enough away, he just Spider-Mans away. The only time he's used perfectly is in the area from the demo. The rest of the encounters with him are scripted, super easy to run away from, and boss fights, which also aren't as hard as you'd think with one of the most notoriously unkillable monstrosities in Resident Evil history. Mr. X is dynamic, he's always looking for you and can pop around any random corner. Nemesis cannot, you always know EXACTLY where he'll be. Nemesis is supposed to be the selling point of this game, and he just isn't used as best as he could or should be. Mr. X is a better stalker and ever-present threat.

The story is fine, it's what you'd expect from Resident Evil. I never played the original so I don't know what's different, so it wasn't a let down like it was for others. All in all, I personally still liked this game, more than RE2 I would say. The level design is not as good, but I felt crowded at times in RE2.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this game. The amount of content cut from the original is staggering. It is more than just being short. (most classic RE games can be speedrun through) Cutting many of those levels far from "streamlining", it just disposes of the actual survival horror gameplay this thing was supposed to remake and modernize. Apart from two areas, one of them being the Downtown included in the demo, the rest of the game is pitifully linear without the puzzles and gathering of key items in the open areas peppered with enemies to hinder you. And speaking of enemies let's get to what was supposed to be the STAAAARs of the show:

[h1]Nemesis who?[/h1]
See, the original Resident Evil 3 had its subtitle Nemesis. For good reason, as this hulking B.O.W. singlemindedly pursued its one objective: hunt down the members of STAAAAARS. That means you. Nemesis was the stalker nightmare realized, appearing at various scripted parts of the game with the intent of hindering your progress as you played in the Resident Evil formula mentioned above. While mostly scripted, the devs made a good enough work of disguising the fact and adding unpredictability via the original game's branching system. 

Why am I mentioning the 1999 version of this character so much? To better explain how he disappoints here. I like his redesign, but guess what, if you played the demo, you saw almost everything of Nemesis in his stalker form. The rest of the game is scripted chase sequences, QTE and boss fights galore, as far as he is concerned. This takes away the feeling of being dynamically pursued by this thing. Defenders of the game point to the fact that OG Nemesis was also scripted. This is true as said above, but they fail to realize or mention that Mr X last year in the Remake of 2 had way more screen time and that his freeform stalking section, the RPD, was considerably more elaborate and longer than RE3r's Downtown Raccoon City. Which leads me to...

[h1] Is the game too short? [/h1]
Yes, but classic Resident Evils were short, too. Hell, the game rewards speedrunning after your first trek through this gutted version of RC, just like Remake 2 did, just as it was in the originals. However, while the shop items and the unlockable NIGHTMARE and INFERNO difficulties add some semblance of replayability, the base experience seems lackluster compared to its predecessor. Why is that? In my opinion it is because the remake cuts many explorable areas available in the original that you could briefly explore and progress through in classic RE fassion. 3 being the more action-oriented of the original trilogy is no excuse to "streamline" the kind of gameplay that made RE what it is and the fact that, well, those areas were there twenty years ago. And they are missin here.

[h1] The Good [/h1]
All the above ranting might make it seem like I hate this game. I don't. I have been having fun with it all throughout my 20+ hours and I plan to 100% this ♥♥♥♥♥. So let's talk about the positives.

Presentation is a big one. The RE engine continues to amaze me with its photorrealistic rendering of both classical characters and monstrosities. While much of the city you explored was scrapped, what is here looks great and the hospital got a much welcome expansion in level design and art direction. 

The story and characters benefit from the reimagined treatment, too. The ham is gone for the most part, although the story does feel like an action movie, and the side characters actually feel like people. Jill herself is shown as strong and likeable and even suffering from her experience in RE1, although that angle of her arc is not mentioned much after the intro sequence. I will also echo many reviewers and players in praising the reimagined version of this games deuteragonist, Carlos. This dude is great as our secondary protagonist this time around, in stark contrast to his original iteration which was only kind of there. His small arc and his banter with Jill are very charming, and I already see fans asking for more of him going forward.

This is not a bad game, but it is both a disappointing reimagining which cuts a lot of the original and IMO is less bang for your buck than Remake 2 was. That game had the Nemesis we deserved here. Get it discounted if you are a fan.

- Game is incredibly short! It's probably a 5-6 hour game on Standard difficulty unless you're really taking your time.
- They removed a lot of key locations that would have been nice to see updated. [spoiler] Clocktower, Gas Station, Park and the Gravedigger fight come to mind. [/spoiler]
- Inferno [spoiler] stage 3 Nemesis [/spoiler] difficulty spike is insane compared to the rest of the game.

tldr; Resident Evil fans will love this new take on a much loved entry to the series. But, it's such a short game that the price tag isn't justified. Bottom line.. Wait for a sale!

Although it uses the Resident Evil 2 remake as a base, the 2020 remake of Resident Evil 3 is an altogether different beast. Whereas Resident Evil 2 revolves around interconnected areas, Resident Evil 3 rarely revisits locales and is generally linear. RE2's Mr. X is an unpredictable threat who will wander around the police station randomly for hours, while RE3's Nemesis is confined to scripted events. RE2 emphasizes expanding on its original game, while RE3 cuts out content from its own original game and instead comes bundled with a brand-new multiplayer game. And RE2 has a largely straightforward presentation, while RE3 is more stylish with first-person sequences and slow motion.

Sooooo....here I completed the game in 06:06:04 and spent some time reading all sorts of complaining about how this game's shorter than the original game, how much content they cut and all this same complaining from thread to thread.

Given that I played the original last time like 10+ years ago, I decided it was worth spending time to RE-play the game to compare and figure out why so many people keep complaining about new one.

Disclaimer: I have no intend to say that original game is worse than remake - we love original game regardless of anything - don't take my words as an attempt to say that the original is bad or anything.

So, some people claim that this game is shorter than the original. (I'll say it now: I'm not that hardcore player who can beat RE game in 10 minutes with no saves and avoiding any incoming damage from anyone/anything. I'm sort of average player). This game took me 06:06:04 for first play through (hardcore) and I took my time, run around a bit, died a few times - usual stuff.

Then I RE-played the original and guess what: 04:55:21. I stood my ground against Nemesis at RPD front door and up until DF disposal room (except for mandatory fights) I was running from him since he always appeared in narrow corridors and I don't feel that masochistic to fight the monster when you can't properly dodge his attack or grab.

Given that I've been playing using PS1 emulator with DS4, it took me some time to configure it and until I did it, I suffered from emulator's freezes what made me use save states (which didn't work properly either, lol). But regardless of my suffering, I was using kind of hack for some time along with regular writer saves, so let's add 40 mins to my original's play through.

So: 06:06:04 (hardcore) vs 05:35:21 (hard mode).

Btw, about his 'chasing'. He doesn't chase you in the original...like, at all. Sure he moves with you from room to room, but he appears mostly behind you when you're either far enough to ignore him or near the door to again ignore him. He 'chase' 2 rooms from the spawn point and then live you alone. You can even go back to locations to take what you need. Even if he 'chase' you longer, you can just run past him - you don't need to spend ammo/herb on him if you don't want to.

Regarding 'cut content'. New game lacks 

Locations: restaurant, news office, city hall, clock tower, park, d̶e̶a̶d̶ ̶f̶a̶c̶t̶o̶r̶y̶

Restaurant is where Jill met Carlos for the first time. It doesn't have any other reason to exist. Well, and give you 2 more gun powder A if you short on handgun ammo while in new game their meeting moved to the very beginning when Carlos saved Jill from Nemesis for the first time

City Hall exists only to be another 20 secs corridor between tram/gas station and previous game part. Well, you take the battery from Warren's statue, but it's not really usual place to take batteries from... and it looks really dumb - not that anybody cared back then or now, but it's a fact!

Clock tower is the most mentioned area people are angry about...lack of it. But it's 20 mins running with the first puzzle in game: clock pictures. Park is another location mentioned a lot. It exists only for making you fight Grave digger and drop some info how evil Umbrella was, to establish observation point and some useless Nikolai's dialogue about how everything went wrong and they're white and fluffy.

Dead factory is still in game but is called NEST 2 and its cover far better than originals with its: 'disposal factory under the guise of abandoned factory' - where unlucky bystanders disappear - of course it was operating and nobody raised any question when more and more people disappear.

What game brings:

4) Nikolai's character is still greedy bastard what game reminds us each time he appears on scene. Not through a few pages of text, but with character and game does good job making us hate him, what helps to get more satisfaction to know he died in the nuclear blast.

Tyrell is actual Carlos' partner, instead of just dead body with a hand grenade and actually wanna help.

Murphy meets the same fate, the difference is that instead of showing how good Carlos was, games shows how bad's Nikolai.

So, new games tightens character together, makes them more interesting to observe and more people in general. And brand new character - Nathaniel Bard which removes that stupid plot twist when a mercenary only knows how to pull the trigger creates vaccine for Jill. Of course machine were producing vaccine agent in automatic mode, but I wonder how much knowledge he possesses to mix vaccine base and vaccine agent to create proper vaccine from the virus infected Jill.

Game in general is tightened gameplay of the original without useless locations and enemies you skipped anyway.

Regarding puzzles: there is ONLY ONE PUZZLE IN GAME and this is clock pictures puzzle. The rest is cute time grab, but unless you have mental problem you're not going to spend more than 3 mins on each: music box, vaccine mixing, water drain in park, water quality check - they doesn't require real brain activity.

This last installment in the REmake (get it?) trilogy is a fitting end. 

Resident Evil HD Remake was pure fan service. Tank controls, slow dreary atmosphere, back and forth puzzle solving, everything fans who grew up on the originals would ever want.

Resident Evil 2 Remake was sort of the middle grounds. The game still made you pace yourself,  you felt very vulnerable throughout the campaign, but the over-the-shoulder and free-aim mechanics gave it a depth that fans of newer gen shooters will enjoy.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is the other side of the spectrum. While there were parts that got my heart racing and adrenaline going, I can't really say it was "scary". This entry  was more action oriented than the others, but not as bad as say RE5 (still a good game, just not scary) The dodge mechanic makes you feel like a god among zombies. It would be one thing if the dodge was optional, but you essentially have to master it to get through some of the encounters. Then you rely on it and soon enough your barrel-rolling past zombie after zombie. There is some replay value for trophy hunters and some unlockables to grind, but sadly the costumes you can unlock are much less than the original RE3. I have a feeling there are some updates to add more content like they did with RE2 Remake. This one was also much more linear, but overall I very much enjoyed it.

And I honestly feel, meh about the whole thing. 

The gameplay is still solid, the graphics are beautiful, and the voice performances are well done. But yet, I could not help thinking that something was missing. The game is very short, while my "on record" time says 6.7 hours, two of those hours are from me sitting at the menu while eating dinner or doing various other shenanigans. I clocked in at around 4 hours and 2 minutes. I almost finished this in a sitting. 

 My other big issue is Nemesis himself. Yes he is a constant threat throughout the game, but not in the way you expect. He only actually stalks you around the first area of the game. After that area, every encounter with him leads to a chase scene of sorts or a boss fight. Mr.X from RE2 did more actual stalking then Nemesis did, which made him a more constant threat.

Overall I feel as if Resident Evil 3 should have been a DLC add on for 2, rather than its own thing. Far too short, and too many re-used assets for $60. So at that price, I can not recommend for anyone except maybe the hardcore RE fans. Wait for a sale, or price drop. Trust me.

[h1][i]A small note: I received this game as a birthday present and not via Curator Connect.[/i][/h1] 

Resident Evil series are near and dear to my zombie-loving heart. They bring together all necessary elements. Action? Check! Attractive characters with interesting backgrounds? Check! Mind-blowing (sometimes) plot twists? Check! Hoards of zombies to kill? Oh yeah, baby! And lots of secrets to discover and puzzles to solve. 

So, as you can see, I am quite biased when talking about these games. But I also have high expectations of them, so any kind of downsides are immediately noticed too. What about remake of Resident Evil 3? Did it live up to the hype? Well…

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2049833898

[h1]Story[/h1]

☢️ [i]The most interesting part about RE3 is that its story takes place in two different lines – the first half tells us about events before RE2, while the second part focuses on the pinnacle of the battle two days after Leon and Claire’s adventures. This way we can see the beginning of Racoon City demise and its actual end – a pretty spectacular one, I should say. [/i]☢️

The T-virus has infected citizens of the famous Procyonidae city; law enforcement teams were annihilated pretty fast, and now survivors have to hide from living dead roaming the streets. 

Jill Valentine has been investigating the massacre that took place in the mysterious mansion during events of Resident Evil when she receives a call from her S.T.A.R.S. friend Brad Vickers. Unfortunately, he is two minutes too late because right at this moment Jill is attacked by Nemesis, the deadly weapon of Umbrella Corporation. This company has never shied away from dirty tricks and now it wants all S.T.A.R.S. members dead. A bad day for Jill, to say the least.  

Only thanks to Carlos Oliveira, a member of Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service, Jill manages to run away. Now she has to join forces with her enemy’s hounds to survive Racoon City and find out the truth behind Umbrella’s activities. And maybe find the vaccine along the way.

 [h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Most of the time you will play as Jill, but at some point, the gameplay will switch to Carlos with his own weapons and tricks. This is a rather refreshing experience because Carlos has a more convenient arsenal to deal with waves of undead monsters. At the same time, I find it really sad that you cannot play the whole campaign from his perspective like it was is RE2 – there you could take the role of either Leon or Claire and see what each of them did during various chapters. In case with RE3, you will never find out what Carlos actually was up to at the time Jill was running away from Nemesis. This also negatively affects the overall length of the game: the whole campaign takes just about 6-7 hours. After it you only have extra challenges and more difficult regime, but nothing new story-wise. For a game that costs so much (2000 rubles in my case), this is concerning. 

The Tyrant [i](my worst nightmare)[/i] is replaced with Nemesis, an even bigger guy with way better weapons to deal with poor Jill. He will haunt you in every way possible often accompanied by zombie goons; and this guy really likes unpleasant surprises – you cannot even imagine what he is capable of! Still, Nemesis never had the same effect on me as Tyrant. Maybe being followed by a deadly creature has lost its novelty after RE2 or maybe the music was not as impressive, but something was off. At least for me. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2050834882

Speaking of the battles, there are a few noticeable improvements. First, Jill can evade attacks completely by dodging them – just press the necessary button (Shift in my case) + direction, and our girl will slide away like a pro. If only Leon knew the same tricks! Carlos is more brutal in this part, and instead of evadsion he prefers direct attacks with his fist. Second, Nemesis himself has become more creative: instead of just walking slowly, he can run way faster than Jill or – the horror! – use his tentacle hand [i](Japanese and their love for the dubious part of octopus…)[/i] to attack from far away. He is also more aggressive and can rip Jill’s throat apart, bite her or through her on the ground. Third, there are completely new types of enemies. One sight of the spider-like creature is worth million curses, and its special ability is nasty to say the least – it catches Jill and inserts lots of smalls bugs into her throat. And the last novelty is the ability to explode some items: red barrels and electrical generators, for example. Saves the day each time you have to face huge amounts of zombies. 

At the same time, there is no great variety in common zombies’ design. Almost each part of the city is inhabited by the same people, so their faces will be imprinted in your memory by the end of the game for sure. You will once again meet the Dobermans – quite dead ones – and policemen, too. Among the new abominations I can mention only three: the spiders, the Hunters (big brutes with lots of armor) and blob fish. Yes, with lots of teeth, but still ugly.  

Speaking of puzzles, there are very few, sadly. Compared to the previous part, RE3 focuses more on battles and running rather than thinking. You will need some smart strategies for more difficult regimes, yes, but this is different from finding solutions to tricky locks.

[h1]Overall Presentation[/h1]

Oh, this part truly shines in many aspects. Visuals are amazing – if you use high settings, even Jill’s hair and small pebbles on the ground look quite realistic. Cutscenes are well-made and I did not notice any glitches. The style is similar to the one you saw in RE2, so if you have already played it, you know what to expect. Everything has been properly updated compared to the initial game from 1999. At the same time, I think I noticed some zombies moved strangely at times – some of them really liked standing in the corner and looking at the wall; other twitched like dancers on the scene in a nightclub. These occasions were quite rare and looked more funny than annoying. Also, they did not affect the overall gameplay.

Soundtracks are also great and create an amazing atmosphere of dread and suspicion. The only one I did not quite like was the main theme for Nemesis – it could have been more ominous, to be honest. 

And the last small note: I did not like Carlo’s new design at all. He looks like some homeless hobo desperately in need of a hairdresser. So I switched him to the original design immediately. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2049832375

[h1]My Verdict[/h1]

The main problem of Resident Evil 3 is its length – about 7 hours for such a price? Not a good deal, if you ask me. The story just ties up all the loose ends left by RE2 and tells a bit more about the very beginning of disaster. Another thing I have noticed: compared to RE2, this part of the series throws you right into action. In Leon’s story you had some time to get used to the madness; Jill barely has such a luxury – she must fight from the very beginning, and not just with minor enemies, but with a pretty brutal assassin after her head. Which once again proves my idea that RE3 remake feels more like a DLC for RE2 rather than its own game. 

On the other hand, if you are craving for some zombie apocalypse, then RE3 will be your oasis. The gameplay is smooth, the visuals are an eye-candy, and the main characters are quite memorable. It was a lot of fun to go through the main campaign; if only it was longer! 

To sum up, I can recommend Resident Evil 3 Remake on 50% sale to hardcore fans of RE series and people who like shooting zombies in scary environment. If you are completely new to it, better start with some earlier and cheaper titles – or you risk missing on important parts of the plot.

Now that a week has past, the main brunt of reviewers and echo chambers have said their thing about Resident Evil 3, let me say as a fan of Resident Evil (having the og RE3 being one of my favorite RE games and the remake being my most anticipated of this year) and currently watching Capcom put out solid games, Resident Evil 3 remake is a solid game. Is it better than Resident Evil 2 remake? No. Is it better than the original RE3: Nemesis? No. Is it disappointing in places that are reasonably been said by people ie cut content? Sure. Is it enough to roast the game and call it a cash grab? No.

I think the best way to look at RE3 is that it is almost a exact repeat of its past but in a modernize level. The original RE3 being a spin off turned full game at the last minute prompted many critics and fans to also criticize the game for it's short length and lack of content. The short length of the remake has an easy thing to say on the surface: "it should be longer than 5-6 hours!" But I find it also hilarious when so called "fans" of the original forget a few things. The first of which is RE3 remake doesn't need a live selection to make replay value. Just because you change up a scenario that plays out doesn't mean it's necessarily better or even necessary. A well made action game doesn't need fluff rather a straight forward experience with great pacing (ie RE4) There are five difficulties that all change up enemy placements, item placements, even typewriters and item box placements that add replay value. Considering this game is more action focused akin to say Devil May Cry with perfect dodges and counters over survival aspects like defensive items in RE2R and RE1R, I refuse to look at this as a "horror game". Even the original I was never scared of the game. Yes Nemesis was intimidating and made engagements tense but he is largely in the position of being the focus and actual nemesis of the plot. Here (while I will admit doesn't show up enough to really harass you) he is just fine with how he was handled. 

He is more focused on scripted set pieces but to me this makes way more sense than being fully loose throughout the whole game. After finishing Inferno and Nightmare mode a few times, it would be literally impossible for Nemesis to work like the original (and mind you in OG he too was limited to scripted moments too sooo) because his speed and power would frustrate players more than empower them. The whole point of RE3 thematically is to show Jill Valentine is overcoming her trauma from the mansion incident and is forced into a desperate escape and struggle throughout. And in the remake she is handled I think great. Some shots like her emerging from the car powerless to Nemesis just walking through the flames to the climax ending the way it does shows Jill overcomes her greatest threat. She is cut up and hurt over the course of the game and by the end feels like she is a badass much like the original. 

Yes things have been changed significantly from the original in the remake but to say this game is bad for cut content is ludicrous. The grave digger boss in the park was an unnecessary boss fight in the og along with the padded out park level itself. The worms are back as Hunter Gammas (there mandibles opening up and sliding out of the sewer drains being a clear reference) and they are more enjoyable to deal with as a result. No spiders but drain deimos practically were in the original but fitted as discount lickers. Seeing that combination in one section though stinks but having them amidst Nemesis or Lickers on higher difficulties would be a disaster waiting to happen so it's probably a necessary evil to only have them for one part and that's it. Clocktower cut is a reasonable criticism as I feel they could make exploring that possible with Stage 2 Nemesis being what it is. That said, the place was not very big or complicated in the first place and its over before it really even gets interesting to me in the original.

Jill's redesign has gotten some flak from some people but to me it's perfect. I have always seen Jill Valentine as the Ellen Ripley of the Resident Evil franchise: A young woman who holds her own ground and overcomes just as much as anyone else. Her mannerisms and tone in this game is surprisingly great. Carlos too also has been redesigned and he is also great. Their dynamic was one of the underrated gems of the original game and here (while not groundbreaking or anything) is solid. Strictly film speak, RE3 has a classic three act structure and while normally Capcom games have poor writing in them, RE3 remake has fairly competent writing so long as you accept the typical liberties of RE plots. The dialogue between Carlos and Jill is great and the lengths goes to save Jill is wholesome and badass that you get to experience. 

Graphically the game is excellent sans less gore effects compared to RE2R. Optimization is mostly solid with some hitches and hiccups when lots of assets are on screen in cutscenes or gameplay. The music in this is great and would argue beats the original by a mile. Perhaps RE2R's criticism for lackluster music sans Mr. X's themes prompted a action focused score, and it is actually well done. Like I said the writing and pacing of the remake is very good and well done so to imply it lacks content because you didn't want to play other modes feels irrelevant to me. Every game prior to RE4 (with RE7 being a return to those roots and run time) were always short games and with the current gaming landscape gravitating towards bloated, lackluster grindfests, RE3 at least makes great enough gameplay to coast on its flaws and successes much easier. 

The unlockables are still there like concept art, models, and weapons (purchased in a shop by beating challenges), the different difficulty modes are there, the game honestly is getting way too much flak for something that people have been jaded by over the years. Could this game be given another year to be ironed out (chiefly Stage 3 Nemesis being a lackluster fight overall)) Sure. Could more be added to it to make it "better"? Yeah but the more a game adds to itself the easier it can be criticized for the pacing (a big deal to me). Is it worth $60? Well for stans and "fans" of og RE3 that claim this is a cash grab proceeded to get og RE3 for 40+ bucks at launch, price is irrelevant since I could put 50 hours in and feel satisfied with the game and not even play Resistance to say it's worth $60. Is it the best RE game I was expecting? Hell no and there are flaws in this game that border on cheapness but is saved by a good story, good music, good pacing, good combat and good challenge. It's a fun mess that I feel is being attacked unfairly by people solely because it was seen as a short game or was cut alot in content to make work. Remember a remake/reimagining's whole point is to change up the original however is deemed necessary. If I wanted what fans are complaining about is missing from the og, I'd rather play the og. Give something new and different a chance. Besides despite the criticisms of the og originally, it turned out a great game and top 5 RE game for fans in retrospect, so watch this will be the same in a decade. Plus even on sale or not, It's a really good game that just shows Capcom have been on a roll. It's not a 10/10 but it doesn't need to be. I just enjoyed it for what it is and that's really all was needed.

I think the first, and most important, thing I can say about this game is that it was tremendously fun and I loved my time with it. If you're an RE fan I think this is a great experience and I personally got my values worth from it. The action horror pace and feel is very different from RE2, which was mostly horror that felt slightly more action in the end. This game feels like that ending from the start, more ammo, more enemies and a great dodge mechanic that makes bosses feel way more engaging, no more G2 BS on a tiny platform where slightly bad guessing of his movement meant nearly unavoidable hits. If that sounds good to you then buy it and have fun!

With that said I can't ignore the reason reviews for this game haven't been as favorable as RE2; the game is short, and beyond the single campaign scenario there isn't any bonus unlockable levels like 4th Survivor or anything. Maybe we will see some added in the future (like The Ghost Survivors was,) but I'm not holding my breath on that one. What we do get is; upon completing Hardcore mode you receive Nightmare mode. And upon beating that you receive Inferno.

Nightmare mode feels like this games true hardcore mode. Feel like Nemesis was too easy to knock down? A single grenade won't work anymore. Think Jill/Carlos had a lot of health for Hardcore? Get ready to go from Fine to Danger from single hits. Nightmare isn't just a harder version of the campaign though. Anyone familiar with RE7's Madhouse mode will feel familiar here. It is the same basic campaign in structure, but enemies appear in greater numbers early on, and harder enemies appear even earlier on top of there speed and attack increases. 

My first playthrough on Hardcore took me about 6 hours including cutscenes and a few deaths. It was a fun as hell ride with great pacing that to me never had a dull moment and didn't overstay it's welcome. For the second run I played nightmare and it felt like the true RE experience, ammo was always a worry, healing wasn't in abundance and enemies felt like a true threat. It was the perfect experience after loving RE2, except for one major part that felt extremely overtuned considering how great it was until then. The final boss on Nightmare is surely balanced around using some of the NG+ unlockables. Without them you can be stun locked and 2 hit in a matter of seconds. I'm not claiming its undoable (skilled enough players will prevail,) but the final boss felt like it jumped right in at the end from Inferno mode to ruin your death count last minute. Besides that blunder it was still amazingly fun and with an item for slightly easier perfect dodges it became a far more balanced fight.

Inferno mode is Nightmare on steroids, every enemy can take you from full health to low danger in one hit. They're fast as hell and tanky to match. It was clearly made to fill two roles; true masochists who want the hardest challenge the game can provide, and people who have invested in unlocking a lot of the NG+ items, to the point that it feels like Nightmare damage/health wise and the only real change is enemy speed and no auto saves. It's good fun and a welcome final challenge. Just note that if you're going for that 100% there is one major unlock that can trivialize even this mode, so don't fret if it sounds unfun.

And to try and conclude my rambling reviews without spoiling anything, I think the story is good fun, not mind blowing, but it is campy RE after all. Jill has been my favorite character in the series since I started playing them and I think this Jill is amazing, the model/VA they used was great and her dialogue was perfect to me. She isn't scared and inexperienced like Leon or Claire, she made it out of the Mansion after all! She is a badass that can hold her own, and even when Nemesis is giving his all to murder her, she talks to him like an annoying stalker, not a massive bioweapon that makes Mr. X feel trivial in comparison. On the subject of our stalking friend; I found his balance to be pretty good, early on he will relentlessly pursue you though the streets that can get your heart racing when he shows up with a roar and start sprinting to give Jill a punch into next week. But this pursuing Nemesis ends about as fast as he appeared. He then becomes more scripted in encounters but they still feel good as chases and bosses. I agree with many people that there could've been a little more of the early style Nemesis but I think the devs new this could get overwhelming for some players and would've required a decent amount of changes to the story. 

The game is, as I said, incredibly fun and no doubt worth playing. But depending on your preferences on replaying a game and if you care about Resistance, it's likely better to buy it on sale later :)

As a final note; the costumes are lacking, there's only one unlockable one in game between both characters. Its my favorite costume but come on, the other 2 being pre-order only is terrible considering the lack of any others in game. Thank Nexus for the modding community I guess, cause it's unlikely capcom will just add more for free.

It's not garbage or awful, but it needs some major improvements to be a mode worth really getting into for me.

A remake well done. There's some controversy surrounding this one and I completely get it. 

-It's too short
-Not enough classic RE Puzzles
-A lot and I mean A LOT of creative liberties were taken with the story
-Missing areas from the original (looking at you Park, but GOD do I not miss that area. But I did really like the clock tower section and was saddened to see it wasn't in the remake ;,[  )
-Certain sequences have been flipped around ( Carlos at the police station?? etc)

Though there are some glaring downsides, I think the game overall came out great.
The gameplay is phenomenal. Excellently optimized, the game runs buttery smooth on my setup and looks absolutely gorgeous (i7 9700k/RTX 2070 Super 8GB/16GB RAM).
I'd say it's a slight upgrade over last year's RE2 remake graphically. RE3 for sure runs smoother than RE2 with the exact same settings.
Speaking of the RE2 remake, this game plays almost identically to that one and the police station was ripped straight out of it, like the classics. There are some nice quality of life improvements to the engine in regards to the GUI and everything which is nice. 

This game also has the dodge mechanic just like the OG RE3. Takes a second to figure out how it works but once you get it down, the whole game becomes a whole lot easier. Although I found it a bit harder to land Carlos's evade punch. I prefer this system over the knife/grenade escape system from the last game, which I felt interrupted the flow a bit. 
RE3 is definitely more action oriented, and that is evident as soon as you boot up the game. 
Plenty of ammo littered across raccoon city and its various environments, so you shouldn't really find yourself in a pinch for ammo very often, if at all. 
On top of that, it's also very linear. There is a TINY BIT of backtracking here and there and some of it is even optional towards the end of the game, but it's nowhere near as bad as RE2. 

The story has been decently modified but I believe that's so it'd tie in better with the RE2 remake. You should ABSOLUTELY play that first before you play this if you want to experience the story the way it was intended. It doesn't do much to catch you up, but you can kind of get a good idea on what's going on if you take the time to read all of the documents you can find. 
It's not quite the same as the original, but it ties in very nicely with the last game and actually explains a good amount of how things happened at the police station, which I really loved. 

Nemesis is absolutely terrifying. As he SHOULD be. He is entirely scripted but man, for the short time he chases you I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my pants. Unlike Mr X from last year's game, Nemesis can sprint and knows the layout of the entire city. He can run off at any moment and suddenly land in front of you or behind you. Or he can cut you off sprinting out of an alleyway up ahead. One thing I love about nemesis in this game is that even though he's mostly scripted, when he chases you through raccoon city early in the game, he isn't on a set path. He just chases you until he's stopped or you get to your objective. (which is pretty easy but he only gets stunned for like 2-3 minutes). He can also use weapons so that's fun. 
The boss fights with nemesis are cool but I don't think they're as good as the original boss fights. Towards the end he reminded me more of a final boss character you'd see in final fantasy than something you'd see in a classic RE game, but it was still cool nonetheless. 

Overall I think this game is a bit easier than your typical Resident Evil title, due to the sheer amount of ammo everywhere and its length. Of course hardcore, nightmare, and inferno modes are waiting for you after you beat it the first time if you REALLY want a challenge, but even then there's a shop on the main menu where you can use in game credits to get infinite ammo, etc. That combined with the evade mechanic kind of breaks the difficulty in half. You can make any enemy in the game look like a joke with evade. I'd say the replay value is definitely there, there's a good amount of collectibles to get and the harder difficulties + the aforementioned shop. 




TL;DR
While it isn't 100 percent faithful to Resident Evil 3: Nemesis, it does its job (which is to be a remake of a fan favorite RE game) and it does it well. It's a different raccoon city but it's all so familiar, and there are plenty of nods to the original. 

BUT, I don't think you should spend 60 dollars on this game unless you're a diehard RE fan looking for a nice dose of nostalgia. There were some apparent shortcomings but I think the game perfectly makes up for it with its visuals, slightly reworked story (which ties in very nicely with the RE2 remake if you played that), gunplay, sound design, etc etc etc. Capcom did a pretty good job with this, but it leaves a bit to be desired. I'd give it a 7.5/10, wait till it goes on sale.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is a game that does a great job of improving on many of the more superficial aspects of the original game and taking some of the things that made RE2 Remake good, while doing a poor job with some of the more intricate aspects that were what made the original so characteristic. If Steam gave me a neutral choice for whether I recommend this game or not, that'd be the one I'd go for, because the thing is that this game doesn't do a whole lot of bad. It's just that it doesn't do a whole lot of great either, especially for those people who played the original RE3. Since I only have two choices, I believe a thumbs down better reflects my thoughts.

A good starting point for getting into why I think this remake isn't all that great would be to state what made the original RE3 (which I'll refer to simply by RE3 from here on) so beloved by some, and also some of its problems. To begin with, RE3 wasn't the big hit back in the day as much as RE2 was. It was criticized for being far more linear than its predecessor, for being shorter and lacking in as much replay value, and for its wonky implementation of a Quick Dodge mechanic, since Capcom wanted to make a game that was more action-oriented; this mechanic required precise timing but could end up doing nothing to save you from taking damage anyway despite having executed it correctly. 

On the other hand, the game broke ground by introducing one of the most infamous antagonists in video game history in the form of Nemesis. Nemesis quickly became known for being one of the most terrifying enemies in a horror game because of how you came to realize that he was specifically targeting you, how he had nigh-invincibility, his ability to pop up seemingly everywhere you went, his ability to ignore loading screens in the form of doors to a certain degree, and even his use of weapons with his rocket launcher, all when most enemies that had been seen previously in the RE games had none of this. For anyone that's played RE3, one of the moments you likely remember the most was Nemesis breaking in through the window while you were in the RPD and which introduced you with a "show, don't tell" approach to most of those traits I mentioned previously, making for a moment that made you know what true horror is like.

Now, of course, this being 1999 when RE3 released, Nemesis' behavior could only go so far because of the technological limitations of the era. What I mentioned about Nemesis going through doors is restricted to only a couple specific ones, and he has to do it when the camera isn't looking at the door he supposedly comes through (he's just spawned next to it instead to simulate him going through). Not only that, but despite him seemingly showing up randomly even if you played the game more than once, you'd eventually come to realize that he was still heavily scripted and whether he'd show up on an area and not on another was dependent on how you had progressed through the game and what choices you had made, but it was ultimately predictable. This was fine, of course, for the limitations the game was restrained to, and Nemesis was still a force to be feared.

Having established that, I'd say most people who had played the original knew Nemesis was the most important factor to consider for RE3 Remake (RE3R from here on). I always like to say Nemesis is a big pool of potential for how much more terrifying and unleashed a proper remake could make him. Most people had already had a taste of this with Mr. X in RE2 Remake, with Mr. X now being much more unrestrained and less scripted than his counterpart in the original RE2 due to the remake making him freely roam the RPD looking for you, and even knowing where you are any time you fired a gun, making for a great risk versus reward system in that game.

So does Nemesis live up to what his potential could have allowed him? Sadly, no. I'd easily say Nemesis' incarnation in the remake is, in most aspects, worse than in the original. He did see some improvements, now being able to execute a high jump to land in front of whichever direction you are running just to block your way and force you to either execute a dodge or find another way to get where you were planning to go. Also, as with Mr. X in RE2R, Nemesis can now go through some doors (not all of them, though) and without getting interrupted by them as much as Mr. X did. These changes, on the surface, help him become more of a threat, sure, but the problem is that you only get to actually interact with Nemesis in a non-scripted environment during the latter half of your exploration of the city's streets. A section of the game, I may add, that is actually MUCH SMALLER and far less complex to navigate than in the original. Capcom made Raccoon City, at least in cutscenes, a much larger, more developed city, ripe for creating a very labyrinthine environment that could have seen Nemesis roaming about in much the same way Mr. X did around the RPD, only it could have been even better than that because Nemesis is supposed to be more intelligent and faster in his pursuit. What we instead got is something that feels even more scripted than it was in the original, with a much more on-rails approach because of how small the area of the city that you explore is, and it all happens for a much shorter period of time to boot. With this and the fact that you encounter him less times in the remake than in the original, it all adds up to make Nemesis not have anywhere as much impact as he did in the original. His final boss battle in the original was a proper culmination of all the times he had constantly made you miserable by interrupting your escape from the city, whereas in the remake, it feels generic.

And then there's not much else to say. With Nemesis relegated in importance, this game just doesn't have much else to stand on. The quick dodge is vastly improved and no longer feels inconsistent, and that's it. It's otherwise painfully short and does nothing innovative that RE2R didn't already make. Despite the fact that RE2R also changed or cut off some areas, and broke the enjoyment of playing A/B scenarios that were far more diverse in the original, at least it still did other plenty of good things that reflect my positive review of it. I believe RE2R is a great game to play despite the fact that it doesn't completely replace the original. This game, however? It shows rush and lack of proper attention, and I was left thinking I'd rather play the original than this one, and I'd advise others to do the same.

Does that mean it is all bad and not worth your time at all? No. It just means I think you should get this game once its base price is lower, and/or when it's on sale. It is not, however, worth 60 bucks.

Let me start by saying this a god awful remake. I've never seen a remake that tries so hard to ignore or otherwise rebel against the source material. While the Resident Evil 2 remake changed a lot, most of it was still recognizable as Resident Evil 2. This remake of RE3 deviates so far from the original that it doesn't qualify as a remake. To even call it a "reboot" would be too generous, as that implies there's a least some effort to follow in the footsteps of the original. They might as well as just branded this a completely new story that just happens take place in Raccoon City at the same as RE2/RE3.

That all being said, it's still a fine game for what it is as long as you don't expect it to actually remake RE3. At all. Also, the real reason I still recommend it is because despite its problems, it's important for us to still buy this game and send the message to Capcom's investors that we do want more remakes of classic REs as well as new REs that are in this style. (emphasis on horror over action) And if we get angry and refuse to buy this just because it wasn't the perfect remake we hoped for, Capcom's investors won't interpret that as "Oh ok, we changed too much in this remake and that's why people didn't like it" but instead will interpret it as "Ok people obviously don't want classic RE anymore".

Also, people are grossly exaggerating how short this game. Yes, it is shorter than the RE2 remake. There's no denying that. But not by nearly as much as people are making it out to be. My first playthrough of RE2R took about 10 hours, and my first playthough of RE3R took about 7 hours. Interestingly, speedruns of RE3R take just as long as RE2R. It is not RE2 Remake. In no way does it hit anywhere near the high points that RE2 Remake does. That said I wouldn't consider RE3 Remake a bad game. It's made great improvements, but sadly takes a few steps in the wrong directions. First off the campaign is short. I'm bad at horror games (even those that aren't scary) but my total play time for a single run is just under 4 hours. This was on standard mode and I collected nearly every item even back tracking when I missed something. This would not be a problem if it had multiple character stories like RE2 or even some bonus modes like the 4th survivor, making RE3 have significantly less content than RE2

On the terms of game mechanics I found the dodge a welcome edition which I'm sure the speed-running community will love. However from my experience they made limb shot to stagger less effective, removing any choice between spending ammo to fully kill a zombie, shoot it twice in the leg and run past, or potentially wasting medicin healing from trying to sprint past. This lead over to the items. The amount of ammo and health you gain is plenty, removing difficulty since if you sprinted past an enemy of two you'd have enough ammo to take out anything in your path. Perhaps this was a choice made by the game developer but I find it less fun if they take out the careful ressource management they had in RE2, where your choice of play style was constantly challange. I'm easily startled and thus tend to kill everything in my path as to reduce the scares. However in RE3 I was never truly scared. From my understanding this is also a case with the source material. I however find this focus from SURVIVAL action HORROR, to survival ACTION horror. It quite simply takes away from the game loop of RE2 and replaces it with action cutscenes, yet with a story that only last 4 hours something is left to be desired. I have also seen online reviewers praise Nemisis. Saying he's a "Better Mr. X" I woefully disagree. The comparison between the two is as fair as the comparison between the two remakes. The two game should be compared yet they have different approaches (where as I and I believe most others perfer RE2's approach). Mr. X is a constant threat that always looms over the playthrough (espeically when he shows up in the police station). He wanders the halls chasing you if he hears or sees you, however he is slow which adds to the scare of being chased. The sound of his boots right behind you (thanks to the excellent sound design) is intense and scary. Hearing him walk around on a different floor of the main hall is so uncomfortable there were points I couldn't go on (Remember I am easily scared). He feels much more invinsible. Meanwhile Nemisis puts on emphasis on action. Not only is he much faster, allowing little time to be scared, he is also much easier to kill in my opinion (perhaps because of the added armory of Jill and the amount of resources at your disposal). However I find Mr. X scary and Nemisis exciting. 

The comparison between RE2 and RE3 is obviously unfair. Each game sticks to the source material when it comes to it's approach to Survival Action Horror. By all means RE3 lives up to the quality of RE2. The graphics, sound design, enemy design and at some points the level design are all on par RE2. Yet because of it's game loop it, taking away a few layers of strategy it's a less enjoyable game. My biggest critizism is it's lack of content as of now. This is a 60 euro game, and as of now it does not justify that price tag for a 4 hour campaign. If this wasn't the follow-up to RE2 and you told me it had 4 hours of campaign I would have never bought it. Surely they will be adding extra modes but I cannot understand why they did not plan to release the game with those extra modes. Because of those 4 hours it feels cheap compared to RE2. 

I will not touch on RE Resistance as I do not believe most people buy RE3 for that addition. Personally I come to the RE series for a singleplayer survival horror experience, and I don't care too much about multiplayer.

I hope whoever made it this far in this review will understand my viewpoint. It is not a bad game. It is decent, not because of some huge horrible thing, but because the choices they took made it so. I still had a grand time and will no doubt be replaying it to get the inifite guns and such. RE2 and RE3 are different games I know but when making a series you need to compare to your previous entry to evaluate if you are taking steps in the right direction. I cannot see an RE4 remake on the horizon, so I hope they bring more of RE2 to RE8 than RE3 as I find it a superior experience due to it being more scare, more fun and more complex with strategy and puzzles.
