[i]It's been just over a year since Capcom has blessed us with Resident Evil 2 Remake, and even then, people were asking for more. They wanted to see Nemesis in glorious high definition, and Capcom has delivered. But is it as good as the original game that people remember and love? As a heads up, this review regroups both my opinion on Resident Evil 3 and Resident Evil Resistance.

Also potential spoilers?[/i]

[h1]RESIDENT EVIL 3[/h1]

[h2]PROS:[/h2]
- Let me just start by giving my [b]opinion[/b] on how long the game is. Yes, roughly five hours. Now look up any longplay, or average playtime for the original game, and you'll find out that they're surprisingly similar. Resident Evil games have always been rather short and intended for speedruns. The only thing that might have made the classics longer were the more in-depth puzzles, which I'll come back to, and the fact that games back then were generally more difficult. Again, this is my [b]opinion[/b], and you're free to disagree, especially if speedrunning isn't your cup of tea.

- The game still tries to encourage replayability, with two unlockable difficulties, and unlockable items for New Game+.

- While it follows the same story as the original for the most part, the game is far from being a 1:1 remake, and reimagines a lot of things. If you're looking for an experience similar to the original game, then you will not find that here. If you're open to a new experience though, or haven't played the original, then I'd say you'll have fun!

- Dodging is reintroduced from the original and expanded upon, and completely replaces defense items from RE2 Remake, which feels much more rewarding to me than simply pressing your Get Out of Jail Free Card™ button when you get grabbed.

- There are a few tributes to the original Resident Evil, such as the full motion opening cutscene and [spoiler]the cutscene that plays upon encountering the first Hunter Beta[/spoiler].

- The new character designs look absolutely fantastic, and Jill's not running through Raccoon City while wearing an inconvenient tube top and short skirt anymore. With that being said, Jill and Carlos' original appearances were available as preorder bonuses. Also Carlos isn't a recolor of Leon anymore. [strike]Also he's HOT.[/strike] [spoiler]also let's be honest, if you're here to see Jill being a bimbo with big polygons, you should probably find another type of game. or play the original.[/spoiler]

- No original game OST option this time around, but the new soundtrack offers a few pleasant surprises.

[h2]CONS:[/h2]
- With the game reimagining a lot of things, a lot of iconic moments from the original RE3 are nowhere to be seen. The Clock Tower's here alright, just don't expect to be exploring it.

- Back on puzzles from the first paragraph, they are almost completely absent in this reimagining. The only proper puzzle appears moments before the end of the game, and can just be easily bruteforced.

- Encountering Nemesis is much more scripted and predictable, which feels like a big downgrade from the original game.

- Mercenaries mode is, as of now, absent from the game, and technically replaced with Resistance. While not that much of an issue to me personally, I get why people would complain about that one, and I hope to see it come back as a (free?) DLC.

[h1]RESIDENT EVIL RESISTANCE[/h1]

[h2]PROS:[/h2]
- It's Resident Evil Mercenaries meets Dead by Daylight meets Tower Defense. And it's a fun concept. Survivor mostly plays like normal Resident Evil/Mercenaries gameplay, killing enemies and completing objectives to get extra time to escape the map. On the other hand, Mastermind plays like a Tower Defense strategy game, where inflicting damage on the survivors will take time away from them until you run out the clock and win. You can also take control of most of the creatures to deal out damage personally. Did someone say playable G-Birkin and Mr. X?

- At the time of writing this review, you get 6 Survivors, with Jill being added as part of a free content update on April 17th, and 4 Masterminds, all of them having unique abilities and counters, and they are fairly customizable, from alternative skills to passive equipment, as well as custom card decks and map layouts for Masterminds. There's also plenty of cosmetics available, ranging from alternative skins for Survivors, weapons and each type of creature, as well as Mastermind voice lines you can play whenever you want, and emotes for Survivors and zombies.

- Four maps as of now, with each one having its own theme. As said above, the items and enemies layout can be customized by the Mastermind, so you'll often get a different experience each time depending on the kind of player you're up against.

- Similarly to Resident Evil 3, the OST offers a few surprises, with remixes of G-Birkin and Mr.x's themes. The music that plays when time is running out is also one of my personal favorites.

- The game, while bundled exclusively with RE3 as of now, is completely standalone, which means you can uninstall one once you're done with it, and still be able to play the other. [spoiler]But let's be honest I should really just buy a new hard drive.[/spoiler]

[h2]CONS:[/h2]
- As it is a concept similar to Dead by Daylight, do not expect this game to ever be balanced properly if you want to have fun. Looking at you, January and Becca mains at the time of writing this review.

- Matchmaking times can be highly inconsistent for both sides, sometimes spending 10 minutes in a queue before even finding players. It also relies on your Steam download region, so feel free to try changing that up if you're having issues finding matches.

- It's a peer-to-peer game, and all it takes is a Mastermind having bad internet for the game to become unplayable.

- Really needs a report button, if only for the lagswitching MMs.

[h1]CONCLUSION:[/h1]
I personally like the fact that the Resident Evil 3 Remake tries to be different from its original counterpart, and I've been getting multiple runs in for personal giggles. Resistance is a fun alternative to Dead by Daylight if you can do your best to ignore the minor issues with it, though I understand why some people have bigger issues with that game.

Resident Evil 3 Remake... Where do I begin.
First of all, let me preface this by saying it's a good game.... A great game actually. However, I think it's a poor Remake, and overall an inferior product when compared to Resident Evil 2's Remake. This is Resident Evil 3 completely remagined; there are nods to the original in the form of a few scenes and set pieces, however you'll be hard pressed to find something that makes you go "hey, I remember that!"

The atmosphere and story beats are nothing like in the original game, rather, this game feels like the developers used the movie Resident Evil: Apocalypse for inspiration, rather than the original game. Resident Evil 3 Remake is very action heavy, and Jill's character is reminiscent of Lara Croft from 2016's Tomb Raider. Still a fun game, but I can't recommend it at its current price point, nor can I recommend it to those expecting a faithful remake.

Instead of making a very, VERY long review, below I will list the things I disliked and liked... SPOILERS BELOW, YOU'VE BEEN WARNED!

1. Gore/physics missing (in 3make, limbs just disappear when damaged, instead of being dismembered like in 2make).

2. Nemesis doesn't feel like an omnipresent threat whatsoever, he instead shows up a handful of times at predetermined points in the story... Compare that to the original, where he would seemingly show up sporadically depending on the route/choices you make. While both versions are scripted, I feel like the original Nemesis did a better job of making you feel pursued.

3. No branching decision mechanic... Definitely hurts the replayability of RE3R.

4. No clock tower, dead factory, graveyard (grave digger boss gone) or park... Some will argue these areas don't matter, and that dead factory is simply NEST 2 (the last area of RE3R), but I beg to differ. For one, Clock Tower was perhaps the most memorable location in RE3 (more on this in a bit), and Dead Factory was a facility designed specifically for waste disposal separate from NEST, while in the re-make it's a full blown laboratory complex for research and BoW creation (aka NEST), which is found beneath the hospital. Its entire purpose, design, and location is COMPLETELY different to Dead Factory, and is not comparable unless if your only point of comparison is the fact that it looks like a run-of-the-mill Umbrella facility, and has one or two things obscurely reminiscent of Dead Factory... Now back to Clock Tower for a second, yes, I know it didn't make much sense overall plot wise, but there had to be other ways they could've changed or added to the story to still incorporate Clock Tower and the segments thereafter. Overall, very disappointing to see these areas missing, and it definitely takes away from the atmosphere that was present in the original.

5. Like in RE2R, the original remodeled outfits are only available to those who pre-ordered, and likely will be purchasable later on. Very greedy move, and I very much dislike how they did that for a game advertised as a REMAKE!

6. Very short & bundled with Resistance to increase the cost of the end product. Nobody asked for Resistance, and it doesn't seem like very many want to play it anyway. Interesting concept, but should've been a standalone release. Now, there are some misunderstandings concerning Resistance & RE3R and I'll address that quickly. No, Resistance did not take away from the development time of RE3R, it was made by a separate company. Also, RE3R was developed alongside RE2R. I personally think RE3R was initially meant to be incorporated into RE2R (see Raccoon City bundle) to create one giant game, but instead opted to cut it out and sell them off piece meal.

7. Because we got Resistance, it likely influenced their decision to NOT include Operation Mad Jackal in RE3R... Very, very disappointing, considering the fact we got raid mode in RE2R. They did incorporate one element of Operation Mad Jackal into RE3R which was the shop, where you can unlock items in subsequent playthroughs. Still incredibly disappointing, as Mad Jackal is many people's favorite version of raid mode (myself included), and would've been amazing in the new engine with the freshly re-implemented dodge mechanic. Here's hoping they decide to add it as free DLC (doubtful).

8. As you can guess from the cut areas and segments, the story's been drastically changed, and the flow/order of events has been basically scrambled up... We have a much longer hospital section as a result, and fairly extensive NEST 2 to traverse. Furthermore, he new story actually ties into RE2R, which I think is a very welcomed change from the original which barely tied into RE2. It really goes to show that this remake was developed as a companion piece to RE2R, and that isn't a bad thing.

9. It's a very short game, and definitely leaves you hungry for more. This game on average seems to clock in at over 3-1/2 to 4 hours without cut scenes on the first playthrough, which is very short for its price tag. It's still a thoroughly enjoyable game, but I don't think it's worth 60 bones (90 for my Canadian bros/sisters).

10. This game has TWO puzzles, and they are practically solvable by a 3 year old! I mean, come on! I don't think I need to say much else on that!

11. More so a gripe with Capcom, but this game (like RE2R) has terrible mod support, and I really wish more companies would open up on that front. The modding community can produce some amazing things.

12. Still has the low-FPS zombies (from a distance) thing going on.

13. The defense mechanic is gone, even though it was in RE2R. You can no longer stop a bite with a stun/grenade or knife. 

14. Tons of ammo everywhere, even in higher difficulties. Not necessarily a bad thing because this game is definitely way more action oriented than RE2R. Also, zombies are easier to kill, which I think is super awesome (many will disagree).

15. No more enhanced ammo, or frozen rounds, which kind of blows. Also, no STI Eagle.

In closing, this is actually a very good game. Is it a good remake? Depends on who you ask, but personally, I think it's a very poor one. So much is missing, and at no point did I feel like I was playing a remake, I felt like I was playing a re-imagined version of RE3. Again, whether this is good or bad depends on the person.

You’ve probably heard by now that [i]Resident Evil 3[/i] does not pass muster. Well, it’s true. It doesn’t. It might be that on the back of the superlative [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] remake it was never going to. The original RE3 was a shorter game, with only one playable character (or at least one campaign) that was more focused on action than survival horror (by the 90’s estimation, anyway).

But that argument doesn’t really pass muster either. If you’re looking for fidelity to the source game, you won’t find it here. Large sequences have been removed to produce a more streamlined, linear experience. The clock tower is little more than set dressing, and you can forget about the park and factory. Worse, the city section – a once much-vaunted, open space worthy of exploration – is truncated to the first hour and change. Once you’re past it you’re looking at a series of set-pieces and boss fights until the credits start rolling, which won’t take long – my actual play time was just shy of six hours.

These exclusions would be forgivable if they served to produce an inspired re-imagining, rather than a remake. But precious little on display here points in either direction. Rather, we’re presented with an unambitious, potentially lazy game that was ushered out the door on the heels of its predecessor last year, secure in the knowledge that a market for this particular template existed. If the 1999 original proved limiting in its brevity and scope, they didn’t have to be a slave to it. The overarching premise – Jill desperately trying to escape Raccoon City, dogged by a relentless, brutal enemy – is pretty fertile ground for fresh, imaginative developments in story and gameplay, even if you decide not to carry over some of the original’s sequences. No such luck, sadly.

The most egregious lapse in judgement lies with Nemesis himself. It’s difficult to express my frustration at their choices here. In the remake of RE2, it felt like Mr. X was a prototype for the inevitable sequel starring Nemesis – Mr. X’s obvious inspiration. Mr. X was a frightening presence, patrolling the police station at random, requiring you to listen very, very closely to the environment, and change your route at the last minute to avoid a costly encounter should he prove too close. A bit like Nemesis himself, back in ‘99.

They don’t go with that here...at all, really. There’s a bit of it in the opening hour, but once you’re through that it gives way to a succession of boss battles and quick time encounters. On their own some of these fights would be pretty cool, but there’s no fear or tension. You’re not afraid of Nemesis, and that’s a big problem. Finally, in restricting Nemesis to tiered boss fights, it repeatedly flags how linear the game is, as the surprise factor has been removed. That’s ironic when you consider he was originally a testament to the original’s non-linear urban setting. It’s an unforgivable, perplexing miscalculation that I’m still thinking about (but probably for not much longer).

As with the RE2 remake, RE3 at least looks gorgeous. It plays well, too. If you’re happy with the truncated world, you’ll find the same slick, engaging combat as in the previous game. For what little there is of it, it’s generally pretty fun. There’s even an inspired sequence near the beginning, which involves traversing a spider-ridden power plant looking for switches and an inventive, if gross, use of green herbs.

I finished my first play-through in around 8 and half hours. I really enjoyed playing it, but I can't recommend it because it's inferior to last year's Resident Evil 2 and doesn't justify its current price. Good things first. The game looks gorgeous. The graphics, character designs and environment are top-notch. Jill Valentine looks cute and badass and her voice acting is really good. Jill and Carlos are a result of good writing and animation. They also have a great dynamic between them. All their scenes are really good. They both function really well too. Carlos has this cool punch that can send enemies flying. Lol. The lighting is good throughout the game but it's not so different compared to RE2. It also looks odd in some areas, and for some reason, RE2 looked better there. The performance on my PC was fantastic and I didn't experience any issues. It runs better than RE2. The game's story was good, it provided us with some cool information and added value to the lore. But it's something we already learned through previous RE games. RE3 takes place before, during and after RE2. So, if you've played last year's RE2, you'll like how this plays into it. The sound was spooky and enticing. There were parts of the game that got elevated solely because of the sound and music. The game has more action compared to RE2, there's a lot of shooting to do, especially when playing as Carlos. You'll find plenty of ammo. The guns fire and sound well. The shotgun wasn't as good as the one in RE2 though. The game has a lot of really good cut scenes, and you can see where the money is. Nemesis was scary as hell and whenever he was around, it was truly terrifying. He wasn't as scary as Mr X though and we'll talk about it later. The boss fights were good. The game's not as scary as RE2, which is completely understandable considering the source material. There are some well-done jump scares and all but not too much. The game relies heavily on the action as I said before. The zombies are more in number and are pretty aggressive this time. There is some variety in the enemies we face. We'll come across parts of sewers, police stations and NEST from the last title. Other than the police station, these old areas add a new touch. There are also some new areas that bring us some new enemy types. These enemies will annoy you like Lickers and dealing with them can be challenging at times. That's pretty much the 'good' about the game. Now, let's talk about the 'bad'. 

The most negative thing about the game is its downgrade of physics and gore mechanics. There is no ragdoll physics, the dismemberment of limbs is gone for the most part, and parts of zombies vanish after you take care of them. They just burst into thin air. There is also the absence of collision mechanics. Unlike the last time, you won't see zombies falling over each other and reacting realistically to environmental objects. The zombie designs are also repeated from the previous title. Nemesis is limited to scripted events. He chases you dynamically only once throughout the entire game, and that isn't long either. I was expecting Nemesis to enter every room if not all safe rooms but he doesn't do that. There are parts of the game when you'll feel weird about Nemesis because it feels dumb for him to not do certain things. There's one room he could have entered but he just stares at you through its window like a fool. It kind of feels lame at times. Also, there wasn't enough Nemesis in the game. And it only gets worse when his Tyrant-like form doesn't stay for long. He's in his Tyrant form for only one boss fight, and that is quite disappointing to me. It would have been a lot better if we had more Nemesis and his chase sequences in the game. His first mutation just feels too soon. Doesn't feel organic to me. Sort of rushed. The boss fight after his mutation was short but decent. The police station parts weren't really great. They were short and there wasn't much to explore in them. The real problem with RE3 is that it feels like a DLC to RE2, and is very linear compared to it. It can be described as a game with a lot of running, cut scenes and shooting. Sometimes, it kind of feels like RE6 running on RE Engine. The game is also very short. It's not even as long as the 2nd run in RE2, which is quite disappointing considering there's no replay value to this one. For the amount price we are paying, the game feels pretty inferior to RE2 on many levels. It's a must-buy if it was $30, but at its current price, it's a must-buy only if it's on sale. Hopefully, they'll give us some juicy DLC instead of focusing too much on the online mode. Overall, the game is fantastic but it doesn't justify its existence when compared to RE2 and the current price tag. This is a 7.5 out of 10.

At the time of submission, Resident Evil 3: Nemesis is the only mainline Resident Evil game I never actually played. That said, I was unable to make comparisons between this and the original. However, I do plan on playing it at some point, especially after hearing how much was missing here in comparison to the absolute delight that was (my favorite entry in the franchise) Resident Evil 2's remake.

Here are the Nifty things I liked, and the Lame things I didn't.

[h1]The Nifty[/h1]
✪  It looks and runs great, performing smoothly through all (6) of my playthroughs. I had no issues with frame drops or glitches.

✪ Jill and Carlos maintain the campy charm that is expected of classic Resident Evil characters; not too serious, not too silly and almost a little too badass.

✪ Jill being able to dodge and Carlos being able to counter feels right, helping the gameplay feel fluid; especially once you master them.

✪ Nightmare mode, which can only be unlocked after finishing Hardcore mode, is an absolute delight. It actually got a few good scares out of me and gave me that rush of a true Resident Evil vibe.

✪ The Records section is finally worth paying more attention to. Finishing challenges within it reward you with points that can be used to buy helpful bonus items, which previously had to be unlocked by finishing the game in X amount of time, on Y difficulty. 

✪ Controversial Nifty: Nemesis being scripted is actually a blessing. Having to deal with him more in his current state would make the game more frustrating, in my opinion. This is especially the case on higher difficulties.

[h1]The Lame[/h1]
✘ Even for a Resident Evil game, the runtime is really short. According to [url=https://www.residentevil.net/three/en/windows/o1906480.html?ref=portal-en--mypage-record-headerselect]ResidentEvil(dot)net[/url], my first run took just a bit over 5 hours. My Hardcore run took about 2.5 hours, and everything else was under 1.5 with the help of infinite ammo weapons.

✘ Resident Evil 2 had some of the best combat reactions and gore effects... Which is weird, because in Resident Evil 3, all of that is gone. Enemies react to your attacks the same way just about every time, with the gore being toned down immensely.

✘ After the city segment, this game felt much more linear and way less engaging than any other mainline Resident Evil game. The absence of fun puzzles, backtracking through altered versions of previous locations, great boss fights and the element of survival are just...oof.
 
[h1]Overall[/h1]
Resident Evil 3's remake runs well and looks great, but as a whole, I can't help but feel like it was a big step backwards from Resident Evil 2's remake. Despite this, I mostly enjoyed my time with it and remain hopeful about future REmakes.

I love the franchise, always have. I loved the original games, as well as the fantastic RE2 remake. I cannot say enough how much I loved the RE2 remake. And even though I played through this one and liked it, I cannot in good conscience "recommend" it. Here's why:

[u]Cons:[/u]

I played through on Hardcore (the hardest starting difficulty), dying somewhere between 15-20 times total throughout the playthrough, and completed the game in less than 7 hours. This alone made me feel like I was a bit ripped off for having spent a full 59.99 + tax on the title on release day. There just wasn't enough content. They even recycled a good portion of the police station from RE2, a good hour's worth of the gameplay, and it felt like outside of that, the content was minimal-feeling. It's like they were riding off the back of their success with RE2 but weren't willing to put in the same love and care into RE3. I honestly should've been more skeptical of the remake coming out only a year after the RE2 remake.

The game was way too easy. Sure, when it came to certain areas, especially boss fights, it could sometimes be a challenge to "chess" my way through what little ammo I had, making sure that I made the right moves at the right times. However, even on Hardcore difficulty, the player is no longer required to have an ink ribbon to save the game (some people may be excited by this but I feel like, again, this reduces the difficulty of the game and feels lame) and they implemented an auto-save feature that made it extremely easy just to grind through the tough parts because most of said tough parts of the playthrough had an auto-save right before them. The third thing that made the game very easy is the new "dodge" system they implemented. I found it very easy to cheese my way through any attacks from larger/"tougher" monsters. Honestly, the regular zombies killed me more than any of the other more advanced monsters.

It seemed like there weren't really many environment puzzles/door puzzles, things of that nature throughout. The game definitely felt more fast-paced than RE2, like the different areas were kind of passed by relatively quickly, not really allowing the soaking in feeling. On the one hand, this game really was more "intense" feeling than RE2, but that's not necessarily a better thing. Even though you have a similar situation as in RE2 (unstoppable thing chasing you [i.e. Nemesis]), Nemesis is really only part of the game through scripted/more linear areas. Not nearly as openly chasing you throughout an entire biome as it was in RE2.

Lastly, and this is a bit less offending but just something to add: Carlos is a terrible character. I'm not one to gripe about social-justice BS or anything of that nature, but he just had no depth, was immediately making "sweetheart" comments to Jill, and even though I liked Jill's initial response to his commentary, he seemed like a shallow character pretty much throughout. On top of that, you only get to play as him in like one portion of the game, which felt very limited.

[u]Pros:[/u]
Hmm. I mean, it [i]is[/i] RE3, and there is a lot of nostalgia involved with it. The gameplay still felt very similar to that of RE2 remake, so it was still satisfying in many ways.

Honestly, do not spend full price on this. I did and I regret it. I would still recommend playing through the game for fans of the franchise, for sure, but this was definitely a step backward compared to RE2.

I've seen that people have mixed feelings on this game so I figured I may as well give my thoughts on it and whether other people should get it.

I've never played the original RE3 so I can't really judge how they compare. But for what this game is, I honestly think it's great. The combat is really enjoyable, especially now that they added the dodge mechanic (which I felt RE2 desperately needed). It's atmospheric as all hell (especially in the early areas), the sound design is awesome, and it looks absolutely gorgeous. It's basically more of that good stuff that the RE2 Remake gave us.

But the problem I have with it, as a lot of other people did, is it just feels short and kinda rushed. I was looking into it, and apparently Capcom cut a lot of content that was in the original RE3, and it shows. I get that certain changes need to be made when you remake a game, but that should only really be adding and improving; not taking away. For example, the first area in the city, while it was great for what it was, felt like it should have been bigger. I was right, because it was apparently around three times bigger in the original. And that's just one of the several areas that got cut down. There was also apparently a bigger variety of enemies in the original, as well as just appearing more frequently.

Speaking of enemies, I feel like Nemesis could have been handled better in this game. Don't get me wrong, he's intimidating and I really like his design. I'd say he's a step up from Mr X in that regard. But Nemesis takes a step down as, for a lot of the game, he's more of just a set-piece. He shows up at different points in the game, causes some commotion, then just sorta disappears. He's been relegated almost entirely to scripted events. In the RE2 Remake, I thought it was awesome how Mr X actually physically walks around the RPD looking for you. While he does have a few scripted appearances, it actually made him feel much more scary since he's just always present, and so you have to constantly be mindful of him when traversing the area; especially when there are other enemies around. That would have been AMAZING with Nemesis. I always found it amusing how you could completely defeat Mr X by just walking around a table or something, since he didn't have any ranged attacks. But Nemesis has his ranged tentacles and even a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocket launcher. How freaking scary would it be to have THAT hunting you as you explore? That would have been way scarier than Mr X. But instead he's relegated mostly to scripted events where the game provides you with the capacity to fight or escape him, instead of forcing you to be mindful of his presence and avoid him. You would be in big trouble if a roaming Nemesis found you while you were unprepared. Plus, we don't even get to see the iconic scene of him [spoiler] killing Brad [/spoiler]. I would have loved to see that in HD; not to mention all the other scenes like the police being overwhelmed that got cut. I feel like if you're gonna remake one of gaming's most iconic bad guys, then you have to do it justice. You can't half-ass Nemesis, Capcom. He deserves better. 

Honestly, while the game is still really fun, it just doesn't have the depth or replayability that the RE2 Remake had. There are no branching paths or alternate stories, and no extra game modes  (*cough* Mercenaries *cough*). I played through the game on Standard difficulty, as I do with all games I haven't played before. Apparently playing on higher difficulties actually changes certain things like enemies and items spawning in different places, as well enemies just generally being more dangerous (similar to Madhouse difficulty in RE7). You also unlock [spoiler] 'The Shop' [/spoiler] after you beat the game which you can use to [spoiler] buy certain items that can help you in subsequent runs such as item pouches, new weapons, and items that improve your stats. Don't worry there's no microtransactions. Your currency is points you earn from completing challenges. [/spoiler]. While there is some replay value in this, it just isn't enough to justify the price tag. The RE2 Remake had much more content than this. What we have is good, but the game needed to be fleshed out more.

I'll do a quick overall Pros/Cons bullet point list below.

[b] Pros [/b]
[list]
[*] Really fun gameplay and combat
[*] Nemesis has a cool design and is pretty intimidating
[*] Looks and sounds amazing
[*] Carlos is hugely improved
[*] The story ties into the RE2 Remake in certain ways (won't spoil how)
[*] Brilliant atmosphere
[*] More difficulty options (and differences between them)
[*] Unlockable items for replays are a cool idea
[/list]

[b] Cons [/b]
[list]
[*] Game is too short (took me around 7 hours and I was taking my time and exploring everything)
[*] Lots of content unnecessarily removed
[*] No branching paths or alternate runs (especially a problem considering how short the game is)
[*] Nemesis is mostly a set-piece and isn't constantly present like Mr X
[*] Story is kinda meh, but it's Resident Evil, what do you expect?
[/list]

So overall, it's a really fun game and I'm glad I played it. What's there is good, but there just needs to be more of it. The game feels like it should have been an expansion or DLC for the RE2 Remake sold for half the price considering what it gives you; it doesn't feel like a full game on its own. It was obviously rushed out to capitalise on the success of it's predecessor, and that's pretty disappointing considering Capcom suddenly decided to be good game developers again a few years back. I hope they don't go back and make the same mistakes they made in the late 2000s that led them to rebooting the franchise in the first place.

If you're interested in this game, I would say go play the Resident Evil 2 Remake first as it's definitely the better game overall; especially considering it has much more content and replayability. If you enjoyed that then I'd say definitely give this game a try as it's still really enjoyable, it just could have been so much more. I'd probably wait for a sale too since the price tag is kinda ridiculous considering what you get. I dunno if Capcom is planning any DLC or new game modes or anything, but they'd better be free if they wanna justify that price tag.

I've never written a review on any game, but I'm sorry this one needs it. First a short and serious -but angry- review, then some ending comments, less serious but angrier (maybe we laugh a bit together at least).

[u] The good things [/u], in order of importance (more to less).
- The combat system is fun. Different creatures each with their weak point/strategy. Dodges are interesting aswell. I'd like to have more of this. They've improved a bit the formula from the previous remake.
- Nemesis street chase feels thrilling and challenging, but it's way too short. When I say short I mean "inmediately replace all the scripted **** with this and we may have a deal". Nemesis fights are fun aswell. 
- The best moments are: from start to repairing the train, Hospital, Police Station and NEST2 (more to less in my preference).
- Stunning graphics of RE Engine. Not entirely good because of some poor physics and animations.

Now, we come with... [u]The Bad things [/u], from more to less important aswell:
- The quality is too inconsistent. The good moments are too short. When tension starts to build it's already over, so you get a bitter taste of "what if this lasted a bit longer...". They've created Raccoon City streets, Hospital, NEST2 and (recycled) Police Station and it feels like a waste of resources because they don't last enough to shine. They don't have to be bigger but fuller. You grab this item and inmediately find an use for it, from A to B. The original was conceived as an horror-action game, sure, but this is too much. 2 puzzles, no more. Railway pathing was almost OK, but the vaccine one is just a cheap version of the one from RE2R. It seems that this game has been made by someone who hates the original RE formula.
- On the other side, some moments are just [b]bad[/b]. The sewers have little to no interest. It's just following the corridor and avoid/kill Gamma Hunters. No other enemies, no puzzles. I don't know why they put that in the game. The underground facility before NEST2 feels meh aswell. Easy labyrinth, some cheap surprises and you're done. Two parts of the game being a waste is too much for this length.
- The game barely conveys emotions, and this is awful for any kind of art. It's fun to kill monsters or evade them, you have stunning 2020 computers to load your graphics and things are happening, but these parts feel uncoordinated and don't make you feel the story. The rythm is off, fragmented in too short good moments followed by awful moments. I won't extend more here but at the end of the review, in case you wanna read it. 
- The QTE/scripted events are awful.  They detract emotion from the experience (this can't go wrong if I just mash the correct button. No challenge, no thrill). They have no replayability value, as they are literally the same everytime. Most of Nemesis chase reduced to an interactive movie that a 5-year old could beat moving forward or mashing a button is just a great disappointment. I feels lazy and absurd waste of material. They invest money on making improvements on Mr.X’s stalker concept, then they use it for 10 minutes.

So [u]overall[/u]:
- Have fun killing monsters, one Nemesis chase and the boss fights with a nice graphic engine. 
- Good moments not THAT good and too short, too many bad moments for the game's length.
- Lost RE puzzle/explore formula.
- QTE/scripted Nemesis. Awful.
- All short of small details feeling lazy/unpolished. Rushed rythm, uncoordinated parts, little tension. 

If you are interested in a more detailed opinion after that, here we go:
 - It's interesting how the survival horror formula applies the same in both remakes with opposite results: start with no guns, escape some monsters you can't fight, start feeling safe but an unbeatable stalker and stronger monsters come to blow it all, overcome your fear and keep escaping ‘till you find powerful guns and climax with a great fight. It’s a good formula. In RE2R you can tell they had a plan for what you should feel and they put it all on their side to accomplish it. You may not be a fan of Mr.X stalking, but he was there to balance the tension loss after you felt comfortable with the P. Station. You even had a subtle joke in NEST (something about "healthy meals" while zombies were eating people). A countless number of details and it paid off. In RE3R the little tension goes back and forth. It doesn't seem like they had an overall plan for the game before they made it, so it's just like pasted segments of different stories. 
- The game is short, of course, (4-6 hours Hardcore, with lots of backtracking), but that's not the main problem. The quality is. I've played shorter games (LIMBO & This War of Mine) and I still remember them as incredible experiences. Their price is lower being indies, of course. I don't know if I'd pay 40-60 € for them, but I wouldn't even pay 20€ for this game knowing how disappointing it is.
- The physics/animation system has some awful moments. Remember the sewers? Because I do. I remember shooting grenades to a Gamma Hunter and watching him twist and die with one animation. Then the next comes and he twists and dies with the exact same animation. So you run from A to B in a repetitive map (hoping that it’s short) and repetitively encounter clonic Gamma Hunters, shoot them, and wait for them to adopt their only death pose. Yes, a great idea to put a lot of them crowding one place so you can notice it better. 
- Oh, did you think that was it? No, we have more. We're now at NEST2, at the corridor with Tyrants and Beta Hunters on both sides. 2 of them come to fight you. You shoot an acid grenade which hits both. You watch the 2 clones twist and die with perfect coordination as they've triggered their only animation at the same time. What a gorgeous ballet. Of course, they twist for 3-4 seconds, so you can enjoy it more. It seems that when someone betatested the game that didn't happen. Ye, no one thinks about using an AOE weapon against 2 Hunters in a forced fight. Or maybe they saw it and decided it was too much work.
- Why if I shoot to a barrel the zombies hit by the explosion get blown with such awful physics? Wasn’t there an intermediate solution between full ragdoll and this joke? What about the Hospital last stand with Carlos? They had to get rid of the dead zombies because they're too many, sure, but why in such a cheap way? Photorrealistic graphics engine mixed with a good ol’ cartoony blood splatter and poof, the body's gone. 
- Hey, Jill, see that Nemesis in front of you? Why don't you just stomp him with the car and push you both from a multi-stored building? Hello Hollywood, did you see what we did? This was [i]cool[/i], right? At least nobody pushed a giant rock with his fists, Right????? Good, get back to work, we have to recycle some more content before lunch.
- Last thing. Why even the model viewer is just worse than RE2R one? At least, if you didn't enjoy the game too much you could enjoy the power of their engine. Now you can only see the models, no animations. We have copypasted a lot of models and created more which have their own animations, so the material is there, but we won't use it. We implement the exact same feature, but downgraded, because I don't know, it's fun. The other option is that the animations were so poor in comparison that it would hurt watching them closely.

Everything screams "let's try hard not to be too ashamed for what we've done". Let's distract you with some scripted chases, shooting and some "great" interactive escenes - the only fight against Nicholai, your main antagonist along Nemesis - What an innovative climax, they wouldn't just let the game rest in peace. Let’s give you “for free” Resistance instead of selling it. That's what I call damage control. If I went to the barber and he decided not to charge me after the haircut, I'd inmediately go watch myself at the mirror. At least, the game is good, right?

As a long-time fan of the Resident Evil series, I have to say that this game is damn fun. Jill is awesome, Carlos is awesome, the characters are great. The visuals are outstanding. The gameplay is pretty fantastic.

That being said, there are some disappointments with regards to this remake. It doesn't stay true to the original very well, while the major plot-points and set pieces are mostly there, a large chunk of the original game was cut. There is no Clock-Tower section, which was the most disappointing as it is a pretty memorable locale. There is no Gravedigger boss fight, and It's kind of disappointing to only fight Nemesis as a boss.

Speaking of Nemesis, while he looks awesome, and as he progresses through different stages, looks more crazy and horrendous; the fights themselves are pretty lame. Nemesis chasing you through the city is pretty straightforward, and his pursuit is quite short. The latter fights are very contained and there is an obvious objective which makes it pretty bland. I will say the final fight on Nightmare/Inferno is insanely difficult, and posed quite the frustrating challenge which felt good to overcome.

There are far too many cutscenes, which on the first play through offer awesome cinematic thrills, but altogether become tedious on subsequent play throughs.

As far as unlockables go, it's pretty scant. Only one alternate costume is unlockable, and even though there is a store which you can purchase helpful items and guns, it somewhat trivializes the harder difficulties.

I wish Capcom had kept this game in development for longer, as it seems rushed and unfinished. They could have expanded the main campaign past the measly 4-6 hour runtime, they could have added a Mercenaries mode. They could have done without the Inferno mode and just made Nightmare the only unlockable mode, and ramped up the difficulty for Hardcore (by the way, the omission of ink ribbons is a damn shame). They could have added a couple more unlockable costumes as an homage to the original.

While I do recommend this game, as it is definitely worth experiencing, the full price is not worth the experience unless you really love Resident Evil and cannot wait for a sale to pick this one up.

Here's hoping some DLC can satiate our mild disappointment. Perhaps a Mercenaries mode is on the way.

MY SUMMARY:
Nice demo, Capcom. This game feels gutted. Were they rushed to release? All I want to know is, where's the rest? Don't get me wrong, this game has its great moments, good graphics and music, but those are betrayed by a lack of content and very few open areas. Linear, scripted, frustrating boss fights. Encounters with Nemesis are frustrating and annoying. 

I do not have very fast reaction speeds so I could never really get the hang of dodging. I either dodge too early and die, or dodge too late and die. Sometimes I get lucky. The only way I beat the final boss on higher difficulties was by spamming First Aid Sprays. I would rather the mechanics reward planning, good aim, correct weaponry loadout, etc. than rely on an all-or-nothing dodge that requires very fast reaction speeds and there is NO indicator that flashes when you should dodge, as many games have for similar mechanics.

I am a big fan of the RE series, I loved RE7 and the RE2 remake of recent years, but I can't recommend this game at $60. I couldn't care less about RE Resistance. I'd much rather have a fully fleshed out campaign.

CONS:
-Extremely short game for a whopping $60 (took me 5.5 hours and I explored all I could). I pre-ordered this game based on my experience with RE7 and RE2 remake, but I should have waited.
-Because it was short, the story got cut down to the bone, leaving a lot of loose ends (DLC?)

Resident Evil 2's remake last year was one of the most finely designed games that I have ever played. It's essentially a simple game that can be cleared perfectly through rote rather than skill, but every aspect is a deeply-considered — perhaps to the point of mathematical perfection. There is no part of the game that can't be defeated by foreknowledge, but that's the essence of survival horror; you barely persevere once by quick-thinking, then you come back and learn the game, you plan routes and deal with unexpected factors until you eventually find the perfect route. 

Resident Evil 3 is a series of scripted events connected by gimmicks. If you played the demo, you basically experienced the entirety of the unscripted Nemesis stalking scenario. Everything else is poorly-designed scripted sequences mixed with the blandest game design that I have ever seen. Is there a level where you are in a sorta grid with blocked off parts and you have to active 4 generators while agile insect enemies spawn and ambush you? Hell yes. How about enemies that instantly kill you when they get near? ♥♥♥♥ yes! Almost the entire rest of the game is scripted sequences and shoddy boss fights. 

Look, Capcom bought a lot of credit from me with RE2. I hated RE7, but they put out RE2 and DMC5 and that was worth a hell of a lot of credit from me. I think that RE3 had burnt all of that. 

Good points: the graphics are good and the HDR implementation is nice. That's it.

Oh, but this is a personal point: Jill is extremely ugly. I don't really mind playing as an ugly character but she really is a dog. To the point where actually looking at her is difficult. People complained about Claire in RE2 looking bad but she really didn't especially compared to this.

------------

Quick edit after more gameplay. The first unlockable difficulty mode seem really poorly designed. They put some effort into the early sections in the town, but it gets increasingly lazy with barely-altered sections and even some encounters that are easier than the base game. It all culminates in the final boss fight being so insane that I didn't bother beating it.
Get it on sale.

Resident Evil 3 is criminally short but incredibly sweet. An action-packed joyride, with great characters, an interesting story and masterful level design.

[h1] Story [/h1]
The game puts you right into the beginning of the Raccoon City outbreak. In typical Resident Evil fashion, a big bad guy wants to kill you (very cleverly named Nemesis), as you try to survive what remains of the city. You play as Jill Valentine, a strong personality filled with charm, snarky remarks and hilarious comebacks. The same can be said for the second playable character, Carlos, who meets with Jill as the city starts to crumble. The story is fairly intriguing, as you learn about the events that transpired during the origin of the outbreak. How did it all begin? Who is Nemesis? Without spoiling one of the best parts of the game, what's especially well done here is how they connect the unexplained elements from Resident Evil 2, making its universe even more immersive.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2053708979
[h1] Graphics [/h1]
Holy smokes, this game looks incredible. This is state of the art animation, surpassing giants like [i] Naughty Dog [/i] with their lifelike character models. Jill and Carlos almost seem real at times, as the line between fiction and reality starts to blur. Every texture is top-notch, every light source creates moving shadows and adds to the creepy atmosphere. If you are graphic fanatic like myself, you will be pleased to know they have gone above and beyond in this department.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2053708965
[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
Resident Evil 3 remake is not a horror survival game like its predecessor. It's a horror action game. Ammo and enemies are abundant. Set-pieces happen often, forcing Jill to run for her life as she gets constantly chased by Nemesis or some other disgusting creature. The game does not give you a second to breathe, relentless in its quest to give you non-stop action. Think Resident Evil 2 on steroids. As high as the adrenaline-filled playthrough was for me, every drug comes with its numerous downsides.

The shooting mechanics simply aren't made for this level of action. It's supposed to make you feel weak, clumsy and easily overwhelmed. This works perfectly in Resident Evil 2, because the game is mostly designed around avoiding encounters and preserving ammo. This time around, the mechanics should have adapted to the more action-oriented decision. In its defense, players now have a dedicated dodge button, but it's poorly executed and doesn't really add much to the clunky feeling of the gameplay. The game mostly shines in the rare instances where map exploration, puzzle-solving and small enemy encounters are the main gameplay loop, but they are very few and far between. During those moments, you can't help but feel like you're playing the masterful Resident Evil 2 again, wondering why there isn't more of this in the game. Nemesis is also a disappointment, following in the footsteps of Mr. X (literally). This time around, Nemesis is mostly kept in pre-rendered cinematic cutscenes, random jump-scares and long set-pieces. He does not have the same function as Mr. X, who never failed to stress me out as I heard his footsteps grow louder and louder, never knowing what his AI would do next. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2053708945
With that in mind, the game is still incredibly fun to play. The gritty atmosphere, superb design and high variety of enemies make the game feel fresh. There's a lot that happens constantly. You never know what you will find around the corner. The game is surprisingly short however, which is not something to be ignored. Keep in mind your wallet will take a hit for what seems to be a five to six hours campaign on normal difficulty. This is borderline unacceptable for the full price, and unless you are a big fan, I recommend waiting for a sale.

[h1] Overall [/h1]
If you can ignore the price tag and know what you're getting into, the game is a ton of fun. Jill and Carlos are memorable, the story adds a lot to the universe and the overall experience is pure entertainment. This feels like a missed opportunity to really hit it out of the park, but I still enjoyed what I got.

- some other unlockables like trinkets and weapons

- some pretty uninteresting boss fights and one of the most pathetic final boss fights I've seen, period

- some good, not great horror-shooter gameplay with pretty gRaFiX, that are ultimately wasted, buried within an overall mediocre product

- zero extra content outside of the campaign (no, I'm not counting Resistance, as that's a different game entirely)

And that's about it.
Now if I were to start drawing comparisons to previous entries, this list would be a lot longer, but no less depressing.

Resident evil 3 remake is a mixed bag, there are so many steps backwards from Resident evil 2 remake that it’s really quite jarring. Dismemberment is neutered to exploding parts and bodies, rather than the ragdoll physics and body parts slowly peeling off of the zombie as they’re shot. This was done under the pretense of there being more zombies, but frankly aside from one part in the story they never appeared in large enough numbers to warrant these downgrades, fourth survivor in RE2 Remake had more zombies and enemies on screen, so it felt like Capcom lied about the need for said downgrade. 

     Couple this with missing areas like the park, visiting the RPD as Jill, no clocktower interior or the city hall, it becomes frustrating seeing how much of the original game was cut to make the “remake” more linear to cater to a broader audience. 

     Nemesis, the once namesake of this game, good god what have they done to my boy. He looks fantastic and what sections where he has the ability to randomly appear and attack you are great. Sadly that lasts for a small portion of the beginning of the game, then scripted sequences or nothing. Not to mention his weapons aren’t particularly threatening, this is more offensive with his trusty rocket launcher which was a terror in the original game. Now it’s a blatantly telegraphed attack that is way too forgiving, even on the hardcore difficulty, much like the rest of this game what they’ve done to nemesis is just frustrating. 

     My overall conclusion is this is a bad remake, it carries over scant parts of the game it claims to originate from and removes all of the puzzles from a game about killing zombies and puzzles. Resident Evil 3 remake was rushed endeavor which sucks compared to how lovingly recrafted and modernized Resident Evil 2 remake was done. 

     If you have to chance to buy the game half off, or less I’d say go for it, its brief playtime will be worth your money, otherwise steer clear, and understand going into this game it’s not a remake it’s a reboot.

Resident Evil 3 Remake can be summed up as a lack luster disappointment. Dont get me wrong, if you enjoyed RE2 remake you will enjoy the game, as its more of the same and doesn't bring much into the story of Raccoon City's destruction. The game is shortened/streamlined for a quicker play through that cuts out a lot of what made the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis a classic.

Ill preface my review with saying I Loved RE3 as a kid so I am of course biased. So if you are a fan, It is immediately apparent how the game is more a re-imagining vs a remake. 

-The more open decision making that was uniquely RE3 was cut in favor of streamlining,which was a staple of RE3. 
-Nemesis has been reduced to scripted events, no longer a threat or a fear of random appearance, and while very beautiful and imposing at times, is reduced to basic deteriorating monster. 
-Characters come off as their basic archetypes and thus more shallow. 
-Story is almost all new aside from said characters and basic locations present in original, many reused in RE2 which is expected if game didnt feel so short and comparable.

RE3 is an enjoyable game, but as a Resident Evil 3: Nemesis Remake, is very disappointing and only improves in terms of graphics and controls. It is of course a new game and thus doesn't have to be a copy of the original, but inherently falls short in most if not all regards.
 I would have loved to replay a new Nemesis with beautifully updated graphics and controls but at least we still have the original.

 If you enjoyed RE2 its a good DLC game, but is a big disappointment for those looking to return to a classic. 
Would recommend if there is a price drop (and uncoupled from Resistance) or a hardcore RE fan but view as a brand new short RE 2.5 and not 'Resident Evil 3: Nemesis'.

Resident Evil 3 Remake has been made with the same engine as Resident Evil 2 Remake. So you can expect the same (Actually better looking) visuals of the game. But is it a faithful recreation / remake of the original Resident Evil 3 ? For the most part...yes. Capcom did however cut / remove / abridge some of the original areas from the game while making that up with expanded / new areas. If you haven't played the original, you wouldn't notice anything. If you did, you would be slightly disappointed by those cuts. 

The gameplay, story, boss battles are all awesome and on par with Resident Evil 2 Remake. However, do note that the game is quite short where you'll clock at around 5 to 8 hours on your first playthrough (Which is on par with the original Resident Evil 3 game). A bit more if you wanna go for 100 percent run. But you do unlock harder difficulty modes and new challenge / item runs for subsequent playthroughs. The game does come with the free Resident Evil Resistance, an asymmetrical co-op / multiplayer game. I didn't play that game and honestly didn't care or ask for it either. But at least its there if you wanna play some co-op Resident Evil with friends.

Overall, is Resident Evil 3 a good game ? Absolutely. Is it worth the full asking price ? If you'll willing to pay 60 dollars or equivalent for a 5 to 8 hour game, a fan of Resident Evil and are dying to play Resident Evil 3 Remake, then go for it. Otherwise wait for a discount to buy it.

My first issue with this game is how linear and short it is. you can beat it in 2 hours, and that's not speed running. Another issue i have is with Nemesis, one, his redesign is sub-par to put it kindly. They made him look beastly and savage, actually, they made him look like the super licker from Resident Evil the Movie, which make it even worst. His voice however i will compliment is good, no other game besides the original had a good nemesis voice, this one does, so that's a plus. His other forms are also not great, except the final form, i didn't mind it, but it wasn't a threat, which is the problem. Nemesis is NOT A THREAT in this game. 1 Frag grenade literally will down him, the explosive barrels and generators you can trigger help stun him as well.  In the original game it took 24 shotgun shells to down him, once, and you had to down him twice in a row to get any loot from him. Now, just shot his chest contraption and BAM, hes down after maybe 5 shots. With these issue, Nemesis isn't scary, which is a serious problem. He is supposed to be the most powerful tyrant ever created, a damn near unstoppable force. He suppose to be challenging and terrifying, which he was for all of 5 minutes, until you discover how to easily dispatch him and now the main bad guy of the whole game is a joke. 

Weapons are pretty bare bones, the original game had weapons you could unlock by battling nemesis and earning parts to craft better gear like the STI Eagle 6.0 or the Lever-Action Shotgun, those are gone and no mine launcher either which sucks. Granted the MGL can fire mine rounds, which somehow damage nemesis more then explosive rounds. Sigh....

Ok, now onto Jill, Jill for the most part is amazing, she looks both beautiful and tough, like she actually was an ex delta force operator turned cop. Her outfit redesign is good in my opinion, it makes senses for her situation. However, she has 2 issues. 1. Her classic outfit, is NOT her classic outfit, its a mock up of it and it looks rather bad on her. Very bad, i dunno why they even bothered it they weren't gonna do it justice. Modders! Fix this heresy! Ok, the second is her attitude. Jill in the original series was tough, kind hearted, witty and determined.  While she still has some of those traits, shes gain a few new ones i do not like. Shes lost that witty charm and gained a foul mouth, which at times is funny, others it makes me roll my eyes. This came out only months after the stellar (though flawed in its own way) remake of RE2. And it shows this was the result of some corporate higherups screaming down the hall that they needed a quick cashgrab on the hype RE2 created. A list:

1. QTC (Quick Time Choices) from the original - Gone! In other words, no replay value whatsoever unless those achievements are really important to you. 3. Most of the original RE3 layout is gone. Park - Gone. City streets (most of em) Gone. News building - Gone. Gas station - Gone. CLOCK TOWER - Gone. Industrial Facility - Gone (some purists will say re-done I guess). And so on, you get the point. They have bareboned the gameplay areas down to basically 3 core elements. A city run with a few areas and a sewer (with a new enemy that EVEN THE GAME MAKES FUN OF!), the hospital (which layout and look is almost noteworthy close to DayMare1998, ill let you figure out the rest there) and shock and awe, a lab area....so original. 
5. Instead of actually doing the original justice, they have paid tribute to them (using that term in its lowest form) by using them in simple puzzles or stuff do list type of elements, like the gems inserted in a jukebox for some reason that resembles the gate opening mechanisms in the original. 
6. Voice acting is decent, especially Jill, but the script makes little to no sense for most of the time. For example, Brad calls you in the apartment freaked out, and then after unstoppable juggernaut murder-machine Nemesis chases you through fire and flame, you just stroll down an alley where you meet up with a casually strolling Brad who cracks jokes and is calm as a Sunday morning. And Carlos (mixed Latin American and indigineous origins) has no accent at all. And....you get the point. They gave 0 ♥♥♥♥♥. 
7. A 60 dollar game that you can finish in under 2 hours......SERIOUSLY? Its even an achievement......

The feelings towards this game seem to be quite mixed overall, and I wouldn't say it's all justified. Now, I am someone that has never played the original RE3 (only numbered game that I had not), and it seems that most new players do end up liking this more. For all the people that don't like reading, this is a very good game and it is worth your time, but you should know what kind of experience you're getting into.

The most common complaint seems to be the length, and I think your reaction to this one heavily depends on your background. RE games have always prided themselves on replay value, and this one does still offer plenty, secrets to unlock, speedruns, difficulties that change the enemy and item placements etc. None of the original RE games are very long, and after some practice you can easily clear them in 1-2 hours, and that is part of their charm. I can see why you'd be disappointed if you expected 1 single lengthy single player experience, but this is a remake of Resident evil 3, which was already known as one of the shortest games in the series. Sure, I was expecting it to be a little longer than it was, maybe 1 or 2 more small zones to explore (like the Clock tower for example) would have helped with this, but because of the replay value I wasn't all that bothered by it. 

This game is easily at it's best during the first half. Exploring Raccoon city is a blast, and I have no major complaints about it. That is also where nemesis gets to shine the most, because he is just hunting you around the city. This is exactly why I find the use of him later to be very disappointing, and this is easily my biggest issue with the game. They really should have had more areas where he could surprise you, instead of making him centered around big set pieces all the time. That extra zone I mentioned above could have helped with this, because the weird use of Nemesis makes the overall pace of the game suffer, especially around the mid-game portion. The game gets too focused on big action set pieces, and you can just feel the tension start to fade away 1 explosion after another. Most of his boss battles are also a bit weak overall, with the 1st boss being my clear favorite. Meanwhile, some of the other ones have weird glitches and camera issues, and the last boss might be the single most unbalanced fight of the series on the hardest difficulty settings.

Is this as good of a remake as 1 or 2? I think it quite clearly isn't because of all the things that were left out, and due to Nemesis himself being a bit disappointing. Is it a bad Resident evil game like some people are saying? No not at all, the gameplay is about as good as in 2, the characters are all charming, and the atmosphere of the game is very strong, especially in that first half. Just don't expect a shot-for-shot remake of the original, and you won't be disappointed. If you happen to be the type of player that only plays through games once, then I'd recommend you wait for a sale with this one. I just hope that Capcom learns the right lessons from this, they've had a good run during the past few years, don't waste it all now.

Let's make one thing very clear. At full price, you're paying $30 for Resident Evil 3 Remake, and you're paying $30 for Resident Evil Resistance. And no, that's not entirely a good thing, unfortunately.

Minor spoilers ahead.

---------

Where to start... Resident Evil 2 Remake was an ambitious, finely engineered machine. It was Resident Evil 2 but remixed to fit the modern climate, while also sprinkling its own ideas to make it a wholly unique game on its own, distinct from the original Resident Evil 2. It ditched a compelling mechanic with unique A/B and B/A campaign runs telling entirely different stories in lieu of a story that fits cleanly into the established series canon with some very minor retweaks (and some unwanted repetition), but it made up for it with the compelling and terrifying Mr. X, motion capture, art direction, acting, and the sense of tension zombies lost over the years.

Then here comes Resident Evil 3 Remake, a thoughtless, sloppy, and compromised experience that cherrypicks moments from the original game, tosses far too much out, and takes too many cues from the wrong pages of Resident Evil design over the years.

The biggest disappointment in this game comes in the form of the co-star of this game next to Jill Valentine; Nemesis. He's hyped up as the unstoppable force against you, and the rivalry you'll have to endure throughout the game from the word "go," yet the game seemed to completely miss the point of what made Nemesis special in the first place. The original Nemesis inspired Alien Isolation's Alien AI; a stalker that could hit you anytime, anywhere while you're looking for key items, weapons, ammo, or just trying to find the door to the next area. RE3 Remake, however, almost completely squanders this opportunity in favor of large, and often-scripted setpiece sequences that ring hollow and deflate a lot of the tension. By the end of the game, Nemesis barely feels like a threat and more of a mild nuisance who's only intimidating because the cinematics want to make us think he is. This hurts because the opening hour of the game shows what this dynamic could've been like had they decided to design their game around him and not on trying to make a big fireworks show of his rivalry with Jill.

Level design also took a serious blow. Where RE2make feels like it opened up the city outside the original's scope and vision, RE3make seemed to box itself in, lock a bunch of doors, and throw out a lot of the nice furniture along with it. The game starts as a continuation of the ideas RE2make began but then quickly devolves into linear action with very little room to maneuver or explore. It feels rushed, uncreative, and dispassionate, like a game that took the engine, assets, but had zero ambition and didn't want to add anything fresh or any new meaningful new mechanics that weren't checkboxes from the original game.

Speaking of mechanics, RE2 Remake added new ideas such as breakable knives, and how they and grenades could be used defensively when grabbed, or how the game supplied boards for shoring up windows to mitigate zombie spawns. These are abandoned, defaulting to an RE3 that feels far too safe, such as going back to unbreakable knives, no defenses against grabs, and even re-adds enemies that could one-hit kill you with a single lunge from the bad game design textbook of yore. The only (un)original idea this game attempts to introduce is mashing a quick-time event to mitigate damage when grabbed, which is something noticeably and lazily bolted on to a pre-existing RE2make animation.

So much of this is inferior to RE2 Remake in general, from the writing to the pacing, the level design and the boss design. Gimmicks replace player resourcefulness, parts of the story feel contrived to pad for time. Parts that were cut from the previous game's remake were substituted with new and interesting things, like RE2's orphanage and the way the "2nd Run" remixes the levels and enemy placements. This game, RE3, removes the decision branches from the original game that led to different encounters or strategies (and altering story beats) and doesn't replace them with anything.

Well, that's not entirely true. Enter Resident Evil Resistance.

For the other half of your game purchase, you're getting RE3's stab at a Dead by Daylight-style mode. One mastermind who can place zombies in an environment, four survivors to go against them. I've had enough time in the Open Beta to understand enough of the game's tricks and find it a bit underwhelming.

On top of missing basic features like a Push-to-Talk, the mode doesn't feel very well balanced. There are cheap instances in some maps where the Mastermind can overpower the players in confined spaces with Mr. X summons, and other times the players can completely shut down and disable the mastermind from being able to act if they're fast and coordinated enough. PC controls for the Mastermind are also awful, and some interface management as the survivors is finnicky and clumsy.

Compared to the inspiration, Dead by Daylight, the Killer in that game was often overpowered and can easily take out one player, but a coordinated enough group of players can use that time to keep tackling objectives, whereas a skilled enough Killer can figure out how to micromanage each player and pin them into corners with their abilities. In Resistance, the Mastermind is often underpowered and easily subdued by the hacker character the survivors can choose, limiting their options (which are already limited because of randomly occurring zombie spawns in a "deck" style format). Some powerful zombies can appear but they can't be manually controlled unlike the standard fare or the big boss types, meaning you're constantly fighting to score damage that can easily be treated and don't slow the players down enough when they're pushing with power weapons. Oh, and in Resistance, the players can respawn. The only penalty is to the Timer, which is increased by the survivors through zombie kills and teamwork, while hits and knockdowns reduce the time along with kills. This means players can respawn and still act instead of being taken out of the game to give the Mastermind a foothold, and the maps are broken up into "areas" instead of a single map to complete objectives. If the players all arrive at the door to the next area, the Mastermind instantly loses all their zombie spawns they made and are suddenly ejected into the next area.

It all just feels clumsy and somewhat stiff to play. Between inventory management as the survivors to using the camera views for zombie placement, to the Peer-to-Peer connection that can lag and stall the match to unpleasant degrees. Level design is really restricted, camera views are obstructed by quite a bit (and are easily shot out), the frequent commentary from the mastermind gets a little grating at times, it all comes off as a fun novelty that pales in comparison to its' competitors in balance and design.

---------

So in summary, RE3 feels like unambitious table scraps of RE2 and RE3, with little substance even on repeat playthroughs. It not only compromises a lot of what the original game offered and challenged, but it backtracked strides in design made by its predecessor feeling like a half-hearted recreation project with premade assets, and not a proper redesign. Resistance, meanwhile, never "feels" polished or balanced enough to stay past the novelty stage.

There's a lot of fun to be had here, and if you enjoyed the over-the-shoulder gameplay of the RE2 remake, you'll get more of that here. But you're basically playing a glorified expansion pack along with a shoddily executed multiplayer mode that might've compromised the package as a result. This game is worth playing, but absolutely not at $60.

If you played Resident Evil 2 Remake and enjoyed it, there is a good chance you will enjoy this game as well. Basically everything that made that game great is present here: creepy atmosphere, a return to survival horror, gruesome enemies and gory deaths, smooth gunplay, and excellent graphics. The only issue is it is very short (I beat it 6.5 hours on my first playthrough on Hardcore) and it banks on replaying the game multiple times on the harder unlockable difficulties (Nightmare and Inferno) to really get your money's worth out of it.

This isn't really a great excuse for this in my mind, because a majority of the game assets are copypasted from RE2R. A lot of things such as the engine, environments, zombie models, licker model, dog model, etc. were all directly ported over, so I don't see why this game couldn't have been at least 2 or 3 hours longer in playtime.

The game is also pretty linear. This is all very frustrating because this game had the potential to really improve on RE2R in basically every way, letting you explore Raccoon City during the outbreak, solve puzzles, and kill zombies, but instead you only get a very small slice of the experience. I still enjoy this game, but Capcom DESPERATELY needs to put out some free DLC like Mercenaries: Operation Mad Jackal or some mini-stories like they did for RE2R.

A bit of a hard sell at launch especially for those who played the original RE3, RE3 Remake is an action-packed but shorter experience compared to RE2 Remake. For most, it's worth playing at the right price.

[u][b]Full Review[/b][/u]

Resident Evil 3 has you playing as Jill Valentine, a surviving member of S.T.A.R.S. investigating the Umbrella Corporation after the events at the Arklay mansion. You start off right in the middle of the viral outbreak in Raccoon City as the bio-weapon known as Nemesis hunts you down and the chaos around you unfurls.

Game-play is very similar to Resident Evil 2 2019 as a 3rd person survival horror game, however with a few changes. The knife is no longer a one time use sub-weapon but something you keep for the entire game. As you play through the game, you'll see why. The game is a lot more aggressive than RE2, with zombie numbers greatly increased from RE2 and their attack patterns changed allowing for double lunges to try and take you out. To counter this, you also have the dodge mechanic, allowing you to either general dodge around enemies. If you time the dodge right before the enemy attack connects, you can perform a Perfect Dodge, allowing you to hold the aim button during a brief slow-mo window and the game will auto target you to the weak point of that enemy. When you include Nemesis and other enemy types you'll face, mastering the dodge and conserving ammo when possible becomes a requirement on harder difficulties. 

Speaking of Nemesis, he's one of the highlights of this game even in the beginning. He is a tyrant like Mr. X from RE2 however he has a lot more abilities & an arsenal of weapons that it'll use against you. I'm not going to detail much on him but know that he's way more aggressive than Mr. X, I would also suggest to play RE2 2019 1st as an introduction before you jump into this.

Environments especially in the beginning look great, it's the most realized we've seen Raccoon City so far with highly detailed storefronts with the city's attempts at maintaining quarantine and civil order sprinkled throughout. Later environments aren't as memorable as you go deeper into specific locations but they get the job done. Graphically it looks fantastic, Jill and the other humans look great with highly realistic facial modeling and motion capture. New enemies looks pretty good too with some being fairly unique (looking at you Hunter Gamma) but with a few downgrades. 

RE3 is actually a fork of the RE engine used in RE2 to facilitate the AI changes needed and the increased enemy count, the price in-game for that is the dismemberment system from RE2 is no longer the same. Limbs can no longer be separated in the same way, an example being in RE2 when you shoot the elbow joint of a zombie, you will see the forearm dangle around if a partial separation is achieved. You can shoot off all the limbs of a zombie and see it still struggle against you in RE2, it was a really fun way to mess with zombies and gives you a way to experiment with weak points in the future. That's not the case here in RE3, there is some basic limb separation provided there's enough damage but it's predictable and not always a direct benefit but just a indicator of health depending on the enemy. There is no longer the persistent bodies after you kill most enemies with some them eventually disappearing after a certain amount of time.

Now is a good a time as any to talk about more the heated elements that have come out about this game. The average 1st play-through is going to be 6-8 hours depending on how quickly you can make your way through the levels. When you complete your 1st play-through, cut-scenes do not count towards this and will likely show a completion of around 5 hours or less. I would agree with others in saying that there isn't enough here as is in RE3. What is here is a ton of fun but you can see where things have been rushed or outright cut from the game. 

The post-completion of the game isn't nearly as robust as RE2, there is a store unlocked to obtain extra items using points gained when completing record challenges in-game. Although in fairness, much of RE2's extra content is 80% the same as it's 1st run. The store in RE3 an ok reason for runs but you can use these items to get an S rank with no issues. S+ is not here so no bragging rights in RE3 if you happened to get that in RE2. I will mention for repeat runs it's holds up a lot more than RE2 with 2 additional difficulties to unlock that change the item placement as well as attack patterns and increased health\damage of enemies. Playing another run on standard or hardcore, Nemesis keeps things feeling fresh much longer than Mr. X.

Even with the cuts compared to the original. RE3 is a really good campaign. It's harder and faster game-play than RE2 with a lot less room for error. At $60, it's a hard sell with RE2 providing more content to try at a lower price point. I pre-ordered this at $45 and feel like I got my money's worth after completing my 2nd run and will continue to get more hours with repeat runs. You'll also receive Resident Evil Resistance with RE3 but I'll save my comments on that in its own review. If you are price sensitive at this time and aren't interested in Resistance, I would hold off on this until a price drop if you only plan on 1 play-through. As it stands, Resident Evil 3 Remake is a great roller-coaster ride and one of the best experiences in the Resident Evil catalog.
