Pros:
It's very cinematic. That was definitely the first thing I noticed when I played my first time.

Jill was a fun character to play as, and I appreciate they put her S.T.A.R.S. outfit in the game.

Nemesis was pretty intimidating, but there's a really big "but."

Looks fantastic, if not better than RE2: Remake. Maybe it's just because of the vibrant colors in the city compared to the drab colors of RPD and sewers.

I don't know why, but I liked the shop. It kind of reminded me of RE5 and all the neat unlockables it had. As long as there's no MTX I hope they expand it or something.

While I loved the horror atmosphere of RE2, I had a lot of fun blastin zombies in this game, and the dodge button's cool but sometimes it doesn't seem to work right or you dodge straight into another zombie. Guess all my time playing Dark Souls didn't help.

The train power station section really reminded me of Dead Space with the same intensity of being attacked by necromorphs. I really loved (or dreaded?) that part.

Cons:
Like what most people said, the game felt a little short. Took me around 4 1/2 hours to beat on standard. $60... a small part of me regrets spending that much.

Carlos's segments weren't that fun for me. I think it was the fact that zombies are bullet sponges and they threw so many in tight corridors.

Ok here's the big one. I think one of my main issues with the game is Nemesis. In my first playthrough before Nemesis chases you through the Downtown section, I had already unlocked everything I needed and fully explored the city. So once Nemesis appeared I just ran past him, he performed spinal realignment with his fist/tentagrab, I used herb, and continued on my merry way to the objective. 
Then that was it. Nemesis was tied to scripted moments and then he turned to stage 2. When I saw all the promotional stuff on the game, I was really looking forward to Nemesis. It conveyed this idea of Nemesis being Mr. X, BUT ON STEROIDS. Then I saw his gameplay and I was like woah! He's pretty intense. Then when you first meet him in the opening, I was like this is pretty intense. But after that it wasn't really that intense. It didn't help that I found out one grenade can knock him down during my second playthrough. 
I never really got a sense of tension or dread in my first play through like I did with Mr. X in RE2. For me, I felt that Nemesis wasn't used effectively in the game, and if I had to be honest, he didn't really leave that much of an impact on me throughout the game. The Hunter Gammas and Pale Heads left a bigger impact (granted the former is one shot kill and the latter is near unkillable). Maybe in harder difficulties he will have that intensity, but my overall impression of Nemesis wasn't that great.

Conclusion:
I never played the original Resident Evil 3 so I feel that I can't say whether or not it was a good remake or not, but as someone that's played nearly every game since RE4, I wanted a bit more from this game. Especially Nemesis stage 1. I really wanted more of him: scripted or free-roaming.

That's not to say I didn't enjoy it. I had a lot of fun, and would recommend buying this game if you see it on sale for $30-$40.

7/10 I would say it is a good game, just not the great game that I was personally hoping for.

I never played the original game so I come at this from a very different perspective to many providing reviews. 

This 'remake' is not as good as Resident Evil 2. But it is an excellent game in its own right. It is more action-packed than RE2 and certainly less tense. 

The game looks great, with excellent performances and cinematics, and it certainly runs very well on PC. 

It is a touch on the short side, although it does come with the multiplayer 'Resistance' game. But as with all RE games there is an incentive to play through the game multiple times either to accumulate game breaking items or test your speed running abilities. 

But if you are concerned about the amount of content at full price just wait for a sale. At 30% off or 50% off this game is a no-brainer and a thoroughly enjoyable game from start-to-finish.

I will say flat-out that the original version of [i]Resident Evil 3: Nemesis[/i] is my favorite game in the series. I think it's important to include this information because it heavily influences my perspective on the remake of [b]Resident Evil 3[/b] in many ways.

The first thing we have to address is the game's length; do I feel like it's too short for its' day-one asking price? Possibly. There is an argument to be made in either direction, but I personally feel like I got the full $59.99 out of the game on just my first full playthrough. That doesn't mean that I had no desire for the game to be longer when I beat it because there is obvious room for additional content; I'm kinda bummed out by their decision to exclude the City Park location from the remake as it has always been my favorite self-contained location from any game in the series. On the other hand, more is not always better. Many games are too long or have too much repetitive "content padding" for their own good. ::cough[i]Assassin'sCreed[/i]cough:: For my part, I feel like this issue is down to a matter of personal taste and mileage will vary from person to person.

Graphically and musically, they have cleared the same high bar that they set for themselves with the remake of [i]Resident Evil 2[/i]; perhaps my only complaint here is the lack of an option to enable the musical score from the [i]RE3:Nemesis[/i] as was possible in the previous remake. The translation, writing, voice acting, and pacing mark an enormous improvement over [i]RE3:N[/i] unless you're a diehard fan of campy horror and/or you're really into seeing where the insanely over-the-top shark-jumping moments that virtually destroyed [i]Resident Evil 6[/i] began to appear in the series; the scene where Jill uses a magnum to shoot down a helicopter comes to mind.

The user-interface is nothing to write home about but serves its' purpose adequately; I feel like the learning curve for dodging is somewhat too high, and quick-turning is less responsive in this game than it was in [i]ReRE2[/i]. Overall, these factors make the difficulty fluctuate wildly. At the time that it was released, [i]Resident Evil 3: Nemesis[/i] was considered by many casual-type players to be quite tough even on the lower difficulty settings. That being said, a lot of the gameplay problems with both versions of [i]RE3[/i] are easily overcome with practice and shouldn't affect most fans of the series or enthusiast-type gamers.

As far as I am concerned, the true selling point for this game are the boss fights, which are especially great when you consider that major battles in the series-as-a-whole tend not to be very good. Without spoiling anything that you can't already guess from the title screen, the second and third battles against Nemesis are amazing and are easily in my top five boss fights in the series. I'd also like to give a small nod to all the content they added to Carlos' role in [i]ReRE3[/i] over its' predecessor; as much as I love Jill, Chris, Leon, and Claire, it's always nice to have a "new" perspective to see things from... unless that perspective belongs to Piers or Helena, but that's a story for another time.

All-in-all, I'd say the game is a very solid 8-out-of-10 or a 9-out-of-10 if I'm feeling particularly generous. It might be a touch too short, the difficulty jumps all over the place, the PC optimization seems pretty good, and the controls rest on a bit of a learning curve, but the game is beautiful to look at, sounds amazing, is well-written, and has some of the best boss fights in the entire [i]Resident Evil[/i] series. As a long-time fanboy of the original, this game gets my seal-of-approval as a spiritual successor to one of the greatest survival horror games of all-time.

It's good.  Anyone saying otherwise... I dunno.  The only REALLY valid critique I could entertain is that it's short.  It is short.  I finished my first playthrough in about 5 hours, and every playthrough after that in 3 hours or less.  It's much shorter than the original.  I can understand the disappointment about that, and the developers should have included more game.  That much is true.  But the game is really meant to be beaten multiple times, so if you're only going to play through it once, I can understand the price tag looking steep for a mere 5 hours.  

There's a great game inside though.

This is no walk in the park.  As you go up in difficulty, you get more and more of a true survival horror game.  Nightmare is where the game hits its stride, and is no walk in the park, even with the extra weapons unlocked.  Even normal zombies are very aggressive in Nightmare, and Nemesis is not only relentless, but appreciably more powerful.   This is one of my few complaints, but I'll talk about that more in a second.  The game includes a whopping five difficulty levels - Assisted, Normal, Hardcore, Nightmare, and Inferno - so you can dial it to whatever masochistic setting you want and enjoy your experience.  The lowest three difficulty levels are mostly the same except the notable difference of Assisted having dramatically weaker enemies, extra starting weapons, and the fact that you auto heal to "Caution" without the need of healing items.  Other than that, the placement of items for the lowest three difficulties is the same, or largely the same, and the difficulty ramps up nominally from one setting to the next.

Nightmare changes everything.  More enemies, different types of enemies in different locations, new and more aggressive movesets for all enemies, item locations changed, ammo drastically reduced, a FAR more powerful and aggressive Nemesis, and on and on.  This mode really sends you reeling with all of this combined.  Everything you thought you knew is different, and the increased damage taken makes this a particularly painful learning curve.  I'd put Nightmare mode on par with the original RE3's hard mode, save that even normal enemies are extremely deadly.  Your first encounter with the no-longer-sluggish zombies in the opening scene is a real shock.   There is one complaint I do have to register about Nightmare, and that is that Nemesis' first and third forms and somewhat poorly designed.  Both of these forms contain a multi-hit combo that you cannot live through or dodge if the first hit connects.  I feel like this had to be an oversight, or something that went untested.  Either way, it makes the final fight an EXTREMELY arduous one.  It's really not fun when you can't make a single mistake or you have to start over.

(As of this writing I have not yet played Inferno, but I imagine it's going to be rough)

The lack of mercenaries mode from the original game is a sad surprise, as it was many peoples' favorite part of the game.  It makes a little bit of sense, however, as this game is split into several distinct geographical locations that aren't linked, whereas the original game had a very long connected area in which to put this extra mode.  I rather hope it's released as a DLC in the future (Any DLC would be extremely welcome, come to think of it), but I won't hold my breath.   As a replacement for it, you are given achievements to earn throughout your playthroughs that earn you in-game currency with which you can buy powerful items to help you along your way.  These range from RE7-ish attack/defense coins, coins that regenerate your health passively, extra inventory slots, and the always-coveted infinite-ammo guns.  A modest playthrough on normal should net you enough currency to buy an infinite ammo pistol which is already a game changer for future playthroughs.  A couple of runs later, and you can be sporting some helpful coins, inventory slots, and an infinite ammo Assault Rifle, which will make Nightmare slightly less of a ... nightmare.

The game runs and looks well.  I did not have any noticeable slow-downs at any point, though there is a very noticeable phasing of enemy animations which will cause their movements to look slow and stuttered if they're far away.  With one notable exception there's never enough enemies on screen at any time to really make me think this was necessary, but perhaps the console versions struggle at times?  Who knows?  Either way, it was definitely by design.  Gunplay feels fantastic.  True to the difference between the original RE2 and RE3, this remake is much more action-focused, and you're given more ammo to deal with the increased enemy count.  I've seen some people complain about this but personally, I always like RE3 the best for this particular reason.

I hope, though don't expect, that some DLC will come out for this in the future.  Whether it's the Mercenaris mode or something else.  Even without that, this game is well worth the asking price, is a great if not-particularly faithful remake of the original, and is certainly a challenging and worthy entry in this historic series.

THIS RESIDENCY IS DEPRESSINGLY VACANT

PROS:
1. graphics sure are a lot better than the original's! 
2. Carlos went from annoying side character in OG version to upstaging Jill in terms of personality and redesign in the remake
3. Nicholai is an awesome villain
4. Dodge mechanic is still welcome after all these years and is fun to pull off. 

CONS:
1. Soundtrack is terrible (read: nonexistent). Maybe one good track during the last section, but that's it. 
2. Jill's redesign is an homogenized, generic mess compared to her original version, concerning both attire and personality. 
3. Game runs worse than RE 2 Remake somehow, at least on my machine
4. Nemesis redesign is so bad it almost makes Jill's redesign look inspired by comparison. 
5. Nemesis is VERY poorly utilized in this iteration. Went from Mr. X on steroids to a glorified set piece instigator some 20 years later. 
6. An hour shorter than the original version, with only a fraction of the content to boot. 
7. Many areas from original have been cut from the game, making this 60 dollar purchase seem like overpriced DLC to RE 2: Remake. 
8. Nightmare mode and Inferno mode are gimmicks at best
9. Very little replay value, especially compared to the original titles (one unlockable outfit! In the words of Jill herself:  "Are you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kidding me?")

Let me be clear before I get into the nit and gritty: I enjoyed the three hour ride. I enjoyed perforating zombies with shotgun shells and dodging Nemesis like Jill was a DragonBall Z character. But this was unequivocally not worth 60 dollars. Classic locations from the original are outright gone, characters are butchered beyond all recognition upon the altar of censorship, and the game overall just feels like a husk of what Resident Evil 3 used to mean to me. Like a zombie, if you will. I mean, the thing is clearly moving on two legs and seems sentient. But it's just a walking corpse. It is undeniably bereft of anything that could be considered a soul. 

Jill now curses more than a sailor on shore leave, and her new personality is abrasive to say the least. I don't mind a few F bombs myself, but Jill Valentine has always been classier than this, and that goes for both REmake and the original Resident Evil 3. The opening section is very interesting though in what it supposedly foreshadows or tries to set up. But like the remake itself, it feels incomplete, like a question half-pondered. I could write a 20 page thesis paper on everything so incredibly wrong about this new Jill, along with the story beats and her subsequent character interactions. But I know the internet doesn't have that kind of attention span, so I'm going to end my criticism of this Jill impostor here.  I will say though, that Jill now feels like every other run-of-the-mill female protagonist/co-star in video-games nowadays. And her VA can't act. Moving on. 

As far as gameplay goes, I don't have any particular qualms. It's RE 2 Remake but with added mobility, which is welcome.  But certain bosses on Nightmare or Inferno mode feel like they weren't balanced at all. Let me explain using a simple term: stun-lock. When Jill gets hit on the higher difficulties the first time, you feel fine because you know you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. But it's when enemies suddenly have the power to hit Jill repeatedly while leaving her UNABLE to dodge or counterattack, the frustration is instantaneous and gets exponentially worse with each passing death.  

There is barely any exploration in this game. During the second half of the game, I felt like I was playing Resident Evil 6 again, only with slightly more polish and budget. RE 3 OG was certainly more action-oriented compared to its predecessors, but the developers of this remake took to that approach a bit too emphatically.  The Raccoon City segment feels like it should have been at least an hour longer, and with so many of the other classic locations removed, the game will more than likely end before you realize it. 

Oddly enough, it is during the Carlos sections that you get the most opportunity to explore. This is great and all, but I was hoping to do the same thing as Jill. Don't get me started on the replay value, because compared to the many other titles RE 3: Remake has less substance than a single-celled organism. Only one unlockable outfit, and it looks like a cheap cosplay attempt at the classic Jill Valentine from the mansion days. 

Game can be finished 100% in the span of a weekend.  Even if you discount the unlockables and weapons with infinite ammo, there is still very little to call the player back for repeat play-throughs. Gone are the branching paths, the exhilaration of Nemesis constantly being on your heels, and the sense of exploration and nuanced puzzle-solving.  Again, I enjoyed the ride, but in hindsight, I shouldn't have paid more than 20 dollars for this. 

It is as clear as a Resident Evil epilogue daybreak that this game was given nowhere near the same amount of care and love as RE 2: Remake, and it shows in almost every facet of the game.  Like going on a ride at a Disney theme park you enjoyed the time for what it was, but still end up feeling hollow and fleeced by the end of it.  If this game was  20 dollars, you would see a thumbs up instead of a thumbs down.

Fiz no modo intenso, analisando detalhes de todos os cenários, lendo cartas, files, cartazes, fotos etc. Foram 11 horas. Tudo isso fez a experiência com o jogo valer a pena. Deixar de lado o fator nostalgia e jogar o com a mente aberta faz toda a diferença. Terminado o modo intenso, recomecei no modo padrão e desta vez terminei em 4 horas. A dica para quem ainda não jogou: comece no intenso! Os modos inferiores são muito fáceis e as batalhas principais são ridículas, ao contrário dos modos difíceis que levam o jogo para um nível muito mais tenso e divertido. Há diferenças nas ações dos inimigos que fazem o intenso ser bem mais dinâmico.
Para mim ficou perfeitamente compreensível do porquê de terem alterado alguns pontos cruciais. O original pode ser tudo aquilo que amamos, nostalgicamente falando, mas precisamos encarar que algumas coisas são superficiais demais. A nova versão é muito mais densa em relação a história, aos personagens e à própria jogabilidade. Sabemos que o RE3 original foi feito às pressas e isso deixou alguns furos de trama que, desta vez, a Capcom soube SIM desenvolver bem. 
1- Tiraram a Clock Tower? Aquele lugar era um espaço limitado que nada mais servia para fazer o sino tocar. A CAPCOM achou que no contexto fazer um sino tocar para um helicóptero aparecer estava fora da realidade dos planos da U.B.C.S. E eu concordo, embora a nostalgia da cena do Nêmesis explodindo o helicóptero fale alto. Todos nós sentimos falta disso pois fomos trollados  pensando que ali era o fim do jogo. 
2- Tiraram o cemitério porque aqueles mortos que saiam da terra era um erro grave na trama, já que o vírus não pode contaminar cadáveres. E não sei para que tanta nostalgia em cima daquele cemitério, que não passava de um cercado bem limitado. Se fosse para enterrar pessoas vivas ou infectadas, ninguém iria fazer isso num cemitério. Qual a razão?  (O cemitério improvisado na frente da delegacia fez muito mais sentido).
3- Deram bastante ênfase neste lado policial investigativo que no original não tinha. O apartamento da Jill, com ela suspensa dos STARS depois da mansão, fazendo investigação sozinha, ligando os fatos naquele quadro. Ligando Anette, Umbrella, Irons. As pílulas contra ansiedade e estresse ao lado da cama, todo um cuidado nos detalhes que não havia no anterior e que fizeram uma boa diferença. 
4- O Hospital e a inclusão do cientista e da vacina deram mais realidade ao que era vago demais no original. Alias, os files que entram em detalhes sobre as BOWS, sobre Nemesis etc foram um grande ponto, explicando bem coisas que nunca ficaram claras nos jogos anteriores. 
5- Nemesis continua implacável e todas as cenas de ação dele são bem mais épicas do que a maioria das aparições do original. A tensão também está lá quando você joga no intenso, com pouca munição e itens de cura. (Toda a sequência até o topo do edifício e a batalha lá em cima foi o ponto icônico deste jogo, por sinal) 
6- A delegacia e toda a ligação com o RE2 foi tudo o que qualquer fã sempre pediu. Até com direito a reprise de lickers. 
7- Brad no original nada mais era do que um cara acovardado, fugindo, sem utilidade. Pelo menos nesta versão ele ajudou a Jill desde o início e se ‘sacrificou’ para que ela continuasse. A ligação com Marvin foi uma boa sacada. Poderia ter sido morto por Nemesis na frente da Jill? Até poderia, vai do fator nostalgia.
8- O grave digger foi incorporado bem ao Hunter. A “minhoca” e o “sapão” que antes tinham uma participação bem simples, sem nexo, ganharam mais efeito com essa releitura. A Capcom se tocou que uma minhoca e um sapo mutante era algo cômico, então decidiu pegar a ideia dos dois e criar uma BOW nova, mais ‘interativa’. 
9- Ver o início do caos na cidade e escutar ela morrer aos poucos, com as ruas ficando em silencio gradativamente foi uma ótima sacada. Por isso que quando Leon chega na cidade, tudo já está ‘morto’. 
10- Quem precisa de uma Dead Factory quando se tem um NEST 2 abaixo do Hospital como uma alternativa muito mais plausível. A ideia de mostrar o local em Raccoon City onde as Bows estavam sendo secretamente armazenadas foi sensacional. Fato que o original nem cogitou em um file sequer. Sem mencionar todo o contexto que criarem neste ambiente. 
11- O que eu senti falta de verdade: poder escolher por situações. O fator replay perde um pouco já que no game há uma única versão. Re2 sofreu com isso quando cortaram o cenário A + B.  Outro momento que achei que poderia ter sido melhor foi a explosão da cidade. Aqui, eu realmente senti falta de mais detalhes. O original mostrava vários pontos conhecidos explodindo. Embora muito bem feito, esperava mais da cena final. 
Eu sou fã desde sempre e sei bem o que é o fator nostalgia que eu tanto mencionei acima. Mas não posso ficar cego por isso e nem ter a mente limitada. De uma forma geral considero o game muito bem elaborado, produzido e inteligente. Não concordo quando dizem que fizeram o jogo às pressas, com preguiça. Pelo contrário, fizeram uma releitura com um background incrível, tanto em RE2 como em RE3!

The actual review:  To say this game is a let down is an understatement, its been a very long time since ive finished a game I really looked forward to and walked away feeling entirely unsatisfied. On the whole the game somehow feels more like a beta test for RE 2 than it feels like RE 3. The game is far shorter than the original version or RE2 , my finished game time on normal while having actually explored around for items,upgrades, etc, was almost 5 hours on the dot.

While the game does feel very good on PC in terms of controls, It cant help the game when alot of the enemy types have one shot kill mechanics that they seemingly decide to do on a whim rather than have to reach a threshold (Example, you being on caution for an insta kill), the weapons are lesser in almost every way from the original and the name sake of the game, the nemesis is tied down to only afew small scripted area's , unlike Mr.X whom patrolled the entire police station and you could hear stomping around (which would cause you to have to think about your pathing), Nemi also suffers from the ability to drop from the sky like a murderous batman to stun lock you with a 3 hit kill. In short, he is a joke and artificially hard rather than a threat.

Dodging returns into the game, from the original , but feels pointless, sure you can get a slow time and power attack with a perfect dodge, but I never needed it, either the enemy would rush me with an insta kill attack or would get blown away far before I ever needed to even learn how to use the dodge properly.

The game itself interms of story is mostly on point though they hacked up what they deemed to be unimportant so much that it feels weird, there are no branching paths through the game (which takes away from later play through's) and their is only one boss in the entire game..correction..there are several bosses but all the same one slightly different barring mutations that you fight once then never handle again. 

I could go on and on about several other things in the game but frankly ive said all I need to on this, I have no desire to pick the story mode back up again. If you dont care about the original or just have money to burn, get it, otherwise just buy RE 2 remake, its way better.

Resident Evil 3 REmake is another FANTASTIC addition to the Resident Evil universe and continues CAPCOMS strong streak of great Resident Evil games. While not as good as Resident Evil 2 (and much shorter), the game is still very good and deserves as much attention as the previous title received.

The most problematic thing about this game is the fact that the campaign is roughly 5-6 hours and that is if you search for essentially everything. If you are a more casual gamer, it can probably take you an hour less. For a $60 price tag, that is a LOT to ask. It comes with a multiplayer component as well, but even this addition doesn't justify the price tag. You can replay the game MULTIPLE times, and beat it in mere hours (I literally just beat the game in 2 hours and 15 min real time). For completionists like myself, this is really nice. You can also skip all of the cutscenes, which makes it a lot breezier to go through. I would've liked there to be some option to skip the opening though, as its all on rails (you can skip cutscenes, but not these bits). That being said, a longer campaign would've been nice to see. There is also a lot of original material that was stripped from this game, which is disappointing especially for hardcore fans of the original.

The short length doesn't completely derail the game, as this is probably the best 5 hour game I have ever played. The polish is still there from the RE2 Remake, and the game runs flawlessly. I don't think I ever had a single FPS dip, and never crashed once. In an age where AAA titles release with mass amounts of bugs, this is a pleasant sight to behold. The gameplay is also as good as its ever been, with the new "dodge" mechanic adding to the more action feel of the game. The pacing is also lightning fast too, so there is never really a moment where you feel bored playing this. The only gripes I would say is the weirdly low fps locks on zombies that are far away and the lack of gore compared to the 2nd one.

Sound design and music is tremendous as per usual, and nothing to really complain about here. If I am being nitpicky, I would say that the Nemesis "STARS" isn't as scary as it used to be, but it could just be that I'm older now. Also on that note, Nemesis isn't really that scary at all in this game. I feel like I feared MR X a lot more, mainly because of the enclosed areas and the unpredictability of him. Nemesis has a lot of scripted events, and nothing really felt like it was random or out of the blue. The Nemesis fights can be tricky though, especially if you don't have any grenades, as these puppies can knock him down in one hit. Fighting him is worth it though, as you can get upgrades for your guns.

I love the Resident Evil franchise and have no regrets purchasing this game (even at full price). Still, this game is spectacular for what it brings to the table and gives me hope for the Resident Evil franchise going forward.

After spending a lot of time with this game and completing it 100%,, I cannot recommend this game at full price. The content simply isn't there to justify it. Numerous sections were removed from the game which include: Clock Tower, Park, and Cemetery. This content was removed for no other reason than rushing this to market in my opinion. There is not even multiple endings or choices to make in the game which hinders replay value greatly. If you're not interested in higher difficulties or getting all of the achievements then the replay factor isn't there. 

Also, several enemy types were removed. Crows, spiders, brain suckers, and the iconic grave digger are not present in this game. The decision to stray so far the source material shows that this dev team lacked vision and that this project should have been left in the hands of the team the that created the RE2 Remake. The decision by these devs to take so many liberties with the story and enemies was a mistake.

Why is there no mercenaries? Seriously. Again, I feel like this was due to wanting this hitting the market ASAP. No one asked for project resistance and quite honestly I think this multiplayer will be dead in a few weeks. It was bundled with a gimped version of RE3 to get sales. I wouldn't put it past Capcom to release mercenaries as paid DLC at this point. Hell, there may be clock tower DLC for sale as well in the future.

Another thing I want to point out is the lack of unlockable costumes and the ranking system. The original had like 7 costumes to unlock. We have one unlockable costume and the classic costume if you preordered the game. The classic costume has been altered as well. Yes, those are shorts... they cannot even make the classic costume have a skirt like the original game. Thank you modders for saving the day. As far as rankings, there is no longer the S+ rank nor costumes locked behind certain ranks. Yet again this was a clear opportunity to get people to replay the game multiple times that was missed. 

At the end of the day this could have been an amazing game if the right people created it. With all of the cut content it is truly a disappointment. It is a good game but falls way short its potential. Hopefully Capcom fixes the mess they created with some true fan service by adding back the playable areas with Jill as well as the missing enemies in a free DLC that fits right into the main story and expands it. Operation Mad Jackal should be added as well. If/when this is the case I will recommend this game.

Resident Evil 3:
~~~~~~~~~~~~ 
The T-Virus created by the Umbrella Corporation is spreading rapidly within the population of Raccoon City. Most of the civilians are now infected and time is running out for those who have managed to survive so far. One of them is Jill Valentine, who is part of the Special Tactics and Rescue Service (S.T.A.R.S).  Jill has been described as a femme fatale if you ever go head to head with her.  Despite the overwhelming chaos, she teamed up with one of the last agents from the U.B.C.S. (Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service) to find a way to either save or escape the city. It’s time to experience the wild ride of Resident Evil 3!

Resident Evil 3 (remake) is a third-person/action/horror zombie game developed and self-published by CAPCOM Co., Ltd. on the 3rd of April 2020 on Steam, Xbox One and PS4! 

In the early to mid-’90s, when the first Resident Evil was released, I was mostly interested in Football (soccer) and first-person shooter games. At that time, I enjoyed playing games as a recreation after work. The Resident Evil series never caught my eye for some reason, and I probably missed something special from that era. In recent years, I started to be intrigued by the Resident Evil franchise, especially when Resident Evil 7 came out in 2017. From then on, I enjoyed playing Resident Evil 2 (remake) and now Resident Evil 3. I won’t make any comparisons between this remake and the original, as I haven’t played the original.

The game has 3 levels of difficulty: Assisted, Standard and Hardcore. After you’ve made your selection, the game will start with a video introduction on the chaos that Raccoon City is experiencing with the T-Virus, which was manufactured by the Umbrella Corporation. From here you’ll be playing Jill first, and let me tell you, it will knock your socks off straight away as she will be pursued from the beginning by a fairly big monster. She will have a few Rendez-Vous with this monster throughout the game, and every time they meet, the monstrosity will become more prominent and harder to beat. 

Not too far into the game, the character named Carlos will appear, and from then, you’ll be playing Jill in some chapters and Carlos in others.  On your first play as Carlos, you’ll find that he has better weaponry than Jill.  Jill, on the other hand, will be able to carry items such as a lockpick which will be very helpful for opening lockers, suitcases and doors that have a key lock on them. 

It’s pretty much a game in which you have to follow the tasks and try to survive the onslaught of zombies and encounters with the Nemesis (monster). To make things slightly harder, you’ll be limited in ammunition from the start. But don’t despair, you’ll find some ammunition here and there within the locations that you visit. You’ll also find items that you can combine to create additional ammunition and health. Your inventory will be restricted to eight items at first, but you’ll find a few hip pouches throughout the game. 

The levels are well-designed, and you can access the level map at any time, which will show you where you are, which areas you have or haven’t visited, along with items that you’ve seen but didn’t pick up. 

There is an auto-saving, but if you want to save your progress, you can only do it in the rooms with the old style typewriter. 

I really like the different types of zombies and creatures you meet in RE3. The interesting point is that I find my first few encounters with the Nemesis more difficult early on in the game than towards the end. 

For me, the most significant impact was these incredible pursuits Jill has with Nemesis, which are part of the playing cut-scene before each of the fights against him. I experienced several moments of what the f…….. ,and jumped a few times off my chair! It is impressive the way they managed to make me, as a player, feel involved in these pursuits. Just brilliant!  

The game is relatively short; within 7 hours, you’ll have finished your first playthrough, but the game offers good replayability in the form of a grade. When you complete the game, you’ll be rated and given points for challenges that you accomplished during the game. These points can be used to unlock items and costumes for your next playthrough. 

Superb graphics, great soundtracks and good voice-overs, but  the initial price tag of A$90 + seems to be a bit steep for a game of that length. Yes, they are providing a multiplayer offshoot, Resident Evil Resistance, which is a 1 vs 4 but I would suspect this multiplayer option will probably soon be forgotten.  

Positives:
~~~~~~~ 
+	Fabulous graphics
+	Good Soundtrack and voice over
+	Well-designed levels
+	Great looming and deadly atmosphere
+	Fabulous pursuit with a WTF factor
+	Achievements and trading cards

Negatives:
~~~~~~~~ 

-	A short game for the initial price tag 

Resident Evil 3 will make you jump out of your chair more than once! A very well composed game.

8/10

That was surprising for me considering I beat the RE2R on Hardcore the same way and it took almost 10 hours on Leon 1st run. The two things I wish would of been in the game is an expanded clock tower segment instead of just a boss fight outside of it and also the entire park segment that they removed. Well I guess to preface this review I have to start with this. I am a massive resident evil fan. Ive played almost every game of the series and grew up with them. I want to be able to give this game a blue thumb and recommend it for people new and experienced in the RE franchise to buy this game and play it as while it lasts the game is very fun to play and looks gorgeous. However I cannot do this because this game has alot of massive issues. For one thing this game cost $60. It took me 5 hours for my first playthrough on the hardcore difficulty. A friend of mine beat in in 4 and a half hours. About 30 minutes of this is running down linear paths from Nemesis to enter the boss fights. There is no bonus game modes such as mercenaries to add extra time. This by far makes it the shortest resident evil campaign on a blind playthrough for the average player. A 4 to 5 hour game has no reason to cost $60 especially when so much of it is linear and more cinematic then true interactive gameplay. There is several cut areas, enemies, the game altering choices, and a boss fight from the original game. There is no excuse for this other then greed and laziness. There is a TON of reused assets from the Resident Evil 2 remake, and while this is not in itself a bad thing because it takes place in the same city with a few of the same enemies and environments so that just makes sense. What this does do is beg the question how the hell is the game so short? When you have so much of the game that is already made how do you not have the time and resources to expand the game and add new sections and redesign old sections and enemies. Especially when the game is so linear, which also isnt a bad thing as Resident Evil 4 is linear and is my favorite game in the series. Difference is Resident Evil 4 had a 18-24 hours campaign with mercenaries mode, a side campaign for Ada, and another small mission for Ada as well, and this game started from ground up with no reused assets. This game is a bad example of a remake as it added little of value and took away a ton. The reason Resident Evil 1 remake is considered to be so good is that it did nothing but add content and improve on the old. This while bringing a modern spin to the original took away too much content for it to be considered a good remake. Nemesis himself while cool and fun to interact with only shows up for boss fights and does not follow you around enough otherwise to make him feel anything like he does in the original. There is a random unpolished things such as reloading animations and low resolution zombies moving at 5 frames per second outside a window during one section.
With the lack of content, $60 price tag, and unpolished parts my final rating Is gonna end up being a 6.5/10. The game is fun and would deserve a much higher rating if it was longer. If this game cost $20 bucks I would maybe give it an 8 or even a bit higher but as it stands it just isnt a complete game and it pains me to tell you to not buy this game unless can get it on sale for $20 or $30 as it feels more like a dlc for 2 then a full game.

Fan of the series from the beginning (though I fell off through the dark years of RE 6 and ORC) and I give this one hearty recommendation with a few caveats.

This is not a shot-for-shot remake of RE3 as everyone knows and honestly I'm glad. If that is what you want don't buy this.

RE3R is more action-heavy than RE2R, just like RE3 to RE2. If that bothers you don't buy this.

If a lack of crows or spiders (enemies I just run past) or a giant penis boss bothers you don't buy this.

These are the most common and silly complaints I see. The game is great and feels like a natural extension of RE2R like RE3 felt to RE2. The dodge mechanics make for incredible amounts of mobility, Nemesis (especially on Nightmare) feels extremely threatening, the sound design on the weapons is excellent and the dialogue is a huge step-up from RE2R. Jill feels significantly more believable than OG (hard-boiled detective struggling with PTSD after watching close friends die) and Carlos is downright likable as opposed to the chump he was in the OG. I get the rationale for the hate and of course wish that the game was more expansive, but that's only so that I could play it for longer. It's a good problem to have.

The actual gripes: lack of unlockable costumes (yeah mods, but still...) and lack of Merc mode. With the heavier action focus and mobility boost this last point is the most egregious to me. Fingers crossed for DLC.

All in all, it's fun, tells a tight story, has expanded difficulty options and an unlock system that allows for player choice. Good game.

This REALLY should've been DLC for the RE2 remake. If there was a "neutral" rating, that's what I'd choose. I'm rating this positive because at least it's not broken and is enjoyable the first time around. The game is just too short. RE2 remake at least has A and B scenarios, even if the differences were pretty minor. RE3 has only 1 scenario. My first playthrough was a little over 4 hours. My biggest gripe is Nemesis. He is such a huge step down from RE2 remake's Mr. X. Nemesis in OG RE3 was a step up from Mr. X in OG RE2 and Mr. X in RE2 remake was a HUGE step up from Nemesis in OG RE3. Where Mr. X would stalk you dynamically (and some scripted events) around the police station in RE2 remake, Nemesis is entirely scripted in this remake, probably addressing the people that hated Mr. X's constant presence in RE2 remake. Turning Nemesis into scripted encounters that herd you into the direction you need to go was definitely not the right balance for those that didn't like Mr. X. The level design seems to be a little off too. Exploration in RE2 remake could lead to whole rooms with goodies. This remake's "exploration" boils down to either go down the hallway you're supposed to or turn the other direction with a shorter hallway that leads nowhere but has some ammo or collectible. This game comes with a multiplayer mode "Resistance." I have no intention in even touching that mode no matter how good it is. Resources and time spent developing that mode should've went into the main game. There's just a lot less game here. Even RE3's Mercenaries mode and the live selection scenarios from OG RE3 are gone. A very slight step up from the RE2 remake are the boss fights. Boss fights usually involve more than just "shoot at it until it dies." A positive and negative is defense. This game has a dodge mechanic (even if it uses the same animation from Revelations 2) which is nice and your knife no longer has a durability. However, this comes at the cost of no defensive options when grabbed. When grabbed, you have to mash a button to mitigate damage. You will always take damage but mashing the button stops further damage. I'm not a huge fan of being so negative about a game in a series that I absolutely adore but it's important to address its problems. This is a definite buy at $20 and maybe $30 USD at most.

This game does really well in the horror department. They toned down the aggression in the zombies and gave them an eerier edge, which was a good change. The art direction is really good too, earlier areas sporting a really good contrast between light/dark which is necessary for a good horror atmosphere. The beginning area was a challenge of item management and door unlocking tangled up in a fairly intricate level structure, and was a pretty enjoyable experience. But this is Resident Evil, so the developers weren't having that and threw in a bunch of amusement park rides and clumsy boss battles to pad the game out between some forgettable survival horror segments because RE4 did it too. I'll give the game credit for not having Nemesis be three feet from you at all times like Mr. X was. There was a segment straight out of Half-Life 2 where you hold down an area against waves of enemies until your partner hacks into the mainframe or whatever. The mechanics are awkward on purpose, so I don't understand why a pure-gameplay segment would be in a game like this. To top things off, the game can be beaten in two sittings.

Like the past two RE games, the dialogue is buried under a mountain of swear words. I'm not bothered by swears, but I don't see the use in having so many dispersed throughout the writing. Is it for realism? Most people aren't big swearers. Even police officers who get guns pointed at them during routine traffic stops don't let out the amount of swears these characters do. It just seems like the game is trying too hard to be cynical. Most of the memos you find in the game are written by handrubbing, greedy stereotypes. If it's to serve the atmosphere, it actually detracts from it because of how unnatural it is. Isn't the purpose of this game's world to trick you into thinking Raccoon City actually existed in our world's United States? But then you have to outrun a gigantic model of a cartoon character's head like a boulder before leaving the first area. So is this game ridiculous on purpose? But I thought RE3 was remade to give it a more grounded edge, but if we're just going to throw every ounce of restraint out the window and have you finish off Nemesis the same way DOOM Guy finished off the Spider Mastermind, what was even the point? REmake completely cut the camp out of RE1, RE2 did somewhat; Resident Evil 3 hardly tried. Furthermore, wasn't the entire series rebooted with Resident Evil 7 because fans ripped RE6 to shreds for being too over-the-top? None of this makes any sense. Oh wait, they remade this game because of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nostalgia.

Theatrical flavor aside: if you too fail to see the point in pointless remakes, point your wallet at something else.

Resident Evil 3 had the potential to be a great game but unfortunately, it is not. It is, by no means a bad game. It's just not on the same standard of Resident Evil 2 remake.

Pros: The story is still great. Jill looks/sounds amazing and has a pretty cool personality. Carlos is also very well-designed. The graphics are amazing and depending on your PC specs, the character models could come to uncanny valley. The controls are responsive and the dodge button is nice welcome addition. Dodge is not easy to pull off so you need to practice a lot and wait for the right to pull that off. The soundtrack is amazing and if you still remember the soundtrack of the original Resident Evil 3, the it will hit you in the feels. Nemesis is also well designed and not easy to put down. He will run towards you to bridge the gap between you and him.

Cons: The game feels linear and doesn't feel as open as it's predecessor or even the original PS1 classic, which is a shame really because the game is set in a city. The Downtown area is open and you can use multiple routes to avoid Nemesis but once you are out of that area, you are pretty much on a straight path. Puzzles are pretty much non-existent in the game. There seems to be more focus on action in this game than horror. Jump scares and scripted moments work in this game but when it came to the atmosphere, I found Carlos's section more effective than Jill's. The campaign is short. I finished it in 5 hours.

Nemesis (IMPORTANT): Nemesis doesn't roam around looking for you like Mr. X. It can be good and bad. The good thing about that is that since the appearance of Nemesis is scripted, the confrontation feels more epic and valued. The bad thing is: the game did feel as tense as Resident Evil 2 did with Mr. X.

Overall, the game is alright. It had the potential to be better than Resident Evil 2 but falls short. It is a must buy for Resident Evil fans but not at full price. Wait for a price slash and it will be worth you money.

This game was a fun ride, but a disappointing remake. I had high hopes after playing RE2R and all that hope was squashed to bits about halfway through the game when I realized what they had done. While RE2 was a great example at how to do a remake, I honestly believe this one is a great example at how NOT to do a remake.

To begin, the complaint from myself and most other people: cut content. This should be a MAJOR sin for any "remake". When remaking something, you shouldn't be cutting stuff so it "is more realistic" or "flows better" (or whatever excuse they'd try to give), you should be EXPANDING on those things--trying to make them fit into the game's narrative better. The original had MORE content than the remake. Without a time machine, I don't even see how they could make that possible, but they did.
The clock tower, park, and dead factory being cut is (imo) equivalent to the courtyard, guest house, and caves being cut from RE1, the island being cut from RE4, or the antarctic base being cut from RE:CV. Which makes me terrified to see what they would do to those if they remade them in this fashion.
(Oh! The game also teases you at the beginning telling you that there's a clock tower and a park. I was extremely excited to go to those places and it feels like the game slaps you into submission when all you get to see is the clock tower's exterior.)

Second: game length. I guess this one kinda just ties into cut content, but this is really sad. I know people say the game being 4-6 hours long isn't that bad, but come on... it's a $60 game with linear "set-piece" gameplay. I tried my absolute hardest to pad out the game with exploration and sight-viewing (and playing on Hardcore), and I still clocked in at about 5 1/2 hours. That is just... sad. Resident Evil games can usually be sped-run very quickly, but it's the EXPLORATION and puzzle-solving that makes them longer games.

Third: Nemesis... About halfway through the game, I had almost forgotten this game was mainly about Jill being hunted by Nemesis. They end up ditching his Tyrant-like look for a... dog? I do like that they tried to add another phase to the Nemesis transformation, I just REALLY wish it didn't happen so quick. A 1v1 fight with classic phase 2 Nemesis in the clock tower courtyard would've been PERFECT with the new dodging mechanic.

Now, that being said, where the game DID deliver is its soundtrack, which I believe was a step up from RE2R soundtrack. The entire soundtrack seems to be remixed/rearranged versions of the classic soundtrack. RE2R tried to remove that for more ambient sounds, while RE3R tried to keep that classic feel with the music. The final boss music was BEAUTIFUL and gave me chills the moment I heard it kick in.

The characterization is also very nice. I enjoyed the interactions with Jill and Carlos, and all the other characters felt a tad bit more fleshed out. I just wish some of them had more on-screen time (mainly Dario and Brad).

In general, I'd give this game about a 5/10 in terms of being a remake, and an 8/10 as a game. However, I definitely cannot recommend it at the current price unless someone REALLY wants to play Resistance (which is actually a lot of fun imo).

I'm hoping Capcom gives RE3R a look over and adds some things (I doubt it), or at least learns from a few of these mistakes for future remakes.

I really enjoyed this game.  Leading up to the release i replayed the original RE 1-3, then played RE2:R right before this game. 
It took me 7 hours to beat the game, plus an additional 15 hours to beat all other difficulties and unlock all achievements. 

Coming from someone who played the original just a few weeks before this game, all the missing content from the original was very apparent, so were the changes they made to the story.  The game is also as linear as they come, the puzzles can't be called puzzles, they just involve getting an item and interacting with an obvious thing in an obvious way 1-5 mins later.  

The removal of the dismemberment and object collision for zombies that was used in RE2:R is frankly a downgrade.  As a designer myself it's easy to see that their deadline didn't allow them the time to come up with a creative solution to solve the problem of fitting multiple zombies on screen, so they just removed those feature from the game as a means to an end.  It just sucks that PC players had to suffer for what was most likely a console optimization issue.  Whats even more aggravating is that this game now uses the DENUVO DRM which is known to use a portion of the systems resources to run, RE2:R didn't have this.  If you are claiming the need to remove features because they are too taxing on the system, then this should not have been added at what may have been the expense of the latter mentioned features.

It's very apparent that the RE series shifted from being more horror focused toward action and large set pieces in its previous games.  But after the renewal of the series with RE7 and RE2:R i was really hoping that this game would keep to the horror theme.  Those two games had moments of genuine horror because they knew how to use downtime and slow pacing to build tension.  RE3:R does away with all of that, it's just one big thriller, the entire game; there is no downtime, no breaks to let you think about what just happened and what is to come.  It has jump scares, but that is no replacement for true horror.

With all that being said, i really can't say i didn't enjoy the game or get my money's worth. The game tells an interesting story in a manner that makes sense, it's a fun and enjoyable game to play and isn't padded with useless filler that wastes my time.  
The game does it's best to keep you on the edge of your seat, and it delivers on that for almost the entire game as short as it may be.

I think it's easy to see the game in a negative light when you consider what the game could have been, especially since it's a remake of an already existing game. But when you look at what it actually is, then you see a decent game worth playing.
I only wish it was more faithful to the original game.  It should have been marketed as a reimagined remake.  I would recommend to anyone coming into the remakes of 2 and 3 to play them together, it's cool the way they show some of the small impacts your actions at the RPD in 3 have on what you see in 2.  The games are also made on the same engine with the same textures and models and feel as they could be one cohesive game.

Its clear Capcom wanted to push this game out as fast as possible to capitalize on the hype and success of RE2:Remake.  But i wouldn't let that stop you form playing it.  If you think that $60 is too much for an initial 6-7 hour story, then i would say give it a few months an grab it on sale.

I also like the tweaks to combat, specifically the dodge mechanic, and all the new monsters are fun and challenging to fight. Despite popular opinion, I actually prefer Nemesis to Mr. X; I found Mr. X to become more of an annoyance than actually scary after he popped up for the 50th time and made you have to awkwardly navigate your way around him or hide in the safe room until he finally went the hell away. That said, I think comparing Nemesis to Mr. X isn't a proper comparison; Nemesis is a lot more like Birkin IMO. I do think Birkin was a bit more interesting to fight seeing as he's a completely different boss each time you encounter him, whereas Nemesis essentially reuses his 2nd form twice in two fights. Despite that though, I still definitely thought he was a really menacing and fun villain to fight. 

I also think the dynamic between Jill and Carlos is vastly superior to that of Leon and Claire who literally only interact with each other at the very beginning and very end of RE2 Remake and which I found to be really odd and disappointing. That said, one of my major complaints with RE3 Remake is the fact that there is two very distinct playthroughs one can do when playing as Leon or Claire, and the fact that that is absent in RE3 Remake is a major disappointment and a huge demerit on replay value for the game. 

My other big issue is the utter lack of any puzzles in this game. I do really like the updated combat, but it really would've been nice if they broke it up with the occasional puzzle that't not too hard but not too easy; RE2 Remake nailed that balance between combat and puzzles and I think it's seriously a shame RE3 Remake basically did away with puzzles entirely. 

So yeah, all in all this is a pretty good game, but I can understand why people think RE2 Remake is superior overall. If I had to give this game a numeric rating I guess I'd give it like an 7/10 and I'd say wait for this to be on sale, because the $60 asking price for a game that's literally got half the story mode content of RE2 Remake is quite steep.

Not quite finished the game (think I am close), but so far I have enjoyed it (for the most part). Here are the takeaways. 

The game starts strong. A bit heavy on the scripted events, but it gave me flashbacks to Dead Space 2 for a brief moment, and for that I was happy. However, I must say that the feeling of dread that came from Resident Evil 2, isn't quite here. This definitely feels more action based, though for there are a few bits that ramp up the horror which I liked. The one thing that I feel really does work against it is the static zombie deaths. Whereas, in the previous game when you shot a zombie a few times, they would fall and give the illusion that they were dead, and creating some genuinely tense moments, this game has a static zombie death animation that plays every time they have been truly put down. Additionally, because ammo is not scarce, and the knife never breaks (admittedly, that never made sense in Res 2), you have no problem spending your time to make sure that every zombie never gets back up. Add to that the scattered barrels, and generators and you have a multitude of ways to defend yourself.

I also found myself less fearful of Nemesis than I did Mr. X. This boils down to the fact that he can't follow you as much as the latter can. In Res 2, Mr. X had pretty much the full run of R.P.D, whereas here, Nemesis only shows up sparingly. Admittedly, this is good in a way, as Nemesis is quite a bit more capable. Where Mr. X walked and his footsteps were foreboding, Nemesis sprints and jumps to knock you off your feet.

Again, at the end of the day what it boils down to is, did I have fun? The answer? A resounding yes, and while I would definitely recommend waiting on a sale(unless you plan to sink a lot of hours into Resistance) this is an enjoyable experience.

[h1]The gist of it:[/h1]
Resident Evil 3 Remake is a very hard DLC to recommend, ugh I mean game, especially at its current price but it does nothing truly bad and overall I enjoyed the experience despite its many shortcomings. 

👍 [u]The good parts:[/u]
+Action set pieces especially at the beginning of the game are really great. 
+Jill carries the game on her shoulders, a very likable protagonist. 
+Gunplays and killing zombies remain satisfying.

👎[u]The bad parts:[/u]
-Level design is a huge step back from RE2R, especially after the first level.
-The price does not justify the content at all.
-The story is pretty basic and not that interesting. 

[h1]Story[/h1]
Resident Evil 3 Remake, takes place before and after the events of the second game, starring Jill and Carlos. You get to play as both, mostly Jill, and this time around you won't have to replay the entire game again to see the other characters point of view which I honestly did not like in the second game. 

As you might expect from a Resident Evil game, the story is obviously not its forte. The game has some lore backing it up but overall it's as generic as they can get. If you haven't played the classic like me then you probably won't be disappointed by the cut content or whatever else they changed in the game compared to the original. As per usual Umbrella ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, and you're on a course to try to get away from a tyrant and save Racoon City. 

The characters you meet are hardly interesting, and you'll obviously figure out the plot as you advance however Jill does a pretty good job at making you care for her. It's mostly because the actress playing her is doing a good job at it but the things the character goes through are quite nice. 

At the end of all things, this is still just a remake of a classic game so don't go in expecting brain-teasing twists or an amazing story. It's a zombie game, you've seen it a million times. Not bad but eh, not good either. 

Story rating: 7/10

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
 You're most likely playing this game because you enjoyed the previous one and overall if you did enjoy RE2R's gameplay you'll enjoy this one as well but to a lesser degree. 

What I mean by lesser is that the game has suffered a downgrade in level design as well as puzzle mechanics which changed the pace a bit in the previous game. It's a hell of a lot linear and there are only 2-3 puzzles you'll have to figure out which take like 2 minutes tops. It's extremely baffling how they went from a map that was had interconnected zones that you had to open and figure out kinda like a Metroidvania to a boringly linear one-way path to objective minus the starting level. Huge bummer, as RE2R tried to do something different than it's predecessors and I was expecting the next one to up its game. 

Gunplay is pretty much the same as before, weapons are with different skins but shoot the same as in the previous game. It's all satisfying but I wish they did something else, something new and that god awful inventory system needs to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ go away, forever. There are more boss fights this time around and they vary from cool to okay. I enjoyed fighting the Nemesis. Persistent villain to say the least.

They also modified the difficulty and how it changes based on what you pick, such as the removal of ink ribbons from harder difficulties. I honestly don't care about limited saves but I love a hard challenge and hardcore while still easy was something I enjoyed more than if I was forced with just a number of saves. Once you finish the game it unlocks the nightmare difficulty. I wish that was an option from start but c'est la vie. There is no reason to replay the game anymore and it's a short ride even though I took my time as much as possible.

Gameplay rating: 7/10

[h1]Audio[/h1]
The good thing is the voice acting surpasses everything in the game, especially Jill as I mentioned before since she practically carries the game on her shoulders. The other characters do a pretty decent job as well but there's not so much you can do when the writing is average.

The soundtrack has a more impactful presence as the game is less horror and more action so you'll hear the music blasting while you shoot zombies and it's not that bad to listen.

As for the other sound effects, it's all similar to the previous one which was good, nice atmospheric sounds which can create some tense moments BUT since the levels have suffered massively that means you'll almost never notice and appreciate the sound design which is a shame. 

Audio rating: 8.5/10

[h1]Graphics, performance and tech analysis[/h1]
Resident Evil 3 Remake uses the same engine so the performance is great. The zombie gore might have suffered a bit but you'll barely notice it. The lighting and the textures have been improved a bit compared to the previous game and as for bugs I have not encountered a single one which is very rare these days at launch. 

Sadly as I mentioned in the gameplay, the level design has taken a massive downgrade which also hurts it visually. Maps are mostly corridors and boring linear pathways to your objective. You'll backtrack some times but it's nowhere near as good as the previous game and you can clearly see this was a rushed game with a lot of cut content and not just maps from the classic. For example, the hospital level could've easily been the same size as the entire Police station from the previous game.

So much potential wasted away. Every time I finished a zone I felt disappointed and it gave me nightmares of the abomination that was RE6 which had a similar bad level design and what it is more scummy is that the first map, the one from the demo as well is quite good but it all goes downhill from there. Don't trust the game based on the demo.

Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  7/10

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I did not want to recommend the game but it's not a bad game however the price tag on it is scummy as hell. Don't trust anyone claiming this is an excellent game. The second one probably is but Resident Evil 3 Remake is an inferior product in almost every way, a downgrade if you want to call it that way. If you're a hardcore fan of the series, buy it but at a lower price and if you're not a fan, then just wait for a bigger sale.

[h1]Final score: 7.3/10[/h1]

[h1]Resident Evil 3[/h1]

Its difficult to analyse this game. While The remake of RE2 was more faithful to its source material, this remake took the "reimagining" too far. By this I mean a lot of places got cut, the map is a lot smaller and linear, there is a minimum amount of puzzles, and the campaign is too short if you're looking to beat it once and not play it again.

So, if you are a hardcore fan of the OG and hoped to replay a modern version of the game, this might not be for you. If don't care much for the differences and/or have an open-mind, this game is a blast.

While I think the RE2R is better in many ways, this game is still really good. The graphics are good (with a good optimization), shooting is fun, running form the Nemesis is exhilarating.

It offers a 4~6 hours campaign. There are 2 unlockable difficulties that make the game harder (similar to how RE7 did). It has many challanges to complete that reward you points to unlock special items such as weapons, coins that provide buffs, early key items, etc. So replayability is still strong in this game.

[h1]Now for the online counterpart (since it doesn't have a Steam page for some reason)[/h1]

RE Resistance was co-developed by an outsourced company: NeoBards. These are the developers that made the HD Colletion of DMC and the port of RE0 and RE1 Remasters to Switch. So I would say that their work is not very reliable since all they did was ports.

It lacks some key features like push-to-talk voice chat, and a text chat. It has a P2P connection which the host is always the Mastermind, so survivors usually have the lower hand. Matchmaking is still buggy, but improvements are being made.

One thing that concerns me a lot is the microtransactions. This game features loot boxes. There are 2 types: Equipment LB (which gives you some boosts over the match) and Cosmetics LB. These loot bloxes can be bought with in game points you get from playing, so you can't directly buy loot boxes, BUT! what you can buy is boosters that increase the points you get after a match. So basically you can boost the amount of boxes you buy.

You could say that this could be pay to win since you can get the boosters than buy a bunch of equipment loot boxes, but these boxes are pretty cheap and there are not so many equipments. So, the main source of income with microtransactions would be from people looking to buy cosmetic LB. These are much more expensive than equipment LB and 80% (NOT exaggerating) is trash (emotes, sprays, etc) and not actually skins. So you would have to play 10~16 matches to buy one without boosters and you have a 20% chance to get an actual skin, and maybe, just maybe, you get a skin for the character/creature you want.

The gameplay is fun tho.. a good bonus mode to a good game.

This review is only for the RE3 campaign, not the multiplayer mode.

First of all: don't buy this game !!! At least wait until its on sale.
I deeply regret spending 60€ on this huge disappointment.
RE2 and RE3 are my two favorite games in the Resident Evil series.
Sure the original wasn't a perfect game either, but why make a remake that is even shorter and "worse". Especially after they have released a really good (not perfect) remake of RE2.

Before RE3 remake was released I watched a complete playthrough of the original again so that I could better compare the original with the remake.

Where do I start? Maybe so that the game is disappointingly short. This feeling is reinforced by the fact that almost everything is announced by cutscenes. Nemesis appears short cutscene, Hunter in the hospital appears short cutscene. Talking about the opponents Nemesis is an absolute disappointment. He has only a few areas in which he is chasing Jill and after changing his shape only arena fights come against him. Zombie models seem to be recycled throughout the game at least I had several situations in which I thought I shot the zombie today. And again no spiders! There is also a reduction in gore effects. Parts of the body that have been shot off simply disappear.

That RE 3 is more action-packed than RE 2 or RE 1 is quite plausible due to the scenario. After all, you fight your way through a city full of zombies and other monsters. You visit places like the hospital that are open and accessible to the people of Raccoon City. RE 2 mostly plays in a partially barricaded police station.

Several places were simply left out, e.g. the clocktower, the cemetery, city hall and smaller locations like the newspaper office and the gas station (yes the gas station is in the remake but only in a cutscene)
I have already read several comments in which people wrote that the omitted places were not fun, or that they did not playfully contribute to the game. But instead of just leaving them out, Capcom could have done them better. The more places I have, the more I have to explore and that's one of the most exciting aspects of Resident Evil for me. Especially because Raccoon City was beautifully designed. Instead of great old locations, we have the boring and small substation with the annoying bugs.

Talking about the substation all puzzles consist almost only of pushing switches. Yes some puzzles in the original were a bit strange but e.g. obtaining spare parts for the subway would also be plausible in 2020.

Jill also no longer goes to the police station. This is now part of Carlos story. Brad is no longer killed by Nemesis, and Nicholai is no longer the somewhat mysterious mercenary who always seemed cold and calculating (in my opinion), he is now the annoying B-Movie villain.

There are still a few small points regarding the weapons so you can no longer get the S&W Magnum (Revolver). You get the same Magnum as Leon even with the barrel upgrade and other weapon models have been changed or no longer exist regardless of whether found in the game or unlocked.
Mercenary mode was also thrown overboard.

All in all, the game is an insult to a Resident Evil fan. Overpriced, too short and a terrible remake. Even if you look at it as reimagined.

Mechanically, it feels exactly like RE2 2019, except now Jill has a dodge button which lets you roll out of the way of incoming zombie teeth or Nemesis punches. Very handy in a pinch! Picking up items is also streamlined; you no longer open up the inventory to place every item - they just go straight into your pouch. A nice addition.

Nemesis is only properly used for the first quarter of the game, where he will chase after you through the map like Mr. X. After that, he only shows up in scripted boss fights, which is a little disappointing. His boss fights are very tense and very fun though.

The parts where you play as Carlos might actually be my favourite bits now. They fleshed out his character and made him likeable, and his action-packed segments are a lot of fun. Gunning down hoards of zombies in the RE Engine is satisfying.

Enemy variety is improved, with Hunters, Drain Deimos and Pale Heads making appearances. They all offer a unique challenge and are fun to go up against.

Graphically, a nice jump from RE2 - with more fancy lighting effects, more colour, better character models and animation and nicer DoF bokeh. Combine with ReShade to sharpen up the game and tweak the contrast and it's beautiful. Optimisation is also stellar - it might even run smoother than RE2, which was already one of the smoothest games in years. With everything on Ultra, it never drops below 120fps on my rig. Considering how it looks, it's one of the best performing games I've ever played. RE Engine is impressive yet again.

I haven't tried the multiplayer Resistance, and honestly don't really have any interest in it.

The Great:

Graphics:

Capcom’s RE Engine is incredible. Is it the best engine in gaming right now? I think so. Resident Evil 3 and 2 are some of the best looking games ever made. The lighting, shadows, character models, and Carlos’s hair look incredible. My god does Carlos’s hair look good! The only complaint I have is the lip-sync is off in some cutscenes. I can’t help, but feel like this game was rushed out the door a little early because of some small issues like this.

The zombies look as good here as they did in Resident Evil 2. The RE Engine is some next-gen looking ♥♥♥♥. The most impressive part of it all is the way my game performed. I ran Resident Evil 3 at 75 fps on the highest settings and it only dipped (down to 72 frames) once or twice my entire playthrough. I didn’t encounter any bugs and I only crashed a single time after 10 hours of straight gaming. This game is optimized really well and it feels good to play a PC game that performs well. The various different graphical options are also a major plus.

Gameplay:

The dodge mechanic in this game gets a lot of hate from people and I’ll agree that it isn’t perfect… until you unlock a certain item and become a dodge master. Resident Evil 3, like 2, plays fantastically.

The gameplay loop is pretty much the same in this game as it is in every Resident Evil game. The big difference is that this game is more action-oriented than the last few Resident Evil games. The original Resident Evil 3 was also action-heavy though and honestly… it works really well in this game.

This game has really good replay value and is about the same length as your regular Resident Evil game. After I completed the game I unlocked a shop to buy things from. There were unique weapons, a costume, and some special tokens that I could buy that would give me a permanent boost to my attack, defense, and even give me health regeneration. It’s really neat and I’ve already unlocked just about everything except the infinite rocket launcher and assault rifle. That’s going to take some time to get.

Sounds:

The biggest complaint most people had about Resident Evil 2 remake was the lack of music. That has been fixed here. Music is almost always playing the background and it really added to the atmosphere. It’s creepy and had me questioning myself about exploring the area because I was scared Nemesis was going to show up and open up a can of whoop-ass on me. The voice acting is actually very good and still has that cheesiness that Resident Evil games are known for. Carlos delivered some great lines and had some really good gameplay segments. I just wish Capcom would have gone all in and just gave him his own campaign.

Jill Valentine:

I know there’s a lot of complaints out there on Jill Valentine’s appearance. I personally think she’s beautiful. Jill has always been a beautiful woman in Resident Evil games and that’s no difference here. As a matter of fact, I think she looks better here than she ever did, but that’s just my own personal preference. The only thing I dislike is her outfit. She looks like Lara Croft and that annoys me. No, I’m not asking for Capcom to make her sexy (she already is), but would it have killed them to give her a better outfit and not just do a copy/paste job of Lara Croft? That being said, Jill is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ badass. She single-handedly kicked the living crap out of Nemesis and taunted him every chance she got. Jill has been through some ♥♥♥♥ and I’m glad they did her justice in this game.

The Good: 

Story: 

The story of Resident Evil 3 has been beautifully reimagined here. This isn’t the Resident Evil 3 of yesteryear just like Resident Evil 2 wasn’t. Things are different now and you can either accept that or become one of many trolls that bash on the game because of it. The story immediately introduces Nemesis (in like the first 5 minutes) and it immediately goes after Jill in her apartment. The story never lets up. Jill went through some ♥♥♥♥ here and she’s tough as nails. I think I’m going to have the way Nemesis blurts out “STARZ” in my head for a while.

The Bad:

The only legitimate complaint I have for this game is probably the tacked on Resistance mode. Everything is me nitpicking like I did in Resident Evil 2.

Carlos Should’ve Had His Own Campaign:

I don’t like the pacing of Resident Evil 3. It switched between Jill and Carlos too much for my liking. It would have been better if they just gave Carlos his own campaign. He’s off-camera for most of the game doing his own thing anyway so him having his own story mode would’ve been great. I think that was probably the original plan and I also think that the developers ran out of time. This game needed more time to bake.

Resistance Mode:

 I didn’t buy this game for Resistance Mode and as it stands, it’s a bare-boned feature that adds absolutely nothing to the game. Thankfully, it’s an optional download and after spending 20 minutes with it I uninstalled it from my PC and went back to the excellent single-player portion of the game. Maybe Resistance will get good eventually, but right now it isn’t.

The Verdict:

 I really enjoyed my time with Resident Evil 3. It's frantic fast pace made for an unforgettable experience and kept me on my toes throughout my entire journey. It was great to finally play as Jill Valentine again and experience this classic game retold with today's technology. Nemesis was an excellent antagonist that never let up and none of that is as important or as a cruel as a  Carlosless world would be.
