Disclaimer: I have not played the original Resident Evil 3, although I have watched playthroughs. I will not be reviewing what could have been in the game, only what I have been able to play in the final product that we have.

Although I can definately understand criticisms with this game (mainly pacing, length and relative underutilisation of Nemesis himself) this was still an incredibly fun gaming experience and one that hooked me from start until finish.

This game, taking my time, provided me with roughly 8-9 hours of story content. This includes making sure I explore all rooms to find all loot, enjoying the story notes left all around the game, as well as enjoying the ingame cutscenes. This will definately vary based on how fast or careful you like to play, or even how invested you can be in the story. I can see a person completing this game on their first try in about 4-5 hours if they rush and like to skip over story related notes & scenes. Although this does seem like a large downside, keep in mind that it is possible to finish a first playthrough within the previous Resident Evil 2 remake in a relatively short period as well. I did not feel dissatisfied with the length of the campaign I was provided, though it is notable that there is a lack of options and meaningful unlockable content in comparison to the last game. 
There is an unlockable shop which opens at the finish of your first playthrough. This allows you to spend points that you accumulate from completing challenges to unlock different bonuses, weapons, or even skins. However, these bonuses cost a lot of points, and even after one playthough I only had enough to unlock two bonuses. Unlocking more would require more playthroughs of the game. Unfortunately though, some of the challenges border on downright tedious and it would surprise me if many of these challenges ever see completion from anyone.

Resident Evil 3 remake, just like its predecessor, remains gorgeous, with few exceptions. Graphically it is still an absolute sight to behold. Zombies, are delightfully grotesque, character models look amazing, Nemesis himself looks great and shadow quality, especially in ambient lighting sources, really set the mood for the environments you will be finding yourself in. The only times where there may have been something unsightly, seems to be in relation to characters hair, or even the shadow the hair is casting on their faces (Looking at you Carlos!) Some cutscenes seem to display a strange, almost grid like appearance, seems to appear in these areas, but this was so few and far between that I hardly noticed by the end of the game itself. 

In comparison to my experience with a typical "A" campaign in the Resident Evil 2 remake, Resident Evil 3 remake very short, but this feels more due to the pacing of Resident Evil 3 overall. Resident Evil 2 kept you in three different locations for large periods of time, allowing you to become familiar and explore for an extended period. Resident Evil 3 contains more locations, including revisiting the RCPD from the previous remake, but these unfortunately always felt like the player never gets to stay in these locations for as long as they may have wanted to. I personally would have loved to explore more of the Racoon City streets, but it felt almost like as quickly as we got to looking around, we had to move on to the next major location. It never really had a chance to sink in, and felt more like the locations under stayed their welcome.

Lets talk about the big guy himself, Nemesis. For anyone who has played the recent Resident Evil 2 remake, Nemesis unfortunately (fortunately?) does not stalk you as often as Mr. X did. He will appear repeatedly as a set piece chase, boss encounter and for a relatively small section of the game will pursue you as you make your way to achieve your objectives. 
Compared to the old Mr. X, Nemesis has more tools in his arsenal that allow him to differentiate himself from his cousin. Boasting the capabilities to sprint after you, jump in front to cut off your route, and seemingly swing in out of nowehere, he is definately a lot more athletic and stress inducing during his pursuit periods.
Unfortunately though, this is limited heavily within the first act of the story. A couple later chases revolve around Nemesis pursuing you with various weaponry. These were enjoyable, but short lived.
Come the start of the second act, Nemesis is almost unrecognisable as the classic tyrant, and is also restricted to boss encounters from that point onwards. This puts a lot less stress on the player, knowing he will no longer pop out of nowhere as they are completing objectives, however, it downplays the level of threat that the determined, terminator-like Nemesis is.
At the end of the day, Nemesis is still a very worthy antagonist for this game, though he will unfortunately stay in Mr. X's shadow.

Overall this experience, although not quite as mind blowing as the Resident Evil 2 remake that hit shelves a year earlier, is still a good time for any person interested in the Resident Evil franchise or even survival horror in general. It has its downfalls, and is an ever so slight misstep coming off of its predecessors success, however it is still a great game that left me glued to my chair until I had it completed. It will unfortunately not be remembered as fondly as other recent entries into the franchise, but it is still a game oozing with quality, and one that I urge people not to miss.

As a long-time fan of the series, I would recommend this game, but only sparingly.

On one hand, this is an excellent recreation and update of Resident Evil 3 for the new day and age. For long time fans of the series like myself, REmake 3 brings a strong new take to an old classic, with more convincing character redesigns, somewhat better writing and pacing (within the limits of what the B-Movie RE plot can acheive), and much more engaging and reactive gameplay, similar to REmake 2. One of my favorite parts is the redesign of Carlos and the practical update to Jill's outfit; Carlos is now more distinct from the other clean-cut protagonists like Chris or Leon, at least visually, and Jill's outfit makes more sense for a disgraced cop than zombie-slaying in a tube-top.

As for the negatives, unlike REmake 2, this one isn't groundbreaking in any respect. The RPD section, while nice from a lore standpoint for explaining some events you would see in REmake 2, is clearly a straight copy-paste from REmake 2; supplies may be specific to Carlos now rather than Claire/Leon, but the locker and safe puzzles are exactly the same, and even the barricades and other assets are no different; those that remember from the original RE2 and 3 might recall that the police station looked rather different between games, not as a result of layout, but to reflect the different state of barricading and reinforcement that the police had taken in the time between each character's visit. 

Nemesis is also a bit of a letdown; while it looks fantastic from start to finish, being torn up worse and worse through every attempt on Jill, its appearance is no longer that tense surprise like it tried to be in the original. In effect, he's an even more toned-down Mr. X from REmake 2, stomping after you only in very specific set areas even smaller than the previous installment, where at least Mr. X would follow you from room to room. Nemesis, by comparison, jumps out in front of you out of nowhere for a very small portion of the game, while the rest are really just scripted chase sequences.

The biggest disappointment here is that the game itself is short. Even an achievement suggests this: "Complete the game in under 2 hours." And aside from increased difficulty modes with shuffled supplies, there is no additional gameplay modes or scenarios like in REmake 2. I was able to complete every achievement and challenge the game offered in just over 20 hours, less than a week after the game's release; I've the same amount of time in REmake 2, and I still haven't played through the joke tofu survivor scenario or any of the Lost chapter DLCs. Capcom says you are getting two games in one by bundling REsistance with this, but in effect, what you are getting is two $20-25$ AAA games for $30 each. Without REsistance as part of this package, this game is certainly not worth $59.99 USD, not when REmake 2 offered far more for $10 less a year prior.

tl,dr: For fans of the series, this game is still a good get, at least if it's on sale; a semi-faithful update that helps complete the major story from start to finish with far less cringe-worthy writing and eye-cutting polygons, although without a branching path and far more 'jump-cuts' in the action. But if you are looking more for the gameplay or gorn that the RE engine offers, look instead to REmake 2 or, better yet, RE 7, both of which offer far more for less.

This is a tough one to review, as I'm sure many would agree. I'll start off by saying that I'm an avid Resident Evil fan, ever since the original releases back on the PlayStation. I have played and own every single title, including spin offs and multi console releases. 

Whilst Resident Evil 3 wasn't my favourite, I did hold it in high esteem as the story was exciting and interconnected really nicely with my actual favourite, RE 2.

With that said, I've been super excited at the possibility of a RE 3 Remake since the original RE1 remake on Gamecube, with that desire only strengthened after the release of the incredible RE 2 remake earlier last year.

This game IS very good. The story is intense, the characters hold their own against their OG counterparts and gameplay top notch. See below for a breakdown:

Graphics: 10/10
Atmosphere: 8/10
Story: 6/10
Sound design: 9/10 (had some slight sound occlusion issues using headphones)
Replayability: 6/10

So for me the game scores quite highly in most areas. The graphics are fantastic and the RE engine is extremely well optimised. Running the game on an relatively old 980, Ryzen 9 3900x and 16gb ddr4 I was able to max out most settings and encountered no visual issues. This also helps to create a brilliantly desolate atmosphere (especially in the earlier street segments).

Echoing what so many others have said though, this remake suffers from vast amounts of cut content when compared to the original. Whilst this isn't completely dissimilar to the RE2 remake, which also suffered from some slight cuts from the story, it's far more of an issue here as Resident Evil 3 was already a very short game (originally intended to be a DLC, even back in the day).

Due to cuts in the story and environment this becomes an extremely short game, with my first playthrough coming in at only 3.5 hours, and that was taking my time.

Whilst there is quite a bit of replayability, with an item shop where you spend points on items gained through in-game challenges, the game still suffers because of the length of the story. Each time you play it, you get more efficient which means a decrease in the time it takes to finish. Without boasting, I've completed the game on all difficulties with an S result, with the lower difficulties completed in under an hour!

I've gained all achievements, completed all challenges and bought all the store items. The game WAS good enough to make me want to go and do all those things, but it is NOT worth the current asking price. 

I am recommending this game as it's good fun and a great dive back into the new RE universe. But grab the game on a sale. If it were around £20 you'd have a bargain.

Regarding others’ reviews:
-	Game length is okay, not good and not bad. To be fair, RE2 and RE3 are very similar in length.

-      The number of puzzles is far less than the original. The game is more action-oriented.

Finally, the RE3 that we always deserved.

   People seem to forget that the original Resident Evil 3 was something of a minor disappointment to many fans; hence why Resident Evil 4 was hailed as a major "comeback", and a much-needed reinvigoration/reinvention of the series. I recall almost no one at the time being blown away by RE3; and believe me, I was one of the Day One people.

   Fast-forward to 2020, and we have a remake every bit as good as the RE2 remake from a year-and-a-bit ago...yet altogether more "necessary", methinks. RE2 was already a classic; many still seem to favour the old one, and even I find it hard to commit to the idea that the new one is invariably "better" than the old one (they're both top-notch games for their times). RE3 was never a classic. It was really bloody [i]good[/i], sure...but it was hands-down the least favourite numbered RE game of many people up to that point, myself included. Now, finally, we have a game well worthy of the title: "Resident Evil 3".

   If you loved the RE2 remake I can't really see why you won't at least [i]like[/i] this one, unless you're one of these people ranting about "lack of content". Hey: the original game was pretty short too, and didn't have much replayability. Too many folks seem to be viewing the original through the rose-tinted glasses of sentimentality: it was hardly anybody's favourite to begin with. Just like the original, this RE3 ramps the action up a little from the game before it - and in accordance, is slightly less scary - but it's mostly the same mechanics and should appeal to much the same folk. The new RE3 merely adds a dodge mechanic - just like the original RE3 - which I honestly couldn't master in the old game, but found genuinely useful this time around.

   Sure, a lot of the locations and enemy types have changed, but only the puritan old-schoolers are going to notice this. Hell, I barely noticed or cared, and I've played the original at least five times. So please: don't listen to the sentimentalists (who, as I've already pointed out, weren't all that overprotective of the original back in the day). This is an extremely worthy addition to the RE franchise, as well as a perfectly excellent game in its own right. And okay, the game is perhaps a tad overpriced for its length and "content" by itself, but now we come to the inevitable subject of...

   Resident Evil: Resistance, the "free" multiplayer game that comes with this new version of Resident Evil 3!

   I have a couple of thousand hours up on the Left 4 Dead games, and I'll be honest: they're just about the only competitive multiplayer games I need. The cooperative elements of L4D and L4D2 only rely, furthermore, on a [i]certain[/i] amount of well-coordinated teamwork, while this game appears to need a good deal more; and probably, therefore, headsets on every single player. 

   Experience tells me that randomly tossed-together human beings couldn't cooperate well enough to produce a four-page fanzine scrawled with crayons, so unless you have reliable friends to team up with, I'm not sure you'll get much joy out of this one. I also found the controls/gameplay highly unintuitive - if I can't learn the basics in five minutes, I'm probably not interested - and the "scenario" presented (one part RE, one part Saw) didn't compel me much either. 

   On the whole, the gameplay felt rather awkward and sloppy, at least for the little time and attention I've given it thus far. Still, it's better than several swift kicks to the face, especially if you think of it as "free"...which it either is or isn't, depending on how much you were willing to pay for the main game.

   So, in conclusion: absolutely top-notch single-player game (the length of which I found perfect, for what it is); and a "bonus" multiplayer game that I, for now at least, can certainly take or leave. Most of you will probably want to wait for a price drop or sale, and that's fair. Me? Extremely happy with my purchase, even if I doubt I'll be getting much value out of the existence of Resistance; though I'll no doubt be tempted to try it again down the track, and by then it may have seen some improvements that make for a more enticing game. Stranger things have certainly happened.

   Verdict: 10/10 (the inclusion of Resistance barely making a difference in my book, as I would've happily paid the price asked for RE3 alone).

After success of Resident Evil 2 remake, it was matter of time before CAPCOM release next remake. And after 16 months they did it.

[h1]GRAPHICS[/h1]
CAPCOM continue to improve RE engine which is used here. The remake looks absolutely incredible. Facial animations and cutscenes one of the best i ever saw in video game. Very good work was done for proper implementation of lights and shadows. Fire and particle effect looks better than in RE2 remake. Also since part of story take in city, color scheme is richer. All enemies look creepy and terrifying. However gore was decreased. You still shoot off limbs and blow up heads but limbs now disappear. Strange decision that probably caused by larger amount of zombies on screen. Overall graphical fidelity very high and on AAA level.

[h1]SOUNDTRACK[/h1]
It's really good. RE3 remake have cool memorable soundtracks that fit perfectly to what happened on screen. They create tension, pomp yours blood or provide relax feeling when it need it.I will listen to some of the tracks outside of game. This is serious improvement compare to RE2 remake.

[h1]STORY[/h1]
The story follow after two main characters: Jill Valentine and Carlos Oliveira that trapped in middle of zombie outbreak in city. She is member of special team that was assigned to investigate bizarre murders (RE1 events). Despite all difficulties her team succeed to find true but their reports was rejected. He is mercenary that was sent by Umbrella Corp. to save civilians. However since Umbrella also responsible for crisis in first place, their relationship didn't start well. Also Jill be targeted by unstoppable killing machine (a.k.a Nemesis) and suffer from PTSD cause by previous events don't help either. And now they need to work together to survive this nightmare. I admit that story don't offer something revolutionary but i like character development and interaction between them. I played the game many time and still watch some cutscenes because i like how they were directed.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]
The game have one campaign but two playable characters. During playthrought you switch between characters and location. Each location have distinguish look and various goals to complete. It fits very nice with story. It is important to know that this game have more actions compare to previous titles. You have more enemies (not just amount but variety) and more weapons. Nemesis much more aggressive compare to Mr. X. But classic elements of RE gameplay still here. You solve puzzles (unfortunately very simple), craft ammo and health item, upgrade weapons, expend inventory, looking for keys or other items that will help advance in story. Just flow of gameplay is faster. In addition your character have ability to dodge attack but it have timing constrains. Also since you switch between location there is much less backtracking and whole game is more linear. If you looking for  slow paced experience like it was RE2 remake it is not here. But if don't mind something different yet familiar it is here.

[h1]REPLAYABILITY[/h1]
Once you beat game you can play again to unlock different costume, weapons, different difficulty or trying to get some achievement/collectable/concept arts/models. Typical things for resident evil serie. Keep in mind that higher difficulties not only come with more tough enemies but also place them (enemies) and in-game items in different location. So if even you learn everything by heart on standard/hardcore, additional modes nightmare and inferno will manage to surprise you. It took me 8 hours to finish my first blind playthrought on hardcore difficulty. Unfortunately there is no second campaign or branches in story. Shame that if compare with RE2 remake there are less reason to comeback to the game. Just to be clear in addition to RE3 remake you will get 4vs1 RE resistance multiplayer game. I don't care about it so i exclude it from review. I suggest to check online statistics to see how many people play it.

[h1]PERFORMANCE[/h1]
I use i5 9600k, GTX 1080; 16GB RAM and Windows 10. I run game on 2560x1440 resolution with max settings. The game runs very smooth, fps almost always (95%) above 80. No crashes. However there is still 2 issue with engine: 1) Animation for enemies 
that from you still locked 30 fps with create weird slow-mo effect. Which more noticeable compare RE2 remake since you travel more on streets, 2) Surface reflection still don't work so recommend to turn it off. Also i suggest to run game with DirectX 11 because using D12 bring some strange colours.

[h1]SUMMARY[/h1]
Ironically RE3 remake repeat destiny of original. It divide community about approach how survival horror should look. As fan of original i appreciate improving in story, character development, smooth flow of gameplay but disappointed that some locations were cut and didn't receive replacement. Is it worth your time and attention? Yes. What it is here well done and the game is fun. Is it worth current asking price ($60)? Not really. One campaign, no matter how good is it, don't look like good deal compare to RE2 remake. Unless,  you really want to play online. I leave positive review since overall it is good game but i recommend to wait unlit price drop to $30-$40. I hope CAPCOM will learn their lesson and will understand that one type of content (online mode in this case) can not replace another (additional locations in singleplayer).

In the pantheon of Resident Evil Remakes, RE3 is definitely at the bottom of the ladder, beneath its far better siblings REmake from 2002, and 2019's RE2 remake. 
RE3 remake isnt a bad game by any stretch of the imagination, but much like being the child of a famous musician, youre always going to compare it to its far better, far more successful Father.

The good things about RE3:
 
-its absolutely stunning to look at
-the gameplay is fun, and getting to see more of Raccoon City as the virus takes hold is great. 
-New Jill is an absolute bae, 
-new Carlos is great too, and Carlos' section in the hospital is really enjoyable. 
-The Nemesis boss fights are good and his new redesign is pretty cool too. 

The bad:

-too damn short
-Nemesis is less like Mr X, and more like William Birkin from RE2. He turns up a few scripted times, and then only in boss fights after that
-hardly any puzzles (actually i cant think of a single puzzle in the whole game)

I've no idea why Capcom removed so much content from RE3, considering that RE3 was already shorter than both Resi 1 and 2, because with a few extra locations and maybe a reworking of the gravedigger boss fight from RE3 this would absolutely be a game id recommend at full price. I can kinda understand why Nemesis doesnt work the same way as Mr X tho, as an entire game of being stalked by Mr X would get really old, really fast. As fun as Mr X is, i spent a awful lot of time just waiting around in safe rooms for his footsteps to go away. He works best as a threat in the police station only, if he followed you everywhere, i think it'd be a far worse experience. But still, Nemesis could have been given a much better role instead of a few scripted sequences. 
Some people have complained that RE3 is more action heavy than RE2, and are worried that this remake signals Capcom screwing up and returning to action RE games like Resi 5, and 6. But RE3 was far more action focused even back in 1999, it had a much higher enemy count and gave you way more guns n' ammo than RE1 or 2. So i dont think criticising it over being action heavy is fair. And honestly, on hardcore difficulty, i was constantly running low on ammo and never once felt like it was turning into a zombie killing power fantasy, it always felt like i was struggling against the odds to survive. 

So to sum up, RE3 at full price is worth it only if youre a big fan of the series OR youre in love with New Jill and wait to spend some quality time killing zombies and enjoying Jill sandwiches. For everyone else, wait for a price drop and you get another short but stunning return to Raccoon City.

Pretty much anything I said for my Resident Evil 2 (2019) review (apparently Steam finds its own links to be malicious so can't link that) carries over to this.

I like the new combat roll as it makes your character seem less incompetent and I like the more action oriented and straightforward focus as I really thought the previous game needed to pick a direction to go in either focusing on horror and survival or combat (or just do all of them well like RE4). There's really no other mechanical changes (other than the boss) so anything that I thought worked or didn't remains the same, with the only difference is in the setting frequently changing, meaning that I dislike the revive after being shot in the head 10 times zombies even more as that aspect just seem pointless now.

In RE2 you were chased around the area you spend more time in by Mr. X/Tyrant in what was more of a brief occasional and badly designed annoyance. In RE3 you are chased by Nemesis throughout the entire game but he only shows up in set sequences. This should have made him a much better designed enemy with the game allowing them to create well done and unique scenarios for him without any awkward AI moments of Mr X. Somehow, they actually made Nemesis worse. The boss fights are dull and tedious, he shows up in chase sequences so brief they are basically pointless, he shows up once demonstrating an ability to put parasites on the heads of zombies to make them stronger than never does it again when you are near him, he is supposed to kill Jill but seems to go out of his way to let her live or to kill other people instead of her, he has a rapid firing rocket launcher that you dodge in a hilarious chase sequence that ends with you running (it's Resident Evil so closer to a light jog) down a small path as he fires rockets while standing on a car that go off at your feet but do nothing with a cutscene that has him then shooting a rocket at Jill's feet that propels her over some cars but does little more than mildly annoy her. Jill takes more punishment than Lara Croft in the new Tomb Raiders from Nemesis and his abilities and weapons are so idiotically used that the game could have gone the route of being a slapstick comedy.

One of the strangest endings that I've seen. The two main characters fight another human character. Jill does nothing and watches a brief fight between the Carlos and the other guy, Carlos holds the guy and tells Jill to shoot him. Jill says she can't because she will hit Carlos (I'm hoping she assumed the bullet would penetrate and hit him not that she is going to miss a stationary target with an arm around him held 10 feet in front of her), he says there is no other way (there are essentially no stakes, no one needs to really be shot and he could probably just let go or move since Jill now has a gun an an unarmed guy), so she shoots and both of them not only survive but don't even seem badly injured.

It's unfortunate that they removed some sections that were in the original game as they could have made for some nice settings. They wouldn't necessarily need it to do what you did there in the original but seeing all the places again in this really good looking game and having some more content would have been nice.

There's probably going to be a lot of happy Source Filmmaker hentai style creators due to some of the enemies in this game.

Moment to moment I liked it more than RE2 but the game would have been a lot better without Nemesis (obviously, even better if any of his sections were good), and I couldn't recommend it for anywhere near the full asking price.

Let me preface, I enjoy the game. However, this game is barebones to say the least. It's easy to finish under two hours, feels less populated with places that you go to than the original, and feels like a glorified tech demo. It is not worth 60$, and I'm glad I got it for 45$, cause I've had 10$ games deliver more fun and longer play times than this.

Nemesis is also trimmed down, most of his time is spent in scripted moments, and lacks that near constant doom-and-gloom oppressiveness that the original gave you when he showed himself. The dodging mechanics can also trivialize his presence, but it isn't nearly as bad as how easily bypassed Mr. X is in the RE2make. 

I would earnestly suggest people to just play the original, whether you emulate it or not, it's still a better game whether you can stand tank controls and the original fixed camera style. 

However, I did enjoy the character and monster redesigns, and the writing felt like the goofy over-the-top writing of classic RE games that I can't help but love. It does feel more like a transition game to RE4, and probably could've benefited greatly by emulating the amount of locations and overall timespan that RE4 tends to require.

I did appreciate the different Stage 2 transformation for Nemesis more than the original though, despite the original being more threatening in gameplay, it felt very lackluster as a mutation and can appreciate the super-Licker esque form. It's the opposite of how I felt about Mr. X and his super Tyrant form in RE2make, which was lazy to say the least.

And my only issue that I really consider a goofy nitpick is how they get rid of Jill's Samurai Edge to replace it with a Glock, despite her being one of the few who were able to hold onto it post-Raccoon City. It doesn't really change anything, but it was one of the few details that I appreciated.

I've noticed people are giving this game a rough time. Yes, $40 would've been a better price considering the main and only campaign takes around 5 hours, but the amount of quality and polish put into that campaign is stunning, even if some of the content from the original was cut out. The graphics and scenery are some of the best I've seen in gaming so far, and the voice-acting keeps me watching the cutscenes even when I'm speedrunning a playthrough. The hard-to-master dodge/counter mechanic is one of the best additions to the new generation of Resident Evil and allows for an entirely new style of play; goodbye to the awkward shuffling around G2 and Super Tyrant. Moreover, even though people say this game is just 5 hours of gameplay and nothing else, there's actually a good amount of replay value here. Not only are there two extra difficulties after Hardcore that completely change and intensify the game, but replaying Resident Evil 3 even on just Standard and Hardcore multiple playthroughs for better times and/or with the many different weapons you can purchase is fun! Just like Resident Evil 2, this release has a lot of room for speedrunning and optimization; you could easily get 50 hours out of this, which definitely makes up for the $60 launch price tag.

However, some of the gripes with Resident Evil 3 are legitimate. First off, I don't know why Capcom cut out some of the areas from the original release, such as the Clocktower and Jill's run of the RPD. This game would've benefited from Resident Evil 2's formula of separate campaigns and '2nd runs'; that implementation alone would've deterred the complaints about the $60 price tag. Another issue I personally have is that some of the level design and enemy placement is respectively too linear and just downright cheap. Compare the areas in this game to the entire RPD from Resident Evil 2, you could get lost for hours in the latter on your first playthrough! The zombie placements are also designed to cheapshot you on your first playthrough, like walkers being placed right around a corner where you can't see them, and BAM they grab you without any slight bit of foreshadowing. Don't get me started on the Hunter Beta's ridiculous one-shot attack! That stupid throat slice looks like just about any other attack if you ask me. Moving onto the topic of Nemesis, he was handled very well in the this game, but I feel he could've been implemented even better, such as a level where you need to hide and plan around him, like Leon and Claire had to with Mr X, rather than all of his encounters being scripted chases or boss fights. Keep in mind, I still really like him, and his introduction was amazing, but we honestly needed more of his iconic bi-pedal first form.

Overall, even though I think Resident Evil 2 is still superior to Resident Evil 3, that's still just saying I prefer an A5 herb-roasted steak to a marinated beef pot-roast. Basically, both of them are amazing, and even though $60 is a hefty price tag for a casual fan of games (and not an epic gamer like myself, jk), you still should invest your time and money into experiencing this awesome release!

Let me start by saying Resident Evil is one of my all-time favorite gaming series. My first experience was RE2 for the PS1 back in the late 90's. With the exception of RE6 and a few of the spin-off titles, Capcom has always knocked these games out of the park for me. When the RE2 Remake was released last year, I played about 30 minutes of it and was very disappointed from what I played in those 30 minutes. Mainly, the very beginning of the game, which in the original game started off by running through the city streets for several minutes and setting the horror tone before reaching the RPD station. So when I played the remake and found out that whole segment was cut and you arrive at the RPD station instantly after the start of the game, I was severely turned off by this and assumed Capcom had botched the entire remake. I didn't give it a fair chance. I refunded the game, got my $60 back, and waited until it went on sale for $20 before I repurchased it and gave it another chance. Then, after playing through the entire game and seeing that the areas I thought had been cut were just rearranged into later parts of the game, I realized I was too quick with my criticism. Capcom nailed everything that a remake of RE2 should have been. It was a brand new game that stayed true to the original, both in terms of the story and the overall experience. RE2 Remake is now one of my favorite games.

Why am I talking so much about RE2 Remake in a review for RE3 Remake? Because that humbling experience made me promise myself that I would give RE3R a full playthrough before I cast my judgement. And that's exactly what I did. So I can now confidently say... this game is BOOTY CHEEKS. Not the good kind, either. Where do I even begin?

Well, let's start with the price. $59.99. My first playthrough was four hours, and I spent time exploring every nook and cranny because that's the type of gamer I am. The game can [i]easily[/i] be beaten in under two or three hours by the average player. That's not a huge deal because I beat RE2R in under two hours. The difference? RE2R has [u]four[/u] different scenarios to play through. RE3R has only one. Which is true to the original game but at least the original had slightly branching story paths depending on certain choices that are made (more on this later). Well, since the campaign sucked, at least you can kill time playing the mercenaries mode. They brought back the 4th survivor mode for RE2R so they have to bring back mercenaries mode for this game, right? Capcom says: "Nah, but thanks for the money, chump." What about other additional content, like extra costumes? RE2R had lots of cool costumes (I would have paid money for the Classic '98 costumes if they weren't already free). RE3R gives you one additional costume for Jill/Carlos once you beat the game, and one additional "costume" if you pre-ordered the game. I use the term costume loosely for that second instance because the only thing it changes for Carlos is his hair. His... Hair... Talk about rewarding your true supporters!

Moving on to the gameplay. I cannot emphasize enough how watered-down this game feels compared to RE2R. For the most part, the entire game is on rails. There's no big areas for you to gradually explore as you unlock new areas through puzzle-solving and back-tracking. It's basically just "find this item that allows you to advance to the next area of the game, repeat." Oh, you like puzzles? How about two puzzles in the entire game, because that's all you get. Also the logic and creativity of both said puzzles are pitiful. I brute-forced both of them because the solution wasn't discernible. Well, who needs puzzles anyway when you have the tense horror of Nemesis chasing you all throughout the entire game just as he did in the original game? Oh... he only does that for literally the beginning of the game (about the first 30 minutes) and then every single encounter after that is a scripted boss fight. There goes 90% of what made RE3 such a terrifying game right out the window. As for other enemies in the game, remember the Drain Deimos/Brain Suckers from the original game? They make a return. For one single area of the game. You kill about 7-10 (much smaller versions) of these and then never see them again. They even introduced a new game mechanic that gives you a parasite if you get grabbed by them, which can only be cured by eating an herb. What an interesting concept to never be revisited a single time in the game. How about something that wasn't even visited once in this remake from the original game? Live selections. There were several parts in the original game where time would briefly slow down and you would have to make a choice between two actions on how to proceed with certain situations, which resulted in slight changes to how you progressed through the game. One of the most iconic and unique features of RE3. Nowhere to be found this time around. Shameful.

It's not over yet, though. Capcom still has a chance to save this game with a fantastic story. But they chose not to, I guess. Because the story doesn't even come close to anything from the original game, and the re-imagined story doesn't deliver enough to justify the change. Remember when I said I was upset about the beginning of RE2 being "cut" from the remake, only to find out that it was there all along later in the game? RE3R cut the ENTIRE clock tower level. Not just rearranged when it was visited in the game, but straight up removed it. One of the biggest parts of the game. Gone. Why? Capcom obviously didn't redirect their efforts into focusing more on the (extremely lackluster) design of the hospital and underground facility areas. Looking back on it, maybe it's for the best that they didn't even try.

My final gripe is that Nemesis looks absolutely ridiculous. When I first saw the leaked images of him, I thought there was no way they would stick with that. He looks so goofy with his over-sized teeth and trashbag jumpsuit. And yet, this is the final design they decided on. If they weren't gonna fix him, at least he couldn't possibly look any worse than that. Ah, wait, did I mention he turns into this weird dog thing halfway through the game? It is with a heavy heart that I have to share my grievances with the game but because the classic is one of my favorite Resident Evil games I have to share my thoughts. 
Resident Evil 3 Remake is a good game but it has a lot of flaws that keep it from being the definative version of the game and that keep it from surpassing Resident Evil 2 Remake. The game functions pretty one to one to resident evil 2 remake with the same controls though some things are changed to make way for the dodging mechanic as well as the loss of the ability to use defensive weapons when grabbed by an enemy. 
Story wise the game feels like its on fast forward through most of the experience. The intro is nice but it doesn't capture the feel of the destruction raccoon city is facing like in the original where both a giant police firing line and multiple groups of armed mercenaries are attacked and killed by only zombies. Instead it tries to go for a news broadcast that seems to deliberately withhold information of the situation within in the city while also featuring the activation of Nemesis after a commercial for Umbrella products to show how evil the company secretly is. The intro goes for a forced complexity that ultimately just conveys what we already know rather than a simple showcase of something that was the result of the information we already know of the company from the previous games let alone from the previous remake that came out just the year before.
The beginning of the game is really nicely done with the first person perspective of exploring Jill's apartment the buildup really makes you want to explore outside the semi-safety of the apartment and into the monster infested streets but the buildup is killed by the comical appearance of Nemesis. Jill gets a phone call from her companion Brad telling her that something is after them and that she should leave the city just as he says he can't explain Nemesis bursts through the wall and begins chase. The chase wasn't interesting as most of it is cutscenes with the only interesting bits happening in real time in the world around Jill during the breaks of the Apartment Escape sequence, Such as people fleeing and or collateral damage from what I can only assume was Nemesis' attack. The apartment escape ends with nemesis trying to crush Jill with a slab of concrete only to be foiled by an escape. Jill then just so Happens to run into brad on the way out of her apartment. 
The sequence following looks great. The city streets look like a city that's been nearly overrun by zombies and Chaos with crumpling barricades and abandoned cars and flaming wreckage everywhere which captures the dirty industrial apocalyptic feel of the original game. The problem here comes with the pacing. Remember Brad? The trailers gave a feeling that he was going to have an expanded role in this game which honestly would have given him some more credit to his character. In the original you meet brad in a bar getting attacked by a zombie after running away from a safehouse full of them. In this game we know from notes in the apartment that Brad was investigating Umbrella with the rest of the S.T.A.R.S. Members who were still in the city. This already makes him more interesting as it gives him a little more character than just the old chicken heart he used to be. The problem comes in with how he is used afterwards sure he leads Jill to a "Safehouse" But he is quickly bitten and forgotten about even quicker than the old game where he gets killed by Nemesis rather than a group of zombies. After Brad is left for dead the rest of the escape sequence you get treated to the first 2 fourths of the original game done in a few minutes. You meet and leave Dario in the warehouse in a matter of seconds later and the scene were the helicopter gets shot down happens only a few seconds later. After which Jill Meets Carlos and the actual game begins. 
The Demo is pretty much the whole beginning portion of the game from this point where you have to get power to the subway this segment is around the halfway point in the original game. Now this is where the pacing becomes even more problematic. 
 If an enemy isn't a zombie it's delegated to a certain area only Such as the Hunter gammas in the sewer and the Drain Deimos in the power plant. you only encounter Drain Deimos One time in the game and they're there for five minutes depending on how well you do activating switches in the plant though they make an impression by planting a larva in Jill though that attack never happens again and it's a middle finger if you have no green herbs even if there were none there are a ton of them in the area of note 2 right outside the power station. 
Nemesis is still scary as hell when he chases his new abilities make him an even bigger threat however the drawback is that his chase segments don't last long and after a certain point they stop happening. Nemesis feels like a setpiece rather than a natural threat. He shows up whenever he's is needed to chase you or for a boss fight until he mutates. Speaking of boss fights He's the only boss in the game and all four boss fights against him are somewhat different though the two mid ones are practically the same.
The first Nemesis fight is a flamethrower battle shoot him in the gas tank and then he turns into a more aggressive William G1 from the previous remake. 
Nemesis 2 is nemesis becoming a werewolf fish monster out of Bloodborne the fight is cool but the arena feels manufactured with various trucks blocking certain paths thus creating the arena.
Nemesis 3 is just nemesis 2 with a tentacle and a new attack
Nemesis 4 is 2 shots and he's dead.
Where is the Gravedigger? I know it's not the most liked boss in the series I don't even like it but the fact that it has no remade boss fight either means they couldn't fix it or they didn't want to try and recreate the monster with a better fight attached to it. Considering you encounter the monster twice along with its offspring. 
Once Jill turns on the subway and escapes both Nemesis and The Hunter gammas ( Who's redesigns make no sense in my opinion.) The game shifts over to Carlos at the police station we see Marvin from 2 uninfected who gets bit by brad who apologizes as a zombie brad goes full zombie and you put him down inside the station there is a reuse of enemy assets from Resident Evil 2 remake where you fight 2 Lickers you also find out the UBCS is supposed to extract a doctor from the city too before it shifts back to Jill who fights Nemesis 2 then gets infected after which the game shifts back to Carlos.
the Hospital segment is the most intact in terms of length in this portion of the game Carlos has to find an antivirus for Jill which is a cool segment though it ends in an enemy rush as a sort of boss fight a 
personal preference of mine Don't do enemy rushes as a boss fight! After this Jill wakes up and she can explore the hospital or leave for the underground lab which once again is lifted from 2 and kills the dirty industrial look and feel of the game with another untouched lab environment here there are more enemy assets from 2 being reused in the Form of the Pale Heads from Ghost Survivors to try and have a Regenrador wannabe for the game. I should say after the point where Jill wakes up from her booster shot the game's story goes from escaping to saving Raccoon City because they need the t-virus vaccine. this is ruined by Nikolai and Nemesis and once you kill Nemesis for good with the Railgun you shoot Nikolai and the game ends.  The game Director needs to understand the more you try and outdo another game the more you risk making it too crappy and uninspired. The reuse of certain assets for points as well as the quick pace show this. Design for enemies are one thing but the gameplay story and pacing matter first designs are mostly nitpicks. I still like the game but I can't vote mixed on this.

This is one of those times where Steam needs to add a third opinion between thumbs up and thumbs down. In my opinion this is a good Resident Evil game (not great but good) but it's a terrible Resident Evil 3 remake so I'm going to write this from the point of view of someone going into this game looking for the same type of atmosphere that the original had. Sadly to say this game does disappoint in that aspect.
(POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD)
When I first encountered Nemesis in this remake my first words were "why are you here?! You're not supposed to be here yet! Where is you suspenseful build up?! where I just barely catch glimpses of you while you stalk Brad" or when you encounter Dario (I think that's his name) in the warehouse at the beginning and he makes no mention of his daughter, his dialogue in the original where he says "I JUST LOST MY DAUGHTER OUT THERE! HOW DARE YOU TRY TO GET ME TO GO BACK OUTSIDE!" that line has stuck with me since I first played the original growing up, I questioned whether I should try to make man face the monsters that likely ripped apart his child right in front of him but in the remake he thinks I'm trying to steal his safe house?

These two events perfectly pinpoint what I think is wrong with this game, and before I continue I will say that I HAVE BEATEN EVERY DIFFICULTY AVAILABLE (Hardcore, Nightmare, and Inferno) so there is no excuse.

This is a action game this IS NOT A SURVIVAL HORROR GAME in my opinion. I replayed the original 3 about a year and a half ago and when I was in the Police Station and Nemesis busted through the window I LITERALLY screamed like a little girl while running away to get to a door with a loading screen(not the proudest moment for a man in his 20's). In the remake I was scared twice, TWICE. Once when I first encountered Nemesis outside of cut scenes until I realized I could throw ONE frag grenade and he gets knocked down into a stunned state (Hardcore mode). And two when I was playing on Inferno difficulty and I was being chased by Nemesis, and I entered a building thinking I was safe until Nemesis opened the door and came in like "HEY BUDDY" I honestly stopped knocking him down because the game was more interesting if I let him follow me. Just think about that for a second I LET Nemesis follow me, he wasn't my hunter that I was trying to avoid he was like my pet hamster that wanted to kill me but was too weak to accomplish anything more than annoy me.

This game does have good moments, but NONE of those moments include Nemesis in my book. At best Nemesis was a pain and at worst I would fight him with the knife so he'd have a chance at killing me. Jill runs into the UBCS MUCH too early taking away from her character, in the original Jill has to survive on her own for awhile moving through city alleys and streets finding infected roaming the streets and showing that she can survive on her (at least for awhile) but in this game tutorial cut scenes end and BOOM there's Carlos, It makes her seem like a much weaker character. To me this is a better version of Resident Evil 6, but I'm sorry this is not Resident Evil 3 it's far too "childish" Jill wasn't just another survivor with an incredibly dangerous super monster chasing her. She went DOOM ETERNAL and slaughters most if not all infected possible. I heard that one of the CEOs from RE2 remake wanted to down the gore but this is supposed to be a scary game, I want to wonder "what killed this many people? how did it do that to their bodies? Is that going to happen to me?" and that's what I think is wrong with this game so PLEASE LESS EXPLOSIONS, MORE HORROR.

On that note judging this game from the point of view of someone who wanted a survival horror game and not and action game I'm going to have to say I wouldn't recommend Resident Evil 3 Remake, but on the bright side it did make me want to go back and play the original

One of my biggest gripes are the puzzles as well. These were the most brain dead puzzles that I have ever encountered. I legitimately found myself running around like a brainless animal, picking random things up that would end up being what I needed to continue. Now, that is in part of steller level design but when the puzzles themselves are bland and uninspired, I cannot recommend this kind of experience over the RE2 remake, for sure. I will say that managing my ammunition for the events was pretty fun and somewhat fair. I found myself restarting a fight once because I underestimated how much ammo I'd actually need. By the end of the game, I had used all but a few rounds and that felt very satisfying. 

Okay, let me just talk about Nikolai-- No spoilers but, who the hell mixed this man's voice? I could not, for the life of me, hear him a lot of the times. The Nikolai I remember had a much more intimidating presence and felt like an actual threat, like a completely Blisk type Mercenary. The choice on his design and all was just completely jarring from what I recall. His introduction was AMAZING, then he talked and I was like "Uh... what?" 

First of all, everything looks stunning. If you're a sucker for looks-- By all means, play this game. Anyway, I think for what this was, it was a good side game, as Resident Evil "Nemesis" was originally meant to be. However, Resident Evil "3" might need a DLC or an extended edition to really earn that title from me. Otherwise, it was not a regretful experience but I'll be playing Project Resistance for the most part. [h1] R3make is a fantastic reimagining of a classic game[/h1]

Though this game is shorter than RE2R and lighter on overall content, it is a much more polished experience IMO that still has a lot of replayability thanks to nightmare mode and the shop. (HOTDOGGER).
The pacing is better, with a lot of the redundancy and lazy back tracking in the structure of RE2R gone. or kept to a minimum without completely making it a full on action game. ALA RE6 (Not that RE6 is bad).
The environments of Racoon City and the adjoining areas are much more varied and lush, full of detail and color and whacky Capcom things like MOON DONUTS.
The soundtrack isn't a complete joke this time, and they even fixed the lack of Safe Room music.  You don't need a classic soundtrack mode when your remake soundtrack respects the original enough to make musical and arrangment references to the original. Or you know having actual music instead of just silence 80% of the time.
The character model for Jill looks far better and closer to the original designs compared to Claire in Re2r

This isn't meant to make RE2R look bad, because it's not. It's great, but I enjoyed R3make a lot more. To me it's an instant classic that sits perfectly alongside it's old classic self.

[b]Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]Play the game on Hardcore to start, anything less makes the game too easy IMO. Hardcore makes the difficulty just right with having to smartly manage your use of ammo and use of environmental combat aids. Enemies are still difficult to take down and you can easily run out of ammo and screw yourself. My initial playthrough of actual counted run time was 11 hours. . Combat is still not always the smartest move, as I died roughly 55 times. 
Complaints that this is "Too action oriented" are absurd. The balance of horror themes vs action is just right. And even if it was, there's no reason why the expansive universe of RE can't be anything other than straight metroid/puzzle/inventorymanagement-Vania. 
[*]Even after 20 years Nemesis is still terrifying.
[*]No more breakable knife nonsense!
[*]Improved controls with a fun reimagining of the dodge and quick turn introduced in the original. Quick turning now works at other angles besides a 180, which can be very useful. The doge roll/counter add a whole new layer of depth to the combat.
[*]Both playable characters have some fundamental differences in how their extra mechanics work that changes things up in a fun way. Being able to more aggressively take down enemies   (Since he's an experienced soldier)like later numbered RE games feels right at home.
[*]The expanded Carlos sections make the narrative feel more cohesive in a way that RE2R didn't between the main characters. This feels more like they claimed RE2R originally would be. Rather RE2R being more like the original game with Claire and Leon almost never interacting at all.
[*]The outdoor sections look visually much better than RE2R, with greater use of debris, color and variety.
[*]Fantastic soundtrack, and [!!] Safe Room music. Suzuki and Sato, RE veterans did a fantastic job compare to the disappointing mess that was RE2R's OST.
[*]The shop and Nightmare mode encourage attaining records and replaying the main game.
[*]The performance at equivalent settings seems better than RE2R. Though not without drawbacks. You can easily dial settings down to get the level of performance you want, and set the appropriate brightness settings. 
Visual issues like the insane HDR Auto Exposure adjustment from RE2R are fixed.
And the constant stutter from streaming while moving around in RE2R is gone. There are still stutters here and there. But nothing like RE2R.
[*]Incredible loading times on an NVME SSD, at 4k  with a stop watch I clocked how long it took from hitting "Play" on Steam to the point I got in game loading any save. [b] 25 seconds [/b].The load times are so damn fast you never have any time to read Loading Screen Tips. (I wish they had a button prompt instead). I missed out on a lot of tips this way haha. 
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b]
[*]Unless you count REsistance, the lack of  extra content here is disappointing. But what is here is very polished. I'll take Quality > Quantity any day of the week.  The length is fine considering the length of the original. (And length of other AAA games that no one complains about)And if you love to take in the sights and marvel at all the details. You will get more out of it.
[*]Removed content from the original game like The Mercenaries, which was a missed opportunity to add more post game content like in other RE games. Honestly the DLC content in RE2R was so good they could have made a spin off game with an entire game's worth of content like that + The Mercenaries.
[*]Enemies can still seem too bullet spongey, and unpredictable how many shots may or may not be needed to kill one. Even more so than RE2R at times. Forget taking them out at the knees. As that's even more unpredictable to determine how many shots that takes. (I have only played Hardcore and Nightmare mind you)
[*]I still feel like the story could've been expanded a bit more and a lot of characters could've used more screen time. I was disappointed they didn't retain how Brad died from the original(Which was nightmare fuel for 8 year old me). But it's an improvement from RE2R.
[*]Hair Rendering is a step down from Re2R with all hair being massively dithered this time around. Which results in really ugly looking hair on models like Carlos and Mikhail without massive downsampling. The TAA can't quite keep up with the dithering, resulting in some rather unsightly flickering at times.
[*]Screen Space Reflections are still garbage. The quality is very poor, it adds smearing artifacts with TAA on objects that don't have issues without it. And the performance needed at high resolutions is large. (Likewise turn down Volumetric Lighting to Medium for a large performance boost with little visual loss)The cube mapped reflections used without are much nicer looking.
[*]Banding, lots of banding. Though RE2R also had this issue. Older MTFramework games often had options hidden for higher quality HDR precision that fixed issues like this. Nothing here. Some light debanding from your display/TV's own options can help a lot. This also seems to lack the grain option that hid a lot of the banding in RE2R
[*]You still can't disable the aggressive sharpening used when TAA is disabled (TAA still needs a bit more sharpening. The built in sharpening Fidelity FX is very light)  and you still can't disable the vingetting effect used on the whole screen. Leading to bright objects looking dull on the edges of the screen.
[*]The game's volume output is very very low, so be prepared to turn your audio levels up. On average with my two amplifier setups, Windows volume of 35/100 is enough for most content. I had to turn it up to 90/100 or so to get similar levels out of RE3R.
[*]The game has problems with 3rd party OSDs and resolution switching which can cause the game to crash as it starts up in Windowed mode and attempts to switch to full screen rendering. Without a recent fix to ReShade, it will hard crash the game every time. Switching resolutions in FSE mode if an OSD is enabled can crash the game consistently.
[*]TAA quality hasn't been improved since RE7/RE2R, still suffering some of the same issues. It is already sharpened internally, but not quite enough. It needs at least a 225% (150% scale in game) oversampling on top to really look it's best and hide some of the problems/artifacts introduced in the process.
[*]Don't use Interlaced rendering unless you have a really, really POTATO PC. It looks awful just like RE7/RE2R. 
[*]FMV encoding is mediocre. But there is only maybe 1 or 2 in the game.
[/list]

This game is just not good.  It is in every way inferior to RE2make.  I'll revise this review after completing it, but I cannot in good faith recommend this to anyone.  Don't waste your money on this.

[Post Completion Edit]

My opinion on this game has not changed, and I'll try my best to highlight where it fails.  Unlike most people, I don't mind that this game was more action oriented than RE2make, or that it reused assets from 2, because the original RE3 did that as well.

My problem is: it doesn't do this well.  This game feels like a very poor attempt to throw anything the developers could think of to keep you entertained.  The new dodge mechanic just doesn't feel like it's very well utilized.  It's spotty, at best, which I suppose is in keeping with the original RE3, but I don't think maintaining frustratingly poor game mechanics belongs in this.  It's supposed to capture the good of the original, not mimic the bad.  You can time your dodge perfectly fine, but sometimes the game will just decide that it would rather tell you no.

Action.  This was intended to be a more action oriented game, just as RE3 did.  Here's the problem: it relies too heavily on cheap gimmicks and damage sponges.  Instant kills existed in RE3 before, but they just haven't aged very well at all.  The B hunters are designed to be this engaging fight where you have to weaken its armor so you can shoot its vulnerable head.  The only problem is that the thing has absurd movement, and a one hit melee kill.  I got so frustrated with them I decided I would just waste my grenades or explosives on them because I just didn't want to keep throwing myself at such a stupid brick wall.  Encounters are just not very creative at all.  It ranges from broken or unfair boss fights that you're just sick of wasting your ammo on, to "danger rooms" where you know an ambush is coming (in some cases even putting the zombie corpses to be invulnerable until you trigger their ambush) which are designed solely to just steal away the ammo you've been trying to preserve.  There are some really great encounters, like the first few nemesis fights or the power station, but they're all gimmicks that go away when you're done.  Especially the power station.  I was led to believe that the parasite affliction would be something to watch out for the entire game, it is not.  You never have to think about those enemies ever again.  And that's a real shame.

In RE2make, you gradually learned more and more ways to deal with increasing challenges, such as the lickers, or the sewer monsters.  Mechanics that were introduced in the game stayed to the end, and let you learn from them.  In RE3, you basically never have to deal with a monster outside of the place you encounter them the first time, with one exception in an incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ambush.

And then there is the weapons.  There is nothing to write home about here.  The knife has been upgraded to be infinite, but now it is severely less effective for you.  There are.....far....FAR too many kinds of grenade launcher ammunitions.  Your inventory becomes a mess of different types, all specifically used for different types of encounters.  Have flame rounds with you?  Sorry those are only useful against one type of hunter.  The OTHER type of hunter uses acid rounds.  Oh wait no, I'm sorry.  See the game TELLS you acid rounds are effective against them, when in reality explosive or mine thrower rounds work far more effectively.

This then brings me to Nemesis.  Nemesis was overhyped.  He lost any and all impact because he's just so....horribly....overused.  A good progressive enemy is someone like Vergil from Devil May Cry 3.  Someone who gradually expands his arsenal every encounter, but the encounters are rare and memorable.  Nemesis, on the other hand, feels like Team Rocket blasting off again with their newest crazy contraption to try and steal PikaJill.  There's also a borderline absurdity to the whole thing.  The remakes are supposed to be a bit more grounded in reality.  Nemesis is just hillariously indestructible in the story, which just really takes away the specialness to him.  And that doesn't even nearly go into how absurd Jill's fortitude is.  If you thought it was a bit absurd that Leon survived being pummelled through a metal grate in the first Burkin fight, yeah you're going to laugh your ass off at how constantly Jill is thrown around in cutscenes.  It's hard to buy that she's really struggling at any point given that she just walks away from crippling injuries and goes back to her every day ordeal.  It almost felt like torture porn the way that Jill is constantly...endlessly beaten around.  

You fight Nemesis...and Oh!  Three seconds later he teleports to another location with a new weapon or evolution.  It gets to the point where you're just tired of him.  What made Dr. Burkin, and to an extent Mr. X, work in RE2make was that they were not CONSTANTLY the only thing you fought.  Burkin is encountered at specific moments in the game, after long periods of time NOT having to deal with him.  This makes each fight more memorable.  With Nemesis, I honestly can't even remember all of the details from the point where he gets his flamethrower, to his rocketlauncher, to his other techniques.  Because they keep coming one after another.  At some point, you just want there to be zombies again so you have something ELSE to fight.

I'm disappointed.  I preordered this game immediately when it was announced because RE2make was handled with such love and care.  I don't feel the same love and care with this game.  It feels like they just threw together any crazy idea they could find, and didn't even think about the overall game flow.  I'm sad.  I'm really sad.  RE2make had me incredibly excited for other titles, such as Dino Crisis.  But now?  I'm going to wait to buy the next one, if I do at all, because this game was not worth the money.  RE2make made me want to unlock everything, and I did.  RE3make does not illicit the same kind of excitement.

Playing Resident Evil 3 Remake isn't all that bad. It tries to deliver on building story bridges and answer a few questions about Raccoon City. It does well to answer the questions left by Resident Evil 2 Remake while establishing itself as its own game. There's many pieces to go over, so I'll focus on the Pros, Cons, and suggestions.

[b] PROS [/b]
- Graphical scenery, lighting, and detail is a huge plus. Raccoon City looks great even during its death throes. 
- The Character revisions are lovely with both main and minor characters all having a strong appearance.
- Voice Acting and dialogue is very well done with lines delivered strong. "♥♥♥♥♥ can't even swim." Has become a well loved line.
- Gameplay is smoother with Jill's Dodge mechanic and rewards you with slowed time moment to take auto-aimed shots at the target. 
- Tension is always high with the action always around the corner. 
- Story is interesting with details filling in the blanks that we had from the Original game. (Jill's Apartment, Carlos's UBCS forces)
- Purchase of Resident Evil 3 also comes with Project Resistance, a Competitive, Multiplayer online game where four survivors face against a Mastermind player. Competing against the clock to survive, or be slain by the Mastermind. 

[b] CONS [/b]
- Game is CRIMINALLY short.  As opposed to Resident Evil 2 Remake, you're only going to get about 5 hours worth of actual gameplay, with about three hours of cutscenes. 
- Much of the replay value that the Original Resident Evil 3 had was cut. (No alternating paths, No puzzles, Hard Paths of No Returns)
- Majority of the game's events is Fetching items to progress further.  (Go to point A, grab Item, run to point B to turn it in.)
- Nemesis wasn't nearly as much a threat as people had hoped for.  You spend most of the game genuinely fleeing from him in Cutscenes than actually making decisions of Fight or Flight. 
- Gore has been toned down due to technical purposes. (You encounter far more zombies in a single area than RE2 RE had).  Enemy physics and gore changed, its noticeable and disappointing to say the least. 


[b] FEEDBACK [/b]

REmake 3 is an OK game, but it isn't $60 good, and I say that as a lifelong RE fan and someone who rarely buys games for full price unless they're new RE games. For anything else, I often wait years to get it for cheap. I should have done that here, and I'll probably exercise more caution in paying full price for RE8 or whatever comes next.

So what's wrong? They cut out WAY TOO MUCH from the original RE3. Locations (Clock Tower, Graveyard, & Park most noticably), puzzles, enemies, characters, the branching paths that gave the original a little more replayability--the list goes on and on. Some people are saying that it's a "4 hour game." I left it idling here and there, but I think I spent about 7 hours beating it blind on Hardcore, and that's with going out of my way to hunt for collectibles/items/etc that weren't necessary. I could imagine from my playthrough that a first playthrough on Standard difficulty, without hunting down optional stuff, would only take four hours or so.

So you're paying $60 for 4-7 hours of content, with the obvious counter to that being the inclusion of 1) unlockable harder difficulties, 2) an in-game store for buying new weapons, items, etc for subsequent playthroughs, and 3) the new Resistance spin-off. Let me address these.

1) The higher difficulties may give you another run or two, but you already know the (VERY LINEAR) layout of the city (which is essentially broken into isolated chunks that serve as levels--no real back tracking here past the first main area or two). The game has awards for speedrunning (which yield in-game currency for the shop), which demand you beat the game in 2.5 hours or less, which is EXTREMELY REASONABLE once you know the layout, you're used to the combat, etc. Skipping every cutscene and ignoring non-essentials, you've got this. Not much to say about a partial afternoon's worth of a new-game plus here.

2) The store lets you get new OP weapons, tokens to carry for health regen, etc. Some of these are essentially game breaking. Maybe even most of them. Of course, they're saved for when you beat the game and you need to clear challenges to get in game currency to buy them. But without even looking at the challenges you'll rack up a lot of points through a single playthrough, and after eyeing them up you'll find that most of what's left are either absurd grinding challenges (yes, Capcom, I would *LOVE* to grind through the linear campaign five times to kill enough zombies with weapon A so that I can start all over with weapon B, how did you know?) or challenge runs (beating the game without opening the storage boxes, or without healing, etc). Your desire to do the latter may vary based upon your enjoyment of the game. I personally don't think it's worth the time to play through this game another few times to unlock game-breaking weapons/items that you'll then play with for a few minutes each before they lose their novelty.

3) I honestly haven't bothered to try it. I never asked for it. Most of us didn't. The broad group of RE fans have been BEGGING for an Outbreak remake/remaster/re-release, etc, and I had hoped that this would serve as a spiritual successor to Outbreak or something, but it doesn't look like my kind of thing. I don't buy RE games to receive pack-in asymmetrical multiplayer spin-offs that are technically separate games. Selling two games for $60 is an alright deal, I guess, but if you don't want one of those games you're really paying $60 for the one you give a damn about. I wanted a single player survival horror game, or a multiplayer co-op survival horror game like Outbreak, but not whatever Resistance is supposed to be. For a rough equivalent, imagine ordering a main course at a restaurant, only to find that it's less than half as big as you wanted, and that half the cost is supposed to be for an appetizer you didn't ask for, but that MUST be served with the main course. Would you want that? No one would. Did you like the mini games that unlocked when you beat the original RE3? Too bad, those are gone. Play a 1v4 trend chasing spin-off instead. No Mercenaries for you.


Did you like the sensation of being pursued by a main enemy around a labyrinth of traps and monsters, sort of how the original RE3 felt and the RE2 remake felt? Nemesis only actually does this one time, for five minutes, towards the beginning in a very limited area. After that he's all cutscenes and boss fights, with scripted "chases" that are entirely linear and often have him using a one-off gimmick for that chase. Mr. X in REmake 2 feels more like Nemesis than New Nemesis. A HUGE waste of potential, in pretty much every way. They even dropped his name from the title, which might indicate that they knew they were neutering him, or it may just be a coincidence. Either way, the fights with him were repetitive and highly scripted. There were plenty of moments where he ignored a good chance to murder me so he could get geared up to go into the same scripted motions all over again. They essentially repeat the same boss fight twice with little variation, too.

I could go on, and on, and on about negatives, missing content, weird plot decisions, you name it. It's 2nd-hand embarrassing to see them fumble such an anticipated game, as it was not only meant to be the follow up to REmake 2, which was GREAT, but simultaneously a remake of many people's favorite entry in the franchise. They won't get another chance to do this anytime soon, but maybe 20 years from now we'll get RE-REmake 3, and they won't completely botch the whole thing. It was SUCH an easy sell and an easy job to just remake RE3 with as much care as they remade RE2, they had to go out of their way to make it something mediocre.

On the positive side, it looks really good. Jill's been inexplicably redesigned in the same vein as Claire, which is to say her face looks weird and I can't quite place why. It's almost an uncanny valley sort of deal, which I don't feel from any other character aside from maybe Carlos. Carlos has also been redesigned, but it's mostly just a new haircut. Other than that, characters look pretty good. Brad looks sort of like an overweight Mike Matei. Nemesis looks different now, too. They cut/changed his forms up, some of them being much more generic than they previously were, but none of them look completely awful. It seems like they dialed back the gore and body damage/deconstruction, definitely didn't feel as prominent/detailed.

The OST is REALLY good. Helps to give REmake 3 a tone sort of like a late 80s action-zombie movie. And I think that's what the developers were going for all around, not just with the OST. In that regard, it fits and was nice to listen to. Some very synth-y moments here and there.

I would recommend paying no more than $20 for REmake 3.

Oh, and replacing Jill's skirt with mom jorts, while mostly inconsequential, looks dumb. I get they were worried about upskirts or whatever, but there are a dozen ways they could have mitigated that, and there will be a mod to fix it sooner or later, so they're just condemning some poor dude with too much spare time to fix their lazy clothing redesign.

[h1]To summarize this review and to reiterate what many others have said: wait until it's on sale.[/h1]

[u]I LOVE the Resident Evil series[/u] and have since I was a kid and the original games came out. When the RE2 remake came out, I pre-ordered it just as I pre-ordered this game. The Resident Evil 2 remake is worth the full $60 launch price all day long. Two campaigns that play differently enough to maintain interest, each a good length. Upon finishing the game, you get access to the '2nd Run' mode, which REALLY makes it interesting. It somewhat speeds you through the beginning of the game and launches you right into the adventure and getting chased by the infamous Mr. X. Puzzles change and become harder, there's less ammunition in general...it's a great way to play the story. And upon beating the 2nd run mode, you get access to 'The Fourth Survivor' where you can play as Hunk and try to set a record time for escaping the city. There's also 'The Tofu Survivor' which lets you play, you guessed it, a gigantic block of Tofu in place of Hunk. Add to that the addition of 'The Ghost Survivors', giving you four unique mini-games with four different characters, and RE2 has [b]hours upon hours of replay value[/b]. [u]Worth every penny.[/u]

Now, on to Resident Evil 3. I pre-ordered it with excitement thinking I would be getting AT LEAST as much as we were treated to in RE2. Unfortunately, I was wrong. [u]Very[/u] wrong. You get the campaign, and that's it. If you beat the game on the Hardcore difficulty, you can unlock a harder difficulty in which nothing meaningful changes. There's no '2nd run' or 'new game plus' mode, there's no 'Mercenaries' mini-game or mini-game of any kind. After finishing the game, you can use points you accrued and purchase items like costumes, weapons with infinite ammo and special coins that increase stats like defense, damage and healing. Don't worry though, it won't take you long at all to discover the aforementioned store since the campaign is short. Really short. Average play time is about half that of RE2. My very first play through was comfortably paced between 'let's explore' and 'let's see the end' and it took me a touch over 5 hours. My disappointment was compounded by the lack of previously mentioned post-game activity. I'm 3/4 of the way through a new playthrough and it's only taken me 2 hours now that I know the game. [b]My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined.[/b]

The game obviously has it's merits though: it is GORGEOUS and it's very fun. The intro is fantastic and really sets the stage and pace of the rest of the game. The enemies can be plentiful and challenging. There are just the right amount of classic 'RE puzzles' but not so much that you get tired of them. Overall, the game is great and is absolutely worth playing, especially if you're an RE fan. But if I could do it again, I would absolutely not spend $60 on this game and I can't recommend that anyone else does either. There is very little replay value, if any. I have high hopes they might release updates that include additional modes in the future, unless they're going to continue focusing on the dreadful Resident Evil: Resistance online game. I know it's a beta, but that thing is...woof, no thanks.

If you're a hardcore fan that absolutely has to play this game right now, go for it. But for now--and with a heavy heart--I can't recommend this game [b]AT THIS PRICE POINT[/b]. I'm truly bummed about that.
