If you liked RE2 Remake  (which would be strange if you didn't) then you will enjoy this. It gives you a good dose of survival horror that fans of the genre look for. I did however notice the fact that it is a shorter game. Some aspects of the game may feel slightly rushed in that regard, but this was only developed over the last year as far as i'm aware (here i'm not talking about the quality of the production but mainly the story telling). A few extra puzzles or a longer take on Carlos's story would have helped. I certainly feel that this game took a more linear approach to game-play, this is not necessarily a bad thing as it contributes to the fact that it feels more like a separate game to RE2 Remake and not an obvious clone. Another difference I found was that (at least in standard difficulty) I was never too low on any supplies such as ammunition and herbs. This combined with the more linear game-play aspect and a reduction in the quantity/length of puzzles came across as a shift to a more action oriented style game, rather than the more spooky take that RE2 Remake had on its atmosphere. Nevertheless the creature design and detail is still remarkably lifelike and detailed for a game of this era, which is a testament to the incredible game engine that Capcom have created. 

All in all I am glad to have this in my steam collection! Of course it stands on the shoulders of Resident Evil 2 Remake, and many will compare it to that game, but I still enjoyed every moment in this one too despite it being a little on the short side. I look forward to all future Resident Evil titles!

Resident Evil 3 should have been $20 worth of DLC for Resident Evil 2 instead of pretending to be a full priced $60 game. It’s a 4 or 5 hour linear experience with little replay value. It doesn’t take good advantage of its Racoon City setting and it completely squanders the potential for engaging and emergent cat and mouse gameplay with Nemesis.

The first hour or so of the game is pretty promising. After getting chased out of your apartment from the STARS obsessed Nemesis, you find yourself exploring a few square blocks of downtown Raccoon City. There are actually multiple stores that you can enter, and a couple of different paths around the environment. You have to move back and forward across this section of the city while you solve puzzles that unlock previously locked stores or alleyways. Your goal is to get a Subway train working again in order to evacuate some civilians. At some scripted point in the story Nemesis shows back up, and he chases you around pre-determined areas while you are trying to get things done. It’s actually all pretty cool, but unfortunately once you get the subway train up and running again (which takes about an hour), the game throws out this semi-open world level design and moves on to tight corridor’s and even more tightly scripted Nemesis encounters. It’s a real shame, because if the rest of the game was actually like the first hour, I could maybe forgive its short length.

You don’t really get to experience the city setting anymore once you get off of the train. The city is there as a backdrop, but it doesn’t factor into the gameplay at all. When you do go back outside, it’s very obvious that you are just walking down what are essentially outdoor hallways. There is always conveniently placed debris blocking off all the side streets and alleyways and generally no branching paths that you can take. A quick glance at the map confirms there is only one path forward.  The remainder of the game takes place mostly indoors anyway, including a short trip back to the Racoon City Police Department, the Racoon City Hospital and of course a secret Umbrella Lab. During these sequences you are mostly just walking down hallways blasting everything that moves. This game has a way more action focus then Resident Evil 2, and throws tons of resources at you. I finished the with tons of ammo and healing left over plus the materials to craft a lot more. You are never resource starved, and the game feels easy as a result.

There is also very little in the way of classic Resident Evil style puzzle solving. It’s almost all traditional keycard hunts that would feel more at home in a Doom game then the odd and elaborate puzzles we have come to expect in Resident Evil games. You won’t be putting Medallions in statutes to reveal hidden passages or slotting chess themed fuses into the correct boxes to unlock doors. Instead, expect to search dead bodies for company ID cards that you slot into card readers in front of doors. Resident Evil feels more like an action game series again instead of survival horror. Bummer.

I think the biggest disappointment of Resident Evil 3 has to be the Nemesis. What I wanted to see was an intelligent enemy that chases you throughout the game. Basically, an expanded take on Tyrant (Mr. X) from the Resident Evil 2 remake. Instead what we got is highly scripted chase sequences where Nemesis shows up and chases you down pre-determined paths until he gets temporarily dispatched in a cutscene at the end of the hallway. Once that happens, he is completely gone until he shows up in the next cutscene / scripted sequence. You can’t kill Nemesis during these sequences either, although you can temporarily knock him down if you do enough damage. There are four Nemesis encounters in the game where knocking him down will cause him to drop a supply case, but its only worth doing during the first two. Knocking Nemesis down at the Power Station and outside the Donut Shop will drop you upgrades for your handgun. The other two encounters will only give you some ammo. Tyrant from Resident Evil 2 was a better take on this concept in my opinion, and I would have just rather had that over what we ended up getting.

The game looks and runs really nice at least. Even on my aging computer I was able to run the game basically maxed out at 1440p and sustain a framerate above 70FPS at all times, often over 100FPS. The RE Engine is really solid technology. There is a ton of detail in the scenery, and I have to mention how exceptional the character models and their facial animation are. The only real complaints I had about the presentation is that the reflections still look really bad, and that zombie animations in the distance run at like 30 frames per second which is really distracting and annoying when you are trying to hit someone far away. I would love to see an option on PC to adjust that, as it doesn’t seem necessary to save on performance.

I think what it comes down to is that this game needed a lot more time in development. Supposedly the game was in the works for years before it was announced, but it just doesn’t come across in the final product. The whole thing feels rushed and unambitious. It’s just entirely too short, and it doesn’t make good on the fantastic opportunities they had to do something special with the series. We get a glimpse of that potential in the game’s opening act, before being pulled back into rudimentary level design and an over emphasis on combat and scripted sequences. The asking price is way too high, wait for a sale before you buy.

Oh boy, I normally don't care if Steam doesn't have a neutral rating, but I think this game needs one, there's a lot to like and a lot to not like.

[h1] The good [/h1]
-Nemesis, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, when this guy's on screen, you better haul ass, it makes for some intense chases, how easy or difficult the chase depends on how many zombies you dispatched. Oh you left a few zombies in a zone that Nemesis chased you into? Well tough ♥♥♥♥ you either runs through them and risk taking damage, or waste ammo as Nemesis closes in.
-The RE Engine impresses, the lighting, the details, basically everything in the environment blends together perfectly, there's no loading screen (except the one you get when load into the game).
-Remember that dodgy emergency evade move in the original RE3? The one that barely works and you need like nanoseconds of reaction time for it to work, well in this Remake, the dodge function is mapped onto a single key, and if timed correctly, it gives you a slow-mo effect, plus an auto-lock onto a monster's weak spot, letting you dispatch foes with ease, much better implementation.
-The downtown section of the game is amazing, I love how the city is all connected via metal walkways and doors, there's a lot of details and environmental story telling with files and scenery. The hospital sequence is also quite tense with the introduction of the newly designed Hunter.
-I think the redesigned Jill Valentine is great, and they also brought back the Carlos camp. I love the cheesy one-liners. While Mikhail and Nicolai doesn't get much changes, I appreciated the added scene with Tyrell.
-------------------------------------------------
[h1] The in-between [/h1]
-This game is incredibly short, which WILL be a problem for a lot of folks, main story took me 5 and half hours, which for a full-priced game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid. I personally really enjoyed the 5 and half hours I played, but for everybody else, please wait for a sale, this should've being a $30-40 DLC for RE2R instead.
-Remember how Mr. X in RE2 remake was an omni-presence in the RPD section of the game, stalking you from room to room? Well Nemesis only appears in scripted sequences, which isn't many. I don't remember how he behaved in the original, but he felt like he was always around. scripted or not, Nemesis definitely felt like he had more of a presence in the original game than the remake, which is just a shame.
-Also in the OG RE3, Nemesis spent the entire downtown portion of the game in his iconic jacket/coat, not in the remake unfortunately, not really a downside, just because I think Nemesis looks way more intimidating in his coat/jacket.
-While Nemesis looks great in his first form (trench coat), his 2nd and 3rd form leaves much to be desired, his exposed tentacle body in the OG RE3 makes him look more like a rampaging B.O.W. than what we got in the remake, but YMMV.
-The new dodge move mechanic takes some practice to get the timing down, and there's no Invincibility Frame, which isn't a bad thing.
-The game is more action heavy, which for me personally isn't a bad thing, as the original was also more action packed, but now we have 2 different remakes with 2 different vibes, RE2R for more survival horror, RE3R for more action horror, but not as stupid and ridiculous as RE5 and 6.
-Just like RE2 remake, the game breaks into 3 parts, where you play as both Jill and Carlos separately, and just like RE2 remake, the the game gradually loses its vibe as it goes on, amazing 1st part, ok 2nd part, meh 3rd part.
-RE Resistance seems ok, I didn't put in a lot of time for it, and to be honest I don't really care about it, if it's something for you, go right ahead, I can see this mode being fun if you can get 4 others in a party.
-------------------------------------------------
[h1] The bad [/h1]
-Remember in the OG RE3, there's a live selection system? Well that ♥♥♥♥ is gone, and Crapcom replaced it with......nothing, yeah they took it out and didn't offer anything in return, which naturally means there's only ONE ending.
-Ammo crafting is the same as RE2R, where in the OG RE3 had enhanced ammo, this one has...nothing.
-The serious lack of puzzles, remember the clock-tower and water-treatment plant puzzle in OG RE3? Well they're gone! And we got NOTHING! The "best" puzzle is a train related puzzle, rest are just you finding several things and put them in a few slots, or combines them THEN put in a slot, very creative.
-The clock-tower area is gone and again, we got nothing, the clock-tower was a pretty pivotal moment in the OG RE3. In the remake we only get a short glimpse and a jaunt through the area, that's it.
-Not only the clock-tower, the graveyard, the park (which isn't really all that interesting anyways), and the sewer disposal facility is all gone, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WHAT!?

I'm a huge fan of RE2MAKE and have lots and lots of hours in it. (Over 200) Sadly, this game does not live up to its predecessor. I'll go into why. Let's work it off one by one.

Also, this review comes from a person that has NEVER played the original Resident Evil games. I have played from Resident Evil 4 onwards. I understand that a lot has been cut out from the original but this review does not go into that, as I would simply not be qualified to talk about it.


[h1]1. Story[/h1]

It's aight. Nothing special but it even falls short in comparison to other Resident Evil games. There aren't really any likable characters here (except Carlos), and the main villain blatantly goes against his own ambitions to be...evil? He just becomes a mustache-twirling idiot. Which would be fine if the game was self-aware about it but it doesn't feel like it is.

There's a whole lot of "meh" that you're going to forget about the moment you lay the game down. Let's just move on.


[h1]2. NEMESIS[/h1]

This is the big one.

Remember how RE2MAKE knocked it out of the park? A tense, survival-horror scavenger hunt in which you need to progress while being stalked by an unstoppable, terrifying force? Granted, X wasn't in all of the game but he was (in my opinion) very fun, and very much gave the game its identity.

Ironically, this game fails in that exact aspect. It's in the title folks, this game is about NEMESIS, the hulking monstrosity that was to end Mr.X and expose him for the weak puppy he is. Let's talk about that.

[b]He isn't.[/b]

Nemesis is a set-piece. Apart from one area (the demo area) where he actually dynamically chases you around, he will only appear in scripted chase sequences that get old fast. I'm all for high-octane set-pieces but this isn't the place for it. And if that's all you got to offer, your game plays itself and is, in turn, pretty boring. All those moments cowering in a corner, listening to Mr.X's thundering footsteps passing by, waiting for your opportunity to pass (hopefully) unnoticed? They don't happen. They kind of promised us that Nemesis was going to be an evolution of X, but he ISN'T. You wouldn't be wrong to feel a little tricked.


[h1]3. Level Design[/h1]

Okay, so, this is not bad. It's just not what you'd expect from a RE. The levels are very, [b]very[/b] linear. You're only occasionally asked to backtrack and will, most of the time, simply follow the linear path to the next set-piece.

The chases are fine. They give you decent indicators of where to go throughout the game. (guidance by light or billboards) The guiding light color in this game is yellow, so if you're ever stuck, just look for a yellow arrow, or anything yellow to guide you forward. It's good level design. Adhering to the standards of the industry. For a linear game.


[h1]4. Puzzles[/h1]

They don't exist. Next.


[h1]5. Gameplay[/h1]

The only place where this game gets the upper hand. And even that is subjective. I love the way you are now able to dodge attacks if you pull it off correctly. They even give you a free critical hit, if you perfect dodge and counter attack! Very fun. This replaces the "joker-system" from RE2MAKE where you can have a joker-item (flashbang, hand grenade, knife) to avoid taking damage upon being grabbed. I personally like the dodge mechanic more. Although this will of course depend on your personal tastes. One thing is for sure, it improves the bossfights! They are really fun if you pull the dodges off. 

For the rest, the gun-play is identical to RE2MAKE. It's still good fun. 


There is a shop you can buy extras in after finishing the game once. This is where you get the infinite weapons and other goodies. Decent.

There are no extra modes. Only 2 extra difficulties which are Nightmare and Inferno. Items, and enemy locations switch around akin to Madhouse from RE7, which is a feature I welcome. But it isn't as good as Madhouse. Key items are in the same places and progression is 100% the same. Meh.

That's it. That's all there is. The only thing holding this game up for me is that the dodge-mechanic is so fun. It is literally the saving grace for me. Without it, I wouldn't even have given this game a second look and just re-played RE2MAKE.


[h1]6. Graphics[/h1]

The graphics are, as expected from the RE Engine, top notch. They deliver incredible visuals while also keeping the FPS sky-high. This game runs silky smooth and never EVER dips. Your mileage may vary, but this was my experience.

Anti-aliasing options adhere to the new standard of FXAA, SMAA, TAA and TAA+FXAA. I'd recommend TAA with a decent Reshade, to sharpen the blurriness that it causes.
The only place where it can fall short is texture quality. These aren't always up to snuff. Character models and essentials are good, but everything else has the tendency to look a bit muddier than you'd expect. This has always been a point of critique with the RE engine, so I won't nag on it too much.

It's really good. The game is pretty.

[strike]I don't like Jill's face though.[/strike]


[h1]7. Soundtrack[/h1]

I'm crying. They butchered my expectations. RE2MAKE had such a phenomenal soundtrack that I, [b]to this day[/b], listen to it on Spotify. I could list so many reasons as to why it was great but I don't want to write an entire essay on music theory or personal taste here, so I'll move on as fast as I can.

But let me warn you, this game does not have a single song, that you will even remotely remember after finishing it. It is devoid of character. Bereft of identity. Barren in terms of soul. Sans particularity. 
You get it yet?
I'm sad. 

The best song in the OST is the Resistance theme which is just... 

[strike]I wanna die[/strike]


[h1]8. Multiplayer[/h1]

I have absolutely no interest in a multiplayer Resident Evil so I have ignored it so far. I won't comment on it since it could, for all I know, be the next holy grail in asymmetrical multiplayer. I've played the beta and lost interest after 2 matches.


[h1]9. Conclusion[/h1]

It's a good game. People have commented on the length (or lack thereof), which I can agree with. It does lack in length. And it does not make up for it in girth (as RE2MAKE did). And I will now promptly stop with the penis analogies.

Wait for it to go on sale, as it will disappoint you as a fan of the remakes, as well as a fan of the original. But it is not bad. It's fun. Others have stated that it feels very much like an OK DLC to RE2MAKE, which I can agree with. In it's own right, without context, this is a fun but overpriced game.

In context and stacked up to the masterpiece that was RE2MAKE, this is a joke. It doesn't even attempt to imitate it and steers more in the direction of RE6 than RE2MAKE. Which is not really what I want after getting a taste of the alternative.

So, I have played this game obsessively and have, by now, finished it around 5 times on Standard and Hardcore difficulty.

(Part of that can be seen here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CpYobfhD4vM&feature=youtu.be )

However, while I do recommend this game, I can NOT recommend it at full price. Wait until it comes out on sale or, if you own a console, wait until you can get it used for cheap. Here are a few Pros and Cons:

Pros: The game just looks beautiful. The gunplay is solid, even if the Zombies lumbering around and their heads flopping all over the place makes headshots really hard to perform. But then again, they are walking corpses, what do you expect? In that regard, the game is just awesome. The story is, however, a bit of a disappointment to me. I have never finished the original RE3 on the PS 1, but I do know from friends and YouTube videos how it is supposed to end in terms of bossfights, but that might be a good thing, adapting them to modern times. Another pro is, that they gave the game the entire RE2 treatment and so the damn tank controlls that we had to deal with, even in the RE1 HD remaster, have been thrown out the window for much more intuitive modern controlls.

Contra: The evasion/dodge mechanic is something that this game relies on quite a lot, and I know I am not the best gamer ever (Still, I managed to beat the game with an S Rank in 1 hour 11 minutes!) but the dodging just doesn't work. You will see a Zombie lumbering towards you and suddenly lunge, and even if you press the right button instantly, it is a gamble if your charakter actually performs the dodge or not. And even if you dodge, your opponent (I had that happen sooo many times) will instantly follow up with another attack. With you basically being unable to do anything for about half a second after you come out of your dodge roll, you are open to that follow up attack and will take damage regardless of your "perfect dodge". The only "ingame" way to make the whole thing viable, is to unlock the physical training manual so that dodging works better.

Some other stuff has to do with the puzzles, which just makes me shake my head. At one part, you have to plot a route for the subway train to take to get to safety, and you are shown a little screen with a map of the RC Subway, with smudged notes on it. There is barely any way to do this puzzle right on your first try, since you have no indication what the shorts on the machine (SA, RA, RE, FO etc.) are supposed to mean and are not labled on the map of the subway that you are shown. However, as soon as you FAIL the puzzle, you are shown a PROPER map of the subway, that hangs on the other side of the room. This way you can easily plot a route.

The second is in the NEST-2 complex where you have to make the vaccine for the T-Virus. The machine tells you to "Insert Materials"... I tried and the machine tells me that an uncompatible substance was detected. I tried over and over, with the same results. (Tried to put them in in another order and such). The solution was to "combine" the two substances in your inventory... Yes... Jill Valentine suddenly became an expert at mixing highly valuable biological substances into a viable solution, using two test tubes that are both over half full. 

In short: The game is nice to waste some time and it definitely is fun, but you will also rage a lot, especially when Nemesis pulls back his arm to hit you, you press space to dodge, and the animation doesn't even start, but instead you get a fist in the face. 

And to those who say that dodging likely just didn't work for me because of lags or something... Guys, I'm running on a 8700k with 16GB Ram and GTX 1080 with a stable 60FPS....

Previously, I considered the Resident Evil 2 (RE2) remake to be the best RE game I've ever played. However, my opinion has changed with the release of Resident Evil 3 (RE3). Despite some common complaints I've read online, I was confident in my decision to purchase RE3, and I'm glad I did. Regardless of what others may think, I believe the RE3 remake is one of the best games I've ever played.

Although I never played the original RE3, I'm aware of the differences between the original and the remake. However, in my opinion, these differences are inconsequential. Similar to the RE2 remake, Capcom has breathed new life into RE3, delivering a tense, atmospheric, action-oriented survival game.

Despite being a modern game, RE3 manages to retain a nostalgic, old-school single-player feel that is increasingly rare in today's gaming landscape. This aspect is particularly appealing to me, as I crave more stellar single-player experiences that evoke the good old days of gaming.

For those who are on the fence about RE3, I can confidently say that if you enjoyed RE2, you will likely enjoy RE3 as well. Yes, it may be a shorter game with less replayability, but it is undeniably a great game.

Now, let's discuss the pros:

Brilliant Graphics: The overall visuals are impressive, creating a great tense atmosphere. The diverse level design is visually stunning and engaging.

Nemesis: When Nemesis appears, he becomes an unstoppable force, relentlessly stalking and posing a significant threat. Unlike Mr. X, you can't simply run circles around a table to evade him. However, he isn't overpowered either. Dealing with Nemesis adds another layer of tension and makes for exciting encounters.

Puzzles: As someone who generally dislikes puzzles in games, I was pleasantly surprised by the ones in RE3. They are not overly challenging, so don't let that deter you from playing the game. If you do get stuck, there are plenty of online guides available to assist you. The puzzles in RE3 are even easier than those in RE2, and there aren't as many of them.

Gore: The game doesn't shy away from blood and gore, which is both satisfying and visually impressive. Although there may be a slight toning down of dismemberment due to the increased number of zombies, it doesn't detract from the overall experience. Everything else gore-wise is as you would expect from playing RE2.

Fun Combat: Similar to RE2, shooting enemies in specific body parts yields different reactions. Shoot a zombie in the legs, and it will fall to the ground. Shoot its limbs enough times, and they will break off. It's particularly thrilling when you shoot off all the limbs, and the zombie is still alive, wriggling on the floor, trying to bite you!

Zombies and Other Creatures: The zombies in this game look great and behave like you would expect zombies to behave. They are genuinely creepy, especially when they pretend to be "dead" and then surprise attack you. Additionally, the Hunter Gammas, Betas, and Drain Deimos provide variety, much like Lickers and G-types did in RE2.

Stealth: I appreciate the subtle stealth elements in this game, such as sneaking past Lickers without alerting them to your location. It adds an enjoyable layer of tension, knowing that one wrong move could give away your position.

Survival: The limited quantities of precious ammo and supplies make you want to thoroughly search every room, locker, and strongbox for anything useful, even if it's just to save for a rainy day.

Encourages Replayability: The ranking system and unlockable items in the in-game shop, along with additional difficulties like "Nightmare" and "Inferno," provide incentives for replaying the game.

Nightmare Difficulty: Nightmare mode cleverly increases the difficulty more than you may initially expect, resulting in a significantly changed and improved experience.

Secrets and Exploration: The game rewards exploration, offering plenty of secrets to discover throughout the gameplay.

Boss Fights: While not the most complex, the boss fights in RE3 are well-executed and superior to those in RE2. They provide an enjoyable challenge.

Good Soundtrack: The game features a great soundtrack that complements the fast-paced, action-packed story, pushing you forward.

Now, let's discuss the cons:

End Game Ranking: Similar to RE2, I find the way the ranking system is handled in the game to be problematic. You are placed under an arbitrary time constraint that determines your rank at the end, and there is also a limit on save games. In order to achieve a good rank or even an S Rank, you are forced to speedrun the game. Personally, I feel this goes against the design of survival horror games and isn't my idea of fun. Furthermore, certain points earned by completing in-game records are tied to obtaining specific rankings.

Before buying the game I read a couple of reviews that said how: "if you're a RE veteran you won't like this one", how so? I am RE veteran and I loved it. If you are a long time RE fan and are unsure if you want to buy this game or not, definitely do it! I feel like a lot of people missed the point of this remake.

For sure, as someone who enjoyed the original RE3 along with the other games, I can definitely confirm that they indeed changed things up a lot more with this one compared to RE2make, and they also really took out a bunch of sections from the original, however, that really doesn't bother me to be honest. If I wanted to re-experience the original RE3 experience with no variation, I would have just played the OG game. It's not like that one disappeared, it's still there and it's still good. 

With this remake Capcom intended to tidy up the whole experience and make a game that would tie up perfectly with the new retconned timeline and boy oh boy, they sure succeeded. If they remade the game exactly like the original, it would have definitely felt a bit out of place and that would have had a very significant impact on the pacing (which I found absolutely perfect in this one).

And you know, from a purely gameplay standpoint, I actually think I enjoyed this one even more than RE2make. 
I do have one problem with it though, in that I only wish Nemesis would have been used more inside Raccoon City. His encounters defeinitely felt a bit scripted and peppered here and there throughout the section inside RC, and I only wish he would have been more of an ever present and contast threat much like Mr X felt in RE2. That being said, every single Nemesis apparition was amazing, they really did his character justice, and that really makes me wish we had gotten WAY more of him. This is personaly the only disappointing note about RE3make.

The gameplay is incredibly smooth, and the evade mechanic makes a return in this remake but with a significant difference, this time it works!! 
They also took out the sub weapons but this was, I suspect, to balance out the aforementioned dodge mechanic. With both of those options I feel like we would have had an abundance of evasive tools, and that would have definitely made the game a bit too easy. 
Now, the style of gemaply is definitely WAY more action oriented compared to 2 (much like the original), but in a good way. This feels like the GOOD kind of Resident Evil action/horror experience.

The RE Engine once again delivers some breath taking visuals, the level of polish that this game has in unreal. Even playing at mid to high settings I can legit count the pores on the character faces. 
Also really loved the job they did with the new voices, especially Jill's, it suits her character perfectly and I really hope we'll hear more of her.

It makes me incredibly happy how they managed to fix up the story of the original game. With the remakes, Capcom is doing an amazing job of fixing up the plot inconsintencies of the old entries, and neatly tying up the timeline of the series. They also improved some of the characters (IE they gave Nicholai some character motivations, instead of just making him evil for the sake of being evil) and they made them all feel way more real and multidimensional, and also set some perfect hooks for a Code Veronica and a RE4 remake.

In conclusion: Is RE3make the same as RE3? No, but it doesn't have to be. Resident Evil 3 remake works perfectly well in the context of the new retconned timeline, if they re-made it exactly like the original it wouldn't have worked at all. Sure, the game may not be perfect, Nemesis should have been way more present, and I feel like the FOV could have been opened up *coff coff a lot coff coff* more during the last boss fights, but the game is still a LOT of fun, and still really REALLY REALLY good. I truly cannot wait to go at it again.

Decided to give this a shot since I bought it for $45 off GMG and figured even with a short experience it was probably worth the equivalent of a couple new movies, time and money-wise.

Things just feel slightly "off" for me with the controls, I can't really put my finger on it but it just doesn't feel as responsive to my inputs.  I ended up needing to use KBM to deal with the spider section of the power plant and even there it almost felt like there was some sort of inertia to the aiming.  Jill actually bounced off the gate and took a hit that should never have happened.  I don't mind one or two hit kills, but only I don't feel like I'm dying because the game isn't doing what I'm telling it to do.

I've also seen weird things where if I mess up a dodge, but am out of a zombie's reach, it seems to teleport a couple of feet it needs to grab me.  Hopefully this is just a camera bug or something because I've also seen Nemesis just seem to appear out of thin air during his encounters in the city.

The lack of rag-doll physics when downing a zombie as well as the limb separation is also disappointing compared to RE2.

Edit 1: I forgot to add, the shotgun is just so very weird.  The spread of the pellets is utterly ridiculous, they have to be spreading before they leave the chamber, let alone the barrel.  I know the developers may not have a lot of shooting experience but 10 seconds online will show that for a regular shotgun you're looking at a couple inch spread for most of the ranges.  The RE2 shotgun was fine but this is just madness.

Hopefully the experience will get better but I cannot recommend this game; wait until it is about $30 or less.

Edit 2:  It doesn't get much better, pretty much everything with Nikolai is just cringe-inducing.  The fact Jill doesn't just take him out on many occasions, couldn't even grab his boot and yank him into the pit for goodness sake.  He's also written as just a cartoon image of a bad guy, no proper motivation than "money" even though saving the vaccine for himself would have been the smartest thing to do.

The hospital hunters had me hanging my head in shame on behalf of whatever play testers had this area.  The room with the two of them was just a sad sack of failure.  One hunter could actually follow me out and was a bit of a challenge.  The remaining one was stuck near the bed, basically I could open the door shoot him once or twice, go back out and wait for him to reset.  If I tried to do anything else, they would just bug/get clipped in the door and one-shot me if I approached.

The firearm audio seemed weird as well, the shots were so quiet I could hear the rounds hitting zombies or pinging off the environment when I missed more than the sound of the actual gunshot.  The M4 had me sighing as well.  Capcom continues to treat rifles and SMGs as weaker than pistols for some reason when getting either should be a massive upgrade.

All-in-all, RE3 was a visually impressive game but I just felt sadder and more frustrated the longer I played.  Based on this experience I probably won't even bother with RE8 when it comes out.

RESIDENT EVIL 2 is much better.
While playing RESIDENT EVIL 3, in some moments the game feels similar to the sixth installment and to the shooter-style elements of previous parts of the franchise. The bosses are very weak, and during Nemesis chases you can take him down with just one grenade. The game feels more like a small DLC for the second part priced at 499 UAH — nothing more.

Overall, the game is not bad, but it is very short. The secret ending hinting at a possible continuation after the events of RESIDENT EVIL 3 (2020) was at least a nice surprise.

The multiplayer mode called Resident Evil Resistance was also enjoyable.
I like Resident Evil Resistance because there are more and more trash-like games similar to DBD (Dead by Daylight), but this one often feels more like Last Year rather than DBD, even though they are all basically DBD clones.

Despite the fact that the story campaign is short, the release price is somewhat justified thanks to the multiplayer game Resident Evil Resistance — but there is one issue:
since it is a DBD clone, not everyone will like this price, because such analogues — and even the original — usually do not cost more than 499 UAH.

Let me explain:
Resident Evil Resistance comes bundled with RESIDENT EVIL 3, but if it were sold as a separate game for a separate price, it wouldn’t cost more than 499 UAH, just like all similar games. In that case, RESIDENT EVIL 3 itself should have been much cheaper at release, not 2000 UAH as it is now.

Conclusion:

1. At release, for 2000 UAH you get two Resident Evil games, meaning each one costs about 499 UAH

2. I recommend waiting for discounts. Not everyone can afford a 2000-UAH game, even if there are two games included.

3. It’s a shame that Resident Evil Resistance cannot be purchased separately. In principle, if it were sold separately, paying 999 UAH for Resident Evil Resistance at release would have been acceptable.

4. Resident Evil Resistance is plagiarism based on Dead by Daylight, Friday the 13th: The Game, Last Year, Deceit, and others.

5. RESIDENT EVIL 7 and RESIDENT EVIL 2 are much better than RESIDENT EVIL 3, at least because they have both paid and free DLC, which RESIDENT EVIL 3 lacks.

I have not played the original Resident Evil games, only RE:7, the RE:2 remake and now the RE:3 remake.

First off RE:3 is not a bad game, not at all. It's fun game play wise and definitely entertaining especially after RE:2 as it explains some things that it's predecessor didn't yet it doesn't live up to the legacy of RE:2.
BUT and this is a big but, it's flawed, way to short and way too expensive.

The RE:2 remake was a good game that had, what in my opinion is the core of Resident Evil, way more horror moments and an oppressing feeling. It wanted you to explore and find all of it's secrets so that my first run lasted around 10 hours maybe a bit longer.
Re:3 took me barely 6 with a lot of useless running around and looking for the last possible green herb. There was not so much of "exploration" to do but rather backtracking and remembering where a lock to lockpick was, a chain to cut etc.

Nemesis, for all the hype that surrounded it, didn't live up to his name in this remake as he never felt as frightening or lethal as Mr. X. Sure he has a  [spoiler] flamethrower [/spoiler] and a  [spoiler] rocket launcher [/spoiler] as well as his iconic tentacle but he isn't as relentless in his pursuit nor has he as much screen time as his counterpart from Resident Evil 2. Where Mr. X got an annoyance at the end Nemesis started with being an annoyance. Nemesis just stays in front of Jill when he knocks her down instead of finishing her off and delivering a "Game Over". His appears in short chase scenes instead of Mr. X's iconic echoing footsteps throughout the RPD really fail to bring him any real sense of fear or danger.

But not all is bad. The gun play, which in all three Resident Evil games I played was meh at best, is still meh at best. Yet the guns feel balanced and serve a purpose although the acid rounds feel neglected for the most part of the game (again). Even the pea shooter pistol that becomes quite useless at the end becomes a bit less useless when u get a three burst alternative? Why an alternative? Why not make it a mod? (I am fully aware that this is not how guns work but Resident Evil has never had realistic weapon or weapon modding to begin with.)

Resident Evil 3 also fails to highlight the strong points of Resident Evil 2 and 7. Where there were puzzle's and riddle to solve in the other games we now get shooter parts with Carlos (he also recycles the RPD map from the RE:2 remake which shows how some things happened before the arrival of the RE:2 protagonist which is amusing to see but overall pretty lazy on the developers side).
I really like the guy, his interaction with Jill are fine, his crush is cute and his face looks more like a Carlos then the original model.

If you played the original before, it is definitely a nice fresh take on it, and if somebody plays with the thought of playing the games in a chronological order, it's definitely a nice addition.

I love the look of the game. If you can run it on high or max settings, it's a catch for the eye, and gameplay-wise, movement was done great—it's fluid and intuitive, even though the hitboxes of enemies sometimes cause frustration.

But it's not flawless.

For people who just play through the games once or twice, it's definitely not worth 60€. The campaign, even if you take your time and investigate carefully on the hardest mode possible for the first run (Hardcore), only takes up something between 5–7h (depending on your playstyle).

So if you don't enjoy the classic way to play Resident Evil games (playing the game over and over), I'd definitely wait until the game is like 20€.

If you are a veteran, get ready to have runs taking not more than 2h.

I would consider myself a veteran in the series, and in my first playthrough I did unlock about 50% of the challenges, and this in like 6.5h (I did enjoy the atmosphere on the first run).

I started with Hardcore and went up the ladder: Nightmare, Inferno—and to be honest, on any difficulty it's not very hard. The only real change in difficulty I witnessed was on the last boss, who started easy on Hardcore but in Inferno and Nightmare had moves that could stunlock you and kill you 100% if you misclicked once, no matter how much health you have.

I am at a point where I can tell every step you need to do to complete the game out of the back of my head, and I am only 35 hours in.

So, to sum up everything:

The game is amazing if you play it for the first and maybe the second time.

I really enjoy both Resident Evil 3: Remake & Resident Evil: Resistance and although both games combined can't reach the excellence, Resident Evil 2: Remake has been last year, both of them are still very good games, with some minor flaws.

Resident Evil 3: Remake

The Main Game you get with this bundle. It's the Remake of the original Resident Evil: Nemesis and like the original, it's more action focused. So players of RE2:Remake keep that in mind, if you expect another game like that, you won't get it here.
What you get here is an action packed, visually stunning and polished RE game, not completely over the top action like RE6, it's more like a faster paced RE2:Remake.
You now get a Dodge Move, more ammunition, especially for high explosives and more scripted action events, in most of them, you have to fight or escape the Nemesis.
Nemesis is unlike Mr.X. He is not constantly stalking you in an area. He spawns at special locations at set times, is faster and deadlier than Mr.X and can use Weapons, like rocket launchers or flame throwers.
You also have to fight him several times as a classic boss fight in arenas and those fights are pretty cool imo.

After a while, the game changes the character from Jill Valentine to Carlos Oliveira. Carlos parts are compared to Jills pretty difficult, because you can't outrun most enemies and you just get swarmed by either many enemies, or a few really dangerous ones. And although you got a heavy arsenal of weapons and grenades, the number and quality of enemies kept me struggling at times.

Alright, now keep in mind that Re3:Remake is a really short game, first playthrough should be around 5-7 Hours, depends on how much you explore or take your time.
This game is also not as good as a remake as RE2:Remake. Many locations and events from the original are missing and although I don't mind the short playtime, if the game is fun, while playing I felt like they could easily implemented some more content, based on the original.
So what I wanted was just more of RE3 - It's still a great game though!

But keep in mind the shortness and missing locations. If you are just here for RE3:Remake, then wait for a sale I would say.
I think 60€ is still a fair price since you also get Resident Evil: Resistance, the Multiplayer Game, which I enjoy a ton right now.
If Multiplayer doesn't interest you, better wait for sale.

Resident Evil: Resistance is a asymmetrical Game where one player as a Mastermind plays against a group of 4 Survivors, each with special perks.
The Survivors get locked inside a scenario, where they have to escape within a time limit.
It's always 3 phases of one level. In the first, the survivors have to find puzzle pieces. The second one is about locating a special zombie, who drops an item with which you can hack inside 3 terminals to proceed.
The last one is about destroying 3 Biohazard Tubes by attacking them.

As the Mastermind, you control all Cameras all around the place and can switch between them. Use that + your map to locate the survivors, watch all the steps they take to complete their objective and do everything you can to prevent them from their goals.
To do that, you can spawn all kinds of Zombies, Traps, lock doors or set up Guns attatched to the cameras.
Also you are able to spawn ultimate Bioweapons like Mr.X or William Birkin.

You are also able to control most Creatures directly.
If you hit or kill the survivors, they get a time penalty and as a mastermind you win if the timer reaches 0 before the Survivors completed all objectives and they get bonus time by doing so.

This game is really enjoyable, especially playing as the Mastermind and a cool addition to the Resident Evil 3 Remake Bundle.
Beware that Queue times for this game for the Mastermind are enormous and unless they patch it, finding a game as a Mastermind is really difficult and that sucks.
Also the game has a steep learing curve. Unless you inform youself, what to do beforehand via tutorials, videos or free play, you will propably loose the first few games, but if you hang in there and learn the mechanics, you can wreak havoc upon the survivors as the Mastermind.

So in conclusion:

If you plan on playing RE3:Remake AND RE:Resistance, just get the game, it's worth it!
If you are just interested in either one of them, better wait for a sale, since you will be paying for the content you get of both games, otherwise you may experience a lack of content you will get here, at least compared to the previous RE2:Remake.
But still, you get great games, there is nothing wrong with the quality - most negative reviews are about the short length and because of missing locations/events from the original RE:Nemesis.

I thoroughly enjoyed the Resident Evil 2 remake. What a way to top an already classic game. Resident Evil 3 has never been considered a classic, but given the advancements and all-round good work done in RE2, who in their right mind would turn their noses up at another instalment?!

Well, keep those noses up people. What you are paying a AAA price tag for, is nothing more than RE2 DLC.

Firstly, the price tag of this game needs to be reduced. It cannot be considered a full game by any stretch of the imagination. Capcom have not inserted any individuality when it comes to RE3. They have taken the backdrops from RE2 and some new characters and to add insult to injury, severely watered down game play also.

The game play is far too linear. There is no freedom to roam, much like there is in RE2. The aspect of having to backtrack and puzzle solve in RE2 is what made feel like a complete game. Hard for me to admit, but RE3 feels like one long, interactive cutscene. You are forced to go from point A, to point B throughout its entirety. In some ways, it feels like an instalment to the Uncharted series. Good to look at, but not a lot of challenging gameplay happening before you.

Nemesis. Jesus. What a pain in the rear he is. Where we had Mr. X in RE2, that random, yet terrifying of beings, we now have some less sinister. The joy of Mr. X was you never quite knew where or when he would appear. Not so the case with Nemesis. His introduction (at every instance) is greeted with a cutscene, very far removed from the suspense of Mr. X. His cinematic cues really take away from the unexpectedness and overall, becomes more of a nuisance than anything else.

The gameplay itself mimics that of RE2. Using the same engine, that's unsurprising. Minor tweaks, such as the knife can't be used as a melee weapon when grappling a zombie, yet doesn't lose damage when you use it as a main weapon.

All in all, I wouldn't recommend this game as it stands. Reduce the price to around the 10GBP mark and that would be a fair reflection.

Tl;dr - Should have been released as DLC. Nemesis no where near as terrifying as Mr. X

[b]Welcome to Resident Evil 3 the sub-par follow up to an already perfect remake, I hope you all enjoy leftovers.[/b]

[h1]Before I Even Get Started[/h1]

I just want everyone to know before reading this review that RE3 was never my favourite RE game in the franchise, in fact, for me, it's not even a true sequel, it was more of a side story and CV for Dreamcast is the true continuation of the story but that's an entirely other subject. Sony was just fulfilling a contract to put out 3 numbered games on the original PSX at the time, so that's proof enough it was rushed even back in 1998.

So here we have a game with re-used assets, toned down gore, removed rag doll physics and cut content... Also the fans who helped Capcom work on the RE2 Remake were not present during it's development and this project was given to Capcom's "B Team" to handle because everything was already spelled out for them.

It was kind of like a paint by numbers project, they were basically handed an engine and told to tweek some things and re-skin all the characters... that's about it.

[h1]What Has Changed From the Original?[/h1]

So I'm not basing this review on this game as a stand alone and this review isn't for people new to the franchise, this game was made for old school fans who know what they're getting themselves in to. What I'm going to do now is just provide a list of things that were removed or added, it doesn't necessarily mean these things are bad or good one way or the other but I'm here to provide information for the curious.

+ Dodge Feature is easier to pull off and damn near breaks the game unlike the original where it wasn't even necessary to use.
+ Characters dialog has been vastly improved.
+ UBCS members all received personality upgrades and are just more realistic people over all and a lot more likable, even Nicholai, whom you love to hate.
+ Carlos is way less obnoxious in this game and his voice is more suited to how he looks, his hair is also amazing.
+  New areas and expanded older areas to explore. The Hospital is by far a huge improvement over the original.
+ The R.P.D. is a much longer section now and Carlos returns there instead of Jill.
+ Lickers make a re-appearance instead of being removed entirely.
+ There's a section where Carlos has to withstand a horde akin to the cabin section with Luis Sera in RE4.
+ The hardest Resident Evil game in the history of the franchise, until you unlock the cheat shop and then it becomes about as trivial as the original did, so at least it stayed true to form in that regard.
+ Hunter Beta's make their return but look more akin to Hunter Alphas for some reason, they can easily one shot kill you and are truly the most terrifying enemy in the game, even more so than Nemesis which is just kind of sad.
+ Hunter Gamma's are amazing looking in this rendition of the game but their only function is to serve as an ammo dump unfortunately.
+ Stayed true to the original ranking system where healing too much actually lowers your ranking.
+ Drain Deimos have been turned in to what looks like some kind of grass hopper type bug that injects you with a parasite that forces you to waste herbs to vomit, otherwise you instantly die. Interesting change.
+ Hospital area expanded on and is probably the best part of the entire game.
+ Ridiculous brain bending puzzles removed so the game stays more akin to it's action roots.
+ Lab section is a lot less frustrating and wraps up the end of the game faster than the original.
+ New sewer area and construction site zone.
+ Improved final Nemesis fights.
-  Still no Crows.
- Knife is complete garbage in this version due to the rag doll physics being removed, no longer even viable.
- Rag doll physics were removed entirely, enemies are now like walking brick walls and you no longer feel the impact of your attacks.
- Gore was toned done considerably, limbs no longer dangle off of zombies bodies and fall to the floor. Instead they just explode and disappear. 
- Head shots are also a lot less frequent, almost to the point of non-existence and don't feel good, they kind of just happen whenever they feel like it.
- Shotgun lost a lot of it's impact because of the toned down gore / rag doll effects and just feels terrible to use.
- Nemesis drops are total garbage and there's only 4 of them instead of 8... The first two of them being crappy handgun upgrades instead of a new shot gun or infinite ammo or even the first aid boxes.
- Nemesis' new forms are complete trash, he follows you on foot and gets a rocket launcher then mutates in to a quadrupedal beast about half way through the game (which originally was his final form) and becomes easier to deal with from here on out for some reason.
- Jill sounds like an adolescent immature 18 year old going through hormone problems and not that of a grizzled veteran adult who's seen some ♥♥♥♥ and has matured because of it.
- Grenade Launcher ammo is all messed up in this version, no freeze rounds either... replaced by Mine rounds. 
- Acid rounds are now the strongest ammo in the game when they used to be the worst in the original RE3, also they're impossible to find / create due to the lack of gun powder for them so you need to conserve them.
- Game is horribly balanced and there's 5 different difficulties instead of 3 so it's just a bunch of redundant nonsense. 
- Saving the game is worthless until you hit Inferno Mode, you can rely on auto saves all the way up until Nightmare Mode to beat the game not saving at all.
- No Ink Ribbons. (Seriously wtf?)
- Once the infinite launcher is unlocked (which doesn't take much effort) it trivializes the entire game. There's literally no reason to ever use another gun after you have this weapon as it doesn't effect your end game ranking.
- No S+ Ranking and no hidden content locked behind performing well, you basically just grind out kills by auto loading Carlos' auto saves when the zombies bust through the hospital doors and toss a grenade. Rinse and repeat until you hit 2000 kills and that's half the cost of the infinite launcher right there.
- Nightmare and Inferno mode are balanced around having some, if not all, of the extra cheat content unlocked, otherwise it's damn near impossible to get through these modes just going bare bones... so again, horrible balancing issues. Game is either ridiculously difficult or way too easy which forces the user to just make up their own mind about how they want to do things instead of the dev's actually taking the time to balance out the game difficulties.
- No hidden Barry ending and no alternate paths, live selection removed.
- Clock Tower area removed completely.

[h1]Final Verdict[/h1]

Meh. It's not a terrible game but it doesn't hold a candle to RE2Remake which is probably among the best RE games in the series at this point, next to the original RE1 Gamecube Remake. 

It's not a true 1:1 remake either like RE2 Remake was. RE3 Remake stays true to form but in a very moot and subtle way where the dev's expect you to unlock cheats to balance out the absurd difficulty. Also I wasn't as open to the changes they made in RE3R as I was to RE2R... I felt like they could have did better with what they had to work with but it fell flat. 

Also there's absolutely no reason to not use the infinite launcher once you have it so it kind of killed the game for me. At least in RE2R there's a reason to replay the game not using infinite weapons so you can get the S+ rank, it felt good to do and was a nice challenge.

 In summation, Is RE3R trash? No... but is it as amazing and wonderful to replay as RE2 Remake was? Not a chance in hell.

It's like eating leftovers from a really good meal, like the food is still good but it's just not the same as when it was cooked fresh. I would wait for a sale honestly but if you're a die hard, you probably already own it.

REmake 3 is an interesting beast. After the near masterpiece that was the remake of Resident Evil 2, I think expectations were set way too high for the remake of Resident Evil 3. Just as the original RE3 was to the original RE2, this reimagining is definitely a step down from its predecessor. That's not to say this game is bad, far from it. I do think REmake 3 is a great game, but it has its drawbacks. Many of the features REmake 2 was praised for are absent in RE3. The level design is significantly linear, the puzzles are nearly non-existent, and perhaps the biggest disappointment is the new Nemesis. After how incredible of a foe Mr. X was in RE2, I couldn't wait to see Nemesis, but unfortunately all the things that made Mr. X great are absent from Nemesis. Rather than relentlessly stalking you, Nemesis only really appears during scripted sequences, resulting in him losing a lot of his intimidation factor. A lot of his forms have been cut from the game as well, making Nemesis overall much less interesting. Speaking of cuts, RE3 has a lot of them from the original. The Clock Tower, Graveyard, Park, Grave Digger boss, and so much more is now missing from the game. While this remake fails to live up to the original, it does improve on it in some ways. I think the storytelling here is much improved over the original, with better dialogue, story progression, and the cast is more interesting than they were in the original. Overall, I don't think this remake is as good as the original RE3, but that's not to say this is a bad game. Like REmake 2, the combat is loads of fun, enemies are interesting, and the game is overall gorgeous. RE3 also has many ties to the remake of RE2 in terms of story and visuals. While I don't think RE3 stands amazingly well on its own, it makes a fantastic companion piece to last year's Resident Evil 2. I still definitely recommend the new Resident Evil 3, but wait for sale!

When the first trailer of RE3 got uploaded only a few months after the release of RE2, I could tell that this was going to be a rushed work. But since Capcom has redeemed themselves over the years and especially with the RE2 Remake, I still had high hopes for this one. And although the game did not fail entirely, it however mostly failed to meet expectations. 
My main issue with the game is of course what has been echoed throughout in almost every review, it's that it's laughably short.(It averages of 4-5 hours for most people the first time) People love to make the arguement that the original was already short so it's justified. This statement makes me cringe so hard. Just because it's a remake doesn't necessarily mean it has to be the same length as the original. Especially when the remake removes a lot of content from the original game:
-Areas: Clock Tower, The Park and Dead Factory
-The Grave Digger Boss
-Decent puzzle challenges
-Multiple branching paths
-Mercenaries mode
All of these made the original much more replayable regardless of its length, which the remake lacks. It's true that RE2 remake also did cut out some things from the original, but since that game was so well designed and well paced it wasn't really a big deal, it's a great game on its own.
I've played this game on standard difficulty, and since I was playing an RE game, I've naturally avoided combat as much as I could. But eventually I got to the end point and noticed I had way too much ammo and way too many healing items. At points the game gave you so much sh*t to store that it became comical. So basically don't play on standard difficulty, it's a cakewalk. Choosing the higher difficulty also doesn't include ink ribbons anymore(dafuq), so even in that difficulty the tension isn't that high.
Now to the positives:
-The game looks amazing, even better than RE2:RE
-The beginning of the game where you are in the city is pretty good(after the city the game slowly goes downhill)
-When the Nemesis chases you in the city(None of that scripted events BS)
-The boss battles are kinda better than in RE2:RE, but still are meh
-The dodge mechanic: I was really hoping they would include it here to make the game stand out more, and it gladly did. However it's not perfect. I hate to say it but QTE's such as these to dodge or counter enemies were done better in RE6, since in that game an icon always popped up at the moment when you could do these moves, hence you could practice it much better. In RE3 it only came in handy as a last resort. Still not bad though.

So despite all of these flaws I still wouldn't say that this is a bad game, far from it. This game was asking for full price at the time of its release, but now it has went down to 40 euros, which is still a little too much for its asking price but definitely closer to its deserved pricing. Wait for a discount and give it a try.

Well, I'm gonna hand it to Capcom. They managed to follow up my favourite game of last year with what could easily be my #1 pick this year. Playing RE2 Remake isn't required, but returning players will find the game easy to pick up with only a few new additions to the mechanics. The story is self contained while still adding depth to the story from 2, and theres also a few locations that will be familiar while still offering a new experience. The pacing is considerably faster this time around and can border on frantic at some points but you are always given ample time to explore every area and ammo and item pickups are abundant throughout the game. Nemesis.. I think he's pretty damn awesome. He's present through the entire game and never fails to raise the stakes when he shows up.. Which is often. He really only ever disappears just long enough for you to get comfortable and start to forget about him. At the same time he never overstays his welcome to the point where he becomes an actual annoyance. He also functions as the games measuring stick for Jill's overall power level and you will go from having no means of fighting him and being forced to flee for your life in several scenarios, to being able to dig your heels in and fight him head-on in a number of climactic battles. Character art and scenery is great. Level design is simple but effective. Music and atmosphere is top notch. Voice acting is quite good. Puzzles are..... a thing. If you were hoping for challenging puzzles then you're probably going to be a bit disappointed. I'll go ahead and say the simpler puzzles are fine here in the interest of preserving the pace. I don't want to say it's a perfect game... but if it'll get the rest of the industry to pull their heads out of their asses then....

After the resounding success of the Resident Evil 2 Remake (Despite its flaws i.e. Lack of true B scenarios), I was hoping for good things from Capcom, but sometimes you can expect too much, right? 

Lets also get this out of the way, I've played every Resident Evil game there is to play, it is one of those franchises that despite its multiple lacklustre titles I will always try the games. 

When it comes to this game there is a giant, S.T.A.R.S shouting elephant in the room. Nemesis, the main threat, the main selling point of this game, the iconic (and I don't mean iconic jacket iconic) biohazard weapon somehow manages to become a footnote. The implementation of Nemesis is sloppy at best. In the early stages of the game I experienced several times when he will phase in and out of existence. During an early segment of the game I found myself cornered by him, I managed to dodge past him and leave the room, I waited for him to start leaving the room so I could keep track of him, nothing... I waited, and then the sound of ominous footsteps behind me, he somehow managed to get behind me. I can understand the developers wanting to make him more of a threat than Mr X, but teleportation!? C'mon now.[spoiler] Most of the encounters with Nemesis are either arena style battles, with very obvious ways to defeat him or moments when you have to run through a gauntlet of Zombies with him chasing you, and oh my, this totally doesn't get old fast.[/spoiler] Instead of a grumbling guttural S.T.A.R.S, Nemesis is more of a wet fart lingering in the air. 

There are so many moments from the original game that are synonymous with the franchise and more importantly the original Resident Evil 3; Brads death, the clock tower, the grave digger, mercenaries mode, [spoiler]being rescued by Barry[/spoiler] and many more. But it seems like those involved with the creation of the game decided to do a David Benioff &  D. B. Weiss and just forget. 

These things being cut only to add to the games ultimate downfall, its length and pacing. Many people have said that the addition of a clock-tower area would have significantly improved the reception of the game, and I agree. Another area where the game fails is its puzzles, they are either too simple to work out or the items to complete them are presented to you within a few minutes. A dark, dank and spooky clock-tower with three or four meaty puzzles to get your teeth into would have been welcome. Don't get me wrong, I loved the hospital section, but the fact it was expanded upon to seemingly replace another area just left a sour taste in my mouth. 

Those of you who have played the original Resident Evil 3 would remember that you have moments where you can choose what to do, ultimately changing the game and the ending. There is non of this, not a single moment where you can choose. Resident Evil 2 had the B Scenarios, Resident Evil 3 had its different endings and choices to draw you back in for another play-though. My play time on Steam is currently sitting at seven hours, and I have a feeling its going to stay that way. What you unlock after finishing the game (and no, I wont spoil it) to me, isn't worth the extra time to play again. For fifty pounds, I expected much more. 

All of this is a shame, this could have been so much more. The presentation of the game is fantastic, voice acting, graphics, design of monsters and sound design are all great steps forward for the franchise. 

Prior to this I was hoping to see remakes of other Resident Evil games, but all I can say is please, Capcom, stay away from Code Veronica.

If you enjoyed the original RE3 and RE2 remake, then you will very likely enjoy this. The same breath-taking graphics and realism that was in RE2 is present in RE3. Jill herself is a far more realistic character with more depth, and gameplay elements unique to RE3 return in such a way that they add to the horror while still balancing the more action-heavy elements present in the original game. As I recommended to a friend: for the best experience, if you've already played RE2, try RE3 on hard mode out the gate. This makes Nemesis and certain portions of the game (specifically the hospital) far more tense and anxiety-inducing. Enemies specific to RE3 are given a breath of fresh air.

That being said, many reviewers have noted certain issues they have with the game that, while I understand, I do not agree with as much. Those include one-hit deaths that feel cheap, linear gameplay, and a lack of replayability. While there are one-hit kills, they are usually similar to the alligator scene in RE2 and are not frequent. RE3 is somewhat more linear than RE2, but this is due to the fact that the areas are not quite as large and you will, at points, be propelled forward to new areas without the option to return due to Nemesis' pursuit. Unfortunately, Resistance replaced the classic Mercenaries mode -- I haven't played enough of Resistance to comment on how enjoyable it may or may not be. However, RE3 does offer some replayability with harder difficulties that are unlocked after completion, with the ability to replay the game with new unlockables.

Overall, RE3 is an enjoyable experience for long-time fans and those who enjoyed RE3, but may not offer as much replay value (unless you are interested in Resistance) until DLC or more mods are released.

When compared to Resident Evil 2's recent remake this game really pales.

First, let me say this: this is an action-oriented Resident Evil title. The atmosphere and terror of the previous two RE titles (7, and 2) are left at the wayside for massive set pieces, Michael Bay-style explosions, and on-rails sequences that play more like cut scenes than anything else. There are entire moments that require you to unload as much ammo as possible into waves of enemies just to survive and trigger the next event. 

The nemesis chases are a shell of what they were in the original title. They feel scripted, and aside from a few gimmicky mechanics the nemesis in this just feels like more of an upgrade from Mr. X than a true menacing creature. I had read from build-up articles leading up to the game's release that Nemesis was going to be menacing, this truly terrifying creature that would have players wetting their pants whenever they encountered him. I read that he was going to invade safe rooms, that he was going to tear down walls, that he would appear in any direction to the player and keep them on their toes. He never did any of that. The walls he did tear down were scripted and never changed.

They've messed with a lot of the story from the original title, so much so that some events that take place in the titles that come after this one don't line up very well now. It's more of a direct sequel to the remake of RE2 than it is a true remake of the original RE3. Entire sections of the original game have been cut out, resulting in a game that took me only 6 hours to beat for my first playthrough, and that's with me exploring every little corridor taking my time to take in the scenery. The writing is sub-par compared to RE7 and the RE2 remake and this title really feels rushed -- I guess that's what happens when you push something like this out in just a year. 

Look, I'm not going to jump on-board with the people that are claiming that this should've just been DLC; it's bigger than that... But I will say that this didn't meet expectations at all. It's worth it at the $20-25 mark, but not worth it as a $60 title. Save your money.

Games like this makes me wish I could leave a "mixed" review. It's disappointing in terms of missing content, but the game itself is far from bad, so it doesn't really warrant a negative review. So here goes.

[h1]Pros[/h1]

The graphics and sound design [b]looks and sounds amazing[/b], every single area looks good and the levels are well designed with [b]neat attention to detail[/b].

The gameplay is easy to get used to and pulling off the perfect dodges are satisfying and rewarding.

The story is engaging with likable characters and interesting lore.

Soundtrack was a huge improvement from RE2make, with the return of save room music and having a better soundtrack overall.

Completing records will now [b]reward players with credits that they can use to buy items/weapons[/b] for their next playthrough, giving the game more replay value.

[b]Smooth, natural and great quality cutscene animations[/b].

Voice acting was on point.

Overall a [b]very easy game to enjoy[/b].

[h1]Cons[/h1]

Now, the cons. This game's campaign is very short [i](especially being ~US$60)[/i], lasting only roughly [b]4 hours[/b] even though I tried exploring everything.

The game also has a huge [b]lacking in content compared to RE2make's extra modes[/b]. Although you can unlock [b]"Nightmare"[/b] and [b]"Inferno"[/b] mode after beating hardcore, it only changes [i]some enemy and object placements[/i], while the relatively easy "puzzles" still have same solutions.

Combat-wise, I have a lot to rant about. For one, there's a noticeable [i]tone down in critical headshot chances and gore in general[/i] which is pretty disappointing. Zombie physics were so much more dynamic in RE2make, which is confusing as this game seems to [b]completely downgrade the ragdoll physics and dismemberment system.[/b]

Despite wanting to be more action oriented, the zombies are still damage sponges. The assault rifle also [b]somehow feels weaker than the pistol[/b], and the shotgun doesn't feel that powerful anymore.

The decision to remove multiple choices and endings was a terrible idea in my opinion as it made R3make a very linear game, removing any depth and extra replay value the game could have had.

Pretty minor issue compared to the rest, but the lip syncing out of cinematic cutscenes is really poor.

All in all, [b]R3make is a very good game[/b]. It just seems rushed and not worth the price, I feel that a couple more months of polishing as well as different development decisions, would have done this game a huge favor. I feel that this game should be worth US$40 instead, just because it feels like it has so much less to offer compared to RE2make.

However, even with all the downsides that I listed, giving it a negative review just doesn't sit right with me. Again, this game is amazing, you're almost guaranteed to have a good time, it just lacks content to justify the price.

I bought the remake of Resi 2 for full price last year, and enjoyed every moment of it. The only reason I didn't pay for this one was because I was gifted a copy by my best friend. With that said, I was overall quite satisfied with my first playthrough of this game and would've been happy for the $60 purchase if it came out of my own pocket, but it isn't without its shortcomings.

This game is wildly different from the PlayStation original. The plot, and the events that occur within it, has been altered and rearranged a bit for smoother progression between story beats and have fewer slow moments. The more open nature of Raccoon City from the original has been toned down quite a bit, with several smaller hub areas during different parts of the game instead of exploring the streets of downtown to get everywhere. I honestly think that this is for the best as the novelty of exploring the winding streets wears off about halfway through on PS1, and it becomes more of a chore during the latter half.

A couple of key locales from the original game have also been minimalized, if not outright skipped, in this iteration. This has lead to the frustration and/or disappointment of many old school Resident Evil fans, and understandably so, but I found that didn't detract from my experience with the game despite their exclusion. I found it's worth mentioning because if you expecting more of a straight remake like 2, you will probably be disappointed.

Much like how RE3 was a structurally different game than RE2 on the PS1, the remake also deviates from how the remake of RE2 does things. You basically hit the ground running from the beginning, the game is more action oriented in parts, there are a few more open in areas, and there are more RE4/5 styled cutscenes and sequences. Jill and Carlos's dynamic has been changed (for the better IMHO), and Carlos has a lot more agency and involvement in the story.

Nemesis has seen the biggest change in this game, both in physical and mechanical design. Without getting into a lot of detail, he isn't exactly like the Tyrant in the remake of 2, and most of your encounters with him are more of a spectacle. I'm a bit torn about how I feel about this: on one hand he feels more like a threat and less of a nuisance than in the original, on the other it takes out the looming threat aspect that the original and Resi 2 remake's Mr. X had.

The biggest complaint I've had about this game though, is the lack of bonus content. There's still stuff to unlock in this game, don't get me wrong, but it pales in comparison to RE2 or its remake, or even the original version of RE3. I do like how you get unlockables in this game, [spoiler]it's a point-store system where you get points to spend on unlockables based on what achievements you've unlocked and your graded score each time you complete the game,[/spoiler] but what you see on offer is pitiful. You don't even get the option to use the original game's soundtrack like in 2 (yes, 3 reused a number of tracks from 2, but it still had its own tracks).

Outside of the classic costumes you get as a preorder bonus, you only unlock [u]ONE[/u] costume for Jill. Sure, you can unlock other helpful items, a few custom weapons, and the obligatory infinite rocket launcher that's been a series staple since the original Resident Evil on PS1, but while there are over a dozen unlockables it's padded with a bit and doesn't even include all of the items from the original or the previous remake. I sincerely hope like with RE2, we'll see some free DLC in the near future to make up for the lackluster stuff on offer, but I'm not holding my breath.

I think the lack of meaningful bonus content, and inclusion of Resistance as a separate game included with the purchase of RE3, speak more about how rushed this game was more than anything else. It's kinda funny that this game feels like an afterthought much like the original PS1 version was back in 1999, but I'm still overall quite happy with the 4-5 hour experience I got for my first playthrough. I say wait for this game to go on sale if you're unsure whether or not this game alone will satisfy you for 60 bones, but with Resistance it could be a worthwhile bundle if you enjoy asymmetrical multiplayer (I haven't played it, nor do I have plans on playing it in the near future).
