Return to Raccoon City to face a new kind of evil!

PROS: Nearly everything that made the previous game good carried over into this title.  The gameplay is wonderful, the visuals are spectacular, and, like the original Resident Evil 3, the game increases the amount of action through the whole game, showing a few signs that would eventually lead into...or I suppose around to Resident Evil 4.  The perfect dodge makes it even easier to slip past the undead, providing incentive to learn the timing and attacks of your enemies.  One of the more notable improvements of this title is the soundtrack.  The audio actually kicks in from time to time, rather than place a few ambient tracks here and there.  The sewers are thankfully a lot more brief than the last title, and there's a larger variety of special infected.  The aspects of the game even change between different difficulty levels, causing different or additional enemies to spawn, keeping the player on edge as the game gets harder.  The Nemesis is an improved Mr. X, amping up the scares as he hunts you down.  Finally, the game actually gives reasons to knock out it's in game records list, as each gives the player points to buy upgrades, such as the infinite ammo weapons, and additional hip pouches.

CONS: Unfortunately, a few cons also carry over as well.  The game allows the player to explore segments of Raccoon City, but lacks a definite set piece like the RPD station.  The revisit to the RPD was a nice touch, but felt a little too brief.  Brief is the real key word there, as the game is noticeably shorter than the last title, using more difficulty levels to make up for that fact.  The Nemesis attempts to provide some additional set pieces, but this causes a detriment to the game.  Even though he's far faster and more dangerous than Mr. X, it doesn't feel as fluid as Mr. X skulking around the RPD.

ACHIEVEMENTS: This list carried over a few challenges from the previous title, opting for that same kind of challenge the last title had.  Once again, memorizing a layout to run through is the best option one can take, and with the records shop, purchasing key items can make a run significantly easier.

FINAL: This is a bit of a tricky one.  One the one hand, it's more of the same, providing another wonderful experience with few in the way of flaws.  On the other, it actually feels a little bit of a lesser title compared to the previous entry.  I'd still give it a hard recommendation for anyone looking for a solid survival horror title, solid game overall, or just someone looking for more of the Resident Evil series, but perhaps go in with the knowledge that this is more or less an add on to the previous title.  A well polished, fun, amazingly designed add on that should be played at least once, but an add on nonetheless.

Edit: Wow, I didn't realize this review would get so much attention so I wanted to clear a couple things. I've been a pretty recent fan of the RE series, starting at RE7, so my perception of what makes a good RE remake is probably different then what long term fans of the series believe, so keep that in mind. I've also never played the original RE2 or RE3, so my basis for how good these games are isn't based on how good of a remake they are, they are just based on how good I believe they are compared to similar games I've played. I would also like to point out that I did enjoy this game, but I definitely had problems with it which I talk about in this review, and I wouldn't recommend that anyone pay full price for this game. Anyway, take my review as you please. 

First off, it's insulting that this game is priced at $60. I was able to beat the game in under 5 hours my first time through since I played through RE7 and the RE2 remake on the hardest difficulties; however, this game was significantly easier to me, even on hardcore mode. The locations which you go through in this game are smaller and much more linear than RE2, which unfortunately makes this game not as fun. In addition, there is only one story to play through in this game, so instead of choosing to play as Jill or Carlos like Leon or Claire in RE2, you alternate playing between the two characters throughout one story. In RE2, the campaigns for both characters were quite short once you got the hang of them, but there were 4 different ways to play through it since both characters had 2 different routes, making the game about 20 hours worth of content if you only played each route once; however, there is only one route to play through in this game (at least at launch), turning what could've been another 20 hours of content into only about 5 if you know what you're doing, which is extremely disappointing. Another large problem with this game is that it reuses far too many assets from the RE2 remake including zombie models, textures, weapons, and even locations you play in from RE2, making it feel like this game was made quite lazily and should've just been RE2 DLC. For instance, I recognized the first zombie that I encountered in this game, and immediately realized it was a zombie I've seen in the RE2 remake. This game also takes away certain mechanics from RE2, but doesn't replace them with anything new or unique, and essentially left me wanting much more from this game than what I was given. I will say that the story telling in this game is better than RE2, but that isn't much of a compliment considering how awful the storytelling was in RE2. One thing I can give this game credit for is that Nemesis is a much larger threat and much faster than Mr.X; however, a huge problem with him is that he doesn't wander around the map and show up at random times like Mr.X does. You mainly only fight him in scripted events that feel pitted in your favor, ruining a huge piece of what made the RE2 remake so great. I haven't tried Resistance yet since I'm not a huge fan of multiplayer games, but talking about this game alone, I see it as a huge missed opportunity to make an amazing game out of what was already a great game (meaning the RE2 remake). If you are considering buying this game, go play RE2  instead, its definitely a much better game with more depth and it's just more fun in general.

R3make.
3/5 - Story
4/5 - Atmosphere/Environment
4/5 -  Gameplay
4/5 -  Audio
2/5 - Replayability

For fans of old. You'll be disappointed but nostalgia is still there. For casual newcomers, the game is almost solid as it sounds. You'll be facing a threat known as Nemesis throughout the game just like the original abeit in a lesser capacity. R3make is a solid continuation from R2make. The experience is rightfully deserved for atleast one playthrough.

Story-wise the game presents it's retelling of the original Re3/Biohazard 3 Nemesis and most of it is presented well. The focus of the game is clear. Escape (defeat) Nemesis and escape the City. Raccoon City is pretty much dead. Several support characters (and new ones) also return to help Jill and Carlos to find a way out of the chaos. There are no more option dialogues and thus, no multiple endings afaik. However, the story is also short but the focus is clear whereas R2make gave a sense of "what the hell is going on." Also, Nemesis doesn't really chase you down in every sequence of the game.

Environment is rendered beautifully. Volumetric lighting and bloom used to it's fullest. Dark areas barely illuminated gives a sense of dread and eerie-esque vibes. Especially, around corners, alleys, sewers, and roads. The modernized Raccoon City feels like complete chaos and abandoned after the outbreak. Immersively impressive. Though the levels are highly linear and personally would like some variance (different routes to try in each playthrough). There are cut areas from original that didn't make it (clocktower/park/etc.) unfortunately. The new expanded areas such as hospital and underground labs replaced them in a way.

Gameplay controls are tight and almost identical to R2make. Knife doesn't break anymore but you don't have a freebie anymore either. If you're attacked, you're definitely going to take the hit. The new dodge mechanic is clunky unless you're timing is just right. Keep in mind that Zombies will lunge 2-3 times at you. Also note that Carlos and Jill have different dodge mechanics. Jill = Dodge. Carlos = Tackle/Punch. Guns feel great and ammo is scarce. The impact of every bullet gives them enough justice and most Z's won't go down that easily. Character movements are solid but not as fluid as Re6. Boss fights are tedious and a chore; doesn't give room for variability. There are less complex puzzles and it focuses more on action. I'd say R2make still has better puzzles compared to this game. Inventory management returns just like in any RE/Biohazard game.

Audio is well done. Every enemy has distinct sound and noise. Every room/area has it's own vibes. It either gives peace or a sense of dread. VA for Jill was exceptional and really portrayed her stress and sense of urgency. The rest of the cast followed suit and provided good support development for Jill. However, the guns sounds are almost identical, Nemesis doesn't shout "stars" unless you're upclose and the distance audio needs some work (hearing zombies 1m away when they're 5m away). Also, hearing "door-banging" when you're 10m away, but it sounds like 1m away is hilarious.

Replayability. There is none...almost none. New Game Plus opens up a shop where you can spend your achievement points from previous playthrough to buy items that'll enhance your next experience. Items include special passives or weaponry. They need a larger selection of firearms and items to use if they plan to use this feature. Simply put, it is too boring and mundane to attempt multiple playthroughs unless you really love the series.

First things first, this is NOT a $60 dollar game, if you liked RE2 Remake then you should get this eventually when it comes down in price. Why I am giving it a postive? Well it is not as horrible as people make it out to be or have a very foggy memory of how the original from 99 suffered from most of the same shortcomings as this one. THIS IS FOR THE SINGLE PLAYER ONLY.

POSITIVES

- The characters, Jill and Carlos are really well realized and the VA is excellent, they actually feel lik e real people this time. For the longest Jill has been given the short end of the stick and its good to see Capcon gave her what she deserves personality and looks wise, it gives for the most part a good conclusion to the Racoon City Saga. The changes made to the ending of the game are particularly a high note and improvement.

-  Visuals and atmoshphere, sure graphics aint everything but they managed to improve the visuals of RE2R especially in the character facial animations. Racoon City looks as spooky as you remember plus a very surprising neon color pallet when you are walking downtown that really ups the general vibe of the game

- Sound design and music is excellent with all the classic tunes from RE3 99 but remixed with new ones, guns have a kick to them and the moans and roars are equally disturbing.

- Replay value, this might be a negative for some but despite the short length (8 hours counting cutscenes) of the only game campaign, the in game point shop adds a lot to unlcok different weapons or gadgets and make different runs with weapons, speedruns, etc. This gives a very Arcade like gameplay to the game which I really enjoy but that just might be me.

- The dodge mechanic and more abundant enemies make it a decent tonal shift compared to RE2 R, this is not survival horror this is action horror. I dont prefer one over another but considering the story and characters it makes sense and makes a nice complement to RE2R.

NEGATIVES (Its very easy to say its short but why is this? )

- Lack of real puzzles, there are hardly any in the game this shortens the backtracking and the fun of the original game, the level design makes a complete 180 and it goes from free exploration and figuring things to linear very scripted sequences.

-Cut areas of the original, while the 99 game had horrible pacing and a lot of padding, the lack of a particular area that is literally teased in front of you to then avoid it completely is really perplexing, by adding at least one more area with puzzles the flow of the game will be better.

- Pre order DLC costumes, RE2R gave you the classic and polygon costumes for free. In this you only unlock 1 more costume in game and if you pre order you get 1 more and thats it, guess we have to wait for modders to correct this.

- Nemesis, the big elephant in the room, being honest he is terribly underused and is kind of a pushover, my guess is that Capcom was afraid from all the complains they got from Mr X on the past game and while he is faster, agile, agressive and has weapons he seems more concerned on toying with you than actually killing you. People keep saying that (its scripted) but anyone who actually remembers 99 game knows that was the case also there, the problem here is that he just kinda appears in 2 sections stalking but you can take him down with ease and then forget about him completely, compared to Mr X who you could stun but he will come back eventually.

- No extra modes, no Mercenaries, no nothing. It is easy to see why, because of Project Resistance but honestly unless you are into the Arcade gameplay of this game and unlocking weapons, achievements and items, there is hardly any replay value for your not RE fan. It would even be cool if they gave mini missions with some of the Outbreak characters.

- Too many save points and auto saves, there is no ink ribbon mechanic and this just makes the game feel like a cakewalk even on hard difficulties.

Overall I am having fun with this game and I plan to 100% it and it makes a decent companion piece to Resident Evil 2 Remake but that I think is the main issue, this shouldnt be a companion, it should stand next to it. If you want a score it is a 7/10 and is just an average game but not Resident Evil Gaiden or 0 levels of bad. RE2 is better overall in production, game and level design, the price tag for RE3R is a lot to ask for whats given so my recommendation is you shouldnt miss out on it, experience it yourself but wait for a good discount, in the meantime give a whirl to RE2!

- Combat feels like it did in RE2 remake but with a lot more ammo to spend and the dodge mechanic shaking it up a bit.
- Like most RE games, it's very replayable and has some cool changes on higher difficulties to mix things up.
- It's a competent game that embraces the more action oriented side of OG RE3.
- Nemesis is terrifying, Jill looks amazing and all of the characters are well acted/mo-capped.
- The sewers section is mercifully short.

CONS:

- Some questionable and downright disappointing story choices and cut content/sections/monsters.
- The above is made more apparent by the notably short story length. My first non-rushed run was 5 hours.
- The lack of costumes and the afterthought presentation of infinite weapons and rewards via a shop is meh.
- Some parts of the game feel quite linear with some "on-rails" action moments that mirror the giant alligator part from RE2 remake.
- There's about 3 puzzles in the game which are all braindead easy and all happen in the first hour of the game.
- Apart from some nice call back tracks, the soundtrack is rather bland and forgettable.

SUMMARY:
A decent remake that doesn't stay around long enough and feels a little shallow due to cut content. In spite of this though, RE3 offers a fun story that modernizes and reimagines Jill's last escape from Raccoon City. This game will forever divide the RE community and while I fall in the camp of having enjoyed it thoroughly. Time will tell if it remains memorable in the same manner as RE2 remake.

Don't let my 15 hours in the game fool you; RE3 is short, and over half of that time was spent with the game minimized doing other things. I feel like that should be gotten out of the way first, because it emphasizes the biggest difference between REmake 3 and REmake 2. 

For context, the two games were originally meant to be released together; each of them would only have one campaign to them, and Resistance was nowhere to be found. But after REmake 2 had been finished for a long time, and was only being held back by REmake 3's development, they split the games. REmake 2 thankfully had its protagonists going on largely similar paths, making it easy to split into two campaigns to salvage it as a full length title, but REmake 3 wasn't so lucky. Before I started REmake 3 I figured them tacking on Project Resistance was for the sole sake of getting people into the multiplayer, but now it feels like the benefit was mutual there. REmake 3 just isn't as complete of a package as REmake 2 was.

It's a little bit unfair to compared it to 2, because 2 did such a good job that I consider it to be one of the highest points in the survival horror genre in a good while. And 3 is plenty of fun too, make no mistake; it just lacks a good amount of the polish. A substantial amount of content was removed, and while I don't like to judge games by their length the game's quality suffers for it. It feels like no one area of the game is ever big enough, leaving you constantly wanting more out of each location (with the exception of the obligatory sewer, which was mercifully short). That feeling only occurs because most of the new areas are pretty good, so it's somewhat of a positive as well, but they just don't do enough with them. The new enemies are similarly underused, though I didn't really lament for that; most of them are either fairly similar to RE2 enemies or just kind of annoying, like the new zombies that wear plagas-style tentacles on their heads.

I was particularly excited to see Nemesis in this, after the amazing treatment Mr. X got in 2, but if anything I found him far worse than in the original game. He rarely appears, and there are only a couple of very short parts where he actually appears during normal gameplay. This is actually a blessing in disguise, though, because those segments are miserable. Nemesis doesn't have to hear you, or even be nearby; as soon as you leave a building, he just drops from the sky to your location, no matter what. He doesn't even have to catch up to you, because he's just as capable of pulling you to him, or even just leaping 20 feet to land in front of you. Where Mr. X was a terrifying, lumbering presence that added a good feeling of tension to the game, Nemesis is just frustrating, detracting from the game's atmosphere whenever he's around in the early hours. I found myself breathing a sigh of relief when I realized these moments were short-lived, and soon he was relegated solely to boss fights for the better.

These all paint a pretty grim picture of the game, and I personally don't think it's worth paying $60 for unless you plan on playing Resistance a lot (I personally have no interest in it). But ultimately, blasting zombies and hoarding supplies is still just as much fun as before, and seeing the story presented in a different way is just as entertaining as it was in REmake 1 and 2. If the idea of "more RE2" appeals to you then you'll enjoy 3 too -- there just isn't as much to enjoy, here. REmake 3 feels more like an expansion to 2 than its own full price-worthy game, but it IS a fun expansion, even if it doesn't quite do the original game justice.

It seems a lot of the not recommended reviews are based on nostalgia for the original RE 3, which to a degree I get.
But when it comes to "why is there no spiders", spiders has always been just bullet spunges, the fly/insect zombies more or less also fulfill that "spider" role.
Blue herbs I'm a bit torn on, on the one hand it's always been a gimmick item and it really didn't help a lot but on the other it's a bit iconic for a reason.
With that said, comparing it to a better example: RE 2 Remake:

[b]The good stuff:[/b]
[olist]
[*] A lot more challenging in terms of map layout, you definately don't have the same circular routing as in RE 2
[*] Nemesis ain't no pushover compared to Mr.X
[*] A lot less starter ammo / or at least it felt that way
[*] Better knife control with Jill
[*] Some new enemies
[*] Some okay streamlining, 1 button for every action, 1 button for every attack, UI is overall better.
[*] Nice to see how RPD got wrecked or how that hole in the wall was made, also a nice touch that the codes are all the same as in RE 2.
[/olist]

[b]The bad stuff:[/b]
[olist]
[*] The intro sequence is way too long and boring, just action, action, action for 5-10min straight.
[*] The pacing is very off putting, playing as Carlos all the sudden felt very off, exploring the first area felt very weird, as soon as you gain certain key items or meet a new enemy you also were introduced to nemesis and never gave you a good enough opportunity to explore the new enemy or optional areas, nope just run, run run from nemesis.
[*] Nemesis is overused and always scripted, in other words, he doesn't roam, he just chases you time and time again, compared to Mr.X where the scripting actually made him more scary.
[*] You can essentially cheese every zombie if you find a door, since zombies can't go through most doors, this might be because of engine limitation (a lot more stuff being rendered this time around) but still really sad since one key game mechanic of RE 2 remake was zombies could now burst through doors.
[*] More mindless action instead of intense action where quick thinking counts
[*] A lot more QTEs
[*] Puzzles makes a lot less sense and there's way too few of them
[*] Way less surprise zombies or they're so blantantly obviously placed, they are invicible until some event trigger is triggered
[*] Semi bad thing: Jill Valentine feels a lot more like Lara Croft with how "unlucky" she is and how every object is out to kill her.
[*] A lot of minor bugs, Nemesis getting stuck in room before a save room, scripted monsters don't know what to do if you manage to get past them without killing them, "intense music" plays continuously if you skip killing some monster (this happens in RPD with lickers).

[/olist]

So yeah there's quite a bit more negatives than positives, it's still an enjoyable game, if you bought it for reduced price.

But it somehow feels like the RE 6 dev team or some Capcom executive who's the biggest fan of RE 6 decided to be included in the RE 2 remake dev team and make the game a lot less slow paced with intense action sequences but instead "more zombies = intense".

Doesn't help that Nemesis doesn't have any of the dread factor Mr.X had.
Nor that Jill worst enemy isn't Nemesis but the objects that keeps on trying to kill her in cutscenes, just like Lara croft, who knows maybe they are related.

[*]It feels very jaring being in RPD and picking up some of the items you literally pick up in RE 2 remake.

I should start this review off by saying, I have not played the original Resident Evil games, nor have I ever been a huge fan of the series (until now). I'd also like to preface that Resident Evil 2 Remake was one of the best single player games I have ever played, I bought it on sale not expecting too much and was absolutely blown away. With that out of the way, here is my opinion. 

This game has been quite polarizing, there are people who enjoy this game a lot and may even put it up there with RE2, then there are those who don't like this game for it's linearity and the fact that it is missing many sections and locations that were in the original RE3. I do understand people's problems with linearity, I won't lie to you, A LOT of this game is indeed scripted. I also understand why lovers of the originals would be disappointed after seeing that sections from the original game are not present in this remake. After having said that though... I absolutely loved every second of this game. The only huge gripe I have is that it's short! I wish it was much longer but sometimes it's the short and sweet games that effect me the most so It's not too much of a problem. I'm normally not a huge fan of linear games but I found myself totally okay with how this game handled a linear story line. I enjoyed the gameplay despite a rather clunky feeling dodge mechanic that often caused some frustration. Any downsides I name from this point are simply nitpicking, I'd like to be thorough and give a good picture for what I found good and bad. I was also very invested in the story and characters, I loved all of the characters in this story, most of them even more than the characters of RE2. Down below will be a list of my pros and cons along with a concluding statement on whether this game is for you just to shorten this up, I don't mean to write a freakin' novel about this.

Pros:
- Great story with amazing and likable characters
- Gorgeous graphics with many changeable options
- Smooth, mostly fluid gameplay (slightly faster and smoother than RE2)
- A few awesome new enemy types and some new weapons

Cons:
- Clunky dodge mechanic that is difficult to get the hang of
- It's a pretty short game (roughly 4 - 5 hours)
- The occasional low quality texture (few and far between)
- There isn't as much of an incentive to explore like in RE2

So is this game for you? Well that's mostly for you to figure out looking at this information. I do believe people are being a bit harsh towards this game, It has come to mostly favorable reviews but some of these negative reviews are a bit far fetched but I can understand why some may be left wanting more. Here's my take on it: If you loved Resident Evil 2 Remake and don't mind some extended linear story, I'm pretty sure you'll thoroughly enjoy this game. If you are a hardcore fan of this series and looking for a faithful remake to the original RE3, you may find yourself disappointed here. Lastly: If you're someone who is new to this series like me and wants to get into these newer entries, I'd pick up Resident Evil 2 Remake first and play through that. That game really is the definitive experience and if you enjoy it, go ahead and get this one as well because you'll like this too. Also a reminder that there are free demos for both RE2 and RE3, so go play those first and if you like them, then both of these games are just more of that, so that should help to influence your decision. Simply because of the short length of this game, if you're not in a hurry to play it, it may be best for you to wait for a sale, It's really hard for me to justify a $60 price tag here, it's borderline pushing it for me. these RE Remakes seem to get low prices fast, I got RE2 for $20 shortly after release so it shouldn't be too long. Thank you for reading! I hope this helped.

The Resident Evil 3 remake is a difficult game to recommend, especially to fans of the original and of the RE series as a whole. Those who prefer RE4, 5, and 6 over the earlier games (and RE7) might enjoy this as it is essentially a big budget Hollywood action version of the original - levels are compact & linear to a fault, you are almost constantly being pushed forward (with areas closing off behind you & inaccessible for the rest of the game, significantly lowering replay value), ammo is plentiful (though, unfortunately, weapons are not), and there are [i]a lot[/i] of cutscenes & set-pieces that cut up the campaign. This is not like the original game at all, and is therefore bound to disappoint a lot of fans. Puzzles are mind-numbingly simple and far & few between, the few levels are minuscule by comparison to the original, and the backtracking elements of the original are virtually nonexistent as you are herded through corridors with little interactivity for the bulk of this bite-sized campaign.

Does this make it bad? Not necessarily, but it's not very memorable nor replayable. The production values are top-notch - the graphical & gameplay upgrades from the RE2 remake work brilliantly here with the addition of some nice touches such as a dedicated dodge command that really suits this game's much more action-oriented take on the original. The problem is how much it omits from the original and sacrifices overall in order to execute this narrower approach. While I prefer shorter games with little to no filler over longer games with artificially padded run times, this game is not quite sweet enough to be "short & sweet." So much of it is truncated that I can't help but see a missed opportunity around every corner. Even the Nemesis itself doesn't quite present like the unstoppable nightmare killing machine it did in the original; much of the time, it feels and is treated like more of a nuisance than anything. The boss fights are comprised of its various iterations as it mutates, and those range from gruesomely creative & fun to contrived & lackluster.

The core flaw of this game is that its breakneck pacing can be quite exhilarating but, before too long, you start to feel like a sheep being herded from one set piece to the next. The notably bland storytelling and character development (which the RE2 remake did exceptionally well) makes this approach even more frustrating. I completed my first run in just under 7 hours, and 100%ing the game only took a 2 hour speed run and a dull third run in Hardcore difficulty mode. I really wanted to like this and have revisited it over the years since its release to see if it clicks with me like it did in my first playthrough, but it is too dismissive of the original's strengths and not nearly up to par with the preceding entries in the series. Where 2019's RE2 remake modernized & improved all aspects of the original game, this feels largely like a cash-in as Capcom undoubtedly knew their fan base would buy this without question and they just copy-pasted a lot from the RE2 remake without bothering to create a fuller & more fulfilling RE3 remake. They couldn't even be bothered to tack on a Mercenaries mode which - given how action-centric the gameplay is - could have been a lot of fun and added immensely to the game's replay value and staying power.

Despite these issues, the production values are truly great (the graphics exceed even the RE2 remake's and the audio & soundtrack are superb) and this can be quite a fun & tense experience the first one or two playthroughs, but given its numerous glaring flaws and frustrating brevity, I would recommend either skipping this and playing the RE2 remake instead or waiting for a deep sale and playing it like an interactive blockbuster action-horror flick.

Having been an avid RE fan for the entirety of my life, RE3 original stands as my favorite game in the series. I've played every main installment, and most spin-offs. I can safely say I like every game in the series, and RE3make is no different. While it isn't what we all expected or wanted after last years marvel of RE2R, it is no doubt still a good game. 

Pros:
- This game portrays Jill the best she has been since REmake back in 2001. She hasn't had much respect or relevance from Capcom since then, but this changes that. She is more likeable, human, and relatable than ever before.
- The same goes for Carlos, his personality is actually good now and not just a campy pervert like in the original. He also plays a larger role in the overarching story.
- The story is engaging and well paced, almost nothing feels like padding.
- What areas are included are very well fleshed out and expanded upon.
- Incredibly redesigned enemies that can definitely strike fear into the player.
- Combat is well refined from last year, with the focus more on action - giving us a lot more freedom mid-fight (i.e. the dodge mechanic).
- A beautiful game that is very well optimized to run on most hardware.
- Includes a free multiplayer game in the form of RE Resistance, which is fairly fleshed out and has a lot of effort put into it.

Cons:
- VERY short. It is no excuse that the original was short, therefore this one should be. The original had begun development as a spin-off and was converted into a mainline game. Much of the game needed to be rewritten and adapted to the new script, story, and characters. RE3make however was developed from it's beginning as so, giving that full development time to expand on what we already had, however they didn't do a good job.
- Iconic locations (such as the Clock Tower, the Dead Factory, The Park and others) were cut from the game, no doubt making the length as it is. Many locations were adapted to be connected more to RE2, rather than the game you're playing. 
- Bosses and enemies (Gravedigger, an entire Nemi stage, Spiders, Brain Suckers, etc.) were also cut from the game, and what enemies were kept are mainly contained to story segments.
- Story is more different then it is faithful, having Carlos visit the RPD being a major example. Many events are changed, (Brad doesn't die from Nemesis, Dario plays a significantly lesser role, Barry doesn't rescue Jill and more). It almost feels like a fanfiction version of the original. However, the new story isn't bad, just not faithful.
- Quite linear, feeling similar to RE4/6 in that regard.

I could go on about more cons, but I digress. It mainly just comes back around to the idea that this does not feel like RE3. But that's not the worst thing in the world. Capcom took chances and they will hopefully learn from this. It is an incredibly engaging game that is a must play for any major RE fan. Overall, a 7/10.

Great game and just as fun as the RE2 Remake, but unfortunately it feels a little short.
I had an ingame time of about ~6hrs when I finished the game and I did a lot of backtracking and exploring, so definitely didn't rush it at all.
Still, even with the short duration, it was a great experience and a game I can 100% recommend!

Positives:
-Combat feels great and interactive.  The ability to time dodges to bypass enemies/avoid Nemesis and combo into attacks is very well done and super fun.  This is an upgrade to the combat in RE2 remake, keeping the amazing gun play from that game and improving almost everything else.
-Story and characters.  Jill and Carlos are both very likable and Nemesis is amazing monster design.  All of the side characters feel real rather than just 2 dimensional.
-Enemy design.  Zombies are weaker and do less damage than in RE2 remake, but there are way more of them.  Hunters are kind of like lickers from RE2 remake (lickers are also in the game but only in a few places) but are less agile in exchange for having a sense of sight.  They are much more intimidating than hunters from previous RE games.  Pale heads are also in the main game this time which is great because it always seemed like a shame such a cool enemy only appeared in a side scenario in RE2 remake.

Neutral:
-Like everyone is saying, the game is short.  I beat it in about 6.5 hours on my first play through while taking my time.  There's a lot of replayability that makes up for this in my opinion but your mileage may vary.
-There aren't any puzzles that the series is known for.  I get they probably did it because of the shortness of the game and puzzles get repetitive on repeat play.

Negatives:
-Nemesis is extremely underutilized.  All of his appearances are scripted.  He's very fast so he's a pain in the ass when he shows up but once you get good with Jill's dodge ability it's always just a case of running until you trigger a cutscene and get away from him.  After your first play through you know exactly when he's going to show up and he's not that hard to put down.  You also get weapon upgrades and ammo for dropping him.  Maybe I bought into the hype a little too much but I've never played the original RE3 and everyone kept saying how Nemesis is so much more badass than Mr. X, and I get how lore-wise he's stronger, but RE2 remake did such a great job of making Mr. X this constant intimidating force stalking you in the police station.  All you could do is run, shooting him was a waste of bullets cause he's just getting up again.  You get loot for dropping Nemesis so you're incentivized to fight him and this makes him less intimidating, at least to me.  Running away from Mr. X through the dark, narrow hallways of RPD is much scarier than getting perfect dodges against Nemesis's punches.  I don't know if I'm making this very clear I just think they really failed implementing Nemesis.
-Bosses are bullet sponges.  I guess the bosses are all just Nemesis but still.  
-Gore has had a huge downgrade from RE2 remake.  No more blood pouring out of crippled zombie limbs or severed arms littering the hallway.  In some places zombie bodies just kind of spontaneously explode in a pile of blood and disappear.  I assume this is all to save system resources due to the larger number of enemies running around but it still sucks.
-The 'Nightmare' and 'Inferno' unlockable difficulties are pretty busted in places.  It's to the point in some places where I wonder if they even play tested on these difficulties as the last boss fight in particular on Inferno is so stupidly broken I wonder how it got released in this state.  I'm all for a challenge, but a boss fight where if you get hit once you get stun locked into a 9 hit certain death combo with no further chance to dodge is just unfair.

Really my problems just boil down to how Nemesis was implemented, the gore graphical downgrade from RE2 remake, and the higher difficulties being busted.  Other than that this game is amazing and I recommend.

My first experience with RE was a big box copy of Resident Evil with a photocopied instruction manual, so I've been a fan of the series for a long time, over 2 decades. This is the perfect blend of classic RE survival horror and 3rd person action-adventure game; it plays as fast or as slow as your mood desires. 

It is a short game. That's it. That's its downfall. Is it worth full price? Heck ya it is to me, but that's not to say it will be for everyone. If you put more that 2 hours into the demo, you'll probably get your money's worth out of R3make at full-price. If you finished the demo once and never opened it again, well, I'd say wait for a sale.

Although not as good as RE2 Remake in most aspects, RE3 still delivers a great experience for most of it's 5/6 hours of gameplay. If you enjoyed RE2 Remake then you'll enjoy this one as well. Having said that, I find it inferior to RE2 Remake for the following reasons:

. The game is almost completely linear, with it's most open zone being the first one (the one featured in the Demo) but it doesn't even come close to the RPD Station in RE2 Remake.
. As most people have pointed out, there isn't nearly as much replayablity as in RE2, once you beat the game you unlock new difficulties which only change some enemies and resources layout, paling in comparison to RE2 second run. 
. There is way more content cut from the original RE3 than there was with RE2 Remake (mainly the Clocktower section, a fan favorite) which results in this game differing more from it's source material than RE2 Remake did (it is more "reimagined"). This wouldn't be a bad thing on itself if the game had featured more new content to make up for it, but it sadly isn't the case. 

I also have a few nitpicks which end up adding up to the overall downgrade, as they were not present in RE2:

. Door animation is less fluid. If you don't press the button to open the door, Jill kinda just bumps into it for half a second until the door starts to open. It's not a big deal but it is definitely noticeable. 
. Zombies have a death animation, making it obvious when you've killed one, which takes away the tension of checking if it really is dead or not.  
. Limbs removed from zombies no longer are cut and then remain on the floor, they instead (literally) blow up. 
. There are barely any puzzles in this game, only a couple really easy ones. To be clear, they weren't great nor numerous in RE2 Remake either, but they really helped with the overall pacing of the game. I get that this is more of an action game (and it shows) but for how little they tried with the puzzles they might as well remove them completely. 
. There is a particular section in the game (which I won't spoil) when whenever you kill a zombie it will blow up, disappearing. Given there are a lot of zombies in that section it wouldn't surprise me if it was related to performance issues, but given than that is probably one of the more tedious and less enjoyable parts of the game, it could have been removed completely to avoid this honestly jarring issue. Seeing a zombie blow up out of nowhere takes you out of immersion. 

As I said, the game is still great, just not GOTY worthy like RE2 Remake was in my opinion. It feels more like a 20 to 30 dollar DLC to be honest, and it would have been awesome as just that. I have to say the new dash mechanic to avoid zombies feels great, as does the combat, which really makes me more disappointed that there isn't a Mercenary mode (although I wouldn't be surprised if Capcom released one as a DLC). And don't worry about Nemesis, he is still very much part of the game and his sections are great. RE3 improved the boss fights a lot compared to the lackluster ones in RE2. 

All in all, I would rate this game an 8/10 (bear in mind that RE2 is a 10/10 for me). Sadly I wouldn't recommend this game for any more than 30 dollars given it's amount of content, as Resistance isn't of my taste and I honestly doubt it will live more than a couple of months. Since Steam doesn't have a "wait for X price" type of review I'll leave a positive one given that the price will eventually drop, and it is an overall great game.

RE3R is an odd game I have a hard time recommending.

It's a fantastic yet flawed experience.

I haven't played the original RE3 at the time of writing this review, so I can't say how faithful it is to the original in terms of story beats, locals, and length.

This game follows hot off the heels of RE2R, and it feels like it. Don't take this the wrong way, but this game feels like what Metal Gear Survive is to Metal Gear Solid V; a game built off of another game. This isn't an inherently bad thing. If you liked RE2R, you'll likely enjoy this package. If you're looking for as much content as RE2R, you're going to be disappointed. A lot of side modes were cut in favor of RE Resistance, which is a neat gamemode in itself, but doesn't exactly make up for the price. Think of it as thirty dollars for RE3 itself, and thirty for RE Resistance. I'm not trying to justify sixty dollars for this, I think it's kind of bloated myself with how little content this game has compared to RE2R.

That being said, what is here is absolutely phenomenal. RE3R is more or less what Not A Hero did to RE7, but on top of RE2R. It takes the core gameplay and makes it faster and more action packed. And it's an absolute blast. Jill's dodging mechanic is super satisfying to master. The Nemesis boss battles are some of my favorite boss battles in recent memory, even if the final one is more spectacle than anything. The presentation is absolutely wonderful.

That being said, if you're going into this expecting a tense horror experience akin to RE2R; YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED.

RE3R has it's moments where it slows down to give you the creeps, and Nemesis running at you at a full sprint is ♥♥♥♥-your-pants worthy (like Mr. X the first couple of times), but by the end, you'll have seen everything, and the scares slow down to a minimal level, and the tension comes from what's going to happen next.

As someone who hasn't played the original RE3 and went in completely blind, it was a blast to experience all of this.

On the downside, it'll probably average you 5-7 hours for a first playthrough. I beat this within 24 hours of it releasing on Steam, twice. My first playthrough lasted me about 5 hours, and then I casually played the game again while streaming it in a discord call, and ended up beating it once again barely even trying. This game is a short, yet sweet experience.

If you absolutely need to play this game right now, then go for it, otherwise, wait for a sale. RE Resistance is probably what's bloating this game's price up, and hopefully Capcom decides to sell both separately as to reduce the price of this game.

[h1] Resident Evil 3 remake is an utter disappointment to the fans of the original, people who enjoyed Resident Evil 2 remake and as a game itself.[/h1]
With the price tag of a standard triple-A game this remake struggles where the original shines. This game feels rushed, unpolished and makes the player frustrated with extraordinary levels of story and gameplay stupidity. For me Resident Evil 3 remake became one of the most disappointing games I’ve ever waited for.

[list]
[*] [b]Nothing like the original?[/b] My first experience with the original RE3 was last year. I played the PC version, enjoyed the hell out of it no matter the “tank controls” and other retro gaming “nuisance”. Atmosphere felt right. It was a well crafted combination of survival and horror elements. And while all the original RE games had this “B movie” type of plot the game still had a good story. You felt the pursue, you felt the struggle Jill goes through, you felt that the city is in ruins, you fully understood the “last escape” and “somehow I’m still alive” parts. However, I had no nostalgia bias towards the remake and I was ready for a new take on this story. A lot of things were cut, replicated or done worse, atmosphere was almost nonexistent to me. The painful part was that I replayed the original game just few hours before I started playing new remake.

[*] [b]Unbelievably short playtime. [/b] My first playthrough of this game was on hardcore difficulty the same way I played the original. It took me 5.4 hours. I explored every corner of the game. I believe I missed only one optional shop to loot with the lockpick. I struggled with enemies due to my ammo greed, took the time to explore random posters and other details. By no means I’m an expert player, I didn’t even play the Resident Evil 2 remake.. I’ll never agree that even 6 hours of gameplay is enough for 60$. “Replayability is the key” one might say, to which I’ll answer that the my second original RE3 run took me almost 8 hours. I’ve watched a lot of guides, speedruns, strats and experienced playthroughs. And the game had WAY more replayability than the remake while giving me more playtime. I’ve played the original on the emulator for the second time allowing me to speed up things that took time. Actual game time was even bigger than 8 hours. My actual playtime of the remake was hardly 5 hours to be fair.

[*][b]Dull characters and plot.[/b] What happened to Jill? She’s not afraid. She’s more annoyed with the things that happen to her. You have this one PTSD moment in the introduction, after this she’s just your typical Mary Sue that acts like a teenager rather than an experienced military soldier in her mid 20s. She acts so cocky, while in almost every case she’s saved by a deus ex machina. In one of the chase moments she’s saved by the rocket launcher explosion and just gets launched across the street to safety. Or when Nemi constantly grabs her, but does literally NOTHING, or just throws her away without doing anything? Or when he poses showing his muscles randomly? He was a joke. I put him down 3 times in a timespan of 15 minutes with a single grenade, got supply case every time and just walked away like he’s a nobody. I took more damage from crawling zombies in this game than from the Nemesis. Secondary characters like Mikhail or Nikolai are irrelevant. Mikhail had this dramatic, but almost fulfilling death in the original. Especially if you witnessed the short scene where he defends the wagon from zombies and then has a small arguing moment with Jill about his dead comrades. You felt bad for him. In the remake? He was a nobody. He gets the explosive while he’s pierced with the Nemi’s tentacle on the fly and just uses it “saving everyone”. It was painful to watch. Nikolai was a comic relief character to me in the remake. He randomly shows up like a G-man, smiles, does the “gotcha Jill” moment and then vanishes. He appears out of nowhere majority of the time and it happens so randomly I hysterically laughed every time. He exists only to be a dull villain. “Russian do bad for money good” is such a lazy plot for the main human antagonist of the game.

[*][b]The Nemesis? More like Memesis.[/b] He’s no longer a terrifying pursuer. All of his appearances feel scripted and break immersion. He has the time to pose to the Jill, but not kill her when he can? Why he can’t break a wooden door when he breaks brick walls like it’s nothing? Why he dies from one grenade even on hardcore? Nemesis loot? You get TWO pistol mods. After that you get shotgun ammo and flame rounds. That’s it. No new craftable weapons, no unique drops like first aid box or a rifle for Jill. Nemesis is a bioweapon. He’s controlled by a parasite. He’s not a stupid anime villian. His second “dog” form makes no sense and looks generic. Both dog fights are generic too. Final form has less detail than the original and the fight is less complex.

[*][b]Linear as hell.[/b] There was some backtracking at the first part of the game with lockpick and bolt cutter, but after that the game starts to be absolutely linear it amazes me how is it even possible in a RE game. The original had decent amount of choices and different routes and their orders you could take. Nikolai dies from Nemesis? Or fights Jill on a helicopter she wanted to escape on? Or she’s able to negotiate? A lot of moments in the game give you a choice that might change your story and path. This is nonexistent in the remake. You can’t even choose if you kill Nikolai or just wound him in the end. 

[*][b]The atmosphere and level design.[/b] Remember those random screams, lonely wind blows and fire cracks while you explore the city in the original, those masterfully detailed background images? It’s insulting to me that there’s more atmosphere and detail in the original game than there’s in the remake. Stupid moments like when Nemesis chases you on the flaming construction site, but vanishes and you find a typing machine and a box before the final fight? Absolutely immersion breaking and idiotic to say the least. Replayability is laughable. On nightmare zombies are bunched up in small places and start raining from the sky. 

[*][b]Lack/cut of content.[/b] Clocktower? Gravedigger? City Hall? Graveyard? Park? Dead Factory? Spiders? Drain Deimos and Brain suckers? Dead Factory? Different story choices and routes? All of this cut or lazily redone. Suckers and Deimos are now random generic bugs that you see for 15 minutes of the game at best. Dead Factory’s cut so they can reuse RE2 Nest assets. Everything else is just cut. “But it’s a reimagine, right?” 3 Costumes for Jill and 2 for Carlos? No difficulty rewards? "You want STARS, I'll give you STARS" was cut from the final fight and now it's a random phrase Jill says on the run. Gore? Enemies can't even cut your head off like in the original. Animations and enemies are heavily reused.

[*][b]Resident Evil Resistance.[/b] Nobody asked for this game, you should’ve put the resources into Resident Evil 3 remake. The fact that you bundle this game with the RE3 remake shows you know this game is unwanted and the remake is low on content. 
[/list]
[b]To be fair, there are things that didn’t bother me or I genuinely liked in the remake though:[/b]
[list]
[*] While majority of OST was good or at least “okay”, some original remixes like “Final Metamorphosis” were really impressive. I guess “don’t redo things that work just fine” worked out this time. I liked some monster designs. Hunter’s Gamma and Beta were pretty cool. Gameplay was okay. I liked shooting and dodging stuff no matter how clunky or stupid it looked. Optimization is on point.
[/list]

All I can say in the end is that Resident Evil 3 is a disappointing product that I truly consider a slap to the fans and regular players. It’s not worth the cost and I’m insulted I preordered the game and couldn’t refund. [b]Capcom[/b], you were doing good. What happened?

[i]Next time... take the fu***ng hint.[/i]

So to preface this: I am aware of classic Resident Evil but only played the first one so I have not played original Resident Evil 3 and thus will not be comparing it to that with any sort of nostalgia goggles.

Let's begin,
Resident Evil 3 is another great remaster from Capcom but it does have flaws. The main positives are the same as Resident Evil 2, it's a shows continued success with the new Resident Evil style however it loses some of the horror aspect that Resident Evil 2 grasped very well and focuses on a little more of an action - horror compared to RE2. I agree for the price tag this game is a very short however it depends very much on perspective, the game to begin with has a goal of getting an S Rank and finishing as quickly as possible. This means naturally the secondary aspect of the game is to replay through and this was the same in RE2 which was also a short game but a lot longer than this one. For perspecitve I completed this game in 03:57:00 and achieved a B rating. The length is the primary issue for myself and many others, but if you take into account the fact this is effectively two games you can split the game price to £25 each and that's a pretty reasonable price tag in my opinion.

The first part involves jill running around the city being chased by nemesis which is a strong point of this game. I wont elaborate on other parts for it might spoil, but they cut the iconic scenes where brad dies by nemesis's hand, and in the original that gave a really strong impression how dangerous nemesis can be and that is how you introduce a boss ..but here...its chasing you, but thats it...just chasing you...and trying to kill you, the first proper boss fight is really good though.

The lack of engaging puzzles and the introduction of some scripted parts in the boss battles drags it down a bit. This game is certainly getting polarizing reviews when compared to its Resident Evil 2 remake (RE2R) counterpart. Having played the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis (RE3:N) multiple times, and as an overall Resident Evil fan, here's my two cents.

This remaster of RE3:N is great. It delivers a modern approach to the original's ideas and concepts. It certainly feels exactly how the change from the OG RE2 to RE3:N felt - more action and better combat. This remake does exactly that - utilizing a lot of the same assets from the 2019 remake, and adding a lot more ammo, more powerful guns, and the combat roll (or punch if playing as Carlos). This is similar to when RE3:N added the (finicky) dodge / shove mechanic.

The story is slightly similar to the original, while removing and adding certain areas and characters to it, which I like. I do feel like the story and characters feel a lot more fleshed out than the original. It was nice to have Tyrell from the original play a more important role in this one.

I'll admit - I was not happy about the removal of the clock tower section or Raccoon City Park and the game overall feels a bit more linear than RE3:N. There are certainly a lot less puzzles in this game which was kind of a downer. Additionally, I do not appreciate the removal of the choice system from the original. That element added additional replay value and completely changed some elements of the story as well as what obtainable items you can get. I feel like if that was added to this game it could've been a lot more interesting. RE2R didn't suffer from not having enough content as there were technically four different campaigns to it.

The game on a standard play through without trying to speed run is about 6 hours (I think my original time was around that more or less). In this day and age, that is laughable but anyone who knows Resident Evil knows these games don't tend to be lengthy. There is literally an achievement to complete the game in under 2 hours, it's not a flaw it is part of the design.

Overall though, I enjoyed my time and will continue enjoying my time with this remaster while I try to get through the harder difficulties and attempt a faster run of this game.

TLDR: This is a great game. This a great Resident Evil game. This does not live up to RE2: Remake. It has many flaws that you will have to live with but you can still have a great time. Last warning: It is a SHORT game, if you are a little short on money I would advise waiting for a sale.

[b]A word of introduction [/b]: I am going to compare this game to RE2:R. We all know that the previous game is an absolute masterpiece that will live through history. It may be unfair but I have to do it since these games are using the same formula.

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

I am starting with this as it matters the least to me. RE Engine kicks asses as it as always done so far. The game looks gorgeous, it handles memory much better than RE2:R and is more accurate when you go in the settings to tell you when you are crossing the line for your current setup. You still have this odd bug where you are not doing anything and a high resolution texture suddenly becomes extremely low resolution for no reason without having your computer heavily loaded. Every engine has flaws and RE Engine is state-of-the-art of game engines.

The level of gore has been reduced. This is possibly to increase the number of enemies on screen but I have my doubts about this. In the end killing zombies is not as satisfying as in RE2:R.

Last complaint: I understand and support the change of models for characters. Claire has been changed every now and then and I believe that she was at her best looking in RE2:R. Capcom has been using Julia Voth's model for 19 years since the gamecube release. It has been too long to change it now. This new Jill does look good as a character, but I think for many people she will never really be Jill Valentine and she feels off.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

I thought that RE2:R gameplay was perfect. It felt active but because the characters couldn't move or do agile moves, I felt oppressed most of the time. Here you get a way more aggressive and active gameplay. I understand that as Jill is a member of S.T.A.R.S. and Carlos is a trained U.B.C.S. operative. These characters should feel stronger than Leon and Claire. It still comes at the cost of oppression.

The dodge feature in the original game has always been clunky and gimmicky. Here it definitely gets better and improved. It is difficult to master at first. I am a massive fan of Dark Souls so I should enjoy dodging but I don't really in this game. It feels off in some ways. Was this a necessary feature? I don't think it was. It could have been a good change to remove it and I feel like it is a missed opportunity.
Because of it, they had to remove the defensive weapons such as the grenades and the knifes.

When you play Carlos, you feel like RE2:R, you never know what is going to be behind the next corner. This was great but Carlos is stronger than Jill physically and has his super-punch that reduces the tension you have from playing him. Jill's path is the other way around. Everything is Nemesis. The next corner is a few enemies and Nemesis. If it's not then it will be a boss fight... which is Nemesis. Enemies will be killed by Nemesis anyway and he is a push-over so just bag 'em and tag 'em.

[h1] Story [/h1]

I am not deep into the lore of RE3: Nemesis so I will not be picky as I may should be.

[spoiler]Carlos has been almost entirely rewrote and that was a relief to me. He was a ridiculous character in the original game and felt like he was an unwelcome comic relief. Here he feels like a sweet guy that is indeed kind of a goof sometimes but still has his own way and reasons and he is pretty much the Lionheart of the game.
Jill feels pretty shallow to me. Claire in RE2:R is by far the best female protagonist I've ever seen in a game. Second is Amicia in Plague Tale: Innocence. Jill is introduced as really in shock from what happened in Arklay. She has a dozen pills on her nightstand, she is having horrible nightmares and to me clearly has a strong PTSD. This is never used in the game. She suddenly becomes pretty generic. A few jokes here and there, the mandatory anti-Umbrella positioning at first that she pretty much turns into anti-Nicholai positioning. Claire felt like having a deeper and more evolved character progression. She starts as a fairly innocent, caring and soft but trained college student. At the beginning she is often afraid of a lot of things, she is confused what to do. At the end she has become so much stronger. She won't take G's ♥♥♥♥ anymore. She has become a genuinely strong female character and she is badass.[/spoiler]

Aside from these spoilers, a lot of content has been cut. This is most likely to be able to develop Resident Evil: Resistance. I am not sure anyone ever asked for this and I seriously doubt the RE community is so keen on Versus Multiplayer games. I think this is an experiment that comes at the heavy cost of the story.

[h1] Nemesis [/h1]

He actually deserves his own section. In RE2:R Mr. X was stalking you at certain moments of the game. He was slow but relentless. You could put him down but it did not last long and you got nothing out of it. He did not have the best AI overall but he was doing a great job in a first playthrough. Once you understood how he works he was almost non-existent.
Nemesis feels like a downgraded versions of Mr. X. He acts way more aggressively. He never stops attacking. That's one of his problems. You always know what he is about, attacking. When he is not is because he is recovering from one of his attack. That makes him extremely predictable.
He is a glass-canon. He deals a LOAD of damage with his punches but you can bring him down with a single grenade. Whatever people seem to believe, he will NOT get up until the next scripted time he is supposed to be here as long as you leave the current "room" he is in. You can try it. If you stay in front of him he will recover eventually but after a much longer time than Mr. X.
He is dumb as a rock.  He can't even open doors except when he is specifically scripted to. You can just enter a building and watch him stay in front of the building angrily waiting for you doing nothing.
[spoilers]Once he gets his rocket launcher he becomes even more of a joke. You don't even need to dodge because he misses on his own most of the time and just side stepping will make you avoid rockets.[/spoilers]

Funniest part is that: Every encounter you have with him, the first time you bring him down he will drop you a weapon upgrade. This means that he is already weak, and beating him is making him even weaker.

[h1] Pros in general [/h1]

- Item picking has been greatly improved. You only have the zoomed item window and inventory opening the first time you pick an item. This is a formidable improvement as it was being such a pain in subsequent runs of RE2:R.
- RE Engine is a wonder of engineering.
- Character writing is greatly improved.
- Gameplay is still good even with the steps back.

[h1] Cons in general [/h1]

- A lot of content has been cut off with a bitter feeling that this is to develop a side game nobody asked for.
- Nemesis overall.
- Boss fights in general who are easier than most special enemies. When they are not they are just a frustrating puzzle that can end up in you being one shot if you don't figure it out.
- The introduction cinematic in Live Action was unnecessary and unwanted. Why making it that way? It was perfectly fine to do it the RE2:R way there was no need to be reminiscent of either the original Resident Evil or the movies. Please don't do that again.
- The game is short even for a Resident Evil game.
- No mercenaries mode.
- Questionable replayability. It doubt you would sink more than 50 hours in this to get everything in every mode while you would sink more than 60-70 hours in RE2:R.
- Some frustrating parts that were unnecessary, especially around the end of the game.
- You can feel Capcom itching to go back to Resident Evil 6 full-action formula and that is scary.

This is one of those situations where I'd ideally want to provide a neutral review, but my gut tells me to review negatively because it ultimately failed to live up to the original or to RE2's remake.

The main thing that disappoints me about this is Nemesis. When you begin the game he largely functions like Mr. X/Tyrant from RE2's remake, chasing you around the area. This is when he is most effective as your antagonist. However then you fight his first boss fight and he stops being anything other than series of setpiece chase sequences and boss battles. You stop getting the impression of being hunted as with Mr. X. and it removes all tension he could have given. Imagine if you met Mr X. and he promptly stopped chasing you after you escaped him the first time you see him in the mansion, and only then showed up for some boss fights. That's what this game essentially does to Nemesis. His boss fights are not bad, but they aren't a replacement for the tension of actually being chased by an unstoppable enemy.

Beyond that the game is just too short. I took time to liberally collect everything in this game and it was still about half as big as RE2. I also got the distinct impression it was easier and less threatening. I always had plentiful ammo for powerful weapons. It is now much easier to dodge attacks if your timing is good, and it felt much easier to control a crowd of zombies with explosives or Carlos' assault rifle.

Its bones are still solid, and I'd still probably recommend it if you are thirsty for more in the style of RE2's remake, but for most people not already invested I would say wait for a sale as the asking price here is too high for too little.

This is a massive maybe for me, but overall if i wrote a long detailed review the end summary is just. "Ehhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh?"...."Ehhhh? Maaaaaaybe? It's okay?" Simply because of the strange structure of the game itself. I am writing this review as a game not a remake.

Simply put, the game is really great for about the first 40% of it. Then after a certain stage it just becomes extremely dull. New enemy types stop being added except for 1? I think. The difficulty is simply increased by placing excessive amounts of zombies, ramping up their health dramatically and trapping you in tiny rooms with said amount of zombies. The nemesis is really thrilling as he's significantly more relentless than Mr X, until he just turns into an extremely generic monster that roars a lot for the rest of the game, which really takes away any tension he can build up.

I'm not sure what happened to the story, as it seems most of it got removed from the original to the point where character motivations make absolutely no sense. Just generally bad writing that left me in fits of laughter in the final scene of the game instead of taking the situation seriously. 

There can also be many situations in which the game just outright feels unfair. You'll often dodge but it feels extremely random if it works or not, even with plenty of practice. Sometimes you'll dodge only to watch that zombie still lunging as it magically slides across the floor without moving its feet another meter and grabs you. Others can simply result in pure stun locks. One boss for me opened with an unavoidable stunning attack. It rushed me before the stun wore off, hit me to which i was stuck as i was unable to move out of the spawning point. It then knocked me down, hit me as soon as my character stood up, then did this again to kill me. Losing the boss fight before i had at any point been given control of my actual character.

Overall, it's not a bad game. It's perfectly... fineeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee.... with some frustrating bits but most people were expecting better than just fine. Especially when 2 knocked it out of the park. I feel they should have focused on the first half of the game so much more than the second. Either way, pick it up while it's on sale. Firstly i'm going to talk about the many, many positives about this game, because there are way more import positives than there are negatives. [B]SPOILERS AHEAD[/B]

[B]Positives[/B]

- Fantastic responsive gameplay, just like RE2 Remake, it's a pleasure to play.
- Fantastic well optimised graphics, similar or slightly improved on over RE2 Remake.
- Character redesigns are spot on, both Jill and Carlos look and sound great, they both have 
   great chemistry and Carlos is funny too.
- Supporting characters Brad, Nicholai, Mikhail, Tyrell are all really well done.
- Enemy designs are all fantastic, same zombies from RE2 Remake, Hunters & Hunter Gammas look great, Nemesis also spot on
- Great Nemesis boss fights
- WAY better music than RE2 Remake, it's not even a contest.
- Ties into RE2 Remake really well, with many questions being answered about certain events that took place.
- Added sewers and expanded hospital section, much more to do and explore in the latter than the original
- Extra difficulties available for more replayability

[B]Negatives[/B]

- Nemesis is easy to down with just one grenade.
- Some cut areas from the original, like the clock tower.
- SLIGHTLY too short, and i do mean slightly, (took me about 8 hours including cutscenes on first playthrough) would have been nice for it to be longer but it's not much shorter than RE2 Remake and to my knowledge it's the same, if not longer than RE3 original.
- Pretty much no new weapons, some extra grenade Launcher ammo and an assault rifle for Carlos but that's it.
- At least one sequence with similarities to the 'survive the wave of enemies' game modes seen in other games, where you will defend a door from waves of enemies, felt cheap and tacky.
- Slightly less gore, you can still shoot zombies arms and legs off but they disappear instead of laying on the ground, overall it's still very gory.

[B]Miscellaneous[/B]

- Dodge mechanic replaces the defensive weapon mechanic from RE2 Remake, feels satisfying when you pull it off and the knife is no longer OP, not a positive or negative, just different.
- Nemesis appears at scripted times and will stop following you when you get to the next cut scene or objective, to me this isn't really a negative as i believe he behaved this way in the original, he certainly wasn't following you the whole game, some people like the compare him to Mr. X, but although Mr. X never leaves you alone that's only for a small duration during the end of the RPD section of the game, he's also less threatening than Nemesis.

Overall i can see why some people wouldn't be thrilled with the length and the cut content, and sure the game would be a much better received with those things fixed but it doesn't take a way from the fact that it's still a joy to play and because of that i want to replay it more and more, on all the difficulties, trying to get all the ranks. The problem is people will compare this to the original and to RE2 Remake, i think if this came out before RE2 Remake it would be better received because the things they've already done in RE2 Remake would feel fresher and more praise worthy, but people shouldn't lose sight of the fact that this is still a very impressive game, so it's a little shorter and there's no clock tower, it doesn't make or break it for me.

[B]9/10 - If you like Survival Horror games or the RE franchise, don't hesitate to purchase.[/B]

Resident Evil 3 Remake sucks, according to popular opinion. Wherever I look, I see hate related to this game. But also sucks, when you like, what everybody hates. I really like RE3, more than I like RE2, and points that haters make as downsides, I see as upsides.

So I want to say something good about the game and here is what I like:

1.Action. Resident Evil series feels better as an action with zombies and monsters. Stop thinking about it as a horror, those days are long gone. It doesn't work anymore. And RE3 has a lot of action, mostly thanks to two things.

1.1. Nemesis. Of course RE3 is always associated with him. Nemesis constantly hunts you, like Mr.X in RE2, but not as a comedian who stomps somewhere and can never catch you. Nemesis is an actual threat. Huge threat. Some players don't like that he is scripted, well, imagine if he was not scripted and always outside your safe room, waiting with a tentacle in hand.

1.2. Dodge. When I was playing RE2 I felt like something is missing in game mechanics, if zombie is too close you will be attacked and not much you can do about it. Now in RE3 you can avoid that, because you're not a rookie, maybe. Most of the time avoiding attacks requires to perform a perfect dodge with a possible counterattack as a bonus. Not a quicktime event [spoiler](stupid RE4)[/spoiler] a manual dodge. And everybody should like perfect dodge, right? Sekiro was game of 2019 after all.

2. Inventory management. Players love it. I love it. I love that in RE3 management is easy and minimal. Don't need to manage ink, knives and puzzle pieces in 8 slot inventory, where you should also keep weapons, ammo and healings, because...

2.1. Ink is no longer required.

2.2. You have only one knife and it doesn't break. Though you can't use it to free yourself (combined with dodge it would be too op), if you're grabbed, you can only minimise the damage you'll take. But you can still do a lot with the knife.

2.3. Game has only a couple of puzzles and thank God for that. Less boredom. I don't need puzzles in an action game, thank you. They're silly in RE games anyway. I'm running away from Nemesis, don't have time for it.

2.4. You get inventory upgrades very fast, I couldn't believe that I got one almost at the beginning.

3. Backtracking. Game is too short [strike]if you rush it on low difficulty[/strike]. Not worth the money. Shorter than RE2. I hear it everywhere. But if you look at the results menu: S rank requires you to finish it in 2:30, just like it was in RE2. Why does it feel shorter? 

Because half of the locations in RE2 had unimportant side stuff and puzzles. Get one piece of a puzzle here, find another piece there, bring both to the third place, trade them for another item that you will use to get a gun, which will go straight to the item box because you don't have a space for it. I like RE2, it's a good game, but it felt so boring at times when I had to go through the empty map. There are less locations in RE3 and only a few rooms that you can skip, or not skip and find a weapon sitting on a table next to the item box. Just like in RE2, game wants you to go back and forth to do the story. But because locations are small it doesn't take long. Conditions changes every time when you progress in the story, you will get more enemies, different enemies, Nemesis etc.

The original Resident Evil 3 was an amazing experience and played during the formative years of my life, so it left quite the impression at the time. Therefore, naturally, I would be wearing my nostalgia googles whenever I think about it and had preconceptions about how the remake, or rather, this re-imagining should be.

So, let me say it now; this is a good game! RE3 Remake (which actually drops the 'remake' in the title, as it is more a re-telling than a remake) is a highly enjoyable experience, that offers a fast-paced storyline, very cool locations and with some white-knuckle action scenes to boot.

Getting to the 3 biggest questions and gripes you will see flying around: 

-Is it different from original RE3? Yes
-Did they remove some locations from it? Yes
-Is this game short? Yes

It is clear this is a re-imagining of the original; and that is the whole point. If you want the original experience; play the original! This game stands on it's own and has superior story-telling and voice acting (play the original today and just see how cringe it is, in classic RE fashion) The characters are far more fleshed out; this is the best representation of Jill yet, who displays some more complex emotional issues, such as PTSD from the Mansion incident. There are some complaints about missing areas, but they do not mention that there are brand new, never before seen areas! I think some fans are bashing this game because it has deviated more than the RE2 Remake, which I think is no issue at all, as I can just pop in the original any time I want to replay that experience (which, believe it, or not, has not aged well with it's tank controls and stiff storyline)

Make no mistake, the is a full blown, big budget Capcom AAA game: the visuals are amazing, along with the environment detail, character models and voice acting (which I even preferred to RE2 Remake). All the visual/gameplay hallmarks from RE2 Remake are here; along with the tight control system, which also includes the new 'Dodge' mechanic, that makes boss fights more engaging from a player perspective. Although, perhaps if you master the dodge ability, may make some encounters easier, but this is not as easy as you would think, as the timing is pretty strict.

The other main issue is length, at around 6-7 hours on a first run; the game is not long by any standard, but was the original? No! This is around the same length and is a highly focused and tightly engineered experience, that certainly rewards multiple playthroughs. The Nightmare/Inferno mode completely remixes enemy locations and items; providing a far tougher and truer survival horror atmosphere! All Resident Evil games are not known for being long; in fact, they are speedrunner preferred due to this (hence why you get the best rankings for the fastest finish) and I believe this game will become a certain RE speedrunner favourite, due to it's design mechanics.

Now, this game has it's negatives; 'Mercenaries' mode is sorely missed and would have been a fantastic addition for a quick-fire challenge option. I do hope this is added in by Capcom at the soonest. Also, the Nemesis has lost the random factor appearance mechanic from the original and always has scripted appearances now. This may actually appeal more to speedrunners, but it does remove some of the tension and unpredictability that the Nemesis brought to the series. However, the actually boss fights with him are amazing and some of the most exciting in the franchise to date!

The bottom-line; is this game worth full price? If you are an RE fan and will play through this game multiple times to see everything (which is rewarded) then yes, it is.  If you just wanted a solid action/horror adventure for a one-shot experience, then no, it is not the right pick for you and I suggest to wait for the sale.
