Resident Evil 3 did a lot right and did some things wrong. Before I get into it I will say this: I like the game a lot. I liked RE2 remake a lot as well. And playing both these games has made me feel Capcom has a lot of care for its fans, and has a new found respect for the origins of its beloved franchise. So lets get into it.

The good things. The game is silky smooth. A level of optimization that is just unbelievable at times. I wish I had some better parts in  my PC to see how far this game can go. How good it can look and how well it can run. But even on the standard settings I'm seeing graphics so good sometimes its borderline ridiculous. 

The writing is a lot better (same as RE2) than previous titles. In situations where you might say "holy ♥♥♥♥!" the character will probably say holy ♥♥♥♥. And for me it adds a level of charm that a lot of horror games are lacking. These games are very dependent on having some connection to who you are playing as (or at least dependent on not hating their guts for me anyways) and its good to sigh with relief. They got Jill right. Probably my favorite character they've ever produced and she kicks ass, dresses in somewhat appropriate attire this time around, and has the attitude of someone who was a special forces operative. Not to mention getting a little slice of her life in her apartment. It really gives a lot of weight to the character, and I am happy to say RE3 remake Jill is now my favorite RE character of all time.

Gunplay I liked a hell of a lot. For a game that was ALWAYS known as the action/fast paced entry in the trilogy 90's titles, it was important we were doing a lot of shooting, and that the shooting was intense and fun. And it is. All the weapons are good. The shotgun is an absolute destroyer. Grenades are extremely powerful even in boss fights. The Magnum is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "take your soul away" piece. Carlos' rifle is now not only useful, but can make high threat enemies melt with pure mag capacity. One small negative here and maybe its just me, the acid rounds for the grenade launcher pack no punch. I don't even use them which is crazy considering the original RE3... But the flame rounds, explosive rounds, and mine rounds, are all extremely useful and plentiful enough that the grenade launcher sees a lot of use. Which is amazing because who doesn't want to see Jill melting her foes in flaming death.

Environments. Great. Thoughtfully constructed, brutally realized, and beautifully detailed. It is Raccoon City outbreak mode in all of its glory. That's really all I can say. They are good. lol

Enemies are obviously important in a horror game. They pretty much nailed zombies in RE2 and they are back. Streets can sometimes  be packed with the lumbering dead. This is most on display in Nightmare and Inferno mode. Nemesis played like Mr. X if Mr. X got mad people kept shooting his hat off and making fun of him for an entire year then decided that he will not take this sitting down anymore. He sprints, he punches/kicks, curbstomps, jumps and slams, tentacle whip grabs. He was brutal and I had to be really on top of my game  whenever dealing with him. Especially on Inferno mode. Also lickers and hunters in the game! AMAZING

Lets talk about why I can't say this is a 10/10 game. I just can't look at anyone and say there is 60 dollars worth of content here. The replayability is definitely high, but outside of superfans like me and speed runners it's hard to imagine an average player beating the campaign 10 times. There is a store to buy items using points you get from completing challenges in game. You get these items and then can use them for your next play through. But overall, even with Resistance, its hard to say its worth it. Its worth is for ME! But I just don't think others would feel the same way. 

Where are the costumes? Seriously. I understand the preorder costumes, but where are the rest. ONE single costume for Jill? How about some crazy shop reward for beating Inferno? There aren't enough post game rewards and the game definitely needed them. All this just serves to hurt the replay. 

This game is sorely in need of a mercenaries mode. And I have a feeling we will get it and it should help with some of these issues, but if they really want to do that it better be 2 things.

1. FREE
2. Fun

To summarize, I love the game. The Setting, Graphics, Characters, Combat, and Enemies are all master class in my opinion. But the replayability will only go so far, and the obvious lack of real rewards for challenges hurts it a lot. Overall I'm happy I bought the game, and would recommend it to not only fans of the franchise, but also newcomers who think the like what they see.

[h1]RE3 Remake: Abit Dissapointing, But Still Great[/h1]
The remake of the 1999 classic Resident Evil 3: Nemesis is a good game, but its not as good as last years RE2 remake and it also might not even be that good of a remake. It has a decent replay value, but not really sure if it's worth the 60$ price tag. Highly recommended to get the game on sale.

[u]Pros[/u]
+ Jill is finally back in a mainline RE game. She hawt, prettier, stronger and thiccer than ever.
+ The mix of action and horror. Some may not like it, but i really enjoyed the addition of more action elements like Jill's dodge move and Carlos' punch.
+ Nemesis in the first half. He's much more threatening in the first half compared to the 2nd half
+ The graphics and performance. I didn't even download the latest drivers as i forgot, but it not only looked great, the performance was smooth as butter.
+ Decent replay value with the added bonuses of a 'shop' once you complete the game once, and harder difficulties if you completed the game on hardcore.

[u]Cons[/u]
- Hardcore difficulty is way easier compared to Last year's RE2 Remake, as there are no ink ribbons and it also enables auto-save. WTF? I thought Hardcore was meant to be a mode for veterans of the series, not a basic hard version of the standard mode. This choice really didn't make much sense if you ask me.
- Nemesis in the 2nd half. His role becomes much more scripted in the 2nd half and more of a boss encounter which is dissapointing since if you compare it to Mr. X from last year, he stalks you till the end of the game, even though some of the moments are still scripted.
- Very short length and no different scenarios (and choices like in the original RE3) or endings. This is really dissapointing as it really downgrades the replay value of the game. Like i said, the replay value overall is decent because of the certain new things you'll be able to get once you've complete the first run. But once that's done, that's really it.
- Cut Content. The amount of cut content here really sucks. There are several parts of the campaign that are missing, and the fan favourite mode 'Mercenaries' is completely absent from the game, replaced with the Resistance multiplayer mode... that nobody asked.

[b]7/10[/b]

[H1]RESIDENT EVIL 3[/H1]
[I]Barebones content[/i]

[h1]DISCLAIMER[/h1]

This game is short and lacks everything that made the original RE3 good. [i]Resident Evil 2 (RE2)[/i] was amazing and I could easily sit and replay that 4 times back to back (Which I did), but I [b]can't[/b] stomach another play of this game, not yet anyway.

This game also saved and imported my settings from RE2 which was nice - not the graphical settings but the controls.

If you are a veteran to this series (played since PSX) then go against my recommendation here.

[h1]Specs[/h1]

Lets begin a review like we always do - Specs.

    [tr]

I ran this game on a mix of medium and high due to streaming. That being said I can easily run this game on the highest settings with no issues and I can attain a solid 60+ FPS. This game does run as good as RE2 and looks just as good.

[h1]STORY[/h1]

[i]Resident Evil 3[/i] takes place 2 months after the incident in [i]Resident Evil 1 (RE1)[/i]. It is now September. You are [i]S.T.A.R.S[/i] (Special Tactics and Rescue Service) operative Jill Valentine. After the incident in the Arklay Mountains (RE1), Jill has been suspended and is being watched by [i]Umbrella Corp[/i] or [i]Raccoon City Police Department[/i]. She is unsure but she continues to investigate [i]Umbrella[/i] as she knows they caused the outbreak that is ravaging the city.

As Jill picks up the phone in her apartment she is immediately attacked by the new Bio-weapon unleashed by [i]Umbrella[/i], the "Nemesis-T Type" (Nemesis for short). After a short chase through the burning apartment, Jill makes her way to the street and meets with an old friend from S.T.A.R.S. He gets a bite taken out of him and leaves himself to perish allowing Jill to escape where she meets Carlos.

Carlos introduces Jill to the rest of his team, the [i]Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service[/i] (U.B.C.S). Carlos (and the rest of his team) have no idea that the company they work for caused this. They only care about getting the civilians out of the city. As such Jill goes to turn on the power for the trains. What follows next is a gruelling run through the city being chased by the Nemesis.

You will make pit stops in the sewers, Raccoon City Police Department, The hospital and the Umbrella Lab beneath the city. Pretty formulaic stuff to be honest.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]

The gameplay of RE3 is good, it's not RE2 good though. You have your usual suspects of puzzle solving and inventory expanding but you lose the quick escape mechanic. I can safely say I failed every quick time event that would have negated all damage.

Having played through the game in such a short time (Play time 4 hours, 55 minuets and 1 second - Clear time 3 Hours 39 minuets and 1 second) I can conclude that: This is Diet Resident Evil 3. Many iconic parts of the game are missing, including the clock tower section. This in turn cuts the game time down and with the inclusion of the third person perspective makes the game significantly easier. 

Fifteen deaths is a fair amount [b]BUT[/b] the Nemesis is an unrelenting force of nature. If you manage to down this beast you will often get yourself a nice little supply case. This can have anything from ammo to a gun mod. You can only do this a few times and he is a bullet sponge but what do you expect for something that size? The biggest issue with the Nemesis though is that he just isn't that scary. The old PSX FMV is scarier than anything in this game has thrown at us.

Like previous entries in the series (Excluding 7) RE3 is more action focused than puzzle and survival focused. Though the puzzles and constant backtracking was a way to bring length to a game using the very limited 700mb on a PSX disc, puzzles define the earlier entries in this series. The puzzles in RE3 are laughable and simplistic. There are no head scratching moments, everything is spoon fed to the player. Last years RE2 was harder.

[h1]PERFORMANCE[/h1]

Just like last years RE2 - this game ran perfectly smooth. I did play a bit on the highest settings before I came to the realisation "Hold on I'm streaming" and lowered it down significantly. The game still looked damn good though. I saw no hangs, freezes or stutters. This game also has 2 API options - Direct X11 and Direct X12 - no Vulkan API here guys. 

There really isn't much to say here in all honesty - unlike in Resident Evil 2 where we had many different areas with lots of different things going on, this time round its very linier. You can go only 1 way and that 1 way is around the hub areas of the game. Not much happens in these areas that isn't constant, be it fire or water running, the area you're in has its own little thing happening, but it can't be stopped or changed.

[h1]OVERALL[/h1]

I have been struggling to write this review. I was honestly tempted to just post a score with the words "Buy it and see why" - but I wouldn't be doing you all justice there. Now this is where things get fun:

Steam is Binary and if you are new to the series then go by the recommendation of YES but if you are like me - who grew up on [i]Resident Evil[/i] then avoid this like the plague and keep your memory intact.

Which is bad against enemies that have instant kills, and they become frequent near the end of the game - which leads to my next point.

The original RE3 was already a very short game, this can't be denied.  However, the problem could've been helped in the remake if they hadn't cut so many areas.  The clocktower was one of the most memorable segments from the original - yet in this game, it gets a passing glance and nothing more.   Also, the horde battle wasn't necessary and felt out of place.

The pacing is inconsistent as well.  At times I felt things were going too crazy too fast, other times I just wanted ♥♥♥♥ to get over with, especially towards the end of the game.

I am making this review after completing the game in one setting, clocking about 6 and a half hours (first run was hardcore mode kinda got my ♥♥♥♥ kicked in here and there).

 RE3make is the retelling of our beloved Resident Evil 3 (1999). As you may of heard this time around the game didn't faithfully follow the original much like last year's RE2make, but that's not to say what we were given was a mediocre release. RE3make still takes the RC incident and changes it up a little. We do visit iconic locations, but unfortunately some areas seemed to have been cutout of the final release. Whether this was a rushed effort by Capcom or an intentional change in the story's direction I personally don't think this really hindered the game. On average, the first timer will take about 5 hours to complete the game, which is unfortunate, because this makes the game feel like an overpriced DLC. I feel it was as if Capcom wanted the RE Team to focus on the multiplayer addition, taking away from the main campaign's development.

Story: RE3make retells the story of Raccoon P.D STARS member, Jill Valentine, and her escape from the fall of Raccoon city along side Carlos. As mentioned before the game does a great job at giving us a modern depiction of the original, but with a few changes here and there as well as some references/foreshadowing to the events that transpire in RE2make.

Gameplay: If you were a fan of the horror, tight spaced, paranoia of RE2make then you will mostly like this game. RE3make reflects the original with it's horror and a pinch of action. This is apparent with the addition of the evasion mechanics, allowing you to time a dodge in order to evade a zombie's grapple. Evading at just the right time will allow you to tap into a bit of a slow motion state, to land some well deserved head shots on your foes. Aside from that RE3make follows the same crafting system from the prior games as well as keeping the same gun play from RE2make. 

Setting/Graphics: This game is quiet beautiful... if beautiful meant a city in absolute chaos and there was a virus turning people into zombies and mutating other forms of life.. It looks great! Also Jill is hot! (and Carlos is pretty too :D) I did run into some graphical glitches, at one point Carlos even had purple highlights, I thought it was a design choice I didn't notice at first, but then is disappeared. Anyways I found it more funny than bad.

Horror: This game does have some pretty good scares and some tense moments, also Nemesis is TERRIFYING. His chases are more prevalent at the beginning of the game and he kinda just appears as bosses after you get past the halfway mark of the game, pretty much appearing as much as Mr. X kinda did in RE2make. 

Enemies: Once again our lovely bois return! We have Zombies! Fish ♥♥♥♥♥! Spiders! Hunters! These annoying little ♥♥♥♥♥ that Nemesis puts on zombies (they're like the parasites from RE4 if their range was stupid), and even the pale heads from the RE2make dlc! That's right! regenerating zomb- ♥♥♥♥...

Overall Cons: Sadly this game does not have really any puzzles aside maybe a couple and they're really easy.
Hardcore mode really wasn't all that hardcore (there are the unlockable Nightmare and Inferno modes, we'll have to see about that). Nemesis is a little more scripted than free roaming up your ass all game (I personally like the adrenaline pumping game play of being chased by this guy). Hardcore mode has no ink ribbons, letting you save without worry. Game's short, feeling more like a 60 dollar DLC. Some areas got cut from the game, whether to laziness or too much focus on implementing a multiplayer mode.

Overall Pros: Great game, good gun play, great horror elements (with a sprinkle of action), Nemesis is scary, Jill is hot, Acting is great, Carlos is cool, very pretty visuals, mostly faithful to the original story,  controls very well, tons of unlockables to promote game replayability.

RESULTS: This game obviously has it's flaws and disappointments, but I can say from what was delivered, we are probably looking at an 8/10. But from a personal standpoint I'd give it a 9/10 because I do like what the game has offered despite the small let downs. I suggest if you don't want to pay 60 dollars for a 5 hour game, then wait for a sale, but if you are a RE fan like I am, then do get this game. Maybe it's not as good as RE2make and hopefully whatever happened with RE3make's development, Capcom will learn and hopefully allow longer development time for the next addition to the series.

This is what happens when you split the budget to make an online mode that no one really asked for.

So what's wrong with it?

On the surface it's an upgrade to RE2. The Perfect Dodge is a fun additional mechanic that rewards skillful play and in some areas even allows you to just dodge an entire mob of zombies and allows you to save ammo. It's also a necessary mechanic as bosses are much more agressive as a result of you having this extra mobility option.

But besides that, you can see it was rushed. It's in the details, and in some other major ways.

 In RE2 Leon would walk into a dark room and pull out his flashlight from his utility belt and hold it up, when he was aiming it would adjust in his animation accordingly. Same with Claire. Jill and Carlos will just have a flashlight beam pop out of. . . somewhere.

In RE2 Leon starts just like Jill in his casual clothes, but later on switches into his police uniform and that's how you play him for most of the game. Jill starts with her casual clothes, finds the gun of a dead cop in an alleyway, and magically has her gear on.

Again though, these are just tiny details, so what about the major faults?

Well, starting out, 2/3rds of the content from the original RE3 are just gone. Nemesis barely shows up, and there's only really 2 rewards you get from "killing" him. They are both upgrades to your handgun and are locked to -when- you defeat him. They really advertised Nemesis as being a super agressive harder to run from Mr. X, and yes, he is, but Mr. X was in the game for more than 5 minutes. Even in a speedrun you'd have to deal with him chasing you around the police station for at least 20 to 30 minutes. In a -normal- run, he is there for 5 minutes where he actually has free reign to move over the very small map.

After that it's a scripted chase and a boss, and he never shows up to act like Mr.X would in RE2 ever again.

It is incredibly short, doesn't have other playthroughs like RE2 did (you can just repeat the game in harder difficulties or to do challenge runs with unlocked super items), and included is the online mode which is OK at best and clearly is what completely ruined the end product. I would rather have had another 2 hours of content in the single player than having gotten Resistance for free. The single player survival horror experience is why I play Resident Evil, not a co-op multiplayer that isn't even at all similar to Resident Evil: Survivor, where people died from getting bit instantly.

Is it fun? Yes. Is it worth full price? No.

Wait for a sale.

The early game is cut. You end up in the subway train (this game's take on the original's cable car) in a matter of minutes.

Most of the game is on rails: very little real exploration, and no choices that affect the plot or the ending. Two areas have some non-linear aspect; the streets we saw in the demo, and the hospital. Entire locations, such as the gas station and the bar, feature only in cutscenes.

Carlos is introduced with a rocket. Nemesis is introduced with an exploding helicopter. Nikolai is introduced with a headshot. There's no build-up to these characters or their capacities, just boom - they're there.

Brad dies to a zombie bite. That iconic tentacle impalement that doubles as Nemmy's intro outside RPD no longer exists. While you can understand and respect most of the plot changes with RE2 remake, most of the changes in RE3 remake are plain stupid, or symptomatic of a rush-job. By the way, there are two whole puzzles in this game, neither of them challenging.

St. Michael's clock tower (a good chunk of the original) overlooks a boss arena. That's all you see of it. Strangely, you find a leaflet about it shortly before that boss fight...it seems the whole place was cut for lack of development time. Despite showing up on a billboard, Raccoon Park is likewise gone, along with its giant worm.

Dead Factory has been replaced by NEST 2, a lab underneath Raccoon Hospital. Here they make cures and showcase one last burst of asset reuse. Even NEST's glass elevator reappears! But yeah...this anticlimactic dungeon is mostly one last linear corridor. The final two boss fights have only a corridor and a save room between them.

The Nemesis we saw in the demo? That's the only time he captures the pursuing spirit he has in the original RE3. The rest of the time he's chasing us through linear corridors or alleyways. Or we're fighting him as a boss in spacious arenas: a large rooftop, the square in front of St. Michael's, NEST 2's circularly arranged specimen tanks, and finally the lab's warehouse...it's all so samey, like a low-rent Dark Souls.

Nikolai no longer flies his helicopter at the end. Instead there's a cutscene fistfight with Carlos, and then you press a button to shoot Nikolai. But wait, he mentions he's working for someone else to destroy Umbrella! In true action B movie style, the game ends on this revelation. The lacklustre ending offered an ironic coda though: the real cause of the disaster was [b]greed[/b]. Was Jill referring to the Raccoon City...or this flawed game?

How about replayability? The brilliant Mercenaries game of the original RE3 has vanished. Instead you earn points from achievements and grinding out kills, so you can buy the rocket launcher. You can replay the game on harder difficulties. And uh...that's it.

When reviewing the excellent RE2 remake I said I hoped lightning would strike twice. It didn't. Capcom's corporate greed once again took the helm, and forced the devs into rushing out yet another mediocre Resident Evil title in service of a nice quarterly earnings report.

[h1]T I T for T A T review[/h1]

I played the original Resident Evil 3 a few months back to have it fresh on my mind and to hype myself up. Re 2 was amazing, so RE 3 looked damn promising. Let's go (possible spoilers ahead)!

[b]T I T[/b]
Graphics and environments look beautiful with the city atmosphere looking dark and gruesome! The models and  facial animation looks fantastic and it's nice to see our old school heroes revamped. I know some people are complaining about the deaths not being brutal enough, but there ARE some brutal and creepy ones still there. Getting caught by a Hunter Gamma ain't a good time!

[b]T A T[/b]
Not a single new zombie model. All are recycled from RE2. I just found this weird because I would expect more variety being in the city seeing more zombies, so more should == to more variety right? Not a huge detail but a letdown. Dismemberment also feels a bit cheaper than RE2.

[b]T I T[/b]
Gameplay definitely is more action paced like the original intended with the new dodge mechanic. In the original I was able to mash it with Nemesis but this one involves more skill with actual timing. I still fail most of the time but when you pull it off it's satisfying, so the balance feels about right. Like RE2, there's still dark horror tones which I hope they keep in this direction (Resident Evil 4 was when it was starting to feel less horror and over the top).

[b]T A T[/b]
As great as the gameplay is, it feels short, and I play slow on my first playthroughs on games. If you played the demo then you did the greatest disservice to yourself. When I was playing the original I remember actually saying "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game feels huge", because there was so much of the city to wander in! I expected that but the demo was *mainly* the city, which just sucks balls. What we get to see is beautiful, but I was expecting x3-x4 that to explore. Oh and another thing I'm surprised no one else mentioned: most enemies are contained to a single *area*, so a zombie can be chasing you and you just step up on some steps to make it U-turn around and walk away. It takes away the horror when I know I can easily step to a place that is "out of bounds" and just pick them off at a safe distance.

[b]T I T[/b]
Carlos is better in about every way possible. To me he felt very cheesy in the original, and let's face it, the new do looks just badass. His section in the hospital and RPD were pretty solid. Would have been more fitting to stick the original and get Jill in the RPD but it's fine.

[b]T A T[/b]
Nikolai on the other hand is worse in almost every way possible. His look is great, but they made him into some comic villain. In the original he felt like he was on your side but had more subtle hints that he shouldn't be trusted. In RE3 he hates on Jill as soon as he shows up and is immediately the "bad guy". There's also not much info on the supervisors at all (or at least I didn't find any on my 1st run)

[b]T I T[/b]
Nemesis!! He looks awesome, and he can be terrifying in his own right. Your instincts are to run but they designed him to take advantage of that so it's usually best to go toe to toe.. which is terrifying! Very cool and nice to see him evolve.

[b]T A T[/b]
Nemesis!! Wait what? Yeah, as great as he seems it feels like they could have pushed it SOOOO much more. They had a great framework setup with Mr. X that makes you feel like you're constantly being stalked. I think they only had one portion like that, and that was the demo area. Any other time you see him it's either a boss fight or you NEED to run. Times between that make you feel like you're not being stalked at all which is kind of disappointing. He had so much potential to be more.

[b]T I T[/b]
They nailed the remade enemies! I felt tense the whole time with the Drain Deimos. Hunter Gammas look so much better, Hunter Betas are brutal as always. The head crab things creep the hell out of me.

[b]T A T[/b]
Still missing some old enemies, but that felt expected considering it was the same with RE2. Would have been nice to see maybe the grave digger but oh well.

[b]T I T[/b]
A new shop system is included so that you get points for every achievement you unlock and get to buy items with that. Nice to have something to give it a bit more replayability.

[b]T A T[/b]
RE2 had 4 campaigns to choose from, with different difficulties, this has one campaign.

Overall I wish there was more city to explore and Nemesis acted like a Mr.X version 2, but still a nice solid game to enjoy.

When I first heard that Resident Evil 3 was being remade in the same way Resident Evil 2 was, I got excited, not because of my love for the original RE3, but because I loved the remake of RE2 so much. For me, RE2 Remake was a masterpiece, even if it varied greatly from the original. In many ways, it was a re-imagining.

Now, I've never once played the OG Resident Evil 3, however, after I preordered RE3 Remake, I went back and played through the original RE3. While it was an amazing game, after playing Resident Evil 3 Remake, I feel that it is very much a masterpiece in the same way Resident Evil 2 Remake was. Will it replace the original? For those who didn't grow up with the tank controls and pre-rendered graphics? Yes. But it's differences don't make it a worse game than it's predecessor.

Pros:

Great Action - The game is far more fast paced than RE2R, and it keeps your blood pumping through the whole game.

Likable Characters - With the exceptions of some obviously forced dialogue, the characters in the game are very likable and endearing. Think cheesy late 90s action movies, and you'll be spot on.

World - Despite the admittedly shorter run time of this game, there is so much more to explore here than in the previous entry. Where-as in RE2R you had the Police Station, Sewers and NEST, alongside the smaller city streets and Orphanage, RE3R has WAY more city streets, roughly 1/3 of the Police Station, a small power plant, a sewer that's admittedly smaller than RE2R's, some segments that are used for intense chase scenes, a very impressive and terrifying hospital, alongside a far more believable underground laboratory. The world feels so much larger because you move from area to area at a more consistent pace, with less backtracking, so it feels like you're constantly moving forward. The game is undeniably larger in scale than RE2R, even if you spend less time in each area.

Still Scary - If you play games like amnesia, outlast or other similar horror hits, this won't feel scary at all. But, if Resident Evil is the extent you dip your toes into horror, then this game has some genuinely scary moments. Whether its running from Nemesis as you hear him stomping towards you, dodging disgusting insects in their own hive, or tiptoeing around dark hallways of the police station or hospital, this game has some great atmosphere and phenomenal music that helps keep the mood.

Unlockables - This game does in fact have far more unlockables, and they come at a more steady pace that is more easily controlled by the player. This means that if all you care about is an infinite ammo weapon, you can get that as early as the start of your 2nd playthrough, but if you prefer speedruns, you can get certain key items before they're given in-game, so you can access containers and item caches earlier than intended. There's also 'gear' you can unlock that increases damage done, reduces damage taken, or provides a passive healing effect. These are great for those who want to complete higher difficulties, but aren't skilled enough to go toe-to-toe with the bigger baddies.

Enemy Variety - Stuff got cut from the OG, yes. There are no spiders, but I consider that a plus. People with arachnophobia can play this game without warning, there are ZERO spiders in-game. Crows are also absent, but they never added much in prior games anyway. What is here is amazing though. The zombies are reused from RE2R, but this is acceptable, considering it's in the same city, and there's enough variety that it's not like you have two of the same type in one area. Drain Deimos are WAY more terrifying in this game than the OG, though I wish they got more screen time. Paleheads make a return from RE2R, in the campaign this time. Hunter Beta and Gamma are here, both wildly different from one another an each terrifying to deal with the first time you see them. Lickers are in the game as well, and more plentiful on higher difficulties. Dogs are here as well, but unfortunately only in limited quantities. 

Boss Fights - Compared to RE2R, the boss encounters in RE3R are FAR superior. Much like in RE2R, you'll be fighting the same villain again and again, but where-as G1 hobbled around, Nemesis toys with you using a flamethrower. G2 you'd dodge around until you did enough damage to knock him off with a crane, where-as Nemesis Stage 2 has you dodging a huge hound-like beast who even now is almost still toying with you as he runs circles around the arena. G3 was the one really great boss in RE2R, and Stage 3 for Nemesis stands toe-to-toe with it in terms of sheer fun(even if the camera can get a bit janky). I cannot compare G4 from RE2R to Stage 4 for Nemesis, as in truth, he's far more of a matchup for G5, but even if you added the fun of G4 and G5 together, Nemesis' final showdown is still leagues better! On harder difficulties, it's insanely tough, borderline unfair, but that gives you a challenge to actually work towards.

Cons:

Lack of Costumes - This could be fixed in a future update, but without preordering, you get only TWO costumes for Jill, and default only for Carlos. Should you preorder, you get Classic Jill, which looks great, and Classic Carlos' hair... his HAIR. It honestly doesn't even look that good. New Carlos looks great! It'd be SO easy for them to throw in costumes. Modders have already been doing this since the demo released! Even if Jill just had like, Clair's Remake outfit, that'd of been great, or her "infected" model, which is in the game as a viewable model! Regina would have been great to see as a costume in HD too. Carlos could have had a Hunk skin, maybe Leon's RPD uniform for laughs? They could have done more, they didn't, it was lazy, there's no excuse.

No S+ Rank - This might seem petty, but the game's highest ranking is S, and this is a problem because unlike RE2R, you can get S rank with infinite weapons. So, you can get S rank Inferno with the Infinite Rocket Launcher, and nobody knows if you did it legit with no unlockables, or if you used cheat weapons. It reduces the replayability and I HOPE they patch in S+ later, maybe with costumes locked behind it.

Game Length - This for me is a very MINOR con. I beat the game in just under 6 hours(as in 5h59m) and I felt immediately as if my $48 was well spent. It was an amazing 8 hours. Wait, 8? But I said I beat it in 6, right? Well, the game doesn't count time spent in cutscenes, on the radio or in the pause(not item) menu. This game is packed with cutscenes, easily over an hour and a half of story spread across the game. So, when people say the game is short because they beat it their first playthrough in 4 hours, remember they didn't count cutscenes. That said, the game is shorter than RE2R. This is expected, since the game encourages you to move hastily. There's less backtracking and a constant need to move forward. RE2R had you backtracking A LOT. My first RE2R run was 12 hours. But, RE2R also has way less cutscenes and smaller areas.

Overall?
For me, I recommend this game because although it was a short initial experience, it's been an amazing and very memorable experience. My husband sat next to me as I played through it, and we have great memories of that adventure we took alongside Jill and Carlos. Was it the best RE game ever made? For some, maybe? Is it better than the original RE3? In some regards, yes. Would I recommend it for $40, $50 or $60? For me? Yes. For you? That's what you need to decide. I've not yet 100% the game, and at the time of writing, I have 22 hours into it. I'll be working on Inferno tomorrow, and  I'm looking forward to grinding the few remaining achievements out for the next 5 to 6 hours. I'll be replaying this again and again, even after 100% because it is genuinely a great game. I think a lot of people came in expecting too much, and since it under-delivered by a bit, people are really sore over it. I think it's a great game and it, to me, feels like a worthwhile purchase.

Having played the majority of the main-line RE series, including last year's RE2 remake....This one falls a bit short of the mark. Don't get me wrong, the game looks and plays spectacularly. 
The issues I have with this entry aren't mechanical, they're not even issues with fun-factor. My biggest gripe is the (I'msureyou'veguesseditalready) length. 

Granted, if you ever played the original RE3, this isn't very shocking.

However...
Coming hot off the heels of last years near-flawless RE2 remake, this game had ginormous Mr. X-sized shoes to fill. The RE2 remake took the original release, made it play like a 2019 game, made it beautiful, and expanded upon it in occasionally surprising ways. 

It is no small-feat to make an 11 hour game so delightful that the consumer dumps 40-odd hours (with more to come) into it.

RE3 remake has that same potential. It's just over far too fast. 

Nothing about this entry feels fleshed-out. It moves at a pace that is far too fast. Introducing you to a few deceptively expansive environments only to usher you along to the next location before you have the chance to realize that it's not.  

I had expected Capcom to use this opportunity to really beef-up the gameplay and narrative experience. But rather than add a bunch of content, or expand the narrative in interesting ways, they removed large chunks of an already short experience. What we got was an entry that feels far too short to justify the price tag, and one that just feels hollow in comparison to the previous entry.

After the mega success of the Resident Evil 2 remake, Capcom saw it in their best interest to go ahead and also remake their classic 1999 title, Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. Taking place a mere 24 hours before the events of its predecessor, this game sees players in the role of Jill Valentine; former Special Tactics and Rescue Services (S.T.A.R.S.) member, and survivor of the horrors that happened at the Spencer Mansion in the original Resident Evil. With most of Raccoon City's population consumed by the virus, Jill is left fighting through hordes of the undead to try and escape the doomed metropolis before it's nuked to dust. Along the way she enlists the help of Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service (U.B.C.S) soldier Carlos Oliveira, who serves to help Jill escape from not only the city, but also a seemingly unstoppable mutant that chases her throughout the entire campaign.

If you've been following this game at all, you'll most likely already know that Resident Evil 3 is short... too short; to be fair though, so was the original. As someone who personally explores every nook and cranny on a first playthrough and goes out of their way to find collectibles and earn achievements, my fullest efforts brought me to just over six hours playtime for the main campaign. It really does feel like more of a DLC since there's no second scenario, and there's not much of a reason to replay it unless you're wanting to earn more achievements or earn points for in-game unlockables; ala Resident Evil 5 style. However, the real factor that will drive up the played hours here is Resident Evil Resistance, a brand new 4vs1 multiplayer game, similar to other asymmetrical horror games like Dead by Daylight and Last Year. How long a player base will stick around is yet to be seen, but with over 26,000 concurrent players at off-peak hours, it's off to a promising start.

The graphics, gameplay, mechanics, and all of the core pulp that make up this title are the exact same as the Resident Evil 2 remake. Everything looks great, plays great, and feels great; Nemesis himself is formidable and imposing, both in aesthetic and functionality. All of the standard weapons make a return, there are ways to upgrade your inventory and guns, there are the usual health items... it's all the same, and not much more can be said; it's Resident Evil. However, the game itself is finicky and unstable. If you so much as ALT+TAB out to try and check an e-mail or what have you, it will automatically close; no ifs, ands, or buts about it. There are some frustrating downsides to the campaign as well, with the major one being just how maddeningly slow Jill runs and the fact that she takes a 1-2 second pause after dodging, making the maneuver nearly irrelevant unless timed impeccably.

There should be more to say here, this review does feel really short... just like the game itself. However, the Resident Evil 3 remake is just that... a solid remake of the original game, albeit missing some locations, enemies, and all of the puzzles. It doesn't go above and beyond what its remake predecessor did, there's not much longevity to it, and Nemesis can be more irritating to go up against than fun. In fact, most of his boss battle appearances are total bullet sponge segments that force you to not only deplete all of the ammo pickups in the immediate area, but also all of your reserves. Capcom did manage to do the story justice, however. The inclusion of Resident Evil Resistance was a smart move, though at the same time it does feel like fodder to justify an AAA price tag. If you have no interest in the multiplayer portion, and especially if Resident Evil 3 isn't your favorite installment, it's best to catch this one on sale at some point.

Be warned that the game does have a rather annoyingly long and on-rails starting segment, which, after playing it about 5 times, quickly becomes chore to do. Resident Evil 2's bosses were somewhat set-piecey, but I feel RE3's Nemesis fights are even more set-piecey and while that makes them cinematic, it can also make them feel weirdly out of place in the otherwise slow a deliberate pacing in the game. 

Overall, I would say that RE3 exceeded my expectations, but not to the degree that the RE2 Remake did, but then again, it might be unfair to compare the two, considering we had been waiting with bated breath for RE2 Remake for years.

This game is enjoyable enough, but it's a very weak follow up to REmake 2. REmake 2 is probably the best example of a proper survival horror game we've gotten in ages. It provided a nice balance between tense horror and exciting, enjoyable combat with plenty of approachable yet rewarding puzzle solving and a fair amount of replay-ability and extra content. if you haven't already, I highly recommend giving that game a playthrough.

REmake 3 falls short compared to 2 in almost all areas. although I completed the game in roughly the same time it took me to complete my first playthrough as Leon, it felt like a much smaller game. The game only feels somewhat interesting to explore in the opening city segment, the portion you'll feel quite familiar with if you played the demo. The vast majority of the game feels very linear and the hidden items are way too easy to find and the puzzles are mind-numbingly simple. It always feels like you're being rushed by the story, which itself gives the impression there are likely large segments from the perspective of Carlos that we were intended to experience but were cut to reduce development time, leaving us with some jarring moments when our hero characters catch up to eachother throughout the story. Once passed the opening city section, the environments are pretty unmemorable. Nemesis feels like much too small a part of the game for being the main enemy. He's also not that big of a threat. in the sections where he stalks you it's pretty easy to evade his attacks and knocking him down a single time nets you enough time to escape to the next area. The whole game honestly lacks much in the way of tension; ammo and healing items are abundant, the heavier enemies can be subdued very easily with the right equipment, and somehow the atmosphere just always feels lacking. The final boss fight is a complete joke. The whole sequence is stupidly easy and it feels like something out of a cheesy B movie, especially Jill's idiotic quips. This is just not a good follow-up to REmake 2 and I believe a lot of core survival horror fans will come away quite disappointed with this.

All that said, the game is still enjoyable. This would make for an excellent port of entry to the genre for those less patient to the quirks generally associated with it. It's not a "great" game and it's not really what I was hoping for, but it's at least worthy of a playthrough. I'd say wait for it to go on sale though. At $30 I would say get it if you're really itching for a return to Raccoon City, At $20 I think it would be definite buy. But at full retail of $60? I say pass. You're not missing much.

When I heard that Resident Evil 3 Remake was happening I was ecstatic. I have a very unpopular opinion that among the original trilogy RE3 was the best one for me. The atmosphere of the original was great, the game had lots of structure in it's story with lots of replayability, I liked the new additions the game had and overall enjoyed it a lot. 

So I had High Expectations for RE3R, Sadly the game did not get the same treatment as RE2R. The pacing in the story sucks, everything happens way to fast from the introduction of nemesis to the issues with certain supporting characters in the story, the game is overwriten with quick time events and linear paths. There are far to many cutscenes in the game, admittingly not as bad as say, MGS4 but it bogs down the pacing and makes you feel more like you're watching a movie less then playing the game. Not to mention the significant lack of inspiration. RE2R toke a lot of liberties with it's source material but they still kept in all the familiar aspects you'd expect from RE2. The Police Station, the Sewer, The Lab, even adding places that weren't in the original but we're still based on area's in RE2. RE3R is missing key area's that we're in the original! And even part that WAS in the original is very different that it feels more like a rough adaptation then a remake! The only part of the game that felt authentic was the Demo part as I call it. Being the streets of Raccoon City, and the various place's you play through as Carlos. Otherwise the familiarity is completely gone and the new places either last only a few minutes or are brushed over completely with only mentions in a magazine or some document you can pick up. 

The Puzzles are non existent and are really only used to obtain bonus items or additional ammo in the game. Did not feel like it was worth the backtracking. I understand that the developpers did state the game would have more of enthusiasm on action as it did in the original, I was fine with that. But when your game has limited playability with nothing to keep me engaged it feels dull. Not to mention not balanced well as there are tons of spots where the game mercilessly throws enemies at you in very cramped spaces. I was playing on standard and still had multiple instances where I was running out of ammo. The Dodge mechanic is much more refined and is more satisfying when you pull off a successful dodge to get away. However it is parrying and requires pin point reflexes and again, when you are in situations where there are hordes of enemies in a small space dodging can help but your limited to 3 dodges before Jill starts stumbling. So even when pulling it off I still had multiple instances I kept getting hit. 

The replay value is minimal. Since they did a bang up job with RE2R's 2nd scenario I figured they we're going to limit the game a bit but what they did is just lazy. The branching paths of the original are gone and none of the items are randomized on a second play through. In fact if you play the game over again the game is exactly the same there is nothing different when you play the game. There are harder difficulties this time which switches up the placement of some enemies but otherwise the game is EXACTLY the same. I won't spoil the bonus's but they suck to. Most of them are borrowed from RE7 and the one's that are original are the standard afair you'd see in an RE game, nothing unique. 

Some good things I do like about the game, the scenery looks good, the atmosphere is still chilling, when walking through the streets of Raccoon City there are faint noises of ambience. Large foot steps randomly through the street indicating Nemesis is near by, the area's that are faithfully recreated look just as fresh as they did when I played RE3 back in 1999 and everything looks super realistic and scary. The zombies are also a LOT more tough, you can hang over a zombie and just knife them now you have come up with new solutions to fight them. But I'm still docking points because there are few points in the game where you can do this because of the horrible placement of enemies. There are new types of monsters that are a welcome addition to the franchise and keep you on your toes. 

Overall I am very disappointed in this Remake. I was really expecting this game to be given even better treatment then it did when it originally came out. Instead it was treated worse and we got an inferior version of the original. If you can do yourself a favor and just get the original game. You'll have much more fun with it then this one.

I have an extremely mixed feeling about the current state of the game and may update this review pending further game updates (or DLCs... given modern game development practice).

TL;DR summary at the bottom.

(SPOILERS AHEAD)

As a remake, RE3 is visually outstanding but also streamlined much of the story and characters (for better or worse).

1. The opening and introduction: 
a. In the original, Jill talks about her last escape and a cut-scene follows with the RPD making their last stand in the streets.
b. In the remake, Jill is confined to her apartment and placed under watch by chief Irons... then is surprised by a visit from Nemesis. When she breaks out of the apartment, she is completely shocked by the events in the streets.

There is a lot of potential here to explore. In the hours before Jill's breakout, Carlos's survival and how the UBCS was deployed and ambushed (hinted at by Mikhail) can be added to the game.

2. Carlos and Jill split journeys.
Rather than going out and assisting Jill in the first hour of the game, Carlos stays behind doubling as security and radio man in the subway station. (Strange, because Tyrell in the remake is appears to be a tech specialist and likely could have worked the radio).
Carlos ends up  investigating RPD with Tyrell without Jill ever going to RPD.

3. Carlos investigates the RPD.
- Carlos and Tyrell arrives to find Marvin being attacked by a zombie Brad Vickers.

The potential additions leading up to this scene is actually the most interesting to me. Based on RE2Make and outbreak (if its still canon), some survivors LIKELY did escape RPD and the city itself. Marvin and Elliot ended up dead and zombified in RE2, but other officers (Rita and Kevin) and their whereabouts remains unknown. 

Also, given the concurrent event of the RPD making their last stand in the streets, the ideas don't seem too far fetched for me.

Either way, I think the potential here is great for further exploration. Perhaps (free?) multiple DLCs or new scenarios titled "Their Finest Hour, "The Last Escape"... or even "The Outbreak" is suitable? Assuming Capcom is working on DLCs/Scenarios for this game.
- I am not including HUNK and/or Ada because they had their moments in RE2Make.

4. Treatment for Jill after her infection by Nemesis.
- Not too much to say, Carlos plays hero but Tyrell supports him in the RE3Make storyline.

5. Final chapter, underground lab
- The final fight against Nemesis; kind of over-the-top sci-fi and no Delta Force.

Summary:
I am CURRENTLY not inclined to recommend the game at full price in its current state.
- I am fine with the story changes, but the streamlined story also leaves me very wanting because of what I have played and experienced in the past.
- The "wanting" is basically me not getting what I am expecting, hence my mixed feelings.
- The game being "too short" isn't an issue for me, but I am assuming RE3Make will also get a similar RE2Make treatment; in which additional scenarios will added.
- Again, this review will be updated depending on how well Capcom going to is meet the expectations I have in the next year or 2 for this game.

[h1] First, the good. [/h1]
The game plays like a dream. For around 45gb you get solid gameplay with some stunning visuals, and you don't need the most impressive PC to enjoy it. The gameplay mechanics are fluent and each serve a purpose. The RE Engine, overall, is very impressive. However, there are a couple shortcomings, notably the in-game facial animations. I'm not sure why, but when there's dialogue in-game, the characters mouth random syllables that don't match up with the script, at all. This is a minor flaw, but compared to the rest of the visual experience, its quite jarring to see.


[h1] Now, the bad. [/h1]
The story writing does not feel very RE3, to me. The campaign moves very fast, almost to a rushed degree. The intro, in particular, started off in a somber, eerie tone; only to be dashed away and next thing you know, you're on the other side of the bar where you left Brad. You don't even get to move around the bar's interior, a lot of that whole chapter is done for you in cinematic. Why they chose this direction, I don't know. But the pacing feels more in line of RE6 than the RE2. The narrative direction is really telling when you looks at Nemesis. To put in perspective, Mr. X of the RE2 remake felt more like Nemesis than Nemesis, itself. With Mr. X, he almost felt like part of the world, where you wouldn't know where he would jump out next, and at that point, you had to actually avoid his presence. This isn't the case with Nemesis. Nemesis felt more like an extra obstacle in a part of the map. Zombies + Nemesis, essentially. I also have to talk about the gameplay, in a negative light. The gameplay, while solid and easy to control, again, does not feel RE3 and more like RE6. The remake here seems to go back to the direction of an action/adventure (I use the term "adventure" loosely) than a proper survival horror game. Overall, all these points really detract from the horror of the game. The only times you'll ever get scared is when you're finally attacked, which isn't the hardest to avoid. Worst of all, where are the puzzles? There is almost no puzzle solving to be found in this remake. [b] Why are there no puzzles? [/b]

If you're looking for what essentially looks like a full-priced, good-looking RE2 Remake DLC, go for it. But otherwise, that's all it is.

It's technically a good game with some cool moments but I think it has a lot of problems and I would not say it's worth it at full price.

- No real bonus modes to the game whereas RE2make had HUNK's mode from the original and the Ghost Survivors. I know Resistance exists, but it's outright not part of this game. I'll probably give it a try but if you launch it as a separate title I don't think it's fair to count it as part of 3. There's a bunch of achievements for speedrunning and whatnot but 2 had those as well in addition to the bonus modes.

- A lot of arbitrary stuff is changed or added, to the point where you could argue this isn't fully a remake of 3, but rather a readaptation. [spoiler]Gravedigger is gone (what's wrong with the giant animal enemies all of a sudden?), the Clocktower is basically entirely removed, the Dead Factory is gone in favor of a copy of 2's final area which felt very dull, among others. Most of the downtown area is also different, substituting areas from the original for a trek through the sewers and a bit featuring the Drain Demos (which don't appear anywhere else). Other stuff is also moved, strangely, to places where they're less cool. Nemesis blowing up the rescue helicopter happens within the first twenty minutes of the game, lessening how much of a hope spot it is, and Jill's "You want STARS? I'll give you STARS!" isn't at the end, but a part where she's running away from Nemesis, which felt like they were reaching to include it. 2make removed or changed some stuff but it was still functionally the same, but I guess you can chalk up the difference to the different team.[/spoiler]

- Nemesis himself. I felt like the game both exaggerated him and also downplayed him at the same time, and I'll explain both in order. In the original game his strength was being a very hard to kill, very intelligent predator who was designed to kill a lone, under-equipped woman. But it felt like they needed to jazz him up, and so in the remake he can do massive leaps in-game, take control of zombies, and he has the flamethrower. [spoiler]They also felt the need to change his second form, another arbitrary change. In the original it was basically him shirtless showing off his mutations, but here it's him on all-fours and much more monstrous, essentially devolved into a bestial state. It reminded me a lot of G-Birkin's fourth form in original RE2 (which was also changed for its remake, funnily enough), and it looks cool, but one thing while fighting him in that form was in the back of my mind, and that's "this isn't Nemesis". The only time he mutated was after you'd halfway killed him in the original - constantly having new forms was the G-Virus' gimmick, so why staple it to him too? Even his final form now goes from a last ditch effort to kill Jill to a monstrosity that fills the room. [/spoiler]

- Paradoxically, it also felt like Nemesis barely had a presence in the game at times. Everybody remembers all the times he'd ambush you in the original game, and they tried to replicate that here, but most of them are static, scripted scenes where you run away from him, with the only time he's hunting you being the downtown area at the beginning. In the original the player almost always had the option of fighting him when he appeared, and him being able to soak up so much ammo could really make him feel unstoppable. You can actually down him in that early portion with one grenade - great Bioweapon, guys. [spoiler]For some reason they decided to change Brad's death to being killed by a swarm of zombies, so he also doesn't actually kill a single member of STARS the whole game. He's also completely gone after infecting Jill until he shows up in the Dead Factory equivalent, whereas he actively made an attempt to finish the job while she was out in the original.[/spoiler]

I do like the voice acting and some of the story changes, the gameplay is still well-done, and it's nice to see Jill playable again after forever, but I feel like this game could have used more time and a bit more thought put into it, at least if they wanted it to be worth a full 60 dollars.

RESIDENT EVIL 3 (remake) is a great time. While there are certain hindrances on the game's perceived quality that mostly stem from the original version, the campaign is always entertaining and extremely well-made.

[h1] PROS [/h1]:
-Graphically impressive. Everything in the game looks great, whether it be Nemesis's distorted facial features or Jill rolling around in an action scene.
-The gameplay is constantly fun, bringing the hybrid of zombie combat and puzzle-solving that the series is famous for. There is a bit of variety between the two player characters, as each has a different weapon set and "special move."
-Controls feel great. Each gun's shots have different weight, and moving Jill is smooth and easy.
-The story is typical Resident Evil fare, but it works really well here. Jill is awesome, and the supporting characters each serve a purpose. I can't say there are many moments of emotional impact, but seeing Jill work through her trauma from the events of the first Resident Evil game through her long combat with Nemesis is moving, and it all culminates in a pretty cathartic fashion.
-The cutscenes aren't intrusive, are directed well, and generally help boost the game's tension, as well as make you care about the main characters.
-The difficulty is pretty balanced. Jill can take quite a few hits, but the late game introduces some pretty tough enemy types that are relatively difficult to kill. It's also not afraid to throw waves of enemies at you, especially in later encounters. Ammo is very scarce, so I sometimes found myself fighting waves of monsters with two grenades and a handful of pistol rounds.
-The game has a moderate level of replayability; there is no NG+, but an in-game shop opens up after your first play-through and offers a variety of rewards and buffs to take into your next run, as well as higher difficulties to take on.

[h1] CONS [/h1]:
-The campaign IS fairly short, especially at a $60 price point. I finished the game in about 7.5 hours, but 2ish hours of that was from runs where I died and was sent back to a checkpoint.  The in-game clock said it took me 5.5 hours, which is... too short. This can be chalked up to a number of reasons I'm sure, such as the original game being very short and also only having one route to play through in comparison to RE2's two separate paths. I got the game on sale for ~$36, and I feel satisfied with that price.
-The game isn't really scary. It unfortunately has a lingering issue that plagues the Resident Evil series and focuses more on action instead of outright horror. Nemesis is pretty creepy at first, but he's really only a threat in the first hour of the game. The fear mostly stems from the high number of enemies and low supplies throughout, which I guess is fine.
-Not much weapon variety to speak of. About 2/3 of the way through the game I unlocked the achievement for collecting all of the weapons in the campaign, so... You can unlock iconic series weapons between play-throughs in the shop to take into your campaign run, but there aren't many of these. You really only need the shotgun, pistol, and grenade launcher to clear the game.

[h1] CONCLUSION [/h1]:
The game is worth playing through once or twice for sure. It's really fun and feels great to play, and the enemy variety and new environments keep the game fresh as you roll through the campaign. I have no interest in playing RESISTANCE, so I can't comment on the game's multiplayer aspect. Overall, this game is a welcome addition to the franchise.

[WARNING, minor spoilers for the original Resident Evil games and the RE2 remake ahead]

As a big fan of the original Resident Evil Games the RE2 remake was an enormous disappointment for me, filled with too many nonsensical and frustrating design choices and a lack of improvement where it was needed. 

Along comes RE3 and thank goodness it fixes every major issue I had with RE2. 

Firstly, the dodge mechanic is back, providing at least some common sense counter to the crazy range of the zombie grab, rather than having to stuff a grenade in its mouth or waste a breakable knife. I mean sure, it's a game about zombies but at least there should be some semi-realistic reactions to attacks. Trying to get out of the way would just be about the most normal response. 

Then, the classic knife is back, useless in actual combat but allowing you to poke at zombies on the floor without worrying about wasting it, classic Resident Evil style. 

Now, at least on the standard difficulty, the damage seems to have been normalised. Sure they can still take a beating before going down but at least you don't frequently encounter ordinary zombies that are somehow arbitrary bullet-sponges. 

The Nemesis encounters are scripted. And yes, that's a good thing, quality over quantity. In RE2 getting chased around the precinct the entire time by the Tyrant very quickly became tedious with having to constantly double back to the safe room after which the Tyrant would simply just take a hike and snoop around elsewhere until you start wandering around and it started all over again.  

Speaking of Nemesis, the boss battles have actually been improved over the original game and in some cases changed altogether, which was something the original Resident Evil 2 could really have used but which it failed to do. The boss battles were possibly the weakest aspects of the originals and It felt like the boss battles in RE2 were copy-pasted. 

The alternate character sections are also far better than in RE2. In RE2 playing as Ada and Sherry is an exercise in frustration, feeling out of place and filled with unnecessary mechanics. In RE3 things are kept simpler and all to the good as it feels like a part of the main game rather than just an annoying interlude. 

Last but definitely not least, half the game isn't set in the sewers. Whatever possessed the designers of RE2 to flesh out that transitional section of the original to such an extent, rather than increasing city exploration or even the laboratory, is anyone's guess. 

The net result is that RE3 feels and plays like a more classic Resident Evil game, while still being modernised. It even managed to reinvigorate some of the genuine dread and tension I felt playing the originals, where I'm constantly fearing when and where the next enemy will rear its ugly head. 

Fair warning, a lot of stuff from the original has been omitted in favour of a more streamlined experience. On the other hand I feel what has been included, old and new, more than makes up for this (some real 'nope' moments in there). And while it isn't the longest game, well, arguably Resident Evil games were made to be replayed. 

All in all an awesome experience with no regrets (except perhaps that the crows and giant spiders have still been left out but you can't have everything xD ).

In a vacuum, this is perfectly functional Resident Evil game that would feel right at home during the earlier part of the last decade - where RE wasn't sure if it wanted to be action or horror. However, the reality of the situation is that Capcom had to not only live up to the legacy of Resident Evil 3, but the mirror-shine-polish that was the RE2 Remake. 

I'm just glad I read pre-release reviews before I played (and have not played the original), because otherwise the disappointment would be crushing. The reviews mentioned that there was very little of the clever open-ended level design found in 2, outright cut areas and concepts from the original game, and – most distressingly – Nemesis having the double-downgrade of not being as intimidating as both OG Nemesis and Mr. X. All of these ended up being true.

This last point is mindbogglingly terrible on so many levels – remember Mr. X patrolling the area, making navigation instantaneously more nerve-wracking when you heard his footsteps? Remember how dynamic his appearances were? How you ended up dreading him? All that is gone. Replaced with utterly scripted sequences (save for one where he actually chases you around the area early in the game), sometimes employing the dreaded quick-time event that I thought Capcom – let alone every other game developer on the planet – got over around 2015. It’s honestly a travesty. It’s especially insane given how heavily Capcom marketed the game around Nemesis being a terrifying threat in the same vain as Mr. X – it’s flagrant false advertising. 

Evidently, Capcom had so little confidence in RE3 as a product that they bundled some asymmetrical multiplayer garbage, microtransactions included. At the time of writing, I have no interest in even touching it. I’m sure the community will last all of two months before dying out. Mercenaries would have been [i]fine[/i], Capcom. 

As a side note I think some of the horror aspects could have been saved with less music during gameplay – with the corny “tense” music playing in the background, it really does begin to feel like one of the lesser Resident Evils. 

However, at the end of the day, this is still a sequel to the most mechanically polished games in the series, and it inherits the basic mechanics that make it so appealing. Inventory management, weapon upgrades, a precision-centric aiming system – they’ve all managed to make it to 3 mostly unsullied. The guns are still fun to shoot and feel immaculately detailed. The game itself looks gorgeous, so good in fact that it almost feels like parody using these near photorealistic characters for a game that originally had faces comprised of four polygons and 50 pixels.

Honestly, the structure of the game and the few new mechanics it adds are an interesting change of pace – if only they could have been expanded upon further. I like the idea of a more aggressive RE that doesn’t entirely buck the horror trend, with way more ammo and health given out per area. The dodge move is a neat way to encourage both defensive and aggressive play – dodge an attack at just the right time and you’ll be given a bit of bullet time to finish off your bewildered attacker. Carlos even gets the ability to clock enemies in the face with this ability, making it a ridiculously fun move to pull off.

From what I understand, this was developed by Capcom’s B-team, instead of the A-team that brought us RE2. First off – I can only imagine how insulting this would be to RE3’s original fans. Secondly – I can only hope that their A-team is working on a Resident Evil that will knock our socks off.  EDIT: Huh, looks like they are.

You know how RE2 is now going for 20 dollars? Wait until RE3 hits that. For 20 bucks, I’d dare say RE3 is an above-average game, but 60 dollars is a ridiculous price for a cut-down sequel with an average first playtime of 6 hours and a bargain-bin multiplayer mode. I do recommend this game – 6 months from now.

The Good:
+ Great atmosphere and the Nemesis feels relentless at times.
+ Level design is strong with plenty of reasons to explore to find new ammo, weapon upgrades and more.
+ The soundtrack is far more present then it was in Resident Evil 2's remake. Which for this games more action oriented approach worked extremely well.
+ The zombies still feel great to shot, albeit not as good as in Resident Evil 2's remake (see below for more info).
+ Both leads (Jill and Carlos) are likeable characters, and one even has an ark. The side characters are also are enjoyable enough in there roles and the story is likewise solid.
+ The graphics here are absolutely stunning, and the redesign of the Nemesis and it's various mutations is gruesomely great.
+ The included Resident Evil Resistance multiplayer game is decent, albiet not incredible fun. It could be expanded on and become something special, though I doubt this will happen. A nice addition none the less.

The Bad:
- The arsenal of weapons you get is rather limited and it would have been nice for an extra weapon or two show up.
- The amount of ammo (in particular grenades) can make some parts of the game a little easier then I think was intended.
- Some minor clipping issues with zombie arms, along with other enemies appendages clipping through doors. This was also in the Resident Evil 2 remake, and it is a shame that it remains here.
- The lack of additional game modes within the main game itself is disappointing.

The Mixed:
-/+ There is no way around it, whilst there is still item management and the like, ammo is plentiful and the game is far more focused on action as opposed to the survival horror of Resident Evil 2's remake. I was fine with this but i'm sure it will not be to everyone's tastes.
-/+ Many have reported a short playtime. My first playthrough was around 8.5 hours and I missed several items and the like. Overall it was only around one hour shorter then my first playthrough of Resident Evil 2's remake.
-/+ The game is more of a loose adaptation of Resident Evil 3, as opposed to a remake. Meaning many elements you may have loved from the original will not be present here. If that is not what you are after this may be something that leads to disappointment.

First off, let me just say how much of a crazy ride this game was. This has been the best representation of Jill Valentine since her appearance in the original Resident Evil 3 in the late 90's. I'll do my best to keep this as spoiler free as possible. With that being said, let's get on with the review.

Plot

Like the original game, S.T.A.R.S. Officer Jill Valentine is trying to escape Raccoon City as the T-Virus continues to infect innocent people. The City is clearly on its last legs, and there are only a handful of survivors left. Jill begins to gear up and plans to evacuate, but is stopped in her tracks by an even deadlier threat than zombies. Enter Nemesis, a hulking behemoth of a creation with his mind set on killing every S.T.A.R.S. officer remaining. After escaping her first encounter with Nemesis, Jill teams up with a mysterious man and begins to plan their last escape.

If you've played the original, you will certainly notice some changes this time around. Without getting into detail, There are quite a few new areas and story points added in this release and some elements from the original game are gone entirely. It was sad not seeing some scenes in this remake, but I get why most of these changes have come into play. It offers a classic story with some new twists to keep players on their toes. None of the game felt like padding to me. Also, some players have stated that this game was too short. I disagree with this, as I felt it was a perfect length. Sure, the story does move a little more quickly than RE2 Remake did, but it just makes sense here.

I also really like what CAPCOM has done with the characters. Jill is clearly dealing with P.T.S.D. from the events that took place at the Spencer Mansion (Resident Evil 1). She feels believable, like she really has gone through a truly horrific experience before. This doesn't mean she is weak, however. She knows what she is capable of. I also love her knew design. It's a fresh new look with a healthy dose of classic thrown in for safe measure. Of course if you love her classic Tube-Top and skirt, that's here too in the form of DLC.

Carlos has seen a makeover as well. This time around, his hair is long and shaggy and decided to grow out his facial hair. He looks fantastic and I actually prefer his new look over his old one.

Gameplay

If you have played last year's Resident Evil 2 Remake, you will know to expect. RE3 plays just as well as RE2 and looks and feels just as spectacular. The areas look great, and the level design had me excited for what was going to come around the next corner. Raccoon City feels like it was lived in. There is so much personality within this game.

Jill has a few new moves compared to Leon and Claire. When a zombie is about to lunge toward Jill, she can preform a quick step to get out of reach. If executed with perfect timing, this quickstep turns into a dodge roll and activates a short slow motion effect to aim at an enemy's weak point. Honestly, I really enjoyed pulling off the dodge roll. It's really rewarding when you're in tight situations.

The Bad

Honestly, I have very little bad to say about this game. However, there is one thing that absolutely surprised me, and that was a lack of puzzles. Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil 2 Remake had wonderful puzzles placed throughout their entire stories, so why wasn't this game given the same treatment? This may be a plus for some, but I honestly miss spending a good 45 minutes on a well crafted puzzle. That's not to say they aren't here, but they are sprinkled so few and far between.

One other thing that I feel is a negative is the lack of Nemesis. No, seriously. I remember playing the original RE3 and he would hardly ever take a break from chasing Jill. In this remake, his presence is so little in the first few hours. Although he does up his game severely towards halfway into the campaign.

Verdict

I really enjoyed this take on Jill's last escape. It was new and exciting and I can't wait to see what CAPCOM does next with the series! If you enjoyed last year's RE2, you should enjoy this one. If I had to rate this game, it would be an easy 9/10 from me. Thank you for reading my review, and I hope you guys enjoy your chase with Jill Valentine as much as I did.

[b]Context[/b]: Casual RE fan. I've played RE Remake, RE2 Classic, RE4, RE7, and RE2 Remake the most. I have only played RE3 Classic twice or so and mostly as an adult, so I don't have any real nostalgia for it like I do some of the others. I won't spoil anything.

[b]Plus:[/b] Story mode is great. Some content from the original has been cut, some has been expanded upon. I don't care for much of what has been cut, and what they expanded upon is good. The action and gunplay are considerably better than RE2R. Dodging, especially, feels great. Bosses are also much better than those in RE2R. 

Acting and characterization are much better, as well, though some hardcore fans of the original RE3 may not agree. 

Music is far better than that in RE2R. Many tracks are reworked from RE3 Classic and it is pretty much always fitting. It stood out to me how good it was for most of my first playthrough.

Friendly for all ability levels. Assisted gives tons of extra perks for new players. Standard is seemingly easier than it was in RE2R. Hardcore is challenging and seems about the same as RE2R, though without the ink ribbon limitation. There are actually two more difficulties above Hardcore that I haven't run myself, but having watched people run them they are almost like entirely different games. The last boss on the highest difficulty may as well be a Dark Souls boss.

[b]Minus:[/b] Much like the original, the game trades much of the puzzles/exploration for more action. There are almost no puzzles in this game, and the few that are present are very easy. 

The game isn't quite Resident Evil 6, but it does lean into some of the bad habits of that game, like QTE. Moreover, those QTE aren't even challenging and don't have much reason to even be QTE. At least two of them can be completed by just holding UP. 

The biggest is overall value and how little effort was put into fleshing this game out. My first playthrough of the game on Standard took me roughly 5 hours. Second on hardcore about 4. S rank times on Hardcore are sub-2 hours. This game is meant to be run over and over again. If you don't see yourself playing it more than once or twice, it probably isn't worth $60 to you. 

Additionally, the game doesn't give you much for running it over and over again. There is a shop unlocked after first playthrough that lets you trade points earned from completing achievements. You can buy perk items and infinite ammo weapons, which can then be used in future runs to unlock other things. This isn't a negative, but just how little else there is in here is. There is ONE costume. It's a good one, but there is no excuse why there is only one besides the pre-order one. And while I'm not personally into records and such, I find it odd that you can earn the highest S ranking using infinite weapons and that there is no 'S+' rank like in RE2R. This would definitely piss that group of people off. Obvious omissions like these show that Capcom rushed this game.

[b]Summary:[/b] This game is fun, but if you don't plan on playing RE Resistance, the value proposition is really hard to justify for most average players. I'm happy with the game and will run it many more times, but I can still acknowledge that many people won't and for them this game objectively offers less to do than RE2R did for the same price. I think most average gamers will want to wait until they can get it at a lower price, but do play it at some point. The core game is exceptionally fun even if the whole package isn't the greatest value currently.
