[h1]Resident Evil 3 is an action packed and thrilling survival horror experience featuring great graphics, 5 difficulty modes and many challenges and replay value. It also comes with the free online multiplayer game Resistance that can be enjoyed with 5 of your friends. After the short review section I also make a little comparison between RE2&3 remakes and their originals. [/h1]

[b]Why buy it?[/b]
Resident Evil 3 Remake features 5 difficulty modes. Two of them being unlocked after beating Hardcore Difficulty. I highly recommend playing Hardcore first because its the difficulty the game seems to be designed around. Once you have cleared a playthrough, you earn unlock points that you can spend on bonus items, weapons and inventory slots for your next playthrough. This means, the more you play the game, the more bonus you can unlock and the more chances you have to survive the brutal and challenging higher difficulty modes. There is a ton of replay value to be found with that.

Also remember. Once you purchase Resident Evil 3 Remake, you will find the complete co-op multiplayer game Resident Evil Resistance in your library for free! You can play this one with 5 of your friends online! If that isn't enough value for a retail price of $60 then I don't know what to tell you.

[b]Should you trust the haters of the game?[/b]
[b]Resident Evil 2 Comparison[/b]
Resident Evil 2 Remake isn't a perfect remake. The second half was completely different, at least 90% of the iconic character interactions were cut out, the A and B scenarios made even less sense than in the original. Even going so far as creating giant plot holes and time paradoxes the original didn't had. There is also no replay value except maybe speedrunning it for better ranks and unlocking 4 weapons. Not counting the bonus modes and DLC.

The average playtime on Hardcore Difficulty was 8 hours on the first playthrough for the A scenario. And yet you don't hear the hardcore fanbase scream and moan about content that was cut in comparison to the original RE2? Some even praise it into heaven as a perfect remake. Which makes no sense reading the points I listed above.

[b]Resident Evil 3 Comparison[/b]
Resident Evil 3 Remake isn't a perfect remake either. The second half is the best part of the remake. In comparison to the original, at least 90% of the iconic locations, mechanics and character interactions were cut out, but got replaced with even better locations and the story makes more sense than the original.

The average playtime on Hardcore Difficulty was 8 hours on a first playthrough. So why is the hardcore fanbase screaming and moaning about content that was cut in comparison to the original RE3?

I believe most of it has to do with being blinded by the fact how good Resident Evil 2 Remake was, as well as - I really don't want to say it but I have to - hardcore fans being biased! They wanted a 1:1 copy with not a single stone turned. And that's not what they got and the reason why they are salty. I am a hardcore Resident Evil fan too, playing the series since the first game came out over 25 years ago and I consider Resident Evil 3 Remake a phenomenal remake that even puts RE2 Remake into shame.

[b]Conclusion[/b]
If you want to play through Resident Evil 3 Remake only once and never ever again. Then I can understand that a retail price is too much for you and that the short playtime of 8 hours for a first playthrough on Hardcore won't satisfy you. In that case you can wait for a discount and still enjoy this phenomenally good and thrilling survival horror experience. And who knows what DLC will be out by then!

Original RE3 was a fun but, let's be honest, inessential addition to RE2. Ironically, that is the part that the RE3 remake captures best - the feeling that you're playing a somewhat lackluster optional scenario.

RE2 remake was a very precise game. Every gameplay mechanic served a purpose, and served it almost perfectly. It was a difficult game, unforgiving at higher difficulties, but it was also fair: most of the time if you died, it was because you did something wrong. Let a zombie get too close, forgot which corridors were cleared out and which weren't, wasted too many bullets on enemies you could have avoided. RE3 takes these mechanics and just... breaks them.

I have played the full game on hardcode, and most of the times when I died were not boss battles. Sometimes it was from being cornered and stun locked by Nemesis, who you can't outrun and who can be very hard to dodge, especially in the early part of the game when the mechanic is still new and the area you're trying to learn it in is full of enemies and nooks you can get stuck in. Or it was from playing as Carlos in the hospital and being forced to battle a Hunter with nothing but an assault rifle, which is just not an effective weapon against them (compare to RE2, where bringing the wrong gun to a fight had to be YOUR fault), lacking the dodge mechanic which you were JUST STARTING TO GET A HANG OF, and having no reliable way to counter the Hunter's one-hit-kill attack.

As for the nostalgia factor, which RE2 heavily and very effectively leans on, RE3 kind of... lacks it. Some familiar characters are there, but their roles are changed (Brad) or reduced to cameos (Dario). They brought back Kendo and Marvin, even showcased them in the trailer... except the trailer basically features the entirety of both characters' screen time. Main characters (Jill, Carlos, Nicholai) get a good treatment and feel vibrant, good old Mikhail "Two First Names" Victor also turned out well in his new incarnation (his choice of swear words makes a certain dramatic moment a little more funny than I anticipated... but it almost works). For whatever reason Tyrell's role was greatly expanded - remember Tyrell? He's a guy who turned up in the original for one cutscene, in which he dies. Well, the new Tyrell is ok, I guess, but of all the characters to get a more meaty role he seems like an odd choice. [spoiler]And where is Barry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? What made them think not including one of the fans' favorite character in the game was a good idea?[/spoiler]

As a boss to fight, Nemesis actually turned out great. I love the changes they brought to its design, making it gradually more feral and keeping you on your toes when you think you've started to get used to it. Like many RE games before it, RE3 heavily encourages you to play it several times, but I don't really see a reason for me to do so. It doesn't have any additional scenarios like RE2's 4th Survivor (despite the original having a very popular Mercenaries mode that started a trend RE games have continued in most of the subsequent main series entries), its campaign is completely linear, its challenges are more frustrating then fun... all for a great price of $60! I actually enjoyed this game for the most part, but is it worth 60 bucks? absolutely not. I beat the game in 5 hours and I have a lot of issues with the game itself. To break it down, it's a 'mostly' good game on its own BUT a terrible remake.

Cut content, so much cut content. 3 entire areas cut from the original game, multiple enemy types and bosses removed. Choice events and alternate paths are entirely removed so the game has no replay value. Game literally has 2 puzzles, and one of them can barely be considered a puzzle. The awesome gore and dismemberment system from RE2R is nerfed. Entire story plot points are either removed or changed for no good reason including one of the most iconic scenes from the entire series being removed. 

Probably the biggest sin of RE3R is that Nemesis is just a joke, somehow Mr. X in RE2R is actually more threatening and better designed than Nemesis is in this game. It starts off well enough in the opening city section, he chases you around the level and its actually really cool. The opening city level is really open and feels like classic RE level design, but the problem is its the only part of the game that's like this and it's insanely short. For the rest of the game, the levels are much more linear and Nemesis is relegated to scripted events and cutscenes. The second half of the game feels closer to RE6 than it does original RE3.

Disregarding all the changes to the original that new people to the game won't even notice, there's still a lot of parts of this game that just aren't designed well. The level design is just not good, mainly in the second half of the game. The hospital section is such a boring slog to play through, mainly because it's much longer than the original game's version. The boss fights stand out as weaker parts of the game too, they're either extremely easy or confusing and don't make it clear how you're supposed to damage them.

I was really disappointed with the game, maybe my expectations were too high after the last 3 years of Capcom games being incredible, but I did have enough fun to where I would recommend it if it's on sale for about 20 bucks, but no more than that.

The game feels like it was rushed. I don't understand how RE2 remake could have been executed so well and then this game, on the same engine, and who was hyped up even more, completely pails in comparison to the original RE3. RE2 was stunning. The combat was a second thought in most encounters and the world was dripping with story. In RE3 however, you will NEVER run out of ammo unless you purposefully waste it and the survival elements take a back seat to the combat. The world is just... It's hard to explain. It doesn't have that same feeling that RE2's world had.


Lastly, the game barely gives you any chance to explore. You can't find the items used to open locked doors and containers until the game deems them necessary for the story; and at that point, nemesis is on you and he DOES NOT STOP until, again, the game decides he should. When he does stop, the game has forced you into the next chapter and you can't go back. Mr. X was a constant threat but it was possible to avoid him. Nemesis, however, knows your exact location at all times and you can't really put any distance between the two of you. Resident Evil is about exploration, not panicked mission rushing.

Anyways, with that all said, it's a good game. Pick it up when it's on sale, not for the full 60 bucks. Oh, and if you want to experience the story for yourself, have at it. Though, I'll tell you, you'll get the same satisfaction from watching someone else's play through for free.

[b]note: i've played through the original resident evil 3 multiple times, if you're new to the series and haven't played the originals then you might have an EXTREMELY different view and opinion on this game, which is okay! but i still want to talk about my personal experience with it, so don't necessarily let this scare you off from playing the game for yourself and building your own opinion on it![/b]

- - -
[b]positives[/b]
- - -

- improved anti-aliasing, in re2 SMAA would pixelate everything whereas FXAA/TAA would overly blur edges and textures. in the re3make you get a pretty decent mix of both
- character (re)designs, ignoring the fact that they've changed carlos and mikhail a bunch compared to their original
- tiny amount of backstory from re2, explaining the reasoning behind marvin telling leon "not to hesitate, uniform or not".
- i LOVED the into sequence, nemesis being introduced as this insanely strong, ruthless and relentless killing machine, continuously trying to wipe jill off the face of the earth

- - -
[b]negatives[/b]
- - -

- they just.. flat out removed almost ALL familiar areas from the original game 
- difficulty felt kind of unbalanced sometimes, e.g. zombies/beta-hunters take a good amount of hits while drain deimos and the final boss go down in a couple strikes
- story progression is entirely out of order or non-existent in regards to the original, it's like an entirely different game
- the fact that they entirely changed nemesis' design and function, especially from mutation stage 2 onward. he basically turns into a quadrupedal, dog/wolf like creature with no distinct facial features aside from his mouth and just.. loses any resemblance to "nemesis". this drastic change to his character alters the entire rest of the game since his methods of "pursuing"  and attacking you have changed as well. now it's like you were being followed by a big, agitated licker. [b]plus all of his encounters are scripted and easy to progress through.[/b]
resident evil 3 is, or rather was, about nemesis constantly being on your tail, clapping your cheeks with his tentacles or just flat out punching you in the face, following you almost everywhere you go and yelling monstrous ♥♥♥♥ at you. now almost all of his encounters are scripted, except for the one in the very beginning after you run into him in front of the donut shop. but even then he pulls weird ♥♥♥♥ from time to time like disappearing into thin air only to reappear at the next corner to knock you out? hm.
mr.x chasing you through the RPD in the re2make is based on RNG and AI mechanics and, comparing the two, mr.x feels WAY more like nemesis than the "nemesis" you get in the re3make, which is.. kind of really depressing lmao. his appearance surprises you the first time around but i don't think it'll scare me anymore in my future playthroughs.
idk, maybe i'm too attached to the original game, maybe i'm too attached to the original nemesis, but to me this giant change to the games very core feature is just a really big .. disappointment. 

- - -
[b]neutrals[/b]
- - -

- jill's personality and i guess the overall.. atmosphere? humor is really poorly placed and timed and overused (a personal favorite being mikhail calling nemesis a "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" before setting off the explosives on the train, breaking the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ vibe of that scene)
- them introducing two characters that A) didn't exist or B) had a very minor role in the original, A being dr. nathaniel bard and B being tyrell patrick (who appears in a single cutscene to get shot by nicholai in the original). especially the doctor felt really rushed and out of place.

Oh boy, I was SO waiting for this game. I rarely pre-order, but in this case I made an exception (because of how much I liked RE 2 Remake). And here I am now, after 5 hours of playing, completed game and thinking "Why did I pre-order this instead of waiting?".

Technically, the game is not a failure (would be a feat, honestly, to ♥♥♥♥ up a game based on RE 2). But, considering price, I was expecting a new chapter of RE series - with new mechanics, new features, etc. Unfortunately, this game feels more like a mod or new campaign inside RE 2.

Ok, let's go with pros first.
- Still same RE 2 gameplay - solid and comfortable mechanics. I was still having my share of fun during the game. But here's the catch - it's all thanks to RE 2. There is NOTHING new in RE 3 in terms of gameplay. We've seen all this in RE 2, but now with changed characters, locations and plot. That wouldn't be a problem if game  was priced at 30$, but it's a 60$ game, so it's only fair to evaluate it like one.
- Very good graphics, the game is still a perfect example of how you should make a remake of an old game. But, again, it's all thanks to RE 2 Remake, considering that RE 3 was created using same engine. I didn't see anything new in terms of graphics or models.
- Optimisation. My PC is becoming more and more old with each month, and I already got used to playing games on high instead of maximum settings and even this does not always garantee comfortable 60+ FPS (144 preferably). During my playthrough I haven't met a single bug, crash or FPS drop while playing on max settings with 100% resolution scale, 1920x1080.

And... That's basically everything GOOD I can say about the game. Now, not so good things:
- Nemesis. I'm not talking about his design. I, personally, found him looking quite good so no problems here. No, I'm talking about his "gameplay part". Obviosly, he's replacing Mr.X, but he's just two steps back in terms of several things. Mr.X was an actual enemy - he existed in game, actively walking around and looking for us, we could hear him, see him, he was always somewhere near and we had to walk and explore carefully. Nemesis? That ♥♥♥♥♥♥ just spawns out of nowhere in one of several scripted "entry points", chases us and, if we managed to escape, de-spawns. He is not actual part of the game world, so to speak, but more of a scripted trap and that's bad.
Also let's talk about location that you run from your enemy. In RE 2 you were playing with Mr. X in RCPD building - 3 floors, many rooms, usually several workarounds (ways to get from A to B) which means that you have to use your brain to plan your way. In RE 3, we play with Nemesis on RC streets. Of course one could think that developers will create a lot of alleys, buildings you can run inside and hide, with several entries, etc. No. The location is very poorly designed with several corridors that you can't avoid (good luck running through them if Nemesis spawns right before you, basically blocking your only way) and very small amount of buildings.
The actual fighting part. Mr.X was basically a big, bullet-proof zombie who punched you instead of grabbing. Nemesis is more complex, which is, of course, a good thing... If his new movements weren't so poorly implemented. He can: run and punch, grab and pull you with tentacle, throw a rock at you, scream. These are all new mechanics that I've seen him doing. Running: almost impossible to avoid, technically impossible in my case becase no matter how I tried I couldn't avoid it even once - I tried dodging, running away, hiding behind a corner and shooting. Nothing helped - dodge didn't save me, Nemesis just auto-aimed at me an managed to hit during or after dodge, running away didn't help becuse he's faster than you, hiding behind a orner is pointless becuase he somehow manages to turn almost 90 degrees without slowing or stopping and shooting didn't do anything to him. Grabbing and pulling? Annoying - yes, dangerous - no. It doesn't lower your health by itself and Nemesis couldn't hit me once after pulling towards himself. Thowing rocks - again, despite my dodges I always was hit, so, either you have to do it perfectly or they don't help. Screaming? Useless, doesn't do anything to you (escept, maybe pushing away). So, although he became more dangerous, he doesn't feel fair, considering his either very difficult to avoid or impossible to avoid attacks and the fact that he just spawns near you and immediately starts chasing you.
And last problem - the part where you run and hide from Nemesis ends very quickly, while RCPD in RE 2 was solid 30% of the game (maybe even more)
- Playtime. Only one campaign instead of two. Yes, it's longer than either Leon's or Claire's, but both of them? No. And, because of new character, new weapons, new scenes and new sub-plots these RE 2 campaigns felt different and worthwhile. Here we have only one campaign and basically nothing left to do after it, escept doing it again on different difficulty level, but there's no new content anymore.
- Weapons. What the hell? In RE 2 we had 11 weapons (excluding knifes, grenades, last boss weapons and special weapons that you open after completing of a game). Here? 7 (plus one of them is basically exact copy of another but with burst mode), again without "special" weapons that you open after completion of game, last boss weapon, and knifes/grenades.
- Boss battles. Every boss battle in RE 3 includes Nemesis, there are litirally no other bosses or special enemies/encounters. In RE 2 we had: fighting several stages of Birkin, several stages of Mr.X, some special parts of the game (like running from giant crocodile, hiding from Irons as little girl).
- RE Resistance. Now, I haven't played this game, so I'm not saying that it's bad (although, considering "mixed" reviews of an open beta in Steam, I'd say it's not especially good too). My problem with it is that CAPCOM do not allow to buy these games separately. I do not want to have it, I do not want to play it and I sure as hell do not want to pay for it. Let me buy RE 3 for 30$ or at least 45$, but nope. I have to pay for Resistance if I want to play third one. And of course I pay for it, it's quite silly to think that Resistance is a free game and RE 3 alone priced at 60$.

What I'm trying to say is: the game is not bad, it's to similar to RE 2 Remake with some little changes (some of which made game worse). But it's still a solid game by itself. But, considering that it's a 60$ game and the fact that RE 2 exists, I say it's a dissapointment.

Back when i was a little girl not only was I utterly forced by my parents to focus on my studies, but we were also, not very rich. We had enough money for a decent house, for daily living and some more, but not enough for things of luxury, such as was video game consoles back then. Furthermore, being a girl, I was expected to like dolls not video games. Therefore you can expect their surprise when I asked for a Playstation One back then. It took awhile before I was granted my wish, it was as a reward for being 'top 1' in my class back then, I still remember my first 2 games, they were 'Tekken 3' and 'Resident Evil 2'. I enjoyed both games, but enjoyed Resident Evil 2 more because I didn't have anyone to play with on Tekken 3. I never got to finish Resident Evil 2 no matter how much I loved it because ironically, despite my love for horror games, I'm scaredy cat. After some years passed I heard Resident Evil 3 was released and immediately bought it.

Resident Evil 3 for me was a step up from Resident Evil 2, and I loved Resident Evil 2! While Leon will always have a place in my heart, Jill Valentine, back then stole my admiration. Furthermore, because I was older, finishing the game was an easier ordeal for me than it was before. Sadly, despite my new found courage and fortitude, Nemesis made sure I'd run out of pants to pee in and eventually give up and leave another unfinished game, but I at least made it past the clock tower before letting my cousin finish it for me while I hide behind him.

When I heard about Resident Evil 3 remake, it was a 'must buy' for me. I couldn't help it. I wanted to see the RE3 Jill properly remade for the new generation of gaming consoles and the PC. Furthermore I saw this as a challenge from my younger self. I wanted to see, if I could finally finish what 10 year old me couldn't! Have I grown enough metaphorical balls to finally beat my demons? Well.... yes but....

You see, to compare this game to Resident Evil 3, is to compare shooting a gun, to shooting a bow. They're just too different. The original RE3, like its predecessor the original RE2, will choke you with its dreary atmosphere. Every time you open a door, you literally open a door into the unknown wherein you're not sure if you're going to be someone's dinner after the screen loads. There was a sense of foreboding, that maybe the saferoom you're currently in is the last saferoom you'll ever see before you load an older save file because you used your last ink ribbon. You don't feel any of these in the remake.

RE3 remake commits the sin, of not being very scary. When I played this game the only thing that worried me was the jump scares. Giving Jill a very powerful dodge and perfect dodge mechanic removed much of the suspense which I loved from the original. I get that Jill is a badass, but she's not a super human who should be able to do 'bullet time'! Furthermore, the original, and its predecessor RE2 remake, were very dark, but this game apart from very select places, was instead very bright, maybe because everything's on fire! Lastly, where is the gore?! Sure you get pierced by tentacles sometimes, and get some salami bitten off from your neck by zombies, but is this really all the gore you're willing to put in a zombie game? Even when you explode the head of zombies they only burst into boring chunks of meat and strawberry jam! Resident Evil, I do believe your audience is mature enough to watch a hunter decapitate someone's head off!

And then... there's nemesis. Call me crazy, but I always found Nemesis' original design to be incredibly intimidating. Mr. X from RE 2, the original not the remake, always scared the living daylights out of me. Imagine my surprise when Nemesis, something like Mr. X, but is able to move faster, use weapons, and make sinister voices especially "STAHHRS". The new Nemesis gave me that same feeling... until they turned him into a bloodborn boss. In the original, Nemesis transforms too, but that's only near the end. His transformation in this game feels too early and pushed the game even more towards the action shooter genre than survival horror. 

So the game wasn't very scary was it at least enjoyable? Mmm... yeah. I can't lie, as much as I didn't want the direction they pushed this game to, I still enjoyed playing it. Getting chased by Nemesis was a thrill until he became the Bloodstarved Beast at least and shooting felt fun, probably because of how accurate Jill's aim is. I know I complained about the dodge mechanic, but as soon as I accept that this wasn't 'survival horror' anymore, I began to appreciate it to the point that I became good at it.

Overall I can still recommend this game even though I dislike how unfaithful it is to the original. As a survival horror game, it's borderline mediocre, but as a game itself it was pretty good. I mean Jill is still very pretty and Miguel from Tekken made a cameo I guess that's a plus but I didn't like playing as him because... reasons. It was also very nice to see how some people we saw in RE2 remake got into the situation they were in like Mr. Kendo and that police guy. Yes, I think I can say that despite some disappointing choices, this game still made me smile. I just hope the next entry would be more faithful to its survival horror roots than this one is.

I'd like to preface this with a statement regarding all of the people who are bashing the Resident Evil 3 Remake.
Yes, it's got a bit of content cut out and areas missing that are present in the original RE3:Nemesis. Yes it's more action oriented compared to the Resident Evil 2 Remake.

That being said, Resident Evil 3 is a glorious game. The atmosphere, map, weapons, enemies, characters, and general feel of the game is great. It feels like a city that's been ravaged by the undead and left in ruins because people tried to evacuate without a second thought. 

Resident Evil 3 definitely is more action oriented than RE2R, however, if anyone has ever played the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis, you'd realize that it, too, was more action oriented over the previous release. This game is absolutely fantastic. 

Nemesis, though he looks quite different than the original, is just as menacing as he was in the OG game.
Jill is a great character. She's confident, strong, and well aware of her skills and experience in these situations. People want to bash her because she makes smart comments toward Carlos and other characters, but if you played the previous games with her in it, you'd know that she has firsthand experience in these situations and has been betrayed before so she plays it cautiously with who she trusts.

The entire game overall was great and very well put together, and is tied for my favorite RE game with the OG RE3 being alongside it. I'd definitely recommend playing it if you're not going to be expecting the dark, eerie, and horror-esque feeling that RE2R gave.    10/10 game.

[h1] RESIDENT EVIL 3: RESIDENT EVIL 2 2 - ELECTRIC BOOGALOO [/h1]

First of all, let me say I'm a huge fan of both Resident Evil as a saga, and Resident Evil 3 in particular.
Now, I have a few major complaints about the game, but also some kudos to give. There's a TL;DR at the end of this review.

[h1] GAMEPLAY [/h1]
I finished my first playthrough on Standard in 6:24 hours, taking my time to explore most areas as best as I could and making sure I missed as little as possible. My first playthrough on RE2 took me 19:00 hours. In comparison, RE3 felt underwhelming and rushed. Gameplay itself isn't bad, the core is solid as bedrock, but exploration was cut short and the city is basically a single hallway with a few turns. The game doesn't feel more action-packed, just more compressed and badly stitched together.
Gore and dismemberment have also been heavily toned down - this is in my opinion because the game wants to balance on the knife being indestructible, plus some zombies *need* to get up again after a while and apparently the devs thought playing smart and disabling threats was off limits.

Battling zombies isn't much different, except that now there is no point in aiming. Just shoot your biggest gun until they go down. Limbs disappear instantaneously after being chopped off and zombies have no ragdoll physics anymore, which is hella disappointing. And I don't care the arguments, this engine CAN handle all of that.
Battling Nemesis is honestly a bit meh. He does give rewards when beaten, but I managed to only get two as he stopped going down after that. Gave me a weapon mod ([spoiler]pistol's extended magazine[/spoiler]) and then 6 shotgun cartridges. Then, nothing. His encounters feel just like boss battles, and they're all too close one to the other. With no more exploration needed (nor allowed), you simply meet him time over time. He switches to other weapons and tactics, but he's just the same mean Nemesis. After a while, you just get bored of him.
In fact, most events here are just giant boss battles and nothing else. Plus, two boss battles are virtually the same in a different environment. I must say, they're not bad though.

Puzzles have been heavily cut as well. There are about four or five and they're all pretty easy. I wouldn't even call them puzzles really.

Other content that has been cut from the original includes a few bosses ([spoiler]big worm, Nemesis's second humanoid form[/spoiler]), most locations (half Raccoon City, the park, death factory), choices (you're forced on a rail, story never changes in the slightest) and Mercenaries mode. Yes, the iconic mode that was featured in every single major game since RE3 and that was literally born with said game. Yes, they removed it.

Finally, and I think this deserves its own spot, the ending of the Hospital section with Carlos is a bit cringey.

[h1]THE "NEW" CHARACTERS [/h1]
The new characters are honestly pretty good for me. They look different, but in a good way. More mature, more alive. Interactions feel real and the new facial expressions really seal the deal.
Only exception would be Nemesis, unfortunately. His design is a huge let down for me.

[h1] ENVIRONMENTS AND ART DIRECTION[/h1]
Here come the kudos, really. Every single area (except a few rooftops maybe) is exceptionally well made. The city feels credible, the desolation around you is visually brutal, the section at the Hospital really revitalizes the 1999 memories, and the endgame is... well. I won't say what it is, but it's lovely. Different than the original, but very well made.
Weapons feel good, character/npc models are well done and detailed (although it seemed like there were fewer zombie variants this time around), music is great. 

[h1] TL; DR [/h1]
Same core mechanics from RE2, but a lot of content was cut and what's left was heavily rearranged and altered to the point it feels either very different or very dull. The game has no choices, no Mercenaries, and lacks a few bosses.
The game feels a bit rushed on the story and gameplay side, while all that is visual and artistic is simply perfect.
In the end, Resident Evil 3 feels more like a censored, rushed, and weirdly stitched-together DLC than a standalone game. For what it offers, I wouldn't pay 60€ again for it; Capcom can still make this right though, with some (hopefully free) DLCs to add replayability.

I love the RE series and have since I was introduced to RE 3 on the Dreamcast. Overall the Pros outweigh the cons for this remake but it's funny because some of the cons could have been easily adjusted.

[b]Pros:[/b]

The intro: The entire first person intro where you go through Jill's apartment and look through stuff was not expected but so welcome. Seeing her wall with all of her notes on Umbrella and the Mansion were great to take time and look through. I also loved how they handled her PTSD from the mansion and how it affected her emotionally; some nice foreshadowing as well.

Jill Valentine: Everything about her from her now model, new costume and voice actress are all simply amazing. There was not a single moment where I groaned at anything they did with her character and her story. They hit the mark dead on here.

Carlos: Not corny like he was in the original which is great because it's 2020. The dialogue between Carlos and Chris is perfect and doesn't feel overdone.

The visuals: All I wanted was to explore more of Raccoon City and that's exactly what I got. The beginning section with Brad was fantastic. I wish more time in the game was spent here. The lighting, textures, costumes, facial animations, cutscenes, environments were all fantastic. The nods to the dresses in the window and the chalk drawing were a nice and subtle touch.
Nemesis design: I was look warm on his design at first but it grew on me. 
Cutscenes: Very well done. Great character design and great voice acting.

[b]The Cons:[/b]

Nemesis could have been better handled. I would have like more random encounters and hearing his theme blaring as he charges at you. Also when fighting him he could just box you in a corner and ropa-dope you which was more frustrating than scary. Some of his boss fights I flat out ran out of ammo because I wasn't sure what I was supposed to do. Made things more frustrating than anything.

Pacing: I wish they spend more time in the city portion of the game. Slow it down a little bit and let it breath. The first part of the game went by very fast. Some sections of the game felt very well done whereas others felt quick and kind of choppy.

Nikolai: Let his character slow burn a little bit. I feel this could have been done by fleshing out the city a bit more too. He doesn't need to twist his mustache in his introduction. How does he know Jill is unreliable exactly? They didn't set this up.

Too much ammo/supplies. Took away from the tension.

No puzzles except for two quick ones. No Water puzzle?

The entire electrical plant part of the game was AWFUL. The bugs were frustrating and not challenging. The "puzzle" was annoying and not challenging. Hate this part.

[b]The "Odd":[/b]

Jill handles a rail gun like an anime character? Oh no baby what is you doing???

No Gravedigger? Nani?

No clock tower? You only see it during one of the boss fights with Nemesis.

In general I enjoyed my time playing this. Not as good as RE2 as I assume that had more time in development. The stuff I liked they did really well and the stuff that was bad was so bad. 70/30 good to bad.

So i'd like to preface this review with the fact that I'm an avid fan of the series. I grew up playing the originals on PSX and honestly I was young and they scared the crap out of me while also giving me a sense of accomplishment when I beat them knowing I'd overcome my fears. I have the fondest memories of this series (before RE5-6).

That being said. 

Last year we got RE2 Remake, and I'm heavily biased likely on my opinion about that game as RE2 is by far my favorite resident evil. RE2 remake to me was a masterpiece, capturing everything in the original including the b side storylines perfectly. 

On to RE3 remake. I can't help but stop to shake my head in dissapointment. I can do this best by breaking it down further below.

1. The story is at times more loosely based on the original RE3 than true to heart.
That's not to say this is completely different from the original but it breaks character to try and focus on a more action oriented gameplay that may be entertaining to many but I craved a return to the original storyline. The clocktower is completely missing (a fairly big chunk of the original) and the city feels as if it really isn't all that large, honestly walking through the streets felt underwhelming, I should feel like I'm in the city trapped with zombies in every direction at the start of an outbreak. But I did not. And it felt small, with very little opportunity for exploration. Which leads to #2...

2. The entire game is on rails.
Now this is a pretty standard way of building games these days and I genuinely hate it. Even in open world games you usually are just walking to the next marker on the map. Compare to RE2, which is a police station that was built in an old museum. Sure you had objectives to complete and doors to open with keys, but you felt the need to explore every nook and cranny because it was just that interesting. in RE3 they pretty much have you going one direction the entire time. You can go off on some side areas but honestly you're on a disney theme park ride and the rails are always moving forward to the next scripted encounter with nemesis which leads to #3.

3. Nemesis isn't all that scary and the scripted encounters leave a lot to be desired.
It's pretty clear in the game when you're about to encounter nemesis again, and I wasn't surprised once by when he showed up. Which was a real surprise to me as this is one of the things that scared the ever living hell out of me in the original RE3. I can still remember being Jill sprinting through RPD to run from him. This is mostly an issue because of the disney park theme ride version of RE3 remake that we got. It's super clear when you hand me a bunch of supplies.. I'm about to fight nemesis. Not to mention that instead of him just popping on screen and attacking you most of the time you're made aware of him with a cutscene.

4. The game is short, and has almost 0 replayability.
RE2 Remake I probably put over 100 hours in doing every storyline getting S+, not because I wanted the cool infinite ammo weapons but because I loved the challenge and RPD felt like my own house where I know the combination to every lock and where I stored that key to the door I need to pass. Sure you can speed run to get S+ (and you have to do it in sub 2-3 hours) but my first playthrough of RE2 remake was well over 10 hours, because I explored until my eyes bled, I took in everything it was amazing. RE3 remake the maps are so ridiculously small it barely feels like a fully developed game. It even reuses RPD from RE2 so it's not like they had to do that much work considering a fourth of the game played as carlos is in a fraction of RPD. This whole argument leads to my fourth point.

4. No mercenaries mode.
Do I need to even go into detail here? This mode rocked and I looked forward to doing it again on current gen. (and it would have given the game some semblance of replayability.

Honestly there are many reasons why this game left me feeling empty when I saw the credits roll by. But These were some of my top.

I can say with an unprovable certainty that this was originally just DLC for REmake2
and at some point they decided to spin it off into its own $60 product. From the beginning the game wastes no time introducing you to anything at all and just assumes you know the ins and outs of how the game works. In their haste they took what would have been the first 30-45 minutes of the original games run time and showed it as the first 5 minutes of this game with a cutscene. They even made a model of Dario and his trailer he hides in at the beginning of OgRe3 and you never go back nor explore it ever again. The real gameplay takes place at what would probably be the 25% mark of the original game and the pace just doesnt slow down from there. Its a chopped down truncated version of RE3 that misses out on alot of stuff but was made on the premise that we would be seeing more of Raccoon city than before. Instead we get one area that is an amalgamation of 3 from the original game and then a truncated romp through reused assets from REmake2 before jumping to the hospital then blink and you're in another Umbrella Lab. There was also rumors that the Nemesis would be faster and deadlier than Mr. X but he's actually worse as there are only 4 times you encounter him outside of boss fights and each time he can be downed if you've been surveying your environment and have the obscene amount of ammo thats lying around. In the original game there was also cut and dry areas where he would or would not go but fighting him had rewards, weapons you couldnt even get in the game without downing him, or item management savers like a case that could hold 3 first aid sprays in one slot. In this besides two moderately better attachments for your base pistol and some ammo. Thats it, its as if production got pulled half way through finishing the game and they threw it out hoping to cash in on the name sake. When he does show up, with the exception of one showing its highly scripted. I still get the shakes remember playing OgRe3 and having a pucker moment from him yelling "STARS!" before charging me out of nowhere but thats lost in this game. Its too streamlined for its own good.

 The only positive notes I can say about this is that it looks good, with the exception of the Zombies which are copied directly from 2 but lost alot of their animations. The rest of the character models are great and as photo realistic as the ones in REmake2 were. Nemesis looks better than every now wrapped in plastic with flesh jutting out as opposed to the leather bdsm outfit he had originally. Also the Dodge system that was often ignored and never worked like it should in OgRe3 actually works better in this game. However I just ended up using it more like a Dark Souls roll to try and create distance as opposed to the bullet time parry its designed to be. Iam willing to admit that might just be my lack of skill but I was able to get Carlo's parry down and doing so makes the Hunters he encounters a joke. In a better time this would have been a $30 expansion pack for Remake2 or alternatively given more time to actually add everything with the love and care that was put in to REmake2. Unfortunately this leaves us at a place where RE1 and RE2 have basically been replaced by their remakes as the best way to play that game but RE3 as usual is just left in this weird miasma where the Original Version is still going to be the best way to experience Jills Last escape. I hope going forward Capcom realizes they cant rush these remakes and if its supposed to just be DLC or an expansion leave it be. God willing they do not try to remake Re4. That would be a complete travesty akin to Star Wars Special editions. Why tamper with something thats already great and will be hard pressed to improve upon? But if you're a fan of Resident Evil like me you've already bought it and are living the same nightmare as I am. If you havent wait for it to go on sale before you give this a shot.

Resident Evil 3 is a tough game to review simply because of the $60 price tag. On one hand, the game looks, feels, and sounds phenomenal due to a much needed upgrade from the original 1999 title. On the other, it's realistically a 4-6 hour game with not a whole lot to explore which is what most people are complaining about. So naturally, this leaves the community very divided in whether or not it deserves high praise or if it should be chastised for its flaws.

Personally, I had a lot of fun with the game. I've been a big fan of the Resident Evil series since I was a kid and these last few titles (RE7, RE2 Remake, and now RE3 Remake) have made me ecstatic about the future of this franchise. The combat feels smooth and responsive, the game looks and sounds phenomenal, and the engine it runs on is a very well optimized one. People complained about cut content like the Clock Tower or the Gravedigger stuff which is understandable but honestly the game flows pretty well without that stuff. Would I have liked to see it? Yes. Am I upset that it's not in there? No. I get why people would be upset but like I said, I just feel like it doesn't take away from the rest of the experience.

Nemesis is great. Some people were weary about the design changes to him, but I think he looks great in game! The sections he is in are fun and get the blood pumping, especially in the first few chase sequences. The boss fights with him are also fairly well done, with the last two being my favourite, with unique mechanics and not just a "shoot him until he is dead" kinda boss fight. Some minor complaints I have about Nemesis are the combos he can do, whether it's while roaming or in a boss fight, where you just can't do anything. It's not fun to get hit to the floor and by the time you get back up you literally cannot react to him hitting you again, resulting in either death or being put into Danger. 

Talking about the two main characters, Jill and Carlos, I gotta say I love em more here than I do in the OG title. Jill is characterized very well, with her PTSD from the mansion incident, the paranoia of being infected from said incident, and her complete distrust of anything and anyone Umbrella. She's also a complete badass from start to finish and this game easily put her in my top 3 characters in the franchise. She's very straightforward and experienced when you compare her to someone like RE2 Remake Leon. Carlos is also a very interesting character with his cocky but caring attitude, even in dire situations. His interactions with Jill feel real and make the characters actually feel like real people, something I absolutely love about this game. 

Overall, I love the game but I do disagree with the $60 dollar price tag. If you're hesitant on getting this game because of the length of the game then I would say wait for a sale ($40 or less), but if you're a big fan of the series and plan on doing multiple playthroughs to unlock all the collectibles then I would say get it whenever you want and enjoy the game!

Last year when Resident Evil 2 remake released and I put a great deal of hours into it and was greatly pleased. It wasn't a perfect reboot but it was done well enough that I had great faith and expectations for further projects Capcom would do. I know this game was only a matter of time, perhaps not so soon. When I heard it was a year apart I thought they were already working on it alongside RE2. I hoped it would not have been the alternative. With regret this game was disappointing on more fronts than not. If I had to summarize it I'd call it Resident Evil 3: Abridged. 

Mind the game length isn't something that is necessarily a big deal.  A single scenario in RE2 was fairly short, so I didn't mind that. However the scope and scale of this game were toned town in comparison to the original material to quite an extent. So let me explain a bit.

First off the streets of Racoon city were rather abridged in comparison to the original. Which I found baffling honestly because it wasn't that long, however here is how this works. In original the city was split into downtown and uptown. Each section had many different areas of interest. You had to go through all of them, figure out puzzles, which let you from one end of the city to the other. You had a great deal to do and figure out. When you knew where to go and what to do it was fairly quick, but still a good deal of work. Here...it's borderline linear. You get a hilighted objective, and generally one right way to go. There is not much exploring, not many puzzles to figure out, which item is for what and so forth. This holds true for the whole game. Everything is linear, at most you explore few close rooms and get an item. RE2 while similar on that end at least had a large RPD, with many doors, keys and routes to set it aside from it. This does not. All picks, upgrade, everything is neatly along the way. The exploration for extra resources is minimal and not as rewarding. In the city there are two extra things, lockpick items and the puzzle clock at the beginning. That's it.

Next is the locations. They cover most of them, not all. Shame since they cut out a great deal, and some are literally just one small hallway section or such. However bigger affront is that they divided the game between Jill segments and Carlos segments. This means some locations that you visited as Jill, you now only visit as Carlos. His gear is underwhelming and the game sort of pushed it more towards action oriented approach. Which is drastically different from trying to scavenge resources, not kill stuff, avoid, being frugal and careful. On hardcore difficulty Carlos has a RE4 type cabin section where the game gives you couple HUNDRED assault rifle ammo, as you mow down dozens of zombies, hunters and such. Just...why? The game isn't even designed for this sort of thing, since the large damage variance still works how it did in RE2 remake. The upgrades you find for Carlos don't transfer over to Jill, and you can't use Jill's items. Seriously, it would have been better if Carlos had a one off short segment similar to how Ada or Sherry had in RE2. Not split the game up like this. There are some sections I REALLY was looking forward to going to. It ended up a Carlos segment...That was like equivalent to one of those memes where a kid gets 2 playstation 2 for christmas instead of a PS4.

Then there is Nemesis. Ok he's pretty neat. The way they designed him is great, and I loved the sense of this hulk hounding you through city streets...Except the city portion of the game is so short. You see this guy maybe 4-5 times during that section. Much like original game's hard mode he drops loot when downed. Which is great! At first... I'll spoil this a little, he has a total of 4 drops. Two of them are ammo. The other two are weapon mods. No new weapons, no first aid box, no assault rifle...Incredibly underwhelming, also consider you can down him with ONE hand grenade on hardcore difficulty. Just one. In original you had to consider what to use, how to go about it, which choice to take when you faced him.  I was really looking forward to having lots of guns in the game...but wish was squashed. When you finish the campaign you earn points you can spend in a shop. There are some guns you can get in the shop, but they are again fairly lackluster. No 1887...

Then there are resources. This is all over the place. I think I have to play nightmare and inferno difficulty to get a better sense of it, but overall the game on hardcore showered you with ammo and gunpowder. Speaking of gunpowder, why didn't they just keep the old system... You have 4 different types of gunpowder, instead of two basic ones then make your own combinations. There is also no enhanced ammo either. If there is something original game let me have is various different combat options. Here it's all the same. It's like Playing RE2's Leon with added grenade launcher. The dodge mechanic is great, and some monsters really nearly require it, but that isn't enough.

On plus side, monsters and zombies are cool. Some scenery is really great. I loved the look of the hospital and some street portions. I liked most of the monsters and such, except for the albino zombie. You had few moments where you felt good, about being economical with an encounter, with all the zombies, all these encounters, monsters and such. Much like you did in RE2, but then it's over, game resets and you go to a new location. Many sections were frankly too short, less pronounced and because of it poorly balanced. I hope top difficulties will be more interesting, but they won't solve the problem how shallow the entire campaign feels.

Post game content? There really isn't any. Outside of buying stuff in the shop for your next runs (I like that) and harder difficulties, but that isn't enough. There is no mercenaries, and I sure as ♥♥♥♥ did not buy this game to play multiplayer. I never play this series for MP. I want a solid campaign. Instead I got an abridged campaign with hints of how this could have been a fantastic game. Story aside, it's the standard RE fare nonsense. Performance aside, it ranges from good to comic book villain laughable.  The actual core of the game is mediocre. It's missing the complex nature of survival horror resource management and puzzles, that while toned down were fairly rooted in the last remake.

Price? Yeah if you haven't gotten the tone from what I've been saying I certainly do NOT approve of the full price tag for this. At most I would have paid 2/3 for, and even then I'd expect more. 

Sadly this isn't a remake I wished they made. Yes that is my opinion, but frankly for the amount you get that you pay for is quite disrespectful. This is as I've been saying Resident Evil 3: Abridged. It is filled with moment to moment gimmicks, that are introduced then thrown away. Nemesis while awesome, is only there for the short time you spend in the city, after that it's all scripted events. The lack of proper rewards for risk, big enough scope, more puzzle solving, larger areas and maps, more interlaced environments, guns and options hold it down from being even halfway decent game I would have accepted. Don't waste your money. Get it on a sale when it's a fraction of the price if you loved the last remake. Otherwise move on. There are better things to play.

[h1]Resident Evil 3 (2020) Review[/h1]

I revisited this reimagining on Linux immediately after finishing 2019's [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] to see how the two pair as a duology. While the technical foundation is identical, the experience is a drastic departure. It replaces the slow burn dread of the previous entry with a high octane sprint through a neon soaked Raccoon City. 

The RE Engine remains an achievement, delivering exceptional performance and photorealistic visuals. However, the transition from survival horror to a linear action piece comes at a significant cost to the scope and soul of the original 1999 classic. It is a polished experience, but it feels more like an expansive DLC than a full numbered entry.

[h2]The Good[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Technical Performance[/b]: The game is incredibly well optimized for PC. On Linux using the DX11 branch, I averaged 240 FPS with zero stability issues.
[*] [b]Visual Identity[/b]: Downtown Raccoon City looks stunning. The use of vibrant neon signs, burning wreckage, and dynamic lighting creates a more immediate sense of chaos than the RPD.
[*] [b]Refined Combat[/b]: The inclusion of the emergency dodge mechanic adds a layer of skill mastery to the gunplay. Timing a perfect dodge to slow down time for a counter shot feels rewarding.
[*] [b]Meta-Game Replayability[/b]: The Extra Shop and point buy system provide a better incentive for multiple runs than the scenarios in RE2. Unlocking items like the Hot Dogger adds a fun, arcade like quality to repeat playthroughs.
[*] [b]Hunter Redesign[/b]: The Hunters are a standout. They are genuinely menacing and serve as a lethal threat that lives up to their reputation.
[/list]

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Hollowed Out Content[/b]: The removal of iconic locations like the Clock Tower, Park, and Dead Factory is a massive disappointment. Raccoon City feels small and truncated rather than sprawling.
[*] [b]Scripted Stalking[/b]: Nemesis fails to live up to the standard set by Mr. X. His appearances are largely restricted to cinematic chases and specific trigger zones, removing the tension of a persistent, roaming threat.
[*] [b]Reduced Bestiary[/b]: The omission of spiders, crows, brain suckers, and the Grave Digger boss fight thins the mechanical variety and creature feature appeal of the original.
[*] [b]Linearity[/b]: By removing the Live Selection system and branching paths, the game loses the player agency that made the 1999 version so memorable.
[*] [b]Character Writing[/b]: While Jill’s design is great, the script often confuses being a hardened survivor with being perpetually abrasive. Her portrayal lacks the layered tension found in her original depiction.
[/list]

[h2]Summary[/h2]
Resident Evil 3 (2020) is a technical powerhouse that highlights the conflict between modern polish and legacy depth. The core mechanics are responsive and the 200 FPS performance on Linux makes for a smooth ride, but the amount of content lost to achieve this pacing is difficult to justify. It lacks the structural depth and environmental scale of the 2002 remake or 2019 reimagining. It is a fun, short burst of action, but it sits well below the standard of the series' best reimaginings. This game is best suited as a sale item, not a full price purchase.

Let’s get this out of the way first—if you were a fan of Resident Evil 3 (1999) or any of its various ported releases—you will be very disappointed. If you were a fan of the RE2 remake, you will also be disappointed. RE3 remake demonstrates yet again that Capcom still hasn’t resolved the franchise’s almost two decade identity crisis. Capcom doesn’t know what it wants RE to be and this latest release appears to be a rushed, mandatory pitstop before the inevitable RE4 remake. In an effort to reconcile its roots of a genre-defining, survival-horror franchise with generic; action-packed explosion-fests, Capcom has done the original game and its fans a disservice.

Others have gone into great detail about the differences between the original and the remake, so I won’t rehash that. I will simply reiterate that there is a lot of missing content and questionable story changes with no clear explanation except that the game was rushed, Capcom was preoccupied with Resistance, and the dev team had no coherent direction. Remakes should build upon and enhance the original, not gut it and replace it with laughable quasi-quick time events. RE2 remake, to a large extent, balanced this well with enjoyable gameplay, tight quarters, and an unnerving atmosphere. I couldn’t remember the last time I had enjoyed a RE game so much. Even though the original RE3 took place in the same sprawling city; Raccoon City felt small and there was always tension, fear, and dread with hoards of zombies and the Nemesis’ unrelenting pursuit. Everything that was great about the original or the RE2 remake is absent. There is no tension with a game that is constantly pushing you forward, almost begging you to complete the game as soon as possible to get to the DLC and prepare for the RE4 remake.

The way to ensure the longevity and continued success of a series is by listening to loyal fans while broadening the base. This doesn’t mean sacrificing the core RE recipe. It doesn’t mean retroactively rewriting RE’s legacy. RE3 remake’s problem is that it’s a generic action game with pretty graphics and few redeeming qualities. Core RE is nowhere to be found. If at the very least the game paid proper tribute to the original, there would be something there. But the RE3 remake will not be iconic or have the longevity and legacy of the original—it will be forgotten and at a steep discount within a year. Maybe that’s when you should pick it up.

Unfortunately, Resident Evil 3 is a rather weak sequel to the success of 2. Given that I was not rushing, knew nothing about the game going in and not even a particularly good RE player, I still managed to complete the campaign in 5 hours with little difficulty on the Standard difficulty. 

In terms of story, there is very little. You essentially are going from point to point as the plot demands. There is little to no character development, both Jill and Carlos start as fairly well trained and powerful characters so unlike Leon and Claire, they do not develop their skill set or views as the game goes on. Secondary characters are given no screen time at all so making them forgettable and their deaths or betrayals lack any impact. Most of the dialogue in the game is not there to give you an insight of characters or explore the world, each line of dialogue is essentially just there to advance the plot. "Alright, I am here, Carlos." "Great Jill, now go there." 

You play as Jill Valentine, who is woefully underdeveloped and Carlos who is equally underdeveloped and somehow less interesting. You don't get to choose who to play either, you play a section as Jill, then one as Carlos, then Jill again, then Carlos, then Jill. Carlos' sections are short and feel tacked on, also he's armed with a machine gun that'll kill most things easily making his sections boringly easy. Jill's sections are more fleshed out and her weapon choice is greater, but she is just not presented as an engaging character leaving her sections feeling that slight bit hollow.

In terms of mechanics, the game plays almost exactly like RE2 with the exception of Grenades, knives and flash bangs now being on use only as opposed to also being able to be used as a defence weapon, instead, Jill has a dodge ability and Carlos an interrupting should bash. 

Nemesis, the big bad of the game, becomes laughable very quickly, with easy to dodge attacks, gimmick based boss fights and becomes increasingly ridiculous each time you fight him, and I mean ridiculous in appearance, scale and how easy it is to beat him. He is not particularly intimidating, certainly no Mr X, or interesting. When he's off screen you forget about him, when he returns, you sigh. 

Overall a weak game that might have served as a decent DLC for RE2 or a game that should be around the £25 mark. £49.99 for barely five hours playtime with no real replayability (lacks any additional/side content and has no B route). Also, no puzzles for some reason, save I think one puzzle at the end which is basically just "Line up three dials". 

Just not worth the money and even at a lower price, not a great game.

Okay I wish there was a "so so" option or a "Meh" because Resident Evil 3 has got some good and bad. Now a lot of the negative reviews I read, are saying that it isn't faithful to the original and I say... Grow the ♥♥♥♥ up. Remake doesn't mean new carbon copy, and I feel fortunate enough that the only Resident Evil game I have played have been the RE2 remake and the RE3 remake. So I base this game on one thing alone, the game. The actual game itself, and nothing more. The only thing I can compare it to is RE2 Remake (which is one of my all time favorite games of all time), so I have a fairly unbiased review. 

So jumping into the game, how is it? The best way I could describe it is, a giant movie with some gameplay. It felt like most of the game was cut scene after cut scene, occasional gameplay, and back to cut scenes.

You can continue to read, if you want a more in depth review of the game... Still here? Good.

The Best Parts Of This Game:

1. The game introduces a new roll mechanic, which makes you think more when approaching an enemy. I think it was a really good thing to add in, since RE2 was just move, shoot, throw something, knife, or run and pray.
2. This game's acting, writing, and dialogue are all around superior then RE2's cringy dialogue, and sit-com jokes from Leon or Claire.
3. Carlos is amazing, and his chemisty with Jill is on point. It's just nice to watch them banter back and forth. When you play him also the best part of the game. 
4. The theme of hopelessness, fear, exhaustion, and anguish is portrayed perfectly. Jill looks, sounds, acts, and feels like she is desperately trying to survive by running away from this monster. Leon seems to be more annoyed by Mr. X (granted Nemisis is more dangerous), but still. 
5. The references to RE2 were cute, don't deny it.

The Worst Parts Of This Game:

1. Nemisis.... Yeah that's probably gonna sting. Look I think Nemisis is cool, and I loved each boss fight except for the one near the bridge. But in the very beginning when you're trying to escape, he can hit you down, and as you are trying to get up he can hit you again instantly killing you. Does this mean it is hard? No, this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! If Mr. X hit you in RE2, you had a reasonable grace period to get up and run or fight back. This doesn't happen in RE3!!!! I died over 4 times in the beginning of the game, because of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic. It could be a bug, but it is hardcore BS. It also happens in one of the boss fights, but whatever.
2. Action over Horror. Resident Evil is a horror series with some action, and the most succesful RE games have been *gasp* horror and not action. RE1, 2, 3, 4, and 7 were all pretty horror ridden games. This is an action movie with some jump scares. You know how you create horror? Tension, and enviorment! What's scary about Raccoon City? Some zombies, a big scary dude with weapons, and some dogs. That's not horror! Here look at RE2; you're in a building for the first time, no idea what's behind the corner. It's cramped, dark, uneasy, and you hear little noises that set you on edge. RE3 has none of that EXCEPT when you're in the police station as Carlos, but you already know what to expect, so it isn't that scary anymore is it?
3. Jill ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Valentine... I know a lot of people like Jill, a lot. Personally, I hate her. She is a cocky, stuck-up, touch ♥♥♥♥♥ one moment and the next she is selfless, heroic, kind, and scared. I don't hate how she looks, or her general character... I hate how her tone gets bounced around so much. You could classify it as "character development", but it doesn't really do it for me. Carlos has a much better arc in this game.
4. The Shop... I gotta be honest, this one is personal... WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥!!!??? So if you haven't beaten the game or bought it let me clue you in. So after you beat the game, you unlock The Shop where you can use these points that you have collected from playing the game to spend on in game items like Jill's Stars outfit and Carlos's gun. Seems fine? No! No it isn't fine! Because you can also buy advantages to the game, so it isn't as cheap as the devs made it to be. And if you want something really good, or something you have to replay the game to get more points. You know what this if ♥♥♥♥♥♥ called?! GRINDING! I SHOULD NOT HAVE TO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GRIND FOR SPECIAL ADVANTAGES! Make me work for it, like actually work for it! In RE2 if you wanted the infinite supplies, you had to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ earn it by being faster, and smarter. Not this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, where you just replay the game! Also the game is unfair enough as it is, I don't wanna try and get an S rank or try on Hardcore. ♥♥♥♥ that! Why would I waste my time on special ♥♥♥♥ to make the game more balanced, when you could have made it balanced in the first place!
5. The Knife. The Knife is useless, you can't stop getting bit, you just get bit. The knife is useless. What the ♥♥♥♥, I don't have enough anger in me to write the rest. But what the hell?

Do I personally recommend this game? No, not for the average person.
Do I recommend this game amongst Resident Evil fans who want to have 60% fun and 40% anger? Yes

Despite all those negatives, I still like this game. It's okay to critique something you like, and RE2 is a great game, but it could've had the roll mechanic, it could've had better writing, and it could've fixed Claire's eyes. Will I replay Resident Evil 3, yes. There is a good game in here, it just takes longer to find.

Wait for it to be on sale tho.

For someone who only ever played the original Resident Evil on the Playstation and who thoroughly enjoyed RE2 Remake... It's a thumbs down for me. It's just not worth the price given the reuse of content from Resident Evil 2, the very short levels and utterly pointless items in the game that make this feel more like it was severely condensed in scope compared to where it was originally going to be.

I did enjoy it. However I did feel like it was rushed and more DLC territory than full on standalone territory.

It took me five and a half hours on standard difficulty, collecting everything(Bar the last two boss fight areas), unlocking everything and doing all the back tracking, dying only five times(Due to the boss mechanics where Nemesis would stun lock you toward the end). It really did not last long what so ever. A lot seemed to be missing like, a lot of the transitions from location to location where you just appear at the next area like when you get to the hospital. They could have had something in between that and could have had you play as Carlos until you found Jill. Instead you're left with plain text saying "Roughly half a day later." and poof! Cutscene -- Carlos comes across Jill and they both end up at the hospital.

Then the sheer amount of reused assets and levels from RE2 Remake was embarrassing. The only content that was new was the opening area in the streets, the power plant and the hospital, all of which were very short and very small levels. The power plant lasted roughly 10minutes to go through because all you did was run and gun and activate three or four switches and that was it. As soon as Jill gets infected you literally eat a green herb and that's the last you see of that infection.

Honestly, it was very, very limited in scope, the content wasn't really there and the items you get are practically just handed to you not to mention key items are pretty much right beside where you need the them to unlock something with the exception of the lockpick not to mention when you get the lockpick you have to backtrack for 5minutes through a freshly cleared area to unlock everything you missed early in the game(Yep). It begs the question as to why they didn't just give you the lockpick earlier?

The bolt cutters was utterly pointless. You have it for two minutes before you throw it away. My mind is blown as to why it was even put in the game given how it's only used for three chain locks that are less than a minute away from each other.

Could have been better, wasn't terrible but wasn't worth full price. RE2 was kind of a short game on a first playthrough but there was replay value there in how the levels played out and a few different areas depending on the character you play plus this was all new textures, levels on an updated engine telling the story in modern gameplay which made it worth the price.

On the other hand you have RE3 which is reused assets, incredibly short and there's only replay value for those who really have nothing else to do other than play the same game over and over. Replay value in RE3 is playing the same campaign on a higher difficulty and spending points to unlock stuff to make early game easier like unlocking better weapons with infinite ammo. Then you have some pointless unlocks in the shop like the bolt cutters or the picklock, both of which you get early on and would only want for about three or four doors/cases before you would have gotten those items anyway, all in all probably wasting, collectively, only five minutes of your time backtracking -- and even this is pointless for speed runners because they will most likely speed run from a fresh file.

Get it on sale or if you really love Resident Evil. This game is enjoyable but Resident Evil 3 deserved far better and something truer to the original and it's story.

Oh, and entire areas are out of sequence and completely cut in this remake compared to the original(Like Carlos going to RPD instead of Jill... for reasons???). The game was rushed.

Ok...what the hell happened?

Since the moment this game was announced, something was fishy about it, game was outsourced to another studio, it was coming out in barely 4 months, and Capcom did little to no promotion for it...plus, this came in a pack with another game (REsistance) for $60?
Since day one this looked like DLC for REmake 2 that they were selling like a full game just to make REsistance (a game nobody asked for and still nobody cares for) more appealing...well, not only is pretty clear that was the case, even expecting that, the game is still dissapointing.
Good things first; the game is incredible well optimized, it runs better than REmake 2 despite looking better and having a lot more stuff on screen at some points, the RE Engine is a work of marvel.
And the dodge mechanic actually works, unlike in the original game.
And the good things stop there.
On your first playthrough, you will beat the game in around 5-6 hours, the game is really, really short, despite having a lot of padding after you reach halfway of the story.
The game has no extras modes. 21 years ago, the original game had "The Mercenaries", which was not only an incerdible adicting mini-game, it started a tradition that carried on to RE4, RE5, and RE6...not present here.
Original game had a "choices" system, which changed item locations and cutscenes, which made you want to replay the game several times...these "choices" are not present in the remake.
The original game had multiple endings...this game only has one ending.
You know what this game has? scripted sequences, lots of them. You know which type, the Uncharted type, the "hold forward until the next cutscene plays" type.
Also, there are some sequences where you have to heal yourself from damage received on a cutscene...that's right, the game sometimes decides that you need to heal yourself because it wanted to, and this is a constant through the game, it takes control away from you.
A lot of locations were cut from the game, some of which are iconic locations in the entire Resident Evil franchise, but you know what they added in place of them? generic sewer and laboratory sections, re-using assets from REmake 2, of course.
Puzzles? there are only two puzzles in the entire game. Yeah, you read that right, two.
Poor Nemesis despite being on the cover of the game, the title screen, and well, being the name of the game, is barely in it, he is less in this than Mr X was in REmake 2.
What's worse, 90% of the interactions with him are (terrible) boss fights, and scripted sequences.
And speaking of boss fights, aside from three encounters with Nemesis, the game has no bosses. None.
The story was butchered, same with the characters. 
Poor Jill went from being the nicest and most calm person in the franchise to being mean towards most people, and saying the F-word every 5 seconds (because as we saw in REmake 2, in Japan they must thing the F-word is the only word in the english language).
Nicholai was turned into a cartoon villain, Carlos, while not goofy as he was in the original game, is now pretty bland (he is basically latino Chris Redfield), and Brad...he is barely in the game, his personality is the complete oposite than in the original games (1 and 3), and his most memorable scene in the franchise (you know which one) is not even present in this game.
Also, developers kept saying again and again that now Jill was going to be a "strong female protagonist", because they felt ashamed of how she was sexualized in the original game...well, they changed her design, but the game has a lot of ass-shots (A LOT), and Jill keeps getting in situations that look straight out some weird hentai parody, I'm not kidding, not only they keep abusing of Nemesis using his tentacles on her, there is an enemy whose gimmick is to literally mouth-rape her...I know japanese folks like this kind of stuff, but in the west these things are uncomfortable to see, especially considering what the studio kept saying about Jill before the game came out.
And lastly, all the problems that were present in REmake 2 (like zombies taking 20 bullets to the head to go down) are also present in this game, except that REmake 2 could get away with it because it was good, but this game doesnt have that luxury...
In its best moments, it feels like a mix of REmake 2 and RE6 (yes, QTEs are back...for some reason).
So, again I must ask myself, what the hell happened? 

Unless you really liked the REsistance beta, stay away from this mess, in no shape or form is it worth $60 dollars.
