I'm going to put the TL;DR right at the start. On it's own merits it is a very fun game and I do recommend it. If you enjoy Resident Evil at all you'll have a great time; even though I think the RE2 remake was a little better. Go into options and change the in-game actions from rapid press to Hold. You'll save yourself and your equipment some stress; you're welcome. The rest of this review will talk about aspects of the game in more depth and will contain spoilers so if you have not played the game yet I recommend stopping here.











To begin, I had fun; this is an enjoyable game and I plan to play it a lot more; that said after the excellent Resident Evil 2 Remake, it was hard not to notice a lot of design flaws and over all bad decisions in the development of this game. Most of these will be nitpicks to be honest but it simply feel like they went a step backwards with the design of 3 when compared to 2.

 First and foremost, the Knife is indestructible again; Capcom was happy to go on press releases about this and how knife-only runs were going to be possible (After the last boss I question this very idea, will be interesting to see who figures out a knife-only method for that.), but at the same time they made the knife incredibly weak again. Capcom seems to have a love/hate relationship with the knife in Resident Evil games, whereas in One, RE2 Remake, 4 for example the knife is incredibly valuable, reliable, and strong. Where as in other installments the knife is as useful for stopping a zombie as using your words. RE3 Remake is the latter. Enemies are quick in this game and you get a fantastic dodge mechanic to help evade them, but the knife takes a tremendous amount of hits to kill, even after shooting zombies several times to knock them down, that it just lacks value. I should state I was playing on the Hardcore difficulty and majority of the game I questioned why I bothered to keep the knife with me. I used it against some of the bosses as well and while it could conserve some ammo, it made the fights take significantly longer and really I was never in a position where I felt I was truly about to run out of bullets. It's best use was killing zombies after I shot their leg off since they couldn't stand again; if you try to knife a zombie that can still stand be warned, all the zombies in this game are secretly Ninjas and even if you stand at their feet while they're face down by the time they get to knee height they will do a lightning fast 180, jump up grab that should not be possible. Best use of the knife so far is with Carlos, since he shoulder rams instead of dodges you can just repeatedly knock a zombie down over and over with knife swipes in between.

Blue herbs are gone, only Green and Red remain but they did get rid of Poison effects as well with one exception. Early in the game you'll encounter enemies that can put a parasite in you, that will kill you over time and can only be removed by consuming a green herb. While this is a one time area thankfully I must say it was pretty ♥♥♥♥ to introduce this area by literally making you get a parasite in a cut scene beyond your control so you are obligated to waste a green herb. Granted they have a green herb right at that location; but I still have to question putting unavoidable attacks into a cut scene that forces you to use a healing item. This goes rather hand in hand with some bad level design where in some areas enemies are right on the other side of doors, but can't cross them on their own. So you end up in these situations where opening a door leads you to getting immediately assaulted, knocked back, and the door closes again. The Treatment room in the Hospital is notoriously bad about this where it contains two Hunter Betas with one poised immediately at the door resulting in a clown fiesta. If the door so much as begins to close it puts up an invisible wall as well. I lost grenades trying to open the door and throw one in only to not be able to throw the grenade until I recovered from the hit stagger, the door begins to close, and even though I throw the grenade at open space it just bounces off the air back into the room with me, blowing up and not hurting the enemies.

Self-defense weapons as a whole are gone. Grenades, flashbangs, and the knife are all in the game but you are no longer prompted to use them to protect yourself as a secondary weapon, they get treated as your primary weapon like your guns. This is somewhat off-set by the dodge mechanic in the game since with practice you can avoid getting grabbed altogether; but some of the zombies as mentioned above will pull off some ridiculous ninja speed grabs that will surprise you throughout the game which just makes the dodge mechanic feel lackluster compared to a self-defense knife. While talking about this I should mention when you get grabbed and you're prompted to press (or hold if you changed the settings in options) a button, you do this to reduce the damage you're about to take; no matter how hard you mash you won't avoid damage, just shakes off the zombie faster so you take less. At no point in the game does it ever mention this so that whole prompt is just really confusing at first.

Probably the biggest disappointment is the Nemesis himself. The trailers and interviews painted a picture of the Nemesis stalking you through Raccoon City Mr X style, but in reality the city is quite small making the game feel very linear and the Nemesis only shows up at scripted points; he doesn't actually stalk you like Mr. X did. You're never in any danger of the Nemesis just showing up unexpectedly and as such these feels like a regression. I'm well aware having played the original RE3 that he was scripted in that too, but this is a remake and coming off the heels of Mr. X they have undeniably dropped the ball. Mr X added a fantastic level of tension and terror to Resident Evil 2 since as soon as you spawned him he was moving throughout the police station non-stop looking for you; you were able to hear his foot steps the entire time as you tried to avoid him. You don't get that with Nemesis who is just a recurring Boss a la Birkin. Speaking of recurring Boss they literally recycle the same boss fight as well. You have a pretty cool boss battle with the mutated Nemesis running around on all fours; then about half an hour later you run into the exact same boss fight with the same mechanics again just now Zombies will sprinkle into the arena. Felt incredibly lazy. Finally the Stage 3 Nemesis fight is just plain ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Anyone who has played on the harder difficulty settings knows what I am talking about; every hit should be instant death because he just chain stuns you until you die if you get hit once. Which actually feels a lot more aggravating than an instant kill hit would.

I could go on, but I think the picture is clear. The game feels like it could have used more development time to flesh out the experience better. That's not to say it's all bad there are some good changes/additions. The challenges now give points that are used to unlock new items, weapons, and costumes after the first time you beat the game which adds a nice level of replayability and thankfully isn't just ham-fisted monetary DLC; a new difficulty mode called Nightmare also unlocks with item and monster placements changed from the original playthrough which is a great touch. I also like that the grenade launcher feels like a real dangerous weapon in this game. Even against the big enemies it's stopping power is present. Can't quite explain it but in RE2 the weapon didn't feel as impactful as it does in 3.

All in all if I had to give the game a serious rating I'd say something like a 7 out of 10 where RE2 was an easy 8. Still fun, and enjoyable; worth getting and playing just undeniably feels like a step backwards from it's predecessor. Not a giant step, but enough of a one you can't help but look at it and think, RE2 did it better.

[h1]Fun and great looking RE game[/h1]

Once again, Capcom brings another great game on the amazing RE Engine, this time in the form of Resident Evil 3.

While the previous remake, RE 2, was more slow paced and conservative, RE 3 quickly switches gears from the start and it really feels more focused on letting the player be a bit more proactive towards the different enemies; we can dodge now, even in a “perfect dodge” way if properly timed, so that’s already a pretty good indicator of the intentions Capcom had with this remake.

Just like in the original RE3, dodging can be an interesting way of dealing with some enemies, but also risky if we have yet to master it; fortunately this time around the mechanics behind it aren’t as obnoxious as in the original game.

When it comes to PC exclusive settings and other stuff, any PC review should mention at least some of these, when it comes to performance, control settings and keybinds, etc. Very much like RE 2 Remake, the game offers a wide array of graphical settings and the controls are pretty customizable, even quite left handed friendly.

On the performance side of things, the game runs flawlessly on my [b]Ryzen 5 3600[/b] and [b]GTX 1070[/b], even on max settings, but as it happened with the previous game, the [b]Volumetric Lighting[/b] can be a bit taxing in certain scenes, but dropping it to Medium solves the issue while not losing much quality on such volumetric effects.

As for the dreaded “short” duration of the game many people are afraid of, on my first run I spent, according to my save, around 7 and a half hours, and around 10 in total (as the save seems to only count time for essential stuff and no other time spent in menus or what not, I guess, not sure). Anyway, what this means is that if you finished the game on your first run in like 2 hours, you skipped a lot of the fun and exploration, so that’s on you. The game felt to me, on the first run, just as long as RE 2 remake, all things considered. 

RE2 Remake on the other hand, I felt it had a lot of wasted potential with the A/B and B/A scenarios, meaning that once you did let’s say Claire A and Leon B, there was no need to do the reverse…none, it was the same, with some plot inconsistencies even regarding some of the Birkin fights. In any case, that didn’t stop me from considering RE 2 Remake a very amazing game, and it is.

For RE3 Remake I felt that this time the [b]story[/b] seems even more [b]consistent[/b] to me, and coherent. It may feel shorter for those who spent the same amount of time doing A/B back in RE 2, but no…it really isn’t any much shorter than RE 2 Remake, just like the originals, both could be completed in a similar time back then, especially when speed running. 

For this remake I also felt that [b]characters[/b] like Carlos have been vastly improved, to the point that now he feels like a very well written character and not the...whatever that was on the original game. Really good job there with Carlos, Capcom, his character development really made me enjoy the character a lot, in a very good way. The rest of the cast is also very well written, even those whose stay is more brief than others, so yeah, solid cast for this remake, most of the original game's characters are very well written and dubbed, at least in english.

Sound design is very decent too in this game, and compared to RE2 Remake I felt that the music here in RE 3 is more varied and very cohesive with the rest of the action packed situations we find ourselves in. Great job in general with the soundtrack, something not many reviews seem to mention, really enjoyed it.

All in all, I’m still face palming heavily myself after having read some of the most bizarre “professional” reviews for the game (like that pathetic 58 score PC Gamer review, if you can call that thing a PC game review, with no mention on performance or PC specific stuff, to be very honest with you here), but luckily from what I’ve seen on Metacritic, from like 90 professional critics reviews, not too many are that low, so they seem like pretty much outliers. In general the game is quite solid, and if you have any reason to believe it isn’t, well good for you, but I myself had a pretty amazing blast playing this game, and hopefully Capcom ignores those people fixated on bland nostalgia and they keep making remakes like these. That seems to be the intention here, they seem to be fixing some of the inconsistencies in the original stories for the main characters and all that, so hopefully they continue revamping these mainline games and we can see more remakes : )

[i]Edit (2 years after release)[/i]: this review stays positive as the game is not as bad as some so called "RE Fans" make it to be. Content was cut and not included in both RE 2 and 3 remakes, in fact RE 2 does have a pretty poor A/B - B/A scenario system compared to the original experience, yet that doesn't make it a bad remake at all.

RE 3 has many expanded areas like the Hospital, or the Carlos sections, or characters that actually have more than one line of dialogue, compared to the original, and it's still a fun game to complete back to back with RE 2 Remake. It's also a very challenging game in Nightmare and Inferno difficulties which many of the "so called fans" haven't even completed yet, I'm sure.

In conclusion, still a decent RE game, and fun to replay. Could have been bigger and with more areas? Yeah, but it is what it is, and it's not a bad game at all, and if you feel like staying within that dumb circlejerking process of hating on this game because "it's not like the original", well neither is RE 2 Remake, because they're remakes, the originals are still excellent games, and you can go and play them too, as I do sometimes.

This game is alright for what it is, but that doesn't mean it doesn't have pros or cons. 

Cons:
The first time you play, it may take you 3-5 hours, which is ridiculous for a $60 game. Buy it when it is $30 or less and you will feel like you are getting your money's worth.

There is only 1 campaign with no other modes that I am aware of.

They cut a lot of beloved locations from the game that either may or may not be mentioned in dialogue or files, a big shame for long time fans of the original RE3: Nemesis.

I do not know whether or not the original locations were able to be visited again before the final areas like RE2 Remake, but in RE3, a lot of locations are not able to be visited again and aren't exactly given a warning. This is just a personal gripe, though I wouldn't consider it to be a HUGE deal compared to the others.

Some of the scenes with characters from past games are shortened and a lot of questions that RE2 left us are not answered.

SPOILER WARNING!!!: Unlike the original RE3, Jill does not visit the RCPD.

The Nemesis Encounters are all scripted and he is fairly easy to down when running after you in some encounters.

SPOILER WARNING!!!: There is an area in the game where you encounter spiders that give you parasites you must get rid of by using a green herb. It was a fun concept but after that area the concept is never used again.

Pros: 

The Dodge and Punch mechanic enable a better means of escape and avoiding damage. Not only that but when you master it, it becomes muscle memory and extremely satisfying to pull off.

Though the chase sequences and encounters with Nemesis are scripted, they are really fun to play, as well as the boss fights.

The new monsters are fun to fight in some instances as well as hard to kill.

Exploring the city is fun and some locations are fairly interesting.

The characters are nice, the combat is fun, and a few of the puzzles are neat.

When you beat the campaign for the first time, the shop unlocks where you can purchase key items or weapons which you can buy and use in future playthroughs. The points are earned from completing challenges and achievements, as well as how well you did in a full playthrough (I think) which encourages replay value.


Personally I liked the game, but I still felt like $60 is too much. [b] Long version: [/b]
It's hard not to compare this entry with the previous Remake from the series. By most regards it’s even unfair to do so but it's a comparison that must be made.

RE2 Remake was one of -if not THE- greatest surprises I've had in 2019. RE2 Remake pretty much attaining vaporwave status that had rumors flying around since forever, having fan-remakes popping around and getting to the point of being confirmed by CAPCOM almost 4 years prior to its release. Boy… it was a fun(not) ride. But the final product was worth it.

RE2 Remake released and it was a fantastic love letter to die-hard fans and a welcoming party to the newcomers to the classic-esque Resident Evil experience. It was a fantastic game by itself and a modernized classic Resident Evil experience from the controls to the design philosophy. It felt like a complete game with classic locations being brought to life with impressive visuals and some enemies being reimagined with interesting mechanics.

Then comes RE3 Remake. A game that doesn’t feel like they wanted to build up on the formula of the previous Remake nor RE3 classic. This game has so much content cut from the original it just feels disrespectful to say the least. Little to no puzzles, some of the most recognizable places like Clocktower, Graveyard, Park and others are straight up absent. But the worst offender in my opinion: Jill NEVER goes to the RPD, which for me is a sin. The first thing that pops in my mind when I remember RE3 Classic is Nemesis chasing Jill through the corridors and cramped rooms of the RPD. 

To be fair, RE2 Remake also has it’s amount of cut content from RE2 Classic, but nowhere near the scale of RE3 Remake compared to RE3 Classic. RE2 Remake there’s a certain respect and attention to detail on the flow of its source material. RE3 Remake feels like it was completely gutted. It feels like a Shell of what RE3 Classic was.

How about the STAR of the show? The most remembered Tyrant in the series that we know as Nemesis doesn’t feel like a pursuer besides in the first area where he chases you akin to the classic RE3. After that he’s just a common Boss enemy and no longer there’s a constant paranoia that he’ll get the jump on you and ruin your plans to get out of Raccoon City alive. Every Nemesis encounter past the first act is expected/obvious instead of being an “Oh f-“ moment. Straight up skipping one of his transformations as well doesn’t help. On top of it the fight you have with him after his first Remake transformation felt like I was playing Resident Evil 6.

But does it hold itself on its own as a game? Perhaps. While the combat feels fluid and weighty just like RE2 Remake, it's far less methodical and resource-management centered due to the more action-oriented nature of RE3, which isn't a positive nor negative point in my opinion. It makes for a solid and fun gameplay… while it lasts, and that's the biggest issue here. The game feels rushed and incomplete. It’s just way too short without anything to back it up after that. DLC levels of Short. I finished my first playthrough in just over 4 hours not particularly trying to finish it fast. After that there’s no “B-side” or alternate campaign, -which they could’ve used the opportunity to develop something of the sorts, but nope- no survivor stories, no mercenaries mode, nothing. You get 3-6 hours, on a first playthrough for a $60 release title that has limited replayability due to how little content there is.

CAPCOM had a chance to expand on RE3 Classic and make it a more fleshed out experience and develop a definitive version of a reimagined a classic. They did not. All this game offers in the end is a very bitter taste of wasted potential.

Actual rant content--note that I number the paragraphs for easy reading; I'm not actually numbering the reasons I dislike this game:

1. I've never played any of the OG RE games. My only exposure to RE before the RE2 Remake was watching my cousin play it on PS1 when we were kids. Just bits and pieces of memory.

2. I enjoyed the RE2 Remake a whole lot; it felt extremely polished, sublimely deliberated, and well thought out. It's a perfect horror game in every sense of the word, and has a huge replay value--which I think what really makes it stand out from many other single-player games (not just the horror genre), and as I understand this is also what makes the OG RE games well-loved by its fans.

3. Through the characters' weaponry shown to me in the game, I can already deduce in the first 10 minutes that this particular instalment is meant to be more action-focused. I mean the first weapon fired by a character in this game is a friggin rocket launcher (nice entrance btw, Carlos)! So I prepared myself for fast-paced combat situation.

4. Considering everything stated above, this RE3 felt like it's in a big hurry to get me to finish. For my playthrough, I killed every single enemy thrown at me, and used the combat knife on fallen zombies a lot to save on ammo (except for the crawler thing in the power substation) and I still managed to finish it in a little over 6 hours. I backtracked a lot especially at the hospital, and had to try 4-5 times during the last zombie siege in that level. Still managed to finish it right above 6 hours.

5. I find that I spend a lot of time aiming at heads and weak spots more than anything in this installment--more than looking at maps and figuring out routes, more than reading through notes to figure out important information, and I definitely breezed through the level "gateways" without having to spend any significant time thinking about how to do it at all. As I was playing, this easiness of solving things didn't really bother me as I was still in the mood of playing an action-focused horror game.

6. By the time I get to mixing up materials for the vaccine, it dawns on me: they're making me rush through this thing. All the pieces fall into place and it clicked in my head. All the facts:
a. weapon attachments are much too easily unlocked--lowering the difficulty of the gunplay at a quick pace (I strongly believe this was what made this game too easy and reduced the horror feel, hence letting me complete my first playthrough much quicker than I wanted)
b. several enemies have multiple weapons that can be used to effectively kill them--reducing deliberating and strategy (including in bossfights!!!! I literally just dodged and fired whatever I have, and won!!!!!)
c. by my super-rough estimate, about 75% less backtracking compared to RE2 remake--a lot of the solutions are spoonfed so I can keep running through without any breaks. FFS they told me to get 2 liquid materials for the vaccine, and I have to mix it up before the vaccine can be made. I inserted the materials one by one into the actual vaccine machine, fully thinking it was some kind of mixer machine I have to use to mix the two materials, before actually getting to another machine to make the vaccine, but NO, I can actually mix it by hand through the inventory, like mixing gin and tonic. This is what clicked it for me, when in RE2 they made me run around in the lab to collect the stuffs and mix it in different stations!
d. to support point -c., after finishing the game and looking up reviews, I discovered that they skipped a lot of parts from the OG RE3 and many other fans share my disappointment about the same aspects.

7. To top it all off, the parts where the Nemesis chased me through the streets was just much too awkwardly executed, and felt cheaply gathered up. They literally threw a Nemesis in front of me, I have to run through some narrow alleys, awkwardly barricaded streets and cross some roads, and they sprinkled some zombies in between. It made for a lot of awkward moments. Throw in some quickstep-dodge mechanics into the mix of all I mentioned, and it makes for a lot of ugly action sequences (watch in Youtube: channel Gameranx, video title RE3: Before You Buy, from 3:00 to 4:05 and see what I mean), which is a waste of wonderful work by the animation team!

8. Conclusion: I was fully expecting an RE2 Remake type game where I get to carefully traverse the map and conserve ammo a lot and deliberate and strategize my movement a whole plenty, and it became clear to me in the first 10 minutes that that might not be the deal here. Nonetheless, as I switched my expectation to a more action-focused game, I still am not satisfied at how much too easy and breezy everything is--from getting from one level to another (level "gateway" system), the distastefully-implemented quickness of unlocking weapon attachments, and the lack of emphasis on strategy compared to RE2 Remake. And while some might argue that I can try the harder difficulties or challenge myself to restrict uses on some weapons/attachments, guess what--I really don't feel like doing it because of 6.-b. and -c.

TL;DR--for the price, this game is much too easy and much too short, and if you're expecting an RE2 Remake-type deal even though you don't mind more focus on action, you'll still walk away disappointed.

The gameplay is wonderful with a perfect blend of action and survival horror, the addition of the revamped dodge mechanic makes for more exciting combat and disengage opportunities. The atmosphere is lovely and truly captivates a city in peril, every inch of detail is just immaculate as well as the re-imagined cast. 

Jill is feisty, vengeful and as accurately portrayed as a zombie PTSD riddled mansion veteran that can possibly be. Her reluctance to work alongside the UBCS carries over a real personal weight, and seeing the cooperative dynamic change as the story progresses is wonderful to see. She is afforded every emotion you could imagine she has, and she expresses them perfectly.

Carlos is more fleshed out, still the confident lover boy we all love but more corny and charming than sleazy playboy. He appears to have a genuine sense of duty and determination for rescuing the citizens of Raccoon City, Jill included.

Mikhael is a don gorgon. They didn't fix what was broken, only made it better.

Nicholi is the same as the above, made better. Still the disgusting sleazebag we all have come to love. Just sleazier, douchier and the person you love to hate. He's been given more motives, more context and ties things together well.

As a lifelong fan of the series, this game is not without it's criticism. While I think the game is great, the product itself isn't. The re-imagining is true to the wording, it holds very little to the original bar the primary elements of the storyline. The game does not include variable monsters, locations, replayable-elements that the original had. Resident Evil 3 Remake compared to the 2nd falls short horribly, while the addition of 2 new difficulty modes add some replayability, the lack of RNG elements, post-game rewards, costumes, mercenaries, and the general pace of the game just seem rather poor. I am hopeful that this is something that will be remedied with DLC, if not then the game really does not warrant £50. (Resistance excluded as it was deemed free content, and not to be seen as part of the RE3 Product). I'll also quickly add here at the end while it came to mind, the rehashed original RE3 soundtrack came across as extremely lazy, and not appreciated on my end. RE2 had a fresh new chilling soundtrack with all tracks beautifully and hauntingly reimagined. RE3's soundtrack is half original with bass added to it and the rest is what you had hoped the entire track would have been.

Overall: Good game, bit bare bones though. Just a bad product. If the review had a Meh option, I would give it that. Sorry. It's aight.

Back in 1999 RE3 suffered for being different from RE2. While many claim that they've always loved RE3, the fact that it sold nearly 2.5 million copies less than RE2  means that there were quite a few gamers that didn't. (https://vgsales.fandom.com/wiki/Resident_Evil)  I distinctly remember many saying that RE3 was not as good as RE2. Though, I will give credit where credit is due, and point out that many journalists saw RE3 for the gem that it is. I think history is repeating itself once again. I think a certain element of the audience is being overly harsh because this time not only is RE3R being compared to RE2R but also the original RE3 as well. 

It's important to understand that RE3 is, and always has been, a much different experience in comparison to RE2.  While RE2 and RE3 are both classified as survival horror games, RE2 leans more towards Metroidvania and RE3 leans more towards action adventure.  

RE2, like any good Metroidvania, is about becoming familiar with and mastering a space. In my S-Rank playthroughs on RE2R, the zombies become an afterthought in lieu of navigating through the environment and accomplishing tasks that cause progression. Whereas in RE3R, its less about being familiar with the environment and more about surviving long enough to get to the next environment. The areas in  RE3R are.. functional, disposable, semi-linear, and utilitarian.

The reason why Mr.X works so well in RE2R is that he forces you to reroute your path on the fly in order to accomplish your goals. He's a test of your familiarity with the police station. Since familiarity with an environment isn't as important to RE3R, Nemesis can't do that. 

In dealing with Nemesis, you're not thinking "ok, I need to go this way instead of that." You're thinking "I need to run in the direction the game is pointing me." There's a difference between being chased, and being hunted. So if you're expecting Mr.X but worse, you aren't going to get it. Add to that the fact that a few fan favourite areas have been removed, the puzzles are kind of bad, and that the game is relatively short and you have a recipe for disappointment.

Yet I'm still rating this as a recommend because for all of RE3R's faults, I had a really good time with it. The updated mechanics make this the best action oriented entry in the series as far as I am concerned. I like the updated look of the characters, and I think this game remains true to the spirit of the original RE3 even if it doesn't get the details right. I know I'd rather play this than RE5 or RE6.    8/10

On a ground based level it has flaws, You need to know that going in. But the gunplay is still fun, Characters are still great. Just some design choice having you going "huh". it's far closer to a Reimagining then a Remake.

Я как фанат именно оригинальной третьей части не могу точно сказать - хороша ли эта игра. Определенно она используется те же приемы что и оригинал, но по моим ощущениями - слишком злоупотребляет этим.  Надо начать с недостатков:
1) Время игры - 4 часа на прохождение в первый раз, до этого я играл в демку, и видел эпизод с "акуа кюре".  Играл - не ломился на пролом, старался играть аккуратно, в итоге умер всего 5 раз.
2) Линейность игры в абсолюте - в оригинале была некая вариативность, теперь же нет ни сюжетных развилок (с выбором) и запутаться (заблудиться нельзя). Далее расскажу про плюс "насыщенность событий", но если бы были в игре были развилки или хотя бы минимальная нелинейность, думаю этот плюс ни куда бы не делся.
3) Немезис - новый дизайн, скажем так - достаточно странный, плюс разработки слишком сильно злоупотребляют встречами с ним, порой это просто мешает наслаждаться игрой.  Манера его преследования достаточно интересная - в городе он может догонять прыжками Джилл, но по сути это все, в первой форме он падает от пары попаданий в голову из дробовика. Вторая форма по размерам примерно как финальная мутация Биркина из оригинальной второй части, и своей головой напоминает королеву чужих создает проблему - для монстра таких размеров не подходят обычные декорации игры, обязательно нужен стадион для битвы. В общем разработчики явно не понимали как нужно режиссировать встречи с Немезисом - старая формула его поведения  их не устроила, а новую они не доделали.
4) Урезанность локаций  - особенно город, по сравнению с оригиналом, ну примерно 1/3 от него (может и меньше), для 2020 это как-то скромно.
5) Состояние персонажа - трудно понять что здоровье уже красное, так как в оригинале персонаж еле ноги волочил, а теперь так же бегает держась за живот(цветовая коррекция еще включается).
6) Хантеры несбалансированны - то есть их нельзя убить без потери здоровья (если из 2шт). Так как один хантер требует минимум два рожка патрон с хвостиком по себе, то есть с ними нужно сражаться только на скилле, тактически не получится (речь об эпизоде за Карлоса в больнице). 
Теперь по плюсам
1) Механика игры - сильно похожа на второй ремейк, только кнопка уворота теперь есть отдельно (и работает достаточно не плохо). 
2) Стрелять по врагам - одно удовольствие, повреждения достаточно детальны (отрываются руки, ноги, головы). Причем разница от попаданий в тело и по конечностям достаточно ощутимая.
3) Обычные зомби - отлично умеют заставать врасплох, особенно при игре за Джилл(так как у нее на норме нет винтовки М4) - как правило патроны нужно экономить, и ходить  с пистолетом (а дробовик до лучших времен). Если отбиться от толпы зомби с пистолетом, то это очень доставляет. Плюс даже так, при всем опыте резидентовских игр - зомби неожиданно но покусывают, то за ножку цапнут (если труп лежал, а когда подходишь к нему неожиданно очухался), то зайдешь в переулок и одного не заметишь в куче мусора, а спереди будет толпа, пока по ней стреляешь сзади и получаешь "кусь".
4) Насыщенность событий - игра не дает скучать, все время приходится куда-то бежать, собирать предметы откуда-то нападают зомби. То есть в отличие от оригинала игрок не попадает в ситуацию "ну и куда теперь идти и что делать??"
5) Графоний - приятный детализированный, тянет даже на старом железе. 
6) Те кому "нравятся песики" - эти враги максимально сбалансированы. Они быстры, у них мало HP.  Если зазеваться - то они быстро загрызут. 
7) Ликеры - отлично сбалансированны, если им стрелять в голову то аккурат хватает одной обоймы.
8) Отсылки к предыдущей части хорошо работают, есть и отсылки к оригиналу, но порой поменяны местами. Например эпизод с приготовлением вакцины - ее делает Джил (изготавливает вакцину в лаборатории). И пробегая через зал с образцами(там есть и тираны и хантеры, еще кто-то...) из резервуаров вырываются хантеры  уже на обратном пути. Так было в оригинале с Калосом.
В целом впечатление от игры омрачил только Немезис и собственно ее линейность и продолжительность. Игра сама по себе отличная.

I was surprised to find out that the remake of Re3 was coming out a year after Re2 did. It came so fast, so soon, and I was worried that it would be unpolished and unsatisfactory. In a way, it was and it wasn't.

With the positives, it gets a lot right. The nitty gritty details you liked about Re2, you'll find it in Re3. The ambient light, the sheer gruesomeness and brutality of monsters, the trepidation of whats to come. That's really it.

The major problem with the game, is that "trepidation" quickly dissolves. You're not really terrified of your enemies and the scenario ahead of you. In Re2 my heart was pounding and I felt genuine fear. Allow me two examples in comparisons ((from memory(spoilers))

Re2 first Licker encounter: You open the door and slowly travel through a hallway. Flashes of lightning coupled by rain pounding against the windows. The long hallway is dark and suspiciously empty. As you progress across the creaking wooden floor, you hear a violent whipping lash of a long gargantuan tongue on the ceiling catching an undead and brutalizing it. If you haven't played the original, you're immediately taken aback. Once that script was over, the beast doesn't pounce on you and you're standing still. You assume it can't see you, if you didn't run out the door behind you, you begin slowly walking towards it with your weapon drawn. It's massive, hideous, and claws the size of a full grown dog. You realize it can't actually see you, and rationalize that it probably hunts based off loud sounds. Your ammo is low and you don't know how much this creature can take. You either waltz around and head out the door on the other side, or you throw everything at the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and let out a sigh of relief as it writhes on the floor in pain and eventually dies.

Re3 first licker encounter: You're walking through the interconnected hallways and the licker, already alarmed, jumps right in front of you ready to steal your life. You shoot the ♥♥♥♥ out of it because you have way more than enough ammo to take it out. For all you know, it was just some other monster. No uniqueness to the enemy, no using the setting to your advantage, nothing. Your full of ammo of your automatic rifle and you quickly and swiftly kill the licker. There's nothing special about it.

The Second example (and my biggest gripe with the game(keep in mind I never played the original and I'm using the perspective of those who have done the same)). 

Mr. X: In Re2, you're introduced to Mr. X in the middle-ish section of the game. He comes unannounced and hunts the bejeebus out of you. He's menacing and hard to slow down. The way he walks towards you-- he wants more than just your lunch money. He's consistent and sometimes chases you in dangerous areas, such as an area with a few lickers. This feeling of "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I gotta go!" never left me in all the play throughs I did in my ~50 hours of playing.

Nemesis: I would've preferred not encountering Nemesis right at the start of the game, it kind of kills any build up the game should've attempted to create, but fine. It's still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Nemesis. But you quickly realize he's kind of a chump. He runs at you, which should be terrifying, but you can easily dodge. Plus he only chases you in very select locations, not everywhere. I rarely saw him. Which sucks because you don't see him in his base form very often, which is my favorite form. When he uses his rocket launchers, they're incredibly easy to dodge. What's the point? Where's that dread? There is none. All of his boss fights are also very simple, very easy. They're not punishing except for the occasional oneshot-kill attacks. It's uninspiring and largely unsatisfying. 

The only time in the game where I felt myself clenching was vs the hunters. And even then, EVEN THEN, I eventually stopped worrying because the game gives you an incredibly high volume of ammunition to quickly dispose of them.

 Re2 dared to do no such thing. Go ahead, waste your ammo, it would say, but you're not going to have any of it back for a while!

Resident Evil is hugely important to me. From a gaming standpoint and a life stand point. The memories I share with my sister with Resident Evil, and how I gradually grew to be old enough to finish the first RE on my own, is such a defining moment in my life. With that said, before I can say my opinion on the RE3 Remake, I need to explain what RE3 was, in the 90's.

A lot of people tend to forget what RE3 was when it first came out. It was always, and I mean always, a more action packed game compared to RE1 or RE2. Resident Evil 3 was made because Sony wanted another RE title on the ps1, in the time when RE games were being developed for other platforms, (namely RE Code Veronica on DreamCast) In this sense, RE3 was always a kind of "here is a bit more" before moving onto the next generation of systems. It was also one of the shorted titles in the series history, (1 hour and 48 minutes is my personal best)

So, how does the RE3 remake take all of this, and reform it? Simple...it doesn't. Unlike RE2 Remake, that basically rebuilt the game from the ground up but follows the script of Resident Evil 2 basically line for line, RE3 remake recreates the entire bang. From a hard core Resident Evil fan, and collector, I thank Capcom for this, not hate them. The game largely feels the same as RE2 remake, even down to the UI being the same. The gunplay is the same, but Jill now has her trademark dodge ability (That was in the original RE3 game mind you) So this review isn't going to be about the gameplay exactly. If you enjoyed RE2 remake, then you will like this in terms of how it plays.

Now, this is the really important part that people seem split about. The story. Some wanted the game to be exactly the same as the original version, and you know, I get it. RE2 remake gave us such an incredible experience, reliving and first timers alike. If you were expecting this to follow that same idea, then yes, you will sadly be left empty handed. Though, for me, this was a breath of fresh air. They did change things yes, but now you can see just how much the original events of RE1 impacted Jill's mental health.

Her worries, her fears, nightmares, are a reality more now than ever. The damage that Umbrella did to her, and the other survivors, are realized here. At the same time, Nemesis is more blood thirsty than before. As you try to get a grip on what is going on with Jill, Nemesis is like a blood hound. Chasing you down, relentlessly. It creates an atmosphere, where you can't breathe, and that is what it should be doing. 

Music, gameplay, story, all come together to give you a better idea of what Jill her self is going through, as Raccoon City falls apart. Watching citizens run, scream, is so refreshing because in the previous versions or titles, you don't really get to see this.  

The bottom line is this. I don't mean any negativity to people who do not like this remake. I get it, I truly do. Though as a huge fan my self, my views and desires were perhaps different. If you wanted a point for point remake, then I am truly sorry. As a fan to other fans, your wish will NOT be granted with this. Though if you are the type of fan, where you are so hungry for anything Resident Evil, and are open to new visions and views, than you will love this. 

Either way, I hope you all, fans and new comers alike, enjoy what you can from this.

This was a bit of a letdown. Is it bad? No. Does it even come close to the brilliance of REmake 2? Also no. It earns a thumbs down as it pales in comparison not only to that game, but also its original PS1 counterpart.

The graphics are as good as ever, and things run smoothly for the most part. I had a bit of stuttering upon loading, but that sorted itself out pretty quickly. The voice acting and motion capture are fantastic, and the breadth of graphical options is about as extensive as I've ever seen. Clearly a lot of care was put into the little details here, as well as things like lighting and fire.
If you've played REmake 2, you'll know how this plays, with a few notable changes that all go hand in hand. Most baffling is the decision to remove the self-defence items. This is odd in part because the items are still there (grenades, knives, and stun grenades) but they can't be used when grabbed by an enemy, only manually. Instead, you are to do a QTE when grabbed by an enemy, which for the life of me I couldn't figure out how to work. Instead of being able to quickly switch to your equipped self-defence item using space bar as in RE2, space bar is now used for dodging, which works well enough and is now your way out of a potentially hairy encounter.
Gone too are the ink-ribbons, allowing for unlimited saves (as the loading screens encourage) and all of these factors illustrate the direction this game has taken. It is an action-horror game, rather than the slow, suspenseful dread of the original games, resurrected by REmake 2. I don't mind action games, but I don't come to RE for action. Some of the boss fights, while fun enough, would have been more at home in Gears of War.
And it's not just action. It is 5-6 hours of balls-to-the-wall, exploding, pulse pounding, trash talking, unrelenting action. Which is fine in short bursts, but this game hardly pulls back for more than a few minutes at a time. Absent are the quiet, contemplative moments, admiring the atmosphere of a police station or an old mansion. Nearly absent are the moments where you strategically plan your route, carefully considering your supplies or the enemies you may encounter. It's too excited to show you the next crazy scripted setpiece or mutated abomination in its repertoire. And it's all a little tiring. Even in a straight action game, there needs to be some time to breathe - RE3 doesn't have much of that. 
This game seems to designed for speed runs (rather than allowing for it on subsequent playthroughs), judging by the level design, unlockable content, and new gameplay mechanics. And maybe that's someone else's thing, but it's certainly not mine.

A competent follow up to the spectacular 2019 RE2 Remake, albeit shorter and with a reluctance to reach the same heights as its predecessor.

RE3make is simultaneously faithful in some aspects and liberal in its changes in others. Nemesis looks and performs spectacularly as the main antagonist, and each encounter with the villain is a delight. Quick dodges have been streamlined and replace the defensive items of RE2. Carlos has been reworked into a more charismatic (albeit still gruff) mercenary and takes up more screen time than the original. Some omissions are a bit more questionable: spiders have once again been removed, as have the scripted “choose your action” events that would affect how encounters with Nemesis would play out.


Final verdict: a solid follow-up to the masterpiece of RE2 which makes some welcome changes to streamline the experience albeit at the cost of other, more beloved aspects. It is because of this that Resident Evil 3 falls short of the previous entry. RE3 boasts a rather minuscule 5-7 hour initial campaign, appropriate given its status as a title which was never intended to be a mainline sequel, but regardless may leave players feeling underwhelmed. It is because of this that I recommend RE3 but only if you fit into the following criteria: 1. You thoroughly enjoyed RE2 and want more, and 2. You get it on sale.

Multiple play through's will most likely be had by the completionist community and those seeking the infinite ammo weapons for some run and gun fun.

Overall this is a fun game and I hope that the Resistance mode will ensure some more life out of my $60 purchase.

The game is fine, but a hefty downgrade from the RE2 remake.

(Non-story spoilers ahead)

It's far shorter, about as long as Leon A in total. Given that you would play Leon A/B and Claire A/B in that game, RE3 is about 1/3 of the length.

Nemesis is a severe downgrade from Mr X. His appearances are entirely scripted. You are never attempting to do anything but run away via the obvious path provided to you when he shows up, versus Mr X who would appear as an unexpected hazard as you explored. He just isn't scary because of it.

The game is less survival horror, more pure action. You can blow zombie ankles off and stab them to death if you want, but its ultimately a huge waste of time. You can spray bullets into heads all you like and never be short on ammo. Same goes for healing items.

There are zombie encounters, and there are hunter encounters. Never are you challenged by differing enemy types combining. There are a whole two dog encounters, and a single spider encounter.

The story feels like a downgrade personally (somehow). The character relationships are rushed as hell despite the short length, and there is a real headscratcher of a change made to the story of the city.

I quite enjoyed this game and I think it further proves the new RE Engine and gameplay really works for the series going forward after using it for 4 games! Jill and Carlos are more fully-realized characters, everyone in the cast is really fleshed out! The graphics and atmosphere is still amazing as it was in RE2R.

The quality of life improvements for picking up items, the dodge/perfect dodge maneuver is great even if I would've liked the sub-weapons to come back - really tired of that zombie bite animation - and enemy variety is great! This is the best Resident Evil game to play with modern controls, it just feels good. If we get more entries in the series that use this control scheme, then I am going to be quite content to play more. (Sorry, Tank Controls, you had your time.)

That being said, I would honestly say that I am disappointed in this entry. Mostly fairly minor things that don't make this game bad or unpolished, but I would say it just detracts from the experience a little. The game is a bit more linear 2/3rds of the way through and doesn't have the fun exploration that the last game had past the first area. Nemesis is used effectively but only comes around for set pieces during those latter thirds and isn't the 'Scarier Mr. X' I thought he would be, which is a shame but I guess that's why his name isn't in the title anymore.

My final criticism: the game's length. I am not one to complain if a game is short and to the point, leaving me wanting to replay it - that is a great quality and I appreciate it in my busy schedule! This game still does that, but I do think it could've used just one to two more areas to explore in, even if it was just a second block of Raccoon City. I think that would've added enough to make the pacing feel more evened out, because otherwise this game can be over quite quickly for an experienced player, especially with no 2nd Run option and only Resistance replacement for Mercenaries.

Overall, I love what they did for Jill, Carlos and Raccoon City - I just wish I could've spent more time in it before it got blown to hell and back.

[h1] Overall [/h1]
A visually pleasing and heavily cinematic remake with some deeply creepy (in a good way) sound design
that winds up feeling incredibly mediocre, as a result of: removal of areas from the original, linear map design, re-use of many assets from RE:2's remake, a complete watering down of Nemesis, and a campaign that will last you no more than 5-6 hours at most. The game feels more like a large chunk of DLC for RE:2's remake, than a full price remake of the original RE: 3. Wait for sale, or update.

[h1] More: [/h1]
- Far fewer models to view in bonus, also all lacking animations
- Nemesis no longer hunts you at random, he is set to chase you down specific areas, then disappear. 
- Clock tower removed entirely (aside from being a set piece in a boss battle)
- Giant worm section and park removed entirely
- Split decision segments removed
- most grab animations, attack animations, movements, hit reactions, models and textures of standard zombies are 1 to 1 with RE:2's remake.
- Mr.X, from RE:2's remake, feels more like the original RE:3 Nemesis than this one does
- Puzzles are reduced to pulling a lever and watch in a mini-cut scene play out
- Voice acting is well done across the board, and cinematics look amazing
- Most textures look like garbage unless at 2GB+ 
- Interactable cut-scenes and quick time events add absolutely nothing to the game, and feel weak
- Sound design is top notch. You'll often be swiveling and turning at distant noises in more ambient areas. 
- Action segments don't ruin overall tension in the same way RE:6 or ORC did.
- Upon completing a hardcore difficulty run, the game offers nightmare mode. Re-shuffling items and enemy encounters are fun, but doesn't make up for the short campaign.
- New dodging mechanic can feel sloppy and inconsistent from time to time. 
- Many enemies (Sewer boys, power plant bugs, etc) are used, then never revisited

As dumb as the dialogue was, it also felt endearing. Leon and Claire were both fun to play, even if Leon had the better story. I love and will always love that game, Capcom truly made a fantastic game.

Extremely disappointing after last year's Resi 2 remake. I wasted my money buying this at full price. Wait till it's $15-20, because that's what it's worth. A few quick reasons why:

- Painfully short campaign (~4 hrs), with little/no replay value.

- Lack of replay value is because the classic Resi level design is GONE. No exploration, no puzzles, no getting to know an interconnected area more intimately as the game goes on. You get a series of hallways that string together set pieces.

- These hallways are often PACKED with Zombies. If you played Resi 2 Remake, do you remember the combined locker room/showers on 2F of the RPD? There are about EIGHT zombies packed in there. Lickers are now put on unavoidable paths where they stalk toward you, giving you no chances to evade them (and thus robbing them of much of their tension in Resi 2).

- Nemesis is a huge DOWNgrade from Mr. X. He has one sequence where he's chasing you in an open environment. That was great. I remember wondering how I could learn to deal with this guy, he was so much more difficult than Mr.X! Well not to worry, that first time is also the last time. Resident Evil 3 (2020) feels more like a reimagining than a remake, as it alters the storyline, locations and events in a pretty significant manner, some for the better, some for the worse and some things are cut out of the game entirely. While the gameplay is significantly more action oriented than RE2 remake, it is not quite in the over the top levels of RE4-6 - but it is not far off either, as it is a linear adrenaline rush type of game, rather than the more classic style survival horror.

When it comes to graphics, audio, pc port quality etc. if you have played Resident Evil 2 remake - you know what to expect. Graphics are great, audio for the most part is great aside from a couple sound mixing issues, lipsync in the cutscenes is sometimes a little off and the things that were bothersome in RE2 remake pc port are still equally bothersome in 3 (mouse acceleration, sRGB brightness being off).

That being said, there is one major exception and that is the soundtrack - unlike RE2 remake which relied largely on relative silence and ambient sounds. RE3 has a rather good soundtrack which features new versions of many tracks from the original game.

My first and very thorough playthrough on the hardcore difficulty took roughly 7 hours of playtime total and I had a lot of fun with it. In general I thought the game was pretty good, but it isn't even among the top 5 RE titles in my opinion as it has plenty of flaws:

- Pacing feels really rough, as the story progresses at a breakneck pace and majority of the areas are completely linear with very little exploration.
- Boss fights leave a lot to hope for, as many of them are gimmick fights that specifically force you to do things in a certain way or you will be facing a bullet sponge of colossal proportions. Also on the unlockable difficulties, especially towards the end of the game any notion of fair balancing gets thrown right out of the window.
- Ink ribbons have been removed from all difficulties and apart from the highest unlockable difficulty, game features autosaves at checkpoints and infinite manual saves at the typewriters. Which in my opinion removes the risk factor completely, things might go sour but who cares, you got an autosave a couple minutes back anyway.
- Gore has been toned down significantly
- One of the most iconic locations from the original game is reduced to a backdrop of a set piece and you don't even get to visit the place.
- Nemesis is very underused and also poorly balanced. While he is fast, surprisingly agile and deals a whole lot of damage, he is also way too weak and laughably easy to defeat. In fact on the first playthrough, the so called stalking sequences ended in Nemesis showing up and then getting downed within 5 seconds and dropping his loot - not to mention he gets reduced to a extremely persistent set piece encounter rather quickly which is a shame.

While I have a lot of complaints about the game, I had good time with it: It's a fun experience that doesn't take itself too seriously and ends a bit too fast. That being said, I think it is fair to say that as a game, it is nowhere near as good as RE2 remake and won't be making in to many "favourite RE titles" lists in the coming years. 

Rather than including a new version of Operation: Mad Jackal, RE3 instead includes an asymmetric multiplayer game RE: Resistance, which has its own take on the 4 vs 1 genre: One player acts as the mastermind placing traps, spawning & controlling creatures as they try to prevent the 4 survivors from escaping their little experiment.

Resistance can be an entertaining experience when everything clicks together and you get a match with survivors & mastermind with similar level range and skill - which can lead to some pretty close victories without either side completely steamroling the other. Unfortunately more than often the matches are awful: Completely one sided, hampered by the netcode or the poor choice of making the mastermind host the peer to peer game (even if their internet connection might be awful), not to mention the awful queue times when playing as the mastermind (personally, I've had queue times up to 30mins+).

That being said, Resistance is in bit of an awful place at the moment, it is not a mode that a lot of RE players would have wanted and being only available as bundled together with RE3 ensures that the playerbase remains rather small. Combine that with the technical issues, some degree of poor balancing and the historical lack of support from Capcom for any of their past multiplayer oriented RE titles - I unfortunately don't see a very long lifespan for Resistance, especially on PC. Perhaps with more polish and Resistance being released as a free to play title, they could have a reasonably fun multiplayer mode on their hands.

Would I recommend RE3, yes but with a caveat. If you're the type of a player who plays through games just once, don't have any interest in even trying RE: Resistance I would recommend waiting for a sale. However, if you're the type of player who plays games multiple times, be it with unlockable difficulties,  trying to achieve better ranks, grinding post game unlockables or have an interest in giving RE: Resistance a try - I think you'll find enough of content worth your money here.

REmake 3 outright did not actually "re make" about 60% of the content of the original game and replaced it with nothing. Resulting in a full price $60 game that most people will finish in 4 to 5 hours only to realize it has no replayability. I finished my first playthrough on hardcore mode in about 6 hours so please keep in mind that my review is based on that.

I'll just get straight to it and list what was outright not included from the original (expect spoilers):

[h1] Areas that were cut from the original game [/h1] 
- Most of the city streets (Gas station, parking garage, pharmacy, almost every alley, City Hall) the demo shows off about 90% of the streets area in the final product. 
- Clock Tower, you see it and have a boss fight right outside, but the entire map was cut. 
- Raccoon City Park
- The Graveyard 
- Dead Factory (the finale is replaced with Nest from REmake 2, it's even literally called NEST 2 in the game)
- The RPD building is still in but you go there as Carlos instead

[h1] Iconic moments from the original game that were cut [/h1]
- Brad's death. He gets bit and turns off screen then shows up later where he bites Marvin in a George Lucas tier "things that didn't require an explanation" tier moment
- Nemesis shooting down the escape chopper outside the clock tower
- No secret ending where Barry gets a cameo at the end (no ending changes at all)
- The handgun is not the STARS Samurai Edge Beretta 92FS (technically not a moment but that was the gun that got me interested in firearms IRL so I'm counting it here)
- Original intro cutscene from the PSX game is not remade and a FMV news cast is used instead.

[h1] Gameplay mechanics that were cut from the original game [/h1]
- Crafting ammo with gunpowder will not create advanced versions of ammo after a certain amount of times crafted like in the original. If you wanted to do a run with a shotgun only with the exploding shells like in the original, or any other kinds of mono weapon runs then you're ♥♥♥♥ out of luck.
- Freeze grenades were cut entirely
- as mentioned before there are no alternate endings, if you wanted to see Barry at the end then sorry he's not in the game at all
- no scenario changes (Mikhail dying early, ect.)
- enemy spawns are not randomized from two to three different encounters like they were in the original. The way an enemy group spawns in a room will always be the same. This severely effects replayability.
- No black and white freezeframe choices, while I'll admit this was never an amazing feature of the original it added some degree of playthroughs proceeding differently which is something this game definitely needs as it's starved for content enough as is.

[h1] Nemesis Changes [/h1]
The one thing people were looking forward to the most after REmake 2 was comparing how a hypothetical Nemesis would work compared to Mr. X in REmake 2. Sadly Nemesis also suffers from barebones design.

- Nemesis can only spawn in at certain points in the story to stalk the player. This only happens twice and he cannot spawn in at random in some areas like in the original
- Nemesis will only use the rocket launcher as a specific setpiece chase that lasts less than two minutes
- Nemesis will not use weapons at all outside a boss fight and the above mentioned setpiece 
- Nemesis is much easier to down than in the original games. The items he drops are attachments to already existing guns instead of parts to a new weapon
- Nemesis in general is barely in the game he appears for two very short sections before mutating into a more animalistic form, thus wasting his one unique quality as being a zombie with semi-sentience
- Nemesis has very awkward animations with his new gimmick where he uses his tentacles to swing around like he's Spiderman. 
- He doesn't seem to aggressively stalk the player at all and his AI is very passive

[h1] Enemies cut from the game[/h1]
- Gravedigger
- Brain Sucker
- Drain Demos 
- Sliding Worm
- Giant Spider
- Infected Crows
- Hunter β (To be fair hunters as they appeared in RE1 are present instead)

While zombie dogs were not cut, only four appear in the entire game on hardcore mode. Two of which are during a scripted escape sequence, the other two of which are at the very end of the game. 

That about sums it up really. While the dodge mechanic working and even being fun is nice, the game is too rushed and incomplete in all other areas so the few enjoyable parts of the game are in service of nothing. The first and final red flag should have been how quickly this game was announced after the success of REmake 2 with a release date alongside the announcement. 

It's a real shame that RE3 has to be the one with the bad remake because it's not only my favorite Resident Evil game but in my top 10 list of favorite games made in general. It's essentially a remake that doesn't actually *re make* more than half of the original game. 

Maybe if this had more time to be finished and released sometime next year it could have been something good. But unless Capcom is about to take the game off the store page and spend the next 4 to 6 months actually finishing the content, then I STRONGLY suggest that you avoid this game. It's starved for content and not worth even half of the $60 price tag. 

There is absolutely no reason to play this over the original, which is still widely available in digital formats as well as a fan made restoration of the PC port floating around online for free. If you really insist on giving Capcom any money for a remade RE game, then your money and time is better spent on the Remastered version of the first Resident Evil Remake.

It sets the standard of how horror survival games should be made, tense, you feel helpless and also exploring feels great, finding secrets and backtracking is very rewarding.

The Jill dodge mechanic as fun and satisfying as it is to use it maybe makes the game way too easy and rarely it doesn't work right, making you getting hit in weird ways.

Raccoon City is *smaller* than the original game somehow. I remember previews suggesting that the playable streets areas were considerably larger than the original game, but what you get ultimately amounts to two streets split by a donut shop, with some smaller side areas tacked on. The clock tower is referenced only, and the park is entirely non-existent. What RE2's remake did so well was keep the original's general idea and run with it, but RE3 instead only takes bits of the original instead. Again, the game isn't bad as a result, but you end up retreading ground far more than can be enjoyable at times and to compensate for that, you're bombarded with enemies that didn't exist on your first visit through there, their presence inexplicable and not really presented all that well.

Nemesis itself is also more disappointing and annoying than scary. The mystique and fear through Mr.X/Tyrant in RE2 was that he was a constant presence but simultaneously you could outplay him and outmanuevre him with relative ease as long as you paid attention. Nemesis however only appears at scripted moments and then does nothing but sprint after you and smack you to the floor. It's not scary, it's not really super threatening, it's just a pain in the ass trying to hit the dodge button at the perfect time only to be knocked over anyway. Then you go through a few doors and he's gone until the next time the game scripts that he should arrive. If the city area was much larger and more freely explored, a more deliberate and methodical Nemesis would have been fantastic, but it just doesn't work as is.

RE3 is also excessively linear outside of maybe two instances and is overly generous with health, ammunition, etc. Granted Hardcore difficulty could counter that somewhat, but Normal should still be a challenge, yet my only deaths were when the game decided that a zombie could chomp me from Caution to dead in one-hit which again was more frustrating than challenging.

RE3 isn't bad. Even with its short length I had fun. It just could have been so much more than it is. Yes the original is reasonably limited too but that was a rushed sequel made in 1999 for a quick buck off the back of RE2 while Code Veronica was made. What could have been way more feels rushed and disappointingly lacking.

Oh and there's a sewer section out of nowhere with monsters that are pointless and look goofy. Could have done with something a bit more than generic action-game locale #114.

Alright, let me get the negative aspects out of the way. 

The game isn't a perfect 1:1 remake of the OG Nemesis title or better than the RE2 remake.

Sure it's a bit on the shorter side (took me 5:15 hours to clear through but my playtime was around 9 ish hours as I had died a couple of times and explored a little bit.) They also removed quite a few things from RE2 Remake such as zombie physics, grapple escape and there were barely any puzzles in RE3.

The maps are quite small, and by small I mean really TINY. I expected raccoon city to be larger than what we got but oh well. 

Nemesis is scripted af and doesn't linger around like Mr.X, in-fact a single hand grenade can put that f*cker out of commission and drop upgrades for you.

Now moving on to things that are good about RE3.

They fixed the annoying glimmering issue that plagued RE2 and DMCV. Reflections aren't that much of an eyesore anymore.

The story explains a lot of things that happened in RE2 and compliments it well. There are a lot of "oooh so that's what happened" moments.

It's enjoyable, yes that's right. I had fun playing it and that's what matters. I'm glad the game didn't overstay it's welcome and ended on a high note.

Despite being scripted, I had fun messing around with Nemesis. He's so damn annoying that fighting him makes it all worth it.

Dodging is a godsend, though I do miss jamming my knife/nade/flashbang into zombies and that feature should not have been discarded at all.

Is the game worth it? Well if you have nothing to play during quarantine and you're a resident evil fan who wants something like RE2 remake then yes, absolutely. 

It's not worth the full price imo even though you're also getting a multiplayer game bundled with it. (I haven't played it yet but i'll update the review once I do.) I feel that RE3 should've been released as a DLC for the RE2 remake or they should've worked a little more on it.

Regardless, it's a solid game on it's on despite not being able to live up to expectations.

I really wish I could recommend this game - especially considering how great RE2 Remake is, but I simply can't - not for its astonishing $59.99 price tag. This game is remarkably short and lacks the value of the previous title. What's worse - it's even shorter than the ORIGINAL resident evil 3, which by itself was already shorter than the original RE2. This was Capcom's opportunity to really expand on RE3 and make it something special. They could have used the design of Mr. X from last years game, and reworked him into an even more intimidating Nemesis. 

Instead, what we're left with is a Nemesis that spawns in at very specific scripted sequences, and has no patrol AI programmed in at all. He only pursues until you reach a checkpoint - then he backs off until you reach the next checkpoint. What's worse - this game spends literally only an hour in the city, then it goes into the hospital section and the finale before you know it. 

The only upside to this game is that it's fun to speed run. Each time you finish the game, you unlock more gear to make playthroughs easier. If this sounds like something you'd enjoy, by all means - try it out, but if you were hoping for improvements on RE2 from last year, you won't find that here.

First of all, the game is embarrassingly short. Now i know classic re games are designed to be played more than once but on a first run, casual playthrough it took me maybe 10 or so hours to complete any one of the classics. Even RE2 Remake took me 10 hours on my first casual play of the first scenario. RE3 Remake took me 5hrs and 3 minutes. That includes hunting for missed items (i collected every item i could) which involved running back through certain areas 2 or 3 times hunting every nook and cranny. It also includes me walking slowly through many areas, taking my time to look at the surroundings and soak in the atmosphere, playing around with different weapons, dying a few times (which doesn't reset the timer) and having to repeat sections etc.

Now i personally wouldn't mind the length if the game felt like it had given me all it could (Hellblade was only 8 hours long but it was the perfect length) however that's not the case. Many areas from the original are either cut entirely or mentioned briefly in passing so i'm confused as to why they aren't included. Nemesis feels so cut-down; he almost never chases you, doesn't feel like this omnipresent force of nature, is only around in his first form for about 1.5 hours before just devolving into a recurring boss fight. The section of the game used for the demo is the best part, and the only open area you encounter the Nemesis in.

The game is pretty linear aside from the one open area used in the demo, not much in the way of exploring to be done here which is a real bummer. Backtracking through areas hunting for keys and finding new enemies in an area you had initially cleared IS resident evil and that almost never happens here.

Aside from these critiques the game is good! its more spooky monsters in the style of RE2 remake with a more focused, actiony story. Controls are good, atmosphere is good, gameplay good. There's nothing really new in that respect which some may consider a bad thing, doesn't bother me too much.

Overall it feels like the original game wasn't so much "faithfully remade" like RE2 but was more "hurriedly compressed and updated". It feels like an absolute tonne of wasted potential which is disappointing.

I honestly don't think i would be making any of these complaints if it had been marketed honestly at an honest price tag or even created as a paid DLC for RE2 Remake, but as it stands i feel a little conned. 

****And the multiplayer game doesn't make up for any of this. I'm never going to play it, its not my thing and i don't appreciate being forced to pay for that if a want to play RE3. They should be sold separately.****

So, after just finishing hardcore playthrough, i think i should give my review. Personally, Resident Evil 3 was my first RE and entry point to the series, i replayed it countless times, and i will still recommend this one, for i have plenty of fun with it and i'm gonna definitely replay it down the road on different difficulties. Let's get some details here.

- Yes, it is somewhat short, but you never feel like something is dragging out. Basically they cut out the part before meeting with UBCS, and went with game after that point. This kindda cuts a bit of exploration, but on the other hand, doesn't drag out the game too much by just walking around and forward. It's remake, not remaster, let them change things around.

- Going back and forward between places is not required, but it is essential if you want to get stocked up on resources. Might not be as required for standard or assisted, but hardcore and up zombies gonna chew you up if you don't get stocked.

- Yes, some stuff was cut out, but on the other hand... Do you really miss Gravedigger? Hunter Gammas basically are its replacement now and they work much better then original ones, which were basically reskins of betas with different instakill. Graveyard and Park were also just basically a running through points, nothing special happened there. I do admit, i miss Clocktower and lack of spiders, but i won't ♥♥♥♥ on this game just because of it. Lack of gore from RE 2 Remake also didn't really moved me, and you still can shoot out the body parts. Difference now is that it's tied to critical hit mechanic, that's it.

- Redesign of characters is fine by me. That's my opinion, and that's that.

- Nemesis works more or less similar to how it worked in old Resident Evil 3. He's not walking around like Mr.X, appearing at fixed times and spots and then chasing you around. It is fine, it is how it worked before and i'm okay with not having him breathing down my neck through whole game. Sure, they could've made it like that, but it would've been nigh impossible to get around and do anything. Making him based around events just seems to work better, making him less of an annoyance (especially since you prolly could not wait him out like Mr.X). Mutations were ok, i guess. They could've stick with old 2nd transformation, but what they did is okay with me too.

- Lack of Mercenaries is a shame, but hey - RE 2 Remake also got stuff sometime after release, who knows what RE 3 might get.

Don't remember what else i can say about it. It is still a solid game, a solid remake of first RE that got me into the franchise. I won't ♥♥♥♥ on it, for i had fun. Trully, i had. And i'll prolly still have, going through harder difficulties, speedrunning and getting the achievements. If you want to play it as "one and done", i'll suggest waiting for sale. If you want to buy it and intent on playing more then once - it's definitely worth the price. For me at least.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is another superb game of a great franchise. I was very hyped for it, and waiting day by day, observing the timer, was absolutely worth it.

First of all, I need to brightly emphasize that both remakes share many things in common which basically means that they're connected. I strongly recommend playing RE 2 Remake, too, and you should do it first, just so the devs thought you'd do. Once you learn the basics of survival and master them in RE 2, playing this part will be easier. You will understand which zombies to kill, where to save your bullets, where you should use your knife (and in this game your knife isn't gonna break which makes it really easier) – you'll manage your resources effectively, and puzzles will be easier. It's not the only reason playing RE 2 first is advisable – both games share some characters and locations, so it'll be interesting for you to see how these characters winded up where they winded up. Well, I think I made my best to make sure you play this game second. Now let's say a few words about RE 3 itself.

I can say that the game looks, as for me, outstanding. When you think that games are going to look like movies, you might consider this game. By the way, my PC isn't a monstrous machine, so I had to keep the video settings not high. The picture is simply enjoyable. I was delighted with the outside landscapes the most. Those streets feel safer, it's like you can take a breath of air yourself, the neon signs make you feel somewhat cozy and welcome... And then you go to less pleasant places. Don't get me wrong, I like all the locations, it's just about my personal preference.

The soundtrack feels quite familiar since I had played RE 2 before. The devs know how to make you feel tense, so you're waiting for danger from anywhere. And playing with the sounds is a thing that is essential for a horror game. This game doesn't have problems with it.

The plot has been changed a lot, but the main idea is still here: there's a pharmaceutical company that paid the local authorities to keep them quiet while they were trying to create a biological weapon. That's just the basics. So... the whole city is going insane, people are getting infected, and you have to make your way out of there. Just a friendly reminder: you have a big a$$ crazy dude on your tail haunting you as a S.T.A.R.S. member.
The game is full of interesting events, the plot is always on its way, and you have to solve some puzzles to keep going. Some of them will give you useful things like additional inventory slots. Just believe me: you are interested in exploring the whole area unless you want to speed run. I enjoyed the story and the interactions between the characters.

Here I just quickly want to add that before the game was realized, people had found out that it takes less than RE 2 Remake (by a third). I was very worried about it as I had big expectations for this game. So... Yes, it's shorter, but it's not just a cut version of something, it IS still a full game that can take you one or two evenings. My first playthrough? I tried to explore the area thoroughly, and it took me about 5 hours and 30 minutes (to my shame, I died many times, but the game loads you back, and that wasted time isn't counted). I suppose now you know what to expect. Either way, I'm gonna play this game again, and I'll try to do better. I just enjoy the story and the characters, and that's enough.

I agree that it has its flaws, but before being negative about it, just explore the content fully. It gives you more opportunities as you play it.

So... The conclusion: this game is worth it even though it's shorter than it could've been. A series fan has to play this game, but if you're new to the franchise, Resident Evil 3 will be a warm greeting.
