As someone who loved both the remake of the first 2 games, the original games and have been with the franchise for about 15 years now, I am incredibly dissapointed with this game. 

If there is one word that can adequately describe this game, it is frustrating. Frustrating because, at times, it takes the ques of its resident evil predecessor REmake 2 and is a fun, survival horror game set around exploration, resource management and planning. But this is, at best, 15% of the game. The rest are clunky trial and error set pieces, incredibly finnicky sections that take multiple resets to actually beat and incredibly awful ammo management and clunky shooting mechanics. The enemies are incredibly hard to hit in this game (as they move around like crazy), yet the game expects you to shoot them down in droves. In this manner, it has an incredible identity crisis. It wants to be a zombie shooting game, but it also wants to be a survival horror game. You can't have your cake and eat it too game. 

If any of you remember the alligator chase sequence from RE2, they are back in this game with full force, and they are no better, heck, they're even worse and make up most of the first half of the game. Which is a good time to bring up the absolutely awful pacing this game has. They've removed 70% of the original RE3s locations, and made small cameos of the ones that are there, instead of full locations. The town of racoon city is gorgeous, for sure, but you're in it for so short as opposed to the original, where you get to explore such a large amount of the city. Ironically, this game is a lot smaller in scale than the PS1 original, and it hurts it a lot. 

All of the content which was cut is replaced by bad setpieces, boring areas (did we need a sewer level?), clunky shootout sections and poorly thought out boss fights along with tacked on resource management that feels out of place for a game trying to be as action heavy as this. Not to manage there are enemies whose entire purpose is to be a bullet sponge, yet the game expects you to have enough ammo for it, despite not providing it for you. 

In conclusion, this game takes everything which worked in every good resident evil game up to now and cuts it out. This game has no respect for it's source material, completely misunderstands what made RE3 work and makes a mockery of the work done by RE2 devs. Complete waste of time.

Resident Evil-3 (Remake)
Release Date:  03 April 2020

Strengths: 
-Refreshing new reboot of RE3
-Outstanding graphics and models
-Superbly detailed character animations
-Nice story, fairly well preserved as compared to the original (they didn't spoil it entirely !)
-Quality voice acting (Jill, Carlos, Mikhail, Nicolai, Brad, Tyrell and even the previously unknown doctor guy, all were superb!)
-Action Packed (Nice weapons, and combat is fun!)
-Hunters Included !

Limitations:
-No Mercenaries Mode (Big Let Down !)
-Short campaign time (2-6 hrs) 
-Very linear gameplay
-Many enemies (esp. giant worm), locations and scenes deleted as compared to the original
-Limited number of weapons
-No multiplayer or co-op or add-on campaigns for RE3 story

Conclusion:
Being the first RE game that I played, the original RE-3 was undoubtedly my favourite one and hence buying the remake was a no-brainer for me. The game has a good refreshing feeling to it with the setting and story has been slightly modified  with more sensible and believable aspects added to some sections. For example, you don't have to place stones in hand of statues to obtain critical items like batteries, characters behaviour more realistic etc. The biggest strength of the remake is how well Capcom has brought out the characters of old RE3 and carefully put them all in almost perfectly in the game. Especially, Jill, Carlos, Mikhail, Nicolai and Tyrell. Amongst the side characters I liked Tyrell very much and refining him from practically zero value character in the old game to the present one was refreshing to see. Jill's personality is more refined and her behaviour is more logical in terms of the situation that she's in. Her toughness and brave character is not compromised though, which is great. Carlos is more sensible and gentlemanly. Mikhail is perfect  as a responsible leader, and I would've liked to see more of him in the game. Nemesis is savage and fighting him is still tough if you don't have grenades or powerful weapons with you. His appearance still instils fear which is good. Fighting other enemies is fun lots of ammo is provided as in original which is good. Original save room music and small segments of classic music in some stages has been included. But  an option like in RE-2 Remake for enabling classic soundtrack is not included. The game's ending is great and satisfying. Stages are OK, but I'd say they aren't as memorable as the ones in the original.

Now coming to the shortcomings. Yes, there are significant lacunae in the game no doubt, like the first fat guy should've been given more story, the young girl and a man that get killed early in the game should've been added (there is a woman killed but that just doesn't cut it). Jill's lonely stroll through abandoned streets is missing which I think was one of the most powerful scenes in the game. Although these sound  as simple things but those events really shaped the tension in the atmosphere at the game's start that made the original game so memorable. Starting cinematic is lazy and extremely casual looking. I'd rather take the one in the original game any day. Cutting the corners clearly show at the game's start (which should've been a slow progression) unfortunately otherwise this game could easily been a masterpiece everybody had hoped for.  Some  stages like Clock Tower aren't fully included (just mentioned on a document in-game; and wrapped-up to the background of a boss fight! Talking about taking short-cuts lol!). Puzzles, one of the reasons I liked RE games for, were not focused upon, which is not a good step as they added to the uniqueness of  RE games and diversified gameplay. "Mercenaries mode" is not included which severely diminishes the game's replay value.  Apart from its largely visible limitations RE3-Remake, is a good "Äction" game to play for newbies and for veteran RE players it is a refreshing, fairly good reboot. It's not a perfect RE game, but is definitely playable and has quality. Also, the game is very short. Capcom has included an achievement that unlocks if you can finish it in 2 hrs! Average is 6 hours for the campaign! Without the  original "Mercenaries" Mode RE3 is an incomplete reboot and "Project Resistance" that comes strapped with RE-3-Remake doesn't seem to be a proper replacement for it (I'll review that separately though). Final verdict:  RE3 remake: great game, definitely worth buying.

Resident Evil 3 Remake is a great game! Is it fantastic? Almost...

But first let me get into what others are saying about this game that is apparently bad:

[b]People saying "This game is way too short"[/b]
A: Wrong. RE3 is just as long as RE2... around 5-6 hours if you explore everything properly without rushing!
Also, people dont seem to be paying attention to the store that unlocks after playing on standard difficulty which adds replayability for multiple runs afterwards where you can unlock different things. Besides, Resident Evil 3 has five difficulty levels, those being:
Assisted
Standard
Hardcore
Nightmare
Inferno

[b]But Smoke, RE2 Remake had 2 campaigns so thats over 10 hours of gameplay![/b]
Right and wrong... It did have 2 campaigns but lets not forget that they where nearly identical to one another... thats a cheap way of adding replayabilty in my book and not really a fair comparison!

[b]People saying "The game sucks cus they cut out some locations from the original"[/b]
A: People dont seem to understand what a "Remake" is and just expect a full on "Remaster".
Its called a REMAKE for a reason because its REMADE with some alterations added! While i can understand people being upset about the clocktower not making the final cut, i cant say the same for the park and the cemetary. The latter 2 being fairly small areas with little to them but crossover sections in the original. Anyways, i do believe that they could have easily snuck in the clocktower by just having nemesis show up like he does in the remake but then something happens and you run into the clocktower. So even story-wise that should have been no problem in the remake... oh well... maybe they ran out of time?

[b]People saying "This feels like RE6 and has too much action".[/b]
A: The devs did state multiple times that this recreation will have much more action than RE2 and as far as im concerned there where plenty of explosions and action in the original "RE3 Nemesis". Also, in no way does this feel like RE6... again people are just using excuses to crap on this game by comparing it to capcoms worst RE game, which is RE6. The combat is still very much the same as in RE2 Remake, as are the jump scares, tension, atmosphere and surprises!

[b]People saying "This should have been DLC"[/b]
A: I disagree. There is still enough on offer here to justify the price tag AND you get another game on top being "RE: Resistance".

[b]Conclusion:
Dont worry too much about all these people who are upset because the game isnt a 1:1 recreation of the original because lets face it, thats literally 90% of the complaints. Let's also not forget that Capcom wanted this game out in just over a year so i feel for the devs.[/b]

Anyways...with that out of the way lets get into the pros and cons:

[b]Pros:[/b]
----------
- More varied environments
- Ties up the original games plot holes well
- Realistic graphics
- Nemesis is relentless and will try to mess up your day in any way he can 
(RE2s Mr. X doent even hold a candle against him)
- Inventory management is done a bit better than in RE2 with quick stash on already picked up items

[b]Cons:[/b]
---------
- Explosive barrels make initial zombie encounters way too easy
- Soundtrack volume in safe rooms is way too low and the "remixed" save room soundtrack isnt as good as the original 
(why cant capcom give us the option for the original soundtrack like in RE2 Remake?)
- 1 or 2 questionable QTE's 
(i.e.: Jill crawling away with tentacle attached to her leg for nearly 30s)
- Sometimes its hard to tell if youre doing damage to nemesis in fights due to vague animations
- No Mercenaries mode
- Barely any puzzles and way too easy
- Some sections felt really short with less intricate level designs compared to the original game
(They should have just reused some of their outdoor/indoor assets to give each section a bit more length)

[b]Final thoughts:[/b]
---------------
Survival horror is still very much present in RE3 so dont let other reviews dissuade you on that! It's just that RE3 Remake has more variety and more action sprinkled on top, thats all.
There are still plenty of jump scares, tension, atmosphere and surprises throughout!

[b]Final Verdict:[/b]
--------------

First off, this isn't so much of a "remake" of RE3 as it is a complete reimagining.  While the rough story is basically the same, a lot of the game content is different.  The places you go are different, and even when you do go to the same places as the original the order is different.  I personally think it flows a lot better than the original.  Some people have reported performance issues but I haven't had that myself...that said I do have a very high end machine so I can't speak for everyone in that regard.  Don't listen to the people watching speedruns and then complaining "the game is too short".  Resident Evil games have never been long, instead they are designed to be replayable with achievements, unlockables, and different difficulties.  My first playthrough is on track to be somewhere between 8-10 hours.  I'm a completionist and I take my time and explore everything.

A list of important missing location sections:
Diner and its cool moments.
Clock Tower and its spooky vibe.
Park/Cemetery and related enemies (if you know what I mean).
Factory

It's like these devs went back in time and got a prototype of RE3 from BEFORE it was expanded into a full game, and made a new game out of THAT prototype.

Those missing sections, done right, could have given some classic "RE crit-pathing/puzzly hub areas" to break up the linear action. Similarly, the intro of this game is exciting, but they clearly front-loaded their effort on that, as the game feels way less fleshed out the further it goes on. We really needed two more big "all hell is breaking loose in the city" visual sections - in the middle and near the end - to make the whole game feel as good as this intro feels.

I swear every time they remake one of these games they leave out MORE classic pieces. RE1 remake EXPANDED RE1 in every possible way. It's definitive. RE2 remade it but didn't expand the lab and left out some cool ideas from RE2 Original. RE3make just cuts entire sections of the game people love. Was this game rushed?

The problem is that "ambient Mr. X style stalking" works best in a hub-based, slow-paced puzzle environment - which this game generally avoids in favor of linear progression.

THE END

People are complaining a lot about this game because it doesn't live up to their expectations of the original, which is fair enough, but we are lucky to even get such high quality RE2 and RE3 remakes which didn't seem like a possibility a few years ago. Sure it doesn't have the wow factor of RE2R because we were introduced to a new engine, everything was shiny and fresh, this is just 'more of the same' and much like the original RE2 and RE3, the latter is more of an action-extension of RE2 where you revisit locations and characters. 

The new Jill is fantastic and not some ugly feminist as some people seem to be describing. She's had the Lara treatment of being made believable to her environment, i.e, jeans instead of a skirt. I'm sure mods already exist to put her in lewd attire so this seems like a pointless argument again.  Her attitude and banter with Carlos is decent. 

You might consider Nemesis to be less trilling than Mr X as he mostly chases you in small segments, scripted events and from point A to point B, but there are still a lot of tense moments with him and a variety of boss battles as he evolves.

Visually the game is as stunning as ever, although it seems to lack some physics properties that were in RE2, zombies don't seem to flop around as much as they fall/die, I'm wondering if this is something in-engine that modders can turn back on. Perhaps it was toned down for performance reasons.

The real negatives compared to RE2 are that it lacks a lengthy open-ended section like RPD. This is far more liner, you do have a few locations like the hospital that are slightly more branching but it's not half of what the RPD experience was. It does have some cool moments where it ties up things that happen in RE2, you see how certain things got to be how they are in RE2, I like how it links those aspects together.

It might be pricey because it's probably 10 hours of content (including cut-scenes, reading notes and diaries etc) so if you can get it for 20-30% off then you've probably hit a decent value as it does include an online 4vs1 mode if you're into that and it will surely come with free DLC stories again in near future.

The remake of the chronologically third Resident Evil / Biohazard game has now been made available and i have to say, that the RE Engine shows it's strengths as well as it's flaws. On the one hand, every minute detail of the character looks astonishingly good, the background is detailed and the quality of sound is pretty high. On the other hand, little bugs can be found and don't have to be forced to show themselves. For instance, if you zoom in (right click) with any bigger weapon (like shotgun, etc.) for only a fraction of a second, then the camera gets stuck that way.

The technical aspect aside, capcom used the level of detail and the fact that the game plays in the biggest city of the RE Universe, so that they can use advertisements to make some cute references and in-jokes. 

The biggest critique this game could get, is probably due to its length. I could now begin to defend this, by stating that some other games are even shorter or that you could (and you are really being incentivised to) restart the whole campaign and play it through multiple times. 
I could do that, but I won't. Why? Because I believe, that a game, a story, an experience has it's individual lifetime. That means, that a game SHOULD only be as long as it has to be, and to be quite honest, the remake of RE3 and RE2 are both "short". But it's for the better. You have seen everything you had to see. I personally needed 4h18min for the campaign, as I tried to search through every nook and cranny of raccoon city. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with RC and that should be the whole point in playing a game. Not some arbitrary length-for-your-buck mental structure should be used. I'd rather enjoy a 2h game then sit through a 30h game I can't stand.

To summarize the game is great, really topical right now and kind of short. Everyone who understands my mentality and likes these kinds of games, i.e. survival horror, should buy and it. Believe me, you can finish it pretty quickly, but you might stay and want to challenge you further.

Well, it pains me for having to give this game a negative review, despite it actually being decent to fairly good (all 4 hours of it, anyway), but I really do have to, and the reason is simple - whether this is worth your 60 bucks entirely depends on how much you care about RE Resistance. I for one think it's just taking up space in my library, hence the rating.

Almost every aspect of this remake (if you can even call it that, it really is more of a reimagining) reeks of either laziness and rush job/cash grab (likely) or tons of cut development work (unlikely). Everything moves at a much faster pace as compared to the original - you encounter Nemesis earlier than expected, one important side character dies not even a minute after they are introduced, getting the tram (now subway train) moving is a much easier and faster job and so on.
Many areas of the original game have been cut, and some were added or expanded, but at least to me the game felt shorter. The city sections are completely linear and, in all honesty, there isn't much to explore. Mercenaries mode was cut, as well as most of the costumes, there is a decent amount of asset reuse - again, it reeks of laziness.

Amongst oldshool RE fans, a common complaint about the original RE3 is that the game is much more action focused than RE2 (which I disagree with anyway), and the developers took this complaint quite seriously and made this reimagining as a full-on action game. They cut out most of the puzzles from the original, but don't worry as they have added plenty of Micheal Bay scripted moments in return, which are neither fun nor exciting in any way, mostly because they are piss easy to complete.

The writing - well it was never this franchise's strong suit, but it feels particularly facepalm inducing in this newest installment. While RE 7 and RE2 had their "cringy" moments, they were by far better than this, as this game almost feels like a throwback to the original games dialogue, just with more profanity and more competent people behind the microphones.

I could honestly go on and on about this disappointment of a game, but I doubt anyone wants to read a huge wall of text, so I'm just going to conclude by saying that lying buried below all the aforementioned crap is at heart a decent game, decent in no small part thanks to its RE engine and RE2R heritage, but one that probably isn't worth your 60 bucks. Get it on a sale. If CAPCOM only wanted to spend the bare minimum amount of effort and money into remaking this game, then the only appropriate and sane response is to invest the bare minimum amount of money into buying it.

[i]This review is written from my own perspective who never played the original version released in 1999. Hence, I considered such remake is my novel and very first experience to the epic story segment of Resident Evil 3.[/i]

[h1] Resident Evil 3 (remake) is generally recommended subject to my own perception [/h1]

Just finished my first play through on Standard difficulty. As I have completed Resident Evil 2 Remake ("RE2") many times on various difficulties, my feelings after finishing Resident Evil 3 Remake ("RE3") are somewhat unexpected. 

Subjectively, there are two contradict flows of emotions emerged in my head after the credit roll:
[b](i) RE3 is a very promising title and considered as a bright stone for the whole legendary Resident Evil franchise of CAPCOM;
(ii) RE3 was kinda rushed in production and many core values contributing to the excellency of its predecessor RE2 are absent;[/b]

In short, I think RE3 is worth-investing your time, the game is generally fun to play and also really challenging. Honestly, albeit the overwhelming of negative reviews swarming everywhere on the internet, I enjoyed every moment of the game in my first play through. Nevertheless, I cannot deny the shortfall of RE3 in comparison with RE2 in the remake family. 

[h1]My assessment: Resident Evil 3 Remake is an excellent game being put under urgent and somewhat negligent production process.[/h1]

To backup my claim, I will only go over all the factors that subject to my own opinions are what have contributed to the shortfall of RE3 in comparison to its predecessor.

1. First thing first: the price tag is unreasonable. I pre-purchased both RE2 as well as RE3 and remember when RE2 was first released on Steam store, its price was accounted to only 3/4 of the current price of RE3. Both games were supposed to be released at the same time (please correct if I were wrong) because they were subject to the same level of production. Thus, their corresponding price should be similar. Nevertheless, the customers have to pay approximately 25% more for RE3 despite this game reuses a lot of assets implemented in RE2. For instance, a majority of R.P.D can be re-discovered in RE3 as well as other locations. In my opinion, the price for RE3 is higher due to the fact that it also comes with multiplayer mode so-called Resident Evil: Resistance. 

2. Duration of gameplay is fairly short. Back in RE2, it took me roughly 20 hours to finish the story from both Leon and Claire approaches for both first run and second run. However, it is pretty straightforward in RE3. You play as Jill Valentine for certain sectors, then switch to Carlos for certain sectors as well, then come to the end. The whole process took me about seven (07) hours to complete. The replayability values for RE3 are just for unlocking new overpowered weapons, figures, achievement, concept art and contemplating Jill Valentine in new outfits (not sure about the upcoming DLCs, if any). The urge for you to replay the game instantly from a whole new approach and route is no more. That's why I think it is so frustrating to pay $60 for roughly 07 hours of gameplay.

3. Very poor puzzle design. What makes Resident Evil franchise great is puzzle. However, I barely encountered any challenge as to solving puzzles in RE3. Spoiler alert, the only time I can feel like playing puzzle is the time when Jill Valentine setting up the route for the underground train. So disappointed to accept the fact that puzzle elements were poorly implemented in RE3. The hard times working out solutions for chess plugs, circuit board, dispersal cartridge, etc as appeared in RE2 are completely gone in RE3.

4. Nemesis is terrifying, but scripted. Yes, it is undeniable that Nemesis is much more dangerous and insidious than Tyrant - Mr.X in RE2. However, you will only encounter him in (i) certain scripted scenarios where he will chase and you have to run, perform certain button-pressing sequences to escape, and (ii)  during boss fight. It is more quick-time-event driven rather than random ambush and encounter. Such premise, ironically, makes Nemesis become predictable and rest assured that after these scripted scenes, he will disappear. Therefore, the overall ambiance of RE3 is much less scarier than that of RE2. The fear of something indestructible stomping around searching for you randomly is halted in RE3. This mechanism of Nemesis extremely disappoints me, since Mr.X really screwed me many time in R.P.D. 

5. Cut contents. I have never played the original Resident Evil 3, it would be unqualified for me to talk about these cut contents. As I read on the internet, the original game offers bunch of interesting contents  that I really love to see in RE3. These contents would certainly help to prolong the duration of gameplay and justify the high price of the game. For me, it really upset that I learned about the fact that Capcom cut the second transformation of Nemesis, which makes the game lack one boss fighting phase. Aww!

Excluding the aforementioned, RE3 is a [i]really promising title and offers a lot of enjoyable time[/i], especially during the time of uncertainty amid Covid-19 pandemic. I certainly gonna replay this game many time to seek for more challenges and acquire more unlockables.

Which btw, most things are indeed blatantly re-used from the previous remake. 

The game feels, both in design and overall pace, incredibly rushed and has numerous segments in the game that act as significant testaments to this. Is overall a hell of a lot shorter than the original game due to cut content. Boss fights are very gimmick based compared to the RE2R's bosses. No different routes or choice system as present in the original, and many of the in-game areas from the original were cut from the remake. City exploration is virtually non-existent. You will spend the near majority of your time in/on action sequence set piece areas than you will anywhere else in the game as the majority of the game is littered with them. 

Nemesis is not Mr.X on steroids whatsoever. He's more of a nuisance than a threat to be concerned over, and is pitifully under-utilized over the course of the game. He isn't even a persistent chaser in the remake. His even more heavily scripted behavior compared to the original literally prevents him from doing so, once you've escaped a specified chase sequence of his. Game pace, setting, cohesiveness and quality takes a nose dive not long after the prologue. This is certainly not a game that feels like it was developed over the course of 4-5 years as was implied by the devs but rather a year and a half to 2 years max. After 100% the game I can finally review it. RE3 Remake at this point is a quite polarizing title. Some people praise it as a great RE game, while others are unhappy with changes Capcom implemented, such as removal of some areas and enemies. I'll go through pros, cons, and the neutral side of the game. Keep in mind that A) A lot of this is going to be my personal subjective thoughs, and B) I was never a huge fan of the original RE3. In fact, I personally found it to be the weakest of the original trilogy. 

So, let's start with [b] Pros [/b]

1. The game looks great. Just as RE2 before it, RE3 uses Capcom's RE Engine, and it shows. Characters and surroundings look pretty good, and it's nice to finally see more of Raccoon City in high quality. 

2. There are a lot of things to unlock. Unlike RE2, you don't get anything for finishing the game except for unlocking a new difficulty mode (and one more if you finish it on the new one). Instead, for completing challenges, such as collecting all documents or killing X zombies you get points which can be spent in the in-game shop. Unlocks range from items that can help you on harder difficulties, such as coins which increase your damage and defence, to guns with infinite ammunition, namely Rocket Launcher, Pistol, Assault Rifle and RAI-DEN, a unique weapon that can one shot almost every enemy as long as you hit their weakpoint, but does 0 damage otherwise. 

3. Sections where you play as Carlos have been expanded, and now he takes up roughly 40% of the game. While some see it as a negative, I personally have always liked Carlos, and since he didn't appear in any sequel titles since it's nice to be able to play as him a bit more.

4. Nemesis is much more dangerous than Mr. X in RE2. While you can still play around with him if you perfect your dodge, Nemesis is faster, stronger, and not nearly as forgiving to mistakes. 

5. Nightmare and Infernal changes. Many players were disappointed with 2nd run mode in RE2R, since it was basically the normal game with the Marvin part cut out and an additional boss at the end. RE3 takes a similar approach by giving the player some of his equipment early (magnum is located right at the start after you leave the subway) and swapping some item and enemy placements. However, the changes in RE3 are much more drastic. You start encountering late-game enemies very early on, and some areas might not have any enemies at all just to play with your expectations. 

[b] Neutral: [/b]

1. Music. I personally didn't find the music memorable at all. It's not bad, it does its job, but it's not really something that you'll remember after you stop playing.

2. Dodge mechanic. While OG RE3 did have dodge move, here it's a much more important tool. However, I have a few problems with it. First of all, it can trivialize the experience. From what I've seen, every, or almost every enemy can be dodged as long as you time the evade correctly. This means that in theory the player can be nearly untouchable. There's even an item in the shop that increases your window for perfect dodge, which only makes this ability more OP. My second, and much more pressing issue with it is that it feels like the dev responsible for combat has been playing too much Dark Souls. On difficulty levels above Hardcore (that is, Nightmare and Infernal) dodge is pretty much mandatory, especially in boss fights. This wasn't a big issue for the majority of the game, however, the last boss punishes any mistake to such an extent that the player is pretty much forced to dodge every attack of his perfectly. What ensues is a repetitive rhythm where you evade his combo, destroy one or multiple weak spots, evade combo again and you keep repeating this until the boss is dead. 

3. Jill's looks. While I personally don't find here outright masculine as many other people do, I dislike most of the changes to her design. For the record, this has nothing to do with her outfit, but rather her face and hair. The new haircut just looks awful. However, her STARS outfit from the first game is available in the game as an unlockable costume, and it's a massive imrpovement. Ever since I unlocked it I didn't use any other costume (not that there are many, Jill has 3 and Carlos has 2). Her hair there is shorter, or at least seems so, and she wears her trademark beret.

4. S Rank and shop unlocks. I'm not sure if this is a bug (though I highly doubt that considering that this game is built even more around replaying it than any other RE I've played), but the unlockable weapons and items don't affect your end-game rank. What that means is that you can theoretically save up for a rocket launcher and breeze through hardest difficulty with S rank. I don't really have a huge problem with that, but it just seems like a very weird change. For the record, this also doesn't disable specific achievements. For example, you can get two coins that allow you to regenerate HP to "fine", and get an achievement for never using a healing item. 

[b] Cons [/b]

1. Game length and linearity. The game is pretty short and can be finished in less than 2 hours (in fact, that's the intended time for S rank on most difficulties). While this usually was fine for RE titles, since you constantly got unlocks to play around with, another issue RE3 suffers from is that it's much more linear than other games. Unlike RE1 or RE2 which, while somewhat linear, usually threw you into some big area and let you figure things out before moving to next one (Mansion-Guardhouse in RE1, RPD-Sewers in RE2), here most areas are extremely linear and have almost no side rooms to explore. Raccoon City section that was featured in the demo and the hospital are the only areas that feel open and allow the player to look around and figure things on their own. Other areas, including the RPD section with Carlos, are extremely linear and have almost no deviation from the path except for one or two additional rooms that the player is going to pass by anyway. These two issues lead to my next complaint:

2. Pacing. The game's pacing is pretty good at the start, but after you leave the first area it just becomes weird. At one point the game very rapidly swaps between Jill and Carlos which just looks sloppy. 

3. Cut content. There's a lot of information available online about cut content, such as enemies and locations. While I personally don't mind the removal of most of those things (except for giant spiders. Come on Capcom give us giant spiders in a 3rd person view RE), it's undeniable that the amount of content that was cut is huge, and things that replace it, such as the expanded hospital section, aren't an equal exchange. 

4. Nemesis appearances. Sadly Nemesis in his Tyrant-looking form doesn't appear for that long. Around 30% point he transforms into a giant feral monster and until the very end all his appearances are going to be like that. Another issue is that the sections where he does appear don't last very long. The only area where he really "stalks" the player is the very first area featured in the demo, with most of his other appearances afterwards being for scripted boss fights or escape sequences. 

5. Physics downgrade. Corpses no longer seem to have ragdoll physics, instead falling into a specific pose depending on death animation. In addition to that limbs that the player shoots off don't fall on the ground like in RE2, instead magically disappearing, and in one section near the end of the game even corpses disappear, bursting like corpses in the No Way Out section from RE2's DLC.

I hit the word limit, so I'd like to say that despite everything I still liked RE3, and would recommend it if you can get it on sale or from key store for cheap.

[h1]OVERVIEW[/h1]
[b]Game Description[/b]
After the success of the Resident Evil 2 Remake, it was only natural that Capcom was going to follow up with a remake of another classic RE title. In Resident Evil 3, you take control of Jill Valentine, who awakens to a nightmarish outbreak happening in Racoon City. Now she must escape from the city, along with the mercenary Carlos Oliveira.

[b]Short Review[/b]
Resident Evil 3 is unfortunately far from as good as Resident Evil 2, mainly due to a lack of puzzles, and the game being way too short for the AAA price tag to be justified.

[b]Pros and Cons[/b]
+ Intense gameplay
+ Nemesis is scary
+ More diversity in terms of environments
- Too short
- Lack of puzzles
- Undeveloped plot twist
- Not enough Nemesis sequences
[b]RATING: Mediocre[/b]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2323028492]Click here to see my rating chart[/url]
Even if you can come to terms with the game being very short, I would recommend you wait for a sale.

[h1]FULL REVIEW[/h1]
Last year, Capcom set the bar for remakes with the release of Resident Evil 2, a fresh take on the classic game from 1998. Now they've returned with yet another remake, this time of the sequel, Resident Evil 3. But can it manage to live up to the expectations?
[link
The gameplay, to start, is very reminiscent of that of RE2 Remake; the ammo is sparse, and you'll need to think before firing your gun, and health can be recovered by consuming herbs. If you've played RE2, you know the deal. One of the new mechanics is the ability to dodge incoming attacks, leading to more fast-paced combat. You can no longer perform counter-attacks when being grabbed by enemies, so dodging is very important. Other than that, there aren't many changes to the gameplay, other than a few small adjustments. One thing the game lacks is puzzles. RE2 was filled with puzzles to solve to progress, which resulted in a little break from the intense combat. RE3 only has a few puzzles, and they're all pretty simple and not very hard. While I can see that the devs might have chosen to do this to make the game more action-packed, it does result in the game not being as engaging as RE2.

In terms of visuals and audio, the game is just like its predecessor. The graphics are stunning with lots of small details, and the audio design helps you immerse yourself into the game world. That being said, the atmosphere doesn't feel very scary, unlike Resident Evil 2. There are only a few jumpscares, and only one of them managed to scare me.

The environments are more diverse this time, ranging from downtown city areas filled with stores to loot from, to underground sewers filled with disgusting monsters. The game does reuse a lot of assets from RE2, which is a shame, and a portion of the game even takes place in the R.P.D, with some of the same puzzles and locations being accessible.

The last thing I want to talk about is the story. It takes place both before and after the story of RE2. You play as Jill Valentine, a member of the S.T.A.R.S. team, who suddenly finds herself in the middle of a nightmare. It took me about 5 hours to complete the main story (not including cutscenes), which is very short for a price of 60€. A price of 30€ would've been fairer. During the game, you're often going to be chased by Nemesis, a biohazard weapon with only one goal: to kill you. These parts of the game are very intense, and Nemesis himself is much more dangerous than Mr. X, being able to run towards you, grab you from afar and much more. Sadly, these segments are only apparent at the beginning of the game, after which Nemesis only appears in boss battles.

Sometimes you'll also get to play as Carlos Oliveira. These sections are much easier than Jill's, resulting in them becoming a bit dull compared to hers. While the story of the game is engaging, there is also a plot twist, which I, of course, won't spoil. Unfortunately, this plot twist is way too undeveloped, and not very memorable.

While not as good as RE2, the game is still a fun experience, but it's way too short for the price tag to be justified.

We know how amazing was the original trilogy for Playstation. We also know how Capcom is trying to bring back these old classics with their new engine to give us a chance to experience the same feeling with a new makeup.
Resident Evil 2 remake was a huge success, even though that game lacked a lot of content compared to the original. It brought us back the survival horror feeling to us old timers, but it also gave the newcomers a very good game to play.
Resident Evil 3 did the same thing. It was inspired by the action mechanics of the original and followed more or less the same approach the prequel's remake did: "Give players a new experience while paying a tribute to the original".
The original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis was a short game though and more action oriented, as already stated. It also was rich of scripted events and was very fast.
The remake follows the same pattern but, unlike the previous remake, tries so much of being a tribute to the original by adding references at all costs and... well, it feels weird sometimes and it feels even weirder the moment you realise a core part of the original game has been omitted and the whole game appears to be rushed.
The game is great, I replayed it already and I have fun with it but the cut content killed the "reference game" which could've been handled a bit better, perhaps. I will make examples below with spoilers, so be careful.

[spoiler] 1) Dario Rosso: We know he wasn't that relevant in the original game, but the acting and the dialogues served the purpose of building tension from the beginning. In RE3R he is useless, you encounter him "randomly", right after meeting and straight away saying goodbye to Brad, and he was just standing there waiting for Jill to talk to him to then run away hiding in the container while quoting some of the lines from the original. It was so disappointing.
2) Brad Vickers: He was handled better than Dario but I hoped it would be a bit more relevant in the first section of the game. However he was still loyal to his demise in the RPD main entrance.
3) Marvin Branagh: You see him for literally 5 seconds in the last scene with Brad. In the trailer he felt more relevant, he was not, but that was the same with the original game where he was just lying on the floor fainted.
4) Resident Evil 2 Remake 2F broken wall: There was a speculation about that broken wall implying that Nemesis passed through it and destroyed it while chasing Jill in the RPD.
The RPD section is completely different than the original game but I guess that was a change in the script by the developers. Re3R doesn't add anything to that wall even though it is still intact.
There are other things but I think I spoiled already too much.[/spoiler]

Conclusion: This remake is a bit of a downgrade compared to the previous one but that doesn't make it a bad game at all. It's fun, it's also scary at times, it feels great to blast zombies and it's also very hard and rewarding if played on higher difficulties. Graphically is impressive and the sound effects are mind blowing.
There's even a free interesting multiplayer game added to the purchase but that's probably a way to counter the short length of the main game.
I forgot to say something about Nemesis, the main element of the game. He has been handled in a proper way, in my opinion, sadly the cut content affected him too, obviously but that didn't stop him from being amazing.
I recommend this game cause it's good, maybe with another year of development it could be even better, but it's nostalgic for the fans like me and I think it is very entertaining for everybody even the ones who aren't familiar with the original game.
Resident Evil 2 Remake had tons of flaws too and its length wasn't that huge as well but was still a great game just like this one.
Perhaps is better to wait for the price to drop a bit but I definitely recommend to buy this game at some point, it's totally worth to play.

[h1]RE3 Remake recommended![/h1]
This game is decent in my opinion. If you played RE2 Remake, you know Capcom has tried to learn from their mistakes and fix the problems in RE3 Remake. 

In the following, I will talk about what is good and what is not-so-good in RE3 Remake, hope you can read it until the end of this simple review.

[h2]The good ones[/h2]
RE3 Remake introduces a [b]new dodging system[/b] that does not appear in RE2 Remake. Instead of strafing left and right to dodge your enemies ahead of you, or running around in circles hoping the boss won't hit you, the new dodging system gives a more fun experience to the players, as it feels satisfying when you perfectly timed a dodge and get a good chance to kill your enemies, especially when you are able to execute a [spoiler]"Carlos punch"[/spoiler] to an enemy, which gives you more time to shoot or run away. 

Weapons feel more satisfying than in RE2 Remake, sounds are more realistic and visual effects look decent. 

As a person who hasn't played the original RE3, I could not tell if the story is good or not. However, Capcom learnt from their mistakes from RE2 Remake, which was disconnecting Leon and Claire too much throughout the campaign. In RE3 Remake, although you don't get to choose which character you want to play first, the two main characters Jill and Carlos crossover much more than how Leon and Claire did, so I would give a thumbs up to Capcom here.

[h2]The not-so-good ones[/h2]
Zombie movements are just as weird as the ones in RE2 Remake, some of them would just bang their heads into the wall and get stuck in that position until the player shoots them. [b]Capcom[/b] please fix this :P

The story is rather shorter than RE2 Remake, my first run (in assisted mode) is completed in 3:42:26, which is much shorter when I played RE2 Remake for the first time, which was like 12 hours (yeah I was so slow becoz I played on the ps4 and I got scared easily back then). 

Maps are kinda small compared to RE2 Remake, there are less rooms and spaces for the player to explore, resulting in a room packed with an absurd amount of supplies, ruining the scariness of running out of ammo/healing items.

There is one scene (spoiler alert) that makes RE3 Remake into a "just mindlessly shoot and kill all of them for the game to continue" game. [spoiler] In a hospital scene, Carlos have to defend Jill and whoever his teammate is called from a wave of zombies. However, that scene turned the game into a mini WWZ game as there are so many zombies coming in every now and then, which does not match what RE was suppose to be: slow and methodical. It's like how RE6 was presented back then.[/spoiler]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
RE3 Remake has carried some of the goods from RE2 Remake, but also some bads, as well as its own problems. But if you are the type of player who does not care much about these details or small parts in the game, you are going to have a good time player RE3 Remake.

Therefore, I recommend this game.

Not a bad game at core but there's so much lacking, and now that this exists I'm genuinely afraid that RE3 for the PS1, which is my favorite title in the Resident Evil series, is never going to get the proper remake treatment like 1 and 2 did. 
This has very little incentive of generating replay value unlike 2 did last year, but knowing how the last release was i anticipate or at least hope more stuff will be added over time. (However the purchase does actually come with 2 games, you also redeem the multiplayer title RE Resistance. I won't go into detail on it, it doesn't have its own Steam Store page yet.) 
I can say it's pretty great as a reimagining (not remake) until about halfway through when it becomes clear the developers lost all comprehension of what made the Nemesis such an intimidating setpiece by giving him a stupid animalistic transformation. Some of his most iconic moments are gone too like he no longer kills Brad who instead gets taken out by standard zombies, and on top of all that, his encounters are now purely scripted. You won't experience being actively hunted down like with Mr. X in RE2. This is all a shame because I'd even say his first form is fundamentally an improvement with added abilities of leaping across areas to block your escape route and even using multiple weapons.
Also, I have to mention at some point that some of the game's most iconic locations are gone (the graveyard along with its worm boss fight, and clock tower, mainly) The clock tower's story events now take place in a hospital in this remake, so a even quick jaunt through these areas may have honestly been enough.
Lastly it's worth noting that the original RE3's replay value came in the form of choices that affect the outcome of the plot but now the story has been largely rewritten and every event is set in stone. This does have some benefits in that it expands on a few characters that were originally largely ignored, but I would have preferred them to take an extra year or two implementing dynamic choice-based playthroughs if nothing else, instead of crunching and rushing the game out. I know game development is very different nowadays, but it does not look good when you take a step backwards from a game that came out in 1999.
This is worth playing, but not worth its current retail price. If you want to play through it then you absolutely need to play the original as well, because you'll miss out on a whole bunch of stuff.

- Graphics are good for the most part, besides the 30 fps zombies in the distance
- Voice acting & character movements look great
- Gameplay feels smooth, and the dodge mechanic is pretty fun once you master it
- Multiple difficulties to try out 
- The game is short (I beat it in about 5 1/2 hours on my first run). The RE2 remake was pretty short too, but I think it's more noticeable in the RE3 remake because they cut out some locations from the original game. I list this as a pro because this game doesn't overstay its welcome. Even though I would have preferred a longer campaign, this short and sweet/fresh experience satisfied me still. 

Cons:
- This is half pro/half con, but the fact that they cut a lot out of this remake that was in the original 1999 RE3 is a bummer, but in addition, they also reworked the whole game, so it's a fresh experience for new and old re3 fans.

- It's 2020... I expected Nemesis to be a little more intelligent and stronger than the original RE3, but in this remake, he goes down with 1 grenade & mainly stalks you in the beginning of the game. After that, he just becomes scripted boss battles. (However, his boss battles are extremely cool). 

- Where are the puzzles? There are only like 5-6 puzzles max, and most of them aren't even actual puzzles that require thinking. It's mostly "Go pick up this item, and put it here". There was only one puzzle I did that actually took some time, but overall, the puzzle aspect of this game is little to non-existent. 

- The cutscenes are intense and good looking, but there are way too many scripted moments and cutscenes in this game. Resident Evil isn't known for that in my opinion. While I still enjoyed watching them, I prefer to have control over my character most of the time, rather than the game play it for me. 

VERDICT: 9/10

While 60 bucks is a little too much for a game this short, we also have resident evil resistance included. That game isn't everyone's cup of tea, but at least it's included to help kill time. If you don't plan on playing resistance, then you might want to wait for a sale on RE3. Not a perfect remake, but it's definitely one worth remembering.

Quick:
     1/5  This game is horrible.  I find it hard to say anything good about it.
More:
     I have never been more disappointed with the purchase of a game, than with Resident Evil 3 (2020).  It is astonishing, at least to me, that such a well renowned 'Triple-A' game and the successor to VGC's Game-Of-The-Year 2019 could be so lackluster.  It emits the stench of laziness and rushed development.  I sincerely wonder if anyone play-tested this with a shred of objectivity at their disposal (or reviewed it with that same objectivity in mind, for that matter).  I think there is no way that the bulk of testers, if there were any, did just that.  Where do I begin?
     The dialogue is abysmal.  There are so many corny one-liners, quotes, and instructions that quickly it became unbearable.  It is a wonder that my eyes did not roll completely out of my skull during my play-through.  Almost every tense cut-scene and character building story-beat was interrupted with some cheesy line that destroyed my immersion.
     The protagonist is uncharismatic and unbearable.  No well written or believable character would attempt so desperately to sound like an action hero, or a knock-off Arnold Schwarzenegger when surrounded by that much death, despair, and destruction.  Not even a person who once survived a mansion full of zombies and grotesque monstrosities.  Especially not a person who once survived a mansion full of zombies and grotesque monstrosities.  It's tone deaf.  People are dying all around.  The entire city's population are infected and being eaten alive.  Meanwhile... the protagonist comically insults a giant menacing eight foot tall asocial and amoral death machine, and then struts off.  That death machine in the previous scene involving the protagonist killed dozens of people swiftly and callously in front of her, while she was helpless to do anything about it and she barely survived the encounter.  Yet the monster is just an -insert curse word here- ... and she's so unconcerned about it's presence that she nonchalantly walks away and assumes that it is dead.  This is after falsely assuming she killed it before, and realizing that she did not do so.  She even remarks about this to her self avowed not-partner.  She literally tells him that she thought she killed it, while being attacked by it, and running for her life in a scene prior to the one in which she verbally jabs it casually.
     The scripted game-play sequences are ridiculously grand.  They are everywhere, and they occur all the time.  It's annoying.  There are so many over-the-top scenes in this game that I just stared blankly at the screen on several occasions while wondering what the developers were thinking.  I assumed that they were thinking what Ron Burgundy was thinking when he wanted more graphics.  
     I haven't even gotten to the game-play, yet, and I'm already weary of writing this review.  The game-play is bad.  It contradicts itself at every turn.  There are sparse amounts of ammo in the game.  There is even a document explaining this to you in the beginning, and imploring you to take advantage of mixing gunpowder to ensure that you have as much ammo as possible.  Why then, is there a section in the game in which you are trapped in a room with enemies that you have to kill, almost immediately following another section in which you are presented with a new type of enemy that takes copious amounts of ammo to put down?  This makes no sense whatsoever.  There is even a document explaining that this new threat can heal so rapidly that the staff in charge of overseeing it have requested special weapons for it.  If the player is supposed to save ammunition, then why are they presented with enemies that are bullet-sponges?  Why is the player forced to engage with those enemies directly before an encounter where it is mandatory that you have enough ammunition to progress in the game?  If the player isn't supposed to engage those enemies... then why do they have a supernatural ability to grab you, and attack you from almost any angle and at long distances?  Why also, do they have the ability to attack you before you've recovered and had a chance to respond to a previous attack?  All of this game-play feels cheap, tawdry, pedantic, and nonsensical.  
     There are so many over-the-top scenes and barely interactive quick-time events in this game.  The developers filled up the kitchen sink with every game-play trope that they could find and threw the sink at the game until the game began bursting at it's seams with cliche features.  There are quick-time events, mobs of enemies that spam you repeatedly, and there's even a wave defense portion in this game.  It's abysmal.  I can sincerely say that I do not recall one single moment in this game where I was having fun or feeling anything other than frustration or cynical detachment.  The characters, all except for one, are unlikable and uninteresting.  The story is shallow, under-developed and boring.  The game-play is atrocious in it's execution and laughable in it's contradictions.  I do not like anything about this game.  I would say that I like the graphics, yet I spotted a lot of reused models from the Resident Evil 2 Remake.  Therefore, I'm going to assume that most of these models are leftovers from another game that were unused.  So in essence, I like Resident Evil 2's graphics, and I'm not fond of this $60 in-house asset flip that should be DLC for an older game.

A quick word about me: I grew up on Resident Evil. Since I was 8 years old in 1998, I've been watching, playing, fearing, nightmaring, dreaming... everything about the survival horror Resident Evil games (so, Zero through Code Veronica). The original and Nemesis is the source of many of my greatest fears. It's also easily in my top five favorite games of all time. I've played the Resident Evil 2: Remake, and rated this a 90/100. I thought it was a good modern telling of the story, and while it did take detours, it still remained on track for majority of the game. I did still prefer the layout and story of the original, though. But gameplay wise, I find re2make to be the best zombie game of all time, and it's not even close. 

Back to here: So, I've just completed the game for the first time... a single 9 hour session (minus 10 minutes to walk the dog). I am not at all complaining about the time spent... that is the least of my worries on why I am writing this review tonight. There's quite a bit of replay value (as with any Resident Evil), so those complaining it's too short aren't very valid in my eyes. 

What is a valid complaint, is that this is somehow titled... Resident Evil 3. 

I want to be perfectly clear: I did not expect this to be a shot by shot remake... I played re2make, and understood the direction this game likely would have followed. However, while re2make made significant changes, you still had an idea of where they were coming from. While the laboratory in re2make looked completely different, you at least knew what they were trying to pay homage to, for example. In addition, if they were to change the clothing and names of the characters, make the setting not Raccoon City, and title this Resident Evil 8... I would be a heck of a lot more forgiving here. This is a fairly entertaining and fun game. The fact is, this is called Resident Evil 3, so no matter how you would like to skew it, you need to base this on the original. 

And I'm sorry. It's just not there. 

Too much is changed. Too much is cut. Too many iconic moments are not there. Where is Nemesis? What in the ungodly blue hell is that second and final form supposed to be? This is most certainly not survival horror (and before some kid wants to tell me that the original was more action packed than the second... I'm extremely aware of this fact... but re3 original was still survival horror). Why in the flying youknowwhat is Jill literally picking up the cannon and firing it at the end? This is not Resident Evil 3. This is barely Resident Evil. But more importantly, this is not Resident Evil 3. 

They did do one thing right: They took Nemesis out of the title, as he's barely present in this game. And when he is, he feels extremely stage-y. He's not the persistent, random attacking titan he is in the original. He feels very scripted, way moreso than Mr X. While after you play re2make once you can very easily learn how to make Mr X a simpleton, I found Mr X way more challenging, difficult, and annoying on my first playthrough, than I did Nemesis in this game. That should not happen. I think Nemesis only had two occasions where he randomly stalks you... elsewhere, his appearances were chase scenes or scripted boss battles in an arena. And when he did show up randomly, he was so easy to dispatch... just a single frag grenade brings him down, AND gives you a prize. And even on hardcore mode, these frag grenades are plentiful, and almost always one popped up immediately preceding an encounter. There also really wasn't any jump scares involving Nemesis... and to make matters worse, the two that were in the game, were in the teasers... so you already saw it! Sure, when he grabs you on the ladder it still makes you shout a curse, but I expected it! Why would you show that in the teasers, when that was your only good jump scare!? Nemesis is supposed to be the main attraction in this game, and he's a complete dud. Don't even get me started on his second form. Whoever made the decision to take Nemesis, and turn him into that... needs to never have a creative job again. There's doing things differently, then there's messing things up beyond any comprehension. I'll let you decide how I feel about this "change". Nemesis running around aimlessly like a dog in a circle... you have absolutely got to be kidding me. 

There are no ink ribbons, making saving completely useless, and the auto-save feature is so frequent and obvious, that you know whenever something bad is coming. Why do games do this? Why do games completely ruin any surprise? Once you see the auto-save icon, you know to get out your big guns, or go back to the item box and get your stuff. I have no idea why they went for this change. It completely ruins it. With the auto-saves, death has no consequence, and when death has no consequence, you play sloppy because you just don't care. And that's how I felt majority of my time on this game. 

While there are a fair amount of different enemies, they only appear in certain sections of the game (besides one occurrence, which was a rare bright spot), making the game feel... yet again... stage-y. I liked the variety of the enemies, and would've liked to have seen them more dispersed throughout the game, or with other enemies as well. While talking about enemies and rare bright spots, I liked how they made the zombies smarter... ie, it was difficult to knife them on the floor because they'd lunge at you while ascending, unlike in re2make. 

And I have to be honest... I've written how many words here, and that's the only positives I could think to mention. I did like the dodge mechanic, and I liked that Carlos had a different ability, but he shouldn't have been able to use that on Hunters. Carlos getting more play time was also a welcomed change. Carlos taking Jill's spot in the RPD was an awful design choice. And if I can turn the rage meter down a smidge, I did really enjoy the game and was wrapped up in it up until the train crashes and Carlos plays at the RPD, when you realize that Jill will never see it, and then the second form battle happens at the Clocktower (that again, you don't properly see), and that was it for me, as the rest of the game is a complete mess. 

In closing, while I normally would still "recommend" games with the score I'm about to give, Steam only gives these two options, and I feel more strongly on the "not recommend" side. If only to (fail to) attempt to waiver that very positive score it has now. If I give it a lukewarm rating, but still recommend it, then Steam doesn't let Capcom know that people are unhappy. So, there's that. At least I could have tried. At the end of the day, I can't remember the last time I was this sorely disappointed and unhappy with a game I've purchased and played on launch. After re2make, I thought I could get back to trusting Capcom again. But, this game just goes to show you, it's extremely difficult to blindly trust any creator nowadays. I'm going to rate this a barely passing 65/100. If this game was titled something different, this score would be in the 70-80 range. But it gets an instant demotion for attempting to wear the crown that Resident Evil 3 deserves.

Update: I was able to 100% the game in under 20 hours, and 4 playthroughs. While the harder difficulties offer somewhat more of a challenge and additional scares, they are negated by shop items, and the fact that you already know the game by heart at this point. The hardest difficulty also doesn't have auto-save, which is good. Playing the game more made me realize some problems from re2make have not been fixed (ie, you need to load game twice to reset the timer properly on death, zombies animate at a very low FPS at some distance, some textures in the RPD and elsewhere are extremely low resolution), which doesn't help. Ammo also doesn't always stack properly in your inventory. Ultimately, these findings will decrease my final score to a 60/100

Did I enjoy the hours I spent playing? Yes. And you will too. Sadly, those hours spent come at a hefty price tag of $60.00 for such a small amount of content .... and worse, offers little in the way of replay value when compared to RE2R or any other entries in the franchise (a hallmark for all Resident Evil games). As such, I can't recommend this game at its full listing price. [b]WAIT FOR SALE.[/b]

For anyone looking at this game with even the dullest critical eye, they would immediately notice the game was made in great haste. They could not ignore the exorbitant amounts of content omitted from the original, including entire levels and bosses, fail to mention how the story was vastly changed to account for these omissions. Half of RE3 Remake recycles the exact stages/level designs used in the RE2 Remake (including the Gun Station, Alley/Parking Garage; RPD HQ) and for the new parts this entry brings to the table, it rushes you through their linear level design in such quick and mindless fashion (by way of scripted cut-scenes and Quick Time Events) that you have little time to take in the sights, explore, or enjoy them.

The Demo was very misleading. It offered the most robust amount of content the game has to offer: the [b]only[/b] time Nemesis is hounding you without the involvement of scripted cut-scenes/quick time events; the most open level design the game features; and the most exploration/puzzle solving. The rest of RE3 Remake puts you in very linear levels, generally fleeing from Nemesis (every other footstep) with very little puzzle solving or exploration. Items (including weapon/equipment upgrades) are haphazardly thrown into the game with little thought. 2 hours in and you've already maximized your shotgun + pistol, and all bag slots to boot --- and without having to do anything challenging or mind-boggling feats to accomplish them. From a player's perspective, the game oozes of rushed design with little creative thought put into the product, nor does it feature enough content/level design for Capcom to allow themselves even had they wished to do so. 

Overall, while the game plays well and looks fantastic (it does look amazing, especially when compared to RE2R), it simply does not offer enough in its 5-6 hours of game time, replay value, or other offerings to warrant it's own game and $60.00 price tag. It honestly feels more like a good DLC package for RE2 with enhanced graphics and dodge mechanics thrown in.

It's a shame Capcom didn't take another year to really craft this out like they did with the RE2 Remake. This is a big miss on their part, and from a consumer standpoint, feels like nothing more than a quick cash grab off their previous surprise success. I can't help but feel frustrated knowing how much better this could have been had they taken the time, nor do I have a clue why they didn't give themselves another year or so of development. It would have benefited [i]everyone[/i].

Alas, I'd love to write a review explaining how RE3R is every bit as great as the RE2R, and while it is responsive and more beautiful looking than its 2019 counterpart, it simply lacks the depth and New Game Modes that RE2R did. 

No one can argue against this feeling more like DLC than a standalone game. There's just no way to avoid the comparisons to RE2R given how much is shared between them: mechanics, game engine, levels, intertwining stories, and nearness to the 2019 RE2R release.

Do yourself a favor and wait until it's available for $25.00 .... along with whatever content they add over the next year and all the costumes. At least by then the modders will have everything up and running without bugs.

[h1] RE3make REview [/h1]

[b] TLDR: Resident Evil 3 Remake is a shorter, faster paced, and action packed game compared to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/883710/RESIDENT_EVIL_2__BIOHAZARD_RE2/] Resident Evil 2 Remake[/url]. I personally enjoyed myself playing the game for the first time. However it may not be worth $60 to you. Overall, thumbs up from me. Also note that you do receive Resident Evil Resistance, the multiplayer game similar to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/381210/Dead_by_Daylight/] Dead by Daylight[/url], with the purchase of this game.[/b] 

[b] A few details before we start:[/b] I just finished my first playthrough of Resident Evil 3 Remake. I played it on hardcore difficulty and finished it in 6 and a half hours. I have never played the original game. My only knowledge and experience prior to playing this remake was from playing the demo disk I had from owning Dino Crisis for PlayStation 1.

[b] Time for my thoughts on the game:[/b] I have seen other reviews of this game. Many state that fan favorite areas from the original game have been removed. I cannot comment on how that impacts the story or the gameplay of this remake. However, I have played the Resident Evil 2 Remake. Other reviews also say RE3make is shorter than RE2make, and it is. People feel like it should be an expansion instead of a full game. I do believe that this game is probably not worth the $60 price tag, at least compared to RE2make. However with all that said, I thoroughly enjoyed the game. It is a bit more fast paced and action-packed than RE2make and I enjoy that bit more personally, although I can definitely see people having the opposite reaction to that. The characters and story of the game were fine to me, nothing spectacular, and about what I was expecting from a Resident Evil game. Nemesis wasn’t quite as terrifying as Tyrant, but he was distinctively different from him. Nemesis is much more of a threat and I found myself dying to him much more often than Tyrant. He is quicker and much more aggressive, which I believe is a big factor with why the game feels much more fast paced than the last game. To switch gears, the game is stunningly beautiful, the lighting in Raccoon City is gorgeous, and the graphics in general are not lightyears ahead of RE2make, but they are slightly better. Just like the last one, this game runs just while being just slightly more pretty. I played at high/max graphics never dipped below 100 FPS and usually maintained around 144 FPS at 1440p with a R5 2600 and RTX 2070 Super. 

[b] Final Thoughts:[/b] I liked it, however if you guys were fans of RE2make and were looking into it, maybe wait for the next sale it is included in to get it.

Eventually I decided to try RE3 myself and when I encountered the first zombie, I was so scared that I turned the game off and didn’t touch the game for years.. Now, 20 years later the remake is here and I cannot recommend this game enough. The game runs identical to the RE2 Remake, aside from a few gameplay changes, such as a dodge move. In my opinion this game plays great. The graphics are beautiful and seeing Raccoon City and exploring the streets was incredible. The story is similar to the original with a few parts changed. Some areas don’t return and some new areas are available. I won’t share my exact opinions on these changes because I don’t want to spoil anything. I personally don’t have any issues with the game other than it felt a bit short. The in-game timer says that it took me about 5 hours to beat the story, while Steam says I have played for around 8. When I played the RE2 Remake for the first time, the in-game timer said it took me about 8 hours to beat the story. Keep in mind that I am the type of person who will explore all of the areas, check every part of the map, read all the notes, and will happily backtrack. And to me, RE3 Remake still felt a bit short. It is important to note that in both games, I chose to play on Hardcore for my first playthough. There were sections of this game that I felt like were going by too fast, but other than that, I had a blast playing this game. Being a huge Resident Evil fan (yes, I have played them all), I can see myself spending so much time replaying the story and trying all of the challenges the game offers. To be honest, the issue about the game feeling short isn’t even a problem for me. When I think about it, the original games aren’t that long. Some might say this one isn't as good as the RE2 Remake, I'd probably agree. But more from a place of RE2 being my all-time favorite than RE3 Remake being too flawed. The game is way shorter than RE2, but more because there's a lack of extra sceneries, and the more urgent plot points, when compared with the slower ones in the previous entry, make for a sensation of a very short game. But even so, I can't say I didn't enjoy it or felt the game as a whole was inferior to the original.

RE3 was a shorter game than RE2 even back on the PSX days, and while there a bunch of places cut from this remake when compared to the original I can't honestly say it was anything of much importance. Focusing more on the parts that really got the plot going instead of spreading too much through too much of a big area. Maybe they could've treated Raccoon City's streets as a hub, like the RPD in 2, but then again I think the story pacing is just too different for something like that too work.

The characters are way better fleshed out when compared to the original. While in the PSX game I could say some of the characters were there just for a single scene to play out this time they seem to actually have some unique character. Carlos himself was expanded a lot and having a bigger chance to play him was great.

If anything, I think the only thing they really missed was a chance to get Carlos's stuff to be a separate campaign from Jill's, so we could focus more on him. But then again I feel like the remakes are following too much of the original's structure for it to happen. Besides that, we do have the multiplayer piece to cover for that, though that is a different thing. And luckily it really is completely separated from the single-player experience so you don't have to feel like you're forced into it.

Nemesis itself was fun. Having him following you as a supped up version of Mr. X through the streets was quite tense. And the new versions of his boss battles are really fun. The final battle in special was a welcome upgrade, as you actually had things to do instead of just running around to pushing power sources to shoot a big rail.

In conclusion, this is a good game, a good modern take on the original setting and story with nice visuals and a good time to play through. If it's worth the full price it's up to you but I'd say it's worth taking a look.

This is a personal issue I had with the game, so it may not apply to you but in the first area of the game, Nemesis is so damn annoying. He is very fast so he can catch up to you fairly quickly if you run away. This is not the issue, the issue is the terrible dodge mechanic they implemented into the game. When nemesis catches up to you he attacks you, but how can you see his attack and dodge it if you cant see the attack coming from behind? The only remedy to this is running with the camera facing him, but then you have to dodge zombies blind, and that is equally impossible. Plus his tentacle grab attack is near impossible to dodge, and you lie on the ground for literally 10 seconds which breaks the flow of game play so much. 

This is the only 'true' encounter with Nemesis, the other encounters in the game are QTE's and boss fights (and not very good ones at that). The final boss fight with Nemesis is possibly one of the worst fights in any game I have played recently, it is abysmal. Dodging an instant kill move with an essentially broken dodge mechanic is not fun.

A good, criminally short re-telling of the classic Resident Evil 3.

Let's start with the bad:

While the game is enjoyable, it ultimately left me disappointed, or at least wanting more,....a lot more. Huge chunks of the original game are simply missing here with very, VERY FEW (if any) light puzzles scattered around the 5 hour campaign (Yes, only 5 hours, and that's with me trying to collect everything). Nemesis, while good in my opinion, is nowhere near as threatening as the 1999 version, with scripted encounters and is massively underutilized. While RE2 Remake got the 4th survivor mode (a nod to 1999 RE3's Mercenaries mode), Capcom decided to omit Mercenaries mode from this remake altogether.

Now the game also got a lot of things right: the original (re-scored) music is there, not only in save rooms as RE2 Remake did, but also while roaming around the streets of Raccoon City, which invoked feelings of nostalgia and the same dread I felt 20+ years ago. Gameplay is spot on (same as RE2 Remake), and the new versions of the characters (specially Jill) are better than the original. 

In conclusion, I would recommend this game to any Resident Evil fan or any fan of the survival horror genre in general, however, fans of the original telling like myself will be left disappointed with the lack of iconic content that made the original game oh so charming.

I love this game. I also love seeing the reviews hating on it for being short. As if the original RE:3 wasn't pretty short itself. Some areas are cut out I will agree, but the areas that are in get much more attention, you spend a lot more time at the hospital for example. Expect your first playthrough to last about 6 hours on a standard pace, if you take the time to look at read all the notes and view all the cutscenes of course. To get S ranking expect to complete the game at 1:45 for hardcore. They did a good job at encouraging following playthroughs, minor rewards you can pick up over time making each run easier, and earning your way to the infinite weapons. 

The soundtrack is an actual soundtrack, which has a good amount of remastered RE:3 soundtrack, which is amazing. Compared to RE:2 remake where I used the original audio versus the remastered audio, I would pick the remastered tracks over original for RE:3. Guns are sastifying to shoot and while you can get yourself quite a bit of ammo if your frugal, you will lose a lot of time in the process. So you have to determine which ammo is vital to get to progress if you want to get a good time. 

My only complaint is how quickly the game picks up, the beginning feels much like a action movie, and while it does settle down I do prefer how the original was over this remake. I see how people see this beginning and complain, however I like how they handled Nemesis. He is much more linear then how Mr. X was handled, but they managed to retain some mechanics that you see from the original game that wouldn’t really have meshed well with a free-roaming boss. I will agree with other reviews that not having the live selections that the original had is disappointing, and does slightly hinder replayability. But I personally can overlook it.

Second-ish complaint, although I’m hoping a mod will fix it soon is the fps issue for zombies farther out, as RE:2 remake had. 

TL:DR; Get the game, don’t spoil yourself of that magical first playthrough. I ignored all media until I played it and I do not regret a single moment. Just be open to a little reworking of how Jill escapes Racoon City compared to the original and you will have a great time.
