Literally takes everything RE2make did right and throws it out the window in favor of more QTE's and action set pieces. I am so disappointed. 

The beginning section of the game is great, solving some puzzles, avoiding enemies, it felt like a continuation of the Resident Evil 2 remake. But around the time the Nemesis appears with the flamethrower the game goes down the toilet. It becomes incredibly linear save for one section halfway through in a hospital where it opens up a bit again and allows for some extra exploration for more supplies and ammo. Soon after however it goes right back to explosions, action setpieces and QTE's. The final boss is literally dispatched by holding W and left clicking once, I kid you not lmao.

It takes the scaling enemies and damage based on how well you're doing from RE2make, which I didn't care for in that game either, and somehow made it more glaringly obvious and worse. The dodge will sometimes function properly, other times it will not, funny enough a lot like the original RE3. 

The voice acting and changes to Jill's character were obnoxious, she comes off as overly sarcastic and annoying. Every other word (this goes for all characters) is ♥♥♥♥ this or ♥♥♥♥ that, it's like a 12 year old wrote the English script. 

The boss fights were all pretty lackluster and incredibly gimmicky wait for X monster to go behind tank, shoot blinking lights. As I mentioned before the final boss was basically just a QTE, with the only gameplay being SHOOT THE GIANT GLOWING ORBS ON THE BOSS TO STUN IT. Nemesis itself felt more annoying to deal with than in the original game, he'll literally teleport behind you if you get to far ahead of him and knock you down or jump in front of you.

There's also literally no replay value other than grinding for points by replaying the game to unlock infinite ammo guns or other bonuses in the shop. Mercenaries mode is missing for some reason. I was under the impression that both games were in development at the same time but after playing through this it feels like Capcom really did just slap this together in a year or so.

I'm very disappointed and I wouldn't waste my money. If you're still curious at least wait for a sale, 30 dollars tops.

The devs clearly didn't understand what made Mr. X so menacing and the (very very few) moments that involve Nemesis stalking you feel more like a chore than a legitimately frightening experience.

Nemesis himself has been drastically changed, taking on the figure of a quadrupedal beast for the majority of the game, which honestly makes him a much less imposing figure in my opinion. The redesigns of Nemesis look great, as does everything else in the game (save for a few moments of wonky lip synching).

The game is highly set-piecy, with many areas existing only to be used by a cutscene with mayyyyybe a quick-time event or two. It feels like they wanted to make a movie more than a video game. That being said, the cutscenes they have in place are all fantastically exciting, especially the beginning. Which brings me to the next issue: this is an action game. You will get far more ammunition than you will healing items, taking away all RE-style tactical decisions to instead just blow through every enemy you see (one enemy in particular you have no choice but to dispatch almost every single time you encounter it).

I like it, all things considered, it was a blast to play, but it tried to do too much with too little and feels like a rushed sequel instead of the fully realized game it is based on.

Oh, also, the humor in the game is very crude and modern (game takes place in 1998), relying on teenage insults far too often. This comes after the very serious RE2make that handled its tone very maturely. It's just jarring and feels completely out of place.

It's a shame no one will read this because it's too far down this list of reviews. After I beat RE3 Remake (RE3R) I initially thought that RE3R wasn't too bad, but I did seem short and I felt like there was a lot missing, missing not only content from RE3 Original (RE3O) but mechanics that were missing from RE2R.

Let's start with the RE2R stuff that was mysteriously not included for RE3R. For example RE2R, you could shoot off limbs of zombies and also there was a defense mechanic with knives and grenades if you were grabbed by an enemy. Instead RE3R had this really weird button smashing that I could NEVER get to work. It was confusing and awkward. They did however add a dodge mechanic, that was pretty helpful. Also RE2R never despawned monsters you killed, they were always there leaving you feel like maybe you didn't fully kill that monster and it would pop back up later(sometimes it did). Not the case in RE3R, once it was dead it was erased like it never happened. Did these missing things really hurt RE3R? No not really, but they would have been a nice touch considering the team responsible for creating RE3R did have access to all the assets of RE2R.

Now let's briefly discuss what I thought was a major issue with missing content. After I finished RE3R in around 8 hours, a couple hours of which I spent just back tracking and looking for things like the bobble heads, I decided to load up RE3O on my playstation. It had been over 10 years since I last played it, I needed to know why I felt something was missing when I played RE3R. Less than an hour in and I realized a few things. #1 RE3R was much faster paced then the original. Almost not stop action and cut scenes. 

#2 Nemesis in RE3R was a minor pest and only bothered you very early on (without a cut scene to acknowledged his presence) in the original he'd chase you all over the damn place without warning. 

#3 Back tracking, this gaming mechanic was common in games for years, DOOM is another example. I know some would argue that this was a stall tactic by developers to increase the game length, maybe it was but I felt that was one way of making the game more complicated. You'd pick up and item and then remember oh yeah I passed the place the item is needed an hour ago OR you'd need to go around trying to figure what goes where etc, while also being attacked by new enemies spawning in areas you'd already cleared. Sometimes you'd have to take a step backward, to again start moving forward this was especially true for these types of games. RE3R pretty much decided to remove that iconic RE mechanic thus shortening the game. This leads into issues 

#4 & 5, exploration and puzzles. RE3O had plenty of this, not as much as RE2 or RE1 but still more than what they gave us in RE3R. I think there was only 1 major puzzle in RE3R the part where you were connecting the train stations. Otherwise, all the puzzles were cut. Exploration you say? There sure as hell wasn't any of that in RE3R, completely and utterly on a roller-coaster rail the whole time with cut scenes in between and this leads into the final issue. 

#6 Content cut from RE3O. Locations missing, yet referenced in the remake such as the brochure about the clock tower. Also no graveyard, no gas station, no newspaper building, no factory or park and enemies were cut too. No crows and gravedigger. Characters were cut down or changed. Brad Vickers was just a passing fart in the wind, Carlos seemed to me to be white-washed. No accent? And what the hell happened to Nicholai, his attitude reminded me of Wesker from RE5. 

Add all this up and you have a game with such a promising title and promising groundwork that was done with RE2R, and you somehow SH*T the bed. With little to no replay value for a $60 game that included a side game no one wanted it's just tough to justify Capcom's decisions. It feels like RE3R was a rushed job that Capcom outsourced it's title to a different company and team that didn't know what do with itself. It knew the game would look great and would play well (thanks to the team that did RE2R) but that's as far as they got. What their final product turned out to be was an expansion to RE2R with a heavy price tag of a separate game. My recommendation is this: plenty of people are going to give RE3R a positive review and Capcom won't consider this title a failure, SO we aren't endanger of not getting other remakes we want ie. RE4 and Veronica. With that being said, don't buy this game at full price. They don't deserve $60 for a 25% reimagining of a game. They deserve a deep discounted price and so do we. My parting words are for Capcom. Don't outsource your ♥♥♥♥ OR at least don't rush your games and expect everyone to clap their hands and pat you on the back. Your fans deserve better.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 (2020) fails to capture and reincarnate the great title that is the original Resident Evil 3. I understand this game is not meant to be a full on remaster, but it still falls flat on every premise. It fails to provide to the gamer the greatest aspect of the original, which is the dynamics.

The original Resident Evil 3 is the most dynamic Resident Evil title out there. Enemy spawns are randomized at certain parts in the game, as well as item spawns. The live decisions you make alter the game, and even such a silly choice as pushing Nemesis off a bridge resulted in you not having to shoot down a chopper. The ammo creation system was unique, and provided the player with a choice that would either save them, or be their demise. Combined with the ability to dodge enemies, these aspects are what make Resident Evil 3 the most dynamic Resident Evil game.

Beyond the mechanics of the original title, we hopefully can all remember the great setting and pace that the game had to it. The characters were all likable (except Dario), the setting was superb (especially the clock tower/town hall, which is absent from the Remake) and the story just had the right time to it. Jill wasn't sassy or uptight, she was just a strong and willfully minded character.

And the greatest part about the original title is of course Nemesis. Single handedly the most intimidating enemy in any Resident Evil game. He could do so many things to mess up your day; shoot you with a rocket launcher, run at you and punch you, grab you and mangle your face like Brad, or just toss you around as if you were a doll. Nemesis was scary, well programmed, and well implemented and designed. He was so glad handedly what made Resident Evil 3 scary.

I've droned on about all of these great things about the original title, so a lot of you may be wondering why I'm writing a review. Well, here it goes.

I spent probably 6 hours trying to configure RE3 Remake to run on my PC, for the game was micro stuttering and had all sorts of issues right off the bat. I had to eventually install Windows 10 on my backup hard drive and run the game on that so it wouldn't stutter. So I ha e had the luxury of spending my time poorly, just to get go this game. So that's a starter.

Now to the actual review. Keeping in mind everything stated previously, it follows that RE3 Remake fails at everything when it comes to the original. The game is very linear, and lacks any variety in how your in game decisions affect the survival horror experience. The dodge mechanic is well implemented, but is not as good as the original. 

The story is lackluster, and is missing many of the interesting scenes/settings that made the original game so great and as stated earlier, the clocktower is gone, so isn't the cemetery and Gravedigger. That's right, Earthworm Jim on roids is not in this game. The game jumps around too much in terms of setting, and fails to be one coherent piece. 

Nemesis falls flat as well. He is poorly implemented, and you only fight the "true Nemesis" once. After the first fight, he just turns into a dog like William Birkin in the original Resident Evil 2. Nemesis is used in mainly scripted chase scenes, and is unfortunately poorly utilized in this game.

While it may be rougher around the edges compared to REmake 2, Without giving any spoilers away, what we didn't get is made up for with what we did get. People can complain about cut content from the original and that is a legitimate grievance but I feel what we got instead was just as good if not better! If you are a fan of Resident Evil, you will be a fan of REmake 3.

Resident Evil 3 tries to do exactly what the previous installment did. And it fails. While RE:2 Remake did provide the same feeling and nostalgic atmosphere while advancing the game in general to fit the "standards" of 2018, RE3 simply does not. It didn't extend the length like the previous game, it didn't improve much even from the 1999 version, just as it didn't deliver as a "sequel" for the remake that came out 2 years ago. RE2 is better in almost every aspect. 

But, does that make it a "bad" game. Probably not. As a really big fan of the 1999 version, I think this is a good enough adaptation for the duration it has. It stayed at 5-7 hours long like the original. It kept the same linear but fun script, gameplay and mechanics. And of course it looks gorgeous. Fun equipment management, terrifying atmosphere and enemies, very good levels and all. 

The bad stuff? The "Nemesis" enemy is totally and 100% scripted. Every single time. They removed the story-line options were you choose what you want to do next that actually impacts the plot. There is no ultra hard difficulty that gives you access to the "ink ribbons" save system. Zombies feel less "interactive" than the previous remake game. Bullets do less impact and everything feels a bit.. "spongy" rather than providing the satisfaction of shooting monster flesh. They completely removed regions, levels like Factory, Clock-tower and ALL the puzzles. It's not that what it has inside the game is bad, but a lot is missing!

My conclusion? It's disappointing if you compare it with the excellent RE2 Remake. It is very disappointing as a remake of the 99' version. But it's not a bad game by any means. It delivers a similar experience as the 1999 version more or less, but a bit botched. Is that bad? Some would say yes because it should elevate it and evolve and provide more. Still, a good enough experience. I only wish it was bigger, with more content, modes and stuff to do after you finish it. 7/10.

Now this is a release I was excited for that I can safely say did not disappoint. RE3 Remake is an excellent follow-up to RE2R from last year and brings back some interesting elements of the original while improving upon them.

First and foremost, the story. Without spoiling anything it's about 3-8 hours long depending on your preferred difficulty setting and overall skill at the game. Most of the core elements of the original are present but events unfold in a much more cinematic fashion than the original if you can believe that.

Enemies are relentless, stubborn and absolutely devastating if you let them do their thing. One death scene in particular had me feeling like I needed a cold shower and I hope that you don't experience it in your runs just for the sake of mental well-being. Many of the old enemies make a return with some key mechanical differences and some with new weak points that you'll have to pin down through trial & error or by reading the files found throughout the city.

Weapons feel just as smooth if not better than last year's instalment with a decent variety throughout the run. Ammo scarcity is still an issue as is the standard with the first three games and some of the side games. Choosing when to fight or run can end up with you running into a tough fight with little offensive power or with an arsenal capable of dealing with anything Umbrella can throw at you.

The wonky dodge from days of yore is back and relegated to a single button press. Timing is still key but a well-placed dodge is all you need to turn the tide in a fight or when running from Nemmy. Thankfully it's a lot more simple due to having its own button, you just need to learn to read each enemy's moves and know when best to use it.

The city layout is great, plenty of open space in many areas and tons of tighter ones that can really nail the horror aspect of the game in a great way. Instead of cheap jump scares the game tends to rely more on back to the wall style encounters where you need to make your shots count and dodge when necessary.

There are some minor flaws that diminish the remake when compared to the original. Some parts of the game are a bit too easy, even on Hardcore. Some enemy types were omitted (though lowkey the new versions of the ones that did return more than make up for it.) More cinematic action which I know is off-putting to some and lastly (though not something I personally care about) Jill's appearance has been less than appealing to some users. I think she's fine as is, but to each their own.

Overall I'm pleased to say RE3 Remake is a resounding success from where I'm sitting. A celebration of a truly legendary game from half a lifetime ago. Thank you Capcom for not dropping the ball again!

Locations that showed off the hellscape that the city became were removed. Clock tower, the pond, the outskirts. these locations changed the mood of the game, as you got further away from the cityscape and concentration of human activity it changed and showed how the outbreak affected not just city life but suburban and rural and the reach and power of the umbrella corp. the graveyard is gone, and it showed how even the virus can affect creatures by leeching into the soil, gravedigger location is gone.  The railway showing different locations was obviously going to be a transit system used to visit several other locations and flush out the story with new encounters, locations, cinematics and puzzles. Creatures were in certain locations in the original that co-incided with their either location of development, or their base ecology; drain deimos and brain suckers were insects in back alleys or the docks. in this there is only one kind of insectile creature and they are only in one location. Resident Evil 3 2020 is a remake of the 1999 game of the same name. Almost none of the original game is here save for characters, some locations and base plot. The game follows STARS member Jill as she tries to escape Raccoon City during the Outbreak that would seal the fate of the town, however a new Tyrant named Nemesis is hunting after the remaining members of STARS and will be her greatest threat in her last escape.  

Before I get into the bad, let's talk about the good. For starters the controls are wonderful, they feel responsive and the aiming and shooting just feel good. Resident Evil 3 introduced a dodge mechanic where Jill could knock back attacks at the last second, this has been completely overhauled compared to the original game and if done correctly will allow Jill to slow down time to counter attack the enemies weak spot, it feels great and looks cool, assuming you don't dodge roll into a zombie for some hugs.While not featuring all the original enemies in the games, crows, spiders and the giant worm boss are gone, most of the enemies we know and love are back, including the Hunter γ, which looks really bad. The game is also optimized extremely well for PC, just like Resident Evil 2 was. Outside of that though, the rest is bad or worse, lackluster.

This game cuts out a lot of content from the original, including large chunks of the town, some are missing altogether while others, like the Gas Station, have been reduced to cut scenes or boss battles. There is no replayability in this game, the branching story choices are gone, the randomized enemies are gone, the multiple endings are gone and the epilogues for the cast of characters are also gone. Item crafting has been dumbed down and you can no longer craft super ammo. Mercenaries mode is gone, though you can unlock 'cheats' via a shop in game that can make going for the S rank, the only reason to keep playing, that much easier. The game itself is extremely short, my first playthrough was under 4 hours and with very little practice you can easily beat this game around 1~1.5 hours on next playthroughs. 

The difficulty of the game is alright. Zombies are still bullet sponges and have long lunges to get you, if you are skilled you can pull of a perfect dodge to escape so they are only a threat if you get corned. Ammo is extremely plenty, even on higher difficulties. The most frustrating thing is enemies, like the hunters, that have 1 hit death kills regardless of health. Depending on the difficulty the bullet sponge hunters will probably hit you with this more than once. Boss fights are also easy, the game gives an abundance of ammo before and during the encounter. Speaking of boss fights, let's talk about the big man himself.

The biggest disappointment is the games namesake, Nemesis. Nemesis is a joke in this game. In the original game, he came in two flavors, scripted battle or surprise battle. Unless it was a forced battle, like the clock tower, you could run and the Nemesis would chase you around, it could be very frantic. In the remake however this only happens in one area and that's the small section of town you can play in the demo. The nemesis will spawn in after a certain event and will hunt around, the thing is however you can backtrack before completing the event and grab all the items making the nemesis chasing after you pointless since getting to where you need to go is easy, thanks to how quick he can go down. One grenade or red barrel will do him in making him pointless. The rest of the encounters are scripted run away sequences that do not pose you any harm, since they always give you a means to stun him (shooting red barrel or transformers). Outside of that you get boss fights, of that there are 4. Only 1 of them is the Nemesis as we know him, he mutates very soon in this game and you have the same boss fight twice with the final boss not really being a boss fight. If anything the bullet sponge zombies will be more terrifying than the Nemesis. Also the iconic and unsettling STARS groan is gone.


At the end of the day, if you love Resident Evil as much as I do you will probably buy this game and play it and you may play it again and again, the original game is still around and people that want a better experience can easily track it down and play it (and I encourage this). The bottom line is this game is a hollow shell of its former self, all of the good stuff has been gutted and replaced with fluff filling that on paper could sound like a lot (more difficulties, unlockable 'cheats' ect..) but it's not a lot when you really look at it. The game is too short, the game has no replayability, the difficulties are just number tweaks, there is no unlockable costumes or game modes at time of writing this to justify a $60 price tag. Your time would be better spent tracking down or buying a copy of the PS1 game and playing that than this until the price drops or on the off chance that more content gets added, but I am not holding my breath.

This is an extremely difficult game to review, especially given my feelings for the wonderful Resident Evil 2 remake last year. This one just doesn't cut it the same way. Resident Evil 2 2019 was a full on remake, building upon the original material to create a contemporary reconstruction of 90s era adventure-exploration horror with resource management and survival elements. It followed the original game's structure and pacing closely while also allowing itself enough wiggle room creatively to create a brand new experience. It was a near-perfect remake.

This remake is no such thing. Many features introduced in Resident Evil 2 2019 (and even the Resident Evil 1 remake back in 2002) have been removed, and substantial sections of the original Resident Evil 3 have been removed entirely to create something far more linear and streamlined. It deviates so far from the source material that it feels more like a "re-imagining" rather than a remake, and it's heartbreaking because the original Resident Evil 3 had so much potential to be renewed after 20 years of industry evolution. This package just feels so shallow in comparison. This "remake" is filled with scripted sequences, removed content, the levels are very linear, and there is little sense of exploration and resource management. As a result, it is predictable, plodding, poorly paced. I replayed Resident Evil 2 2019 at least five times in a row. It was a game filled with replay value and content. I don't imagine myself playing through this game more than twice--if that.

Is Resident Evil 3 2020 a bad game? No, it's not. In fact I'd say it's worth a play-through if you're a fan. But is it great? It's not that either. It's mediocre. Resident Evil 3 1999 deserved much better than this.

Resident Evil 3 first playthrough fun? Yes!
Does it be begged to be played again? Well... No... Unless you are going for S+ Ranks and all of its unlockable weapons. Mind you, you can only really use them for speedruns, mod playthroughs, etc...

For me, this game fell short of expectations, putting alot more into liniar, scripted actions scenes rather than focusing on more complex puzzles, nemesis encounters, etc.

This game has ALOT missing from the Original 1999 release...
Where is the clocktower?
Where are the other Nemesis encounters that are not scripted?
Where is the mercenaries mode?
Where are the spiders, etc?
Where are the animations in the model viewer?
Where's Barry? lol

I will say that the dodge mechanic in this game is NEEDED. When nemesis is sprinting at you, you need to dodge at the right time, come with a little bit of practice.

I honestly feel like this remake is a step DOWN from RE2 remake with its shorter, scripted campaign.

Would I recommend this game? Right now... No... Not at full price. Wait for a sale. Something around the $40AUD price range. 

And hey, we get another entire free game with it that is pretty much online only... I wonder how long that will last before we get tired of it...

I rate this game a 6/10... It would be a 7/10 if the price was 40AUD or lower.

It's a crying shame what this game could have been, because the general gameplay here is absolutely awesome. With REmake 3 largely working in the same engine as REmake 2 both games play similar, however in this one shooting and movement has been refined in welcome ways. Changes like automatically picking up items instead of having to place them in your inventory individually are welcome as well, and improve the pace of the game with no detriment. If this game had a mercenaries mode, I can imagine that it would be incredibly fun.

Nemesis however, has been butchered. Encounters play out identically. He breaks through a wall, chases you to the next saveroom, you exit the saveroom and then one of three things happen: he breaks through another wall and chases you to the next save room yet again, there's a cutscene where something happens that interrupts the chase (like an explosion taking him out of commission for a short time), or he engages you in one of the game's four terrible, terrible boss fights.
The kind of boss fights where your task is to guess what the developer was thinking. The designers were apparently aware of this because if you die the loading screen "hints" tell you exactly what you have to do to defeat him.

The game is 5 hours long. This doesn't mean you're going to spend 5 hours on one playthrough, it means you're going to get 5 hours out of this game. There are no alternate scenarios like in REmake 2, and many annoying sections like the spider room breaker search segment or HORDE WAVE DEFENSE (WHAT THE HELL?!) deter from its replayability. There is also no side content (such as Mercenaries or REmake 2's survivor stories) to speak of. The fact that Project REsistance was originally meant to be a standalone title but was tacked onto this game because of its awful reception tells you everything you need to know about how much value it adds to the purchase of REmake 3. Also it has lootboxes and sells boosters to earn them faster for real money so I won't waste a minute of my life on that and neither should you.

If more singleplayer content is added to the main game I can imagine this being a decent purchase, otherwise I'd recommend getting it on sale, as it is a fun game, but the amount of content offered for the asking price is laughable.

The game is not bad, it's actually pretty fun, but the lack of content, locations, and puzzles hurt the game a lot compared to RE2 2019. Yet at the same time, people need to remember this is not a remake but a reimagining, Capcom is changing the canon.
If this game was cheaper I think it would've been fine but at this moment despite it being really good it lacks content. Hopefully, this gets fixed with a DLC, but at this moment, sadly despite how good it is, it is still disappointing and a missed opportunity.

I suggest waiting for a DLC (if there's any) or get the game on discount, it is a good experience after all but it could've been way better.

Going to break this one down.

Length:

Yes, this game is short. It took me 6 hours on hardcore on the first playthrough going at an incredibly leisurely pace. (Edit: including all the cutscenes) Would have definitely been less had I gone on standard mode, at least an hour or so was spent dying and  replaying boss fights. While RE2 Remake at least had two campaigns that were far too similar and don't make sense as a narrative (perhaps my only complaint about that game as a whole), at least there was something there for a second playthrough.  This is pretty much a one shot game without much replayability. The length might be the biggest flaw at first, but perhaps not the most egregious. 

Source material and pacing:

The elephant in the room is that the game disrespects most of the source material. While RE2 Remake honored most of it's source material, maps, and concepts while adding it's own unique take on it, this one throws most of that out. Sure there were some changes to RE2, but nothing that hurt the overall game. This one falls short of that standard the previous one established.

Did you expect labyrinthine city alleyways packed with zombies and monsters with a constant need to check your map? Did you expect to see iconic locations that you visited in the city the first time around back in '99? Did you expect locations such as the clocktower or the park or maybe the gas station to be fully fleshed out and realized? Almost all of this is stripped from the game, and not really replaced by anything, just a big empty hole. Raccoon City should have been shown as a complete decaying mess, but most of the set pieces seem to have been construction sites. Strangely lazy. I almost don't feel the need to use a spoiler tag on the majority of this review, because if you watched any trailer of this game beforehand you've already seen about 80% of what the game has to offer.  With RE2 you had 3 major sets,the RPD, the sewers, and labs. 75% of the game was connected together, with only the labs being isolated. This meant plenty of places to flesh out, much like the original versions of all the games. Staying true to the "find a key, and back track to find new things" formula that has been tried and true since 1996. This one has completely isolated set pieces that play out in an incredibly linear fashion. So linear in fact, that I don't think I ever even opened my map to look at it. Rarely is any sort of backtracking needed, and if there is, [spoiler] such as early in the city, or late game in the hospital[/spoiler] it is a very short distance. There is also a lack of ink ribbons on hardcore mode and forced autosaves. Probably due to the linear nature of the game making it obsolete. Unfortunate because the lack of ink ribbons really eliminated another strategic element to the gameplay. Also, a staple of every classic Resident Evil, puzzles, are all but gone. Making for an unsatisfying experience. I mean, you literally just pick up new weapons, without having to work for them at all. Adding to the lack of replayablilty, this game neglects the incredibly important choice mechanic of the original. Perhaps this could have brought out different pathways and scenarios, and extended the game's life. Such wasted potential. 

Nemesis, action, and....quicktime events:

Well, for a year we heard, "if you think Mr. X was scary and foreboding, just wait until we have to deal with Nemesis". Except, well, you really don't. Due to the layout of the maps not being connected and so incredibly small, you'll never quite get that feeling you did with Mr. X. X would be a constant looming presence around the RPD. One that would make you cautious how you are moving, where you are going, and make you come up with a strategy for avoiding him. Constantly hearing his footsteps and knowing he's hunting you down adds a huge layer of creepy atmosphere to top it off. Nemesis doesn't have that going for him at all. [spoiler] In the very early city area, which has a map that is fairly open, he will hunt you. I would have expected the entire game to play out generally like this, with him showing up to chase you around after unlocking new areas, but this only happens for a short time in the first half an hour or so of gameplay just to disappear.  After this, he shows up at very scripted segments with either a rocket launcher or flamethrower and is either something you have to outrun for 30 seconds, or is just a forced boss battle, removing the choice of engaging in combat with him. Also, about a month ago, there was rumor that he could follow you into safe rooms, making for some real intense encounters. Not only is that not true, but he'll hardly follow you into any rooms or buildings whatsoever.[/spoiler] Nemesis doesn't hunt you in this game like we were all led to expect. When Nemesis does show up for some reason, so does the heavily scripted action parts of the game. Now the game isn't full of quick time events, but there are a few that are pretty annoying. The action segments aren't quite as over the top as, say Resident Evil 4, but some of the realism of the RE2 Remake has faded away. [spoiler]Jill basically survives getting blasted outright by a rocket at one point.[/spoiler]  One thing that was actually brought back from the source material is the dodge mechanic, which is fairly fun, and amplifies the more action filled pace of the game, but the perfect dodge/slow-mo thing is kind of out of place. Feels like something that belonged in Resident Evil 6. Ammo seems to be everywhere, even on hardcore mode, which deviated from the previous as well. The only time I ever had to be concerned about inventory management was during a boss fight.


What this game does right:

After all that is it still a good game? Yes, sort of. It just doesn't come close to the polish, writing, and design that RE2 Remake had, and that is a shame, because I always preferred the original 3 to the original 2. This seems rushed. It should have had another 6 to 8 months of development and probably been an early 2021 release.

The gameplay is almost identical to the previous game, so if you liked that, you'll like this. One notable exception that I had to get used to is that now you have to actually select grenades to use them, rather than them being bound to a key in the last game, and the removal of them being used as an emergency weapon when grabbed. It's a good game. It stands up with the rest of the Remake line of the series as a good storytelling game with all the notes and pieces of information you get throughout. I'm one of the many who experienced the first three back on the PS1 and I can tell when it's time to give a solid divide between the old school and the new age of Resident Evil games.

Resident Evil 3 takes almost everything from Remake 2 and then adds a little bit of flavouring from Resident Evil 3 (Ps1).  Jill can do a dodge, of which can be timed to be a perfect dodge which will be used exclusively for a boss or two. This mechanic is loosely taken from the PS1 era game but it actually works much easier than the predecessor. This game takes the same vibe of being a bit more action heavy vs the slow, survival pace of RE2 (Remake and PS1)

What did I like personally?
- It looked great. I was very excited to see Racoon City and the story that is told from the destructive look of the city during an outbreak.
-The Dodge. When it works, it works well and it feels good to nail that perfect dodge.
-Jill hits more critical shots than Claire or Leon. Netting a critical on a zombie and saving the extra bullet is a great feeling.
-Carlos is great. He looks great, he's acted well, and his sections are fun.
-The introduction of the monsters are cool. Many are just simply cool and horrid.
-The same resident evil 2 formula is used and it's familiar. It works out well, and you can feel the beginning middle and end, but more on this later.

What I didn't really like?
-The dismemberment system from 2 is gone. If you shot an zombie enough in certain parts or knifed them, their limbs would literally fall off. It added so much to the grotesque nature of the virus. But sadly, it doesn't exist.
-There are some shoehorned horde mode esque fights. They aren't great. But I understand why theyre there besides the story point and the player feeling of letting loose.
-Puzzles. There aren't a whole lot to be honest. Some people hate them, some love them, I follow the latter.
-Nemesis. This game has nemesis and it's hard to not know about him. The game on PS1 was called Resident Evil 3:Nemesis. The first half could have used more of him in my opinion. Could really let the feeling of being hunted sink in.
-The same Resident evil 2 formula is used. Following my point above, it's too familiar and some parts feel a touch reused. Sectioning out both games beginning, middle and end, you can lay them out on top of each other and it's a bit too close for comfort.

-Post credit fun. Not too much, or rather, not too much YET I'm assuming from looking at Resident Evil 2's post content added dlc.

But honestly, it's a fun game, If you are looking for a game that is RE2++ and also touches on a story within the raccoon City outbreak, this is your game. If you don't mind it's about 8 hours long and doesn't offer additional content, this is your game. Besides that, maybe wait a little bit before purchasing.

The new one feels it relies way too much on fancy graphics and action, not to mention a completely different (and significantly smaller) map.

2.  The Environment:  There was A LOT more to explore in the original RE3 than the remake.  I won't list everything since it seems like everyone else already has a list of locations they wanted to see but were disappointed in.  The city's history felt completely cut out in the new one, making everything feel much more disposable than if you saw all the historical landmarks like the original (and the puzzles that show just how much Umbrella hid out in the open)

3.  Overall Gameplay:  I'll be honest.  This one felt rather linear.  The only real payoff for any remote exploring is if you find the 3 gems near the beginning (which apparently unlocks an achievement), but otherwise weapons pretty much are right in front of you instead of getting rewarded for being a completionist.



The game itself isn't bad.  It kept me occupied for a few hours, but for what it was supposed to be, it was disappointing.  This is one of those games that I would only recommend if it sometime down the line goes on sale for $5USD just because of what you actually get.  You're paying more for graphics than anything.

Resident Evil 3 remake is a far cry from the greatness that was released last year. Besides from recycling areas from RE2 the game’s biggest shortcoming is that it doesn’t feel like a Resident Evil game. Instead of freely exploring, you are instead rushed through sections, which is probably why there are very little puzzles in this game. You want to make sure to pick up every item because once nemesis locks on to you it makes it very hard to back track. This annoyance is amplified because of scripted events that permanently block off routes.
 
The issue with this is that it makes it very easy to miss important items like the inventory increasing hip packs. What is worse is the game feels designed to expect the player to pick up all of them since you are always out of room. The biggest design flaw though is Nemesis. The game is constantly telling you to run away, so you expect to flee. What it doesn’t tell you is that if you stay and fight, Nemesis will drop items and not just any item. In key spots Nemesis will drop game changing upgrades for your primary weapons, yet they can all easily be missed. It’s a baffling design decision, and one that cripples an already subpar experience.

With a bar set so high last year it is disappointing to see that they didn’t try to reach the same level of greatness and makes me weary to purchase the next game they plan to remake.

What can I say? If you liked the RE2 remake, you'll like this game just as much. The better game play and controls that come with the RE Engine are just incredible. 

With this game, it brings you an improved dodge mechanic, that some people will like and some won't. The amazing graphical fidelity and detail quality puts this game alongside RE2 as some of the best looking Zombie / survival horror games for a really long time.

//However, this game is quite a bit shorter than RE2, Its campaign is about the same length as RE2, at about 5 Hours, except there is only one campaign instead of 2 (and then another 2 for another character like Leon and Claire). Not only is the game quite a bit "shorter" but there is also plenty of removed content. Many memorable places are removed like the actual clock-tower puzzle (although you do visit the clock-tower for a boss fight) some enemies are removed like the gravedigger. The story is also changed up a bit, like how Carlos visits RCPD instead of Jill, but it doesn't make the game any less enjoyable, atleast in my opinion. Gore has also been downgraded in this game compared to RE2. Where damage seemed to feel real and intense, it is replaced by simple blood pops and limbs disappearing. In RE2 you could slowly shoot a zombies arm off where its flash would slowly stretch and fall onto the ground, or you could blast a zombie in the stomach and watch it collapse and break in two, here they just pop, disappear and the bodies become inactive. Nemesis is only "dynamic" for some of the game, (unlike the original where he was always scripted) unlike Mr. X who spends around an hour in a dynamic state, Nemesis is only dynamic for around 30 minutes or less depending on how fast you rush through the area. 

Now, what you may be asking . . . if there is cut content and downgrades? 

because despite that, the game is still fun and enjoyable. The game play is a step-up from the original, yes thats right, the tank controls of the original RE3 did not fit into the game style as it moved into a more action oriented gameplay/story. The story is still cohesive ( although they could have spit the story up more and gave us two campaigns, one for Jill and one for Carlos, but, oh well) and fun, and even scary / intense at plenty of points. Even though the game takes a more cinematic angle, its still fun none the less. 

Creature designs are gross in the best way possible. The way the T-virus effects things is still grotesque as the RE2 remake. Just like in RE2 the Tyrant in this game looks stunning for the short times you get to look at him. Texture quality for just about everything is stunning and amazing. As Nemesis slowly transforms the gross details show more and more. Hunters and Gammas look just as good as you can tell that lots of time went into their designs. 

Boss battles are engaging and fun (and even frustrating at times), although they usually come down to: Run Run, Dodge Dodge, fire grenade launcher, shoot shotgun and repeat. 

And despite all these positives and negatives, Ill still recommend the game even for its full price, but only if you're really into Resident Evil, and even then I would still strongly recommend that you pick it up for a reduced price on a LEGIT (NOT G2A) key site.

[h1][b]Ce n'est pas un remake de Resident Evil 3, mais plus le Resident Evil 3 d'une dimension parallèle.[/b][/h1] 
[h1]On a plus l'impression de jouer à un DLC de RE2 qu'à un véritable jeu à part entière.[/h1] 

Dimension parallèle, où les USA sont encore en guerre froide avec l'URSS. Dans laquelle des Asiats n'ont pas encore mangé de soupe à la chauve-souris assaisonné au pangolin.
Une dimension dans laquelle le Président de l'Univers n'est autre que  Dwayne Elizondo Mountain Dew Herbert Camacho.

[h1]Si vous aimez l'original va falloir s'accrocher et être prêt à mettre de côté votre amour propre.[/h1] 
[h1][b]Perso' j'ai apprécié le jeu malgré un grand nombre de défauts, je suis quand même gavé car aimant énormément Resident Evil 3: Némésis, j'ai eu l'impression qu'on enQlait un jeu cher à mes yeux et ce justement... devant mes yeux et qu'en plus de tout ça... au final... j'ai payé pour voir ça et j'ai même participé ![/b][/h1] 

[i]Stop, it is already dead![/i]

En effet, on a plus l'impression de jouer à un jeu fait par des fans sous coke, avec un scénario alternatif, que de jouer à la version originale reboostée... Tellement il y a de changements, en plus  [b] ils ne sont pas foncièrement bon...[/b]

[h1]Techniquement :[/h1]
Le jeu tourne à fond, 1080p, 60fps + aucun bug,
Le moteur est maîtrisé depuis le temps, les effets visuels rendant vraiment bien.
La DA est stylée cependant, je n'aime aucune des refontes des charadesign (Jill, Carlos, Némésis, etc.).
Aussi, par moments, la caméra part en cacahuète, [i]"J'y vois que dalle ! Allô ?! Stop les gros plans sur le Q du Némésis !"[/i], certains endroit étant tellement étroits, que bon... 

[h1] Histoire :[/h1]
Alors, tu prends la trame scénaristique de Resident Evil 3: Némésis, tu lui fait un gros doigt d'honneur, lui dit d'aller s'faire mettre, qu'elle est adoptée (pour quelle pleure un peu) et lui crache à la gueule pour humidifier le tout et si la légende est correcte après avoir laissé tout ça mariner environ 4 mois, t'arrives à l'histoire de ce REmake 3, qui n'est que des bribes périmées de l'histoire principale.

Globalement, c'est moins dramatique que l'original, "This is, my last escape" on avait une Jill qui s'était préparé mentalement, prête à tout, notamment à faire face à ses peurs pour survivre...  Là, on a une Jill Jovovich qui est en plein bad trip dans son appart, elle se fait agresser par sac poubelle-man, ultra détèr.., 

Puis elle croise Brad la baltringue, ah non dans ce jeu c'est un flic lambda qui se sacrifie.
Jill Jovovich a trop traîné en bas des tours elle fait que jurer pendant tout le jeu car s'plus cool tu vois...
Tous les moments cultes du jeu, tu oublies en fait tu oublies : des zones entières, des monstres et des boss...

En gros, ils se sont dit "tiens, on va prendre 10% du jeu original et on va refaire un jeu de A à Z", sans garder les bonnes idées...

[h1] OST :[/h1]
Ça explose tellement de partout, ça crie et hurle, que les musiques... j'ai pas souvenir d'en avoir entendu une seule si ce n'est celle de la salle de sauvegarde mais en extrêmement faible et discrète... 
Les doublages... J'aime pas les voix (US) de tous les doubleurs, donc j'aime pas ce qu'ils disent, comment ils le disent et les personnages (visuellement), s'pas mal ! 
Même le S.T.A.R.S du Némésis est flingué, faut tendre l'oreille pour l'entendre.

[h1]Gameplay :[/h1]
Le gameplay, comme RE2 avec l'ajout des esquives/dodges et de la slow-mo, c'est sympa. 
Jeu full action, on n'est pas là pour réfléchir, tue seulement !
Ce qui manque par rapport au jeu lui-même... c'est les choix, t'as aucun choix alors que RE3: Némésis, tu avais des moments clé où tu devais choisir entre deux alternatives avec une mise en scène, ici tu oublies, c'est tout droit Roger, fonces !
Le jeu est très dirigiste et linéaire, difficile voire impossible de se perdre.
Il est relativement court aussi, niveau durée de vie la moitié c'est des cinématiques, tu le vois vraiment en refaisant le jeu et en passant toutes les cutscenes...
Pas d'énigmes, peu de backtracking, pas de mode mercenaries, 5 modes de difficultés (faudra qu'on m'explique l'intérêt d'avoir 5 modes de difficultés). 
Le Némésis, s'plus le Némésis (comme ce qu'ils ont fait avec Mr. X dans REmake 2) non, tu le vois pendant une zone puis il passe directement à sa 3e forme, sac-poubelle doggo... N'importe quoi... 

[h1]Conclusion :[/h1]

Je n'ai pas aimé le gros doigt d'honneur à la fanbase de la part de Crapcom, Resident Evil Rebirth est un bon exemple (sans parler du REmake 2) de comment plaire à tous et surprendre la fanbase, tout en se respectant. C'est-à-dire, créer un nouveau jeu, avec de nouvelles énigmes, mécaniques tout en gardant [i]l'âme du jeu de base[/i]... 
Ici, c'est un nouveau jeu qui garde que les nom des protagonistes/antagonistes ainsi que deux voire trois parties de l'histoire et encore même les parties conservées sont modifiées et pas en bien...

S'pas un mauvais jeu à part entière, j'ai bien aimé au final, car j'partais déjà du principe (dès le premier trailer) que le jeu n'allait pas rendre hommage à celui de 1999, que j'apprécie tant.
Dire que je ne suis pas déçu serait mentir, par contre je m'adapte, je n'ai pas envie de tout casser.

J'aimerais lui mettre un 6/10 car on m'a craché à la gueule, mais s'pas une daube infâme non-plus.

A reimagined take on a cult classic. Definitely tugged at nostalgia as a gamer who grew up facing Nemmy on PS1, both in good and bad aspects. Ironically this is releasing towards the end of a console generation and once again attempts to bridge the gap between the suspenseful masterwork that was RE2 Remake and the more modernized gameplay of RE4 just as RE3: Nemesis did back in 1999. Unfortunately, its this games identity as a bridge gap that puts it in a position where it is doomed to always be runner up. It has SOME of the suspense of RE2, SOME of the action set pieces of the later entries, but this title never really leans too heavily in either direction to capitalize on either aspect. The primary antagonist never really instills that sense of paranoia you would expect after dealing with Mr. X in RE2, and in fact should have had more interaction and screen time in my opinion. In terms of visuals and audio this title is fantastic, and a 1:1 remake of the 1999 classic with assets this sharp would've been amazing, but thankfully this isn't too far off even with some questionable omissions in terms of level design and storytelling. Gameplay wise, this title is as fluid as RE2 Remake, if not more so. Still a solid entry in the RE universe and worth a play through albeit maybe at a slightly discounted price point. It's a short but sweet roller coaster of an adventure that I'd recommend to be viewed not for what once was, but what this groundwork could mean for the franchise moving forward.

Review:

Honestly I just had an absolutely brilliant afternoon and evening on this. Do yourself a favour and play it on hardcore for your first run through. The tension level will be just right for you to have fun while also having to be careful.

Anyhoo, here's the classic pro/con list:

[b]Pros:[/b]

- Way more zombies on screen and they die more consistently than in RE2:Remake. They can still surprise you though

- The gameplay actually varies. One minute your panicking round a spider filled (well, not actually spiders but close enough) tunnels, the next doing a last stand battle against a horde of monsters. There's enough normal RE gameplay between these moments to make them feel exciting rather than forced

- Nemesis has a new tactic/weapon every time he appears

- For me personally, I liked that Nemesis appearances are scripted. I felt like Mr X was more of a chore in RE:2 than anything. He quickly became a case of exploiting his AI whenever he showed up. RE3 Remake Nemesis knows how to crash a party with style.

- Nemesis gets a truly memorable final fight

- Doesn't outstay it's welcome. Had a six hour clear time after trawling through the whole game, with about 
another hour added on top of that for cutscenes (not counted in clear time). This was just right for me.

- Bosses require a bit of thought and have mechanics, rather than just being bullet sponges

- Nemesis's final form is beautiful

- Fun plot with decent character growth and everyone getting a chance to do something

[b]Cons (mostly nitpicks)[/b]

- The initial streets section does feel a bit small, with the game having you run loops around it. This is made up for with the hugely expanded hospital section

- The game artificially increases it's length by having locks and chains you have to come back later to snip, hiding a gun attachment or a weapon. In fact if you don't bother to backtrack at two points you're gonna completely miss [spoiler] the magnum [/spoiler]  and [spoiler] the shotgun [/spoiler] (though if you'd have to be a goon to miss the latter)

- [spoiler] Brad's offscreen [/spoiler] death is incredibly naff

- No Mercenaries mode feels like a huge missed opportunity

- The game doesn't auto heal you when it sometimes should. I was on danger and just got away from nemesis. It autosaves and then without a chance to pick up a healing item it launched me into a chase sequence. Jill moves slower when hurt so I had to do a bunch of perfect dodges immediately after the cutscene ended or I couldn't outrun him. This led to lots of Jill having her opening quip cut off in a scream.
I love the game not much to complain about besides needing a few more hours in the story and getting back cut content.

Okay. Let me make this clear. I've been a Resident Evil fan since I first played RE2 back when it came out for N64. I love the franchise, I liked this game. But I feel that being a fan of a franchise, I have to point out its flaws. It pains me GREATLY to thumb this game down.

This game man... It's like playing the classic RE3 again. And not in a good way. I know a lot of people love RE3, but it was personally my least favorite, since it did not really feel like what I thought an RE should feel. This remake unfortunately fails the franchise in an even greater way.

Don't get me wrong; the game is good, it has its moments, graphics are absolutely gorgeous, the music is fantastic, the gameplay is very solid. But... it lacks soul... What happened Capcom? With RE2R, it seems they were infinitely inspired to create a tribute to what part of the fandom think is the best title in the franchise. You can feel the love they put in that game, not only reviving the highlights of the original, but adding more to it and taking the experience to a whole new level.

But RE3R? They had a chance to give new life to RE3. The original was not bad, but it lacked that feel that the previous two games had. Here they had a chance to add to that experience, yet strangely they took even more from it. Most of the most memorable moments of RE3 are pretty much gone. Memorable locations? Gone. Those elements left from the classic are almost like a "lite" version of them. The game almost feels like those amusement park rides based on movies, which is nothing more than an 'abbreviated'  (and almost parody) version of their source. RE3R is pretty much a series of short and linear corridors filled with references and easter eggs of itself. Just shoot here, run there, fight boss; no puzzles, almost no backtracking, no planning ahead, no nothing. And just when you think the game might get even better (after a phenomenal first half hour), you realize that's it; that's all you get.

I'm all for team T-00 (Mr.X), but I feel sorry for what they've done with my boy Nemesis here. Nemesis has a huge fanbase, and in this game they've taken all of its essence away. Sure he was scripted in the original, but at least in that game you did feel like the guy was roaming all around the city looking for you. You feared that you might encounter him around some random corner, and sometimes you did! No; this Nemesis is anything but. There is no chasing around the city anymore; he's just a bunch of cinematics and boss fights. Even copying Mr.X's gameplay elements and A.I would've made this so much better than what we got. He does look badass, though. I'll give them that...

I just hope this game was not just a quick cash-grab, and/or just made to push Resistance, which seems ripe for monetization. Because they've messed up on an opportunity to rock the videogame industry like they did with RE2R .

I hope things are better in the future of Resident Evil. I'm all for these remakes, and would love to see Code Veronica or even RE4 running on the RE Engine. But you got a do it right, Capcom!! For now, take a break , gather your brain power, embrace the love for your franchise once more. You were doing an amazing job with RE7 and RE2R. Don't fall in the same cycle you did with RE6 and all the spinoffs after it, please...

[h1]UPDATE[/h1]
Review was written after beating game first-time on hardcore difficulty but before I tried the multiplayer "REsistance". Now I have tried it and it changed my view of the game for the worse. For my overall opinion on that mode go to the end of the review.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
RE3 remake is okay, but disappointingly light on content. The single-player mode took me less than 6 hours to play through first time on the highest difficulty. It's also not nearly as well designed as the last attempt of remake with RE2.

Buy only on a sale. Not worth full price.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[b]+ Satisfying gameplay[/b]
[b]+ Jill looking good![/b]

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[b]- Nemesis chases[/b]
[b]- Lack of main game content[/b]
[b]- Too intense, not enough slow moments[/b]
[b]- Dialogue[/b]
[b]- Dodging takes the game in a wrong direction[/b]
[b]- One boss fight was a joke[/b]

More about pros and cons below.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[b]+ Satisfying gameplay[/b]
I think it feels a bit tighter than RE2 remake did. The weapons hit where I expect them to and movement is responsive. The parts of the game that deal with zombies and you can explore and deal with them the way you see fit are the strong point.

[b]+ Jill looking good![/b]
After Claire in RE2 remake looked weird and uncanny it's nice to see that Jill didn't end up the same. I don't remember her being sassy, but it's not a big deal and doesn't take away from my appreciation of her.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[b]- Nemesis chases[/b]
There is only one section of the game where Nemesis is a constant threat as you are trying to complete an objective. It's designed poorly. He teleports around instead of actually chasing you - it's even worse than Mr X from RE2 remake and it was pretty bad there. When you run from him he can easly land a cheap hit on you because there's not enough audio telegraph when he attacks. He can be forced to stop and regenerate with enough damage and he drops weapon upgrade when this happens. Ultimately that entire section of the game is a wasted potential.
Other sections where Nemesis is chasing you are scripted and don't feel good at all.

[b]- Lack of main game content[/b]
The old PS1 version of RE3 Nemesis had a lot of sections that were cut from this release. The remake does seem to be a longer game in comparison, but that does not excuse cutting that stuff when you can finish this full priced game in less than 5 hours when played on normal difficulty. And I'm talking about first-time clear. There is a multiplayer mode and the usual unlocking of upgrades and costumes by completing specific challanges, but that doesn't change that the main game is short as hell.

[b]- Too intense, not enough slow moments[/b]
This game starts off with an adrenaline pumping scripted sequence followed by the best part of the game - the city. About 1/3rd of this area was already in the demo and it's easy to understand why. It shows the best out of Resident Evil - exploration, item management and careful combat. After the city chapter you are almost always forced forward with little deviation from the main route and little to no exploration required. I know that the original RE3 was similar in that respect, but it's a shame that they didn't change that for the remake.

[b]- Dialogue[/b]
The script feels like someone in Japan imagined how Americans talk. It's weird and bad. The actors try their best not to sound stupid and I cannot blame them for failing where the lines they are supposed to deliver are just all wrong.

[b]- Dodging takes the game in a wrong direction[/b]
The dodge works kind of similar to how Nier Automata handles it. If you dodge at a correct time during an enemy animation, you will perform a roll which makes you unable to be attacked/grabbed. The problem is that while RE3 had the dodge it was very difficult to pull off to the point of being unreliable. Making the dodge one of the core mechanics in the game for most encounters, especially bosses was a bad idea and diminishes what's good about Resident Evil. Interestingly - after dodge is over you can follow up with a counterattack using your equipped weapon, be it a gun or a knife... and oh boy, do I have a story to tell with this...

[b]- One boss fight was a joke[/b]
... I ran out of ammunition in one of the boss fights. It's already disheartening that this game does not learn from the problems of RE2 remake and still has you fight bullet-sponge bosses, but this one boss... When I couldn't find any more bullets and had only knife to deal damage I started treating this game like Dark Souls and simply went up close and personal with the boss, stabbing it with the knife and dodging every telegraphed attack. It took a lot of time, but I defeated the boss with a knife.
I feel next time I play this part I will go in the boss arena with the knife and nothing else since it's that easy.

[h1]The lowdown[/h1]
The lack of content is inexcusable in a full priced game. I don't really care that you get a multiplayer minigame with it, because as a RE fan I care about single-player story-content first and foremost. I liked co-op of RE5 and RE6, but here I will have to give it a good play before I make up my mind about it, but as it stands I can't recommend RE3 remake. It's too short, lazily designed and delivers very few moments of what's actually good about the series.

Maybe it was rushed so they could get to doing RERE4 or figure out if M2 could do RERE4 next while their core in house team worked on brand new projects or maybe, just maybe it was because it was just down to it being outsourced to begin with but it's baffling to see RE3, a game that out of the original PS1 trilogy had the most replay value and content have so little to do or see. With the Resident Evil 3 remake, who cares if it cut something from the OG when it's also VERY clearly cut most of it's own work too.
The nicest thing about RERE3 for me was it perfectly supports 21:9 out of the box.
That's it.

Some would argue the OG was not a masterpiece but turning what was a classic into mediocrity is as unacceptable as it is impressive. My first run through was 2 hours and while I wasn't quite quick enough and it's too late for me to refund it it's not too late for me to tell you to skip this game for now. If not for desperately trying to find something to do since then or checking to see how it works on my new setup my play time would be even shorter. I've tried but there is no deluding myself. 

Repeated playthroughs showed just how poor most of the level design is, lacking what made the prior remake, the PS1 titles or even RE4/5 good.
The intro is FAR too linear and outside of not pressing W there is little to see or do even on your first time through. Once you get past that you get rail roaded again as if the game has TWO intros and the first one you got to play was added later, making the second one redundant. Once that's done you do more holding forward as you follow behind an NPC.
Once you get past the subway cinematic, you are free for a wee bit as the best part of the game occurs...which is where the game peaks and then that's over as fast as it had started.
To sum up Nemesis, the originals titular stalker, he is so little of a thing in this remake that his name was also removed from the title.

They focused all their resources and energy on seemingly every single thing they shouldn't have and I am extremely confident that I am not exaggerating about that one bit. This wasn't a problem in the remake of RE2 which was done by a different team even though both were apaprently initially started and developed around the same time together. How can something developed for 3 years be this short,rushed and unfinished? More has been cut than added and in both regards not for the better and it's not as if what is now gone was replaced with something else. The good parts are way too short and the bad parts are DAMN long. 

The original RE3 had maybe one sewer and maybe two or so basements in that entire game but in RERE3 anytime you would have or could have been entering an interesting place instead you'll find yourself entering a sewer which seems like a move done to stitch together the remaining non sewer locations. Inbetween most of this are some painfully linear walks to get into these. The filler is so hard to stomach, at a certain point there is filler for the filler once you've long passed the promising stuff from the demo.

If the game was really and I mean really good in this instance or kept what was good in RE3 or good in the prior RERE2 I wouldn't mind the length but this just isn't the case. It is absurdly short and I mean shorter than Jill's skorts (not a skirt) which for now you can only get if you pre ordered it. Game shouldn't even cost 35 dollars and I paid 60 but having played it I don't know if I would have parted with 20. If this was a DLC for RERE2 it still wouldn't work as RE3 as they've completely missed the appeal of Nemesis and even then RERE3 deserves/deserved better than this.
So linear, so little content, so little tension, so little survival, so little horror, so little variety, so little unscripted Nemesis and so little care, effort or ambition or SPIRIT. The original which I played WAY after it's prime was while old and coming close to being dared was still fun to play (my dis taste for tank controls aside) and apparently it was basically made in a single year. Other than the graphics (which have issues like zombies exploding to save performance or animating at a lower framerate) this is a remake that feels like a downgrade in almost every way. To reiterate, this is a remake that feels like it would need a remake. Something could and maybe should be done to improve the game and I just can't imagine Capcom is happy or satisfied with how it is in it's current state and I don't know how much they could afford to add or fix or if they would even be willing or bother to do so it's kind of hopeless.

The ending is also awful but I gotta wrap this up as my review threatens to be longer than the game or for the sake of accuracy, it's demo. At best it's meh, a wasted opportunity.
At worst, long after I've stopped playing Resident Evil 3 Remake still offends me.

In conclusion it would be worth a play when the price is right to minimize discontent but you'd be disappointed if you played the original and still risk being disappointed if you've played the other new games and besides being a bad remake it's quite meh.
I desperately tried to squeeze my moneys worth out of it by at least getting all the achievements like I did for RERE2 but skill aside it took far less time and not even terribly replayable to begin with which is kind of a death sentence for Resident Evil game.

Let me preface this review by saying that the original RE 3 was my favorite of the RE series. Overall i think Resident Evil 3 is a worthy remake to the original and a competent successor to the Resident Evil 2 remake. As a veteran of the original Resident Evil 3, the new clock tower was the biggest let down that i had. Also i lament the gravedigger!!

Pros:
-Gorgeous graphics, the lightning, animations, blood and gore, textures and reflections are truly beautiful. The RE engine steals the show once again. The optimization for weak and powerful machines alike is a perfect representation of what the AAA industry should strive for. 
-Personally the lack of puzzles for me is a Pro. RE 3 has a couple smaller, much easier to solve puzzles than the previous game, and as a player who primarily plays these games for the action and terror i really liked that about RE 3. In RE 2 the puzzles were difficult and pace killing to the point that i would just look up the solution to advance. 
-The horror is back and better than ever. Nemesis is truly terrifying, his chase scenes and boss fights are extremely frightening, the various forms you encounter are unique. When Nemesis appears on the scene you must decide whether you are going to fight him or run.
-The survival horror elements are still spot on. You do acquire lots of ammo but frequently use it because there are substantially more zombies and other enemies to encounter.
-The game has much more action than the last title.
-A couple enemy types are back from the previous RE 3. Some are gone. More on that later.
-The action is ramped up thanks to a dodge feature which makes combat in RE 3 much more satisfying than the last remake.
-Completing challenges during the game unlocks an item shop in lieu of a new game plus mode, for things such as unlimited ammo for certain weapons or coins that make your attacks more powerful. Which can make attempting the game on harder difficulties much more manageable. 
-Lots of beautiful cutscenes and improved story and voice acting. 
-More difficulties after completing hardcore mode.

Cons:
-The game is shorter than RE 2 i think its hard to argue against this point. 
-Cut enemies and locations are sad to see. Capcom could have had another masterpiece if they added in a few more areas, focused more on replayability and dumped the RE resistance mode. 
-The gore level does seem to have been slightly reduced after witnessing some of the more gruesome deaths from RE 2. Nothing like that is in RE 3
-Removed choices and branching paths from the single player. Would have added to replayability.
-No RE 3 Callout on the title Menu? WTH capcom it was bad enough i had to pay for it extra in RE 2 but i still would have done it again in RE 3. Give it to me for 2.99$. I hate saying it to myself every time i hit the start button!!
-Removed ink ribbon saving..... im not sure who thought this was a good idea....

Tldr: good game, worthy of the RE 3 name. Shorter than i would have liked but even with the limited replayability still worth a full price purchase in my opinion as ill be playing the game on its multiple different difficuties. Ill give REsistance a try sometime but wish Capcom would have just focused exclusively on the single player.

I honestly don't know what went wrong here. I've completed one playthrough on standard so far and these are my impressions.

Pros:
-Looks great. Seriously phenomenal looking graphics (played on an RTX 2080).

Cons:
-Nemesis isn't nearly as present a threat as it should have been. In RE2 I spent probably the entire playthrough after Mr X was introduced wondering when he'd next pop up. Here it quickly became apparent that Nemesis was restricted to scripted encounters and I think only one segment where it actually followed you around the map like in the original game (which itself turned out to be extremely scripted, and not dynamic like RE2's Mr X was).
-The action feels worse. Something about the weight and impact that weapons had in RE2 is gone. The knife is infinite, but has been rendered primarily a box opener by its newfound inability to damage limbs (or it seems like even stagger enemies).
-No real backtracking. I remember an earlier article about this game that said there would be fast travel. What happened? (In general it seems like there was a LOT of misinformation spread about it, particularly by what should be reputable sources).
-Where is the replayability? The choices from the original game are gone, and unlike RE2 there's only one playthrough. While you switch between Carlos and Jill on occasion, it's nowhere near the amount of variation RE2 had and presents almost no reason to touch this again after the first playthrough.
-There's some frustrating difficulty spikes that really contrast with how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy the game is in general. The hunters in this game can one shot you from full life on normal difficulty, but only under some circumstances (I could not figure out what made it happen)? 
-A lot of the setpieces were just not great. The first fight with Berkin in RE2 was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ setpiece. He plows through the environment, pipes burst, you can lose track of him as he disappears behind machinery. The sound and feel of that fight was amazing. The first proper fight with Nemesis you're just in a place. There's like a couple stacks of boxes. Some fire. [spoiler]The final fight is laughably easy and involves Jill lugging around a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like, lightning gun twice her size.[/spoiler] 

It feels weird to give this a negative review because it's still a perfectly fun, playable game. It's just SO much worse than RE2 in basically every way. Resident Evil 3 gets a 6/10 from me, bumped to a 6.5/10 if you can get it for <= $20. It feels and plays like an expansion to RE2, not a standalone game, and I'm hoping that post launch support can fix at least some of the issues I have with it.

With all the cut content from the original, the lack of choices, the garbage AI, Nemesis being reduced to a prop instead of a consistent threat, etc, I've been finding myself more and more disgruntled with this clearly half-assed product they pumped out to make more of that REmake cash. Your *first* time through this game won't take any longer than 6 hours of game time, tops, and there's zero replay value present aside from farming 'records,' in order to get bonus points to buy neat little things at the bonus shop. My current major gripe as I replay the game a second time is how the enemies are just so... cheap. There's not really another word for it. Dodge/Charge mechanics are present, sure, but the number of times I just got ganked in tight quarters despite all efforts - and in a few places insta-killed by what seem to be lock-on attacks by the few mid-tier monsters the game bothered to port over (There is *very* little enemy diversity) - just chaps my ass pretty raw. I wanted to love this game and I was ready to accept a different vision from the original just to see it in glorious updated graphics, but what I got was something that could've been released as RE2 DLC. I fully believe Capcom didn't  take the time or energy that was needed to make this something really great and it shows. That's just a damn shame.

RESIDENT EVIL 3 Remake is a fantastic action based resident evil experience that was an absolute blast to play through but it is currently hindered by it's price point.

Before going any further I must say that the game is very short for the price tag and you should wait for the game to be about half the price before diving in. The game lasts about 5-6 hours and doesn't have any additional playthrough modes unlike it's predecessor Resident Evil 2. You get your standard run, your hardcore run and a point based unlock system after beating the game and that is it.

Having said that RESIDENT EVIL 3 is a fantastic game and definitely should be played. It goes for a more linear action based approach than Resident Evil 2 and feels like a collection of the later sections of RE2 as opposed to the police station approach of having one large area to explore. It's a shame that approach wasn't taken here but the levels designs while small are still great and suit the action based approach very well. 

The action has been ramped up dramatically with the game giving you plenty of ammo and upgrades to take down zombies with and it makes you feel like an utter badass once you've kitted Jill out with a hefty amount of gear. With the higher emphasis on the combat there has been some work put into the boss fights which are improved compared to Resident Evil 2 mostly due to the addition of a combat roll which makes defence much easier alongside the addition of the captivating villain Nemesis.

When it comes to Nemesis he ramps up the excitement and drives the narrative forward at a blasting pace. I found nemesis to be an interesting and intimidating villain and he kept me hooked the whole way through. I do think the portrayal of him in pre release footage was a bit misleading. He is portrayed to be a Mr. X style replacement. Whilst he is a bit like that in a few points in the game for short periods he doesn't keep it up and is mainly encountered through scripted segments and action set pieces.

Seeing as I never played more than 20 minutes of the original resident evil 3 I never knew of any of the missing moments in the story that had been rewritten so from a fresh point of view I thought the story was great and nicely ties in with resident evil 2.

The feeling of Resident Evil 2 remake is very much here with this remake but the lack of a large sprawling area to explore and the lack of any extra playthrough mixups leaves the game feeling rather sparse in comparisson to the previous entry in the series especially at this price.

While falling short compared to Resident Evil 2 I wholeheartedly recommend this game if the price is not a problem as I truly think it stands with the better games in the series but the game is very hindered by it's lack of additional content for the price its being offered for at this time. 

I'm giving it a recommendation but don't buy it just yet and wait for a sale.
