I recommend it, but not at full price. Maybe on a 33% or 50% sale, as it feels like a major downgrade compared to the remake of Resident Evil 2. Spoilers.

It's much faster, it has many more enemies, ammo is much more frequent and the areas are generally much wider. The focus was definitely far more on having lots of enemies on screen and fighting them.

I had tons of ammo and health items left despite killing almost all enemies and getting hit quite often. And that was when playing on Hardcore, which puts you on about half health after one zombie grab.

The game is super linear and exploration is a joke. Not only is it always obvious where you have to go next, it's almost impossible to miss items because the game tells you where you missed a few. There are only rare cases where you can actually choose where to go first and even that is at most just half a minute of going through a straight path that you have to return from anyway.

Nemesis was disappointing. He appeared a lot, and while you can still down him for extra items the amount of effort it takes is trivial. One grenade, one explosive barrel or just a few shots are enough. That is usually also enough for you to run to the next location for him to disappear for a while.

A lot of enemies can't enter a lot of places. Nemesis can't enter a lot of buildings, zombies can't get through most doors. It's also possible to open doors, kill a lot of enemies in a room while standing in the door frame without them reaction to you.

Gore was toned down a LOT. You can't shoot off zombies limbs anymore, at least I couldn't do it like in 2. They also got no ragdolls after death, so they won't move at all no matter what you do.

What I didn't like:
- The whole beginning is mostly an action sequence. There are also a lot more later on.
- Brad got killed right when he appeared, probably only for nostalgia reasons, but with no way to save him (he dies again as zombie in front of RPD)
- No Ink Ribbons on Hardcore.
- Frequent autosaves on Hardcore despite there being typewriters in safe zones.
- Nikolai seems more like a comic book villain.
- A lot of humor everywhere, be it in written notes or when the characters talk. The tone doesn't feel serious at all.
- A lot of Zombies walk back to their starting location after you leave the area, even if you can still see them. They just instantly turn around and "hide" again.
- Shooting Zombies has none or barely any feedback during most pistol shots, no matter where you shoot them. They only get staggered after a specific amount of shots.
- Savezones every few minutes, with an item box and typewriter so you never get any inventory or saving problems.
- It feels like Jill had no idea about anything getting so bad, she just woke up one day with people shouting, dying, half of the city burning and everything being ♥♥♥♥ in general. At least the original had an implied timeskip of some sort at the start to make it more believable.
- Nemesis can kill you in one combo. And on Hardcore he only needs two single hits (the second one often hits you after the first hit, with almost no chance of avoiding it).
- The game crashes sometimes, from my experience it seems to have problems with being tabbed out, not during normal gameplay.
- It added a generic, boring looking sewer section.
- There are moments that just spam enemies and you have to kill them to proceed, basically "kill rooms" you find in many action games.
- Raccoon City feels much different than it did on the original. There are lights and neon signs everywhere, lots of lighting and everything feels much bigger compared to the often small pathways the original had in the city.
- Areas that appeared in the original were cut, like the clock tower and the park.
- The game does not have a scary atmosphere at all.
- There is apparently only one ending.
- The decisions you could make when Nemesis appears in the original are gone.
- It's very short. I was AFK for over 2 hours when I played it, picked up all items, downed Nemesis all times and was done after 7,4 hours. If I look at the time I actually played it it's probably only like 5 hours.
- No mercenaries mode, and Resistance (what they added instead of mercenaries) feels unpolished.
- No choices at all, the game will be the same when you replay it. Almost no replay value.

Despite that, the game does have changes I like:
- The hospital actually feels like a hospital now.
- It makes much more sense for them to go to the hospital to look for a vaccine compared to the original.
- There's an underground lab section below the hospital now, which fills the purpose of the factory at the end of the original. It explains how the hospital researched things for Umbrella, and is also the waste disposal the factory was.
- While Nemesis is super annoying in this game, they really managed to make him feel more like this unstoppable monster he's supposed to be.
- Carlos and the others feel more competent and even found and protected multiple survivors in the subway. It makes sense because their "official" mission was to safe civilians.
- Jill doesn't go to the RPD, instead Carlos (and a new character) do while Jill uses the repaired subway. Carlos and the others had a mission to save an important Umbrella researcher, who apparently hides in the police station. This means there are now two parts where the player controls Carlos.

It feels like they were not sure what they really wanted to do, as if someone played the remake of 2, watched a playthrough of 3 and then started to work on it.

They could have went back to the old, smaller areas to make it feel more like the remake of Resident Evil 2 (Yes, I know the original 3 was also more action heavy compared to the previous ones, but the remakes being 3D already does that). Rely more on horror, atmosphere, slow paced gameplay, more cramped areas (like more indoor sections), less ammo and such. The game actually had a part that felt more like that, the new hospital. It was by far my favorite part of the game.

Or they could have taken a different approach. Make the city bigger (considering their obvious focus on fighting more enemies in wider places), make more areas explorable and make multiple endings depending on your choices. Maybe even let Jill save some survivors or something. Or add optional areas or just alternate paths through the city, considering how big it is. More focus on having scarce supplies and gathering them from what's left of the city.

Resident Evil 3 Remake delivers thrilling action, tight controls, and gorgeous visuals, but it doesn’t quite capture the complete story of the original. Some story beats are condensed or altered, and certain moments that made the OG game memorable are missing, which can leave longtime fans feeling a little shortchanged.

Verdict

Resident Evil 3 Remake is enjoyable and polished, but the story feels trimmed compared to the OG. Fans looking for full nostalgia might be disappointed, yet it’s still a solid action-horror experience.

Whilst it's not deserving of the praise RE2's remake achieved, it has its merits, though some nitpicks concern me, greatly.

Characters show up for no more than a quick cameo before vanishing into the ether, exacerbating the game's linearity. The dodge function is initially horrible, to the point that you have to unlock an item just to get it to be reliable, which is unfair considering there are a few enemies with guaranteed insta-kills.

The game *forces* you to look at a screen advising you to lower the difficulty every few deaths, which is patronising as hell on your first run, especially considering the aforementioned OHKO enemies, dodgy dodging and nemesis itself. An option to turn this off would be welcome, considering we have the CHOICE to change it with the shift key.

The level design is decent, but I feel as though some aspects of the game are more diluted than its predecessor and its classic incarnation. There are less puzzles, and though some areas feel expanded upon, not quite enough. A lot has been cut from the game. It feels shallower for it.

Where it doesn't feel shallow is in the representation of the plot and its characters, despite them only being prevalent for a short time, in some cases. Carlos is likeable now, instead of abhorrent. The re-imagined storyline moves a little too quickly, however. The fact that you can finish the game in under 2 hours in a speedrun attests to that.

The weapons and combat feel decent, but the dodging and such let it down, somewhat. All in all, it's a fine rebirth of RE3, considering that RE3 classic was considered the more difficult, combat-focused cousin of the more successful, more popular RE2.

I have a feeling that more time, money and manpower went into RE8, or the other, secret REmake that's going on behind the scenes. It might feel a little insipid compared to our hopes for it, but upon reflection I think it was fine enough, and with the COVID-19 outbreak, I'm happy we got it at all; if it had more time it'd be a better game for it, but it might also end up floating in limbo for a while.

TL;DR I'm happy with it, but it's not as bright a spark as I hoped it might be.

As a huge fan of the original Resident Evil 3 I thought RE3 remake all in all is a bad adaptation of it's source material. That being said I would still recommend the game it's difficult for me to separate my feelings towards the original game to this game however they are so drastically different I could hardly call them the same game at all. They've both got the same characters and the same general story beats but they are in no way shape or form the same game and when I separate RE3 Remake from the original RE3 what I'm left with is a solid game that's definitely not worth $60 but it's still very fun and I enjoyed it for what it is!

**Difficulties played:** Assisted, Standard, Hardcore, Nightmare, Inferno

**Pros:**

- Visuals and overall art direction are just as good as RE2 Remake. 

- A lot of enemy variety, I think maybe a little bit more than the RE2 Remake.

- Boss fights are just as good as RE2 Remake, if not better due to the dodge ability. 

- General Gameplay is just as good as RE2 Remake. Jill's dodge ability works a lot better than the original game. Overall, it's a blast to play. 

- Carlos is much more likable, at least to me, and has more playable sections.  Some people take issue with this, I do not. 

- When the game allows itself to have an atmosphere, it's damn good. 

- Nightmare mode offers an experience similar to the OG game's hard mode. There are different enemy placements and different item locations when you play this mode. However, it's annoying that you have to beat the game on hardcore mode in order to unlock this mode. 

**Cons:**

- Insultingly short with no side game modes, it only takes 4-5 hours to beat.  My clear time was 3 hours 30 minutes, but my total playtime was at around 4 hours 30 minutes. This is unacceptable for a $60 game. Not everyone is going to want to replay the game, unless you're a resident evil mega nerd like me.  

- There is no decision system, unlike the original game. Alternate endings, and branching paths are all elements that were taken out as well. 

- Nemesis barely has a presence at all in his humanoid form. He doesn't chase you that much and is way too easy to take down. His transformation is pretty disappointing as well.

- Puzzle solving is basically nonexistent. There are only two puzzles in the entire game. 

- Cutting out some of the best sections from the original game, such as the Clocktower, the Park, the Graveyard, and the Gravedigger boss. This is unacceptable as they aren't replaced with anything better. 

- The storytelling is okay, it's clearly rushed, and can come across as run of the mill. There are cutscenes that comprise of nightmare sequences. You can't get more generic than that. 

Summary:

A very fun game that ends way sooner than it should. I would only recommend buying it at full price if you are die hard RE fan that has to own and play every game in the series. If you're not, wait for a sale.

If Resident Evil 2 Remake became an emaciated zombie it'd be Resident Evil 3 Remake. I was ready to LOVE this sequel, the original RE3 was always my favorite of the saga. Yet I ended up terribly underwhelmed with such wasted potential, the good moments make it all the more tragic and unpalatable to think about.
At times it feels more like RE6 than RE3, particularly the first minutes. The prologue is a good summary of what could've been GREAT and what is bad about the game, you start in 1st person in Jill's apartment in a really moody and atmospheric moment; suffering from recurring nightmares and traumatized by the events in the Arklay Mountains, a document even points out her fears that she might have been infected and that she hasn't turned yet due to a long incubation period.  One of her apartment's walls is occupied for an investigation board on Umbrella and its activities and a pizza box sits on her kitchen's table bought by her friends at RPD with a supportive note from Brad that was snuck inside. So far so good isn't it? 
Well... Half a minute later it turns into a tensionless heavily scripted and railroaded garbage setpiece where Jill survives being chased by Nemesis through "crazy" action movie feats including ramming someone with a car off a parking's rooftop and surviving, QTEs included.
The prologue also makes less sense than the original and makes Jill look like a bit of a simpleton: despite the obvious signs (including TV news reports of a pandemic of unprecedented contagion rate!) that the same pathogen she encountered in the Mansion is infecting the whole of Raccoon City she decides to stay an arbitrary amount of days until leaving the city (and for reasons unrelated to the incidents themselves) and she seems to be completely oblivious about what was happening to the city and its inhabitants.
The game is alarmingly short too. I am the complete antithesis of a speedrunner, I like to take time with my games, taking in the atmosphere and the world I'm immersed in, trying to interact with the world and characters as much as I can, explore the world and what it says about those who live in it; still I managed to finish this in just 5 hours (Clear time around 3 and a half hours). In great deal due to an incredible amount of content cut from the original (characters and interactions with them, locations, creatures, events...).
Such as:
· The entire first act of the original game is absent or done away with in the first cutscenes, you start basically at the subway station.
· Incredibly linear, little to no backtracking nor meaningful exploration.
· Nemesis is a joke as an antagonist: Imagine how tense and oppressive, how GREAT would've been to have a Mr X. that can run and is heavily armed relentlessly chasing you through the city. Well, Capcom certainly didn't: you'll only get a glimpse of that in the first and only open area of the game (the one from the demo).
Because of the way his encounters are designed, which are heavily scripted, he comes off as comically incompetent, which is exacerbated by the arsenal he has at his disposal. His "aim" with the Rocket Launcher is so bad that you can escape through the entire sequence unscathed just by running. In the construction building chase he will be shooting his flame thrower at empty space  instead of pursuing because his scripted sequence can't catch up with you. In cutscenes, every chance he has to go for the kill he will go out of his way not to: if he grabs Jill by the head it will only be to throw her to the floor or a wall, if he has her cornered in the floor he will walk as slowly as possible towards her.
He is not a threat, he is an annoyance.
Mr. X did more of a "Nemesis" job than this Nemesis, and he only had his fists.
· Very promising secondary characters, such as Mikhail, get their potential development tragically cut down. I'd loved for them to get the RE2 Remake treatment (The only character close to this is Carlos, with him they did a fairly good job, everyone else is either "blink and you miss them" or one dimensional).
· Barely any walking through the streets. Part of the charm of the original was fighting through the streets and finally getting to see the city of the damned itself after having gotten just a glimpse in the previous game,trying to piece together how life might have been observing the beautiful pre-rendered backgrounds.
Now characters mostly teleport to wherever the plot needs through the magic "fade away"s. In one instance, Carlos has to take Jill to the Hospital while piggybacking her after she's been incapacitated: I thought to myself "hey that might be challenging and interesting, nice change of pace too"... cutscene fades away and another shows him having reached the Hospital already. The game shoots itself on the foot like that constantly, calling it rushed might not even begin to cover it.
· The final location is an uninteresting "slick", aseptic, shiny white walled super secret laboratory. It is a "movie set" laboratory. 
· Only 2 puzzles worth being called puzzle, in a RE game!
· No RPD station visit as Jill
· No Clock Tower
· No Sales Office
· No newspaper building.
· No Raccoon Park 
· No Cementery
· No Disused Plant
· No Incineration Disposal Plant proper.
· Locations such as the STAGLA gas station, Bar Jack and the warehouse where Dario Rosso locks himself are only thrown in in glorified cutscenes. Cannot meaningfully explore or interact with them at all.
· Maybe it wouldn't have been so much of an issue if in place of all the cut environments there was new ones with the potential of being interesting on their own. There aren't any.
· Many, many assets are reused from RE2, zombie models are the most notable.
· And yet, even features from RE2 Remake are absent aswell!! Most notably enemy bodies' physics.
· Documents are so uninspired and short, most of them not even worth reading.
· The final battle (half shooting gallery, half hold button), and the whole finale really, are incredibly anticlimactic.
· Jill saying "It's my turn, ♥♥♥♥♥!" and "♥♥♥♥♥ can't even swim" is just wrong.
Etc. Etc.

By the way, about extra modes: there are none! Only artwork and models. If you liked The Mercenaries tough luck chump!

Welcome to The Nerd Clubs' first review, Resident Evil 3 Remake. 

Youtube Review Link:https://youtu.be/_xTt9wqgdOU

Coming into Resident Evil 3 my expectations were high as a big fan of resident evil and Capcom's previous game being resident evil 2 remake which has critical success. The question is were my expectations met or did they end up going down the raccoon city drain, lets find out.

[b] Gameplay [/b]

First up is the gameplay, shooting still feels great as its predecessor shooting system is the exact same over the shoulder style,  although it has a lot more action to it, there are still times when I had to limit my ammo and be smart with gunpowder which is keeping it faithful to the original RE3 which was more action-heavy than its predecessor also.

One game-changing mechanic is the dodge button, if you successfully time a dodge you are rewarded with max paynesque time slow which will allow you to punish your enemy for trying to chomp on you! Admittedly i found myself spamming the button a few times due to being scared out of mind but I manage to actually use the dodge mechanic correctly and pulled off some amazing dodges which made me feel like a badass, its a great mechanic for casual gamers and speedrunners alike. 

Nemesis is also a core part of the game, now nemesis does have a few new tricks up his trench coat, he can jump around like crazy in the streets, tentacle pulls you towards your doom and what seems to be an endless amount of rockets and flamethrower fuel, now because the game runtime is quite short it can appear the nemesis does show up often but in fact, I feel like we did not get to see enough of our Tyrant Stalker, we only got experience him once or twice in the streets of raccoon and then following types were an arena type boss battle. 

The boss battles were fun, we only got to experience one boss but in different multiple forms which for me took away from the game as I wanted to see famous bosses like Grave Digger! I feel like a bit more variety within this particular area would have been great.

Puzzles, I love resident evil puzzles as its how you figure out to move onto the next area, you have to earn it but in resident evil 3 there are no puzzles, the closest we get is a train segment finding the clear train to go onto, for me this is a big blow as in the original they were plenty of great puzzles to enjoy.

Within the game you will take control of both Carlos and Jill, both have different aspects of play. When Carlos uses the dodge button perfectly I found him haymaking beta hunters across the room, which although made me laugh the first time I did come to find it reminded me of Chris punching boulders in resident evil 5, to summarise the main difference between Jill and Carlos, Jill's gameplay is much more focus on survival horror and Carlos is more action packer horror, which if I am honest I enjoyed, it changed the pace up and I found myself wanting more.

The game seems to be missing a lot of content from the original, which I could usually forgive if they replaced it but they didn't, it kinda ruined the pacing of the game and it felt rushed.


[b] Graphics [/b]

On the PC the game looked great, the characters within the game sometimes looked human in the cutscenes and I would sometimes forget I was playing a game and not watching a tv series.

The environments tell a story, if you place close attention to your surroundings you can find hunter marks on the walls with tons of dead bodies, blood trails with dead bodies, teddy bears with wheelchairs in which give the game its mature feel. 

All of the characters within the game were really well made, I completed the game with the standard models and I have to say they were really well done, something that I picked up on that really impressed me was how dirty jill got, no not like that. As you progress through the game Jill and Carlos both get dirtier, with blood and scratches on their arms, armor and clothes which again done a really good job of immersing me more into the game.

Nemesis' new look is great, him slowly mutating as the game continued was interesting and had me wondering how far he could go, the final boss form for me is one my favorite form of bosses I have seen in a resident evil game. The only thing I missed out on was the second form of Nemesis from the original, it seems the developer decided to cut that form out.

Graphically the game is pleasing, the lighting has been well done and really adds that extra spooky factor, you can be looking down an alleyway and it will all be dark but at end of the tunnel is a stores neon light, your mind will play tricks walking down the alley, is their zombies or am I missing loot.

Everything from a graphics standpoint compliments the gameplay which is a testament to Capcom's great visuals team.  

[b] Audio [/b]

The soundtrack within this game has a lot of recognizable songs from the original resident evil 3 which have also been remastered to make them more atmospheric.

The voice acting within this game was on point, every character was cast perfectly, not once did anyone feel out of place. I do want to highlight Jill, Nicholai and Carlos's voice actors really created a stellar performance, not to take away from anyone else but these had me invested through their performances.

[b] Story [/b]

The game takes places 2 months after the incident at raccoon city, the city is invested with flesh-eating zombies and umbrellas terrifying bioweapons, Jill is the main protagonist and has several layers to the character with her fighting PTSD and sleeping issues while trying to save the residents of raccoon city which made me full in love with the character more. The story follows Jill trying to avoid the umbrella created Tyrant Nemesis, who had been created with one mission in mind to kill all remaining star members, Jill being one of them.

The story is the same as the original but it fleshes out the lore and the characters but not through gameplay but through the files you find, in fact they cut allot of content and replaced it with files. I would say my main gripe was with the ending, it felt lackluster. There also seemed to be a pacing issue from the last third of the game when you take over Jill in the hospital, it really rushes the story and when you complete it you can tell it needed more time.

[b] Overall conclusion [/b]

Resident Evil 3 remake is majorly high quality and is an impressive game but felt really short and lacked allot of content. I personally bought my copy from Gamersgate for £38.99 and if the game did not include the Resident evil resistance I personally would have felt I did not get my money worth, of course, there is replayability by playing in a different costume and doing certain challenges but for the average consumer, I would wait until the game goes on sale.

I can't help but feel sad for the game, its missing loads of content from the actual story to no extra content like mercenaries or a different game mode, which every main installment of resident evil has had.

Here we are in 2020, and by today's writing we've had all three classic RE titles remade.  A total of five years of painful waiting since 2015 and now both 2 and 3 are totally remade.  Crazy to think about.

If you've never played the original Nemesis, a lot of the hype may fly over your head for this game.  After steamrolling through the base difficulty, I think what Capcom produced was a flawed but solid game that delivers on its concept and Jill Valentine's famous "last escape."

I think of all things, the tension, Jill and Carlos's retooled banter, and the infamous Nemesis are where this game shines the most.
 
Obviously there are issues, content was clearly cut or all together changed, but as a Resident Evil game being short is real no surprise, games like 6 are a huge exception.  I can't help but wonder if changes were made to make Nemesis less-chasey so as not to shy away the modern gamer but maybe we'll never know.

I'll dive in for more, try some harder difficulties, but as of now, I still recommend this despite the changes and short length.  RE Engine is stunning, the monsters are fantastic (particularly the Hunters, one of the best redesigns since the original, they are truly some of the scariest enemies among all RE games), the music is stellar (something RE2make lacked) and Jill herself remains a badass.  

I wouldn't say this replaces the original, it's different, and definitely more of a reimagining than a remake.

Still, a definite recommend.  Solid 8/10.  Flawed, but still good.

It's ok, but there are definitely some issues that really got to me as a diehard RE fan. 

-It's short and there's only one campaign, you won't hear that just from me though.
-Nemesis shows up at scripted events. Most of them are visually spectacular, but you don't feel like you're hunted like with Mr. X.
-The movement doesn't feel as good as RE:2 Remake. Feels a little faster and floaty. After about 2 hours, even an average player can master the dodge roll and it really takes away the feeling of danger when there's a lot of zombies. You can literally just wait for a lunge and then nail a dodge roll and get through all of them. 
-Unless you are double-tapping literally everything in your path, ammo is not scarce. Spent way too much time playing inventory manager simulator. Not once did I have that moment of, "Oh man, better make this shot count". 
-The grenade launcher... Too many options of ammo type. There are 4 types (acid, fire, explosive, mine), which are sure to clog your inventory real quick. Mine rounds felt redundant when there is the explosive type, and explosive rounds felt like they were just better fire rounds.
-If you never played the original, I'm sure it won't be a problem but there are some DEEP cuts as far as iconic areas and story. 
-While I think the idea of giving Nemesis some new mutations and arsenal is good, I just didn't feel like Capcom captured the essence of the character well like they did with Mr. X and G Birkin. I don't know if that makes sense to anyone that hasn't played it, but I think you'll get my meaning if you do. 
-Only one challenging boss fight (2nd to last), and I felt that a lot of the challenge was more that the game decided to cheat and just make the hitbox for the boss's moves bigger. I would dodge the move where he steps on you and bites you, but then he just teleported on top of me. 
-What the hell happened to Brad at RPD? Where is Barry? Huge character moments rewitten/cut entirely. Already made mention of story cuts, but they are supposed to be like the A team as far as supplemental non-player characters in the RE universe. Without these characters/moments, the game feels completely disconnected from RE:1 and Jill just feels like some lady trying to get out of the city with no emotional ties to anyone except Carlos and maybe Tyrell a little.

All in all, it's fun to play, but at the end I just had this feeling of 75% satisfaction. I had such a boner to play this game and I didn't climax. That's my review header.

Have a pretty mixed feeling regarding this title, to the point where I hesitantly slammed a "not recommended" rating for this thing (at least when it is priced at $60).

Let's get the good out of the way first:
- Great graphics
- When it tries to be a horror game, it REALLY is terrifying
- The shotgun feels a lot of useful this time around
- When nemesis is chasing you, he is a much more intimidating than Mr X
- Dodging mechanic is satisfying to pull off yet does not break the survival horror theme by itself
- Although nothing groundbreaking, the soundtrack is more memorable than RE2:R
- Boss fights are much more enjoyable than RE2:R
- Backtracking is still as enjoyable as RE2:R
- Jill and Carlos are cool i suppose
- New Game+ support is there, offering some unlockables for future playthroughs

Now, here comes the bad stuff:
- The standard difficulty is far too easy. I recommend bumping it up to hardcore mode
- Ammo is abundant, at the end I have a lot more ammo than I really should
- Making the knife unbreakable is a mistake
- The whole game feels extremely linear, despite the supposedly increased emphasis on the city itself
- Many locations from the original game are cut from this remake
- Some unlockable weapons from the original game are cut
- Nemesis item drops are toned down; he stops dropping anything special for you after the second encounter
- Carlos in general is a bit OP, playing as him either felt like a power fantasy or a frustrating mess
- ♥♥♥♥ beta hunters and their random one-hit kill nonsense
- Nemesis is severely underused. Overall, he felt more like a recurring boss rather than a relentless stalker hunting you throughout the game
- For the second half of the game, Nemesis nearly felt completely absent from the game (when he's not being a boss I mean)
- They removed the ragdoll physics for some reason
- Zombies interaction has been toned down from RE2:R. For instance, you can no longer cut off all the limbs from a zombie
- The gore isn't as satisfying as RE2:R
- Performance is much more unstable than RE2:R, had a lot of minor hic-ups on my machine
- Game is way too short. Even taking it really slowly, I beat it under 6 hours
- Scripted sequences are cool for the first run but can get irritating for future playthroughs I assume
- Compared to OG RE3 and RE2:R, the replay value just isn't as great as these two games. Mainly because there is no alternate route/ new stuff for future playthroughs.
- No mercenaries mode or any extra single-player modes for that matter

Conclusion: No matter how you are looking at it, this remake is a disappointing title and does not live up to the standard set by RE2:R. Instead of a faithful remake that tries to expand on the original materials, this felt more like a reimaging that borrows some of the original materials for use. This doesn't mean that RE3:R is a bad game, but given its short length and the shortcomings listed above, what's offered here really doesn't justify the $60 price tag. I recommend trying this out ONLY when it is on sale (Like around -50%).

I was excited for this game for months and when I was playing through the game I was getting progressively disappointed. My expectations were very high because of how incredible RE:2 Remake was. I already set the bar very high because of this and sadly RE:3 Remake couldn't deliver. 

The whole campaign felt lazily made. Instead of referencing the events of RE:2 Remake, it based a lot of its campaign storytelling on the RE:2 campaign. I liked that they made quirky references to the previous game but it just felt like they shaved off hours of potential storytelling by just hitching a ride on the other game, so to speak. 

RE:2 Remake's progressive puzzle solving and map-unlocking was not consistent in this game. It very much felt like you were rushed through areas of the game by grabbing stuff immediately and leaving the area to never go back to it again. The constant fearful presence of Nemesis was intense and exciting within the early stages of the game when he was most present, but later on you slogged through boring areas of the game waiting for Nemesis to come back. 

If you liked RE:2 Remake you will like this game for what it is. If your expectations were as high as mine then you will be let down. But there were some great aspects. Action was intense. The next boss fight was just as crazy as the last. References to the original were appealing. The dodge mechanic was a good idea, needs a little work but it adds flavour. Graphics are stunning, Absolutely stunning. It was nice to see the Remake complimented the original game by keeping some of the original's ideas and certain gameplay mechanics. 

But the bottom line is; it felt rushed. It felt like there could have been more. In RE:2 there were 2 (technically 4) campaigns to play, which were sort of mirrors of each other but at least there was something to keep you invested to keep playing. There is only one campaign in this. You play as both Jill and Carlos in one campaign, The only thing keeping you to play this game, is to play the game on progressively harder difficulties and unlock even harder ones. All this to unlock achievements/unlocks that won't really be utilised fully.

Edit:

I have played the game for an additional 12 hours since my original review. I have completed the game on Inferno and completing the challenge felt rewarding. It reminded me of running hard challenges on RE:2 Remake. 

I still stick to my overall original point that the game could have been a whole lot more. The game made me wanting more from it; I couldn't feel satisfied with finishing it. 

Jill's story is rather short and lacking in content - when she's not active you have Carlos, who feels like shoot 'em up filler with no character at all. Which sucks because in the conversations you have with him in cutscenes he is a very likeable character and I would have liked to see a lot more from him. Like, what he was doing before we are introduced to Jill, his work in saving civilians, the part of the story when Jill is inactive for half a day and Carlos IS, but there was no story up until discovering Jill. There could have been a lot more substance to Carlos. He had a lot of potential than just filler in my opinion.

Jill's story is good but short-lived. The relentless and constant looming presence of Nemesis is what had your blood pumping, when he was chasing you down you could feel the adrenaline. There are areas of the game where he isn't present where you slog through (what I felt to be) boring areas of the game. I wish there was more to them, like, running into people and developing something with them, Jill learns something from them, you work together. Just. Something. Instead of having new items thrown at you and mowing down zombies with them. I feel like what ~would~ have made me like those areas more is knowing that Nemesis is just around the corner. 

For example, when you enter the sewers and you walk past the office window, going into that room and looking out to see Nemesis would have been perfect. Knowing that he is ALWAYS following you, it just felt like, when you escaped him, nothing happened and then he just appeared and you had to deal with him there and then, then have another break. A perfect example of that was Mr. X, you knew he was always there, looking for you. Always. You could hear him all of the time. When you escaped him and you forgot about him for a moment. Bam. He appeared and scared the hell out of you. 

The moments when you are being chased by Nemesis were intense. You could never outrun him, so you hard to play smart and lose him somehow. With Mr.X you knew you could just walk faster than him or enter a doorway and you'd get seconds of leeway to get away and never really have to worry about him. With Nemesis he is relentless. That excitement of running away is what made those areas. 

The boss fights on Standard - Nightmare were fun. On Inferno they were incredible, they were so unforgiving and intense. Sometimes I felt the mechanics were a little unfair because sometimes you couldn't escape taking hits ie. dodging not working perfectly or getting combo'd to death. Finishing the final boss fight on Inferno was so incredibly rewarding; it felt amazing. The boss fight was TOUGH, there was no room for error and you had to be perfect when doing it, putting all that hard work into the fight and winning? The sensation is second to none. 

Conclusion:

For what it is; the game is incredible. The graphics are stunning. What makes Resident Evil games is the fear of "Science has gone too far" and how gross they can make mutations and enemies. When you can visually see how vile and disgusting the abominations are; really getting immersed in the beauty of how realistic things look and are, it makes a VERY good horror game. You feel like it COULD happen. It looks and feels realistic when you're fully immersed and feeling that sensation of awe/terror. The acting felt real and like there was real emotion there. Animations were smooth and fluid, there were some mild exceptions where the game glitched but nothing stood out. (Except for when you go down the elevator and Jill's necklace starts floating above her head? Her shirt and chest have a weird jiggle sometimes for no reason.)

The story was short-lived and I felt like there could have been more quantity AND quality. I know a lot of players who expected a deeply-invested story finished the game feeling dissatisfied. References to the original RE:3 and the RE:2 Remake game were nice. The game leaned a little too heavy on references to RE:2 Remake story wise. It had the potential to be 11/10 but felt more of a 6/10 - 8/10. It could have been so so much more.

Overall, it just left me wanting more. It didn't feel like a £50 game. 

I wish CAPCOM acknowledges this and release some free DLCs for some more content and substance to the people wanting more. Hopefully a mini Carlos story. Maybe Brad, Nicholai, Mikhail or Marvin. Or all of the above.

I'm a massive Resident Evil fan. I loved the hell out of the RE2 remake, thought they kept it 90% faithful but the stuff they changed made sense for a modern take on an old classic. That said, Resident Evil 3 is my favorite in the entire franchise for a number of reasons. Despite RE3 taking the blame for kicking the RE series into action, I thought it was a nice mixture of horror, drama and action that traumatized me as a kid and continues to entertain me as an adult. I have almost the whole script memorized, I know how to speedrun it, I loved the Mercenaries mode which had you strategically race through the city on a 10-minute timer that gets longer for every enemy kill, every dodge, and every civilian rescued, with 4 characters to play as that have different weapon arsenals.

I knew RE3 wouldn't have Mercenaries mode and is instead implementing the "Resistance" game which is an online multiplayer game capitalizing off of the "Dead By Daylight" trend that everyone and their mother is trying to cash in on (including the makers of Outlast, Red Barrels, announcing their new game will be multiplayer). Capcom would make everyone very happy if they just remastered Resident Evil Outbreak but apparently they'd rather just recycle assets from RE2 and call it a day.

Preface aside, here's my review: the game isn't bad, but it's extremely mediocre.

The entire intro in the remake is different from the original, and it's all a downgrade. Instead of Jill fighting through an urban wasteland crawling with what feels like a hundred zombies, meeting up with her teammate Brad, hearing him warn about Nemesis "coming for us" as he ominously puts it, watching him get slaughtered by Nemesis in front of the RPD before choosing to either fight Nemesis or run inside the building, we instead get an intro with Jill slowly touring her entire apartment (with some exposition in the form of documents for whatever reason) before experiencing a nightmare about her turning into a zombie. She wakes up, gets a phone call from Brad sounding alarmed, and immediately the wall blasts open and Nemesis appears with his face covered by a plastic bag and attempts to kill Jill. No buildup, no tension, just WHOAH FIRE EXPLOSIONS RUN AWAY FROM THE BIG MONSTER IN THESE INCREDIBLY EASY SCRIPTED SEQUENCES THAT HAVE YOU HOLDING FORWARD TO GET AWAY. Then you encounter Brad who JUST SO HAPPENS to be passing by the alleyway you're emerging from (and is now suddenly cracking jokes and sounds very relaxed considering he was flipping out just moments prior over the phone) and you run into a nearby cafe to get away from the zombies. The zombies break through, bite Brad, and he pulls the cliche'd "I'm infected and we both know I'm done for so I'll buy you some time and hold them off knowing I'm gonna die anyway" schtick as Jill runs into a nearby alleyway. Brad was on-screen for all of 3 minutes before they killed him off to advance the plot. Okay.

She picks up a handgun from a nearby zombie and says "Sorry." Jill makes it a regular gag to apologize to corpses for taking their stuff. It's just kind of annoying and she does it multiple times.

Then she runs into a room and meets Dario Rosso, a writer/poet in the original game who had red hair and looked like a chubby dude in his 30's, but this game decided to make him about 70 and balding. Dario Rosso in the original is a super unimportant character, but his vocal performance is superb and he was someone that always impressed me in the beginning of the game. He screams at you at the top of his lungs, mourns the VERY RECENT death of his daughter, and then locks himself in a storage container and says he'd rather starve to death than be eaten by "one of those undead monsters." This Dario Rosso mocks Jill, when she says "I'm a police officer and I'm here to help," he laughs and says "Oh yeah, you're doing a bang-up job." His vocal delivery sounds annoyed and sarcastic, which compared to the original VA sounding on the brink of losing his mind, is a downgrade that let me know immediately this game was going to be mediocre. They also cut the bit of dialogue where he mentions he "lost his daughter out there" because the game is in an INSANE hurry to move the plot along and apparently one of my favorite characters just needs to get out of Jill's way so she can get to the shooting.

The characters in this game are super obnoxious. Jill is always talking to herself and making goofy observations, saying the obligatory "♥♥♥♥" and "♥♥♥♥" and "♥♥♥♥ THAT WAS SO GROSS," and when she's approached by people she barely knows and are trying to cooperate with her she just speaks to them sarcastically and it really paints her as a c*nt considering she was so focused and stoic in RE1 and RE5. She picks up a Magnum and comments "Guaranteed to give you a headache." Just stop, oh my god.

Carlos is a Hispanic Umbrella Mercenary who comes to Jill's aid, but the most he said in the way of flirtaciousness was "All the foxy ladies love my accent!" and for the rest of the game he was extremely serious and dedicated to protecting Jill and his platoon. In the remake, he's a white guy (no noticeable accent or dialect) with dark skin and curly black hair who constantly, CONSTANTLY cracks jokes. A door won't open? He says "Open sesame." He tells Jill he won't die and leave her in a "Cold, cruel, Carlos-less world." He calls Jill "Supercop" numerous times. Even when Jill is in critical condition he's making inappropriate jokes. A tertiary character waiting for Jill to wake up from a medically-induced coma says to her "Morning, sleepyhead!" as soon as she wakes up. Ugh.

Carlos' commanding officer, Mikhail, was on death's door in the original game. He was laying down in the subway car, bleeding profusely, hallucinating and having war flashbacks, saying "Fire... FIRE!!! Stay... together!" and he was completely useless as he laid there struggling to stay conscious. In the remake, he's only slightly wounded, sitting up, walking around, cracking jokes about the remaining civilians, referring to them as the "soon-to-be undead."

Nikolai, who is the villain, is also just ridiculously over-the-top in terms of his nefariousness. In the original it was played subtly, he was a competent soldier and leader and he was made out to be a pragmatic leader. Now he just mugs, smirks, and winks at Jill as he makes no effort whatsoever to hide his ruthlessness. It's like I'm watching a children's cartoon.

Also they cut the entire Clocktower section from the game and just skip straight to the hospital. That was my favorite locale from the PS1 version and it's just gone now. Cool.

Also you've probably heard from the press but yes, this game is incredibly short. I beat the RE2 remake in like 20 hours I'm pretty sure, and I'm 5 hours in and already at the end of the game. I've seen playthroughs beat it in 4 hours max. Just embarrassing. Capcom is one of my favorite companies but they absolutely shoveled this out and cut so many corners that it's depressing to know I was incredibly excited for this.

And if you enjoy the game, good. I'm happy people are enjoying it. As far as action games go, it's not the worst thing on the planet, but compared to the original upon which it's based, it's woefully wasted potential. For 60 dollars (and tax) I expected a lot more than 4-5 hours of playtime. Just stop dismissing criticism as "TEH HATERZ" when we have pages upon pages of valid criticisms. I was okay with the changes in the RE2 remake as it felt like it was an improvement over the original. The changes in this game compared to the original are an objective downgrade. The people who will defend this game are clueless to its' original origins and just want to consoom big blockbuster action game for their funny LetsPlay/Twitch audience.

tl;dr an okay action game but it completely bastardizes the original. Only buy if you're okay paying $60 for 4-5 hours of gameplay with no replayability.

Resident Evil 3 is the latest of remakes for the classic games, treating them to a fresh coat of paint for the current generation. The Resident Evil 2 Remake revitalised the hype for the series, but does the current game hold up?

...Yes. Ohhh dear goodness yes it does. (In my opinion.)

Pros:

Visuals: Every single segment of the game looks absolutely incredible, the attention to detail was truly bumped up from the prior game, and it was surprisingly extremely smooth to run. Not a single graphic-related issue occurred, which is a welcome change from the usual gaming habits of "Release a game, then patch it to finality." Every set piece looks stunning, and the character models look more real than ever before seen, from my experience.

Gameplay: The gameplay is more of the same from it's predecessor, but it feels surprisingly fresh this time around with the addition of dodging. Usually, if you time it decently enough, a sidestep or backwards dodge will save you from a lunging zombie's strike, but if you time it at the very last moment, another new mechanic shows in the form of Perfect Dodges. Pulling these off not only has your character dodge faster, but aiming with your weapon will slow time down to allow you to deal some immediate reprisal damage. It's tricky to pull off, but boy is it ever satisfying when you time it just right.

Map Design: Compared to the usually claustrophobic halls of the Racoon City Police Department, having to survive out in the open streets amidst the rampant chaos makes you truly feel a sense of overwhelming odds. You feel like everything is out to get you, from the initial threat of the zombies, to the ever looming presence of Nemesis hunting you with unrelenting zeal. However, it never feels like it's unfairly laid out, enemy placements are fair, if sometimes a bit startlingly compact at times. Careful consideration of your surroundings is a must.

Not-So-Pros:

Campaign Length: Compared to RE2, RE3 has only one campaign with no different paths to take, and with how generally fast-paced the story progression is, the entire experience feels surprising short in spite of everything that bars you from the end. As always, there is a time-attack factor to consider with rankings, so it was designed with realistic, but difficult goals, but it somewhat feels like that's the initial mindset rather than the foreboding dread of your next encounter.

There are some things I'm not covering like the records challenges or the shop which works with currency you earn from said record challenges, but that's mainly for repeat playthroughs. In spite of how seemingly short it may appear, Resident Evil 3 offers an almost unparalleled adrenal high throughout the game's story. There's no pace-breaking segments, leaving me with nothing but praise for it.

Overall, I'd rate the experience 9/10, I absolutely love near everything about it, and I cannot recommend it enough.

(P.S. You also get an entirely extra game in Resident Evil Resistance, so, get your money's worth, I suppose.)

Resident Evil 3 (2020) starts straight away with a nostolgic confrontation, to remind and instill in us who we all feared back in 1999. Nemesis provides a far more brooding presence in this remake as you progress, chasing you through Raccoon City. There is still a lot of charm and connections to the original, but it sets itself apart by completely reworking the areas (in part also removing some) and storyline progression. The gameplay is far more action packed, and fast paced. There's constantly a sense of endangerment from every and all types of enemies, but that's where the new quick dodge mechanic comes in handy.
	Both Resident Evil 2 (2018) and Resident Evil 3 (2020) set themselves apart in their own way compared to the orignals, and it's hard to like everything about them through rose tinted glasses. This game in particular has a lot of glaring "flaws" for some people. It's relatively short, there's practically no replayability unless you want collectables or unimportant unlockables. There are no modes besides the main game, no "split second" choices, or alternate endings, Ii's entirely linear now. At a full price of 60 USD, this game is a hard sell for non-resident evil fans
	I personally still really loved the game. It has an immense amount of charm, and the retelling of the story impressed me. RE2 sets itself apart from the orginal, but RE3 goes even further. Seeing all the familiar faces was great, and how some characters get bigger roles was a welcome change. Exploring new parts of Raccoon City only makes me want more. (Please remake Outbreak...) All the boss fights were amazing. Even though the story at times really set you on a linear path, what happens is just stunning. A couple areas were abandoned for newer ones, and while I do miss one in particular.. and also wish there was an uptown area like the original, it's just a breath of fresh air compared to RE2. Still, it feels like an expansion of RE2 as oppossed to a full fledged remake. Nevertheless, it was a great experience to play through the game and an absolute must for an RE fan. I highly suggest waiting for a sale.

Resident Evil 3 remake is likely to go down as a game that almost was, because frankly, in its current state, it’s unfinished and missing core parts. Quite simply, the first two acts of Resident Evil 3 are so harshly compressed together that even a strong finish can’t really save it. But first, I need to issue at least SOME praise.

The final two hours, with some minor issues withstanding, are actually fairly solid overall. I found myself becoming more and more engaged with seeing where the game would go and how things would be executed. It’s not quite on par with the RE2 remake, but it felt like it was in the same ballpark. I do wish to strongly underline that I REALLY enjoyed this third and final act.

Likewise, the action horror gameplay remains to be highly engaging, and the handling of the core characters, Jill and Carlos most notably, is particularly strong. There’s a slightly cheesier touch to RE3’s delivery than its predecessor (and tonally it’s closer to Resident Evil 4), but it works. From a purely mechanical perspective, RE3 is a solid-to-great game, but there’s greater issues at play here.

The grand problem, however, is that these 2 hours or so of effective gameplay feel like the final acts of what was supposed to be a MUCH larger game. What occurs prior to this is so rushed and slapdash that it borders on the infuriating (or for fans of the series, deeply depressing). The entire first act of RE3 remake is rushed through and reduced to a series of awkwardly stapled-together dot points.

The first act in particular compresses a staggering amount of content in its first 20 minutes-to-first-hour and it all feels awkwardly thrown together, rather than anything cohesive. It’s a surge between high points of action without any pacing, build, or logical progression, and one that leaves you constantly bothered by the sudden forward lurches.

The second act does get a LITTLE better, but again, it feels awkwardly stapled together and this sudden and awkward shift between sequences continues. Ironically, it isn’t until things slow down a bit with the switch to Carlos, that this sense of whiplash slows down. This final act DOES have a similar style of large set pieces and Nemesis battles to the earlier parts, but they feel earned after exploration and puzzle action in a range of settings.

Again, this game does feel like a strange edited TV bootleg cut of what is supposed to be a much larger game. The final act, which runs about 90 minutes to 2 hours of the 5-6 hours gameplay, feels like something that should have followed 5-8 hours of game before it. Unfortunately, this is ultimately what damages RE3 and makes it little more than a curiosity in its current state.

Were there to be a ‘Director’s Cut’ or ‘REmix’ edition that restored the content to the first two acts, I would easily recommend the Resident Evil 3 remake, but it’s a pale shadow of what it could have been, and that… is deeply disappointing.

Getting it done right off the bat. If you expected any sort of faithful remake of the 1999 release, look elsewhere. BUT if you want a really well done Resident Evil game, that connects VERY well to the remake we got in 2019 of Resident Evil 2, and having more sense timeline wise, this game is for you!

I love both this and the original 1999 release. They both have their good and bad points, and for what time Capcom had (or even gave themselves) this is an astounding game, and a lot of people are giving it flak for some reason. Anyway, instead of gushing over this game how about I just give the pros, cons, and the stuff in-between?

Pros:
-Finally, we have a set of games that actually connect and make sense in each others continuity. Seriously. The original 2 on PS1 tried and failed at this, and I'm glad to see this fixed.
-The dodge mechanic is actually functional AND fun to use now. Seriously, pullin' them perfect dodges feels amazing!
-Nemesis has a few new moves that I guess he learned in these 21 years, and they will scare the ever living crap outta ya. 
-Brad dies as a freakin' CHAD this time. I won't spoil how, but I guess he's trying to make up for being a coward all those years ago.
-RE Engine looks freakin' beautiful and Raccoon City feels ALIVE, like it was an actual city. You see a bunch of shops, I believe wander into peoples homes at a couple points, and a few other things!
-Jill seems like one of my favorite characters here because they got her personality and everything about her down pat. I'd say all the characters are really well done and are either likable or dislikable as intended.
-There's now a mechanic where you can take less damage with certain attacks against you by mashing a button or holding it. (You can change between mash/hold in the options menu)

Cons:
-Choice system from the original 1999 release was excluded, and for me that's a huge issue for this game because that added a ton of opportunity for replaying the game in the PS1 release.
-Some moments feel very cheap in this game. Such as having to use so many healing items because Nemesis or a zombie or other creature got a cheap hit in, and you have to heal.
-Graphics were definitely downgraded from REmake2. They're not bad, and they're still amazing but it's definitely noticeable.

In the middle:
-Nemesis isn't really around much, though I can understand this decision. Here, the world is much more fluid and doesn't have door loading screens for him to follow you through. So I guess I can understand peoples complaints of it feeling scripted but it was always this way and it just feels a bit off now because this is a more modern game. 
-A couple weird choices were made near the middle/end of the game, not that they're bad but it could have been better too. 

If you want to wait for a sale on this game, I'd say go ahead! There's no problem there, I can understand shelling $59.99 for a game like this would be rough on some, but if you can I'd say this is worth full price, and one of my favorite Resident Evil's so far, especially if you played REmake2. They both feel like they connect so well, and it's amazing.

I'm completely in love with the SURVIVAL HORROR GENE and I usually play all these games in hardcore difficult and try to get all achievements, if possible. This said, let's review:

Pros:
- It includes a couple of new mechanics that make the gameplay even better than its recent predecesor.
- So far, one of the best scenary and map designs of survival horror history. You DO believe you're in 1998 visiting stores in a village in the USA. The Raccoon City is just awesome.
- Enemies are so cool that it hurts your heart to kill them :_( Of course they're pretty similar to those in RE2 Remake.
- Story has enough of the old to be loyal to the original RE3 and enough new plot twists to be considered a completely new game. Just embrace it.
- The characters: brilliant and realistic, more realistic than ever. Thank you Capcom.
- Acting voices: very good ones.
- Weapons: nice designs and great game experience. Specially at the end...
- Maps are an absolute remake, I mean: they are completely different to the original ones.
- Sound design: lovely. I'm playing the game with 5.1, I recommend that if you don't have periferic speakers, use headphones.
- Music is so epic I take a long time in each scenery to be sure I've enjoyed it enough.

Cons:
- It's not a remake, it's more a re-imagination.
- The game ends before you realize it. :P
- Capcom have recicled way too much from RE7 and RE2 Remake. Items/Props specially.
- The engine seems a bit rusty for a "AAA title" in 2020.
- Some clipping that shouldn't be there... and other minor bugs (not noticeable in the majority of the game).
- Textures in some places are low quality. The contrast sometimes between high quality and low quality sometimes is disturbing...
- The last third of the game seems to have been "rushed" in the production way. The designs are ok but just that, ok, not at the level of Raccon City or the police station. Too much simplicity / cloning things. You might have the feeling that they were designing a longer game at first but they had to rush it to accomplish the release date. You might understand that when you see save rooms incredibly (realy, a lot)  next to others.
- It seems it might be way too short for what we, the fans, could wish. But hey, good things, when short, are twice as good.

[h1][b]Resident Evil 3 Remake: My Honest Review[/b][/h1]
[b](SPOILER ALERT! DO NOT READ IF YOU HAVE NOT PLAYED THE GAME)

(Updated April 6, 2020)[/b]

[b]So, is the Resident Evil 3 Remake truly what the majority (or minority) claims it to be? Is it too short? Is there too much cut content? Should it have just been DLC? Is it as action-packed as RE5 or RE6? There is some truth and some falsehood to these claims, at least in my opinion.[/b]

[h1][b]1. Is the game too short?[/b][/h1]
[b]If you compare it to the RE2 Remake, then yes. However, this is because RE3 only has one scenario, whereas RE2R had two. While RE2R allowed you to explore at your own pace if you avoided Mr. X, Nemesis is a different story. I tried to explore, but with Nemesis constantly stalking Jill, it’s much harder.

Mr. X is easy to avoid because he is slow and easy to dodge. Nemesis, on the other hand, runs and uses his tentacle/whip to pull you down. While he is dodgeable, he doesn't let you roam the area peacefully. My first playthrough on Medium difficulty took about 4 to 5 hours. I imagine that playing on the hardest difficulty for the first time would take closer to 6 to 8 hours.[/b]

[h1][b]2. Is there a lot of cut content?[/b][/h1]
[b]I wouldn’t say "a lot," but some iconic scenes and locations from the original were removed, such as Brad’s original death scene and the Clock Tower. Instead, these elements were "reimagined."

We get to see what happened to Marvin and other RPD officers, connecting the story to RE2R. While some classic scenes are gone, they added new locations like the Umbrella Underground Lab.[/b]

[h1][b]3. Should this have been DLC?[/b][/h1]
[b]Are you kidding? I can’t believe people are saying a game with this much production value should have been DLC. It is much more than that. Just because it is shorter than RE2R doesn’t make it a DLC.[/b]

[h1][b]Action vs. Horror[/b][/h1]
[b]RE3R brings new interactions between Jill, Carlos, and Nikolai, along with new locations, death scenes, and redesigned monsters.[/b]

[h1][b]Is it scary?[/b][/h1]
[b]There are some locations that gave me the chills, but if you want pure horror like RE2R, you might be disappointed. RE3 was always meant to be more action-oriented. You are given plenty of ammunition to fight zombies and Nemesis. It feels different from RE5 and RE6, though; in RE5, I felt tension but not fear, whereas RE6 (specifically Leon and Ada’s campaigns) tried to balance both.[/b]

[h1][b]Final Verdict: 7.5 to 8 / 10[/b][/h1]
[b]The game isn't a 10/10, but it’s still very good. Is it easy? Not necessarily. Even on Medium, it provides a challenge. I am disappointed that certain iconic scenes were removed, but that doesn't make the game "bad." They replaced them with new content that connects well to the overall story.

Short length doesn't equal a bad game. Personally, I’d rather play a high-quality 5-hour game than a 20-hour game that drags on. That’s just my preference.

Pros & Cons
Cons: I wish the game was a bit longer, I miss the removed iconic scenes, and I wish there were more costumes for Jill (hopefully we get some DLC later).

Pros: The "Shop" unlocks after your first playthrough, adding replayability by letting you unlock Jill’s RE1 costume and powerful weapons.

Difficulty: For those who found Hardcore too easy, Nightmare and Inferno modes are much more challenging. In these modes, Nemesis can even follow you into certain safe rooms![/b]

[h1][b]Resident Evil Resistance[/b][/h1]
[b]This is a new multiplayer IP from Capcom. RE fans were originally hoping for an Outbreak remake and were disappointed to get this "Dead by Daylight" style 4-vs-1 game instead.

Is it fun? Yes! Despite my initial skepticism, it has a lot of potential. Playing as a Mastermind against four Survivors is quite entertaining. Since it's included for free with RE3R, you should definitely give it a try. I hope Capcom continues to update it with new characters like Jill Valentine (added April 10th). Don't let it sit in your library—give it a chance!

Agree or disagree? That’s up to you. In the end, there is no right or wrong answer—it's all about whether you enjoy the experience.[/b]

Okay, changing my review from before.
I judged the game too quickly, based on my own nostalgic feelings coming back when I was playing it at release.

To say this is a good Resident Evil 3 remake, would be really far off base. It's a good re-imagining of Resident Evil 3. But, no. It's not a game that's gonna when you play it bring you back to all of the nostalgic moments from the original when trying to escape Raccoon City with Jill and Carlos.

Is it a terrible game? No. Is it a underwhelming game in terms of making you wanna not replay it over and over? Yes. Nemesis hardly feels like a threat in this game, compared to the original. Growing up, I was always so scared to come across him in Raccoon City because the paths were so narrow and he would literally chase you through 80% of the game. Where as with this game, it's mostly through scripted locations here and there where he'll appear. Otherwise, you're pretty much free to roam around until it gets to that point of no return and he appears. 

I wouldn't consider the original Resident Evil 3 to be big on puzzles, but neither is this one. In fact, how many puzzles are in this game? 2 maybe tops? Most of the time, you're just trying to  to get from point A to point B back to point A so you can jump to the next part. The fact that most of the time it feels very linear is quite upsetting. Sure, you can explore the downtown/uptown area (as small as it is) freely until Nemesis appears in a scripted sequence. But, otherwise, it doesn't really bring me the joy of just exploring Raccoon City like the original.

Let's also not talk about the fact they offer what? 2 costumes for the whole game? Well, I should say 3..but are we really gonna count that costume they want you to buy, that's not even a 100% replica of the original? But tbh, that whole ordeal doesn't really concern me in terms of it being a deal breaker since I find her new default costume to be fine. I just wish they had offered more like the original. At least unlockable costumes, or something.

The pacing is definitely very quick. You should be able to beat this game even for a first time under 3 hours. That is if you're not taking a lot of breaks here and there. I would say sure, it could be completed around the same time as the Resident Evil 2 remake. But except in that game, pacing felt a bit more natural and to the original as where this one..you're just kind of rushing to get from one spot to the next. Which goes back to the fact, you don't really get to enjoy the locations you're at for too long because once you get the parts you need, you just book it to the spot they're used for and continue on (which is why I loved the original because backtracking meant unlocking new locations, and getting to enjoy more of the city than just quickly rushing from one spot to the next).

I will say my favorite parts of this game come from the soundtrack, and the last bits of it. The hospital, and NEST lab 2 are probably my favorite points of the game. Not because the game is coming to a close, but because those locations I felt really amped up the RE feel of the series. The hospital in the remake is 100% better than the original by far. As where the original one you were just kind of in and out, didn't feel like a real hospital to me where as this one, you kind of feel like you are present in a hospital that's been overrun with zombies and other virus bioweapons. Plus, this part is where Carlos shines the most. Minus that little ending sequence with the shutters...I'm not sure why Capcom has to continually place some wait it out survival sequence in their newer games. It might have been an interesting spin in RE 4..but none of us asked for it in a remake.

As for NEST 2, I actually enjoyed this NEST more than the one in Resident Evil 2 remake. I think mainly because even though it's smaller, it feels more believable in terms of a laboratory.  I am aware with the NEST 1 from the 2nd remake is based on the original one, which was more open spaced and larger than this one so I get it..but I just enjoyed the atmosphere more so in this variation an Umbrella lab. 

And for the soundtrack, they really didn't let us down with this game as opposed to the 2nd remake. I love the neat remixes of some of the original songs you'll hear in certain spots in the game. It's a neat moment of just a glimpse of nostalgia, but all well placed where you feel like.."Wow...I really feel like I'm in Raccoon City again" that is until you realize that they've condensed the city from the original in to like a 2-3 block map. But I digress. At least the soundtrack will make you still feel a little bad ass as Jill when trying to escape. 

All and all, the game is okay. I would consider this a buy if you played RE 2 remake and enjoyed it since it's clearly a follow up game. Would I consider this if you were a fan of the original, and want that nostalgic hit? No. Because you're only gonna get it in small amounts and then feel a bit disappointed afterwards. I'm aware I didn't include the RPD in my review (because let's be honest...I still don't get that change..but I don't think it needs to be said since a lot of us were confused, and probably angry they switched the roles for Carlos going there instead of Jill).

Is the game worth $60? That's more so on the buyer, and if they're willing to pay that much for a remake...and yes, you're gonna say "but you spent that much on RE 2 remake.." yes I did. And guess what? At least then I was getting a full game, with tons of costumes, endless replay value, and just overall a great remake (minus a few misses here and there). But for RE 3 remake, you're literally paying for two games when in reality...you're more so paying for Resistance..so ya, take a long thought process on that one. I'd say wait until it's on sale again, and then buy it..otherwise, wait it out and maybe play it once or twice and put it down.

Unsurprisingly, Capcom messed up and more or less missed the point with this game. They cut out a lot of RE3's content and literally all of the puzzles, as well as the core mechanic of RE3: Nemesis - the actual Nemesis encounters. There are literally 2 puzzles in the entire game and the majority of it takes place in the same city block where Nemesis only shows up after you've reached certain story markers. After that, he is either a cutscene, or a mandatory boss fight every time he appears. 

On launch, the game had the same issues as RE2 remake. Connection to RE Net broke the game, causing massive stuttering and frame loss. Frequent bluetooth controller desyncs on the game's behalf completely nuke the game too - causing an endless spin which eventually caused a game crash, and might even completely crash Steam. Without a wired controller, there was no point even trying to use one, which is utterly ridiculous. Those issues were fixed, fortunately.  Enemies that are any further away than 20 feet are still animated at 30 FPS just like RE2. The game lacks any alternate costumes besides the pre-order DLC and the 2 unlockables, and unlike RE2 pre-order did not come with a swappable "Classic OST" option. Some of the original OST tracks are in the game or are remixed, but you won't ever hear them because the game doesn't last long enough for you to unintentionally stay in one area for too long.

If that weren't all bad enough, RE3 is objectively a functional downgrade from RE2. The game still has flashbangs, knives and grenades for example, but none of these any longer function as defense weapons - just equippables. If an enemy grabs you, you literally can't shove a knife in their head or a grenade in their mouth and are forced to just take damage. As if it's a trade off for the quick dodge system. When you pick up an item that can be combined, you can't move it directly onto the combinable item when it's picked up. You have to open the inventory, again. This was a vital trick when it came to speedrunning RE2 and considering how many achievements and unlockables in RE3 are based on S rankings - of which time is a key requirement - it's ridiculous. 


Recommended specs are also utter nonsense - to max the game out you allegedly need 14 gb of video ram, which no graphics card actually had at the time of release.


RE3R features the laziest, most derivative possible "evolution" of Resident Evil i.e vania level design. The majority of gameplay revolves around making sure you explore what little area is available in order to get to the next scripted event - the only two parts with any real gameplay are the hospital and the downtown area. 

Proper RE level design would require solving puzzles to get keys or progresion items, or solving puzzles that only Jill could solve, or better yet - requiring Carlos and Jill to each solve part of those same puzzles on their playthrough, thus edifying the concept of playing both characters in the same area. Think biometric lock room in RE2 Umbrella Lab that could only be opened in Scenario B.

There are exactly two "puzzles" in this entire game and the solution for one of them is directly in your face while you're solving it.

It's pure dreck. The game features literally nothing from the original in terms of gameplay when you're talking about signature RE level progression and as stated initially, huge sections of the original RE3 Nemesis just aren't there like the clock tower, the park, the newspaper office, the gas station, the dead factory and more. What's worse is that the game blatantly tells you where key items are with a giant arrow, just like RE2R and RE7 did. So what little exploration you can pretend there is, gets immediately spoiled by this games casual design.

Fortunately there's a mod on PC to get rid of that to make this closer to a real RE game. But it's not enough.

It's (trademark RE gameplay) all entirely replaced by even lazier, on rails design than RE4. The only games that did a similarly poor job of not being a RE game were 4, 5, and 6. 

The game is worth playing but it pales in comparison to any other title in the franchise, even in action sequences. Another example of why the review system needs a "Meh" option.

I loved the resident evil 2 remake (RE2), I loved the exploration aspects of the game and the item discovery along with the puzzle solving. The pacing of RE2 is very good as well, slowly building up the suspense and allowing you to absorb what is happening on screen while feeling the terror of being chased by Mr.X (Later on). Resident evil 3 remake (RE3) either lacks in these in some aspects or ignores them completely.

RE3 has exploration mechanics but all while you are getting chased constantly and hit without mercy. It's nearly impossible to dodge the new "big boss" Nemesis, and I hate how they changed it from the original. It has a new dodge mechanic that allows you to side step and roll out of the way if you hit it just right, but how do you dodge an enemy that is charging behind you that you cannot see? You can't most of the time which allows it to grant free hits on you.

Item discovery in RE3 is constant and boring. In RE2 you are able to take your time with looking around at the police station and finding items, while new storage upgrades/weapons are few and far between. In RE3 you are constantly running, only have time to explore your surroundings in brief instances and when it does slow down while you are doing the very childish puzzle solving as it just throws new items and upgrades at you. 

What makes Resident Evil great? The suspense and terror of not knowing what is around the corner, the close calls with enemies when you are 1 hit away from death, that breath of relief knowing you made it to a safe room in time when a licker was inches from your heels. Those are things RE2 had. In RE3 as stated before you are constantly being chased and hit at all times. It is annoying and not fun. I was stuck for 20-30 minutes on the third encounter with Nemesis just because he kept either grabbing me with his tongue or hit me from feet away when he charged. Why don't you just dodge it? Because like I said, its nearly impossible to hit the dodge roll at the right time when you can't even see him!

In its defense, I was only able to get as far as the subway leaving the station because it took me almost 2 hours to get there. I however, wanted a refund because of the fact I had nearly no fun while playing this game. The only good parts that I experienced while playing were looking at the stunning graphics for the brief moments that I could stand still and a brief part when you are turning on the power and these new scary spider zombies are chasing you.

I may buy this game in the future when it is on sale for the story, but as of right now I am not paying full price for a crappy run and gun simulator.
